title: Advertise with Us
content:
Yotta Data Services has partnered with IntelliDB Enterprise to offer managed database-as-a-service (DBaaS) for AI applications on Yotta’s sovereign cloud in India.

The partnership combines Yotta’s cloud and AI infrastructure with IntelliDB Enterprise’s PostgreSQL database management platform and native vector database capabilities. The companies said the service will allow enterprises and government organisations to run AI workloads within India while meeting data residency and regulatory requirements.

The offering is targeted at government organisations, banks and financial services companies, regulated industries, enterprises and digital-native businesses that need databases for both conventional applications and AI workloads.

The companies said the service will support applications using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), semantic search, and AI agents by combining PostgreSQL with vector-database capabilities.

AI applications increasingly require databases capable of handling structured enterprise data alongside vector embeddings used by systems that retrieve information for large language models. Yotta and IntelliDB said their joint platform will provide these capabilities through a managed service.

Customers will also be able to modernise applications running on legacy databases and consume managed PostgreSQL with automated operations, high availability and security features.

“The next wave of enterprise transformation will be driven by AI, and every AI application depends on trusted, intelligent and sovereign data,” Sunil Gupta, Co-founder, Managing Director and CEO of Yotta Data Services, said.

“Our partnership with IntelliDB Enterprise strengthens this vision by adding an AI-ready database layer that enables organisations to build secure, scalable, and future-ready AI applications entirely on India's sovereign digital infrastructure,” he added.

The companies said the database services will be hosted entirely in India, allowing organisations to keep their application data in the country while running AI workloads.

The partnership comes as enterprises and government organisations look to run AI systems on infrastructure that meets local data residency and compliance requirements.

Yotta has been building its sovereign cloud and AI infrastructure portfolio, including cloud services, GPU infrastructure, AI model services and enterprise AI platforms. The IntelliDB partnership adds managed database services to that stack.

Gagandeep Singh, co-founder and CEO of IntelliDB Enterprise, said database infrastructure would play a central role as organisations scale AI deployments.

“AI initiatives and scaling for any organisation is only as strong as the data infrastructure underneath it,” Singh said.

“This partnership brings our secure, AI-powered and intelligent database platform to more Indian enterprises and government organisations, hosted entirely within India. Together with Yotta, we are simplifying database operations while giving customers a secure, scalable, AI-powered platform.”

The companies said the service will allow customers to move from traditional enterprise workloads to AI applications on the same sovereign cloud infrastructure, without moving data outside India.

title: Advertise with Us
content:
Wispr, the artificial intelligence company behind AI dictation tool Wispr Flow, has raised $280 million in Series B funding at a $2 billion valuation, led by long-time investor Menlo Ventures. The company said the round brings its total capital raised to $361 million.

“In a little over a year, voice has gone from something people were questioning to something they rely on, and it happened faster than we expected,” Tanay Kothari, Co-founder and CEO of Wispr, said in a statement.

The company said the new funding will support investment in its products, research lab, models, and team.

Existing investors Notable Capital, NEA, Neo Ventures, 8VC, and MVP Ventures participated in the round. New investors include Acrew, Activate, Forerunner, Goodwater, Peak XV, Together Fund and PLUS Capital, along with a select group of artists, athletes, and cultural leaders.

Wispr also previewed Canto, its first proprietary speech model. The company said the 2-billion-parameter model was built for conditions in which speech recognition is more difficult, including background noise, wind, heavy accents, and music.

Wispr said word error rates in the hardest conditions fall from more than 30% to between 5% and 10%. The company also expects Canto to reduce the number of dictations users need to edit by 30–35% across everyday use, according to Reuters.

The model is also designed to handle multilingual speech, including situations where speakers switch between languages. Wispr used Hinglish as an example, saying speakers may switch between Hindi and English while expecting the resulting text in Roman script. The company said Canto can also use a user's dictionary and names to improve transcription.

Wispr said future versions of Canto will become larger and more capable, with each model intended to improve Flow's dictation. The company has not announced a general availability date for Canto.

Wispr said more than 60 billion words have been written with Flow, which is used by people at almost all Fortune 500 companies and more than 10,000 enterprises.

The company is also expanding beyond dictation. Wispr launched Flow Notetaker for meetings shortly before the Series B announcement and said it is building an intelligence layer for human-AI interaction, starting with voice and eventually extending to other modalities.

“If by the end of the year, the voice dictation platform is the only thing that Wispr has—it will probably die. We did something with Wispr once, and that is a playbook that we need to rise and repeat,” Kothari earlier told AIM.

The Series B follows Wispr's $30 million Series A led by Menlo Ventures in June 2025 and a $25 million Series A extension led by Notable Capital in November 2025. The November round brought total funding to $81 million and valued Wispr at $700 million, according to Reuters.

Kothari said Wispr's broader goal is to make voice a primary way of interacting with computers

content:
Tagbin has launched Brixx, an AI platform that generates designs and project plans using natural-language prompts for the construction sector.

Initially developed for the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region, Brixx now supports multiple stages of construction projects.

Gurugram-based Tagbin has launched Brixx, an AI-powered platform that aims to transform architecture, engineering, and construction workflows by letting users generate designs, CAD drawings, BIM models, bills of quantities (BOQs), detailed project reports (DPRs), and implementation plans using natural-language prompts.

Brixx initially started as an AI-powered DPR solution for the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER), Government of India, before expanding into a broader platform for the architecture, engineering, and construction sector. Users can describe project requirements in natural language, after which the platform generates coordinated designs, drawings, BIM models, cost estimates, DPRs, and project plans.

The platform is designed to cover multiple stages of a construction project, including architectural concept generation, space planning, CAD layouts, technical drawings, and coordinated BIM models. It can also prepare itemised BOQs and preliminary cost estimates, apply relevant building regulations and development controls, and generate DPRs, schedules, and implementation plans.

Brixx also extends beyond design and documentation into project monitoring. The platform is being developed to review designs for potential compliance issues, monitor construction using digital and visual evidence, and compare on-site construction against sanctioned designs. It can identify deviations, delays, and cost variations during execution.

“Software development is being transformed by platforms that convert ideas and prompts into working applications. We believe architecture and construction are ready for the same transformation,” said Saurav Bhaik, Founder and CEO of Tagbin, in a statement.

He added that Brixx can convert project requirements into coordinated designs, BIM models, drawings, BOQs, and execution plans while helping verify whether construction follows the sanctioned design.

The company said Brixx aims to create a digital connection between approved designs and construction, allowing stakeholders to track project progress and identify problems across the project lifecycle. Its longer-term vision covers stages from project conception and statutory approvals through procurement and completion.

For government agencies, Brixx can support DPR preparation, building-plan scrutiny, digital approvals and occupancy inspections. Private developers, architects and engineering firms can use the platform for design, estimation, documentation, and coordination between design and execution teams.

Superhealth aims to expand its AI-native hospital model from one facility in Bengaluru to 100 across India.

Dalvir Singh Suri has been appointed as Head of Operations to build systems for scaling Superhealth's model.

Bengaluru-based Superhealth has appointed former Dunzo co-founder Dalvir Singh Suri as its Head of Operations, as the healthcare startup looks to scale its AI-native hospital model from its first facility to 100 multispecialty hospitals across India.

Suri will be responsible for building the systems, teams, and operating processes needed to replicate Superhealth’s model across its planned network over the next five to seven years. His appointment comes as the company seeks to move beyond proving its model at a single hospital and build the operational backbone required to scale it.

At the centre of that model is SuperOS, Superhealth’s proprietary AI-native hospital operating system. The company says the system has been running its flagship hospital since day one, with real-time patient monitoring, clinical audits, and digitally orchestrated clinical and operational workflows.

Superhealth opened its first hospital in Bengaluru 10 months ago and describes its model as combining AI-native software with doctor consultation and all-inclusive pricing.

The appointment aims to replicate an AI-native hospital model that works at one facility, then standardise and reproduce it across a 100-hospital network.

Suri brings nearly 17 years of experience building and scaling operating systems, including more than eight years at Dunzo, where he worked on hyperlocal operations.

“Operational excellence is how a great care model becomes repeatable,” said Manoj Kumar, Founder and COO, Superhealth Hospitals. He said the company wants patients to experience the same operational standards across every Superhealth centre.

The move comes as healthcare companies increasingly use AI not only for patient-facing applications but also to automate and coordinate internal workflows. In Superhealth’s case, the ambition is to make AI part of the hospital’s underlying operating layer—from monitoring and audits to coordinating clinical and operational processes.

“The next challenge is to scale that experience with speed and discipline,” Suri said, adding that he will focus on building the operations organisation needed to support Superhealth’s expansion.

content:
Razorpay has announced Vulcan, a transformer-based AI foundation model designed specifically for payments, trained on nearly 3 trillion data points spanning 4 billion payments on its network.

Built with NVIDIA GPUs and AWS cloud infrastructure, the model is intended to improve payment routing, fraud detection, risk assessment and checkout personalisation.

Razorpay said it has already tested early components of the model on live transactions across its network.

The company claims an 8–10% improvement in payment success rates, an eightfold increase in international card fraud detection, and five times more fraudulent or disputed transactions identified without increasing the number of alerts.

The model learns from roughly 3,000 signals per transaction. Razorpay said it developed the model as a proprietary system, with both its architecture and training data built in-house.

The company’s rationale for a shared model is that payment decisions often depend on overlapping signals. Routing, fraud, risk and checkout systems have traditionally been developed as separate machine-learning models.

Vulcan is intended to provide a common intelligence layer that can use those signals across multiple payment decisions.

One application is real-time routing. The model scores available payment routes before a transaction is attempted and selects the route it predicts is most likely to succeed.

Razorpay said the model is also being used to detect fraud patterns across merchants, identify risky cash-on-delivery orders and predict which payment method is most likely to work for an individual shopper.

Razorpay’s Magic Checkout has also seen a 40% increase in shoppers being shown their preferred UPI application, which the company said is helping complete an additional 100,000–200,000 purchases each month.

The model is not an LLM. Razorpay said it uses transformer architecture but is trained to model patterns in payment transactions rather than language.

The company described it as a foundation model because the same underlying representation of payment behaviour can be adapted to multiple downstream use cases rather than requiring a separate model for each task.

NVIDIA GPUs are being used for training and running the model at scale, while AWS infrastructure, including Amazon SageMaker, supports its development, training and deployment. Razorpay said customers including Blinkit, Bachatt and redBus have begun using capabilities derived from the model in live payment environments.

Harshil Mathur, CEO and co-founder of Razorpay, said the objective was to address reliability across India's expanding digital payment base. “Every payment teaches the system something that makes the next payment better,” he said.

Pahal Patangia, head of global industry business development and payments at NVIDIA, said the work combines payments data with “real-time contextual intelligence”, while AWS said the model consolidates billions of transaction insights into a single intelligence layer.

Razorpay said it eventually intends to extend the model across more payment decisions, including authentication, routing, fraud detection and lending.

In March, Razorpay launched Agent Studio, a marketplace and builder for AI agents designed to handle payment and financial operations. Initial agents included tools for recovering abandoned carts and failed subscriptions, responding to payment disputes and forecasting cash flow.

Its agentic onboarding system, for example, was designed to reduce merchant onboarding from 30–45 minutes to about five minutes, while its integration agent can help businesses connect Razorpay to their technology stack in under 10 minutes.

India has approved 31 new electronics manufacturing projects aimed at boosting local production of critical components.

The projects will create nearly 9,600 direct jobs across 10 states and involve an investment of ₹6,844 crore.

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has approved 31 new electronics manufacturing projects. These projects carry a projected investment of ₹6,844 crore and span 10 states.

The approvals seek to expand domestic production of electronics components and raw materials. They cover 20 products, including filters, coils, speakers, optical transceivers and battery materials. The projects are expected to create 9,588 direct jobs.

The approvals form part of the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS). They take the total number of approved projects under the scheme to 106.

The latest projects include India’s first domestic manufacturing proposals for several critical components. These include filters, coils and speakers. They also cover acetylene black and electrolyte additives used in electronics supply chains.

Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said ECMS is building a ‘Swadeshi’ electronics value chain. He added that the scheme is moving beyond assembly into domestic component and raw material production.

The 31 projects together entail ₹7,877 crore in investment, including the additional approved investment. They are expected to generate ₹82,243 crore in production.

Additionally, Wipro Global Engineering and Electronic Materials also received approval for an additional ₹1,033 crore investment. The company will use the investment to manufacture copper-clad laminate.

The approved projects cover three sub-assemblies, 10 components and six supply chain products. They also include capital goods and their parts.

The sub-assembly projects cover camera modules, display modules and optical transceiver SFPs. Companies receiving approvals include Minda Instrument, TXB Optics and SkyQuad Electronics & Appliances.

The component projects include connectors, relays, transducers, filters, capacitors and coils. Other approved products include antennas, speakers, microphones, enclosures and metal shielding covers.

The supply chain projects include anode material, rare earth permanent magnets and acetylene black. They also cover electrolyte additives, metallised films and hermetic terminals.

The new approvals cover Goa, Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.

The government said 38 of the 106 approved projects have already started manufacturing. Another 16 projects have reached advanced construction or machinery installation stages.

Across all 106 projects, approved investment now stands at ₹69,548 crore. The projects are expected to generate ₹5.34 lakh crore in production and 74,628 direct jobs.

Production capacity has already exceeded domestic demand in some categories. Output reaches about 110% of demand for anode material, 350% for optical transceiver SFPs and 200% for relays.

The government launched ECMS to deepen India’s electronics supply chain. The scheme targets components, sub-assemblies, camera modules, optical transceivers and manufacturing equipment.

Groq uses its language processing units (LPUs) to provide AI inference services. The company said its platform processes trillions of tokens every week across its developer, enterprise, and AI-native customer base.

Groq and NVIDIA entered into a non-exclusive licensing agreement in December last year under which NVIDIA licensed Groq’s inference technology.

Groq continues to operate independently, while its GroqCloud service remains operational. Groq founder Jonathan Ross, president Sunny Madra, and several other employees joined NVIDIA as part of the agreement.

Experion Technologies has inaugurated a 58,000 sq ft AI Centre in Thiruvananthapuram to enhance its product engineering operations.

The centre will accommodate over 700 engineers and act as an AI Centre of Excellence.

Product engineering and digital transformation services company Experion Technologies inaugurated a 58,000 sq ft development centre at Technopark in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam. The centre will house more than 700 engineers and serve as the company’s AI Centre of Excellence (AI CoE).

Renowned aerospace engineer and missile scientist Tessy Thomas, widely known as “The Missile Woman of India”, inaugurated the facility. She is known for her leadership roles in the Agni-IV and Agni-V missile programmes.

Experion said the centre will expand its global delivery capacity and AI engineering operations.

Experion also announced ARC, its AI-native product engineering operating model, and the Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) Academy. The company designed the academy to prepare engineers for customer-facing AI roles. The CoE will support product discovery, engineering, AI model integration, deployment, and optimisation for global customers.

“Customers leveraging ARC have already reported project timeline reductions of 15–30%,” said Binu Jacob, Co-founder and CEO of Experion Technologies, in a statement. He added that the company is scaling operations and investing in infrastructure to meet demand for AI-native product engineering.

The AI CoE will serve as the operational hub for Experion’s ARC framework. The model embeds AI across the software development lifecycle, from product discovery and design to deployment and continuous optimisation. Experion said the approach aims to help teams build production-ready software faster.

The centre will support projects across banking and financial services, automotive, retail, healthcare, and insurance. Its customers span markets including the US, UK, Australia, and Japan. The facility also includes AI innovation labs, embedded IoT labs, and rapid prototyping spaces. It also has collaborative engineering zones and learning facilities.

Jacob said the new AI CoE will support AI-led product engineering at scale. He added that the facility will create opportunities for engineers to work on product engineering challenges for global customers.

Experion’s FDE Academy will train engineers to work directly with customers on AI deployments. FDEs will identify business challenges, build AI solutions and deploy them into production. The academy will use AI labs, customer workshops, mentoring, hackathons, and live projects.

“AI is not replacing engineers; it is redefining engineering and helping businesses scale faster,” said Sreekumar Pillai, Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer at Experion Technologies.

Pillai said the CoE and FDE Academy will immerse engineers in AI-led product engineering. The programme will also prepare them for deployment-ready roles that involve close collaboration with customers.

Experion has nearly 1,800 professionals across delivery centres and offices in India, the US, UK, and Australia. The company works across banking, healthcare, retail, automotive, logistics, and insurance.

Digantara has launched the MOSAIC network to enable continuous tracking of objects in Low Earth Orbit using AI-powered optical sensors.

MOSAIC aims to decrease India's dependence on foreign providers for critical orbital tracking services.

Bengaluru-based Digantara has unveiled MOSAIC, an AI-powered optical sensor network for continuous tracking of objects in Low Earth Orbit. The company said the initial deployment has five nodes operating as one coordinated surveillance network.

Digantara said MOSAIC will reduce India’s reliance on foreign commercial providers for time-critical orbital tracking. The network combines electro-optical sensors, onboard processing and AI-based detection to identify and track Resident Space Objects.

It has positioned MOSAIC against the growing need for sovereign space surveillance capabilities. It said the system builds on India’s push for self-reliance in strategically critical technologies.

Anirudh Sharma, Founder and CEO of Digantara, said the company wants to build resilient infrastructure through distributed systems.

“Every big infrastructure problem eventually stops being about having one perfect system and starts being about having many resilient ones,” Sharma said.

He said Digantara began by asking what exists in orbit and is now focused on what operators need to know about it. The company aims to deploy more sensors globally and maintain independent orbital catalogues.

The launch also follows lessons from Operation Sindoor, according to Digantara. India used domestic satellite assets alongside commercial imagery during the operation, the company said.

Digantara said MOSAIC addresses the need for continuous access to orbital data without relying solely on foreign-owned sensors. The system is designed to provide wide-area detection and custody of objects across orbital regimes.

Each MOSAIC node combines an Optical Head Unit with an Electronics Head Unit. The optical unit handles sky imaging, while the electronics unit manages processing, timing, communications and autonomy.

The nodes operate on solar power with battery backup. Digantara said it designed them to operate across environments ranging from the Thar desert to the Himalayas.

The system combines sensor sensitivity with a wide field of view to detect faint objects across large sections of the sky. Its AI and machine learning system identifies stars and Resident Space Objects, including faint targets.

MOSAIC then uses a Lost-in-Space attitude estimation approach to determine an object’s position. The approach requires no prior information or cueing.

Digantara also plans to extend MOSAIC to alternative navigation applications. The company specifically cited celestial navigation in GPS-denied environments.

MOSAIC extends Digantara’s existing Space Domain Awareness infrastructure. That infrastructure combines space-based tracking, data fusion and an in-house processing engine.

The company said MOSAIC will provide the wide-area detection and custody layer for this infrastructure. Digantara aims to detect, characterise and track objects from LEO through Geostationary Earth Orbit.

AI4Bharat and Bodhan AI have developed Indic-Transcribe, a 1.2-billion-parameter speech recognition model trained on 1.3 million hours of audio to transcribe speech across 26 Indian languages and English.

The organisations said the model is built to handle code-mixed speech, accents and children’s speech, with its first use case focused on education. Indic-Transcribe is scheduled to go live on Bodhan AI on September 5.

“India is a voice-first nation with several languages, diverse scripts, and countless accents that no single ‘Indian English’ or ‘standard Hindi’ ever quite captures,” AI4Bharat said in a LinkedIn post announcing the model.

The model supports applications where spoken Indian languages need to be converted into text, including education, healthcare, finance and governance. AI4Bharat said its first priority is to allow teachers and students to interact with technology “in their own voice, their own accent, their own language”.

Indic-Transcribe also includes code-mixed speech recognition, reflecting conversations where speakers switch between Indian languages and English.

The teams said the model was trained to handle children’s speech, with data collection involving parental consent, child assent and clearance procedures.

The launch builds on AI4Bharat’s earlier work in speech recognition. Its IndicConformer model supports all 22 constitutionally recognised Indian languages and is available as an open-source ASR model. The model uses a Conformer architecture and supports both CTC and RNN-T decoding.

AI4Bharat has also previously worked on IndicWav2Vec, a multilingual speech model pretrained on 40 Indian languages, and has released speech datasets and models as part of its broader effort to build language technology for India.

Bodhan AI, based at IIT Madras and founded in 2026, focuses on AI for education and is building multilingual technologies across text, speech and vision. Its research programme is part of what it describes as the Bharat EduAI Stack.

The Indic-Transcribe launch also comes as speech recognition becomes a larger focus of India’s AI ecosystem, with developers building models that can handle regional languages, accents and code-switching rather than relying on English-centric speech systems.

TCS has launched the AgentHub platform to enhance clinical development and pharmacovigilance in the pharmaceutical industry.

The platform aims to improve efficiency in clinical data management by up to 40% and reduce safety case processing costs by 30%.

TCS has launched TCS ADD AgentHub, an enterprise AI platform designed to help pharmaceutical companies deploy agentic AI across clinical development and pharmacovigilance while meeting regulatory and audit requirements.

The platform is built for highly regulated pharma environments, where fragmented systems, growing data volumes, and increasing regulatory expectations have made scaling AI across research and development workflows challenging. TCS said AgentHub allows companies to create and deploy AI agents with defined roles, human oversight, and built-in auditability.

According to TCS, solutions powered by the platform have delivered up to 40% efficiency gains in clinical data management, reduced clinical study build effort by up to 30% through metadata-driven automation, and generated up to 30% cost savings in end-to-end safety case processing. AI-powered safety agents can also cut quality-control effort by as much as 50%, the company said.

AgentHub supports workflows including individual case safety report intake, data entry, coding and review, literature analysis, study design, protocol digitisation, clinical data review, SDTM transformation, and medical monitoring assistance. TCS said its catalogue of AI agents can be deployed progressively based on an organisation's requirements, with minimal integration and implementation effort.

The platform follows a human-plus-AI operating model, in which AI agents are embedded into enterprise workflows while humans retain responsibility for governance and decision-making.

“TCS ADD AgentHub is a role-based, enterprise-ready, and trusted AI platform that will enable our customers to accelerate drug development using agentic AI at scale,” said Debashis Ghosh, President, Lifesciences and Healthcare, TCS. He added that TCS aims to move towards autonomous enterprise functions where AI agents work alongside humans to drive innovation in drug development and improve patient safety.

Stripe has finalised an agreement to acquire AI infrastructure startup OpenRouter for more than $7 billion, according to a Bloomberg report. The acquisition would give the payments company control of a platform that lets developers access and switch between hundreds of AI models.

The deal comes just months after OpenRouter raised $113 million in a Series B round that valued the company at about $1.3 billion.

OpenRouter operates an AI gateway that provides access to more than 400 models through a single interface. Its platform lets developers and businesses choose models based on factors such as cost, performance and the requirements of a particular task, rather than relying on a single AI provider. Its model lineup includes systems from companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and xAI, as well as open-source models.

The startup was founded in 2023 and has grown rapidly as companies increasingly use multiple AI models instead of committing their workloads to one provider.

OpenRouter said in May that it had eight million users globally and was processing about 100 trillion tokens a month. Its weekly token volume had increased fivefold in six months, from five trillion to 25 trillion.

OpenRouter’s business also fits closely with Stripe’s expansion beyond payments. The companies already have a commercial relationship. In April, OpenRouter announced an integration with Stripe Projects that allowed developers to create OpenRouter accounts, generate API keys and connect billing through Stripe’s command-line tools. The integration gives developers access to more than 400 AI models through a single API.

Stripe has been building its presence across AI infrastructure and the broader technology stack as AI companies generate increasing volumes of usage-based transactions. Acquiring OpenRouter would put Stripe closer to the point where developers select and pay for AI models, potentially giving it a larger role in the flow of AI inference spending.

OpenRouter’s growth has been fuelled by the proliferation of AI models and companies’ growing need to control inference costs. Its platform can route workloads towards different models, including lower-cost alternatives, allowing customers to avoid being locked into one model provider.

The Wall Street Journal previously reported that Stripe was considering buying OpenRouter for around $10 billion, while other technology companies had also shown interest. At the time, the talks were not final and could have attracted competing bids.

OpenRouter’s financial performance has also risen rapidly. The Information reported in July that the company was generating about $140 million in annualised revenue, up nearly threefold from April.

The company’s API aggregates more than 400 proprietary and open-source models and frequently routes requests to closed-source providers, including Anthropic.

Rather than building its own foundation model, OpenRouter operates as an intermediary through which developers can access models from multiple companies.

For Stripe, the acquisition would extend its existing position as a payments layer into a part of the AI stack where model selection, usage tracking, routing and billing are becoming increasingly connected.

IPL team Rajasthan Royals is using OpenAI across cricket analytics, player scouting, ticketing, content creation, and fan engagement, positioning AI as a tool to support human decision-making rather than replace it.

The IPL franchise has integrated OpenAI into its technology stack to analyse cricket data, build AI agents, and make information more accessible to coaches and other teams.

In an interview with Hindustan Times, RR COO Alok Chitre described the technology as a “thinking and doing layer” that brings together information from cricket-specific tools and data sources, turning it into actionable insights.

The system can process both visual and non-visual data, including bowling actions and batting strokes. The franchise is also using AI to reduce the amount of manual work required to analyse large volumes of information.

One application is giving coaches direct access to the franchise’s analytical database. Using voice-to-text, a coach can ask a question verbally and receive an answer based on the available data without having to go through an analyst for every query. The coach, however, remains responsible for the decision.

RR is using OpenAI’s Codex to build AI agents for cricket and commercial operations. During the IPL season, the agents analyse ticket-sales data, identify gaps and highlight opportunities.

The system can also generate visual representations of how different ticket-sales scenarios could affect stadium occupancy. Those insights can help the franchise decide when to open stands or change pricing.

The franchise has also experimented with AI in IPL auction planning. RR organised a hackathon where engineering graduates and other participants developed models and recommendations for an ideal 25-member squad using generative AI and OpenAI APIs.

The strongest participants were invited to Abu Dhabi to present their models to RR’s cricket leadership, including Kumar Sangakkara. Some recommendations influenced the franchise’s eventual decision-making.

RR has crossed 10 billion views and has built an in-house generative AI studio with two people focused on GenAI-led visual content. The team has used ChatGPT to create sets and backgrounds for player photoshoots, allowing creative staff to turn concepts into visuals without requiring formal design expertise.

The franchise has also used GenAI for commercial campaigns. In one tourism campaign, AI-generated visuals placed RR players at different destinations, reducing the need to physically move players for multiple shoots.

RR said human oversight remains part of these workflows. Content goes through people before publication, while coaches continue to decide how cricket data should be used.

OpenAI’s Head of Marketing, India, Sheeladitya Mohanty, pointed to the possibility of more personalised cricket experiences, including through integration with JioHotstar.

OpenAI has disbanded its “preparedness” team, which assessed whether its AI models could pose severe or catastrophic risks, according to the Financial Times. The team was dissolved in July. Its responsibilities have shifted to existing groups focused on areas such as biosecurity and cybersecurity.

According to another report from Wired, Dylan Scandinaro, the head of this preparedness team, has moved internally to assess the safety risks posed by self-improving AI systems.

The move comes after numerous reorganisations at OpenAI this year, where several senior executives have also left or stepped back from their roles.

Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser announced her departure this week. She joined OpenAI in December to lead its efforts to win corporate customers. Brad Lightcap also left this month after eight years at OpenAI. He served as Chief Operating Officer until April, and was then moved to a special-projects role before announcing his departure.

Chloé Bakalar, OpenAI’s Head of Ethics, left in July. She had joined less than a year earlier. Joshua Achiam, the company’s chief futurist and former Head of Mission Alignment, also left in July after almost nine years. Fidji Simo, who ran OpenAI’s applications business and was regarded as CEO Sam Altman’s number two, stepped back from her full-time role in July. She is now an adviser.

The Financial Times report added that these exits are part of the company’s streamlining process ahead of its IPO. OpenAI has also said that it “was moving at an exceptional pace and unafraid to make organisational changes”.

The company confidentially filed for a US listing in June. While the filing did not include a confirmed timeline or offering size, reports suggest that OpenAI could seek a valuation of up to $1 trillion, with a listing in 2027.

OpenAI’s annualised revenue run rate has now crossed $40 billion, according to reports, doubling the $20 billion figure at the end of 2025. The company officially closed its latest funding round in March, with $122 billion in committed capital at an $852 billion post-money valuation.

IISc's SPIRE Lab has released SraVaani, a multilingual speech recognition model for 65 Indian languages and dialects.

The model aims to support low-resource languages often overlooked by existing speech technology.

Researchers at the Indian Institute of Science's (IISc) SPIRE Lab, in collaboration with ARTPARK and with support from Google, have released SraVaani, a multilingual Indian speech recognition model covering 65 languages and dialects.

The model is designed to extend automatic speech recognition into regional and other low-resource Indian languages that remain underserved by existing speech technology, according to IISc.

"As India builds its own capabilities in artificial intelligence, inclusive language technology must be part of that ambition. At IISc, research has always been in service to the nation, and SraVaani, serving more than 60 Indian languages, is a contribution toward that," said Prof Govindan Rangarajan, Director, Indian Institute of Science, in a statement.

SraVaani is publicly available on Hugging Face under an MIT licence, according to IISc.

IISc said the model covers 20 scheduled languages and 45 regional languages and dialects. Its coverage spans languages from across India, including Garo, Angika, Chakma, Kokborok, Tulu, Bundeli, and Bajjika. According to the institute, more than 40 of these languages and dialects are not officially supported by most existing speech-recognition systems.

SraVaani is built on Project Vaani, an IISc initiative that has collected more than 31,000 hours of speech from more than 156,000 speakers across 165 districts, the institute said. The project spans 28 states and three union territories, with participants describing images in their own words rather than reading prepared sentences.

According to IISc, the model was trained in three stages. It was first trained on the complete Vaani speech corpus, followed by audio-image alignment using 11.8 million Vaani audio-image pairs. In the final stage, SraVaani was trained on transcribed speech from Vaani and other Indian speech datasets, including IndicVoices, RESPIN, SPRING-INX, SPICOR, and SYSPIN.

The researchers evaluated SraVaani across eight public benchmark datasets covering Indian languages. IISc said the model achieved the lowest average word error rate among the systems evaluated, while delivering accuracy comparable to leading Indic speech-recognition systems on India's widely supported languages.

On the Garo benchmark, SraVaani recorded a word error rate of 9.5%, compared to 69.4% for the next-best system evaluated, the institute said.

Prof Prasanta Kumar Ghosh, Professor at IISc and Principal Investigator of Project Vaani, said the project began with the goal of making voice AI usable across India's linguistic diversity.

"When we began Project Vaani four years ago, the aim was simple: that voice AI should work for every Indian, not only for those whose languages already had the resources behind them," Prof Ghosh said. "SraVaani is that aim taking shape. It reaches languages today's systems do not serve at all, and it is free and open for anyone to build on."

SraVaani aims to support further research in low-resource speech-to-text, Indian language and dialect recognition, automatic language identification, and sovereign AI applications. Its release also gives developers and researchers access to the model, a demo, and fine-tuning code for further experimentation.

Project Vaani remains the underlying data foundation for the work. Its district-by-district collection approach aims to create speech resources that reflect how Indians actually speak rather than relying only on prepared or standardised text, the institute said.

The collaboration introduces Kivi, a voice app supporting more than 22 Indian languages and code-switching for everyday computing tasks.

HP, the technology hardware company, and AI startup Sarvam, which is building models across voice and language, have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to bring Sarvam's AI capabilities to HP devices at scale.

The companies said the collaboration is designed around how people in the country speak and work, while making everyday computing more natural, multilingual, and accessible.

Ipsita Dasgupta, Senior Vice President and Managing Director, HP India, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka, said, "AI adoption will depend on how naturally the technology fits into the way people already work and learn. By bringing Sarvam's AI capabilities to HP devices, we can make these experiences more accessible across languages and everyday computing tasks."

The first area of this collaboration is Kivi, a voice app powered by Sarvam. According to HP and Sarvam, Kivi lets users speak to their computer to get things done across the applications they already use, including dictating instead of typing, drafting or rewriting content, searching for information, and getting help with tasks.

The companies said Kivi supports more than 22 Indian languages and allows code-switching, letting users interact with their PC in the way they already speak. HP and Sarvam said this is intended to create a simpler, faster, and more accessible computing experience, particularly for people who find typing or navigating traditional interfaces difficult. The companies said they will bring Kivi to HP devices at scale.

While voice is the first area of collaboration, HP and Sarvam said the MoU envisions a deeper partnership as AI reshapes what people expect from their computers and what the PC itself can do. The companies said they aim to bring a broader set of AI experiences across the devices and workflows people rely on every day, over time.

Pratyush Kumar, Co-founder, Sarvam, added, "The PC remains the primary interface through which much of the world gets work done. Voice offers a more natural way to interact with it. By bringing Sarvam's voice and language capabilities to HP devices, we can make that interaction available across the applications people already use every day."

title: What Actually Matters.
content:
Z.ai launched GLM-5.3, which improves performance through post-training enhancements rather than a new base model.

The model demonstrates a significant performance increase over GLM-5.2 on various benchmarks, particularly in coding and cybersecurity tasks.

Z.ai has released GLM-5.3, the latest version of its open-weights model. The company said GLM-5.3 uses the same base model as GLM-5.2, with all of its performance gains coming from post-training.

GLM-5.3 is available through Z.ai's Coding Plan and ZCode, as well as coding agents including Claude Code and OpenCode. Z.ai said the model weights will be publicly released two weeks after launch, following safety evaluation and hardening.

Z.ai said GLM-5.3 delivers a 50% improvement over GLM-5.2 on its in-house Z.ai Code Bench and achieves what the company describes as open-source state-of-the-art results on public benchmarks including Terminal-Bench 3.0 and Agents’ Last Exam.

On Terminal-Bench 3.0, GLM-5.3 scored 28.3, compared with 4.6 for GLM-5.2, while its DeepSWE v1.1 score increased to 66.9 from 46.2.

The company said the gains came from scaling the post-training system used for GLM-5.2. Z.ai continued scaling IndexShare for long-context processing, SAO for reinforcement learning on long-horizon tasks and slime for large-scale asynchronous training, while adding more environments, more diverse tasks, and more compute.

Z.ai said cybersecurity capabilities developed faster than expected as post-training scaled. The company said GLM-5.3 moved beyond identifying individual vulnerabilities and began reasoning across multiple stages of an exploitation chain.

On CyberGym, GLM-5.3 scored 84.5%, up from 77.2% for GLM-5.2. Z.ai said this was the best result on the benchmark. On ExploitBench, GLM-5.3 scored 54.4%, more than twice GLM-5.2's 24.4% score.

On ExploitGym, GLM-5.3 completed 105 tasks under the two-hour budget and 130 under the six-hour budget, compared with 29 and 39 for GLM-5.2. Z.ai said these budgets are normalised using each model's inference speed, so the figures are not simple real-time comparisons.

Z.ai also tested GLM-5.3 against real-world codebases with several security teams in China. After expert review, screening, and deduplication, the company said the model identified 2,436 vulnerabilities across 269 open-source projects, including 1,097 medium-to-high-severity issues.

Z.ai’s Security Disclosure Ledger breaks those 1,097 findings down into 107 critical and 990 high-severity vulnerabilities. The findings covered system kernels, operating systems, browser engines, open-source infrastructure, web applications, and network protocols, with the oldest flaw dating back to 1981.

Z.ai said the work has become an ongoing disclosure program through its Security Disclosure Ledger, which tracks affected projects, severity ratings and CVE identifiers where available. At the time of the announcement, the ledger listed 53 publicly disclosed findings and 2,383 under embargo.

Z.ai said the model weights will be publicly released two weeks after launch, following safety evaluation and hardening.

TCS and Vodafone Business have partnered to enhance digital transformation for UK enterprises.

The collaboration aims to modernise technology and improve customer experience through digital adoption.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has partnered with Vodafone Business to help enterprise customers across the United Kingdom modernise technology, accelerate digital adoption, reduce complexity, and scale to achieve stronger business outcomes and customer experience.

Vodafone Business is the enterprise arm of UK-based VodafoneThree.

TCS said the partnership will help Vodafone Business further strengthen its ability to support UK organisations with secure, resilient, and scalable digital foundations for growth and modernisation.

"UK businesses are looking for partners who understand their market, their customers, and the pressure to modernise quickly," Nick Gliddon, Business Director at VodafoneThree, said in a statement.

"The challenge for many organisations is not ambition, it is execution: making the right technology choices, integrating them properly, and turning investment into measurable impact. We are pleased to welcome TCS to our growing ecosystem of strategic partners, helping Vodafone Business deliver the services, expertise and digital experiences customers need to move faster, reduce complexity and grow with confidence," he added.

The partnership will cover cloud transformation and migration, artificial intelligence (AI) and automation, cybersecurity, network modernisation and digital infrastructure, data and analytics, Internet of Things (IoT) and connected business applications, managed services, and operational transformation, according to TCS.

The partnership also builds on VodafoneThree's £11 billion ($14 billion) investment to create the UK's best network for business, according to TCS.

The combined capabilities intend to support organisations across the public sector, healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, retail, and critical national infrastructure, the company said.

TCS said the partnership builds on its more than 50-year presence in the UK, where it has invested in innovation, talent, and enterprise transformation. The company said it has created 42,000 jobs in the UK, both directly and indirectly.

TCS's AI Experience Zone and London Design Studio, a reimagining of its flagship TCS PacePort facility, will support innovation and client collaboration in the UK.

"We see enormous potential to leverage AI and digital transformation, scale of operating model, deep technology expertise, and wide industry domain experiences to unlock greater value for Vodafone Business, TCS, and its customers in the UK, to not only improve revenue but enhance customer experience," said Vinay Singvi, Head of UK and Ireland at TCS.

TCS said the partnership builds on its continued investment in innovation, talent, and enterprise transformation in the UK.

Samsung has opened a new HVAC manufacturing facility in Pune, enhancing its production capabilities in India.

The facility will primarily focus on cooling equipment for AI data centres, with a planned annual capacity of up to 6,500 units.

Samsung Electronics announced on August 13 the completion of a new heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) manufacturing facility in Pune, operated by FläktGroup, a subsidiary of Samsung. The facility is intended to strengthen Samsung’s HVAC manufacturing in India and support customers across India and the wider Asia-Pacific region, including AI data centre operators.

“The completion of the production line in Pune marks a significant milestone in expanding our HVAC supply beyond India to the broader Asia-Pacific region,” said Cheolgi Kim, Executive Vice President and Head of Digital Appliance Business at Samsung Electronics. “By combining Samsung’s AI and platform technologies with FläktGroup’s HVAC expertise, we will deliver exceptional value to a diverse range of customers, including AI data centres.”

The Pune facility is the first new FläktGroup manufacturing facility to become operational since Samsung completed its acquisition of the HVAC specialist in November 2025. Samsung said the site is located near Mumbai and has major logistics infrastructure, which will help FläktGroup supply HVAC solutions more quickly to customers in India and across the Asia-Pacific region.

Samsung said the Pune facility will manufacture FläktGroup products including air handling units (AHUs), fan wall units (FWUs) and computer room air handlers (CRAHs) for AI data centres and other critical infrastructure. AHUs use chilled water to cool indoor environments while helping maintain air quality and are widely used in data centres and large commercial buildings.

FWUs use multiple high-capacity fans to remove heat from server environments, while CRAHs provide precision temperature, humidity and air-quality management for mission-critical IT equipment, according to Samsung.

The facility, including its production line, offices and auxiliary facilities, covers approximately 13,826 square meters. Samsung said the facility moved from equipment installation to mass production in six months, while FläktGroup plans to progressively expand production capacity to as many as 6,500 HVAC units annually.

The Pune operation builds on FläktGroup’s existing manufacturing presence in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh. Samsung said the two facilities will strengthen local manufacturing and improve customer responsiveness in India and the wider Asia-Pacific region.

The Pune facility also forms part of FläktGroup’s broader manufacturing expansion in India. The company announced the Pune investment as Project GAGAN in May 2026, describing the site as a base to meet the demand for serving data centres and other critical infrastructure in India and across Asian markets.

Samsung said combining FläktGroup’s HVAC and critical-cooling expertise with Samsung’s AI and technology capabilities, global reach and scale is intended to accelerate the development and delivery of cooling solutions for AI data centres and other high-growth infrastructure sectors.

content:
The Karnataka government’s Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence has launched

Tathyakosh.in, a unified data discovery platform that brings together more than 1.5 million datasets from 458 sources, aiming to make India’s fragmented public data ecosystem easier to search, assess and use.

“Tathyakosh addresses a fundamental gap by making this data discoverable, structured and easier to use. By building it as an open, non-commercial Digital Public Good, we are creating an important piece of infrastructure for researchers, startups, developers and policymakers to build with Indian data,” Karnataka IT-BT Minister Priyank Kharge said.

Tathyakosh currently indexes more than 1.5 million datasets across 16 domains, including healthcare, agriculture, education, infrastructure, environment, economy and governance.

The platform draws data from 346 Indian sources and 37 international repositories containing India-relevant datasets. More than 92% of the catalogued datasets are open access, while 95% are machine-readable.

Instead of requiring users to search individual government portals, research institutions and repositories, Tathyakosh provides a single interface through which they can discover datasets and assess their suitability.

“India has no shortage of data. The challenge is knowing where the data is, whether it is relevant and reliable and whether it can be used. We wanted to make it easier for a researcher, developer, policymaker or startup to discover what already exists before spending time and resources looking for it elsewhere,” said Ashok Kamath, Director, ACSEL Technology Forum.

A key feature of Tathyakosh is its dataset quality assessment. Each dataset receives a score across seven parameters such as findability, accessibility, machine-readability, freshness, completeness, granularity and coverage completeness.

The platform also provides information on factors such as the dataset’s domain, geography, time period, format and access type. Its historical coverage currently extends back to 1947.

“There is a lot of data available, but it is often spread across different platforms and institutions. Tathyakosh gives users a way to find that information without having to search each source separately. Importantly, the platform also helps users assess the quality and fitness of data for their specific needs, making it easier to identify reliable and ready-to-use datasets. That can save considerable time for developers, researchers and data scientists,” said N Manjula, Secretary, Karnataka’s Electronics, IT and BT.

Karnataka has a significant presence on the platform, with more than 50,000 Karnataka-specific datasets already catalogued.

These include datasets from the Karnataka Open Government Data Portal, Mahiti Kanaja, KSRSAC/K-GIS, the Indian Institute of Science and the Raman Research Institute, among others.

The platform could be used by universities and researchers for cross-sector studies, by startups building data-driven applications and technology companies developing AI systems that require structured datasets.

The launch comes as access to reliable and usable data becomes increasingly important for AI development.

Startups and research teams working in areas such as healthcare, agriculture, climate, legal research and financial inclusion often need to identify available datasets before developing applications or training computational systems.

Tathyakosh is intended to address this initial discovery problem by allowing users to assess what data exists, where it comes from and whether it is suitable for their intended use.

The platform does not host or store the underlying datasets. Instead, it indexes information about datasets and directs users to the original source, preserving ownership with the institution that published the data.

This model allows Tathyakosh to function as a discovery layer across India’s public data ecosystem rather than becoming another repository of datasets. The platform is expected to expand as more government departments, research institutions and other organisations make their datasets available, potentially creating a broader discovery infrastructure for India’s growing AI and data economy.

HCLTech and US-based data infrastructure company NetApp have expanded their partnership to offer hybrid cloud storage-as-a-service (STaaS), targeting enterprises looking to scale artificial intelligence and data-intensive workloads.

The offering combines HCLTech’s Utility for Everything (U4X) digital infrastructure framework with NetApp’s Keystone pay-as-you-go storage service. It will allow enterprises to scale storage, performance and data services based on changing workload requirements, the companies said in a statement on August 13.

The offering is designed to support AI and generative AI applications alongside traditional enterprise workloads. HCLTech will also integrate its AI Factory suite into the solution to support AI development, deployment and operations.

The expanded partnership comes as enterprises move from AI experimentation towards larger-scale deployments, increasing demand for infrastructure that can accommodate fluctuating storage and computing requirements.

“By combining flexible infrastructure models with strong data management capabilities, we are enabling clients to unlock the value of their data and accelerate their AI journeys,” said Rampal Singh, Senior Vice President, Hybrid Cloud Business Unit at HCLTech.

The consumption-based model aims to reduce the need for upfront infrastructure spending while allowing customers to scale capacity up or down based on demand.

The companies cited deployments involving a global food and beverage company and a European telecommunications provider as examples of their existing work. The food and beverage company adopted a consumption-based model to improve operational flexibility and reduce upfront investments, while the telecom provider used the approach to improve scalability and resilience across distributed environments.

“We believe strong partnerships are built by co-creating technology offerings, business models, solutions and services that deliver meaningful customer value. This collaboration gives customers access to NetApp’s intelligent data infrastructure through a flexible, accessible business model, backed by HCLTech’s hands-on expertise,” said Alvaro Celis, Chief Partner and Ecosystem Officer at NetApp.

HCLTech reported a 20.3% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to ₹4,626 crore, while revenue rose 13.9% year-on-year to ₹34,579 crore during the quarter ended June 30, 2026. In constant currency, revenue grew 2.6% from a year earlier but declined 0.5% sequentially, reflecting the seasonally weak first quarter.

Google has announced Gemini 3.7 Flash, a new version of its Flash model family with improvements in coding and agentic workflows.

The model arrives just three weeks after Gemini 3.6 Flash, which was released on July 21.

It is also being offered at introductory prices of $0.75 per 1 million input tokens and $3.75 per 1 million output tokens, half the standard rates for Gemini 3.6 Flash—$1.50 and $7.50, respectively.

The introductory pricing is valid through December 31, after which the standard rates apply.

The model is also optimised for speed and, according to Artificial Analysis, is one of the fastest AI models, delivering 340 tokens per second via the first-party API.

Besides, Arena AI, which evaluates AI models on coding tasks using both performance and pricing data, places Gemini 3.7 Flash on the Pareto frontier of Code Arena.

In this context, the frontier represents models that offer a competitive balance between coding performance and cost, with no other model providing both a higher score and a lower price.

Anastasios Angelopoulos, Co-Founder and CEO of Arena AI, said on X, “This makes Google DeepMind the only US lab other than Anthropic that’s on the Pareto frontier of Code Arena.”

The launch comes as the arrival of Google’s next flagship model, Gemini 3.5 Pro, remains delayed. A report from SemiAnalysis said Google had put the model on hold and was instead looking towards Gemini 4.

Google has already confirmed that Gemini 4 is in pre-training.

The launch also comes amid a major shake-up at Google DeepMind. Jeff Dean, Google’s longtime chief scientist and a co-leader of Gemini’s development, left the company after 27 years alongside several senior AI researchers to start a new AI venture.

Demis Hassabis has also stepped down as DeepMind CEO to become chairman and Alphabet’s Chief Scientist, while Koray Kavukcuoglu has taken over day-to-day leadership of the lab.

DeepSeek has released the production version of its V4 Pro model alongside DeepSeek Harness, an open-source agent runtime designed to handle the tools, sessions, sandboxes and execution loops around the model.

The V4 Pro is now available through DeepSeek’s API, web and app, while Harness has been released as a Developer Preview under the MIT licence.

V4 Pro is a 1.6-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 49 billion active parameters, according to DeepSeek’s earlier technical documentation.

DeepSeek first released V4 Pro in April as a preview, alongside V4 Flash.

It retains a 1-million-token context window and is positioned around coding, tool use, and agentic workloads. Independent testing by Artificial Analysis gave the production model an Intelligence Index score of 53, compared with 40 for V4 Flash.

The production release also comes with a major change to DeepSeek’s API pricing. From August 16, the company will introduce peak and off-peak rates for V4 Pro and V4 Flash, with prices varying by model, token type and time of use.

Peak-hour rates for V4 Pro will be more than four times its current output-token price, while the overall increases across the two models range from 50% to 1,100%, according to DeepSeek.

DeepSeek is also moving beyond the model itself with Harness, which provides the execution layer for agentic applications.

The Developer Preview is built around Cordis, a plugin system in which models, tools, sessions, sandboxes, storage, agent loops, and user interfaces can be replaced or extended as plugins.

The system includes four operating modes—Standard, PTC (Programmatic Tool Calling), Minimal, and Creative. Standard provides a broader toolset for general agent tasks, while Minimal restricts the environment primarily to shell and file-editing capabilities for model evaluation.

PTC allows the model to generate code that orchestrates multiple tool calls, while Creative is designed for experimentation with the runtime and Cordis plugins.

Harness also uses an append-only session log as the source of truth for an agent run. The system can reconstruct conversations and execution state from recorded events, allowing runs to be resumed, branched, and replayed. Tool calls, results and other execution events can be inspected through its trajectory interface.

The release puts DeepSeek into the same infrastructure layer as agent frameworks surrounding models from OpenAI and Anthropic.

Rather than treating an agent as only a model with tool access, Harness packages the control loop, context management, state persistence and tool execution into a modifiable runtime.

DeepSeek’s own API documentation had already positioned V4 as compatible with external agent frameworks including Claude Code, OpenClaw, and OpenCode.

Databricks has crossed a $7 billion revenue run-rate after growing more than 80% year-over-year in its second quarter, while closing a $5 billion strategic funding round at a $190 billion valuation.

The round was led by Coatue, with participation from Blackstone, MGX, accounts advised by T. Rowe Price, and new investor Sixth Street Growth. Other new investors include BOND, Clearlake Capital, Point72, Premji Invest and TPG, alongside existing backers.

Databricks said the new capital will support further development of Lakebase, Genie and Unity AI Gateway as enterprises increasingly use AI agents to work with business data and perform tasks.

Lakebase, the company’s serverless Postgres database built for AI agents, has crossed a $100 million revenue run-rate. Databricks said its Lakehouse data warehousing product has also surpassed a $1.5 billion revenue run-rate, growing more than 100% year over year.

The company now has more than 1,000 customers generating over $1 million in annualised revenue each, while more than 100 customers are consuming at over $10 million revenue run-rate.

Databricks also said it has generated positive adjusted free cash flow over the past 12 months.

“Enterprises don't just want AI that talks. They want agents working across their business that remember context, deliver accurate answers, and execute work without blowing through their budgets,” said Ali Ghodsi, Co-Founder and CEO of Databricks.

Ghodsi said Lakebase provides real-time operational data, Genie provides context from across the business, while Unity AI Gateway offers multi-AI cost controls.

The funding comes as Databricks positions its data platform around the growing use of AI agents inside enterprises. Lakebase provides the database layer, Genie turns business data into answers and actions, and Unity AI Gateway provides governance and controls for using multiple AI models.

“Databricks has spent a decade being early to where AI was headed. Now it's the infrastructure the industry builds and scales AI on,” said Thomas Laffont, Co-Founder of Coatue.

Laffont said the company has shortened R&D timelines from years to months and compared its pace of development with that of a research lab.

Databricks’ latest valuation marks a sharp increase over its previous funding rounds, as investors continue to invest in the infrastructure needed to support enterprise AI adoption.

title: OpenAI Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser Steps Down
content:
Dali Rajic, former President and COO of Wiz, will succeed Dresser.

OpenAI Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser will leave the company in the coming weeks to pursue other opportunities. Her departure comes as OpenAI grows its enterprise business and prepares for a potential public listing.

Dresser announced her decision in a LinkedIn post, saying she had made “the difficult decision to leave OpenAI in the coming weeks.” She did not disclose her next role.

“I am so proud of what we have accomplished and, even more, of how this team has shown up for our customers and one another,” Dresser wrote.

Dali Rajic, formerly President and Chief Operating Officer at cloud security company Wiz, will take over as OpenAI’s Chief Revenue Officer.

Rajic previously held revenue and operating roles at Zscaler and AppDynamics, giving him experience in enterprise sales and go-to-market operations.

“Dali will turn what we’ve learned into repeatable execution as we build out the full system to make AI broadly useful for people and businesses,” OpenAI President and Co-founder Greg Brockman said.

Dresser joined OpenAI in December 2025 after serving as CEO of Slack. OpenAI appointed her to oversee its global revenue strategy across enterprise and customer success. Before Slack, she spent more than a decade at Salesforce, where she held senior sales leadership positions.

Her departure comes as enterprise has become a larger part of OpenAI’s business. In April, Dresser said enterprise revenue accounted for more than 40% of OpenAI’s total revenue and was on track to reach parity with consumer revenue by the end of 2026.

OpenAI now says more than 2 million businesses use its products, up from roughly 1 million a year earlier. Dresser had also highlighted demand from companies including Cursor, DoorDash, State Farm, Thermo Fisher, and LY Corporation.

Dresser had taken on a broader role at OpenAI after former COO Brad Lightcap moved away from day-to-day commercial responsibilities.

She picked up responsibility for partnerships and advertising after Lightcap moved to special projects.

Lightcap announced his own departure earlier this week after eight years at OpenAI.

Dresser’s exit is therefore the second senior leadership departure at OpenAI in the same week. It follows a series of executive changes this year, including the departures or transitions of Lightcap, former Applications Chief Fidji Simo and other senior leaders.

In her note to employees, Dresser said she had been working with Brockman on the transition and the future needs of the business.

“I’ve been working with Greg to ensure a smooth transition as we’ve discussed the future needs of the business,” she wrote. “He will share more about those plans shortly.”

Dresser said she would remain at OpenAI for a period to work with employees and customers through the transition.

For Dresser, the move ends an eight-month tenure at OpenAI that included a push to expand enterprise adoption and position the company’s AI products as tools for broader organisational use.

title: Aheesa Digital Innovations Signs MoU With Tamil Nadu Govt for ₹250 Cr Semiconductor Design Centre
content:
Aheesa recently initiated its MPW process for VIHAAN-I, its broadband networking System-on-Chip (SoC) based on the RISC-V architecture

Chennai-headquartered fabless semiconductor company Aheesa Digital Innovations has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Guidance Tamil Nadu, the state’s investment promotion agency, for its proposed semiconductor design, R&D, and product engineering centre in Chennai.

The proposed facility involves an investment of approximately ₹250 crore and is expected to create more than 300 jobs. The centre will focus on developing networking chips, router operating systems and original equipment manufacturer (OEM) platforms, strengthening Aheesa’s semiconductor design and product engineering capabilities.

The proposed Chennai centre will expand Aheesa’s work across semiconductor design, research and development and product engineering. The company plans to build a portfolio of networking silicon targeting broadband, telecommunications, edge computing, and related infrastructure markets.

Aheesa recently initiated its MPW process for VIHAAN-I, its broadband networking System-on-Chip (SoC) based on the RISC-V architecture.

Under the MoU, the Tamil Nadu government will facilitate the proposed project through infrastructure support, single-window clearances and applicable policy incentives, subject to eligibility.

Saket Singh, Director and Chief Growth Officer, Aheesa Digital Innovations, said: "Tamil Nadu has emerged as one of India's most promising hubs for electronics and semiconductor manufacturing, and this MoU reflects the strong alignment between our vision and the state's ambitions for the sector. As we build out our design, R&D, and product engineering capabilities in Chennai, with this proposed investment of Rs 250 crore expected to create around 300 jobs, the facilitation and support extended by the Government of Tamil Nadu will be a valuable enabler."

The proposed centre is expected to expand Aheesa’s capabilities in networking silicon and support its longer-term ambition of developing semiconductor products for broadband, telecom and edge infrastructure. The investment also adds to Tamil Nadu’s growing push to build capabilities across electronics and semiconductor design and manufacturing.

title: Advertise with Us
content:
SpaceXAI has released Grok 4.6, a new version of its AI model that targets long-running agentic tasks, software development and interactive applications.

Grok 4.6 is available through Cursor, Grok Build and xAI’s API, as well as platforms including OpenRouter, Vercel and Cloudflare. Pricing starts at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens. A faster variant is priced at twice those rates.

“Grok 4.6 builds on Grok 4.5 with a particular focus on long-running agents and more ambitious interactive and visual work,” SpaceXAI said in its announcement.

The company said the model can sustain tasks across multiple steps, including researching topics, analysing information, working across codebases and building applications.

On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Grok 4.6 scored 61, matching GPT-5.6 Sol and trailing Fable 5’s score of 62. The index combines results from nine benchmarks.

Grok 4.6 also scored 69.9% on CursorBench v3.2, compared with 67.2% for GPT-5.6 Sol and 70.5% for Fable 5. On DeepSWE v1.1, it scored 65.9%, while GPT-5.6 Sol scored 73% and Fable 5 scored 70%.

The model performed better than Grok 4.5 across the benchmarks published by xAI. Its score on DeepSWE increased to 65.9% from 54%, while its CursorBench score rose from 66.7% to 69.9%.

SpaceXAI said Grok 4.6 underwent a longer supplemental training run than Grok 4.5 using model-generated data covering reasoning and technical concepts, engineering data, and an updated training recipe.

The company also used Grok 4.5 to generate supervised fine-tuning trajectories across different reasoning efforts, agent environments and areas including STEM, software engineering and knowledge work.

Grok 4.6 was then trained with reinforcement learning on tasks covering coding and knowledge work, along with environments for kernel optimisation, web development and computer-aided design.

SpaceXAI said the model is particularly suited to turning broad product ideas into working applications. It can research unfamiliar areas, structure an application, implement interactions and refine the output through multiple rounds of feedback.

“On longer trajectories, we also started to see more self-testing and verification, with the model checking its own work before moving on,” the company added.

The model is also being positioned for visual and interactive development. xAI said Grok 4.6 can establish the structure and visual language of an application in a single pass before iterating on the result.

The release comes as AI companies increasingly position their models as agents capable of completing multi-step software and knowledge-work tasks rather than responding to individual prompts.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk also said that the company is planning to launch Grok 4.7 soon. “Grok 4.7 is significantly better than 4.6 and should be ready in three to four weeks. Initial training is complete, and now we’re adding a massive amount of SpaceX company data in supplemental training. This will be something special,” he wrote in a post on X.

title: What Actually Matters.
content:
L&T has entered the AI Factory business by securing a deal to deploy a 10,000-GPU NVIDIA B300 AI Factory.

The deployment will occur at Vyoma.AI's Chennai data centre, which is designed for gigawatt-scale AI infrastructure.

Marking its entry into the AI Factory business, Larsen & Toubro (L&T) has secured a deployment to build a 10,000-GPU NVIDIA B300 AI Factory for US-based AI cloud company Together AI, the company announced on August 13.

“Artificial Intelligence is becoming foundational to every industry and AI Factories will power this transformation,” said S N Subrahmanyan, Chairman & Managing Director, Larsen & Toubro. “Our deployment of an NVIDIA B300 AI Factory for Together AI marks a significant milestone in L&T's Gigawatt AI Infrastructure Mission and reinforces our commitment to making India a global hub for next-generation AI infrastructure.”

Vyoma.AI, an L&T company, will undertake the deployment through its AI infrastructure subsidiary LTN Compute. The AI Factory will support Together AI's AI Native Cloud platform for large-scale inference, fine-tuning and training workloads.

The infrastructure will be hosted at Vyoma.AI's Chennai data centre campus, which L&T describes as a gigawatt-scale AI infrastructure site. Phase 1 of the campus is designed for 250 MW capacity, with power infrastructure readiness of 150 MVA, providing capacity for future AI Factory expansion, according to the company.

The integrated AI Factory will have capacity for 10,000 NVIDIA B300 GPUs. L&T said the platform combines hyperscale data centre infrastructure, accelerated computing, high-performance networking, ultra-low-latency interconnects, high-throughput parallel storage and AI infrastructure operations.

The combination is designed to allow customers to deploy and scale AI workloads through a unified, end-to-end AI infrastructure stack, according to L&T.

L&T described the deployment as India's largest single-cluster AI infrastructure. The company said the project supports its broader Gigawatt AI Infrastructure Mission to build large-scale AI infrastructure in India.

"Making AI globally accessible is going to be the biggest infrastructure build-out in human history, and L&T understands that. That's exactly why we partnered with them, to bring the scale, resilience and engineering excellence this moment demands to India," said Vipul Ved Prakash, Co-founder and CEO of Together AI.

LTN Compute, operating under Vyoma.AI, is building AI-ready digital infrastructure across India through hyperscale AI data centres, sovereign cloud platforms, AI Factory services, GPU-as-a-Service (GPUaaS), and managed AI platforms. The company said these offerings are intended to support governments, enterprises, cloud providers, and AI innovators.

L&T said the Chennai campus's power infrastructure readiness leaves room for additional AI Factory capacity as demand for AI computing grows in India.
