title: AI is Reshaping Enterprise IT & Commercial Models, Says Wipro at 80th AGM
content:
The company stated that enterprise clients have moved beyond AI experimentation and are increasingly deploying the technology across core operations, while commercial models evolve towards outcome-based engagements.

Enterprise AI adoption has entered the execution phase, with clients embedding the technology into core business processes and increasingly moving away from effort-based IT contracts, Wipro's top executives said at the company’s 80th annual general meeting.

“The focus is shifting from experimentation to execution,” Chairman Rishad Premji told shareholders, adding that AI was already altering the nature of work across both operations and technology functions.

In operations, he said, employees were moving away from routine transaction processing towards exception handling, compliance and decision support. In technology, he said AI was changing the economics and speed of software engineering and modernisation, opening up new pools of growth for the industry.

CEO and Managing Director Srini Pallia went further on the commercial implications, saying the AI shift was pushing clients and vendors alike away from effort-based pricing towards consumption-linked, transaction-based and outcome-based contracts.

“Success in AI is not driven solely by models,” Pallia said, noting that real transformation required integrating domain expertise, data, cloud, security and organisational change management together.”

However, Premji cautioned that turning AI into business outcomes was “easier said than done”, because enterprises carry technology estates and operating models built up over decades within regulatory and operational constraints. For most clients, he said, this would not be a single project but a multi-year transformation journey.

On the financial front, Wipro’s IT services revenue for FY26 came in at $10.5 billion, down 1.6% year-on-year in constant currency terms, as clients stayed cautious on spending through the year even while shifting conversations towards AI and modernisation.

Operating margins for the segment, however, grew 0.2% year-on-year to 17.2% in FY26. In April, Wipro’s board approved a ₹150 billion share buyback, the company’s largest ever, even as it continued investing in AI capabilities, platforms and talent.

Pallia said Wipro has had a dedicated AI-native business and platforms unit since the last quarter, tasked with scaling enterprise-grade agentic AI and building industry-specific platforms.

The unit will also develop domain-specific small language models meant to lower operating costs for clients, support sovereign AI requirements, and serve as an efficient foundation for deploying specialised agents at scale, he said.

Wipro has committed $500 million to Wipro Ventures to back frontier startups working on AI, data and security, enabling the company to co-innovate with emerging technology providers, Pallia added.

Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar announced plans to establish a government-backed AI university, an AI innovation hub, and a next-generation green data centre at Google I/O Connect 2026 in Bengaluru.

Addressing developers, researchers, policymakers and industry leaders, Shivakumar said Karnataka wants to become “one of the world’s leading centres of responsible artificial intelligence”.

“We want to build one of the world’s leading centres of responsible artificial intelligence,” he said.

The chief minister said Karnataka already contributes nearly 40% of India’s software exports and is home to more than 17,000 startups, adding that thousands of global capability centres have chosen the state to build products and engineering talent for the world.

“Our first ambition is to make Karnataka an AI-native state,” Shivakumar said. “By AI-native, I do not mean using AI as a slogan.”

He said the state government plans to establish “the first and the largest university by the government” focused on AI while creating a world-class ecosystem for research and talent development.

Karnataka also plans to build an AI innovation hub that will bring together startups, researchers, academia and industry, while introducing AI education from the school level.

Shivakumar also said the state is working on a next-generation green data centre in Karnataka’s coastal region alongside infrastructure development around Bengaluru.

Shivakumar said Google had chosen Bengaluru not merely as an office location but as one of its most important global centres for engineering, research and innovation.

He said millions of Indians first experienced the internet through Google’s products, including Search, Android, YouTube, Maps, Chrome and Google Pay, arguing that these services have become part of everyday life.

Citing figures shared with him, Shivakumar said Google employs more than 18,000 people in India, with around 12,000 based in Bengaluru.

“I was told that Google employs more than 18,000 people in India and in Bangalore, it is 12,000,” he said.

The CM invited Google to deepen its partnership with Karnataka, saying the government was prepared to support the company as it expanded its AI efforts.

“I am ready to give you any support you want,” Shivakumar said. “Let us build AI for education. Let us build AI for healthcare, agriculture, climate resilience and urban mobility.”

Acknowledging Bengaluru’s infrastructure challenges as the city’s population has grown rapidly, he said the government would work with industry to address them.

Google unveiled a series of AI initiatives for India at Google I/O Connect India, including on-premises access to its Gemini models, new AI education programmes, cybersecurity tools, and support for 25 Indian languages in Gemini Live, as it seeks to expand enterprise and public sector adoption of AI.

The company also said the Google Play and Android ecosystem generated ₹5.3 lakh crore ($60 billion) in revenue for app publishers and the wider digital economy in India in 2025, up 28% from the previous year, based on third-party research.

A key announcement was the availability of Gemini on Google Distributed Cloud, allowing enterprises and government organisations to deploy Google’s frontier AI models entirely within Indian data centres. Google said the offering is intended for regulated sectors that require data localisation and disconnected environments.

Google also said Gemini 3.5 Flash will now be available to Indian enterprises and startups with in-country machine learning processing commitments through its Gemini Enterprise platform.

“As we drive the shift into the agentic era, where AI moves from answering queries to securely executing tasks, our focus is on providing the underlying infrastructure and guardrails the ecosystem needs to scale safely,” said Preeti Lobana, Country Manager, Google India.

“Today, we are delivering just that across the board, from flexible on-premise cloud environments for highly regulated sectors, to open security protocols for developers, to localised tools for healthcare and classrooms.”

The company also expanded its AI education efforts.

Google DeepMind is bringing its AI Research Foundations curriculum, a free 56-hour programme on building and fine-tuning large language models, to India. The programme will be available through Google’s Skills platform and will be rolled out with NASSCOM, IISc Bengaluru, and AVPN.

Google DeepMind also introduced ATL Saathi, a Gemini-powered assistant for teachers in the Atal Tinkering Labs network. The web application will initially be deployed in 100 schools this year, with plans to eventually reach 10,000 schools.

In healthcare, researchers at AIIMS Delhi are using Google’s MedGemma open models to develop India-specific AI models for leprosy and sexual and reproductive health. Google said the resulting models will be made available to Indian developers.

The company also expanded Gemini Live to support more than 25 Indian languages and dialects, including Sanskrit, Bhojpuri and Maithili.

On the security front, Google announced that Sec-Gemini V3, its cybersecurity AI agent, will be made available to trusted government and enterprise testers, including Flipkart. The tool is designed to help security teams analyse incidents using AI.

Google is also open-sourcing Capabilities Security for Agents (CAPSEM), a runtime environment that isolates AI agents inside virtual machines to reduce the impact of compromised agents or malicious prompts.

The company introduced additional security standards for the agentic AI ecosystem, including Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) to prevent session cookie theft, and an Agents-to-Payments framework for low-value AI-led financial transactions, and the open Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol.

Google said it has partnered with IIT Delhi and IIT Madras on research into agentic AI safety, including early threat detection and AI systems designed to mitigate institutional risks.

The company also announced that it will bring its Google Play Academy curriculum to 10,000 developers in partnership with the governments of Rajasthan, Odisha, and Madhya Pradesh. The programme will focus on helping developers build and scale AI-powered applications.

Around 1,500 developers attended Google I/O Connect India 2026, where startups including Adya.AI, VideoSDK, Sivi, Superjoin, Knit, PolicyBazaar, Emergent, and RedBus showcased AI applications built using Google’s models.

Richard Sutton, widely considered the father of modern reinforcement learning, has launched a new AI startup, Oak Lab, alongside researcher Khurram Javed.

Sutton and Javed announced the same in a post on X. The latter revealed that Oak Lab has developed a “fairly complete roadmap” centred on its OaK architecture, which aims to create “animal-like intelligence that learns purely from its own experience”.

The company plans to build a prototype over the next few years that it says would resemble “a baby learning in its first year” more closely than today’s AI systems.

Rather than immediately pursuing large-scale foundation models, Oak Lab said its research strategy will first demonstrate the limitations of current AI methods in simple environments, then develop domain-independent algorithms to address those shortcomings.

The company said it will only build larger systems after making sufficient progress on core learning algorithms.

The startup’s broader research agenda focuses on continual learning, reinforcement learning and AI agents that adapt in real time without relying on static datasets or replaying stored experiences.

According to Oak Lab, its long-term goal is to develop AI systems that can continuously learn and plan while operating efficiently in dynamic environments.

Sutton and Javed previously worked together at Keen Technologies, John Carmack’s AI research company, where they were part of a small team exploring reinforcement learning, robotics and real-time decision-making systems.

Javed joined Keen as a research scientist in October 2024 after completing his PhD at the University of Alberta under Sutton’s supervision.

Sutton, who won the Turing Award for reinforcement learning in 2024, has been an outspoken critic of scaling current deep learning techniques.

In recent months, he has argued that generative AI models excel at imitation but lack the ability to autonomously evaluate their own outputs and discover new knowledge, positioning continual learning as a more promising foundation for future AI.

Elevation Capital has launched Fund IX at $500 million, focusing on seed and Series A investments in AI and deeptech.

The fund aims to support India's emerging technology giants, particularly in AI-native application development.

Venture capital firm Elevation Capital has closed its ninth India-focused fund at $500 million, reinforcing its conviction that the country's next generation of technology giants will emerge from AI and deeptech, even as the broader venture funding environment remains selective.

The new vehicle, Fund IX, will focus exclusively on seed and Series A investments, marking a return to Elevation's early-stage roots. Unlike its previous $670 million Fund VIII, which invested across multiple stages, the new fund will work alongside Elevation Holdings, the firm's recently launched $400 million late-stage vehicle. Together, the two funds give Elevation $900 million in deployable capital across the startup lifecycle.

"We are following a barbell approach," Co-Managing Partner Mukul Arora told Moneycontrol. "Elevation Capital IX will remain sharply focused on seed and Series A opportunities, while Elevation Holdings will partner with category leaders well beyond their IPO. Across the two funds, we will be investing from a combined pool of $900 million."

According to the firm, AI represents a fundamental platform shift rather than a passing technology cycle. Global capital has largely flowed into foundation model developers. Elevation believes India's opportunity lies in building AI-native application companies that solve complex problems across healthcare, education, and financial services, as well as globally competitive software products.

The firm also sees opportunities in deeptech sectors, including robotics, defence, space, energy, and precision manufacturing.

"AI isn't just another technology wave. It is a new computing paradigm," the firm said in a blog announcing Fund IX, adding that India now has the ingredients to build globally significant AI companies through its engineering talent, digital public infrastructure, and growing founder ecosystem.

The fundraising comes amid a mixed venture capital market. While late-stage investments and IPO timelines have been affected by macroeconomic uncertainty and cautious public markets, early-stage funding has remained relatively resilient, particularly for AI-native startups. Elevation said it intends to write larger initial cheques and double down on breakout companies over time.

Elevation Capital has backed several of India's best-known startups, including Swiggy, Paytm, Meesho, Urban Company, FirstCry, NoBroker, and Unacademy.

content:
Anthropic has introduced India-specific pricing for its Claude AI subscriptions, allowing payments in Indian Rupees.

Claude Pro is priced at ₹1,999 per month, with Claude Max tiers at ₹11,999 and ₹23,999.

Anthropic has rolled out India-specific pricing for its Claude AI subscriptions, allowing users to pay in Indian Rupees instead of US dollars, as the San Francisco-based AI startup deepens its presence in what has become its second-largest market after the US.

The new pricing is being introduced across Claude’s web platform and mobile apps in phases. Under the revised plans, Claude Pro is priced at ₹1,999 per month, while Claude Max is available at ₹11,999 per month for the 5x usage tier and ₹23,999 per month for the 20x tier.

Claude Team, aimed at businesses, starts at ₹2,399 per seat per month with a minimum of five users. Previously, Indian customers had to subscribe using international payment methods and were billed in US dollars.

The move simplifies payments for Indian users and reflects the country’s growing importance to Anthropic. According to the company’s India Economic Index released earlier this year, India accounts for 5.8% of global Claude.ai consumer usage, making it Anthropic’s largest market outside the US.

The localisation comes as competition intensifies among AI chatbot providers seeking to expand in India, one of the world’s fastest-growing AI markets. OpenAI offers ChatGPT Plus at around ₹1,999 per month, while Google’s Gemini Advanced is bundled with Google AI Pro at ₹1,950 per month. Elon Musk’s xAI recently introduced local pricing for Grok in India as well, making pricing a key competitive lever alongside model capabilities.

Anthropic has also extended its promotional offer for Claude Fable 5 until July 19, allowing eligible paid subscribers to use the model without additional charges within their existing usage limits.

The pricing announcement follows a series of India-focused initiatives by Anthropic, including the launch of Claude for Small Business and the expansion of its enterprise offerings. By removing foreign-currency payments and aligning subscription costs with the local market, the company aims to lower barriers to adoption among developers, startups, students, and enterprises as demand for generative AI tools continues to accelerate in India.

title: Demis Hassabis Says AGI Could Arrive Within ‘A Few Short Years’, Calls for US Frontier AI Standards Body
content:
Hassabis argues that the pace of AI development is exceeding the current understanding of the technology.

Artificial general intelligence (AGI) is likely only “a few short years away”, according to Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis, who has called for the creation of a US-led Frontier AI Standards Body to assess the risks posed by the most advanced AI models before they are deployed.

In a blog post titled A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age, Hassabis said humanity is approaching a turning point in AI development.

“This is a pivotal moment in human history. Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), a system that exhibits all the cognitive capabilities the brain has, is probably only a few short years away,” he wrote. “When we look back on this time in the decades to come, I think we will realise we were standing in the foothills of the singularity.”

Hassabis compared AGI to the discovery of electricity and fire rather than previous computing advances. “AGI cannot be compared to standard technological breakthroughs, not even ones as consequential as the internet or mobile,” he wrote. “It is much more akin to the discovery of electricity or fire.”

He said AI could accelerate scientific research in areas including drug discovery, clean energy and advanced materials. “The magnitude of this technology's impact will be unprecedented, perhaps 10x of the Industrial Revolution at 10x the speed,” he wrote.

Alongside the opportunities, Hassabis warned that frontier AI models could introduce new security risks. He said cybersecurity challenges are already emerging and that “nuclear and bio risks may soon emerge as capabilities continue to advance”. He also said future AI systems may require safeguards to maintain control over "increasingly agentic, recursively self-improving systems".

Hassabis argued that the pace of AI development is exceeding current understanding of the technology.

“At the moment, we are locked in an extremely intense, multilayered commercial and geopolitical race,” he wrote. “Advances on the frontier are outpacing our understanding of the technology.”

He added that “nobody in the world knows for sure what is going to happen from here”, calling for "public policy that promotes innovation while also incentivising responsibility and security".

To address these concerns, Hassabis proposed establishing a Frontier AI Standards Body in the US, modelled on a federally overseen public-private partnership or self-regulatory organisation similar to the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA).

Under the proposal, the body would develop benchmarks to determine whether an AI system qualifies as a “Frontier-class” model and would work with US federal agencies and national laboratories to conduct security evaluations.

Initially, AI companies would voluntarily submit their frontier models for review up to 30 days before release. Hassabis said that once the evaluation framework is proven effective, passing these assessments could become a requirement for deploying frontier AI models in the US.

He said the evaluations should test models for cybersecurity, biological threats and other high-risk capabilities. They should also assess whether agentic systems attempt to bypass safety guardrails or exhibit deceptive behaviour. Hassabis further suggested practices such as digitally watermarking AI-generated images and generating human-readable output tokens to help researchers understand model reasoning.

The proposed framework would apply to frontier AI models regardless of whether they are open or closed source or where they are developed, while exempting non-frontier models from startups and academic institutions.

Hassabis said a US-led framework could become the basis for international AI standards.

“Since this technology is going to affect the entire planet, ideally this framework would spur the international community to reach a consensus on how to manage the most serious risks while ensuring everyone has access to and can benefit from the opportunities that AI brings,” he wrote.

He concluded that the period before AGI arrives is critical for shaping its development.

“The future is not yet written,” Hassabis wrote. “We must use this precious window before AGI arrives to shape this technology for the benefit of all humanity.”

TVH has expanded its Pune Global Capability Centre by adding 150 seats, increasing capacity to 400 employees.

The expansion aims to enhance technology, engineering, and digital operations while facilitating collaboration with global teams.

Belgium-headquartered TVH has expanded its Global Capability Centre (GCC) in Pune by adding a new office floor at Phoenix Fountainhead, increasing the facility’s seating capacity from 250 to 400. The company announced the expansion, saying the additional 150 seats will support its next phase of growth across technology, engineering, digital products, data and enterprise functions.

The expanded centre will help it scale business-critical capabilities from India while strengthening collaboration with teams across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific. The Pune GCC supports technology, engineering, digital transformation and enterprise operations for TVH’s global business.

Vishal Rajani, Managing Director of TVH India, said the expansion reflects the company’s continued investment in India as a strategic hub.

“India continues to play a strategic role in TVH’s global operations, with our Pune Global Capability Centre supporting critical capabilities across technology, data, engineering and digital transformation,” Rajani said. “This expansion reflects our long-term commitment to strengthening these capabilities by investing in the right infrastructure, talent and collaborative environment.”

According to the company, the added capacity will allow the Pune centre to accelerate work across engineering, digital products, data, enterprise technology and business support functions.

The new office includes an innovation space designed for workshops, technical discussions and knowledge-sharing activities. It also features collaboration areas, recreation spaces and a medical room.

TVH said the Pune GCC remains one of its key global capability hubs. Founded in 1969, TVH supplies parts and accessories for material-handling, industrial, construction and agricultural equipment. The company serves customers in more than 180 countries through a network of over 90 branches worldwide.

TCS has signed a multi-million-dollar, multi-year agreement with ABB to modernise the industrial technology company's global network operations using AI, expanding a partnership that spans more than two decades.

Under ABB's Future Network Model programme, TCS will design, integrate and operate the company's global network as an AI-driven, secure and standardised digital infrastructure. The Indian IT services giant will deliver the engagement through a network-as-a-service model, marking an expansion of its role from managing infrastructure and applications to running end-to-end global network operations.

The deal includes the establishment of a global network operations centre, service integration and management (SIAM), advanced cybersecurity capabilities, and the modernisation of ABB’s LAN, WAN and software-defined WAN infrastructure. TCS will also provide end-to-end monitoring and orchestration across ABB's multi-vendor network ecosystem.

"The Future Network Model represents an important milestone in reinforcing the digital foundation of ABB's global operations," said Alec Joannou, Group CIO at ABB. He added that the initiative aims to build a resilient and secure network ecosystem aligned with the company's long-term transformation goals.

Anupam Singhal, President and Head of Manufacturing at TCS, said the company would embed AI into ABB's network operations to create systems that can "sense, adapt, and improve continuously" while improving reliability, security, user experience and scalability.

The latest engagement builds on more than 20 years of collaboration between the two companies, during which TCS has supported ABB's ERP consolidation, SAP transformation and cloud modernisation programmes.

Shares of TCS rose around 5% on Monday following the announcement, extending gains seen after the company's June-quarter earnings last week. The company reported a 13.9% year-on-year rise in June-quarter revenue to ₹72,275 crore, its fourth straight quarter of sequential growth, alongside $9.5 billion in fresh order bookings.

TCS also said that its annualised revenue from AI-led engagements crossed $2.6 billion, up 13.6% sequentially.

LTM, formerly LTIMindtree, has deepened its partnership with Anthropic by integrating the Claude family of AI models into its BlueVerse AI platform and launching a large-scale programme to train thousands of Claude-certified engineers.

The partnership will see Claude, Claude Code and Claude Cowork embedded into LTM's AI Delivery Fabric for software engineering, application modernisation, agent orchestration, site reliability engineering (SRE), observability and chaos engineering, the company said in a statement on July 13.

LTM will also expand its AI1000 initiative to train and deploy thousands of Claude-certified architects and Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), who will work with enterprise clients on AI assessments, implementation and continuous optimisation.

“LTM helps clients accelerate AI adoption and translate AI investments into measurable business outcomes through our partnership with Anthropic. Combining Claude with LTM’s BlueVerse ecosystem, deep domain expertise, technology capabilities, and AI1000 talent initiative creates a powerful foundation for enterprises to embed AI across their business and modernise at scale,” Venu Lambu, CEO and Managing Director of LTM said in a statement.

The company will additionally establish a dedicated Claude Centre of Excellence to develop reusable AI capabilities, reference architectures and governance frameworks around responsible AI, model governance and data privacy.

The announcement comes as Indian IT services companies move beyond simply offering access to large language models and instead position themselves as implementation partners capable of embedding AI into enterprise workflows.

As clients shift from experimentation to production deployments, service providers are investing heavily in specialised engineering talent, industry-specific AI assets and governance capabilities.

The latest partnership also reflects Anthropic's growing enterprise push in India, where the company has increasingly relied on systems integrators to scale adoption of Claude among large enterprises. Other AI developers such as OpenAI, and Mistral have similarly expanded partnerships with global and Indian IT companies to reach enterprise customers.

"LTM brings delivery expertise, trained people, and long-standing client relationships across industries, and their customers want to embed Claude into the systems they rely on. LTM is embedding Claude and Claude Code in BlueVerse, bringing trusted frontier AI technology to the center of how they do what they do best - help their clients build, modernise, and run their software," Chris Ciauri, Managing Director of International, Anthropic, said in a statement.

The contours of the deal, including the size of the stake, valuation and transaction structure, are still being finalised, the report said.

If the transaction materialises, it would add to a growing wave of consolidation in the IT services sector, as companies pursue acquisitions to build scale and strengthen capabilities in areas such as artificial intelligence amid slower discretionary technology spending by enterprise customers.

For the financial year ended March 2026, Happiest Minds reported revenue of ₹2,315 crore, up 12.3% year-on-year. Digital Infrastructure and Cloud accounted for 53.2% of revenue, followed by Software-as-a-Service at 21% and AI & Analytics at 11.1%, indicating the company's strength in high-growth digital services.

Founded in 2011 by Ashok Soota, Happiest Minds focuses on digital transformation, cloud, artificial intelligence and cybersecurity services.

HCLTech said it will invest up to ₹3,500 crore to build an AI data centre business, marking its biggest push yet into AI infrastructure as the company looks to move beyond traditional IT services and capture a larger share of enterprise spending on artificial intelligence.

The initial investment will create AI-ready data centre capacity that can eventually scale to 50 megawatts, chief executive C Vijayakumar said in a press briefing on Monday. He added that the company is already in advanced discussions with customers and is close to signing its first client with committed capacity.

"We are starting with an initial investment of ₹3,500 crore, but our bigger vision is to grow it to a 50-megawatt capacity," Vijayakumar said during the company's June-quarter earnings briefing.

Unlike conventional data centre operators that primarily sell computing capacity, HCLTech said it plans to build a full-stack AI platform spanning AI data centres, GPU infrastructure, foundation models, enterprise applications and managed services.

"For infrastructure companies, megawatts become the product. For us, megawatts are just the anchor," Vijayakumar said. “Our whole value is in delivering full-stack AI services. Which means it's the data centre, GPUs, models, the applications we will deliver on top of it.”

The move reflects a broader shift in enterprise AI spending, where technology vendors are increasingly seeking greater control over AI infrastructure as inference costs and GPU availability become critical to delivering AI-powered services.

Vijayakumar said global data centre demand is expected to nearly triple by 2030 because of AI adoption, while growth in India is likely to outpace global markets as governments and enterprises increasingly require AI workloads to remain within national borders.

"Sovereign data requirements are increasingly mandating that workloads for governments, enterprises and even global consumer platforms be delivered in-country," he said.

Owning AI infrastructure will also help HCLTech reduce token consumption, one of the largest emerging cost components in AI services.

The announcement came alongside HCLTech's Q1 FY27 earnings, where the company reported a 20.3% year-on-year increase in net profit to ₹4,626 crore. The revenue for the quarter rose 13.9% to ₹34,579 crore. The company retained its FY27 revenue growth guidance of 1-4% in constant currency.

content:
Dhruva Space is the first recipient of investment from the Antariksh Venture Capital Fund.

The startup secured ₹60 crore to support its growth in the space technology sector.

Hyderabad-based space tech startup Dhruva Space has become the first company to receive funding from the Antariksh Venture Capital Fund (AVCF), securing a ₹60 crore investment from the government-backed space technology fund.

The announcement was made at the 10th IN-SPACe Industry Connect event in Ahmedabad. The fund, anchored by IN-SPACe and managed by SIDBI Venture Capital Limited, was initially approved in 2024. Post which, due to regulatory processes and the early-stage nature of India’s spacetech ecosystem, the fund was postponed to begin investing in early FY 2027.

Chaitanya Dora Surapureddy, Co-founder of Dhruva Space, said the investment validates the company’s long-term strategy.

“As demand for space-based solutions continues to grow globally, this capital will enable us to accelerate infrastructure development, scale manufacturing, and execute on our growing order book,” he said.

This investment now marks the first deployment of capital from the ₹1,600 crore AVCF, which was set up to provide institutional funding to space technology startups across different stages of growth.

Dhruva said it currently has an order book exceeding ₹500 crore across satellite platforms, space infrastructure, mission services and national programmes. The new capital will support the next phase of growth, including the expansion of satellite manufacturing and the development of critical technologies, infrastructure and customer programme execution.

With the latest investment, Dhruva Space’s ongoing pre-Series B round has reached ₹275 crore, including ₹150 crore in equity and ₹125 crore in debt financing.

Arup Kumar, Managing Director and CEO of SIDBI Venture Capital Limited, said the investment reflects confidence in companies that can combine innovation, manufacturing and commercial deployment.

“Our first investment reflects a strong belief that the next generation of space leaders will be built by companies that can integrate innovation, manufacturing, mission execution, and commercial deployment under one roof,” Kumar said. “Dhruva Space has established itself as a full-stack space company with the vision, technology, and execution capabilities to compete on the global stage.”

The investment comes as India seeks to expand private participation in the space sector and increase the flow of institutional capital into domestic space technology companies. According to the company, the funding signals growing confidence in the commercial potential of India’s private space ecosystem.

title: HCLTech's AI Revenue Surges 62% to $171 Mn as Automation Reshapes IT Services
content:
The IT company reported a 20% rise in June-quarter profit, with AI revenues climbing to an annualised run rate of $688 million.

What Actually Matters.

HCLTech's AI revenue increased by over 62% year-on-year, reaching $171 million in Q1 FY27.

The company's AI annualised run rate has reached $688 million, reflecting its focus on AI-driven services.

HCLTech's bet on artificial intelligence is beginning to show up in its revenue mix. The company reported a 62.1% year-on-year jump in its Advanced AI business in Q1 FY27, even as traditional IT services continued to face pricing pressure from AI-driven automation.

The Noida-based IT services company said its Advanced AI revenue reached $171 million during the first quarter of the current fiscal year, up 10.6% sequentially in constant currency, taking the annualised run rate to $688 million.

"Our intent is to benefit disproportionately from AI-native and AI-amplified opportunities, which together represent the fastest-growing pool of enterprise spending," chief executive C Vijayakumar said in a press conference after announcing the company's results.

He said HCLTech's strategy is to grow faster in emerging AI services while innovating rapidly enough in traditional IT outsourcing to stay ahead of the deflationary curve created by AI-driven productivity gains.

"In AI-disrupted services, we intend to innovate faster than the market to stay ahead of the deflationary curve rather than be defined by it," Vijayakumar said.

His comments come at a time when India's IT services industry is facing challenges as AI-led productivity improvements reduce effort, compress contract values, and reshape traditional outsourcing economics.

HCLTech reported a 20.3% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to ₹4,626 crore, while revenue rose 13.9% year-on-year to ₹34,579 crore during the quarter ended June 30. In constant currency, revenue grew 2.6% from a year earlier but declined 0.5% sequentially, reflecting the seasonally weak first quarter.

Vijayakumar said the June quarter is typically softer because of planned productivity commitments in several large managed services contracts, but described the overall performance as resilient.

The company also posted its highest-ever first-quarter net new bookings of $2.4 billion. The deal pipeline, Vijayakumar said, remains healthy for the company and noted that it increasingly reflects a split between AI-native work, AI-enabled transformation programmes and conventional services that are being automated.

He said AI-native and AI-enabled services continued to grow while traditional commoditised work was increasingly being automated.

As part of its AI strategy, HCLTech recently completed the acquisition of Jaspersoft, adding data visualisation capabilities to its software portfolio and strengthening its enterprise data stack.

The company also highlighted its $151-million strategic investment in Sarvam AI, saying the partnership would help it build sovereign AI capabilities spanning foundation models, enterprise platforms and managed services tailored for India.

The company also announced plans to enter the AI infrastructure business by investing up to ₹3,500 crore in AI-ready data centres, betting that sovereign AI requirements and rising GPU demand will create a new growth engine beyond traditional IT services.

"We believe AI-ready data centres and full-stack AI infrastructure will become a new growth vector for HCLTech," Vijayakumar said.

Despite continued macro uncertainty, HCLTech retained its FY27 guidance of 1-4% constant currency revenue growth.

title: Advertise with Us
content:
Meta has withdrawn its newly launched AI image feature, Muse Image, just days after its debut following widespread criticism over privacy and consent.

Meta acknowledged that the feature had failed to meet user expectations.

“Our intent was to provide a useful creative tool and to give people control over whether their public content could be referenced in this way. We've heard the feedback that this feature missed the mark, so it’s no longer available,” the company said in a blog post.

The feature allowed users to generate and edit AI images using photos from public Instagram accounts simply by tagging a user's Instagram handle in a prompt, without notifying the account owner.

Muse Image, introduced earlier this week by Meta Superintelligence Labs, was positioned as an image generation tool competing with offerings from OpenAI and Google. Besides creating images from text prompts and sketches, it could incorporate photos from public Instagram profiles into AI-generated visuals.

Public accounts were automatically enrolled in the feature by default, while private accounts and users under 18 were excluded. Users who wanted to opt out had to manually disable the setting in Instagram's ‘Sharing and reuse’ menu or make their accounts private.

The rollout quickly sparked backlash from privacy advocates, creators and entertainment industry groups, who argued that people should not have to opt out of AI systems that use their likeness. Critics also warned that the tool could be misused for impersonation, harassment, non-consensual image editing and deepfakes.

Actor Hannah Einbinder publicly criticised the feature, while SAG-AFTRA urged members to disable the setting and called for AI systems using people's likenesses to require explicit consent.

“With the dangers of nonconsensual digital replicas well known to all, a feature that encouraged that behavior is unwise. We appreciate its discontinuance. It is the responsible thing to do,” wrote SAG-AFTRA in a post on X.

The controversy centred on Meta’s opt-out approach. Users whose accounts remained public could have their posts and reels used in AI-generated images without receiving any notification. Even after opting out, AI-generated images that had already been created using their content would not be removed.

title: Apple Sues OpenAI Over Alleged Theft of Trade Secrets
content:
The complaint names former Apple executives Tang Tan and Chang Liu and seeks damages along with the return of allegedly misappropriated confidential information.

Apple has sued OpenAI and two former employees, accusing the ChatGPT maker of orchestrating a campaign to obtain the iPhone maker’s confidential information to accelerate its AI hardware ambitions.

Following its acquisition of Jony Ive’s io startup, OpenAI has been building a dedicated hardware division staffed by several former Apple executives and engineers to develop AI-native consumer devices beyond smartphones.

“Apple has uncovered a pattern of theft of Apple’s trade secrets by OpenAI employees who were formerly at Apple,” the company said in its filing.

The lawsuit was filed on Friday in the US District Court for the Northern District of California. It names OpenAI and former Apple executives Tang Tan and Chang Liu, alleging that Apple’s trade secrets were misappropriated to benefit OpenAI’s consumer hardware efforts.

OpenAI denied Apple’s allegations. “We have no interest in other companies' trade secrets. We remain focused on building innovative technology that empowers people everywhere,” the company said in a statement.

According to the complaint, Tan, who spent nearly 24 years at Apple before becoming OpenAI’s Chief Hardware Officer, allegedly encouraged Apple employees and job candidates to disclose confidential information, including supplier relationships, unreleased hardware details and physical components during recruitment conversations.

“He has directed job candidates still working for Apple to bring ‘Actual parts' from Apple to their interviews for ‘show and tell’ sessions in which he and his team at OpenAI can elicit still more Apple confidential information,” the company wrote in the filing.

Apple also alleges that Liu exploited a software bug that allowed him continued access to Apple’s internal systems after leaving the company, downloading confidential documents and retaining company property.

“After leaving Apple, Mr Liu failed to return an Apple-issued work laptop that he had previously authenticated to Apple’s network,” Apple wrote in its complaint.

Apple claims OpenAI ignored concerns it raised earlier this year and that the alleged conduct went beyond isolated incidents “This case is about OpenAI’s systematic campaign to obtain Apple’s trade secrets,” it said.

The company further alleged that what it had uncovered was “only the tip of the iceberg,” accusing OpenAI of fostering “institutional misconduct” around confidential information.

The lawsuit seeks unspecified monetary damages and a court order preventing OpenAI and the former employees from using or disclosing Apple’s confidential information. Apple is also asking the court to require the return or destruction of any trade secrets allegedly taken from the company.

The legal battle marks a dramatic deterioration in the relationship between the two companies. Apple and OpenAI announced a high-profile partnership in 2024 that integrated ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence across iPhone, iPad and Mac devices.

The case adds to a growing list of legal challenges facing OpenAI. The company is also facing several ongoing copyright lawsuits from authors, publishers and media organisations, including The New York Times, which alleges that OpenAI and Microsoft used millions of its copyrighted articles without permission to train AI models.

OpenAI also recently prevailed in a high-profile lawsuit brought by co-founder Elon Musk, who accused the company of abandoning its original nonprofit mission in favour of commercial interests. Musk sought $150 billion in damages but has said he plans to appeal the ruling.

title: MiniMax CEO Gives Up Salary Until AGI as Company Announces $2 Bn Funding
content:
He also committed to transferring shares equivalent to 4% of the company’s total equity from his personal holdings over the next four years to reward long-term employees.

MiniMax, the Chinese AI lab, is seeking to raise approximately HK$16.04 billion ($2.05 billion) through a combination of a Hong Kong share placement and zero-coupon convertible bonds.

This marks one of the largest AI capital raises by a publicly listed Chinese model developer this year.

The proceeds will be used to expand AI infrastructure, fund research and development, accelerate commercialisation, and support general corporate operations, according to the company.

The financing consists of 35.6 million new Class A shares priced at HK$268 per share, raising about HK$9.54 billion, alongside HK$6.5 billion in zero-coupon convertible bonds maturing in 2027.

The bonds carry a conversion price of HK$335, a premium to the placement price. The announcement sent MiniMax shares down about 12% as investors reacted to the expected dilution

Alongside the fundraising announcement, MiniMax employees shared a letter from Founder and CEO Yan Junjie, who said he would forgo his salary until the company achieves artificial general intelligence (AGI).

“Starting today, and until the day we reach AGI, I will no longer receive any compensation from the company,” he wrote in the internal note, translated and shared publicly by MiniMax employees.

An additional 1% of his holdings will be allocated to establish a fund supporting open-source communities and the broader AI ecosystem.

“I will devote all my time, energy, and resources to this mission,” he wrote, describing the move as his long-term commitment to the company, its employees and its pursuit of AGI.

The fundraising follows MiniMax’s Hong Kong IPO in January, in which the company raised roughly HK$4.8 billion (about $614 million) at a valuation of approximately $6.5 billion, priced at the top of its marketed range amid strong investor demand.

Financially, MiniMax reported 2025 revenue of $79 million, up 159% year over year, with more than 70% of revenue generated outside China. Consumer AI subscriptions and enterprise AI services were the primary growth drivers.

The company, however, remained loss-making, reporting a $1.87 billion net loss, largely driven by fair-value changes in financial instruments following its IPO.

The company’s latest major model launch is MiniMax M3, released in June.

MiniMax positions M3 as its flagship open-weight multimodal model, combining a 1 million-token context window, native image and video understanding, and a new MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) architecture designed to reduce long-context inference costs while improving coding and agentic performance

title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Work Powered by GPT-5.6 for Enterprise Workflows
content:
The launch marks OpenAI's biggest push yet to turn ChatGPT into a workplace productivity platform with connected apps and AI agents.

OpenAI has launched ChatGPT Work, a new AI agent that can complete multi-step tasks across connected workplace applications. The company also rolled out its latest frontier model, GPT-5.6, which powers the new offering.

ChatGPT Work is available on web and mobile for Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users, with Plus and Business subscribers set to receive access over the next few days.

ChatGPT Work can access connected applications such as Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Drive, SharePoint, email, calendars, and CRMs to gather information, create documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and web apps, and carry out projects that can run for hours with limited user intervention.

The company said GPT-5.6 powers ChatGPT Work, improving its ability to reason through complex tasks, follow templates, and reference files while producing finished work products.

“ChatGPT Work is an agent in ChatGPT that helps you take on more ambitious tasks,” OpenAI said in its blog post. “It can gather information across your apps and workflows to create finished materials like sheets, slides, docs, and web apps, and stay with complex projects for hours by breaking them into smaller steps and completing them independently.”

The launch builds on Codex, OpenAI’s coding agent, which the company said is now used by more than 5 million people every week. While Codex initially targeted software developers, OpenAI said more than 1 million users now rely on it for work outside software development.

The company also announced that Scheduled Tasks can now automate recurring workflows. Users can ask ChatGPT to review Slack updates, monitor websites, summarise changes, update presentations from email feedback, or refresh meeting agendas on a recurring basis. Users can track progress, modify tasks, and approve important actions when required.

On desktop, ChatGPT Work introduces a built-in browser that allows the AI agent to access websites, online tools, and files from Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 within the application. OpenAI also expanded Computer Use capabilities, allowing ChatGPT to interact with local applications, browsers, and files to complete tasks in the background.

OpenAI said the standalone Codex app will merge into the new ChatGPT desktop app. The combined application adds capabilities including inline code editing, pull request reviews, support for multiple repositories, and faster computer use powered by GPT-5.6.

The existing ChatGPT desktop application will be renamed ChatGPT Classic.

The updated app is available globally for Windows and Mac users, while Chat, Work and Codex features will be available across all plans, including the Free tier.

The company is also launching Sites in public beta, allowing users to build and share interactive websites and web applications directly from ChatGPT. The feature can be used to create dashboards, project trackers, prototypes, reports, and internal portals that update as underlying information changes.

To support enterprise adoption, ChatGPT Work includes security and governance controls inherited from ChatGPT Enterprise. Administrators can manage plugin access, connected tools, browser permissions, and workspace policies. OpenAI also introduced an Auto-review system that checks important actions involving connected tools and APIs before execution.

According to OpenAI, nearly all internal teams, including finance and sales, already use ChatGPT Work and Codex.

GPT 5.6 is Here

OpenAI has finally launched GPT-5.6, after delaying its rollout at the US government’s request to assess security concerns. It has introduced a new family of AI models comprising Sol, Terra, and Luna, as the company seeks to improve coding, scientific reasoning, cybersecurity and enterprise AI workloads while offering different performance and cost trade-offs.

OpenAI has rolled out GPT-5.6 across ChatGPT, Codex and the OpenAI API, with availability beginning today.

GPT-5.6 Sol is OpenAI’s flagship model and the company’s most capable model to date. It can do complex tasks requiring advanced reasoning, coding, biology research, and cybersecurity. Terra is positioned as a lower-cost alternative for production workloads, while Luna is the fastest and most cost-efficient model in the family.

Together, the three models are intended to serve a wider range of developers and enterprises depending on performance and pricing requirements.

GPT-5.6 Sol is priced at $5 per million input tokens and $30 per million output tokens. Terra costs $2.50 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, while Luna, the company’s lowest-cost model, is priced at $1 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens.

According to OpenAI, GPT-5.6 Sol sets a new state of the art on Terminal-Bench 2.1, a benchmark that measures command-line workflows involving planning, iteration, and tool coordination.

On Agents’ Last Exam, GPT-5.6 Sol model scored 53.6, outperforming Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 (adaptive) by 13.1 points. At the medium reasoning setting, Sol exceeded Claude Fable 5 by 11.4 points while costing roughly one-quarter as much. OpenAI added that GPT-5.6 Terra and Luna also outperformed Claude Fable 5 on the benchmark at around one-sixteenth of the estimated cost.

In cybersecurity, GPT-5.6 Sol achieved a score of 73.5% on ExploitBench, a benchmark that measures a model’s ability to progress from identifying vulnerable code to arbitrary code execution, compared with 47.9% for GPT-5.5 at a comparable output token budget.

The company also reported gains on coding agent tasks. GPT-5.6 Sol, with its maximum reasoning mode, outperformed Claude Fable 5 while using 54% fewer output tokens.

OpenAI said the advantage extends across the model family, with GPT-5.6 Terra narrowly surpassing Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Luna outperforming Claude Opus 4.8 at their highest-scoring configurations. According to the company, both Terra and Luna achieved these results at roughly one-fifth of the estimated API cost and in about one-third of the time.

content:
The NeGD project will use AI to help government departments draft, review and standardise procurement documents while retaining human oversight of decisions.

What Actually Matters.

Cactus Technology Solutions has secured a contract from MeitY to develop an AI-powered procurement platform for government departments.

The platform will assist in drafting and reviewing procurement documents while ensuring human oversight in decision-making.

Mumbai-based Cactus Technology Solutions has won a contract from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology's (MeitY) National e-Governance Division (NeGD) to build an AI-powered procurement authoring platform for government departments.

The platform will help officials prepare Requests for Proposals (RFPs), Requests for Quotations (RFQs), Expressions of Interest (EOIs) and other procurement documents by using AI to draft, review and validate content. It is intended to streamline procurement workflows while keeping human oversight at the centre of the process.

The award comes weeks after Cactus Technology Solutions and Kyndryl Solutions emerged as the only two technically qualified bidders for the project. According to official records cited by Moneycontrol, Cactus secured a perfect score of 100 in the quality-and-cost-based selection evaluation, ahead of Kyndryl, which scored 85.36. Cactus also submitted the lower financial bid of ₹2.27 crore, compared with Kyndryl’s ₹2.86 crore.

The procurement process narrowed significantly during the technical evaluation. While Cactus and Kyndryl qualified for the final stage, CoRover was disqualified after submitting its financial bid as part of its technical proposal, while Innefu Labs and NEC Corporation India failed to secure the minimum qualifying marks.

“Winning this mandate for NeGD’s AI-based RFP Authoring Tool project is a proud moment for our team at CACTUS. With government procurement representing nearly 22% of GDP, and RFP creation today requiring significant technical know-how, there's a real opportunity to bring efficiency and transparency to the process,” Akhilesh Ayer, CEO of Cactus Technology Solutions, told Moneycontrol.

“We look forward to building a solution with robust security guardrails at its core, leveraging our experience delivering AI products in complex, regulated environments, ensuring this initiative delivers real impact at scale,” he added.

Once deployed, NeGD intends to roll out the platform across ministries and departments, providing officials with an AI-assisted tool to draft, review and standardise procurement documents. The project is expected to improve consistency and efficiency in public procurement while ensuring final decisions remain with government officials.

title: India's AI-Led E-commerce Market to Touch $250 Bn by 2030: Shiprocket-Deloitte Report
content:
AI, vernacular commerce, and rising adoption in smaller cities are fuelling the rise of India's e-commerce market.

What Actually Matters.

India's e-commerce market is expected to grow to $250 billion by 2030, driven by AI and increased digital adoption.

AI technologies such as product discovery and checkout intelligence are transforming online shopping experiences.

India's e-commerce market is projected to grow from around $90 billion in 2025 to approximately $250 billion by 2030, driven by AI-powered shopping experiences, vernacular commerce, and increasing digital adoption beyond metropolitan centres, according to a report released by Shiprocket in partnership with Deloitte.

Titled AI for Bharat Commerce: Unlocking the $250 Billion Business Opportunity, the report found that AI-powered product discovery, checkout intelligence, and fulfilment innovation are expected to reshape online shopping as India's internet user base expands.

The report noted that 488 million rural internet users account for 55% of the country's active internet population, while 98% of internet users consume content in Indic languages. Vernacular voice queries have grown 156% faster than English, and tier-2 and tier-3 cities now account for more than 60% of India's online shoppers.

The study identified AI-powered personalisation, conversion intelligence, and Bharat-led digital adoption as the three key trends shaping the next phase of e-commerce growth. It also found that 90% of Indian consumers believe generative AI has improved their online shopping experience.

Commenting on the findings, Saahil Goel, MD and CEO, Shiprocket, said in a statement, "Consumers today expect faster, more personalised, and more convenient shopping experiences. For businesses, this means investing in AI, strengthening fulfilment capabilities, and building experiences that cater to customers across both metro and emerging markets."

The report highlighted AI-powered personalisation, conversational commerce, visual discovery, and predictive recommendations as technologies that help businesses improve conversions and customer retention. According to the study, recognised returning customers convert at 2.1 times the rate of new-to-ecosystem users, while brands with repeat purchase rates above 25% post profit margins 3.4 times higher than those below 15%.

Anand Ramanathan, Partner and Consumer Industry Leader, Deloitte India, added, "As India charts its path toward becoming one of the world's largest and most dynamic commerce markets, the winners will not simply be those who adopt AI, but those who learn how to apply it with precision, speed, and discipline. The opportunity is large. The next phase will belong to those who act decisively."

title: Open-Source AI Platform Ollama Raises $65 Mn in Series B Funding
content:
Ollama’s total funding now stands at $88 million.

Ollama, a developer platform for open-source AI models, has raised $65 million in a Series B funding round led by Benchmark partner Peter Fenton, with participation from Theory Ventures, 8VC, Y Combinator, and several technology executives, as the company looks to expand its cloud platform and developer tooling for open AI models.

The company did not reveal the pre-money or post-money valuation. It has raised a total of $88 million to date.

The company said its platform is now used by 8.9 million developers and by 85% of Fortune 500 companies. Ollama plans to use the new funding to expand its hybrid inference capabilities, add support for newly released open models more quickly, and grow its cloud platform while retaining its emphasis on local model execution.

Founded by Jeff Lindsay and Michael Crosby in 2023, the company is best known for software that allows developers to download and run open-weight AI models locally through a single command and access them through a local API.

“This funding is fuel for what's ahead,” the founders wrote in a statement. They added that Ollama intends to deliver “seamless hybrid inference, support for new open models the day they’re released, and a cloud that lets any developer and their team reach the most powerful models without giving up ownership or privacy.”

Ollama works to remove the need for API keys or dedicated server infrastructure, enabling developers to run models on their own hardware while retaining control over data and deployments.

The company also disclosed growth figures for its hosted offering, stating that token volume on Ollama Cloud has more than doubled every month on average.

The cloud service provides managed access to open models including DeepSeek, GLM, Nemotron, Kimi, and MiniMax. The company is building a hybrid deployment model to let developers move between local and cloud inference without giving up ownership or privacy.

Lindsay and Crosby previously founded Kitematic, a Docker management application that Docker acquired in 2015. Their work later became Docker Desktop, which the founders said is now used by more than 10 million developers.

title: Elon Musk says He Was ‘Clearly Wrong’ About Anthropic, Calls it the AI Leader
content:
Meta also introduced the Meta Model API in public preview, allowing developers to build applications using Muse Spark models for the first time.

Meta has launched Muse Spark 1.1, a multimodal reasoning model for agentic AI tasks.

Alongside the model launch, Meta introduced the Meta Model API in public preview, marking the first time developers can build applications using Muse Spark models through the company’s own API platform.

The company said Muse Spark 1.1 is available in Thinking mode through the Meta AI app and Meta AI website. For API access, Meta has priced the model at $1.25 per million input tokens and $4.25 per million output tokens.

The release follows the launch of Muse Image earlier this week as Meta continues to build its AI offerings under Meta Superintelligence Labs.

“Muse Spark 1.1 is a multimodal reasoning model built for agentic tasks, with major gains in tool and computer use, coding, and multimodal understanding,” the company said in a blog post.

Meta said the model is built to execute tasks across multiple applications and external services, with support for native tools, model context protocol (MCP) servers and custom skills. The company said the model can coordinate multiple AI agents by planning tasks, delegating work to sub-agents and combining their outputs to reduce execution time.

The model supports a context window of one million tokens, allowing it to retain information from earlier interactions, retrieve relevant context and compress conversations while preserving information required for later tasks.

According to Meta, Muse Spark 1.1 scored 88.1 on MCP Atlas, ahead of Anthropic’s Opus 4.8 (82.2) and OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 (xhigh) (75.3). On JobBench, it also led both models with a score of 54.7, compared with 48.4 for Opus 4.8 and 38.3 for GPT-5.5. On Humanity’s Last Exam with tools and Finance Agent v2, Muse Spark 1.1 again outperformed both competitors.

However, Anthropic’s model retained its lead on benchmarks such as Toolathlon-Verified, OSWorld-Verified, SWE-Bench Pro and CharXiv Reasoning, while GPT-5.5 topped Terminal-Bench 2.1, DeepSWE 1.1 and BabyVision.

Meta also highlighted improvements in computer-use capabilities. The company said Muse Spark 1.1 can automate workflows across applications, deciding whether to generate scripts or interact with graphical interfaces depending on the task.

The company also positioned the model for software development. Meta said Muse Spark 1.1 can diagnose bugs, implement features in large codebases and perform code migrations. It added that the model supports agentic coding workflows, including planning mode, goal conditioning, sub-agent delegation and context compaction.

Beyond coding, Meta said Muse Spark 1.1 can combine visual understanding with reasoning and tool use. The company said the model can generate visual-to-code outputs, create image and video descriptions, and execute multimodal workflows.

On safety, Meta said it evaluated the model under its Advanced AI Scaling Framework across chemical and biological risks, cybersecurity and loss-of-control scenarios.

The company said Muse Spark 1.1 remained within its deployment thresholds and showed resistance to jailbreak attempts, prompt injection attacks and developer prompt attacks.

Musk praised Anthropic’s Mythos and Fable models and said he would not use SpaceXAI’s infrastructure advantage to hurt the company despite competing in the AI race.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has publicly acknowledged that he was ‘clearly wrong’ about Anthropic, describing the AI startup as the current leader in artificial intelligence and praising its latest models, Mythos and Fable.

In a post on X on July 9, Musk said no other company had released models as capable as Anthropic’s Mythos and Fable series and predicted that the company would soon launch an even more advanced successor.

“I was clearly wrong about Anthropic. They are obviously currently the leader in AI. No company has released a model as good as Mythos/Fable, and they will undoubtedly have Mythos 2 ready soon.”

Musk also dismissed suggestions that he could use his company’s infrastructure relationship with Anthropic to undermine the AI firm.

“I would never cut them off in a way that hurt them badly, even as a competitor. That’s not my style.”

To make his point, Musk pointed to Tesla’s decision to open-source its patents and make its Supercharger network available to rival automakers. He also said SpaceX continues to launch competing satellite systems without raising prices or imposing unfair terms, adding that even his critics are free to use and criticise him on X.

The remarks mark a sharp reversal from Musk’s earlier criticism of Anthropic. Over the past year, he had repeatedly accused the company of political bias and questioned its prospects in the AI race. “Your AI hates Whites and Asians, especially Chinese, heterosexuals and men. This is misanthropic and evil,” he wrote on X in February earlier this year.

His latest comments come weeks after Anthropic entered a major compute partnership with SpaceXAI, securing access to more than 300 megawatts of compute capacity—equivalent to over 2,20,000 NVIDIA GPUs—from the Colossus 1 data centre. The agreement is reportedly valued at $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, although either side can terminate the deal with 90 days’ notice.

Anthropic’s Fable and Mythos models have been at the centre of industry attention in recent weeks. The US government temporarily restricted foreign access to the models over national security concerns before later lifting the export controls after Anthropic agreed to additional security measures and government collaboration.

Its ADRs are scheduled to begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker SKHY on July 10.

SK Hynix has raised about $26.5 billion through its US listing after selling 177.9 million American Depositary Shares (ADSs) at $149 each ahead of its Nasdaq debut as investors continue to back companies supplying the infrastructure behind the AI boom.

The South Korean memory chipmaker priced the offering at a 2.7% premium to the average price of its Seoul-listed shares over the previous three trading sessions. Its ADRs are scheduled to begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker SKHY on July 10.

SK Hynix’s US listing is the largest ever by a foreign company, surpassing Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba’s $25 billion debut in 2014. It is also the second-largest US stock sale on record, behind SpaceX’s offering.

SK Hynix’s primary listing will remain in Seoul, while the ADR offering was underwritten by Bank of America, Citigroup, Goldman Sachs and JP Morgan.

The proceeds will be used to finance new factories and equipment to increase production of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, which are widely used in AI accelerators.

The US listing is also expected to improve the company’s visibility among global investors and help narrow its valuation gap with US-based Micron, despite SK Hynix holding a larger share of the HBM market. Micron currently trades at a higher forward price-to-earnings multiple than SK Hynix.

The company also continues to compete with Samsung Electronics for leadership in the memory chip market. While Samsung remains the world’s largest memory chipmaker by volume, SK Hynix has established an early lead in HBM.

SK Hynix has emerged as NVIDIA’s largest supplier of HBM chips, a position that has placed it at the centre of the AI infrastructure build-out. In May, the South Korean chipmaker crossed the $1 trillion market capitalisation mark, becoming the third Asian company to reach the milestone, following Samsung Electronics and TSMC.

Last month, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang said SK Hynix would remain the company’s largest memory partner and added that shortages of advanced memory chips were likely to continue for several years because of strong demand.

title: OpenAI Kills Atlas
content:
Instead of maintaining Atlas as a separate application, OpenAI is moving those browser capabilities into ChatGPT Work.

OpenAI is shutting down Atlas, its standalone AI-powered web browser, marking the latest step in the company’s effort to consolidate products around ChatGPT.

The announcement was made as part of the launch of ChatGPT Work, a new agentic workspace that combines ChatGPT, Codex and long-running task automation into a single desktop experience.

In its announcement, OpenAI said it has updated its Chrome extension to work directly in Chrome’s sidebar and that the new capabilities “build on what we learned from Atlas.” “We'll begin sunsetting the standalone Atlas browser and will share information with users about how to transition to ChatGPT,” the company added.

The new desktop app includes a built-in browser, computer-use features, access to local files and integrations with enterprise applications such as Slack, Google Drive, Microsoft Teams and Salesforce, positioning ChatGPT as a unified productivity platform rather than a collection of standalone products.

Atlas was introduced in late 2025 as an AI-first browser built on Google’s open-source Chromium engine, integrating ChatGPT directly into the browsing experience.

Rather than functioning as a conventional browser with an AI assistant layered on top, Atlas was designed around agentic browsing, allowing ChatGPT to understand web pages, assist with research, summarise content and carry out browser-based workflows.

Although OpenAI did not prominently advertise it at launch, the browser was built on Chromium, the same browser engine that powers Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge.

The Atlas shutdown follows OpenAI’s decision earlier this year to discontinue the standalone Sora video-generation application, while retaining parts of the underlying technology for other products. Sora’s API is scheduled to be retired later this year.

Atlas’s retirement also aligns with broader reports that OpenAI has been scaling back experimental consumer-facing initiatives to focus on enterprise software, coding agents and ChatGPT.

A March report from The Wall Street Journal stated that company leadership had begun reassessing “side projects” such as Atlas and Sora to prioritise products more closely tied to business adoption and revenue, while the upcoming ChatGPT super-app became the central product strategy.

title: After Medical Leave, OpenAI Applications CEO Fidji Simo Steps Down to Focus on Recovery
content:
She said she will continue contributing to OpenAI as an adviser while supporting AI-driven healthcare initiatives through Chronicle Bio and Coda Research.

OpenAI executive Fidji Simo has stepped down from her full-time role at the company and will transition to a part-time advisory position after taking a three-month medical leave to recover from a chronic illness.

In a post on X on July 9, Simo said a severe exacerbation of a chronic illness she has lived with for seven years made her realise that her recovery would take longer than expected and required her full attention.

“Today, I shared with the OpenAI team that I have decided to leave my full-time role at OpenAI and transition to being a part-time advisor,” Simo wrote.

“Three months ago, I had to go on medical leave after a severe exacerbation of a chronic illness I’ve lived with for seven years. During that time, it became clear that the road to recovery would be much longer and more complex than I had anticipated—and that I needed to focus on it fully.”

Simo said she had repeatedly ignored advice from doctors, friends and colleagues to slow down, including an earlier offer from Meta to take a year-long medical leave.

“Over the years, doctors, friends, colleagues, and loved ones encouraged me to slow down,” she wrote. “Facebook offered me the opportunity to take a full year of medical leave. I didn't even pause to consider it. I immediately said no.”

She added that Meta Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg had advised her to “play the long game”, saying, “I wish I had listened.”

Simo said the experience reinforced her belief that AI should address everyday problems in areas such as healthcare, finances and time management.

“In particular, curing disease is the most important thing AI could accomplish,” she wrote, adding that she would continue to support that work through OpenAI as well as ChronicleBio and Coda.

Simo thanked OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, President Greg Brockman and the company’s board for allowing her to continue contributing as an adviser while focusing on her recovery.

Simo joined OpenAI’s board in 2024 and became the company’s CEO of Applications in 2025 before later overseeing AGI deployment and commercial operations. Before OpenAI, she served as CEO of Instacart and previously led the Facebook app business at Meta.

During her absence, Greg Brockman took over product responsibilities as the company reorganised its product teams around ChatGPT and Codex.

IBS Group has launched Naviq Technology, an AI company targeting airlines, airports and hospitality firms, with hiring under way in Kochi.

What Actually Matters.

IBS Group has launched Naviq Technology, an AI firm focused on the travel industry.

The company plans to invest $500 million over the next five years.

Singapore- and Kerala-based technology company IBS Group has launched Naviq Technology, an artificial intelligence company aimed at the travel industry. The company will receive an investment of $500 million over the next five years.

Naviq Technology intends to partner with airlines, airports, cruise lines, vacation providers, and hospitality groups. The company will work on business transformation, operational modernisation, and the use of AI to build revenue streams for these partners.

IBS Group Founder and Executive Chairman V K Mathews said Naviq Technology would initially hire 2,000 people, with plans to expand the workforce to over 5,000 within five years across its 16 centres worldwide.

"Naviq Technology's business plan envisages rapid growth from its 16 centres worldwide, headcount growing to over 5,000 high-tech professionals in the next five years,” the company said in a statement.

The company draws on the travel industry experience of IBS Software as a provider of AI-first innovations to help clients improve operational efficiency, personalise end-user experiences, and unlock revenue opportunities.

IBS Software operates as a SaaS provider across aviation, hospitality, tour, cruise and logistics segments, and employs staff in Kerala.

Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan is scheduled to inaugurate the Naviq Technology campus in Kochi on July 23.

"Naviq reflects a clear structural shift in how travel technology services are delivered, pairing deep industry expertise with an AI-first model built for speed and commercial impact," said Jason Wright, Partner at Apax Partners, an investor in the venture.

title: Electronics Major Arduino Opens Edge AI Invention Lab at IIT Delhi for Hands-On AI Learning
content:
Expanding its Physical AI for All initiative, Arduino looks to strengthen AI education in India with innovation labs, a 120-hour edge AI curriculum, and partnerships with over 300 institutions.

What Actually Matters.

Arduino has launched an Edge AI Invention Lab at IIT Delhi to enhance AI education in India.

The lab will offer hands-on experience in building real-world edge AI applications through various interactive learning methods.

Italian open-source electronics platform Arduino has launched its new Edge AI Invention Lab at the Student Innovation Lab (SIL) in the Department of Electrical Engineering at IIT Delhi, expanding its ‘Physical AI for All’ initiative aimed at making edge AI and physical AI education more accessible across India.

The new facility will provide students with hands-on experience in building real-world edge AI and physical AI applications through project-based learning, hackathons, interdisciplinary research, innovation challenges, and industry collaborations.

The company said its initiative aims to bridge the gap between classroom learning and practical applications by combining innovation labs with Arduino hardware, student workshops, digital learning platforms, academic partnerships, and industry-focused curricula.

“Arduino has spent more than two decades making technology accessible through open-source innovation. With our Physical AI initiative, we are extending that mission by helping universities create hands-on learning environments where students can build the next generation of intelligent systems,” said Guneet Bedi, Senior Director of Sales at Qualcomm Technologies.

Prof Amartansh Dubey from IIT Delhi added that the collaboration would help students turn innovative ideas into practical AI solutions with real-world impact.

The IIT Delhi lab joins Arduino’s growing network of AI innovation hubs in India. Similar centres have already been established at Manav Rachna International Institute of Research and Studies, while new labs are planned at Adani University, Symbiosis Institute of Technology, and Shiv Nadar School in Faridabad.

According to the company, the initiative has reached more than 23,000 students, developers, educators, and innovators within six months through over 100 workshops, bootcamps, and innovation programmes. The company has also trained more than 1,000 educators across 25 faculty development programmes and partnered with over 300 universities and higher education institutions.

To strengthen AI education further, Arduino has developed a 120-hour credit-based Edge AI curriculum with education partner STEMLORE Innovators. The company is also supporting the establishment of 10 Edge AI Centres of Excellence across state technical universities while continuing to promote local manufacturing.
