title: RBI’s Financial Stability Report Flags AI investment risk, says Indian Banks Stay Resilient
content:
The June 2026 report flags AI-driven investment and NBFI risks globally, while stating Indian banks remain stable and well-capitalised.

What Actually Matters.

The RBI's Financial Stability Report highlights growing risks associated with AI-driven investments globally.

Indian banks are reported to be stable and well-capitalised amidst external pressures.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has published its Financial Stability Report for June 2026, noting that risks are mounting to AI-linked investment worldwide, while stating that India’s financial system continues to hold up under external pressure.

Global markets have moved past the initial shock from the West Asia conflict and are now being supported largely by momentum in AI-related spending. The Economic Times reports that AI investment is now spilling into bond markets, with hyperscalers ramping up capital expenditure on AI infrastructure even as their free cash flows have declined.

Companies including Microsoft, Meta, Google, NVIDIA, Amazon and Anthropic have sharply increased debt issuances over the past two years to fund this buildout, with longer-tenor borrowing rising notably in 2026. The RBI notes that a correction in AI-linked asset prices could carry systemic consequences, since banks hold indirect exposure through private credit firms and other intermediaries that finance the sector.

The report also points to non-bank financial intermediaries (NBFIs), which it says are expanding at twice the rate of the global banking sector. Their rising footprint across asset classes heightens the risk of shock amplification and of turning market turmoil into financial instability, the report states.

On sovereign debt, the RBI notes that bond yields in several advanced economies have reached levels not seen in 20 years, following the war in West Asia. It attributes this to inflationary pressures from higher energy prices, expectations of central bank rate hikes, sustained fiscal deficits requiring higher bond issuance, and quantitative tightening.

Governments have also shortened the maturity profile of their debt, leaving them more exposed to refinancing risk at a point when borrowing needs are rising, with refinancing needs among Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development countries reaching a record $13.5 trillion in 2025.

On the domestic front, the RBI states that Indian banks remain in a stable position, supported by capital levels, asset quality and profitability. Macro stress test results showed that the banking system remains well-positioned to absorb potential shocks.

Non-banking financial companies were also described as financially sound, supported by capitalisation, profitability, and improving asset quality, while the insurance sector maintained solvency levels above the minimum threshold.

The report flags funding as an area for monitoring. It notes that banks’ liability profile is shifting from low-cost current and savings account deposits to higher-cost term deposits and certificates of deposit, which raises the marginal cost of funds.

Banks have also been drawing down excess statutory liquidity ratio investments to support credit growth, leading to a decline in liquidity coverage ratio buffers. Gold loans were identified as a segment for close monitoring.

The RBI reported that gold loans have become the largest segment within non-housing retail loans, expanding at a compound annual growth rate of 42.4% since March 2024, compared with 23% growth in overall non-housing retail loans. Both banks and NBFCs are increasing disbursements during 2025-26 amid rising gold prices.

The report added that a sustained correction in gold prices could reduce collateral cover, increase borrower stress, and lead to higher delinquencies.

Regarding cyber risk, the RBI identified AI-enabled cyberattacks as the most significant near-term challenge from a cyber threat perspective. It also noted that growth in gold imports slowed substantially in May compared with April.

Household debt reached 45.5% of gross domestic product by the end of September 2025, driven mainly by non-housing retail loans, which made up 58.4% of total household borrowings as of March 2026.

Summing up the domestic outlook, the RBI stated that India’s macroeconomic fundamentals provide a cushion against external shocks, while flagging that repeated global disruptions could tighten financial conditions over time.

title: AWS Invests $1 Bn to Launch Forward Deployed Engineering for AI Deployments
content:
AWS will embed AI engineers within customer teams to build and deploy agentic AI systems, with deployment timelines shifting from months to days.

What Actually Matters.

AWS has committed $1 billion to establish a Forward Deployed Engineering organisation focused on AI integration.

The initiative aims to embed AI engineers within customer teams to expedite deployment timelines significantly.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) has announced a $1 billion investment to launch a new Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) organisation that will place AI engineers inside customer teams to co-develop and deploy agentic AI systems.

The new unit targets enterprises that have moved beyond AI pilots and want to integrate AI into business operations. AWS said the teams will work directly with customers’ engineering, business, and security teams to build production AI systems using their own data and governance frameworks.

“Customers have moved past exploring what AI can do; they want to make it core to how they operate,” said Francessca Vasquez, Vice President of Frontier AI Engineering and Services at AWS, in a blog post. “They want to recreate their business processes with agentic AI built in so they can increase productivity and deliver AI-powered products.”

According to AWS, the FDE organisation will use purpose-built AI agents alongside engineers to shorten deployment timelines from months to days. The company said projects will follow an AI-driven software development approach in which AI agents handle parts of the development lifecycle while engineers validate the outputs.

Unlike traditional consulting engagements, AWS said the FDE model focuses on transferring knowledge to customers. At the end of a deployment, customers will receive production AI systems, knowledge graphs, documentation, operational runbooks, and trained internal teams capable of maintaining and expanding the systems independently.

AWS said the engineering teams deploy a semantic layer inside the customer’s AWS environment that connects enterprise data sources and creates a governed knowledge graph for AI agents to reason over. Customer data remains within the customer’s governance framework, supported by hardware-based isolation and end-to-end encryption.

The company said FDE teams are already working with customers, including the Allen Institute, Cox Automotive, the NBA, NFL, Ricoh, and Southwest Airlines.

“The NFL partnered with AWS FDE and got engineers building alongside our team to launch into production in just weeks,” said Gary Brantley, Chief Information Officer at the National Football League. “Together, we created new fan-facing products like NFL Fantasy AI and NFL IQ that allow fans to interact with NFL data like never before.”

AWS said the new organisation builds on experience from its Generative AI Innovation Centre, which has worked with customers on AI deployments over the past three years. The company cited projects with BMW, where AI was used to reduce service disruptions across 23 million connected vehicles; Jabil, which built a manufacturing assistant; and Lyft, where an AI system reduced driver support resolution times by 87%.

Initially, AWS Forward Deployed Engineering will serve organisations which deploy production AI systems in sectors such as financial services, government, and other regulated industries where governance, security, and compliance requirements are critical.

What Actually Matters.

The US has lifted export controls on Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5, enabling global access from July 1.

Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet 5 as the default AI model for users, enhancing capabilities in coding and reasoning.

The US Department of Commerce has lifted export controls on Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5, allowing the company to restore access to the models starting July 1. The announcement came alongside the launch of Claude Sonnet 5, Anthropic's latest AI model for coding, reasoning, and agentic tasks.

Anthropic said it had received notice that the Department of Commerce had lifted export controls on Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 after a two-week review.

“We’ll begin restoring access tomorrow and will share an update soon,” the company said in a post on X. “We’re grateful to our users for their patience and to everyone who worked with us on redeploying the models.”

US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said the government had worked with Anthropic before approving the model.

“Over the past two weeks, we have worked closely with Anthropic to analyse and approve Fable 5 to ensure alignment across the US Government and strengthen America’s leadership in AI,” Lutnick said in a post on X.

Anthropic said Claude Fable 5 will be available globally from July 1 across the Claude Platform, Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork. Pro, Max, Team, and select Enterprise subscribers will be able to use the model for up to 50% of their weekly usage limits through July 7, after which it will be available through usage credits. The company added that access on AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry will be restored as soon as possible.

The company also said it has restored access to Claude Mythos 5 for a group of US organisations after receiving approval from the US government on June 26, and is working with authorities to expand access to additional domestic and international partners participating in its Glasswing program.

Anthropic released Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 on June 9. On June 12, the US government imposed export controls on the models, requiring the company to restrict access for foreign nationals.

Meanwhile, Anthropic introduced Claude Sonnet 5, making it the default model for Free and Pro users and rolling it out across Max, Team, Enterprise, Claude Code and its API.

Sonnet 5 is available immediately through the Claude app, Claude Code and the Claude API.

The company said Sonnet 5 delivers improvements over Sonnet 4.6 in reasoning, coding, tool use and knowledge work, while narrowing the performance gap with Opus 4.8 at a lower price.

“For many developers, the agentic AI era began with Sonnet-class models,” Anthropic said. “Sonnet 5 narrows the gap: its performance is close to that of Opus 4.8, but at lower prices.”

The model is available at an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens until August 31. Eventually, pricing will increase to $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens.

Anthropic said Sonnet 5 supports different effort levels, allowing developers to balance cost and performance. At higher effort settings, the model can match Opus 4.8 on some agentic search and computer-use tasks while offering lower operating costs.

According to the company, early access users reported that Sonnet 5 completes more complex tasks, verifies its own outputs without explicit instructions and performs autonomous workflows more consistently than previous Sonnet models.

Anthropic also said its safety evaluations found that Sonnet 5 has lower rates of hallucinations, sycophancy and other undesirable behaviours than Sonnet 4.6. The company added that the model performs worse than Opus 4.8 and Mythos 5 on cybersecurity evaluations and was not specifically trained for offensive cyber tasks.

Because of improvements in general capability, Anthropic has enabled cyber safeguards by default on Sonnet 5. The safeguards are less restrictive than those used for Fable 5, which the company said block a wider range of cybersecurity tasks.

title: MeitY Plans AI-Led Overhaul of Govt IT Systems, To Empanel 20 Tech Firms
content:
The selected firms will be responsible for evaluating existing government applications.

What Actually Matters.

MeitY is modernising government IT systems through a panel of up to 20 technology firms.

The initiative aims to streamline procurement processes for government departments over three years.

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) is preparing to accelerate the modernisation of government digital infrastructure by creating a panel of up to 20 technology firms that will help ministries upgrade legacy IT systems using AI, generative AI, and agentic AI technologies, as reported by Moneycontrol.

The initiative, proposed through a Request for Empanelment (RFE) issued by the National Informatics Centre Services Incorporated (NICSI) on June 25, aims to establish a ready pool of technology partners that government departments can engage without having to undertake separate procurement processes for each project. The empanelment will remain valid for an initial period of three years, with the possibility of a two-year extension based on performance.

Under the proposal, NICSI plans to empanel up to 10 companies under the general category and reserve another 10 slots for startups and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), encouraging broader participation from India’s emerging technology ecosystem.

The selected firms will be responsible for evaluating existing government applications, identifying outdated technology stacks, and recommending modernisation strategies to improve the efficiency, scalability, and resilience of public-sector digital systems.

A key feature of the initiative is the government’s emphasis on embedding AI into core digital infrastructure rather than treating it as a standalone capability. The scope of work includes integrating machine learning, generative AI, agentic AI, intelligent automation, and advanced analytics into government applications, as well as establishing AI governance frameworks to ensure responsible deployment and oversight.

Beyond application modernisation, vendors will also be expected to strengthen government data infrastructure by developing data lakes, data warehouses, and other modern data management architectures that support AI-driven decision-making.

The empanelment process will involve multiple stages of evaluation, including eligibility screening, technical assessment, presentations, and financial evaluation, with technical capability carrying significant weight in the final selection.

By creating a common panel of AI-focused technology partners, NICSI is expected to streamline technology procurement while enabling ministries and departments to rapidly execute AI-led digital transformation projects across government.

title: Razorpay Partners With NPCI Bharat BillPay to Launch Banking Connect for NetBanking
content:
Genpact has introduced an AI-based solution built on Microsoft Azure to automate how consumer goods companies identify and resolve disputed deductions.

What Actually Matters.

Genpact has launched an AI tool to automate deduction management for consumer goods companies.

The solution aims to reduce financial penalties linked to promotions, logistics, and compliance issues.

Genpact has launched Genpact Deductions Recovery, designed to automate deduction management in accounts receivable for consumer goods companies, using AI agents to identify, validate, and resolve disputed deductions. It forms part of Genpact's wider portfolio of agentic AI solutions.

According to Genpact, consumer goods companies often miss up to 20% of preventable deductions, which the company describes as financial penalties linked to promotions, logistics, and compliance issues. Genpact also stated that more than 30% of invalid claims go unresolved, attributing this to manual processes that rely on spreadsheets, emails, and separate portals.

Anil Nanduru, Global Business Leader for Consumer and Healthcare, and High-Tech Software at Genpact, described the reasoning behind the solution. "Disconnected trade data and manual reconciliation are slowing businesses down," he said in a statement.

He added that the company is deploying agents built to understand industry-specific issues and resolve disputes without constant manual input.

The solution runs on Microsoft Azure and uses AI agents to manage the deduction process from start to finish. It uses several Microsoft tools, including Azure AI Document Intelligence in Foundry Tools, Azure AI Search, and Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models.

Genpact said the system pulls deduction data from customer portals, carrier systems, and internal ERPs, matches debit memos against proof-of-delivery and internal records, and carries out follow-up actions such as bill-backs for unreturned products, with limited manual intervention.

Genpact said clients using the solution could see cycle times reduced by up to 20%, additional annual recoveries of up to 15% from previously unidentified invalid deductions, and a reduction in financial leakage of around 1.5%.

The company also said the tool can reduce recurring deductions through data-based root cause analysis and free staff from manual data entry tasks.

Dylan Jetha, Global Trade to Cash at Kraft Heinz, said, "Visibility and control are essential given the nature of deductions in a complex business environment like ours,".

He added that Genpact's use of pre-trained agents in the deductions process was a development he was watching with interest.

Keith Mercier, Vice President of Worldwide Retail and Consumer Goods at Microsoft, said Genpact's experience in the consumer goods sector positioned it to support the industry with the new solution, combining its domain knowledge with Microsoft Azure's infrastructure.

The solution aims to simplify NetBanking for businesses and consumers, with support from banks including SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank.

What Actually Matters.

Razorpay has partnered with NPCI Bharat BillPay to enhance NetBanking for mobile payments in India.

The solution aims to streamline high-value transactions across various sectors, reducing operational complexities for businesses.

Razorpay on July 1 announced that it has partnered with NPCI Bharat BillPay Limited (NBBL), a subsidiary of the National Payments Corporation of India, to join Banking Connect. The companies describe the solution as an attempt to update NetBanking for mobile-first payments across India.

According to Razorpay, NetBanking remains widely used for high-value transactions in sectors such as financial services, lending, education and government.

The company said that offering NetBanking at scale has typically required businesses to manage separate integrations with individual banks, along with settlement and reconciliation processes, adding operational work as businesses expand.

Razorpay also said that many NetBanking transactions still involve several steps, including redirects and repeated entry of banking credentials, which can add time to the payment process compared with other digital payment methods.

Through Banking Connect, Razorpay said businesses can access multiple banks through a single integration, rather than connecting to each bank separately. The company said the solution supports payment journeys through banking apps, intent and QR-based flows, and centralises settlement and reconciliation processes.

Razorpay said the feature is available through its existing checkout system, without requiring further integration work from businesses already using its platform.

Arif Khan, Chief Information Officer at Razorpay Technologies Private Limited, referred to the RBI’s Annual Report for 2025 in commenting on the initiative. “As per RBI’s Annual Report ’25, India is today the global leader in real-time digital payments," he said.

He added that the next phase of innovation involves extending the same speed and reliability standards to NetBanking through Banking Connect.

Noopur Chaturvedi, Managing Director and CEO of NPCI Bharat BillPay Limited, described the aim behind the initiative. “Our focus at NBBL is to build interoperable, future-ready payment infrastructure that improves experiences for both businesses and consumers,” she said.

She added that the partnership with Razorpay would help expand the Banking Connect ecosystem and support wider adoption of updated NetBanking methods.

Banking Connect is currently supported by State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Federal Bank, AU Small Finance Bank and YES Bank. Razorpay said further banks are expected to join the ecosystem over time.

title: Anthropic Introduces Claude Science for End-to-End Scientific Research
content:
Anthopic’s new platform helps researchers analyse data, generate scientific outputs, and manage large-scale computing jobs from a single interface.

What Actually Matters.

Anthropic has launched Claude Science, an AI-powered platform streamlining scientific research processes.

The tool consolidates literature analysis, data processing, and computing resources within a single interface.

Anthropic has launched Claude Science, a new AI-powered workbench designed to help scientists conduct research more efficiently by bringing together literature analysis, data processing, scientific visualisation, and computing resources on a single platform.

The tool is now available in beta for Claude Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users on macOS and Linux.

Claude Science is aimed at researchers who typically work with multiple tools, including PubMed, Jupyter notebooks, R, and high-performance computing (HPC) clusters. Instead of switching between different platforms, scientists can now perform much of their workflow within a single environment.

The platform is powered by a coordinating AI agent that works alongside more than 60 pre-configured scientific skills and connectors covering genomics, proteomics, structural biology, cheminformatics, and single-cell analysis. A built-in reviewer agent also checks citations, calculations and figures, helping identify, and correct potential errors before publication.

The company said Claude Science generates not only research summaries but also reproducible scientific outputs such as figures, manuscripts, protein structures, genome browser tracks, and chemical structures. Every output includes the code, environment and message history used to create it, allowing researchers to validate and reproduce results later.

The platform can also manage computing jobs by connecting to researchers’ existing infrastructure, including local machines, remote servers and HPC clusters. It can submit large-scale analyses, monitor progress, and retrieve results without requiring users to manually configure computing environments.

According to the company, researchers have already used Claude Science for applications including single-cell RNA sequencing, CRISPR screen design, protein structure prediction and molecular epidemiology. The company said scientists at organisations such as the Allen Institute, Manifold Bio and the UCSF Brain Tumor Center reported significant reductions in research time using the platform.

Alongside the launch, Anthropic announced support for up to 50 AI for Science projects, offering up to $30,000 in Claude credits, while cloud computing platform Modal will provide up to $2,000 in compute credits for selected projects.

title: Genpact Launches AI Tool to Manage Deductions for Consumer Goods Companies
content:
The new venture targets rising power demand from AI data centres and semiconductor manufacturing.

What Actually Matters.

SK Inc and KKR have launched South Korea's largest renewable energy platform, valued at $1.3 billion.

The venture aims to meet increasing clean power demands from AI data centres and semiconductor manufacturing.

South Korea’s SK Inc and global investment firm KKR have signed definitive agreements to launch what they said will be South Korea’s largest renewable energy platform, valued at KRW 2 trillion ($1.3 billion). This comes as demand for clean power rises from AI data centres, semiconductor production facilities and other industrial users.

The companies announced the deal, wanting to bring together renewable energy assets from SK affiliates into a single platform spanning solar, onshore and offshore wind, and fuel cells.

The platform will start with about 1.7 GW of operating capacity and has a development pipeline that could increase total capacity to 10 GW. According to the companies, the platform would be capable of continuously powering 100 large-scale data centres, each with 100MW of capacity.

KKR will hold management control in the initial phase, while SK will participate as an equity investor and retain the option to pursue control rights in the future.

The companies said the platform will help South Korea address growing demand for clean electricity from AI infrastructure, semiconductor manufacturing and other energy-intensive industries.

By combining renewable energy businesses from SK Innovation, SK ecoplant and SK eternix, the venture aims to integrate the value chain from project development and construction to operations and maintenance.

The platform will also manage renewable energy assets across solar, offshore wind, onshore wind and fuel cells. It excludes hydrogen-based projects. The companies said the combined structure would improve operational efficiency and create economies of scale.

Keith Kim, Partner at KKR, said the venture would build on growing corporate demand for clean power in South Korea. “We are delighted to work alongside SK, a strategic partner with deep local operational capability,” Kim said. “Together, we are establishing a scaled renewable energy platform that can supply reliable clean power to Korea’s most demanding industrial users.”

The deal marks the latest collaboration between SK and KKR. SK said it is integrating its renewable energy businesses as part of a portfolio rebalancing effort designed to strengthen competitiveness and support long-term growth. The company said combining KKR’s capital with SK’s execution capabilities would help meet rising clean energy demand.

KKR is making the investment through its Asia-Pacific infrastructure strategy. The investment firm said it manages more than $100 billion in infrastructure assets globally and has invested over $31 billion in energy transition and renewable infrastructure projects since 2011. In Asia-Pacific, its renewable energy investments include India-based Serentica Renewables and Australian platforms CleanPeak Energy and Zenith Energy.

SK said the platform would strengthen the foundation of its renewable energy business, support future growth, and improve capital efficiency across its portfolio.

title: Only 14% of Indian Companies Have Full Visibility Into AI Agents: Okta Research
content:
Okta research shows most Indian organisations are preparing for AI-powered digital experiences, but only a small share have full visibility or control over AI agents operating in their systems.

What Actually Matters.

Indian organisations are moving towards AI-powered digital experiences but lack sufficient governance and control over AI agents.

While 73% of respondents feel prepared for AI integration, there is a significant gap in necessary controls for secure deployment.

While Indian organisations are working toward AI-powered digital experiences, many have not yet built the governance and access control systems needed to manage AI agents and non-human identities. The findings are based on polls conducted by cloud-based identity and access management platform Okta at Okta AI Identity Summits held in Mumbai and Bengaluru.

According to the research, close to 73% of respondents in India said their organisations were either very prepared or somewhat prepared to deliver AI-powered experiences across applications, customer services and AI agents.

Okta noted that this level of preparation contrasts with the governance measures currently in place, describing a gap between adoption plans and the controls needed to support secure deployment.

The polls found that only 14% of respondents had full visibility into all AI agents and non-human identities operating within their organisations. A further 17% said they could restrict or suspend an AI agent across all environments if required, while 51% said this was possible only in some cases.

On managing non-human identities such as service accounts, APIs and AI agents, 17% of respondents described themselves as very confident, and 53% said they were somewhat confident. When asked about access governance, only 14% said they were very confident that AI agents were limited to the systems and data required for their tasks.

"As organisations move beyond experimentation and begin embedding AI into business processes, governance becomes just as important as innovation," Matthew Graham, Chief Security Officer for APJ at Okta, said in a statement.

He added that organisations gaining the most value from AI would be those building visibility, accountability and security into their AI work from the start.

Graham also pointed to a shift in how organisations are approaching AI deployment. "The conversation around AI is shifting. The focus is no longer solely on adoption," he said.

He noted that organisations are now focused on governing AI consistently, managing access, and maintaining trust as AI agents become more embedded in daily operations, and said identity management has a role in addressing these questions.

Okta said the findings point to a need for stronger visibility, lifecycle management, and access governance as AI agents, service accounts, APIs and other non-human identities become more connected to enterprise systems and data in India.

Spense has raised $2.8 million, with plans to build an AI-based infrastructure and intelligence layer for asset-backed credit.

What Actually Matters.

Spense has secured $2.8 million in seed funding to develop AI-based infrastructure for asset-backed credit.

The funding round was led by Arkam Ventures and included several prominent angel investors.

Spense, a startup building banking infrastructure that combines agentic AI with asset-backed credit, has raised $2.8 million in a seed funding round led by Arkam Ventures.

Razorpay Ventures, GrowthCap Ventures, and Atrium Ventures also took part in the round, along with angel investors including Kunal Shah of CRED, Madhusudhan E of KreditBee, Ravishankar of Active.ai, Suresh Rayasam Venkatasubbaih of LinkedIn, and Sayandeb Banerjee of The Math Company.

The company will use the funds toward banking partnerships, product development, engineering and go-to-market hiring, and to launch Credit Line on UPI (CLOU). Spense also said the round supports its plan to build an AI-based infrastructure and intelligence layer for asset-backed credit.

Founded by Pawan Kumar and Srinivas Krishnamurthy, Spense lets banks launch credit cards and credit lines backed by customer assets such as fixed deposits, mutual funds, equities, bonds, invoices and property, without replacing existing banking systems.

The platform connects to core banking, deposit, and card management systems, and uses AI agents to handle onboarding, servicing, collections, and customer support—tasks the company says have traditionally required manual operations teams.

Spense currently works with seven banks in India, including one large public sector bank, along with a number of fintech distribution partners. The company said its platform supports more than 200,000 active cards and issues over 40,000 cards a month, which it estimates represents close to 8% of India's monthly credit card issuance.

Pawan Kumar, Co-founder and CEO of Spense, described the credit gap in India as a matter of infrastructure rather than risk. He added that India has assets but lacks the infrastructure to convert them into usable credit, and said access to credit should follow from asset ownership.

Srinivas Krishnamurthy, Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, linked the company's approach to a broader shift in banking technology. "For decades, banks digitised accounts, payments and transactions. The next phase of banking is the digitisation of collateral itself," he said.

He said that as assets become programmable and AI becomes reliable for operations, banks will be able to scale credit services further, changing how institutions originate and manage credit.

Bala Srinivasa, Managing Director at Arkam Ventures, added, "We backed Pawan and Srinivas because we believe Spense is building foundational infrastructure for the next era of credit in India."

He added that as lending shifts toward asset-backed models, platforms such as Spense will help financial institutions scale while expanding access to formal credit.

Spense said its longer-term aim is to let banks offer credit products against a wider range of assets, including fixed deposits, investments, and business receivables.

title: Razorpay Partners With NPCI Bharat BillPay to Launch Banking Connect for NetBanking
content:
The solution aims to simplify NetBanking for businesses and consumers, with support from banks including SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank.

What Actually Matters.

Razorpay has partnered with NPCI Bharat BillPay to enhance NetBanking for mobile payments in India.

The solution aims to streamline high-value transactions across various sectors, reducing operational complexities for businesses.

Razorpay on July 1 announced that it has partnered with NPCI Bharat BillPay Limited (NBBL), a subsidiary of the National Payments Corporation of India, to join Banking Connect. The companies describe the solution as an attempt to update NetBanking for mobile-first payments across India.

According to Razorpay, NetBanking remains widely used for high-value transactions in sectors such as financial services, lending, education and government.

The company said that offering NetBanking at scale has typically required businesses to manage separate integrations with individual banks, along with settlement and reconciliation processes, adding operational work as businesses expand.

Razorpay also said that many NetBanking transactions still involve several steps, including redirects and repeated entry of banking credentials, which can add time to the payment process compared with other digital payment methods.

Through Banking Connect, Razorpay said businesses can access multiple banks through a single integration, rather than connecting to each bank separately. The company said the solution supports payment journeys through banking apps, intent and QR-based flows, and centralises settlement and reconciliation processes.

Razorpay said the feature is available through its existing checkout system, without requiring further integration work from businesses already using its platform.

Arif Khan, Chief Information Officer at Razorpay Technologies Private Limited, referred to the RBI’s Annual Report for 2025 in commenting on the initiative. “As per RBI’s Annual Report ’25, India is today the global leader in real-time digital payments," he said.

He added that the next phase of innovation involves extending the same speed and reliability standards to NetBanking through Banking Connect.

Noopur Chaturvedi, Managing Director and CEO of NPCI Bharat BillPay Limited, described the aim behind the initiative. “Our focus at NBBL is to build interoperable, future-ready payment infrastructure that improves experiences for both businesses and consumers,” she said.

She added that the partnership with Razorpay would help expand the Banking Connect ecosystem and support wider adoption of updated NetBanking methods.

Banking Connect is currently supported by State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Federal Bank, AU Small Finance Bank and YES Bank. Razorpay said further banks are expected to join the ecosystem over time.

title: Keysight, WIN Semiconductors Launch Workflow for Faster RF Component Development
content:
The companies will target component development for 5G, satellite and defence applications.

What Actually Matters.

Keysight and WIN Semiconductors have launched a workflow for faster RF component development targeting 5G, satellite, and defence applications.

The workflow enhances first-pass tapeout success and reduces fabrication risks for high-frequency RF components.

Keysight Technologies and WIN Semiconductors have launched a joint monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) design workflow. This is to help gallium nitride (GaN) MMIC design houses achieve first-pass tapeout success and reduce fabrication risk for high-frequency radio-frequency (RF) components.

The companies announced the workflow, targeting developers building products for 5G base stations, Wi-Fi access points, satellite payloads and defence radar systems.

It combines on-chip multi-domain simulation, 3D layout verification and off-chip MMIC evaluation board design within a single environment. It also automates simulation, optimisation and verification processes before designs are sent to foundries for fabrication, addressing delays and costs associated with failed tapeouts that often require additional manufacturing runs.

The companies said the workflow allows engineers to design and optimise both on-chip and off-chip components. This includes the MMIC, packaging, printed circuit board (PCB) and test connectors. The approach aims to help designers verify performance before fabrication and demonstrate results on physical evaluation boards, a key requirement for customers before committing to purchases.

The workflow integrates WIN Semiconductors’ NP 120P GaN Process Design Kit (PDK) with Keysight’s Advanced Design System (ADS) and RF Circuit Simulation Professional tools. The integration provides designers with access to process models and layout rules while automating design verification steps required for tapeout.

Richard Kuo, Director of Design Service at WIN Semiconductors, said the collaboration delivered “a comprehensive verification solution that streamlined the customer’s design flow and accelerated the time-to-market for advanced RF products with greater confidence and reliability.”

The announcement comes as demand for GaN-based RF devices grows across telecommunications, satellite communications and defence sectors. According to the companies, the global GaN RF device market is projected to reach $2.77 billion by 2031, increasing pressure on MMIC design houses to validate performance and shorten development cycles.

Nilesh Kamdar, General Manager for EDA and Design Engineering Software at Keysight, said the combined offering gives designers “a single path from chip design through evaluation board” and enables them to “prove full system performance before fabrication, giving their customers the confidence to commit.”

title: Hexaware Launches Agentic AI Platform for Enterprise IT Operations
content:
The Tensai for Reasoning Ops platform uses AI agents to analyse operational data, recommend actions and help enterprises shift from reactive IT support to preventive operations.

What Actually Matters.

Hexaware has introduced the Tensai for Reasoning Ops platform to enhance enterprise IT operations through AI-driven analysis.

The platform employs AI agents to analyse operational data and recommend actions, shifting from reactive to preventive IT support.

Hexaware Technologies has launched Tensai for Reasoning Ops, an agentic AI platform designed for enterprise IT operations, as the mid-tier IT services company looks to deepen its artificial intelligence offerings for infrastructure management.

The platform, now generally available to mid-to-large enterprises, deploys AI agents that analyse live operational signals, enterprise data and system dependencies to recommend evidence-backed actions.

Human operators remain responsible for validating and executing the recommendations, the company said.

The launch comes as IT services companies increasingly embed generative and agentic AI capabilities into managed services and IT operations, aiming to automate routine tasks, improve service quality and reduce operational costs.

According to Hexaware, the platform is designed to move enterprises beyond traditional automation based on scripts and predefined workflows by enabling AI agents to reason across operational signals, configuration data, change records and infrastructure dependencies before making recommendations.

The company said the system follows an evidence-first approach, where actions are recommended only when supported by operational context and policy checks.

Hexaware said the platform is benchmarked against customers’ pre-AI operating baselines and is expected to deliver 25-40% faster mean time to resolution, reduce manual intervention by 35-45%, lower cost-to-serve by 10-18%, improve service-level agreement performance and user experience by 10-20%, and reduce incident demand by 5-12%.

It added that actual outcomes will vary depending on customer environments and will be validated using customer-specific scorecards.

“With Tensai for Reasoning Ops, we’re helping enterprises move from reactive support to more autonomous, self-healing IT operations. The platform brings reasoning, evidence, and governance into operational decisions, helping clients reduce manual intervention, improve SLA reliability, and build a stronger path toward preventive operations,” R Srikrishna, CEO and Executive Director, Hexaware, said in a statement.

title: Meituan Open-Sources LongCat-2.0 Model Trained Entirely on Chinese AI Chips
content:
The model supports a one-million-token context window and introduces a new sparse attention architecture for coding and agentic workloads.

Chinese technology company Meituan has open-sourced LongCat-2.0, a 1.6 trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) large language model. The company says the model was trained and deployed entirely on domestically developed AI chips, underscoring the country's efforts to build AI infrastructure independent of NVIDIA hardware.

LongCat-2.0 is available to download on GitHub and Hugging Face, along with API access for developers.

According to Meituan, LongCat-2.0 matches or exceeds proprietary models such as GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus on several coding and agent benchmarks. These claims have not yet been independently verified.

“Both the full training run and the large-scale deployment are built entirely on AI ASIC superpods,” the company announced. Pretraining spans millions of accelerator-days across more than 35 trillion tokens, with no rollbacks or irrecoverable loss spikes.

The release comes as Chinese AI companies increasingly shift toward homegrown chips following US export restrictions on advanced AI chips. While companies such as DeepSeek have previously used domestic hardware primarily for inference, Meituan claims LongCat-2.0 is the first trillion-parameter model to complete both pre-training and inference entirely on Chinese AI hardware.

It further said LongCat-2.0 activates around 48 billion parameters per token and was pretrained on more than 35 trillion tokens across millions of accelerator-days using AI ASIC superpods.

LongCat-2.0 supports a native one-million-token context window and introduces LongCat Sparse Attention (LSA), an updated sparse attention mechanism that combines streaming-aware, cross-layer and hierarchical indexing to reduce long-context inference costs.

The model also incorporates an N-gram Embedding module, which expands the embedding space by nearly 100 times while accounting for less than 10% of the model's total parameters.

To support the model’s scale, Meituan said it trained LongCat-2.0 on more than 50,000 AI ASICs using a six-dimensional parallelism strategy, deterministic training operators, memory optimisations, and fault-recovery systems. The company said these optimisations improved training throughput by over 35% compared with a baseline implementation.

Meituan is positioning LongCat-2.0 as an agentic coding model. It said the model integrates with developer tools, including Claude Code, OpenClaw, and Hermes, for repository-level code editing, automated task execution, and software engineering workflows. The company also introduced three post-training expert groups focused on reasoning, agent execution and interaction quality.

title: Merck Opens AI-Focused Global Capability Centre in Bengaluru: Report
content:
The new Bengaluru facility will become a strategic hub for Merck’s AI, digital and enterprise technology operations, supporting global innovation efforts.

What Actually Matters.

Merck has opened a Global Capability Centre in Bengaluru to enhance its AI and digital technology operations.

The facility spans 17,000 square metres and will employ around 3,300 staff across various technology functions.

Pharmaceutical company Merck has launched a new Global Capability Centre (GCC) in Bengaluru’s Electronic City, bringing together its India technology and services operations under a single integrated campus as it deepens its focus on AI, digital transformation and enterprise innovation, according to The Economic Times GCC World.

Spread across 17,000 square metres, the facility will house around 3,300 employees working across data, digital, process and technology functions. The campus has been designed to foster collaboration and innovation, with dedicated innovation labs, neurodiversity zones and collaborative workspaces.

The Bengaluru centre will serve as a key node in Merck’s global digital operating model, with teams developing and managing enterprise-wide solutions that support research and development, manufacturing, supply chains, commercial operations and business functions across geographies.

At the core of the centre is Merck’s Digital Enterprise Solutions (DES) organisation, which oversees process optimisation, enterprise platforms, data and AI, technology infrastructure, hyperautomation and process excellence.

“The Merck Global Capability Centre is much more than an operational hub–it is a strategic engine for our digital enterprise. By bringing data, technology and process teams under one roof here, we are strengthening the foundation needed to scale innovation faster, improve agility and deliver greater impact across Merck's global businesses,” Alessandro De Luca, Head of Digital Enterprise Solutions and Group CIO at Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, said in a statement.

The new campus also houses business technology teams supporting Merck’s Life Science, Healthcare and Electronics divisions, creating a cross-functional centre of excellence spanning AI, analytics, automation and enterprise technology.

The company said India is now its fourth-largest workforce hub after Germany, the United States and China. Building on nearly six decades of presence in the country since 1967, the new centre is expected to play an increasingly important role in driving the company’s next phase of innovation and digital capability development.

title: Delhi to Roll Out AI-Enabled PUCC 3.0 Ahead of Winter Pollution Season: Report
content:
The company announced Voyage Context 4, Hybrid Search, and Native Reranking, saying the technologies work together to improve retrieval quality.

What Actually Matters.

MongoDB aims to upskill two million builders in India by 2030 through its MongoDB for Academia programme.

The company plans to partner with over 1,500 educational institutions and support 5,000 educators with training resources.

MongoDB on June 30 announced that it plans to upskill two million builders in India by 2030 through an expansion of its MongoDB for Academia programme, alongside announcing new AI retrieval capabilities for enterprises at its MongoDB.local Bengaluru event.

The company said it will partner with more than 1,500 educational institutions across India and provide training and curriculum support to 5,000 educators. It will also deepen its collaboration with the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) through a joint Virtual Internship Programme to help students build AI and database skills.

Since launching MongoDB for Academia in India in September 2023, the company said it has trained more than 650,000 students through partnerships with AICTE, SmartBridge, ICT Academy, and universities.

As part of the expansion, MongoDB will work with HCL GUVI to make its curriculum available in Kannada, Hindi, and Tamil. It is also partnering with the ICT Academy of Kerala (ICTAK) to bring training programmes to more than 100 institutions across the state.

The company said institutions including BITS, SRM Institute of Science and Technology, KL University Hyderabad, and Ramaiah Institute of Technology will integrate MongoDB and database concepts into their curricula.

“MongoDB’s founding mission was to make data incredibly easy for builders to work with,” said Raghu Viswanathan, Vice President, Education, Academia and Documentation at MongoDB.

“This mission is as important as ever because the hard part about building AI in production isn't the model. It’s the data layer underneath it.”

“That’s exactly why we're so committed to expanding modern database skills to be available in more languages and more regions so we can help India's next generation of great builders thrive in the AI era,” he added.

Dr Buddha Chandrasekhar, CEO of Anuvadini AI, Ministry of Education, and Chief Coordinating Officer at AICTE, said India needs developers with strong data skills to support AI adoption.

“In India, we have a massive opportunity with AI to transform our economy and the lives of our citizens. But to take advantage of it, our developers must have the right skills,” he said.

“While the technology is changing fast, the importance of strong data skills remains the constant foundation for any builder. We are excited to expand our partnership with MongoDB to ensure every Indian student has access to the tools they need to succeed in the AI era, regardless of what language they speak or where they live.”

Alongside the education initiative, MongoDB introduced new AI capabilities to improve retrieval accuracy and support enterprise deployments in regulated environments.

The company announced Voyage Context 4, Hybrid Search, and Native Reranking, saying the technologies work together to improve retrieval quality. According to MongoDB, Native Reranking improves retrieval quality by up to 30%, while the underlying Voyage AI models outperform Google and Cohere on the public Retrieval Embedding Benchmark leaderboard.

MongoDB also said Search and Vector Search are now generally available for MongoDB Enterprise Advanced and Community Edition, allowing enterprises to deploy the capabilities in on-premises, private cloud, and local environments.

“The biggest barrier to enterprise AI in production and at scale isn't the LLM. It's memory, retrieval, accuracy, and compliance,” said Ben Cefalo, Chief Product Officer, Core Products at MongoDB.

“Whether you’re running in the cloud, private cloud, or behind a firewall, MongoDB gives you the same production-grade retrieval capabilities wherever your data lives.”

The company also shared a customer example from Emergent Labs, an AI application development platform.

“MongoDB gives us the retrieval accuracy to keep agents working from the current state of the data, and that's what lets us run two million applications at scale,” said Mukund Jha, CEO of Emergent Labs.

MongoDB said it serves half of India’s top 100 listed companies by market capitalisation and more than 50 unicorn startups. The company has over 700 employees in India across Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Gurgaon, including engineering, consulting, finance, human resources, and go-to-market teams.

What Actually Matters.

It aims to eliminate fraudulent vehicle emission certificates through automated validation and data encryption.

The Centre is set to roll out a new-generation Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) system that uses AI, geotagging and automated validation to tighten vehicle emission testing and curb fraudulent certification practices, The Times of India (TOI) reported.

The upgraded PUCC 3.0 regime, expected to be launched before the onset of winter, will use an AI-enabled system to verify the physical presence of vehicles at testing centres, ensure live testing, confirm the correct placement of emission-measuring probes and upload data directly to a central database.

Delhi has around 900 PUC testing centres, while the National Capital Region (NCR) has nearly 4,000. Speaking at an event, Mahmood Ahmed, additional secretary in the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, said the new framework would make the emission testing process significantly more stringent.

According to officials, the system will automatically capture vehicle registration numbers, validate emission parameters and reject suspicious or invalid test records. All testing data will be encrypted end-to-end to reduce the scope for tampering.

During a speaking engagement, Mahmood Ahmed, an additional secretary in the Ministry of Road Transport, stated that the new PUCC framework would be significantly more rigorous, with all information encrypted end-to-end.

According to information received by TOI, the updated system will automatically record vehicle registration numbers and will feature automated verification of emission standards, along with the dismissal of questionable or invalid test results.

Ahmed said the government hopes to introduce the new system within the next few months. “We are hopeful of rolling out the PUCC 3.0 in the next couple of months and certainly before the onset of winter,” he said.

Explaining the changes, Ahmed added that the Centre was working on a notification that would take the pollution-control regime “to another stage wherein we would like to say and specify and hopefully ensure too that the vehicles are geotagged, meaning they are in and around the PUCC centre”.

He also highlighted gaps in the current system, noting that many vehicles obtain pollution certificates without physically visiting testing centres. “We would also like to ensure that the data is end-to-end encrypted. The probe is actually inside the tailpipe of the vehicle, and there is no manual feeding of data,” Ahmed said.

The proposed overhaul comes as authorities seek stronger enforcement mechanisms to curb vehicular emissions, a major contributor to Delhi's air pollution, particularly during the winter months.

title: CoreWeave Launches ARIA to Help Researchers Find Hidden Patterns in AI Experiments
content:
ARIA analyses thousands of experiment runs in minutes, surfaces hidden patterns and recommends improvements to accelerate AI innovation

What Actually Matters.

CoreWeave has launched ARIA, an AI research assistant to help teams analyse experiments and identify patterns quickly.

ARIA automates the analysis of thousands of experiment runs, providing actionable insights and recommendations for model improvements.

CoreWeave has launched ARIA (AI Research & Iteration Agent), a new AI research assistant designed to help AI teams analyse experiments, identify patterns, and improve models faster. The company announced that ARIA is now available in public preview within Weights & Biases (W&B), its machine learning development platform.

Built using W&B Weave, CoreWeave’s agent development platform, ARIA is designed to automate one of the most time-consuming parts of AI research - analysing thousands of experiment runs and turning them into actionable insights.

According to CoreWeave, AI researchers often spend hours manually creating dashboards, analysing results and comparing experiments before deciding what to test next. ARIA aims to remove that bottleneck by automatically reading experimental data, generating reports, creating visualisations and recommending next steps.

“Researchers are making rapid progress in model development, but their management tools have not kept pace,” said Chen Goldberg, Executive Vice President of Product and Engineering at CoreWeave. She described ARIA as an “always-on research collaborator” that helps turn experimental data into continuous improvements.

The agent can analyse thousands of experiment runs and tens of thousands of metrics within minutes. It also creates live dashboards, including heat maps, parameter comparison charts, and reports that automatically update as new experiments are added.

Unlike traditional AI assistants, ARIA enters every conversation with the entire project already loaded. It can analyse experiments across multiple projects and identify patterns that researchers might otherwise miss.

The company said ARIA was developed using insights gained from supporting some of the world’s largest AI training workloads through nearly one billion experiment runs tracked on Weights & Biases.

The company believes the future of AI development will depend not only on faster computing power but also on faster experimentation and iteration. By automating experiment analysis and surfacing insights in real time, CoreWeave hopes ARIA will help research teams build better AI models and agents more efficiently.

title: Gujarat Taps IBM, IAIRO to establish Industrial AI Centre of Excellence
content:
Envisioned as a ‘living lab’, the Industrial AI CoE will support the development, testing, and adoption of industrial AI applications

What Actually Matters.

The Gujarat government, IBM, and IAIRO are collaborating to establish an Industrial AI Centre of Excellence.

The Centre aims to support AI application development in sectors like manufacturing, energy, and supply chains.

The Gujarat government, the Indian AI Research Organisation (IAIRO), and IBM plan to establish an Industrial Artificial Intelligence Centre of Excellence (Industrial AI CoE) in Gujarat to accelerate Industrial AI innovation, build AI talent, and strengthen India's sovereign AI ecosystem.

The proposed CoE will focus on advancing the application of AI across asset-intensive industries such as manufacturing, energy, utilities, and supply chains. Envisioned as a ‘living lab’, the Industrial AI CoE will support the development, testing, and adoption of industrial AI applications while promoting indigenous sovereign AI technologies.

The initiative aligns with Gujarat's ambition to position itself as a leading destination for Industrial AI by fostering innovation, research, and industry collaboration.

Beyond technology development, the Industrial AI CoE is expected to develop the ecosystem through pilot projects, technology demonstrations, workshops, conferences, and stakeholder engagements connecting industry, academia, startups, and government.

The Centre will also focus on developing AI talent through academic collaborations, research initiatives, hackathons, certification programmes, and training in emerging AI technologies.

Additionally, it aims to contribute to the development of AI frameworks, reference architectures, standards, and best practices to support responsible and scalable AI adoption across industries.

As part of the collaboration, IBM and IAIRO will serve as technical and strategic advisors to the Department of Science and Technology in the Gujarat government.

Their role will include providing expertise in industrial AI, sovereign AI technologies, enterprise asset management platforms, and best practices to accelerate AI adoption across industrial sectors.

Highlighting the importance of combining research with industrial deployment, Amit Sheth, Founding Director, Indian AI Research Organisation, said in a statement, “The next generation of industrial systems will require AI that combines learning with domain knowledge, human expertise, and trust. Translating these capabilities into real-world impact requires an ecosystem where research, policy, and enterprise innovation evolve together, and Gujarat's industrial leadership provides a strong foundation for that transformation. This initiative will help advance indigenous innovation, nurture world-class talent, and translate frontier research into real-world impact, strengthening India's leadership in trustworthy Industrial AI in collaboration with the Government of Gujarat and IBM."

Emphasising the need for enterprise-ready AI infrastructure, Sriram Raghavan, General Manager, IBM Software, India and Software Innovation Lab, said, "Realising this opportunity requires not only advanced AI models, but also access to real-time and historical data, enterprise-ready platforms, governance, and ecosystem partnerships. We look forward to collaborating with the Government of Gujarat and IAIRO to help create a platform that fosters innovation, develops skills, and accelerates the adoption of sovereign AI technologies."

The announcement comes as Indian states increasingly invest in AI infrastructure and innovation ecosystems to drive industrial competitiveness, support digital transformation, and position themselves as global hubs for next-generation technologies.

What Actually Matters.

Kapture CX has secured $10 million in pre-Series B funding, led by Bajaj Finserv Ventures.

The funding will facilitate Kapture's global market expansion and enhance research and development efforts.

Kapture CX, a comprehensive agentic AI platform tailored for specific industries, has successfully completed its $10 million pre-Series B funding round led by Bajaj Finserv Ventures (BFSV). Existing investors, Cactus Partners and India Alternatives, also participated in this round.

The new funding will drive Kapture’s expansion into global markets and support ongoing R&D investments. The company targets a fivefold revenue growth in the coming years to capitalise on opportunities in today’s enterprise landscape.

Kapture's deep-tech capabilities, including model training, combined with its strong understanding of enterprise workflows and robust partner ecosystem, position the company strongly within the evolving AI landscape."

Kapture streamlines the entire technology stack, including models, the agentic layer, and the user interface, enabling enterprises to implement AI easily without the hassles of multiple providers. The platform is specialised and leverages advanced technology to customise solutions for various industries, effectively transforming complex enterprise operations.

"Since our Series A round in 2023, Kapture has grown 4x and achieved what remains rare in the AI economy - profitability. Having an AI-first organisation like Bajaj Finserv Ventures lead this round is powerful validation of our value proposition," Sheshgiri Kamath, Co-founder and CEO of Kapture CX, added.

According to the company, Kapture’s platform is currently trusted by more than 1,000 enterprises in 18 different countries, including major players like Bajaj Finance, as well as several companies within the Tata Group and Reliance Group.

title: Palantir and NVIDIA Bring Nemotron Models to Sovereign AI Deployments
content:
The platform allows organisations to train, deploy and improve open models while retaining control over their data, intellectual property and AI systems.

What Actually Matters.

Palantir and NVIDIA have launched a joint initiative to deploy AI models in sovereign environments for US government agencies.

The platform allows organisations to train and enhance open models while maintaining control over their data and intellectual property.

Palantir Technologies has announced an initiative with NVIDIA to develop an AI engine that enables the deployment of NVIDIA’s Nemotron open models in sovereign environments, targeting US government agencies and operators of critical infrastructure.

The joint offering combines NVIDIA’s AI platform, including its compute infrastructure, AI ecosystem and Nemotron open models, with Palantir’s Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP), Foundry, Ontology and Apollo.

The companies said the platform allows organisations to train, deploy and improve open models while retaining control over their data, intellectual property and AI systems.

The platform includes capabilities such as explicit data authorisation, customer-specific isolation, secure perimeter enforcement, data portability, right to erasure and audit logs.

Customers will also be able to own and improve models tailored to their operational requirements by using telemetry, trace data and post-training feedback generated within their environments.

The companies said the offering enables US government agencies to deploy base and customised Nemotron models in classified, air-gapped and other sensitive environments. It also supports context engineering to optimise prompts and workflows, model engineering to modify model weights using proprietary data, and enterprise deployment through NVIDIA AI Enterprise software and NVIDIA NIM microservices.

“Combining Palantir infrastructure with NVIDIA’s AI and Nemotron models will allow the U.S. government to unleash the full power of LLMs while removing the underlying security risks and rational concerns around proprietary insights migrating into the weights of closed models,” said Alex Karp, Co-founder and CEO of Palantir. “Moreover, many of our US clients are already using these models, including multiple supporting critical US infrastructure — both private and public — and this will facilitate their radical expansion.”

NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang said open-source AI is becoming increasingly important for national security and public safety.

“Open source AI is foundational to national security, public safety and U.S. technology leadership,” Huang said. “Palantir's Nemotron-powered intelligent engine shows how open models can strengthen America’s leadership in AI — giving U.S. government agencies a secure, customisable and fully controlled foundation to build mission-critical AI systems in support of national security.”

The announcement builds on the companies’ previously announced Sovereign AI Operating System Reference Architecture, which is intended to help governments deploy and manage AI systems within their own infrastructure.

title: Indian IT Wants to Break From Its US Addiction. But It's Harder Than It Looks
content:
The Medical Data Toolkit converts unstructured medical records into standardised digital health data, while Gemma 4 helps generate user health profiles in the Aarogya Setu 2.0 app.

What Actually Matters.

Google's Gemma 4 and Medical Data Toolkit enhance the Aarogya Setu 2.0 app by creating digital health profiles from unstructured medical records.

The Medical Data Toolkit enables extraction of information from various medical reports, providing users with a consolidated view of their health history.

Google said the National Health Authority (NHA) has adopted its Gemma 4 AI model and Medical Data Toolkit in the newly launched Aarogya Setu 2.0 app, allowing users to generate digital health profiles from unstructured medical records.

The search giant said that NHA is using Google’s Medical Data Toolkit alongside Gemma 4 to extract information from medical reports, including text and images, and present users with a consolidated view of their health history within the app.

The integration is part of a broader collaboration between Google and the NHA to strengthen India's digital public infrastructure for healthcare.

Google also announced that it has open-sourced the Medical Data Toolkit, allowing developers and healthcare organisations to use it at no cost.

“We are pleased that our AI capabilities are helping strengthen the country's digital health stack and Digital Public Infrastructure. These tools are designed to empower Indians to more closely control their health journeys, while the release of the toolkit reduces barriers to entry for health tech innovation," said Preeti Lobana, Vice President and Country Manager, Google India.

According to Google, the toolkit identifies the type of medical record and extracts information such as laboratory test names, methods and results. The extracted data is then mapped into Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR), a global standard for exchanging healthcare information across systems.

The company said the toolkit currently supports common health records, including laboratory reports and observations, with plans for developers to build applications that digitise and standardise legacy medical records while complying with interoperability standards under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM).

Google said the Medical Data Toolkit uses a rules-based system to structure extracted information, while all health records and related information remain under the user's control within the Aarogya Setu 2.0 app.

Gemma 4, Google’s open AI model launched in April 2026, is used alongside the toolkit to process unstructured health records and help generate individual health profiles.
