title: Infosys Expands AI-Led IT Collaboration with Semiconductor Giant GlobalFoundries
content:
The multi-year mandate will see Infosys manage applications, infrastructure and service desk operations for the semiconductor manufacturer.

What Actually Matters.

Infosys has secured a multi-year mandate to manage GlobalFoundries' enterprise IT operations, enhancing their partnership.

The agreement focuses on transitioning GlobalFoundries' IT environment to a managed services model that leverages AI and automation.

IT services major Infosys has expanded its partnership with semiconductor manufacturer GlobalFoundries, securing a multi-year mandate to manage the company's enterprise IT operation, as enterprise clients increasingly turn to artificial intelligence and automation to modernise technology infrastructure.

Under the agreement, Infosys will oversee GlobalFoundries' end-to-end application, infrastructure, data, and service desk operations, the company said in a statement.

The expanded engagement deepens Infosys' relationship with GlobalFoundries, where it has already been serving as a technology provider. The latest mandate shifts the semiconductor company's IT environment towards a managed services model that relies on AI and automation to improve operational efficiency and support functions.

GlobalFoundries, one of the world's largest contract semiconductor manufacturers, said the renewed partnership would support its broader digital transformation efforts and help improve the resilience and efficiency of its IT operations.

“The renewed collaboration marks a significant step forward in GF’s journey to modernise IT operations and achieve higher levels of efficiency, resilience and user experience,” Vishal Mehra, Chief Information Officer, GlobalFoundries, said in a statement.

For Infosys, the engagement strengthens its presence in the semiconductor sector, a vertical that has attracted growing attention from technology services companies as chipmakers ramp up investments in digital infrastructure and AI capabilities.

“By combining our deep domain expertise, AI capabilities and an outcome-based operating model, we will help GF reduce incidents, improve end-user experiences, and sustainably lower TCO over the long term. Infosys will unlock AI value at scale to play a central role in driving intelligent operations, helping GF transition from reactive IT management to predictive and autonomous service delivery,” said Anand Swaminathan, Executive Vice President and Global Industry Leader for Communications, Media & Technology, Infosys.

title: Why Indian Students No Longer Have to Choose Between a Global Degree and Staying Home
content:
Aampe's AI technology will be integrated into MoEngage's platform, enabling brands to implement seamless, individual-level decision-making.

What Actually Matters.

MoEngage has acquired Aampe, integrating its AI technology to enhance personalised marketing features.

Aampe's founding members will join MoEngage to lead agentic decision-making projects.

Bengaluru-based customer engagement SaaS company MoEngage has acquired the San Francisco-based AI startup Aampe in a cash-only transaction, integrating Aampe’s AI decision-making technology into its platform to enhance its personalised marketing features. The company has not disclosed the transaction value.

With this acquisition, Aampe’s founding members, Paul Meinshausen, Schaun Wheeler, and Sami Abboud, will join MoEngage to spearhead its agentic decisioning projects. Aampe will continue to serve its current clients while leveraging the enhanced engineering, data science, and customer support resources MoEngage offers.

Aampe’s agents are actively employed by prominent consumer brands such as Grab, Swiggy, ZenBusiness, and Taxfix. The platform operates hundreds of millions of dedicated AI agents at scale and handles over 200 billion decisions each week.

“We built Aampe on one conviction: one agent per user, not one model per segment,” Paul Meinshausen, Co-Founder and CEO, Aampe, said in a statement. “A per-user agent builds a persistent and continuously evolving understanding of each individual customer, their rhythm, their content preferences, and what actually moves them to act. MoEngage gives us the infrastructure, channel depth, and customer relationships to make that the default for every brand, not the exception.”

This acquisition enables what MoEngage describes as a 'Start Anywhere' strategy, the company said. B2C brands can integrate Aampe’s per-user agents into their existing customer engagement or marketing automation systems, and MoEngage clients will receive Aampe’s services directly, requiring no changes on their end. In both cases, agentic decision-making at the individual level becomes available for every brand.

Moreover, it brings together the AI Labs of both companies under a unified goal of developing the next generation of agentic marketing, providing Aampe’s research team with the context needed at production scale across MoEngage’s worldwide customer network to expedite the success of existing initiatives.

“Aampe has built something the rest of the market hasn’t cracked: a system that continuously optimises content, timing, channel, and frequency together at an individual level. What impressed me equally was the team behind the technology,” Raviteja Dodda, Co-Founder and CEO, MoEngage, added.

MoEngage’s Merlin AI platform focuses on AI-driven marketing, while Aampe delivers tailored decision-making for top consumer brands. Agents customise messages for individuals based on timing and channel, with marketers setting the guidelines and agents ensuring transparency.

The University of Southampton Delhi offers UGC-approved, world-class UK degrees locally, combining global academic standards with extensive industry employability.

What Actually Matters.

Indian students can now obtain world-class UK degrees locally through the University of Southampton Delhi.

The UoSD offers the same curriculum as its UK counterpart, ensuring academic standards are maintained.

Universities in India still route many students to choose between two imperfect options: stay close to home and compromise on global exposure, or go abroad and absorb the cost, distance, and uncertainty that come with it. For years, that trade-off has been accepted as a feature of the system. The University of Southampton Delhi (UoSD) is making a case that it does not have to be.

The University of Southampton, founded in 1862 and a founding member of the Russell Group, ranks 52nd in the world in TIME Magazine's World University Rankings 2026.

It is placed in the top 100 globally across 12 subjects and within the top 50 in three. Through its UGC-approved campus in Gurugram, Delhi NCR, Indian students can access that academic framework without leaving the country. It was the first international university to be approved by the UGC and open in India.

Bringing Global Academic Standards to India

The most obvious question about an India-based international campus is whether the degree carries the same weight as one earned abroad. At the University of Southampton Delhi, the answer is built into how the institution operates. Students follow the same curriculum as their peers at the University of Southampton, with programme design, assessment, examinations, and moderation governed by the same academic frameworks as at the UK campus. All degrees are awarded by the University of Southampton, with no distinction on the certificate.

The campus offers six undergraduate and four postgraduate programmes. At the undergraduate level, students can enrol in three-year degrees in BSc (Hons) Business Management, Accounting and Finance, Computer Science, Economics and Creative Computing, alongside BEng (Hons) Software Engineering.

Postgraduate offerings include MSc Finance, MSc International Management, MSc Economics and MSc Data Science, all one-year programmes. The recent additions for the 2026 intake include the STEM programmes and the MSc in Data Science.

Academic oversight is maintained through regular collaboration with UK-based faculty, who work alongside Delhi academics and conduct ongoing programme reviews. Faculty recruitment follows the same standards as Southampton, UK. Every PhD held by academic leadership was earned outside India, and three-quarters of university leadership, Heads of Programme and academics have taught or researched internationally.

The campus at International Tech Park in Gurugram is built around that model. Most of the infrastructure is standard for a university of this standing. What stands out is the Financial Lab equipped with Bloomberg Terminals, which gives students direct access to tools most graduates encounter for the first time only after joining a firm.

Building employability through industry and global exposure

Academic equivalence answers the credential question. The harder question is whether students graduate ready to use it. This is where the two halves of the University of Southampton Delhi proposition connect.

Students increasingly evaluate universities through career outcomes, and the University of Southampton Delhi has built employability into the structure of its programmes rather than treating it as an add-on.

Through the Successful Futures programme, every degree is mapped against a research-led framework of 14 skills that employers have identified as priorities.

The aim is to help students understand how academic learning translates into workplace value and to empower them to develop capabilities beyond their subject area. Students engage in case studies, industry projects, live business scenarios, internships, and assignments designed to reflect professional environments.

Career development begins in the first year with an onboarding Employability Week and continues through one-to-one mentoring, CV workshops, interview preparation and personalised career coaching.

University of Southampton Delhi has built engagement with organisations including Investec, Deloitte, L.E.K. Consulting, and Genpact, creating opportunities for internships, live projects and industry interaction. Global exposure is embedded in the curriculum through shared academic standards and internationally informed teaching, rather than being treated as a separate programme element.

In addition, selected undergraduate students can spend a semester at the University of Southampton during their second year, with further exchange pathways under development. Graduates from Delhi-based bachelor's programmes also have progression routes to postgraduate programmes at Southampton's campuses in India, Malaysia and the UK.

The university's alumni network spans more than 160 years and includes over 1,700 Indian graduates working across consulting, technology, finance, policy, academia and entrepreneurship. Alumni are associated with organisations including Deloitte, Airbus, Rolls-Royce, Shell, Boeing, GSK, Merck & Co. and Grant Thornton.

India's National Education Policy opened the door for international universities to establish campuses in the country, and the UGC formalised that framework in 2023.

University of Southampton Delhi, the first international university to open a comprehensive campus in India under those regulations, is less a product of that policy moment than a test of it. Whether the model holds up over the next few graduating cohorts will matter as much to students weighing this option as any ranking.

title: Vishal Sikka Launches AI Startup Hang Ten Systems, Raises $32 Mn in Seed Funding
content:
The startup is working with companies such as Siemens Gamesa and Fresenius to help enterprises build and run software using AI.

What Actually Matters.

Vishal Sikka has launched Hang Ten Systems, an enterprise AI services startup focusing on AI deployment in business-critical software.

The startup raised $32 million in seed funding to enhance its team and expand its enterprise AI services.

Former Infosys CEO Vishal Sikka has launched Hang Ten Systems, an enterprise AI services startup that aims to help large organisations deploy AI in business-critical software and operations.

The Palo Alto-based company has also raised $32 million in seed funding, led by Mayfield with participation from Aramco Ventures and angel investors, to expand its team and scale its work with global enterprises.

The company said the new capital will be used to hire across engineering, delivery, sales, and leadership functions as it expands its enterprise AI services business.

Hang Ten focuses on helping enterprises deploy AI in business-critical software systems. The company says many organisations have struggled to translate AI investments into measurable outcomes, often taking on additional costs and risks without seeing significant benefits.

Hang Ten is targeting software that powers core business operations. The company argues that generative AI is changing how enterprise software is built and maintained, reducing the need for traditional customisation, integration, and testing processes.

Its approach combines agentic code generation, a reusable skills library, and domain expertise in areas including finance, human resources, enterprise transformations, and product development.

The company is already working with customers, including Siemens Gamesa Renewable Energy and Fresenius on AI-driven project delivery initiatives.

“Every single enterprise will be transformed by AI. A few are already reaping massive benefits, building in days what used to take years. But most are stuck at the starting line, or worse, and the gap is widening every day,” Sikka said.

“We are building Hang Ten to close that gap, and help enterprises ride the AI wave. We bring together the rarest combination — frontier AI expertise, decades of building the systems that enterprises actually run on, and the judgment to deliver real value when everything is changing at once.”

Sikka previously served as CEO of Infosys and was a member of SAP’s Executive Board, where he oversaw products and technology.

Mayfield Managing Partner Navin Chaddha said the firm backed Hang Ten because of Sikka’s experience leading large-scale technology organisations.

“Within a few years, the gap between enterprises that use AI to real advantage and those that don’t will define entire industries,” Chaddha said. “Hang Ten is focused on enterprise transformations to put companies on the right side of that line.”

Aramco Ventures CEO Mahdi Aladel said enterprise AI deployment is becoming one of the largest challenges facing businesses.

“Their combination of Frontier AI experience, decades of delivering enterprise solutions at scale, and deep enterprise relationships worldwide is rare, and is what it will take to deliver on the promise of Enterprise AI,” Aladel said.

Vinod Philip, CEO of Siemens Gamesa Renewable Energy, said enterprises are looking for guidance on AI adoption and operational improvement.

“We at SGRE are delighted to work with Hang Ten on several strategic initiatives,” Philip said.

title: OpenAI, Broadcom Unveil Custom Inference Chip Jalapeño for LLM Workloads
content:
OpenAI claims Jalapeño went from design to manufacturing tape-out in nine months.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI and Broadcom have introduced Jalapeño, a custom chip designed specifically for large language model inference.

Jalapeño is OpenAI's first in-house Intelligence Processor, developed to enhance the company's AI infrastructure.

OpenAI and Broadcom have unveiled Jalapeño, a custom AI accelerator built for large language model (LLM) inference. The chip is OpenAI’s first in-house Intelligence Processor and reflects the company’s effort to build more of the infrastructure behind its AI products.

The companies said the chip was designed specifically for LLM inference rather than being adapted from existing AI accelerators. Engineering samples are already running machine learning workloads in the lab, including GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark, with OpenAI claiming early tests indicate the chip delivers performance per watt above current state-of-the-art systems.

Jalapeño is the first product in a multi-generation compute platform being developed by OpenAI and Broadcom, with deployments planned at gigawatt-scale data centres beginning in 2026 alongside partners including Microsoft.

“The world is moving to a compute-powered economy,” said Greg Brockman, President and Co-founder of OpenAI. “Jalapeño is part of our long-term full-stack infrastructure strategy to make compute more abundant, resulting in AI which is faster, more reliable, more affordable for people and businesses, and can be used to solve more important problems.”

OpenAI said the chip was designed using insights from its model roadmap, serving systems, kernels and product requirements. Broadcom contributed silicon implementation and networking technologies, while Celestica worked on board, rack and system integration.

According to the companies, the architecture is intended to reduce data movement and better balance compute, memory and networking resources, allowing the hardware to operate closer to its theoretical performance limits.

“Jalapeño was designed from the ground up for LLM inference using detailed insights from our close collaboration with OpenAI researchers,” said Richard Ho, who leads OpenAI’s hardware program. “We optimised the architecture around the kernels, memory movement, networking, and serving patterns that matter most for frontier AI models.”

The announcement comes as AI companies seek alternatives to relying entirely on third-party accelerators for inference workloads. OpenAI said designing its own hardware allows it to optimise the stack across models, software, networking and infrastructure.

The company also claimed the accelerator moved from initial design to manufacturing tape-out in nine months, which it described as one of the fastest ASIC development cycles in advanced semiconductor development. OpenAI said its own AI models were used to accelerate parts of the chip design and optimisation process.

“The same models served to users are helping improve the infrastructure used to run future models,” the company said, adding that AI-assisted chip development could lower compute costs across the industry.

Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said the partnership extends beyond a single chip generation.

“Our collaboration with OpenAI represents a fundamental commitment to scaling the physical infrastructure required for the next decade of AI,” Tan said. “This is just the beginning of a multi-generation roadmap.”

OpenAI said improvements in inference efficiency could translate into faster ChatGPT responses, lower API costs, and more dependable access during periods of high demand. The company plans to share detailed technical performance data for Jalapeño in the coming months.

title: ‘AI Will Amplify, Not Replace Us,’ Says Infosys Chairman Nandan Nilekani
content:
At the company’s 45th annual general meeting, Nilekani argued that closing the gap between AI’s promise and its enterprise reality is exactly the work his firm was built to do.

What Actually Matters.

Nandan Nilekani emphasised that AI will enhance rather than replace companies like Infosys.

He highlighted the challenge of integrating AI into existing enterprise structures as the key focus for Infosys.

Speaking to shareholders at Infosys’s 45th Annual General Meeting on June 23, Nandan Nilekani, Chairman of India’s second largest IT services firm, said that AI will not replace companies like Infosys.

“It will amplify those who move with purpose and adapt with speed,” he added in his speech.

The argument Nilekani laid out is one that the industry has been reaching for but rarely articulated with this much confidence: that deploying artificial intelligence inside the world’s largest enterprises is not a software problem but an integration problem, and integration is precisely what firms like Infosys have spent decades learning to do.

The gap between what AI can do in a demonstration and what it can do inside a multinational corporation, like navigating legacy infrastructure, regulatory obligations, security requirements, and decades of accumulated technical debt, is, in his telling, real. And closing it is where the work is.

“Enterprise context is paramount,” he said. “Solutions must complement existing investments. They demand rigorous testing, resilient architecture, and foundational cybersecurity. Data governance must reflect an organisation’s own obligations, not the convenience of any external platform or provider.”

He called this the “AI deployment gap”, and framed it not as a headwind for Infosys but as its central commercial opportunity for the decade ahead.

According to him, Infosys is already working with 90% of its top 200 clients on their AI journeys. The company’s own estimate puts the addressable AI-first services market at $300 to $400 billion by 2030, a figure it believes it is positioned to capture through Infosys Topaz, its AI platform, and Infosys Cobalt, its cloud capability.

Nilekani also identified a second dividend from the AI wave: it has made legacy modernisation urgent in a way that nothing else has. Companies that spent years deferring overhauls of their core systems are now moving, because those systems are increasingly the bottleneck to deploying AI at scale.

“The AI revolution has made legacy modernisation urgent in a way nothing else has, and clients are moving to retire the technical debt accumulated over decades,” he said.

The workforce picture he painted was one of redeployment rather than reduction. Infosys recruited more than 20,000 college graduates in the last fiscal year and ended it with a headcount of more than 3,25,000, and employees freed by productivity gains, he said, are being moved toward new areas of growth.

“It is said that to anticipate the future, we should skate to where the puck is going. In this case, the puck is coming to where we have already positioned ourselves,” Nilekani said.

Whether that confidence proves warranted will depend on how fast clients move and how quickly competitors make the same argument. The speech, however, reflected a broader Infosys argument that is gaining traction across the Indian IT industry: that AI is not a substitute for large-scale enterprise technology partners, but rather a force multiplier for those with the implementation depth, client trust, and institutional knowledge to deploy it responsibly.

title: In a First, an AI Lawyer Wins a Court Case, Recovers £7,000
content:
In a global legal first, AI Law Firm Garfield AI secured a £7,000 court victory for a freelancer, pairing AI preparation with human courtroom advocacy.

What Actually Matters.

Garfield AI achieved a historic court victory, marking the first successful use of an AI lawyer in a trial.

The case involved a freelancer recovering £7,000 for unpaid work, highlighting the accessibility of legal support via AI.

A British AI law firm, Garfield AI, has won in an English court, marking what is considered the first instance of a trial won with the assistance of an AI lawyer.

Tamires Camal Taquidir, a freelance HR consultant, paid Garfield AI around £400 to draft a legal letter and initiate court proceedings concerning an unpaid debt of £7,000.

“I was owed money for work I had done, but it felt like the process of recovering it could be too stressful, expensive and time-consuming. Garfield made it possible for me to pursue the claim and keep going. When the counterclaim was brought, it was intended to intimidate me, but I knew I had accessible, cost-effective, and competent support. I'm delighted by the result,” Taquidir told The Financial Times.

Philip Young, CEO and Co-founder of Garfield, described it as a "historic moment" for access to justice and noted that many small businesses have had to forgo debts due to the high cost of litigation relative to the potential recovery. “Here, a freelancer who had done the work and not been paid was able to take her case all the way to trial, resist a counterclaim, and win,” he said.

Garfield can handle claims ranging from £30 to £10,000 and prepares the case, subsequently enlisting a human barrister to represent the client in court.

“AI did not replace the judge, the barrister or the legal system. What it did was make the process more accessible, more efficient, and more affordable, so that a meritorious claimant could get to the point where her case could be heard, and justice could be done,” Young added.

While the AI lawyer automated the document-heavy preparation stages, the firm integrated human expertise for oral presentation. Shortly before the trial, Garfield AI instructed Dominic Li, a junior barrister from One Essex Court, to represent Taquidir in front of the judge.

It produced four witness statements and compiled a set of documents for the three-hour trial held at Wandsworth County Court on May 14. The court ruled in favour of Taquidir and awarded her the outstanding amount.

Li, barrister for the claimant, told FT, “This was a hard-fought small claim that turned on the existence and terms of an oral agreement. Garfield AI's preparation helped ensure the case was presented clearly and efficiently, while the advocacy at trial remained essential and a fundamentally human exercise.”

title: Adani Targets 3 GW Data Centre Capacity by 2030, Bets on Nuclear Power
content:
Gautam Adani says infrastructure and intelligence will be the twin pillars of growth as the group expands its digital infrastructure footprint.

What Actually Matters.

Adani Group aims for a significant expansion in digital infrastructure, targeting 3 GW data centre capacity by 2030.

Gautam Adani emphasises the integration of AI and infrastructure as core components of the group's growth strategy.

Adani Targets 3 GW Data Centre Capacity by 2030, Bets on Nuclear Power

Adani Group Chairman Gautam Adani has outlined an ambitious digital infrastructure roadmap, positioning AI and data centres as critical pillars of the conglomerate's next phase of growth.

Addressing shareholders at the group's annual general meeting (AGM), Adani said the conglomerate's strategy would be driven by the twin themes of "accelerating infrastructure" and "leveraging intelligence," reflecting a broader shift towards integrating AI capabilities across its businesses.

As part of that vision, Adani said the group's data centre business is targeting 3 GW of capacity by 2030, making it one of the largest digital infrastructure ambitions in the country. He highlighted a major agreement with Google for a gigawatt-scale data centre project in Visakhapatnam, describing digital infrastructure as a key foundation for India's AI-led growth.

He said the group sees AI-driven intelligence and physical infrastructure as the twin engines powering India's future competitiveness and sovereignty. The strategy seeks to combine the group's strengths across energy, logistics, transport, and industrial infrastructure with emerging digital infrastructure requirements.

Adani also underscored the growing link between energy and computing infrastructure. Announcing the group's entry into the nuclear power sector through Adani Atomic Energy, he said the company aims to develop 10 GW of nuclear capacity by 2035 through renewable energy.

Beyond infrastructure investments, Adani said the group is restructuring itself for the AI era through a three-layer organisational model aimed at faster decision-making and execution. He added that the company has an industrialised workforce training program that delivers thousands of training hours to strengthen workforce readiness for future technologies.

title: Los Angeles Opens a Museum to AI, Features AI-Powered Exhibition on Environment
content:
Founded by media artist Refik Anadol, DATALAND combines artificial intelligence, sound, scent, and wearable technology to create immersive experiences that challenge traditional ideas of art and authorship.

What Actually Matters.

Los Angeles now hosts the world's first museum solely dedicated to AI-generated art, called DATALAND.

DATALAND combines AI, sound, scent, and wearable technology to create immersive, evolving artistic experiences.

Los Angeles has become home to what is being described as the world’s first museum dedicated entirely to AI-generated art.

DATALAND, founded by Turkish-American media artist Refik Anadol and cultural researcher Efsun Erkılıç officially opened at The Grand LA in downtown Los Angeles. The museum aims to explore how artificial intelligence, environmental data, and human interaction can come together to create immersive artistic experiences.

Unlike traditional museums that display static artworks, DATALAND uses generative AI, large-scale projections, sound, scent, and visitor-responsive technology to create exhibitions that continuously evolve.

The museum’s debut exhibition, ‘Machine Dreams: Rainforest’, transforms ecological data collected from rainforests into dynamic visual and sensory experiences. Visitors move through five interconnected gallery spaces featuring AI-generated imagery, rainforest sounds, interactive displays, and environmental storytelling.

The museum featured an exhibition powered by Refik Anadol Studio’s Large Nature Model (LNM), an AI model trained on permission-based datasets related to plants, animals, and ecosystems. The experience also incorporates real-time environmental signals from rainforest locations including data on humidity, soil moisture, and light conditions.

A key feature of the museum is its wearable technology system called ‘Data. Link’. Visitors are provided with wrist-worn devices and scent-enabled neckbands that anonymously respond to movement and behavioural signals allowing the exhibition to adapt in real time based on audience interactions.

The opening of DATALAND comes at a time when debates around AI-generated art, copyright, authorship and creative labour are becoming increasingly prominent across the art world.

Anadol said in a statement, “LA was the ideal location for the project due to its long-standing role as a centre for innovation across art, cinema, music and technology.”

“LA is the perfect city to launch DATALAND, a forward-thinking, revolutionary museum in support of the fields to which I have dedicated my career: art, science, technology and AI research,” he added.

The museum has also attracted attention across social media platforms. On LinkedIn, several technology and design professionals praised the project.

David Sheldon-Hicks, Founder of design agency Territory Studio, congratulated Anadol on the launch and described DATALAND as an “incredible project.” Beauty giant L’Oréal, which partnered with the museum on its scent-based experiences, said the initiative could help “redefine how we experience digital art.”

Reactions on X and Reddit, however, have been more mixed. While many users shared videos of the immersive installations and called the museum a glimpse into the future of art and entertainment, others questioned whether AI-generated works belong in museums and raised concerns about copyright, originality, and the growing influence of artificial intelligence in creative industries.

Aampe's AI technology will be integrated into MoEngage's platform, enabling brands to implement seamless, individual-level decision-making.

What Actually Matters.

MoEngage has acquired Aampe, integrating its AI technology to enhance personalised marketing features.

Aampe's founding members will join MoEngage to lead agentic decision-making projects.

Bengaluru-based customer engagement SaaS company MoEngage has acquired the San Francisco-based AI startup Aampe in a cash-only transaction, integrating Aampe’s AI decision-making technology into its platform to enhance its personalised marketing features. The company has not disclosed the transaction value.

With this acquisition, Aampe’s founding members, Paul Meinshausen, Schaun Wheeler, and Sami Abboud, will join MoEngage to spearhead its agentic decisioning projects. Aampe will continue to serve its current clients while leveraging the enhanced engineering, data science, and customer support resources MoEngage offers.

Aampe’s agents are actively employed by prominent consumer brands such as Grab, Swiggy, ZenBusiness, and Taxfix. The platform operates hundreds of millions of dedicated AI agents at scale and handles over 200 billion decisions each week.

“We built Aampe on one conviction: one agent per user, not one model per segment,” Paul Meinshausen, Co-Founder and CEO, Aampe, said in a statement. “A per-user agent builds a persistent and continuously evolving understanding of each individual customer, their rhythm, their content preferences, and what actually moves them to act. MoEngage gives us the infrastructure, channel depth, and customer relationships to make that the default for every brand, not the exception.”

This acquisition enables what MoEngage describes as a 'Start Anywhere' strategy, the company said. B2C brands can integrate Aampe’s per-user agents into their existing customer engagement or marketing automation systems, and MoEngage clients will receive Aampe’s services directly, requiring no changes on their end. In both cases, agentic decision-making at the individual level becomes available for every brand.

Moreover, it brings together the AI Labs of both companies under a unified goal of developing the next generation of agentic marketing, providing Aampe’s research team with the context needed at production scale across MoEngage’s worldwide customer network to expedite the success of existing initiatives.

“Aampe has built something the rest of the market hasn’t cracked: a system that continuously optimises content, timing, channel, and frequency together at an individual level. What impressed me equally was the team behind the technology,” Raviteja Dodda, Co-Founder and CEO, MoEngage, added.

MoEngage’s Merlin AI platform focuses on AI-driven marketing, while Aampe delivers tailored decision-making for top consumer brands. Agents customise messages for individuals based on timing and channel, with marketers setting the guidelines and agents ensuring transparency.

title: Google DeepMind & A24 Partner on AI Research for Filmmaking
content:
Google has invested about $75 million in A24, its first known equity stake in a film studio.

What Actually Matters.

Google has made a significant investment in A24, marking its first equity stake in a film studio.

The partnership aims to develop new tools and workflows for filmmakers through collaboration between Google DeepMind and A24.

Google DeepMind and independent film studio A24 have announced a research partnership to develop new tools and workflows for filmmakers, marking a deeper collaboration between an AI research lab and a film studio.

As part of the agreement, Google has invested in A24. According to The Wall Street Journal, the investment is worth about $75 million, making it Google’s first known equity stake in a film studio.

Founded in 2012, A24 has become one of the most prominent independent studios in Hollywood, producing and distributing titles including Everything Everywhere All at Once, Moonlight, and Beef.

The companies said the partnership will create a long-term research and development collaboration spanning multiple projects.

A24 filmmakers and creative teams will work alongside Google DeepMind researchers to test and shape emerging technologies intended to support storytelling and production workflows.

“We believe the best way to develop tools that empower artists is to work directly with them. By collaborating with filmmakers and industry leaders like A24 from the beginning, we can build new AI features to support artists in authentic, meaningful storytelling that helps enable their creative vision,” said Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis in a statement.

“The collaboration pairs a world-leading research lab with the industry's most filmmaker-forward studio to help artists develop new workflows and techniques,” Google DeepMind said in a statement. “This ensures the tools of the future are shaped by the creators who use them.”

According to the companies, the goal is to embed Google DeepMind’s technology directly into the creative process, allowing filmmakers to provide feedback that could influence future product development. The partnership will initially focus on bridging the gap between AI research and entertainment, though specific projects and technical outputs have not been disclosed.

The agreement comes as Hollywood continues to debate the role of AI in filmmaking. Studios and creators have raised concerns about copyright, training data, and the potential impact of AI-generated content on creative jobs. Against that backdrop, A24 says the partnership is intended to develop tools that support artists rather than replace them.

Reports indicate the partnership is non-exclusive and will not give Google access to A24’s film and television library. Instead, the companies plan to collaborate on production and distribution technologies informed by filmmaker feedback.

title: BMS Opens Mumbai GCC to Scale AI, Data & Analytics Capabilities
content:
The facility will be led by Nipun Mapara, who has been appointed Managing Director of the GCC.

What Actually Matters.

BMS has launched a global capability centre in Mumbai to enhance its data, analytics, and AI capabilities.

The new centre will support various BMS teams globally, focusing on broking, data analytics, and operational functions.

Independent insurance and reinsurance broker BMS has launched a global capability centre (GCC) in Mumbai as part of its strategy to expand data, analytics, and artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities across its global operations.

The new centre will support BMS teams worldwide across broking operations, data analytics, technology, client services, and operational functions. The GCC is expected to play a central role in the company’s long-term operating model by strengthening access to specialised talent, AI expertise, and technology capabilities in India.

The facility will be led by Nipun Mapara, who has been appointed Managing Director of the GCC, while Sanjeev Poojari will serve as Head of Operations.

The move comes as BMS accelerates investments in data infrastructure and AI technologies, including the deploying of AI-powered tools across broking and operational functions. The company said the Mumbai centre will provide the specialist expertise required to scale these initiatives globally.

BMS was supported by EY in designing and establishing the centre, including advising on feasibility, operational structure, and talent requirements.

The GCC also complements BMS’s broader India strategy, following its recently announced strategic partnership with Berns Brett India (BBI). Together, the investments aim to strengthen the company’s geographical footprint, diversifying operations, and supporting long-term growth.

Commenting on the launch, Nick Cook, Group CEO of BMS, said, “The opening of our GCC in Mumbai is more than an operational milestone. It is a platform for building the data and AI capability that will help BMS serve clients better and compete more effectively. India has extraordinary professional talent, and we are committed to making the BMS India GCC a genuine centre of excellence for the group, not just a support function.”

The company said the centre is already operational and contributing across multiple business functions.

Nipun Mapara, Managing Director of the GCC, said, “We are already operational and contributing across multiple workstreams, from broking support and client services to analytics and technology. The team here understands that what we build in Mumbai directly impacts how BMS performs globally. That sense of purpose is energising, and we are ready to go.”

Highlighting the broader industry trend, Benedict Reid, EY UK Commercial and Specialty Insurance Leader, said, “Brokers are reimagining their operating models to bring advanced AI analytics and specialist talent closer to the heart of their business.”

title: Almost All Indian Govt Agencies Are Evaluating or Deploying Sovereign AI: IDC-Dell Study
content:
The IDC-Dell report found that nearly 98% public sector leaders believe autonomous AI systems will help accelerate adoption across government operations.

What Actually Matters.

Nearly all Indian government agencies are evaluating or implementing sovereign AI initiatives, reflecting a significant shift towards active deployment.

India is integrating AI regulation and innovation through its digital public infrastructure, enhancing governance and data stewardship.

India’s push to build sovereign artificial intelligence capabilities is moving from policy discussions to active implementation, with nearly all government leaders surveyed already evaluating or deploying sovereign AI initiatives, according to a new IDC study commissioned by Dell Technologies.

The report, ‘Building a Sovereign AI Foundation for the India Government’, found that 96% of government organisations are actively pursuing sovereign AI with 46% evaluating technologies and another 46% running proof-of-concept projects. A further 4% have already moved into significant investments.

Unlike many countries where AI regulation and innovation are treated as separate priorities, India is increasingly integrating the two through its digital public infrastructure stack. Platforms such as Aadhaar, UPI, ONDC, and BHASHINI are emerging as key pillars of the country’s sovereign AI strategy, enabling governance, trust, and data stewardship to be embedded directly into digital systems.

“India has built something truly pioneering which is a digital public infrastructure that functions as both a governance framework and an innovation platform,” Manish Gupta, President and Managing Director, Dell Technologies India, said in a statement.

The study suggests that national security and strategic autonomy are becoming major drivers of sovereign AI investments. Around 73.3% of respondents said sovereign AI is essential for protecting sensitive national data and ensuring compliance with local regulations. Meanwhile, 70% view such investments as a safeguard against geopolitical uncertainty and supply-chain disruptions.

Government agencies are prioritising sovereign AI deployments in national security and defence, cited by 46% of respondents followed by procurement and supply chain operations at 36%.

The report also points to growing confidence in agentic AI, a new class of AI systems capable of autonomously performing tasks and making decisions. Nearly 98% of government leaders expressed confidence in agentic AI, with 44.4% believing it will play a major role in accelerating adoption. This is significantly higher than the Asia-Pacific average of 36.9%.

However, the path to scaling sovereign AI remains challenging. More than 92% of respondents identified specialised digital talent as a critical requirement, particularly in areas such as AIOps, network integration, and sovereign data governance.

Cybersecurity and regulatory complexity also remain key concerns. Around 36% of respondents highlighted the need to strengthen cybersecurity capabilities, while 34% pointed to challenges associated with navigating cross-jurisdictional regulatory frameworks.

The findings indicate that India’s public sector is increasingly viewing AI not merely as a technology initiative but as a strategic national capability with sovereign AI emerging as a cornerstone of the country’s broader ambitions for digital self-reliance.

title: Wimbledon 2026 Unveils New IBM-Powered AI Features to Personalise Fan Experience
content:
The tournament is leveraging AI across both operations and fan engagement, building on years of collaboration with IBM and rising digital audience participation.

What Actually Matters.

Wimbledon 2026 will introduce AI-powered features to enhance fan engagement and operational efficiency.

The new Key Moments feature will highlight critical points influencing match momentum using AI analysis.

The All England Lawn Tennis Club (AELTC) and IBM have announced a new set of AI-powered digital experiences for fans ahead of The Championships, Wimbledon 2026, as the tournament continues to expand its use of artificial intelligence across fan engagement and operations.

The new features, powered by IBM’s watsonx AI platform, will be available through the Wimbledon app and Wimbledon.com, both of which have undergone a major redesign to deliver a more personalised experience for global tennis audiences.

Among the key additions is Key Moments, a feature that builds on Wimbledon’s existing AI-powered Likelihood to Win tool. While the latter predicts a player’s chances of winning based on live and historical match data, Key Moments explains which specific points and events influence a match's momentum and why.

Wimbledon has also upgraded its Match Chat assistant. Fans can now ask natural language questions such as “What has happened in the match so far?” and receive instant conversational responses. Some answers will also include relevant photos and video clips. The tool is powered by IBM watsonx Orchestrate and uses multiple AI models trained on Wimbledon’s editorial style and tennis-specific language.

The new fan-facing features are supported by a large-scale modernisation of Wimbledon’s digital infrastructure. IBM used its AI-powered development accelerator, IBM Bob, to migrate more than 15,000 digital assets, including articles, videos and photographs, into a new architecture.

According to IBM, a process that would traditionally require several specialists working for months was completed by a single engineer in four weeks, while the extraction of the digital assets took just 47 minutes.

The latest announcement builds on Wimbledon’s growing use of AI over the past decade. IBM first introduced AI-powered fan features at Wimbledon in 2017, and the partnership has since evolved to include automated match insights, player analysis and predictive models. In 2025, the All England Club reported a 16% year-on-year increase in digital engagement and a 39% rise in registered myWimbledon users, highlighting the growing role of technology in attracting younger audiences.

“It’s our priority every year to remain at the pinnacle of sport and deliver the best possible guest experience,” said Usama Al-Qassab, Marketing and Commercial Director at the All England Club.

IBM’s Senior Vice President of Marketing and Communications, Jonathan Adashek, noted that the new capabilities demonstrate how AI can deepen fan engagement while also improving operational efficiency.

The Championships, Wimbledon 2026 will run from June 29 to July 12, with the new AI features available through the Wimbledon app and website via IBM SlamTracker.

OpenAI said it is also collaborating with governments and critical infrastructure operators to strengthen cybersecurity defences.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI introduced GPT-5.5-Cyber to enhance vulnerability identification and remediation in cybersecurity.

The Codex Security plugin has successfully scanned millions of code commits, identifying numerous vulnerabilities.

OpenAI has announced an expansion of its Daybreak cybersecurity initiative, introducing new tools, partnerships, and the full version of GPT-5.5-Cyber, a model to help organisations identify and patch software vulnerabilities.

The company said the initiative aims to address a growing challenge in cybersecurity: while AI has accelerated vulnerability discovery, organisations are struggling to keep pace with patching and remediation.

As part of the announcement, OpenAI released an updated version of its Codex Security plugin, which can scan codebases, validate vulnerabilities, generate patches, and help developers prevent new security issues from reaching production.

Since its research preview launch in March, Codex Security has scanned more than 30 million commits across over 30,000 repositories, with more than 5,00,000 findings automatically determined to be fixed, according to the company.

OpenAI also launched the full version of GPT-5.5-Cyber through a limited release program for verified defenders. The model achieved 85.6% on CyberGym, a benchmark that measures whether AI agents can reproduce known vulnerabilities, compared with 81.8% for GPT-5.5. It also outperformed GPT-5.5 on ExploitGym and SEC-bench Pro, two security-focused benchmarks.

“We are releasing an update to GPT-5.5-Cyber, our model that is both more permissive and more capable for advanced, authorised cybersecurity work,” OpenAI said.

The new GPT-5.5-Cyber model also outperformed Mythos 5 on the CyberGym benchmark.

The company said GPT-5.5-Cyber is designed to help security teams move beyond identifying vulnerabilities and support the full remediation process, including validating issues, developing patches, and preparing evidence for human review.

OpenAI also launched the Daybreak Cyber Partner Program, allowing security vendors to integrate GPT-5.5 with Trusted Access for Cyber into their products and services. Initial partners include Accenture, Cisco, Cloudflare, CrowdStrike, IBM, Okta, Palo Alto Networks, SentinelOne, Sophos, Wiz, and Zscaler, among others.

In a separate initiative called Patch the Planet, OpenAI is working with Trail of Bits, HackerOne, Calif, security researchers, and open-source maintainers to help projects move from vulnerability discovery to remediation. More than 30 open-source projects, including Python, Go, cURL, Sigstore, and pyca/cryptography, have committed to participating.

“Finding vulnerabilities is important, but it's landing the fix that protects the world," the company said.

OpenAI said it is also collaborating with governments and critical infrastructure operators to strengthen cybersecurity defences. Over the past month, the company established Trusted Access for Cyber partnerships with Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Japan, South Korea, and the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA).

The expansion of Daybreak reflects a broader shift in cybersecurity, where AI-assisted vulnerability discovery is becoming increasingly common, and organisations are focusing more on validating, prioritising, and patching security flaws before they can be exploited.

Micron and Anthropic will work together on memory and storage technologies used in AI training and inference

What Actually Matters.

Micron and Anthropic have formed a strategic partnership to enhance AI memory and storage infrastructure.

The collaboration includes a supply agreement and adoption of Anthropic's Claude models within Micron.

Micron Technology has announced an agreement with Anthropic that includes collaboration on AI memory and storage infrastructure, a supply agreement, adoption of Anthropic’s Claude models across Micron, and a strategic investment in Anthropic’s Series H funding round.

In May, Anthropic raised $65 billion in a Series H funding round, valuing the company at $965 billion post-money. Besides Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix also joined the round.

Micron said the partnership will align the infrastructure needs of frontier AI models with the design, supply, and deployment of computing systems at scale.

“The AI revolution has permanently elevated the role of memory and storage solutions from the data centre to the edge,” said Sumit Sadana, Executive Vice President and Chief Business Officer at Micron. “Micron’s strategic collaboration with Anthropic brings together the industry-leading capabilities of both companies to innovate and scale next-generation AI infrastructure.”

As part of the agreement, Micron and Anthropic will work together on memory and storage technologies used in AI training and inference. The companies will evaluate how memory and storage subsystems perform across different workloads and interact with the broader infrastructure stack.

Micron said the collaboration is expected to improve memory and storage performance, energy efficiency, and token economics within Anthropic’s AI infrastructure.

The companies have also entered into a multi-year supply agreement covering Micron’s data centre memory and storage products. Micron said the arrangement will support Anthropic’s long-term compute requirements as demand for its AI models grows.

“Our compute strategy depends on getting every layer of the stack right, and memory and storage are central to how efficiently we can train and serve Claude,” said Tom Brown, Co-founder and Chief Compute Officer at Anthropic. “Partnering with Micron means we collaborate closely on optimising these systems for our workloads and secure the supply we need.”

Micron also said it has deployed Anthropic’s Claude models across engineering, manufacturing, and enterprise functions to support coding and other AI-driven workflows. The company said the models are being used on operational and engineering challenges and have contributed to productivity gains.

title: Indian Army, Zoho Sign MoU for Indigenous Digital Upgrade
content:
Indian Army partners with Zoho to accelerate digital transformation under JAI mission, boosting indigenous capabilities

What Actually Matters.

The Indian Army has partnered with Zoho to enhance digital transformation under the JAI mission.

This collaboration aims to develop secure digital systems and strengthen technology-driven skills within the Army.

The Indian Army has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Zoho Corporation to accelerate its digital transformation efforts under the government’s Jointness, Atmanirbharta & Innovation (JAI) mission.

The agreement was formalised by Lieutenant General Harsh Chhibber, Director General Information Systems (DGIS), and Rajendran Dandapani, Director of Engineering at Zoho.

The signing took place in the presence of Chief of Army Staff General Upendra Dwivedi and Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu, according to an official post by the Indian Army.

The collaboration will focus on developing application-oriented research and development, building secure and sustainable digital systems, and strengthening technology-driven skill sets within the force. The initiative is aimed at transforming the Indian Army into a future-ready, digitally empowered organisation.

Zoho, in its response, said it is proud to contribute to the JAI mission. “As an indigenous technology company, we remain committed to building secure, sustainable digital capabilities,” the company stated, adding that it looks forward to working closely with the Army.

The JAI mission, introduced as a strategic doctrine to modernise India’s military, is built on three pillars: Jointness, Atmanirbharta, and Innovation. Jointness focuses on seamless coordination among the Army, Navy, Air Force, paramilitary forces, and state agencies.

Atmanirbharta emphasises self-reliance in defence manufacturing and technology, while Innovation highlights the adoption of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, drones, robotics, and cyber capabilities.

What Actually Matters.

Tredence has acquired KMK Consulting to enhance its growth in the healthcare and life sciences sectors.

KMK Consulting brings extensive expertise in commercial analytics and market research, working with leading pharmaceutical companies.

AI and data science solutions company Tredence has acquired KMK Consulting, a specialist analytics and consulting firm focused on the pharmaceutical and life sciences sector, to accelerate growth in healthcare and life sciences sectors.

Headquartered in Morris Plains, New Jersey, KMK Consulting works with eight of the world's top 10 pharmaceutical companies and brings more than two decades of expertise in commercial analytics, real-world evidence, and market research.

Tredence said the acquisition aims to strengthen its position in the rapidly growing healthcare and life sciences market, which it expects to contribute about 25% of its overall revenue over the medium term.

The deal combines KMK's pharmaceutical and life sciences expertise with Tredence's agentic AI, data engineering, and decision intelligence capabilities. The company said the combined offering will help life sciences customers accelerate AI adoption across research, development and commercialisation functions.

According to Tredence, the acquisition will position the company as an AI partner across the pharmaceutical value chain. It’ll also strengthen Tredence's presence within the Veeva ecosystem. The company noted that Veeva's cloud-based CRM and data platforms are used by roughly 60–70% of pharmaceutical companies worldwide for commercial operations, medical engagement, and incentive compensation.

"While Tredence has consistently operated at the leading edge of AI and data science, our true differentiator has always been deep domain expertise," said Shub Bhowmick, Co-founder and CEO of Tredence. "The acquisition of KMK reinforces this philosophy, bringing unparalleled strength in pharmaceuticals and life sciences."

Michael Karbachinskiy, Founder and CEO of KMK Consulting, said the partnership would allow the firm to combine its life sciences expertise with Tredence's AI and data science capabilities to deliver greater value to clients.

Prashant Sareen, Global Head of Healthcare and Life Sciences at Tredence, said KMK's domain expertise would help the company expand its offerings for global pharmaceutical customers across R&D, supply chain, and AI deployment initiatives.

Wipro is deepening its cybersecurity partnership with Palo Alto Networks as enterprises increasingly seek AI-driven tools to counter sophisticated cyberattacks.

What Actually Matters.

Wipro has enhanced its partnership with Palo Alto Networks to offer AI-driven managed detection and response services.

The collaboration aims to automate threat detection and response in complex IT environments.

Wipro has expanded its partnership with cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks to launch artificial intelligence-powered managed detection and response (MDR) services, as enterprises look to strengthen defences against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

The new offering combines Palo Alto Networks' Cortex XSIAM security operations platform with the IT services major’s managed security services capabilities, enabling enterprises to automate threat detection and response across complex IT environments.

The move comes as demand for AI-driven cybersecurity tools is rising amid growing concerns over attacks that leverage AI. Concerned by the possibility of a Mythos-class attack after Anthropic previewed Claude Mythos, enterprises are now seeking to consolidate security tools and reduce operational complexity while improving incident response times.

According to Wipro, the offering uses machine learning, AI, and automation to identify and respond to threats more quickly, while helping security teams focus on high-priority incidents.

The service will be delivered through Wipro's network of eight cyber defence centres globally.

“As organisations navigate a rapidly evolving landscape marked by accelerated AI adoption, the need for robust governance and strategic cost management has never been greater,” Satish Yadavalli, Global Business Head - Cloud, Infrastructure, and Security Services, Wipro, said in a statement.

The expanded engagement builds on an existing relationship between the two companies spanning cloud, network, and security transformation projects. Financial details of the partnership were not disclosed.

“Our combined capabilities empower mutual customers to consolidate tools, eliminate data silos, and leverage AI and automation to reduce noise, accelerate response from days to minutes, and ultimately stop even the most sophisticated threats,” said Simone Gammeri, Senior Vice President and Chief Partnership Officer at Palo Alto Networks.

Wipro said the service is supported by its internal AI platforms and automation tools, which are used for workflow orchestration and security operations management. The company also cited a recent deployment with a European gaming and entertainment company, where the partners helped modernise security operations and improve productivity.

title: Oracle Confirmed 21,000 Jobs Cuts in a Year as AI Reshapes Operations
content:
Oracle's workforce shrank by about 13% over the past year, with the company saying AI adoption across its operations has led to job reductions and could result in further cuts.

What Actually Matters.

Oracle has reduced its workforce by approximately 13%, equating to about 21,000 jobs in the past year.

The company attributes job cuts to the adoption of AI technologies across its operations.

Oracle has confirmed that it axed around 21,000 jobs globally over the past year, as the technology giant reshaped its business around the deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, according to its latest annual report.

The US-based enterprise technology company said it had approximately 141,000 full-time employees as of May 31, 2026, down from about 162,000 a year earlier. The reduction represents roughly 13% of its global workforce.

“The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce,” according to the report.

The layoffs were first reported by Bloomberg in march this year.

The company noted that its products and services increasingly incorporate AI technologies, including embedded AI-driven automation, analytics, and generative AI capabilities.

“Our products and services include enterprise applications and infrastructure offerings that incorporate and are enhanced by artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, including embedded AI-driven automation and analytics and generative AI capabilities,” it added.

Oracle added that the workforce restructuring resulted in approximately $1.8 billion in severance payments and related costs during the last financial year.

The disclosure comes as Oracle prepares for a fresh fundraise. Earlier this year, the company said it could raise up to $50 billion in 2026 through a combination of debt and equity offerings.

Oracle's workforce reduction comes amid an industry-wide realignment driven by AI. As companies pour billions into AI models, data centres, and computing infrastructure, many are reassessing staffing needs and operational costs.

Amazon and Meta are among the firms that have announced layoffs while stepping up AI-related investments.

title: BHASHINI, Assam Innovation & Startup Foundation to Drive Multilingual AI Innovation
content:
The two organisations will also work on collecting, curating, and enriching linguistic datasets through the Bhashadaan platform

What Actually Matters.

The partnership between BHASHINI and AISF aims to enhance multilingual digital services in Assam.

The collaboration will integrate AI-powered language technologies into various programmes and public services.

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Assam Innovation & Startup Foundation (AISF) to promote language technology, generative AI solutions, and multilingual digital services across Assam.

The partnership aims to expand access to digital services in regional languages while strengthening Assam’s startup and innovation ecosystem by adopting AI-powered language technologies.

Under the collaboration, DIBD and AISF will work together through the BHASHINI Rajyam initiative to integrate BHASHINI’s language translation and voice technologies into AISF’s programmes, platforms, and public-facing services. The initiative will focus on enabling multilingual access to government and innovation-related services, enhancing translation capabilities in Assamese and other local languages, and developing voice-enabled applications.

A key objective of the partnership is to encourage startups, entrepreneurs, researchers, and academic institutions in Assam to build multilingual AI solutions using BHASHINI’s language technology stack. The collaboration is expected to create opportunities for innovators to develop AI applications tailored to local linguistic and regional needs.

The two organisations will also work to collect, curate, and enrich linguistic datasets through the Bhashadaan platform. These datasets will help improve the quality and accuracy of language AI models while supporting the development of more inclusive digital solutions.

As part of the agreement, BHASHINI will provide AI-driven translation services, technical support, training, dashboards, and API integration assistance.

It will also customise language models to better capture regional dialects and linguistic nuances while continuously improving translation quality through machine learning and user feedback.

AISF will help identify language requirements across the state, prioritise languages for translation services, and facilitate participation from startups, innovators, research institutions, and ecosystem stakeholders.

The partnership is expected to support the wider adoption of multilingual digital solutions across sectors, improve digital inclusion, and expand access to emerging technologies for citizens and institutions in Assam.

Commenting on the collaboration, Amitabh Nag, CEO, Digital India BHASHINI Division, said in a statement, "Through this partnership with the Assam Innovation & Startup Foundation, we aim to empower startups, innovators, and entrepreneurs to build impactful multilingual AI solutions that address local needs and create real-world value."

The collaboration reflects a broader push by the government to leverage AI and language technologies to make digital services more accessible.

title: BharatGen Joins AI Alliance’s Project Tapestry to Build Sovereign AI
content:
The initiative seeks to bring together data, compute resources, talent, and funding from multiple countries and organisations to develop frontier AI systems.

What Actually Matters.

BharatGen will lead India's involvement in Project Tapestry, a global initiative for developing frontier AI.

The project promotes distributed model development while ensuring nations control their data and AI systems.

The AI Alliance has announced that India’s BharatGen will anchor the country’s initial role in Project Tapestry, a global consortium working to develop frontier AI through distributed model development while allowing participating nations and institutions to retain control over their data, models, and deployment.

The announcement comes as AI sovereignty emerged as a central topic at the G7 Summit in Evian and VivaTech in Paris, with governments increasingly examining how to build and deploy AI systems without relying entirely on a small number of technology providers.

BharatGen, backed by the IndiaAI Mission and the Department of Science and Technology (DST), joins the project as a founding contributor, bringing multilingual AI infrastructure designed for India’s linguistic diversity.

A letter of intent formalising the collaboration was signed on June 18 by IIT Bombay Director Shireesh Kedare in the presence of Deputy Directors Milind Atrey and Ravindra Gudi, along with Ganesh Ramakrishnan, founding director of BharatGen.

BharatGen will immediately begin co-leading workstreams on distributed model training as part of Project Tapestry. The initiative seeks to bring together data, compute resources, talent, and funding from multiple countries and organisations to develop frontier AI systems while preserving national ownership and control.

“India has long believed that science advances fastest when it is open and shared. Project Tapestry, which lets nations build frontier AI together while retaining sovereignty over their data and models, reflects the collaborative, self-reliant innovation India is advancing,” said Professor Ajay Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India.

The project is built around a distributed development architecture in which a base model is developed centrally and then adapted by participating organisations using local data. Participants can contribute improvements back to the shared model while retaining ownership of their data and any derivative models they create.

“As India builds frontier AI rooted in its own languages and knowledge, IIT Bombay and BharatGen, supported by the India AI mission, are proud to support and participate as a founding contributor in Project Tapestry, an open, global consortium for nations to advance frontier AI together,” said Shireesh Kedare, Director of IIT Bombay and Chairman of BharatGen.

Project Tapestry was launched last month during a technical workshop in Paris attended by around 30 AI leaders from countries including the United States, France, India, Vietnam, Japan, Switzerland, and the United Arab Emirates. Participants included organisations such as Pleias, PRAIRE, AMI Labs, Software Heritage, and Current AI.

According to the AI Alliance, the initiative is designed to enable countries and institutions to collaborate on AI development without transferring sensitive datasets to a centralised provider.

“AI is becoming essential infrastructure. No single company or country should determine who can build on it, adapt it, or benefit from it. Project Tapestry is a test of whether frontier AI can be built as open infrastructure: collaborative, capable, and sovereign by design,” said Dr Yann LeCun, Chief Science Advisor of the AI Alliance and Executive Chairman of AMI Labs.

Vietnam has also emerged as an early participant in the project. The National Innovation Center and FPT Corporation are working with Project Tapestry to develop AI systems aligned with Vietnamese language, culture, and industry requirements while maintaining local ownership and governance.

“With the National Innovation Center and FPT Corporation engaged, Project Tapestry gives Vietnam a path to help build frontier AI that reflects its language, culture, industries, and institutions while retaining control over its own data, models, and deployment,” said Dr Christopher Nguyen, Chief Architect of Project Tapestry and CEO of Aitomatic.

The AI Alliance said future AI capabilities will increasingly depend on access to scientific, technical, industrial, and national datasets that are often unavailable on the open web. Project Tapestry aims to create a framework for using such data in AI development without requiring organisations to surrender control over it.

“Project Tapestry aims to build the most capable frontier AI possible in a way that ensures the value and control of that AI is retained by those developing and deploying it—whether they are in industry, government, a non-profit or an individual,” said Dr Anthony Annunziata, Chairman of the AI Alliance and Director of AI Open Innovation at IBM.

title: Micron Invests in Anthropic, Partners on AI Memory Infrastructure
content:
Micron and Anthropic will work together on memory and storage technologies used in AI training and inference

What Actually Matters.

Micron and Anthropic have formed a strategic partnership to enhance AI memory and storage infrastructure.

The collaboration includes a supply agreement and adoption of Anthropic's Claude models within Micron.

Micron Technology has announced an agreement with Anthropic that includes collaboration on AI memory and storage infrastructure, a supply agreement, adoption of Anthropic’s Claude models across Micron, and a strategic investment in Anthropic’s Series H funding round.

In May, Anthropic raised $65 billion in a Series H funding round, valuing the company at $965 billion post-money. Besides Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix also joined the round.

Micron said the partnership will align the infrastructure needs of frontier AI models with the design, supply, and deployment of computing systems at scale.

“The AI revolution has permanently elevated the role of memory and storage solutions from the data centre to the edge,” said Sumit Sadana, Executive Vice President and Chief Business Officer at Micron. “Micron’s strategic collaboration with Anthropic brings together the industry-leading capabilities of both companies to innovate and scale next-generation AI infrastructure.”

As part of the agreement, Micron and Anthropic will work together on memory and storage technologies used in AI training and inference. The companies will evaluate how memory and storage subsystems perform across different workloads and interact with the broader infrastructure stack.

Micron said the collaboration is expected to improve memory and storage performance, energy efficiency, and token economics within Anthropic’s AI infrastructure.

The companies have also entered into a multi-year supply agreement covering Micron’s data centre memory and storage products. Micron said the arrangement will support Anthropic’s long-term compute requirements as demand for its AI models grows.

“Our compute strategy depends on getting every layer of the stack right, and memory and storage are central to how efficiently we can train and serve Claude,” said Tom Brown, Co-founder and Chief Compute Officer at Anthropic. “Partnering with Micron means we collaborate closely on optimising these systems for our workloads and secure the supply we need.”

Micron also said it has deployed Anthropic’s Claude models across engineering, manufacturing, and enterprise functions to support coding and other AI-driven workflows. The company said the models are being used on operational and engineering challenges and have contributed to productivity gains.

title: The Indian Drone Industry’s Shift Away From Manufacturing to Software
content:
CRED’s Chief Strategy and Finance Executive, Miten Sampat, will take over as interim CEO.

What Actually Matters.

Kunal Shah is stepping down as CEO of CRED to lead WhatsApp globally for Meta.

Meta plans to invest $900 million in CRED, valuing the company at approximately $4.5 billion.

CRED Founder Kunal Shah has announced that he is stepping down from his role as CEO of the fintech company and will join Meta to lead WhatsApp globally.

The move comes alongside Meta’s planned $900 million investment in CRED as part of its Series H funding round, according to a statement.

The round values CRED at a post-money valuation of about ₹43,239 crore ($4.5 billion). The funding will comprise a mix of primary and secondary share purchases.

Meta will join CRED's cap table as a minority investor and, under the terms of the deal, “will not receive access to CRED customer information,” the company said.

Shah said CRED’s Chief Strategy and Finance Executive, Miten Sampat, will take over as interim CEO. He added that he would remain a shareholder in the company.

“CRED is ready for its next phase,” Shah wrote in a post on X. “I’m stepping away from the operating role and will continue as a shareholder. My commitment doesn’t change. Just the role.”

CRED said it currently processes more than 40% of India's credit card bill payments. The company added that its lending business has grown to ₹24,000 crore (more than $2.5 billion) in managed assets under management (AUM) through partnerships with financial institutions.

“CRED has built a platform that catalyses financial progress for creditworthy Indians, with products across payments, lending, insurance, wealth, and lifestyle," the company said in the statement.

At Meta, Shah will succeed Will Cathcart, who has led WhatsApp since 2019.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced that Cathcart will step down as the head of WhatsApp after seven years in the role and will transition to a new position within Meta.

“Will’s been one of Meta's most important and effective leaders, helping to bring WhatsApp to over 3 billion people and championing privacy for our community," Zuckerberg wrote in a post on Facebook. “I’m super grateful for his partnership and contributions over these years.”

According to Zuckerberg, Cathcart will remain at Meta and focus on building new products.

The leadership transition marks the end of Shah’s day-to-day involvement in a company he founded in 2018 after selling digital payments startup FreeCharge.

Since its launch, CRED has grown to 17 million members and expanded beyond credit card bill payments into payments, lending, insurance, commerce, wealth management and credit cards. Shah said the company has scaled from zero revenue to approximately $325 million, or around ₹3,200 crore, in annual revenue.

He also said CRED completed four employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) buybacks between 2019 and 2025 and is now announcing a fifth buyback. The company recently recorded its first profitable quarter, Shah noted.

Shah credited CRED’s growth to a team that focused on ownership, judgment and craft. During his tenure, the company secured multiple regulatory licences and launched several products during the COVID-19 period.

Zuckerberg credited Shah with building CRED into a major technology company in India and said his experience would help him lead the messaging platform.

“Kunal built CRED into one of India’s most important technology companies, and he brings the kind of builder mentality and global perspective that will serve him well in running the world’s biggest messaging app,” Zuckerberg said.

Cathcart welcomed the transition and is expected to remain at Meta during the handover before moving to a new role within the company.

“WhatsApp is in the strongest position it's ever been — and that felt like the right moment to step back. I'm so proud of what we have built. We scaled end-to-end encrypted messaging to more than three billion people,” he said.

Shah said he sees significant room for growth at the messaging platform.

“While it’s come very far, the delta between WhatsApp today and its full potential is massive,” he said. “I look forward to working with Mark, Chris, and the leadership across Meta for the next step in WhatsApp's journey.”

WhatsApp is one of Meta’s largest products, serving more than three billion users worldwide. Meta acquired WhatsApp in 2014 and also owns Facebook, Instagram and Messenger.
