title: US Orders Anthropic to Block Foreign Nationals From Fable 5 and Mythos 5
content:
Anthropic said the government cited a potential jailbreak technique, though it argued the reported capabilities are already available in other AI models.

What Actually Matters.

Anthropic has suspended access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models due to a US government export control directive.

The directive prohibits access for all foreign nationals, including those employed by Anthropic.

Anthropic said it has suspended access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models after receiving a US government export control directive citing national security authorities.

The company said it received the order at 5:21 p.m. ET on June 12 and was required to disable access to the two models for all customers, including foreign nationals inside and outside the United States and foreign-national Anthropic employees. Access to the company’s other AI models remains unaffected.

“The US government, citing national security authorities, has issued an export control directive to suspend all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by any foreign national,” Anthropic said in a statement.

Anthropic said the government did not provide specific details about its national security concerns. According to the company, its understanding is that officials had identified a method of bypassing, or jailbreaking, Fable 5.

The company said it reviewed a demonstration of the technique and found that it exposed a small number of previously known, minor vulnerabilities. Anthropic added that other publicly available AI models could identify the same vulnerabilities without requiring a jailbreak.

“These vulnerabilities all appear relatively simple, and we have found that other publicly-available models are able to discover them as well without requiring a bypass,” the company added.

Anthropic said extensive testing of Fable 5 had been conducted before launch, involving the US government, the UK’s AI Safety Institute, third-party organisations, and internal teams. The company said the testing found Fable’s safeguards to be more effective than those of earlier deployed models and that no tester had identified a “universal jailbreak” capable of broadly bypassing the model’s protections.

The company acknowledged that no AI provider currently appears capable of achieving complete jailbreak resistance and said all industry safeguards remain vulnerable to narrower jailbreak techniques under certain circumstances.

Anthropic said its approach relied on a “defence in depth strategy” that combines safeguards, monitoring and customer data retention policies to detect and mitigate jailbreak attempts.

“We stand by this defence-in-depth strategy. It reduces the risks posed by Fable, making them comparable to the risks of existing models already deployed across the industry,” the company said.

The company said it had not received evidence of a jailbreak that resulted in harm and that the disclosed techniques either generated benign responses or identified minor software issues. Anthropic added that the government had provided only verbal evidence of a potential non-universal jailbreak involving requests to review code and identify software flaws.

Anthropic further said it had reviewed a report it believes formed the basis of the directive and found that the capability described was “widely available from other models (including OpenAI’s GPT-5.5), and is used every day by the defenders who keep systems safe.”

While complying with the order, Anthropic criticised the decision to recall a commercial AI model over what it described as a narrow potential jailbreak.

“We disagree that the finding of a narrow potential jailbreak should be cause for recalling a commercial model deployed to hundreds of millions of people,” the company said.

Anthropic said governments should have the authority to block unsafe AI deployments, but argued that such actions should be carried out through “a statutory process that is transparent, fair, clear, and grounded in technical facts.”

The order comes days after Anthropic proposed a framework for government oversight of frontier AI models. In a recent blog post, CEO Dario Amodei called for mandatory third-party testing of advanced systems for risks related to cybersecurity, biological weapons, loss of control, and automated research capabilities. “The government should have the power to block or deter deployment of the model if it is determined, in light of third-party assessment, to present unacceptable risks,” Amodei wrote.

Meanwhile, the company said it is working to restore access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 and believes the government’s action is based on a misunderstanding.

title: TCS Launches Oracle AI Data Lab in Kolkata, Plans Expansion to 4 More Cities
content:
TCS’ Oracle AI Data Platform Lab marked a deeper push into enterprise AI and data modernisation.

What Actually Matters.

TCS has launched an Oracle AI Data Platform Lab in Kolkata to enhance enterprise AI capabilities and data modernisation.

The new lab aims to address issues like fragmented data and slow analytics, helping enterprises scale AI deployment.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has launched an Oracle AI Data Platform Lab and Center of Excellence in Kolkata, as the country's largest IT services exporter looks to strengthen its capabilities around enterprise AI adoption and data modernisation.

The facility, set up at Kolkata's Delta Park Lords, has been developed in collaboration with Oracle and aims to help enterprises address challenges such as fragmented data environments, slow analytics cycles, limited AI scalability, and operational inefficiencies.

TCS plans to establish similar Oracle AI Data Platform Labs and Centres of Excellence in four more Indian cities over the next three years.

The move comes as IT services firms increasingly invest in specialised AI centres, labs, and industry-focused platforms to help clients move beyond pilot projects and deploy AI at scale.

According to TCS, the new facility will use reusable architectures, industry-specific solutions and accelerators to help customers convert enterprise data into actionable insights and automate business processes using AI.

The lab will leverage Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Oracle Autonomous AI Database, and Oracle's enterprise AI capabilities.

“The facility is designed to accelerate the journey from ideation to experimentation to full-scale deployment,” Sudipto Ray, Vice President and Global Head, Oracle Practice, TCS, said in a statement. “By harnessing Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and the latest advancements in AI, the lab will help customers reimagine their operational strategies both in data analytics and rapid application development.”

TCS currently has a centralised pool of 26,000 Oracle-skilled professionals in India supporting client AI programmes.

The launch also reflects the growing importance of partnerships between large IT services companies and global technology vendors as enterprises seek integrated AI, cloud, and data solutions rather than standalone deployments.

title: Marine Robotics Co Rekise Bags $9.7M Led by Accel, Nikhil Kamath’s NKSquared
content:
Rekise Marine will use the funding to finalise sea trials for its submarine, Jalkapi.

What Actually Matters.

Rekise Marine has secured $9.7 million in seed funding, led by Accel and NKSquared.

The company aims to revolutionise the maritime industry with autonomous ships and submarines.

Rekise Marine, an Indian company specialising in marine robotics, has raised $9.7 million in seed funding, with Accel and NKSquared leading the investment.

The funding round also included contributions from Sameer Brij Verma, Sandeep Singhal, Industrial47, Singularity AMC, a variety of corporate leaders, the company's founders, and several family offices.

The company, founded by naval architect Maitrai Maka, aims to overhaul the maritime industry with robotics. Rekise develops autonomous ships and submarines using a comprehensive approach that integrates vessel design, systems integration, and proprietary autonomy software.

Founder and CEO Maitrai Maka, along with Rear Admiral Shekhar Mital (Retd), the Co-founder and Executive Director, stated, “At Rekise, we build autonomous ships and submarines, and at sea, the autonomy is only as good as the sensors and hardware feeding it. That is why we design the vessel, its sensors, and its software as a single system, rather than bolting them together later. What makes that repeatable is the team we are building, more than either of us, and this round lets us grow it while putting Jalkapi in the water.”

Based in Bengaluru, the startup plans to use this funding to finalise and conduct sea trials for its extra-large autonomous submarine Jalkapi, enhance its in-house autonomy software, and significantly grow its engineering team in areas such as robotics, AI/ML, embedded systems, platform systems integration, and naval architecture, along with the crews required to test and manage new platforms at sea.

The company’s software platform supports a wide range of vessels, from small, portable units to large submarines, enabling capabilities to be used across different platforms with minimal adjustments. Rekise constructs and assembles its vessels in-house, collaborating with leading Indian shipyards, such as Goa Shipyard and GRSE.

Nikhil Kamath, Founder and Investor at NKSquared, remarked in a statement, “Maritime autonomy is the capability it now needs to own. We are excited to be backing a team that brings those strengths together, pairing deep naval systems engineering with autonomy as closely as anyone in the world, and building it to a global standard for India.”

Emphasising its focus on naval autonomy, Rekise envisions its platforms and software being used in hydrographic surveying, offshore energy, ports, and inland waterways, positioning itself to meet India's defence requirements and tapping into the global maritime autonomy market.

title: IndiaAI Mission-Backed Avataar.ai Launches Indigenous Video AI Model Varya
content:
The company says its distilled architecture cuts video generation to four steps, lowering inference costs to ₹ 0.48 per second.

What Actually Matters.

Avataar.ai has launched Varya, an indigenous video-generation model aimed at reducing AI video creation costs.

The model is part of the IndiaAI Mission, which seeks to enhance local AI capabilities and reduce dependence on foreign technologies.

Indian AI startup Avataar.ai has launched Varya, an indigenous video-generation model designed to reduce the cost of creating AI-generated videos while better representing India’s cultural, linguistic, and regional diversity.

The launch marks one of the latest efforts under the government’s IndiaAI Mission initiative to build homegrown AI capabilities and reduce reliance on expensive foreign models.

Avataar said Varya was developed using subsidised national AI compute infrastructure after the company was selected by the IndiaAI Mission to build indigenous foundation AI technologies.

According to the company, Varya can generate videos from text prompts or images and allows users to extend generated clips into longer sequences. The model is designed for applications across education, commerce, governance, citizen services, digital storytelling, and India's vast MSME sector.

“The launch of one of the foundational models supported under the IndiaAI Mission marks a significant milestone in India's AI journey,” said S Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY).

“Varya represents the kind of research-led capability building that we seek to enable,” he added.

A key feature of the model is its focus on efficiency. Avataar said it uses a distillation technique that reduces the video-generation process from 50 computational steps to just four. Based on the company’s internal benchmarks, the model can generate video at approximately ₹ 0.48 per second, making it up to 10 times more cost-efficient than several leading global video-generation models.

“It is a proud moment that reflects our commitment to building indigenous AI capabilities and fostering a vibrant deep-tech ecosystem,” Krishnan said. “Through strategic support for foundational models, we are enabling innovation at scale and creating the building blocks for the next generation of AI solutions.”

Avataar CEO and Co-Founder Sravanth Aluru said the future of India’s AI ecosystem would depend as much on affordability as on raw model capability.

“India's AI opportunity will not be defined only by the largest models. It will also be defined by the most efficient models,” Aluru said.

“Varya demonstrates that frontier-quality video AI can be made dramatically more efficient and accessible. For a country of 1.4 billion people, affordability is not a feature, it is a prerequisite.”

The company said Varya has been trained to understand and generate visuals that reflect India’s diverse regions, festivals, communities, and public spaces, addressing a common criticism that many global generative AI systems are optimised primarily for Western datasets.

Aluru argued that India’s competitive advantage in AI may come from building efficient and context-aware systems rather than competing solely on model size.

“Affordable AI is inclusive AI,” he said. “Indian companies can compete globally not by simply building bigger models, but by building more efficient, context-aware models that expand access."

Founded in 2014, Bengaluru-based Avataar was co-founded by Aluru and Gaurav Baid and has raised more than $55 million from investors, including Tiger Global and Peak XV Partners (formerly Sequoia Capital India)

The company said it plans to release a technical report detailing Varya’s architecture, distillation methodology, and benchmark results in the coming weeks.

title: MNIT Jaipur Gets Advanced Quantum and AI Labs, Access to Lam Research’s Semiverse Platform
content:
Under the collaboration, Infoparks Kerala and Inductus Group will work together to promote the state’s strengths in talent availability, digital infrastructure, and innovation capabilities.

What Actually Matters.

Kerala has signed a strategic partnership with Inductus Group to enhance its global capability centre landscape.

The collaboration aims to promote Kerala's strengths in talent availability, digital infrastructure, and innovation capabilities.

In a move aimed at strengthening Kerala’s position in India’s rapidly growing global capability centre (GCC) landscape, the Kerala government, through Infoparks Kerala, has signed a strategic memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Inductus Group, a global GCC enabler and IT consulting firm.

The agreement was signed by Susanth Kurunthil, CEO of Infoparks Kerala, and Alouk Kumar, Founder and CEO of Inductus Group, as part of the state’s broader strategy to attract multinational corporations looking to establish development centres, innovation hubs, and global capability centres in India.

The partnership follows discussions led by Seeram Sambasiva Rao, IAS, Special Secretary (Electronics & IT), Kerala government, and Chairman of the Executive Council of Infoparks Kerala, aimed at showcasing Kerala’s competitive advantages to global enterprises and increasing the state’s visibility as an investment destination.

Under the collaboration, Infoparks Kerala and Inductus Group will work together to promote Kerala’s strengths in talent availability, digital infrastructure, innovation capabilities, and quality of life to multinational companies evaluating locations for global operations.

Commenting on the partnership, Kumar said, “Kerala possesses many of the attributes that global organisations increasingly seek while evaluating locations for their GCCs, including a highly skilled workforce, strong educational infrastructures and foundations, digital readiness, and a supportive business environment. Through this partnership with Infoparks Kerala, we look forward to strengthening awareness about the state's capabilities and enabling meaningful engagement between global enterprises and Kerala’s vast, evolving and growing tech ecosystem.”

The agreement comes at a time when the GCC sector is evolving beyond traditional shared services into centres focused on innovation, research and development, digital transformation, AI, engineering, and advanced technology functions. As enterprises seek alternative destinations beyond established hubs, Kerala is positioning itself as an emerging location capable of supporting future-ready business operations.

The state is banking on its strong literacy rates, expanding technology ecosystem, growing digital infrastructure, and skilled workforce to attract both large multinational corporations and mid-market global enterprises. The initiative also aligns with India’s broader ambition of strengthening its position as the world's leading GCC destination.

By combining Infoparks Kerala’s institutional and ecosystem-building capabilities with Inductus Group’s expertise in GCC advisory, investment facilitation, and enterprise engagement, the partnership aims to accelerate knowledge economy growth and attract innovation-led investments to the state.

The collaboration is expected to support Kerala’s efforts to expand its technology footprint, create high-value employment opportunities, and establish itself as a competitive alternative in India’s evolving GCC ecosystem.

title: Karnataka Approves ₹27 Crore to Boost Startups, Deep-Tech Research & Industry-Academia Collaboration
content:
This investment, led by CRV and joined by major players such as Samsung and LVMH, aims to enhance Theker’s AI-powered robots.

What Actually Matters.

Theker has secured $85 million in Series A funding, marking a significant milestone for European robotics investment.

The funding round was led by CRV, with participation from notable investors including Samsung and LVMH.

Barcelona-based AI robotics startup Theker has raised $85 million (€73 million) in what the company claims is the largest Series A funding round ever secured by a European robotics company, as investors continue to back AI applications in industrial automation.

The funding round was led by venture capital firm CRV and included participation from Samsung, LVMH, Cathay Innovation, 20VC, Henkel Ventures, Korelya, and Bright Pixel Capital, among others.

Founded in Barcelona by robotics and AI engineers Carla Gómez Cano and Jiaqiang Ye Zhu, Theker develops AI-powered industrial robots designed to operate in dynamic production environments. The company says its systems use proprietary AI and robotics technology to adapt to changing conditions without the extensive reprogramming typically required by conventional industrial robots.

“We didn’t build THEKER to run pilots. We built it to ship robots that work the day they arrive and continue improving every day after,” said Carla Gómez Cano, Co-founder of Theker Robotics, in a statement. “This round accelerates a vision we’ve been building toward from day one: making intelligent, adaptable robotics practical for real industrial operations at a global scale.”

According to the company, the new capital will be used to accelerate deployments with large industrial operators, strengthen its AI and robotics platform, and expand teams across software, electronics, mechanical engineering and operations.

The fundraising comes less than a year after Theker completed an estimated $20.82 million (€18 million) seed round, underscoring growing investor interest in physical AI technologies that bring artificial intelligence into real-world industrial settings.

“THEKER is solving one of the most important challenges in robotics: bringing general-purpose AI into real production environments where reliability, adaptability and scale actually matter,” said Reid Christian, General Partner at CRV.

“What Carla, Jiaqiang and the team have built is exceptionally rare, a deeply technical platform paired with real commercial deployment momentum. We believe THEKER has the potential to become one of the defining robotics companies of this generation,” he added.

The company said its robots are already operating in manufacturing, logistics, and retail environments across Europe, helping businesses improve productivity and address labour shortages.

Theker said the investment will help it scale deployments globally and advance the development of general-purpose AI-native robots for industrial applications.

The largest allocation includes ₹9.26 crore over five years for the establishment of the K-Combinator Startup Accelerator in Mangaluru in partnership with TiE-Mangaluru

What Actually Matters.

Karnataka's government has approved initiatives worth over ₹27 crore to enhance its innovation ecosystem outside Bengaluru.

The K-Combinator Startup Accelerator in Mangaluru will receive ₹9.26 crore to support local startups through mentorship and funding.

In a major push to strengthen Karnataka’s innovation ecosystem beyond Bengaluru, the state government has approved four strategic initiatives worth over ₹27 crore spanning startup acceleration, industry-academia collaboration, medical robotics, and advanced genome-editing research.

The projects, approved through the Department of Electronics, IT, Biotechnology and Science & Technology (ITBT), Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS), Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM), academic institutions, and ecosystem partners, are aimed at accelerating entrepreneurship, enhancing employability, and strengthening Karnataka’s leadership in deep-tech innovation.

“These approvals reflect Karnataka’s commitment to investing across the full innovation spectrum—from startups and talent development to frontier research in biotechnology, genomics and medical robotics. By strengthening regional innovation ecosystems, industry-academia partnerships and deep-tech research capabilities, we are creating the foundations for the next generation of jobs, enterprises and scientific breakthroughs,” said Priyank Kharge, Karnataka Minister for Home, IT and BT, and e-Governance.

The largest allocation includes ₹9.26 crore over five years to establish the K-Combinator Startup Accelerator in Mangaluru in partnership with TiE-Mangaluru under the Local Economy Accelerator Programme (LEAP). The accelerator will support startups in the Udupi-Mangaluru region through mentorship, access to funding, market linkages, and ecosystem support, with a focus on helping early-stage ventures achieve product-market fit and scale.

The government has also sanctioned ₹7.47 crore for the Super 100 Industry-Academia Adoption Programme, which will create one-to-one partnerships between 100 industry partners and 100 higher education institutions, particularly across tier-2 and tier-3 cities. Implemented through KDEM, the programme aims to bridge the gap between academic curricula and industry requirements through mentorship, faculty development, research collaboration, and real-world projects.

On the deep-tech front, Karnataka has approved ₹3.66 crore for the development of an Advanced Surgical Assistive Robot, an indigenous collaborative robotic platform designed for neurosurgical applications. The project will be jointly developed by IIIT-Bengaluru and NIMHANS and aims to improve precision, safety, and accessibility in complex surgical procedures through advanced imaging, sensors, real-time monitoring systems, and software-assisted interventions.

Further strengthening the state’s biotechnology ambitions, the government has sanctioned ₹6.8 crore to expand infrastructure at the Centre for Human Genetics, Bengaluru. The expansion will support the newly established Institute of Advanced Genome Editing and Gene Therapy and create nearly 1,500 square metres of advanced scientific infrastructure, including clean rooms, tissue culture laboratories, and next-generation sequencing facilities.

Two of the four initiatives fall under the state’s LEAP programme, which seeks to create stronger innovation ecosystems outside Bengaluru and unlock new opportunities for entrepreneurship and economic development across emerging regional hubs.

The latest approvals come as Karnataka faces increasing competition from states such as Telangana, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra in attracting startups, research investments, and deep-tech innovation. By focusing simultaneously on startup growth, talent development, biotechnology infrastructure, and indigenous technology development, the state is seeking to reinforce its position as India’s leading innovation and technology hub.

Collectively, the initiatives represent a strategic investment of ₹27.19 crore aimed at building stronger regional innovation ecosystems, promoting industry-academia collaboration, advancing healthcare and biotechnology research, and supporting the development of globally competitive startups and deep-tech solutions.

title: Publicis Sapient Launches AI-Led IT Operations Platform as Firms Seek to Cut Support Costs
content:
OpenAI is acquiring Ona to give Codex persistent cloud environments, allowing AI agents to continue working on tasks long after users leave a session.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI's acquisition of Ona aims to enhance Codex with persistent cloud environments for AI agents.

This development addresses the challenge of enabling AI agents to work independently after user sessions end.

OpenAI has agreed to acquire Ona, a cloud infrastructure startup focused on secure development environments, as it expands Codex from a coding assistant into a platform for long-running AI agents operating inside enterprise systems.

The acquisition targets a key challenge facing enterprise AI deployments, which is to enable agents to continue working after a user leaves a session. This also allows maintaining control over security, credentials, governance and infrastructure.

OpenAI said Ona’s technology will allow Codex agents to run within customer-controlled cloud environments, giving organisations greater oversight of where agents execute, which systems they can access, and how their activity is reviewed.

While AI agents have become increasingly capable of handling complex tasks, many remain constrained by session-based interactions and limited access to enterprise environments.

OpenAI said more than 5 million people now use Codex each week for software development, research, analysis and workflow automation, a figure that has grown 400% since earlier this year.

According to the company, some of the most valuable work performed by Codex now unfolds over hours or days rather than minutes, increasing demand for persistent execution environments that remain available beyond a single device or active session.

Founded to help developers move software development workloads from local machines into cloud-based environments, Ona says its platform has been used by more than 2 million developers.

Ona provides cloud-based execution environments designed specifically for AI software agents. Rather than running on a developer’s laptop, agents operate inside isolated cloud workspaces with access to code repositories, development tools, network resources and enterprise systems.

The platform also includes governance features such as credential management, audit logs, security policies and customer-controlled access controls, allowing organisations to run agents within their own cloud infrastructure.

OpenAI plans to integrate that technology into Codex, allowing agents to continue operating within an organisation’s own cloud infrastructure while OpenAI provides the models and orchestration layer.

Calling it the “next phase of Codex”, OpenAI says that this integration will enable agents to “continue working inside a customer’s cloud environment even when laptops are closed.”

The company said the approach is designed to meet enterprise requirements around data residency, access controls, credential management, logging and review processes.

“Agents need more than intelligence; they need a trusted workspace,” said Johannes Landgraf, Ona’s Co-Founder and Chief Executive. “We built Ona to give agents cloud environments with the context, control and collaboration enterprises require.”

Thibault Sottiaux, OpenAI’s Core Products Lead, said enterprises increasingly want AI agents that can perform operational work while meeting existing security and compliance requirements. “Ona will help us make Codex easier to deploy securely across production workflows for customers operating at the highest standards of trust and scale," he said.

The acquisition remains subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals. OpenAI said the Ona team will join the company after the transaction closes and will work on enterprise execution capabilities for Codex, including software engineering workflows such as testing, issue resolution, application modernisation, and vulnerability remediation, which may require agents to operate continuously over extended periods.

The Ona acquisition adds to a series of OpenAI transactions aimed at expanding Codex beyond its core models. In March, OpenAI agreed to acquire Python tooling company Astral, bringing its development tools into the Codex platform as competition intensified with Anthropic's Claude Code. OpenAI said at the time that Codex had surpassed 2 million weekly active users.

title: Karnataka to Establish 50 AI Labs in Govt Colleges to Boost Future-Ready Skills
content:
Under the IndiaAI Mission, each laboratory will receive financial assistance of ₹68.98 lakh over three years, disbursed in three instalments

What Actually Matters.

Karnataka plans to establish 50 AI laboratories in government colleges to enhance access to emerging technologies.

The initiative aims to equip students in tier-2 and tier-3 cities with industry-relevant skills for the digital economy.

In a significant push to democratise access to emerging technologies and strengthen the state's digital talent pipeline, the Karnataka government will establish 50 AI laboratories in government colleges across the state.

The initiative, announced in the Karnataka State Budget 2026-27, will be implemented in collaboration with the IndiaAI Mission and is aimed at equipping students—particularly those in tier-2 and tier-3 cities—with industry-relevant skills in cutting-edge technologies.

The AI laboratories will offer hands-on training in AI, machine learning, data science, and other advanced technologies through practical learning modules, innovation-driven projects, and skill development programmes. The move is expected to enhance employability among students while preparing them for careers in the rapidly evolving digital economy.

Announcing the initiative, Priyank Kharge, Karnataka's Minister for Home, Information Technology, Biotechnology, and E-Governance, emphasised the importance of expanding access to technology education beyond major urban centres.

“The future of employment will be shaped by technology, and it is imperative that opportunities to acquire these skills are accessible beyond major urban centres. Through these AI Laboratories, we are enabling students in tier-2 and tier-3 regions to gain hands-on exposure to emerging technologies, build industry-relevant capabilities and participate meaningfully in the digital economy,” he said.

The laboratories will be equipped with modern AI-enabled infrastructure designed to support experimentation, practical learning, innovation, and problem-solving. The government believes the initiative will help bridge the gap between academic learning and industry requirements while fostering technological proficiency among students.

Under the IndiaAI Mission, each laboratory will receive financial assistance of ₹68.98 lakh over three years, disbursed in three instalments. Complementing this support, the Karnataka government has sanctioned ₹10 crore for the project, with ₹6.29 crore earmarked for release during the first year.

As part of the rollout, the state has also approved the selection of 23 educational institutions in the first phase to establish AI data laboratories.

The initiative aligns with Karnataka's broader vision of strengthening its innovation ecosystem and ensuring that access to advanced technology infrastructure extends beyond metropolitan hubs.

Manufacturers face pressure to shorten development timelines while managing software complexity. Testing PLM workflows and integrations has become harder as companies expand their use of digital engineering systems, as per Keysight.

“Engineers can now reduce the risk of undetected issues when upgrades or integrations are released, maintaining system performance and reliability at every stage of the product lifecycle,” Smith said.

title: MNIT Jaipur Gets Advanced Quantum and AI Labs, Access to Lam Research’s Semiverse Platform
content:
The Semiverse Solutions platform will enable students to study semiconductor chip structures in 3D, understand fabrication processes, and simulate manufacturing workflows in a virtual environment.

What Actually Matters.

MNIT Jaipur is establishing Advanced Quantum Computing and AI Labs to enhance capabilities in emerging technologies.

The quantum lab will focus on Quantum Key Distribution, quantum computing simulation, and quantum sensing hardware.

Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, Railways and Information & Broadcasting, Ashwini Vaishnaw, announced the establishment of an Advanced Quantum Computing and Quantum Communications Lab and an Artificial Intelligence Lab at the Malaviya National Institute of Technology (MNIT), Jaipur, as part of the government’s push to build indigenous capabilities in emerging technologies.

The quantum lab, to be established under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology’s (MeitY) Electronics and ICT Academic Project, will focus on developing domestic expertise in Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), quantum computing simulation, and quantum sensing hardware components.

The initiative is aimed at strengthening India’s capabilities in next-generation computing and secure communications technologies.

Addressing students and faculty members, Vaishnaw said, “While the current technological wave is being driven by AI, the next major technological wave will be led by Quantum Technology.”

Highlighting the strategic significance of the initiative, the minister noted that research in Quantum Key Distribution would be critical for national security and urged MNIT Jaipur to take a leadership role in post-quantum cryptography.

In a parallel move to strengthen semiconductor talent development, Vaishnaw announced that MNIT students will gain access to Lam Research’s Semiverse Solutions platform, a digital twin-based semiconductor fabrication and training ecosystem. The platform will enable students to study semiconductor chip structures in 3D, understand fabrication processes, and simulate manufacturing workflows in a virtual environment.

The minister said the global semiconductor industry is expected to require more than one million semiconductor design professionals, presenting a significant opportunity for India’s engineering talent pool.

He pointed out that companies such as NVIDIA, Qualcomm, ARM and AMD are already designing advanced 2-nanometre and 3-nanometre semiconductor chips in India, driven by the country’s growing semiconductor design workforce.

Vaishnaw also highlighted the progress of the government’s Chips to Startup (C2S) Programme, under which Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools from leading companies, including Synopsys, Cadence and Renesas, have been provided to more than 323 universities across the country.

According to the minister, over 100 student-designed chips from Indian institutions have already been fabricated at the Semiconductor Laboratory (SCL), Mohali, demonstrating the growing capabilities of India’s semiconductor ecosystem.

Alongside the quantum initiative, the government will establish an AI Lab at MNIT Jaipur equipped with advanced computing infrastructure and research tools. The facility will be integrated with the broader IndiaAI Mission network to support AI innovation and research.

Referring to ongoing AI research in the country, Vaishnaw highlighted work being carried out at IIT Jodhpur to develop deepfake detection technologies, indicating the government’s focus on responsible AI applications.

The minister also inaugurated a new Makers Lab at MNIT Jaipur, along with Rajasthan’s Minister of State for Energy, Heeralal Nagar, and MLA Gopal Sharma. The facility is designed to provide students with hands-on experience across software and hardware technologies, including sensors, embedded systems, electronics, and computing devices.

During his visit, Vaishnaw interacted with students and faculty members and reviewed projects spanning AI, robotics, drones, structural engineering, and post-quantum cryptography, underscoring the government’s emphasis on building a future-ready technology talent pipeline.

title: Equal AI Raises $30 Million to Expand Beyond Call Management Into Everyday AI Services
content:
Backed by Prosus Ventures and Tomales Bay Capital, the company aims to evolve from a call assistant into a comprehensive AI companion for everyday tasks.

What Actually Matters.

Equal AI has raised $30 million in Series B funding to enhance its AI capabilities.

The company aims to evolve from a call assistant to an everyday AI companion for users.

Equal AI, the company behind India’s AI-powered call assistant has raised $30 million in a Series B funding round co-led by Prosus Ventures and Tomales Bay Capital. The funding will be used to expand the platform’s AI capabilities and support its vision of becoming an everyday AI assistant for Indian users.

The latest round comes less than a year after the company raised $10 million in its Series A funding round. The investment also saw participation from Think Investments, Valiant Fund, PhonePe Founder Sameer Nigam, Airtel Family Office’s Zubin Bharti Mittal and several other strategic investors.

Founded in 2022, Equal initially started as a data-sharing and identity infrastructure company before entering the consumer AI space in October 2025 with the launch of its AI call assistant.

According to the company, Equal AI has surpassed one million monthly active users and 3,50,000 daily active users, making it one of India’s largest AI voice products. The platform helps users manage incoming calls by blocking spam, identifying callers, understanding caller intent and taking actions on behalf of users.

The company now plans to expand beyond call management into areas such as communications, financial services, shopping, lifestyle and concierge services.

Keshav Reddy, Founder of Equal, said, “The company is building a long-term AI platform for Indian consumers.”

“More than a million Indians are already using Equal AI every month to take back control of their phones. We are now expanding beyond calls into several everyday services to create a trusted AI assistant for every Indian,” he added.

Thiago Viana, Global Co-Head of Prosus Ventures, described Equal AI as a “category-defining” consumer AI product. He added that the company has the potential to become an AI lifestyle concierge for millions of Indians.

“Equal AI’s rapid growth reflects a broader shift in consumer behaviour, with users increasingly trusting AI tools to handle communication and routine tasks,” noted Iqbaljit Kahlon, Founder and Managing Partner, Tomales Bay Capital.

The company said the fresh capital will be used to strengthen its AI assistant capabilities, scale operations and accelerate product development as it targets India’s growing smartphone user base.

title: NEURA Robotics Raises Up To $1.4 Billion in Series C, Largest Ever for a Full-Stack Robotics Company
content:
The German robotics startup has secured funding from Tether, Amazon, and NVIDIA, among others, to expand its global presence and aims to produce millions of robots by 2030.

What Actually Matters.

NEURA Robotics has secured up to $1.4 billion in Series C funding, the largest ever for a full-stack robotics company.

The funding aims to expand NEURA's global presence and facilitate the production of millions of robots by 2030.

German cognitive robotics firm NEURA Robotics has closed the largest Series C ever raised by a full-stack robotics company, securing up to $1.4 billion to scale its Physical AI platform globally.

The Metzingen-based company, founded in 2019, has received funding from Tether, Amazon, NVIDIA, Qualcomm Technologies, Bosch, Schaeffler Group, the European Investment Bank, imec.xpand, Lingotto Horizon, and InterAlpen Partners among the backers in the round. The funding marks a vote of confidence in the company's bet that the next frontier of AI will be physical, not digital.

NEURA builds cognitive robots capable of perceiving, reasoning, and acting in real-world environments, alongside the AI software and data infrastructure needed to deploy them at scale. Its product portfolio spans humanoid and industrial robots, with existing orders and deployment commitments exceeding $1 billion.

Central to its strategy is the Neuraverse, an open ecosystem where robots across deployments share skills, sensor data, and real-world learning in real time. The company is also rolling out NEURA Gyms, large-scale physical training environments designed to generate the kind of embodied data that digital simulation alone cannot replicate.

The capital will fund serial production toward a target of multi-million robots by 2030, alongside global expansion of both the Neuraverse platform and the Gym network.

Founder and CEO David Reger frames the raise as proof that globally relevant AI infrastructure companies can emerge outside Silicon Valley. “The future of AI will not only live on screens. It will move, interact, learn and work beside us in the real world. We believe Physical AI and cognitive robotics will become one of the largest technology shifts of the coming decades, transforming industries ranging from manufacturing and logistics to healthcare, services and household robotics,” he said in a statement.

"With this financing, NEURA is firmly among the global leaders in the robotics race, alongside the best in the US and China," he added.

Strategic partners are integrating their own stacks into the platform. Qualcomm brings edge AI compute, Amazon contributes cloud infrastructure through Bedrock and SageMaker, and Bosch adds sensor and actuator technology. Tether, through its QVAC and WDK products, is building edge-first intelligence and machine-native financial infrastructure into the ecosystem.

Paolo Ardoino, CEO of Tether, added, “Autonomous machines need the ability to process information locally, make decisions, and transact without relying on centralised intermediaries. QVAC brings that edge-first intelligence to the platform while WDK handles the secure financial layer, together enabling machines to execute tasks, account for outcomes, and operate independently.”

NEURA also signals longer-term ambitions around decentralised AI architectures and autonomous machine economics, areas it intends to develop alongside infrastructure partners as robots move into factories, logistics centres, and homes.

title: Equal AI Raises $30 Million to Expand Beyond Call Management Into Everyday AI Services
content:
Once known primarily for rocket launches, SpaceX now derives the majority of its revenue from Starlink, its fast-growing satellite internet business.

What Actually Matters.

SpaceX's IPO raised $75 billion, making it the largest public offering to date and valuing the company at $1.77 trillion.

Elon Musk's stake in SpaceX and Tesla positions him as the world's first trillionaire.

SpaceX raised $75 billion in its blockbuster IPO on June 11 in what is the largest public offering to date, valuing the company at $1.77 trillion and propelling founder Elon Musk to become the world’s first trillionaire. The listing surpassed the previous record set by Saudi Aramco’s $29.4 billion IPO in 2019 by a wide margin.

The company has sold 555.6 million shares at a fixed price of $135 each, according to its filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. SpaceX begins trading on the Nasdaq today, June 12, 2026, under the ticker symbol SPCX.

Musk’s stake in SpaceX is valued at roughly $866.5 billion. Combined with his Tesla holdings worth about $320 billion, it would make him the world’s first trillionaire.

SpaceX is on track to become among the most valuable US companies at $1.77 trillion, surpassing Tesla, Musk’s electric vehicle manufacturer.

Despite its lofty valuation, SpaceX remains unprofitable. The company reported first-quarter revenue of $4.69 billion, up 15% from a year earlier, while full-year revenue rose 33% to $18.67 billion in 2025. SpaceX posted a net loss of $4.28 billion in the latest quarter and has accumulated a deficit of roughly $41.3 billion since its founding in 2002.

The company going public today looks very different from the rocket startup Musk founded more than two decades ago. The business now spans satellite internet, launch services, and artificial intelligence. Following its merger with xAI in February 2026, SpaceX also owns the Grok chatbot and social media platform X. The company says these assets will help power its plan to build orbital data centres to provide computing capacity from space.

Starlink continued to drive SpaceX’s business in the first quarter of 2026, with connectivity revenue reaching $3.26 billion, or nearly 70% of the company’s total revenue of $4.69 billion. The satellite internet service's subscriber base also doubled year-over-year to 10.3 million.

According to its IPO prospectus, the company continues to invest aggressively in growth. Capital expenditures reached $10.1 billion in the first quarter, more than double the level recorded a year earlier. Approximately $7.7 billion of that spending was directed toward AI infrastructure, with the remainder allocated to its space and satellite connectivity operations.

title: Happiest Minds Launches Agentic AI Platform to Automate Software Engineering Tasks
content:
The platform deploys autonomous software engineering agents across development workflows, signalling a shift from AI assistants to AI systems capable of executing end-to-end engineering tasks with human oversight.

What Actually Matters.

Happiest Minds has launched an agentic AI platform to automate software development and modernisation tasks.

The platform, Rel(AI)Build, deploys specialised AI agents throughout the software development lifecycle.

Happiest Minds Technologies has launched a proprietary agentic AI platform aimed at automating software development and modernisation projects, reflecting a wider push by IT services firms to embed autonomous AI agents into engineering workflows as enterprises seek productivity gains from generative AI.

The company introduced Rel(AI)Build, an enterprise-grade agentic platform that deploys specialised AI agents across different stages of the software development lifecycle.

The platform is built around what the company calls an Agentic Development Lifecycle (ADLC), a framework designed to coordinate AI agents while maintaining governance and human oversight.

The launch comes as IT services providers increasingly move beyond AI copilots and coding assistants towards agentic systems capable of executing multi-step software engineering tasks with limited human intervention.

According to Happiest Minds, early implementations of the platform have helped reduce application modernisation timelines by 40% to 60%, improve engineering productivity by up to three times and lower support costs by 30% to 50%.

“Software engineering is entering a new era where AI actively participates in the delivery process,” Sridhar Mantha, Chief Executive Officer, GenAI Business Services at Happiest Minds, said in a statement. “With Rel(AI)Build and our Agentic Development Lifecycle, we are enabling enterprises to accelerate innovation, improve agility, and achieve measurable business outcomes while maintaining governance and quality at scale.”

The platform is designed to work with existing enterprise development environments and supports initiatives such as application modernisation, platform engineering, quality engineering, data engineering, infrastructure management and cybersecurity operations.

The move highlights how IT services companies are increasingly building proprietary AI platforms and frameworks instead of relying solely on third-party models.

For Happiest Minds, which has positioned itself as an AI-first digital engineering company, the launch forms part of a broader effort to expand its generative AI-led services portfolio and capture growing enterprise spending on AI-enabled transformation projects.

title: Infosys Partners with CMMI Institute to Develop AI Maturity Framework for Enterprises
content:
Infosys has become among the first organisations to complete its pilot assessment on the CMMI Institute’s framework.

What Actually Matters.

Infosys has partnered with the CMMI Institute to develop the CMMI AI Maturity Framework for enterprise AI implementation.

The framework aims to assist organisations in assessing and improving their AI governance and operational practices.

Infosys has collaborated with the CMMI Institute to help develop an enterprise AI maturity framework.

The framework, known as the CMMI AI Maturity (AIM) Framework, is designed to help organisations assess, benchmark, and improve AI implementation across enterprise and regulatory environments. According to Infosys, the framework links AI governance and operational practices to measurable business outcomes.

As an early participant in the pilot programme, Infosys said it contributed insights from large-scale AI deployments, governance models, and enterprise software engineering practices. The company used its AI offerings under the Infosys Topaz portfolio to support the initiative and validate elements of the framework across delivery environments.

“As one of the initial organisations to pilot the CMMI AIM framework and contribute to the content and assessment method, we are defining what responsible, enterprise-grade AI adoption looks like in practice. Powered by Infosys Topaz, our sustained investments in AI maturity across governance, productivity, and outcomes give our clients a tested, structured path to realise AI value at scale,” Dinesh Rao, Executive Vice President and Chief Delivery Officer, Infosys, said in a statement.

The pilot assessment covered AI-augmented software development, maintenance, testing, and support operations across Infosys' service lines and global delivery centres. The evaluation examined how AI is integrated into software engineering workflows, including productivity, quality, governance, and responsible AI practices.

Infosys said its participation helped refine aspects of the emerging model, including performance alignment to business outcomes, consistency of AI practices, risk and compliance management, and accountability in AI-driven decision-making. The company added that the framework is intended to provide enterprises with a structured approach to assessing AI adoption and maturity.

The pilot was conducted by the CMMI Institute, which develops process improvement and capability assessment frameworks, with consulting support from KPMG. Infosys said the recognition reflects its ongoing investments in AI-led software engineering and enterprise-scale AI deployment.

“Infosys brought deep, practical perspectives to the CMMI AIM pilot, reflecting the realities of deploying AI at scale in a global enterprise. Their participation…confirmed the usefulness of the CMMI AIM best practices that will help organisations worldwide adopt AI in a more structured, responsible, mature, and outcome-focused manner,” Ron Lear, Vice President, CMMI Global Strategies, CMMI Institute, added.

content:
LTM has initiated the AI 1000 programme to train over 1,000 AI-certified engineers amid increasing enterprise demand.

The programme focuses on developing forward-deployed engineers who integrate AI expertise with business knowledge.

LTM, formerly LTIMindtree, has launched a workforce transformation initiative aimed at creating more than 1,000 AI-certified engineers, betting on rising enterprise demand for professionals who can help deploy and scale artificial intelligence projects beyond pilot stages.

The programme, called AI 1000, will be anchored by a dedicated centre of excellence and focus on developing forward-deployed engineers (FDEs), a role that is gaining prominence as enterprises seek talent capable of combining AI expertise with business and domain knowledge.

The move reflects a broader shift underway in the technology services industry, where companies are increasingly investing in specialised AI talent as clients move from experimentation to large-scale deployment of generative AI and agentic AI applications.

According to LTM, FDEs serve as a bridge between AI technologies and business operations, helping organisations convert AI initiatives into measurable business outcomes and drive user adoption. The company said the programme is designed to create a structured pipeline of such talent through training, deployment and governance frameworks.

"The role of the technology engineer is evolving rapidly. AI 1000 is built with the purpose of enhancing workforce productivity in creating tangible business outcomes," Venu Lambu, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of LTM, said in a statement.

The programme follows a four-stage model that includes identifying engineers through an internal AI readiness assessment, providing AI-focused learning programmes, validating skills through hackathons and real-world projects, and deploying qualified employees into client engagements.

A governance framework will track performance and feed insights back into the programme, the company said.

LTM said it has already accumulated more than 6.5 million learning hours related to AI, achieved a learning penetration of nearly 84%, secured over 15,000 external AI certifications and trained more than 24,000 employees in AI-related skills.

title: Karnataka Approves ₹27 Crore to Boost Startups, Deep-Tech Research & Industry-Academia Collaboration
content:
The largest allocation includes ₹9.26 crore over five years for the establishment of the K-Combinator Startup Accelerator in Mangaluru in partnership with TiE-Mangaluru

What Actually Matters.

Karnataka's government has approved initiatives worth over ₹27 crore to enhance its innovation ecosystem outside Bengaluru.

The K-Combinator Startup Accelerator in Mangaluru will receive ₹9.26 crore to support local startups through mentorship and funding.

In a major push to strengthen Karnataka’s innovation ecosystem beyond Bengaluru, the state government has approved four strategic initiatives worth over ₹27 crore spanning startup acceleration, industry-academia collaboration, medical robotics, and advanced genome-editing research.

The projects, approved through the Department of Electronics, IT, Biotechnology and Science & Technology (ITBT), Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS), Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM), academic institutions, and ecosystem partners, are aimed at accelerating entrepreneurship, enhancing employability, and strengthening Karnataka’s leadership in deep-tech innovation.

“These approvals reflect Karnataka’s commitment to investing across the full innovation spectrum—from startups and talent development to frontier research in biotechnology, genomics and medical robotics. By strengthening regional innovation ecosystems, industry-academia partnerships and deep-tech research capabilities, we are creating the foundations for the next generation of jobs, enterprises and scientific breakthroughs,” said Priyank Kharge, Karnataka Minister for Home, IT and BT, and e-Governance.

The largest allocation includes ₹9.26 crore over five years to establish the K-Combinator Startup Accelerator in Mangaluru in partnership with TiE-Mangaluru under the Local Economy Accelerator Programme (LEAP). The accelerator will support startups in the Udupi-Mangaluru region through mentorship, access to funding, market linkages, and ecosystem support, with a focus on helping early-stage ventures achieve product-market fit and scale.

The government has also sanctioned ₹7.47 crore for the Super 100 Industry-Academia Adoption Programme, which will create one-to-one partnerships between 100 industry partners and 100 higher education institutions, particularly across tier-2 and tier-3 cities. Implemented through KDEM, the programme aims to bridge the gap between academic curricula and industry requirements through mentorship, faculty development, research collaboration, and real-world projects.

On the deep-tech front, Karnataka has approved ₹3.66 crore for the development of an Advanced Surgical Assistive Robot, an indigenous collaborative robotic platform designed for neurosurgical applications. The project will be jointly developed by IIIT-Bengaluru and NIMHANS and aims to improve precision, safety, and accessibility in complex surgical procedures through advanced imaging, sensors, real-time monitoring systems, and software-assisted interventions.

Further strengthening the state’s biotechnology ambitions, the government has sanctioned ₹6.8 crore to expand infrastructure at the Centre for Human Genetics, Bengaluru. The expansion will support the newly established Institute of Advanced Genome Editing and Gene Therapy and create nearly 1,500 square metres of advanced scientific infrastructure, including clean rooms, tissue culture laboratories, and next-generation sequencing facilities.

Two of the four initiatives fall under the state’s LEAP programme, which seeks to create stronger innovation ecosystems outside Bengaluru and unlock new opportunities for entrepreneurship and economic development across emerging regional hubs.

The latest approvals come as Karnatakafaces increasing competition from states such as Telangana, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra in attracting startups, research investments, and deep-tech innovation. By focusing simultaneously on startup growth, talent development, biotechnology infrastructure, and indigenous technology development, the state is seeking to reinforce its position as India’s leading innovation and technology hub.

Collectively, the initiatives represent a strategic investment of ₹27.19 crore aimed at building stronger regional innovation ecosystems, promoting industry-academia collaboration, advancing healthcare and biotechnology research, and supporting the development of globally competitive startups and deep-tech solutions.

title: Publicis Sapient Launches AI-Led IT Operations Platform as Firms Seek to Cut Support Costs
content:
As enterprises grapple with increasingly complex IT environments amid rising AI adoption, Publicis Sapient has launched Sapient Sustain, an AI-driven IT operations platform that automates incident management and support workflows.

What Actually Matters.

Publicis Sapient has introduced Sapient Sustain, an AI-driven platform for automating IT operations and incident management.

The platform aims to reduce operational costs and enhance the reliability of complex technology environments.

Publicis Sapient has launched an AI-enabled IT operations and managed services platform aimed at helping enterprises automate incident management, reduce operational costs and improve the reliability of increasingly complex technology environments.

The platform, called Sapient Sustain, uses agentic AI to detect issues, automate resolution workflows and prevent recurring failures across both legacy and modern IT systems, the company said in a statement on June 11.

The launch comes as enterprises expand their use of artificial intelligence, creating more distributed and fragmented technology environments that are increasingly difficult to manage through traditional IT support models.

Publicis Sapient said conventional automation tools often struggle to provide the context and coordination required to operate at scale, resulting in slower resolution times and higher operational costs.

The company claims Sapient Sustain can help reduce IT operational costs by up to 45% and improve mean time to resolution by up to eight times through a combination of AI agents and human expertise.

“Enterprises are under increasing pressure to improve reliability, reduce costs, and operate at greater speed,” Nigel Vaz, CEO of Publicis Sapient, said in a statement. “Sapient Sustain introduces a new model for IT operations: one where AI agents and human expertise work together to anticipate issues and resolve them before they impact the business. This is a shift from reactive support to intelligent, self-healing operations.”

The platform is built around an enterprise context graph that connects data from tickets, logs and systems, self-healing workflows, a consolidated knowledge base and predictive models that identify issues before they affect business operations.

According to the company, these capabilities can be deployed across multi-cloud environments through pre-built and customisable AI agents.

The company cited early deployments at Japanese automaker Nissan Motor Corporation and global food and beverage chain Joe & The Juice.

The launch reflects a broader trend among technology services firms to move beyond conventional managed services by embedding AI agents into IT operations.

As enterprises invest more heavily in AI applications, vendors are increasingly positioning autonomous operations platforms to manage growing technology complexity while reducing support costs and manual intervention.

title: Deloitte India Launches AI-Led SAP Delivery Centre in Bengaluru, Plans to Hire Up to 500 AI Specialists
content:
Deloitte plans to add approximately 300 to 500 specialised AI professionals over the next 12 to 24 months.

What Actually Matters.

Deloitte India has launched a dedicated AI-led SAP Delivery Centre in Bengaluru to support enterprise transformation.

The centre will enhance cloud adoption and AI-driven business transformation for SAP and its customers.

Deloitte India has inaugurated a dedicated SAP Delivery Centre in Bengaluru. The centre will serve as an AI-led innovation and delivery hub to support SAP’s transformation priorities while helping enterprises accelerate cloud adoption, intelligent automation, and AI-driven business transformation.

The new facility reinforces India’s growing role as a global hub for enterprise technology, cloud modernisation, and AI innovation. Deloitte said in the release that the centre will support SAP and joint customers across the entire transformation lifecycle, including innovation, architecture, engineering, implementation, and managed services.

The centre is backed by an existing ecosystem of more than 1,000 professionals across India and is expected to expand significantly over the next two years. Deloitte plans to add approximately 300 to 500 specialised AI professionals over the next 12 to 24 months, focusing on emerging technology domains such as generative AI, agentic AI, machine learning, cloud architecture, data engineering, and intelligent automation.

According to the company, the Bengaluru facility has been designed to help organisations modernise legacy systems, accelerate the adoption of SAP cloud solutions, unlock business value through AI, and build intelligent operating models for the future.

Commenting on the launch, Sathish Gopalaiah, president, consulting businesses, Deloitte South Asia, said, “The Deloitte–SAP Delivery Centre underscores our shared commitment to driving innovation through AI, cloud and advanced technologies. As organisations accelerate digital transformation, this centre will serve as a catalyst for developing next-generation solutions, enabling SAP and our joint clients to harness emerging technologies, scale innovation and deliver differentiated, technology-led outcomes globally.”

A key component of the new delivery centre is a dedicated AI Command Centre and prototyping lab, designed to accelerate experimentation and enterprise AI adoption. The lab will provide access to tools, mentorship, and collaborative development environments, enabling both technical and business teams to transform ideas into deployable AI solutions.

The initiative also aims to democratise AI innovation across enterprises by supporting the development of scalable frameworks, accelerators, and reusable assets that can simplify complex transformation programmes and improve operational efficiency.

The launch comes amid increasing enterprise demand for AI-powered business applications and cloud-based transformation services. Consulting firms and enterprise software providers are increasingly investing in dedicated AI delivery capabilities as organisations move from AI experimentation to large-scale deployment.

title: IN-SPACe Backs 3 Startups to Build Rocket Engines, Satellite AI, Star Trackers
content:
Funding under IN-SPACe’s Technology Adoption Fund targets propulsion, Earth observation, and satellite navigation technologies.

What Actually Matters.

IN-SPACe has selected three startups for funding to advance rocket propulsion, Earth observation, and satellite navigation technologies.

The funded companies are Astrobase Space Technologies, SatSure Analytics India, and TakeMe2Space, marking a significant step for non-government entities.

The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) has selected three Indian space startups for funding under its Technology Adoption Fund (TAF) scheme, backing projects in rocket propulsion, Earth observation AI, and satellite navigation systems.

The agency said that Bengaluru-based Astrobase Space Technologies and SatSure Analytics India, along with Hyderabad-based TakeMe2Space (TM2S), will receive financial support. This will take place after a multi-stage evaluation process involving experts from ISRO, the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, the Department of Science and Technology, industry, academic institutions, and IN-SPACe.

The selected projects aim to strengthen India’s domestic space capabilities and reduce dependence on foreign technologies. The three companies are the first non-government entities (NGEs) selected under the TAF scheme, which aims to help Indian firms absorb, adapt and commercialise advanced space technologies.

Pawan Goenka, Chairman of IN-SPACe, said in a statement, “With this fund, our vision is to bridge the critical gap between early-stage development and commercial success. These projects are not just innovative concepts; they are practical, market-ready solutions that will increase our footprint in the global space economy.”

Bengaluru-based Astrobase Space Technologies will develop a high-thrust reusable liquid rocket engine for launch vehicles. The company said it is building an 80-ton Full Flow Staged Combustion LOX-methane engine with an 800 kN thrust class and a modular design for medium-to-heavy lift launch vehicles.

Astrobase said the engine is already undergoing hot-fire testing at its propulsion facility in Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh. The startup operates a 46,000 sq ft assembly facility in Bengaluru, where it designs and builds propulsion and vehicle systems. It said the engine programme forms part of its effort to develop indigenous propulsion systems and reduce India’s reliance on imported technologies.

Also, SatSure Analytics India will build Dhaarini, a Large Earth Observation Model designed as an AI platform for remote sensing applications. The model will be trained on satellite and aerial datasets to generate insights across agriculture, infrastructure, and disaster management.

Meanwhile, TM2S will develop StarSense, an indigenous AI-powered star tracker system for satellites. The company plans to build two variants: StarSense Lite for CubeSats and StarSense Pro for satellites weighing more than 50 kg.

Star trackers help satellites determine pointing direction with high accuracy for imaging and communication missions. TM2S said Indian manufacturers currently import most such systems from the United States and Europe, making the technology one of the key satellite subsystems still sourced from overseas.

The company said the StarSense project follows a 24-month development timeline from laboratory testing to a fully qualified flight-ready model. TM2S added that the technology has already completed space qualification across two orbital missions in 2024.

Rajeev Jyoti, Director of Technical Directorate at IN-SPACe, said the selected projects address “critical technology gaps” in India’s space ecosystem.

India is expected to launch around 150 satellites over the next three years, according to TM2S. The company estimates this could create demand for at least 300 star trackers, as commercial missions often use dual systems for redundancy. It is also developing an indigenous lens assembly with Hyderabad-based Eon Space Labs.

Beyond satellite navigation systems, TM2S said StarSense will support its wider ambition to build a 1 GW orbital data centre through a planned constellation of 20,000 compute satellites. The company said developing critical hardware locally would help secure supply chains for the long-term project.

“Spanning a reusable high-thrust rocket engine, a foundational EO-AI platform, and indigenous high-accuracy star trackers, these projects address critical technology gaps and have strong real-world potential to enhance India’s space capabilities,” Jyoti said.

IN-SPACe said it will provide technical guidance, monitoring, and milestone-linked disbursement of funds to support the selected projects. The TAF scheme was created to bridge the gap between research and operational deployment of advanced space technologies in India.

title: GlobalFoundries, FermionIC Partner to Manufacture RF Chips in India
content:
The partnership aims to help Indian fabless startups move from chip design to commercial production.

What Actually Matters.

GlobalFoundries and FermionIC have partnered to manufacture RF chips in India, aiding fabless startups in transitioning from design to production.

The collaboration supports FermionIC in scaling its RF and millimetre-wave semiconductor products for various applications, including defence and satellite communications.

GlobalFoundries Engineering Private Limited (GF India) and Indian semiconductor startup FermionIC have entered a commercial partnership under which GF will manufacture the startup’s radio-frequency (RF) chips.

The partnership will support FermionIC’s move from chip design to production and help scale its RF and millimetre-wave semiconductor products for satellite communications, defence, and infrastructure applications.

“Moving RF chips from design to production is particularly challenging,” said Gautam Kumar Singh, CEO of FermionIC. “Our collaboration with GlobalFoundries India enables us to deliver complex, production-grade RF silicon, not just prototypes, and build the confidence required by our customers in strategic applications.”

FermionIC is part of an early group of Indian fabless semiconductor firms under the Indian government’s Design Linked Incentive (DLI) scheme. The collaboration also reflects GF India’s push to support chip startups through its India Foundry Connect programme.

RF semiconductor products remain among the most difficult chips to design and manufacture because they require strict process control and manufacturing expertise. The companies said the partnership shows that Indian startups can navigate the entire semiconductor journey, from design to production.

Singh said FermionIC needed more than a manufacturing vendor at this stage of its growth. He said the startup required a partner with RF expertise and production support to help execute commercial-grade manufacturing.

GF India’s India Foundry Connect programme gives companies access to product design kits, multi-project wafer services, intellectual property libraries, and engineering support for RF and other semiconductor technologies. GF India said the model combines local engineering teams in India with GF’s manufacturing operations to speed up the transition to production.

“This partnership is about demonstrating what’s possible and then replicating it across the Indian fabless startup ecosystem at scale,” said Rohit Tickoo, Sales Director for GF India.

FermionIC said it plans to expand its RF product roadmap into additional applications and use more GF technologies as its semiconductor portfolio grows.

title: Space Startup PierSight Opens Trials for New Forest-Penetrating SAR System
content:
The SAR system, Vidura, aims to help defence operators detect movement and structures beneath dense forest cover.

What Actually Matters.

PierSight has launched trials for Vidura, a Synthetic Aperture Radar system designed for forest surveillance.

Vidura enables detection of movement and structures beneath dense foliage, regardless of weather conditions.

PierSight, an Ahmedabad-based space tech startup, has opened trials for Vidura, an airborne Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) payload designed for tactical surveillance through forest cover.

The company said defence operators can begin testing the system immediately. Vidura aims to support reconnaissance by detecting concealed movement and structures beneath dense foliage in all weather conditions.

The radar system works through foliage, cloud cover and darkness, unlike optical systems that often struggle in such environments. It can also support stand-off intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance missions from friendly airspace. The company developed the system in India and designed it for use across multiple unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) platforms.

Vidura marks PierSight’s second SAR system after Varuna, the company’s planned 32-satellite SAR+AIS constellation for maritime surveillance. The startup said it adapted the same SAR technology used for maritime monitoring to land-based tactical surveillance.

“When we built Varuna, we built more than a satellite; we built a team and a body of IP that could be reshaped for any SAR mission,” said Gaurav Seth, Founder and CEO of PierSight. “Vidura came directly out of that work. The same engineers, the same core technology, redesigned for a completely different operating environment.”

PierSight said Vidura supports P, L, and X-band configurations, allowing wide-swath coverage. The system also remains drone-agnostic, which means defence personnel can deploy it on different UAV platforms without depending on a single manufacturer.

The system has already secured initial contracts from a few organisations and plans to conduct several field trials through 2026. PierSight also seeks partnerships with drone manufacturers to integrate the radar payload into their systems and take a combined radar-drone solution to market.

Founded by former ISRO scientist Gaurav Seth, PierSight builds application-specific SAR systems for maritime, defence and related sectors. The company said Vidura is currently available through an early, limited-access launch for defence operators.

title: AI is Eating Away at Indian IT's Old Business. Can it Rewrite Enterprise Playbook?
content:
The funding will support the development of humanoid robots and advanced AI systems, following Reliance’s previous $132 million investment in 2021.

What Actually Matters.

Addverb Technologies aims to raise over $100 million to enhance its robotics and AI capabilities.

The company plans to develop humanoid robots and advanced automation technologies, building on Reliance's previous investment.

Reliance Industries-backed robotics firm Addverb Technologies is looking to raise more than $100 million to accelerate investments in humanoid robots, artificial intelligence, and advanced automation technologies, according to Bloomberg.

The fundraising effort comes as the company seeks to strengthen its position in the global robotics industry and expand its international footprint. Addverb, which develops robots for warehouse automation, logistics and industrial applications, has already established operations in markets including the US, the Netherlands and Australia, according to Founder and CEO Sangeet Kumar.

“We want to be in the top 10 in the next five years and top five in the next 10 years,” Kumar reportedly said, adding that the company currently estimates its position at just outside the world's top 30 robotics firms by revenue.

The proposed capital raise would be Addverb’s first major funding round since 2021, when Reliance invested $132 million and acquired a controlling stake in the company. The fresh funds will primarily be used to develop humanoid and quadruped robots, build artificial intelligence systems and collect data to train increasingly sophisticated machines.

Kumar said that Addverb sees significant opportunities in the emerging humanoid robotics segment, where global players such as China’s Unitree Robotics and Tesla’s Optimus are vying for leadership. He said Indian companies can remain competitive by developing proprietary technologies and reducing dependence on imported components.

Founded in 2016 by four former Asian Paints engineers, Addverb has expanded beyond warehouse automation into factory automation, electronics manufacturing, healthcare, defence and research applications. Its customers include Lenskart, Hindustan Unilever and Reliance.

According to Bloomberg, nearly half of Addverb’s revenue now comes from international markets. Kumar expects revenue to reach 13 billion rupees ($136 million) in the current fiscal year, supported by an order book worth about $200 million, while an eventual initial public offering remains a longer-term objective.
