title: US Judge Strikes Down Trump’s $100,000 H-1B Visa Fee, Indians Stand to Benefit
content:
The ruling came in a lawsuit filed by 20 state attorneys general, while the Trump administration plans to appeal.

What Actually Matters.

A federal judge has ruled against Trump's $100,000 fee on H-1B visas, deeming it an unlawful tax.

The ruling was prompted by a lawsuit from 20 state attorneys general challenging the fee's legality.

A federal judge has struck down US President Donald Trump’s controversial $100,000 fee on new H-1B visas, ruling that the administration lacked congressional authority to impose what amounted to a tax on employers hiring foreign skilled workers.

US District Judge Leo Sorokin in Boston on June 8 ruled that the fee, announced by Trump in September, was unlawful and could not be enforced by the US State Department or US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS).

The decision came in response to a lawsuit filed by 20 state attorneys general challenging the measure.

The Trump administration had argued that the charge was a lawful penalty imposed under the president’s authority to restrict the entry of foreign nationals deemed detrimental to US interests. However, Sorokin found that the fee functioned as a tax rather than a penalty.

“Here, the substance and application of the $100,000 payment reveal that it is a tax, regardless of what the payment is called,” Sorokin wrote in his ruling.

The judge also pointed to a recent US Supreme Court decision that invalidated Trump’s broad tariff measures, saying the same legal reasoning applied in this case because immigration law does not grant the president authority to levy taxes.

The White House signalled it would challenge the ruling. “President Trump has clear legal authority to restrict entry of any class of aliens he determines is not in America’s best interests, and that is exactly what he did,” White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers said in a statement, adding that the administration expects the decision to be overturned on appeal.

The H-1B programme, widely used by technology companies and other employers to recruit specialised foreign talent, issues 65,000 visas annually, along with an additional 20,000 visas for applicants holding advanced degrees. Indian nationals account for the vast majority of visa recipients, securing over 70% of all approvals. Before Trump’s proclamation, employers typically paid between $2,000 and $5,000 in visa-related fees.

When introducing the fee, Trump argued that the H-1B programme “has been deliberately exploited to replace, rather than supplement, American workers with lower-paid, lower-skilled labour.”

The fee did not apply to foreign nationals already in the United States on student visas, a group that accounts for a significant share of new H-1B recipients. Even so, adoption of the measure remained limited. According to a USCIS official, the agency had received only 85 payments of the $100,000 fee as of February 15.

The administration has simultaneously pursued tighter scrutiny of H-1B applicants and proposed a revised visa allocation system that would prioritise higher-skilled and higher-paid workers.

title: Paytm Targets 10% Workforce Growth in AI Push Despite 400 Planned Layoffs: Report
content:
Reports say the pivot follows Paytm's recovery from recent regulatory hurdles, as it prioritises growth of its broader financial services suite.

What Actually Matters.

Paytm is set to grow its workforce by 10% through a hiring initiative, aiming to recruit around 4,000 employees.

Despite the recruitment drive, the company plans to lay off about 400 employees following performance reviews.

Paytm plans to hire around 4,000 employees over the next nine months as it expands its merchant network and AI-led product offerings, even as the fintech firm prepares to cut about 400 roles following its latest appraisal cycle.

According to reports, the recruitment drive would increase Paytm's workforce by roughly 10%, taking its headcount beyond the current level of around 40,000 employees. At the same time, the company is laying off about 1% of its workforce, or roughly 400 employees, after completing performance reviews, a company spokesperson said.

The hiring programme, which includes senior leadership positions, will continue through March 2027. Paytm plans to recruit across product, technology, and AI teams as it seeks to strengthen its offerings beyond payments.

"Over the last two months, we have added more than 800 people and are in the process of recruiting a further 4,000," the company said in a statement to Bloomberg.

The move comes as the company continues to rebuild after regulatory action against Paytm Payments Bank disrupted its operations. The digital payments company has been revamping its business since Indian regulators targeted its banking affiliate two years ago, Bloomberg reported.

CEO Vijay Shekhar Sharma said the company has been focusing on increasing the adoption of lending, investment, and other financial products among Paytm's large user base. The company has reported four consecutive profitable quarters, recovering from turmoil stemming from restrictions on its banking affiliate.

Bloomberg reported that Paytm cut more than 4,500 jobs in the aftermath of the regulatory curbs, citing company disclosures and previous reporting. The Reserve Bank of India subsequently cancelled the operating licence of Paytm Payments Bank, forcing a formal wind-down of the entity. Most employees at the banking affiliate have already been laid off, while some were absorbed into other parts of the group.

Paytm's shares gained about 2.5% at 12 pm on June 9 after the developments; however, they were down 18% year-to-date.

title: Dell Expands Solar Community Hubs Across India to Boost AI-Enabled Skilling & Digital Inclusion
content:
The Solar Community Hub programme has reached 18 districts across 14 states, directly impacting 2.67 million beneficiaries.

What Actually Matters.

Dell Technologies has launched five new solar community hubs in India, collaborating with the National Skill Development Corporation.

The initiative aims to bridge the digital divide and enhance employability through AI-enabled learning for underserved communities.

Dell Technologies has announced the launch of five new solar community hubs across India in collaboration with the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) and implemented by the Learning Links Foundation, expanding its global initiative to bridge the digital divide and enhance employability through AI-enabled learning.

The new hubs will be established across Uttar Pradesh, Delhi-NCR, Karnataka, Telangana, and Maharashtra, bringing solar-powered digital infrastructure, AI-enabled learning tools, and structured skilling pathways to youth, women, and underserved communities.

Each hub is powered by renewable energy and equipped with laptops, interactive screens, internet connectivity, and AI-driven learning systems designed to deliver education and training in areas where traditional digital infrastructure remains limited.

The initiative goes beyond basic digital literacy, offering customised skilling modules aligned with emerging labour market demands and extending support to more than 50 vocational, higher education, and community institutions.

Speaking on the expansion, Manish Gupta, President and Managing Director, Dell Technologies India, said, “Dell Technologies is committed to India's vision of inclusive, technology-led growth. The Solar Community Hubs are proof of what becomes possible when government, industry, and communities unite around a shared mission. These five new hubs will prepare a new generation of learners and workers for the jobs of tomorrow right in their own communities.”

The initiative was flagged off by Jayant Chaudhary, Union Minister of State (I/C) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, and Minister of State for Education, who highlighted the role of technology in expanding opportunities at the grassroots level.

“These hubs are more than digital spaces, they are centres of aspiration that combine clean energy, AI-enabled learning and industry-aligned skilling to prepare young people for emerging opportunities,” he said.

Since its launch in FY23, the Solar Community Hub programme has reached 18 districts across 14 states, directly impacting 2.67 million beneficiaries. Globally, Dell now operates 63 such hubs across 12 countries, reinforcing its focus on inclusive digital transformation.

The expansion reflects a broader push to integrate AI-enabled education, renewable energy infrastructure, and employability-focused training into community-level development models, aimed at preparing a future-ready workforce for emerging digital economy roles.

NXP Semiconductors’ new radar chip aims to cut costs and simplify advanced driver assistance systems in vehicles.

What Actually Matters.

NXP Semiconductors has introduced a new radar chip aimed at making advanced driver assistance systems more accessible.

The SAF8444 chip supports Level 2 and Level 2+ ADAS functions while simplifying design and reducing costs.

NXP Semiconductors has launched a new automotive radar system-on-chip (SoC) designed to bring advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) to mainstream vehicle platforms, including economy and entry-level models.

The SAF8444 chip enables on-sensor processing for Level 2 and Level 2+ ADAS functions while reducing system costs and design complexity. The company said the chip could support wider adoption, particularly in EV platforms.

NXP said the SAF8444 is currently in pre-production and targets next-generation front- and corner-radar systems. Development support for lead customers is already available.

“SAF8444 strengthens our one-chip radar portfolio with a solution that balances performance, power efficiency, and cost,” said Meindert van den Beld, Senior Vice President and General Manager, Radar and ADAS at NXP Semiconductors, in a statement.

“It allows customers to meet tightening safety requirements while reducing system cost, an essential step toward democratising ADAS adoption,” he added.

The chip also combines radar and camera data processing directly on the sensor, reducing dependence on central computing systems inside vehicles. NXP said the technology can help automakers and tier-1 suppliers meet safety demands, including future Euro NCAP 2030 requirements, while managing performance, compliance and cost.

The announcement comes as vehicle manufacturers face growing pressure to improve safety systems across price segments. Euro NCAP 2030 standards will require features such as detecting obstructed pedestrians in low-light conditions and maintaining performance in difficult weather environments.

NXP said the SAF8444 chip addresses these challenges by supporting perception-level processing directly at the radar sensor. The company added that this approach can reduce power consumption, simplify vehicle architecture and lower the overall bill of materials.

Built on NXP’s 28nm RFCMOS technology, the SAF8444 operates across the 76–81 GHz automotive radar band. It supports short-, medium-, and long-range sensing for functions such as adaptive cruise control, autonomous emergency braking, blind-spot detection, and park assist.

The chip also integrates embedded radar processing through an Arm Cortex-A53 application processor, an Arm Cortex-M7 real-time core, and NXP’s radar accelerator technology. The company said the system supports anti-jamming functions to improve radar reliability in congested radio frequency environments.

title: Google Orders Over 3 Mn AI Chips From Intel: Report
content:
NVIDIA is also reportedly testing Intel’s technology for some of its most advanced future AI chip designs.

What Actually Matters.

Google has ordered over three million AI chips from Intel to secure future capacity for its Tensor Processing Units.

The partnership with Intel may reduce the industry's reliance on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company for chip production.

Google and NVIDIA are exploring Intel as a potential backup manufacturing partner for advanced AI chips, according to a report by The Information.

The move could strengthen Intel’s ambitions to become a major contract chipmaker while reducing the industry’s dependence on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC).

Google has reportedly placed an order with Intel to manufacture more than three million of its in-house Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) in 2028.

Google’s commitment represents a concrete step to secure future capacity for its in-house AI accelerators, which power services like Search, cloud computing, and emerging agent platforms. The order would leverage Intel’s 18A process node and advanced packaging technologies, the report added.

NVIDIA has not committed to a production order but is evaluating Intel’s manufacturing technology for future AI processors. The tests reportedly include Intel’s advanced packaging capabilities and 18A process, which could be used to produce complex chips that integrate four GPUs into a single package, including future architectures such as Feynman.

The discussions come as soaring demand for AI hardware continues to strain TSMC’s manufacturing capacity, prompting some of the world’s largest AI chip designers to seek alternative production partners.

Intel’s foundry business, which manufactures chips for external customers, has been a key focus area under CEO Lip-Bu Tan as the company attempts to regain ground lost to TSMC over the past decade.

The filing comes as ChatGPT reaches about 900 million weekly active users and OpenAI pushes to expand the product beyond conversational AI.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI has filed a draft registration statement for an IPO, marking its first step towards going public.

The filing allows OpenAI flexibility in pursuing a public listing without revealing financial details immediately.

OpenAI on June 9 said it had confidentially submitted a draft registration statement on Form S-1 to the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), taking the first formal step towards a potential initial public offering.

“We have not decided on timing yet; it may be a while because there are things we want to do that are likely easier as a private company,” the company wrote in a post on X.

The announcement was made under Rule 135 of the Securities Act of 1933 and does not constitute an offer to sell securities.

OpenAI said the decision involves a complex set of trade-offs and that the filing provides flexibility to pursue a public listing sooner if it determines that is the best course of action.

OpenAI’s move also arrives as investors prepare for a wave of AI companies’ listings. Elon Musk’s SpaceX has already filed publicly and is expected to pursue one of the largest IPOs in market history, targeting a valuation of roughly $1.75 trillion and seeking to raise about $75 billion, according to Reuters.

OpenAI rival Anthropic also confidentially submitted its own draft S-1 registration statement to the SEC on June 1. The company recently raised $65 billion in fresh capital at a post-money valuation of $965 billion, overtaking OpenAI’s last reported valuation of $852 billion.

While OpenAI has not disclosed financial details, a confidential S-1 filing allows companies to begin the IPO process without immediately releasing revenue, profitability and governance information to the public. Those details typically become available closer to a public listing.

Meanwhile, OpenAI is preparing a major overhaul of its flagship product, ChatGPT. The company is reportedly working on its largest redesign since the chatbot’s launch, planning to transform ChatGPT into a superapp that combines coding tools, AI agents, and third-party services in a single interface, the Financial Times reported.

The move is intended to expand user engagement and create new revenue opportunities as competition intensifies across the AI industry.

With around 900 million weekly active users, ChatGPT has become one of the most widely used AI products globally.

In its latest blog post, OpenAI said it has entered the third phase of evolution, where AI is reshaping the economy.

Among its priorities, the company said it aims to build an automated AI researcher capable of accelerating the research process itself. “Our internal belief is that by March of 2028, we may have a significant fraction of our research being done by AI systems in tandem with our own researchers,” it said.

OpenAI also said the industry is moving beyond a focus on frontier AI models toward broader deployment and accessibility. “The central question now is how to make advanced AI abundant, affordable, safe, useful, and easy enough for every person and organisation to benefit from it,” the company said. “Frontier capability is only part of the job.”

It argued that access to AI should be broadly distributed rather than concentrated among a small number of institutions. “A good AI future cannot be one where a small number of institutions control most of the capability and most of the upside,” OpenAI said. “It should be a future where many people, companies, communities, and countries can build, benefit, and hold power.”

title: Zoho’s Sridhar Vembu Calls Salesforce a ‘Garbage Bin’
content:
Zoho’s Chief Scientist questioned Salesforce’s long-term pricing model and urged buyers to seek multi-year pricing commitments before switching.

What Actually Matters.

Sridhar Vembu criticises Salesforce for its aggressive discounting strategy to attract customers from Zoho.

He warns potential buyers to request multi-year pricing commitments before switching to Salesforce.

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu on Tuesday accused Salesforce of using steep discounts to win customers from Zoho. He took a dig at its global competitor, after Salesforce ran a campaign offering 40% discount on its flagship products and cloud services.

“We have watched this playbook for years where they give deep discounts to get you in, followed by aggressive escalation once you’re locked in,” he wrote on X.

Vembu urged prospective buyers to seek multi-year pricing commitments from Salesforce before signing contracts. “Before you switch anything, ask them to show you standardised multi-year pricing. If they don't, that's your answer,” he said.

He further described enterprise software pricing practices as “a con-game” by players like Salesforce.

The Zoho executive also took aim at Salesforce’s technology stack, arguing that years of acquisitions have left the company with a fragmented product portfolio. “Salesforce is a garbage bin of acquired enterprise software companies over decades, held together with bubble gum and duct tape,” he wrote.

The remarks mark the latest escalation in the long-running rivalry between Zoho and Salesforce in the customer relationship management (CRM) software market.

Responding to questions about competition from Zoho in an earlier interview with AIM, President & CEO of Salesforce India and South Asia, Arundhati Bhattacharya, said the company continues to rely on innovation to stay ahead. However, she did not directly comment on the pricing.

“We believe that we are always at the market, not behind the market,” Bhattacharya said. She added that customers trust Salesforce because they believe the company will help them keep pace with technological change.

Bhattacharya emphasised that innovation remains a core value for Salesforce, arguing that companies that can innovate at scale and at speed are likely to attract customers.

Founded in 1996, Zoho has increasingly positioned itself as a lower-cost alternative to larger enterprise software providers. The company offers a broad suite of business applications, including CRM software, and remains privately held. Vembu stepped down as Zoho’s CEO in 2025 to focus on research and development as Chief Scientist.

title: TCS Sets Up Dedicated GCC Unit to Oversee Strategy, AI-Led Transformation for Clients
content:
TCS has launched a dedicated Global Value and Innovation Centres business unit and appointed veteran executive Soumen Roy to lead it.

What Actually Matters.

TCS has launched the Global Value and Innovation Centres unit to aid enterprises in establishing and transforming global capability centres.

The new unit aims to integrate artificial intelligence into offshore operations, enhancing the roles of GCCs beyond traditional support functions.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has launched a dedicated business unit focused on helping enterprises establish and transform global capability centres (GCCs), as multinational companies increasingly look to embed artificial intelligence into their offshore operations.

The new unit, called Global Value and Innovation Centres (GVIC), will provide services spanning strategy, setup, operations, and AI-led transformation for GCCs.

TCS said the offering will help enterprises build "AI-native" GCCs and modernise existing centres into hubs focused on innovation and business outcomes.

The launch comes at a time when GCCs are moving beyond their traditional role as delivery and support centres to take ownership of products, platforms, and business functions. India remains the largest GCC market globally, with companies across sectors expanding their captive centres to access engineering talent and drive digital transformation initiatives.

As part of the move, TCS has appointed Soumen Roy to head the business unit. Roy, who most recently served as TCS Canada country head, will report to CEO and Managing Director K Krithivasan.

According to the company, the GVIC unit will bring together its GCC consulting and operational expertise with AI, cloud, engineering, and talent capabilities. The offering includes support for data and cloud foundations, enterprise platforms, talent development, and responsible AI frameworks.

“With TCS GVIC, we are bringing together TCS’ deep experience across the GCC lifecycle with our strengths in AI, engineering, talent, and operations to build high-impact, future-ready global centres that deliver sustained business value for clients,” Krithivasan, CEO and MD, TCS, said in a statement.

TCS said it currently works with more than 150 enterprises globally across different stages of the GCC lifecycle, from setting up centres to scaling and transforming operations.

The move also reflects the growing importance of GCCs for India's technology services industry.

As enterprises seek to integrate AI into business processes, IT services providers are increasingly positioning themselves as partners not just for technology implementation but also for designing and operating AI-enabled captive centres.

The collaboration focuses on design optimisation, AI-driven tools, and production-ready chip development to meet future computing needs.

What Actually Matters.

Intel and Cadence are expanding their partnership to enhance the design of the Intel 14A chip for high-performance computing.

The collaboration will focus on design optimisation, AI-driven tools, and production support to streamline chip development.

Cadence Design Systems and Intel Foundry have expanded their partnership to optimise Intel’s next-generation Intel 14A process technology for high-performance computing (HPC) and mobile chip designs.

The multi-year collaboration will focus on design technology co-optimisation (DTCO), design IP readiness and production support to help customers develop chips faster and lower design risks.

Cadence President and CEO Anirudh Devgan said the expanded engagement marks a deeper relationship between the two companies. Devgan said the collaboration would help customers “unlock new levels of performance, power, and efficiency” while accelerating the development of next-generation products.

The partnership will combine Cadence’s AI-driven electronic design automation (EDA) and design IP solutions with Intel’s process technology and chip design expertise. The effort will begin with Intel 14A, one of Intel Foundry’s upcoming process technologies, and aims to deliver production-ready process design kits (PDKs) for customers.

Under the agreement, the companies will improve performance, power and chip area, often referred to in the semiconductor industry as PPA. They will also use Cadence’s agentic AI tools and core design products to speed up product development.

Intel Foundry Executive VP and General Manager, Naga Chandrasekaran, said the partnership supports Intel’s technology roadmap and ecosystem strategy.

“By combining Intel’s process and packaging with Cadence’s AI-driven design tools, we are enabling deeper co-optimisation, strengthening our ability to deliver on customers’ needs, and showcasing the ability of both companies to drive innovation at scale,” Chandrasekaran said.

The expanded cooperation comes as semiconductor companies increase efforts to improve chip performance and shorten development timelines. Foundries and chip design firms are also investing in AI-led tools to reduce engineering complexity and support advanced manufacturing processes.

title: Apna Launches India’s First AI Interview Prep Lounge in Mumbai to Transform Job Readiness Experience
content:
The AI Interview Prep system supports over 25,000 roles across companies.

What Actually Matters.

Apna has launched India's first AI Interview Prep Lounge in Mumbai to enhance job readiness for candidates.

The facility offers mock interviews and AI-driven feedback, supporting over 25,000 job roles across various sectors.

Apna, an AI-native early-career talent platform, has launched an AI Interview Prep Lounge at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Kaushalya Vikas Kendra in Mumbai. The facility, inaugurated by Union Minister Piyush Goyal, is designed to help job seekers practise interviews, receive real-time AI-driven feedback, and access job opportunities through an integrated preparation ecosystem.

Inaugurating the centre, Goyal said, “The Apna AI-enabled Interview Centre represents the future of skill development and employment generation. By leveraging artificial intelligence to identify opportunities, bridge skill gaps, and prepare candidates for the evolving job market, this initiative will empower our youth to build successful careers and contribute meaningfully to India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047.”

The new facility features three AI-powered interview preparation kiosks. They are integrated with Apna’s interview preparation platform and will also be part of weekly walk-in hiring drives at ABVKVK, creating a unified journey from preparation to placement for candidates.

Job seekers at the centre can access role-specific mock interviews, receive instant AI-based feedback on their responses, and explore relevant job opportunities across sectors. The AI Interview Prep system supports over 25,000 roles across companies, offers multilingual capabilities, and is available free of cost to candidates visiting the centre.

Speaking on the initiative, Nirmit Parikh, Founder and Group CEO, Apna, said, “As technology reshapes the world of work, access to guidance, preparation, and opportunity must become universal. The AI Interview Prep Lounge reflects our belief that every job seeker should have the tools and support needed to realise their potential.”

He added that for many first-time job seekers, the biggest challenge is not skills acquisition but navigating the interview process. Limited access to coaching and structured preparation often leaves candidates underprepared, and the new lounge is designed to bridge this gap by offering hands-on practice, feedback, and confidence-building support.

Commenting on the launch, Kartik Narayan, CEO, Apna Jobs, said, “Through the AI Interview Prep Lounge, we are giving candidates a practical way to prepare, build confidence, receive feedback, and improve their chances of converting opportunities into jobs.”

The Mumbai facility marks the first phase of Apna’s broader plan to expand AI-powered career preparation infrastructure across skilling institutions, campuses, and workforce development ecosystems, aiming to make job readiness more accessible as technology continues to reshape employment pathways in India.

title: HCLTech Launches AI Innovation Zone with Google Cloud in Santa Clara
content:
The facility, located in Santa Clara, will focus on building and deploying AI-driven workflows across agentic, kinetic and physical AI use cases.

What Actually Matters.

HCLTech has launched an AI Innovation Zone in partnership with Google Cloud to help enterprises scale AI applications.

The facility in Santa Clara focuses on building AI-driven workflows for various industry-specific use cases.

HCLTech has launched an AI Innovation Zone in collaboration with Google Cloud, aimed at helping enterprises scale AI applications and move from experimentation to production.

The facility, located in Santa Clara, will focus on building and deploying AI-driven workflows across agentic, kinetic and physical AI use cases. Powered by Gemini Enterprise, the centre is designed as a dedicated environment where enterprises can design, test and operationalise AI systems, including robotics-led solutions, for industry-specific outcomes.

The launch builds on the expanded partnership between the two companies announced in March. It combines Google Cloud’s AI infrastructure with HCLTech’s industry-focused AI offerings to support enterprises transitioning toward what both companies describe as “agentic enterprises”.

“Enterprise AI has moved rapidly from the experimentation phase to a focus on driving tangible business outcomes at scale,” said Kevin Ichhpurani, President, Global Partner Ecosystem at Google Cloud. He added that the Innovation Zone will provide customers a framework to build, test and deploy advanced workflows and bridge the gap between innovation and enterprise-wide adoption.

Vijay Guntur, CTO and Head of Ecosystems at HCLTech, said the collaboration enables organisations to operationalise AI systems capable of executing autonomous, multi-step workflows at scale, with a focus on measurable business outcomes.

The company plans to expand its R&D team in India over the next 12 months to meet rising demand for investigative analytics.

What Actually Matters.

Cognyte plans to expand its R&D operations in Pune to enhance AI-driven technologies for law enforcement and security agencies.

The company aims to add roles in engineering, AI, machine learning, data analytics, and software development over the next year.

Cognyte, an investigative analytics company, plans to expand its research and development operations in Pune as it looks to build more AI-driven technologies for law enforcement and security agencies.

The company intends to scale its India hub over the next 12 months and add new roles across engineering, AI, machine learning, data analytics, and software development.

The expansion comes as Cognyte responds to growing global demand for investigative analytics tools that help governments and security agencies process large volumes of data and generate intelligence. The company said Pune will continue to serve as a key global innovation centre supporting its engineering and product development efforts.

“India has emerged as a critical innovation centre for Cognyte,” said Ashutosh Kar, General Manager APAC and Managing Director India at Cognyte, in a statement. “The technical depth, problem-solving mindset and calibre of talent here are directly shaping our most advanced analytics platforms.”

The company aims to strengthen its local capabilities in software-led innovation while supporting customers across global markets.

The Pune centre will focus on engineering work related to large-scale data processing, AI-based analysis, and investigative software for operational environments. These platforms are designed to help agencies turn complex and high-volume data into intelligence that supports investigations and decision-making.

Headquartered in Israel, Cognyte develops investigative analytics software for law enforcement, intelligence and national security agencies. The company said the India expansion aligns with its wider strategy of growing global R&D centres and bringing together engineering talent across markets.

title: AIM — India's Leading AI & Data Science Media Platform
content:
Eros Innovation has launched a Cultural AI Platform designed to understand and preserve culture in 34 languages.

The platform features Eros LCVM and Eros Persona AI, focusing on cultural context and emotional expression in storytelling.

Eros Innovation has launched its new Cultural AI Platform, which the company describes as the world’s first artificial intelligence ecosystem designed to understand and preserve culture across multiple languages.

The platform was first introduced at the IndiaAI Impact Summit in February 2026 and is now available in 34 global languages. It is powered by two key technologies, Eros LCVM (Large Cultural Voice Model) and Eros Persona AI.

According to the company, the platform goes beyond traditional AI systems that mainly focus on generating text or language. It has been designed to understand cultural context, emotional expression, and identity while generating content.

The company added that the technology has been trained using a rights-cleared dataset of more than 11,000 films and over 100,000 fictional characters. The platform can generate multilingual voice performances, storytelling content, and digital character interactions while maintaining cultural authenticity.

The Cultural AI Platform consists of five layers: Eros LCM, which focuses on cultural intelligence and storytelling; Eros LCVM for multilingual voice and performance generation; Eros Persona AI for creating digital identities; Eros Creator, a toolset for creators and businesses; and Eros Universe, the consumer-facing platform where users can interact with AI-generated characters.

The company clarified that all AI-generated personas are fictional and do not replicate real actors, performers, or public figures.

Speaking on the launch, Ridhima Lulla, Co-founder and Co-President of Eros Innovation, said, “The platform was developed after years of research into creating AI systems that understand culture in addition to language.”

“The technology supports India’s efforts to build sovereign AI capabilities. LCVM as the voice layer that enables cultural intelligence to be delivered across 34 languages,” added Founder and Chairman Kishore Lulla.

S Krishnan, Secretary at the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), noted that India has an opportunity to lead in developing AI systems that understand culture, identity, and context. He added that preserving linguistic diversity and cultural heritage will become increasingly important as AI technologies continue to evolve.

The platform is currently live while its first consumer-focused product is expected to be launched next week.

content:
Sriram Krishnan will leave his role as Senior Policy Advisor for AI at the White House after 18 months.

He plans to focus on addressing significant AI challenges in the United States post-departure.

Sriram Krishnan, Senior Policy Advisor for Artificial Intelligence at the White House, said he will leave his role at the end of June after serving for about 18 months in the Trump administration.

The Indian-American technology executive announced his departure in a post on X, saying he plans to continue working on issues related to artificial intelligence in the United States.

“I'll be leaving my role at the White House at the end of this month,” Krishnan wrote. “After a break, I’ll be working on helping tackle some of the large challenges facing America on AI.”

Krishnan thanked US President Donald Trump and White House AI and crypto adviser David Sacks for American leadership in AI.

In his post, Krishnan highlighted several initiatives he worked on during his tenure, including the American AI Action Plan, international AI partnerships, a national AI policy framework, and efforts to promote US AI technologies with allies through engagements in France, India, the United Kingdom, and the Middle East.

“Architecting and publishing the American AI Action Plan” and advancing “AI acceleration partnerships to help American AI stack win globally” were among the accomplishments he listed.

Krishnan said the next phase of his work would focus on challenges surrounding AI infrastructure, energy requirements, data centres and broader adoption of the technology.

“The past 18 months have given me a front row seat to this critical moment on AI facing America and our allies,” he wrote. “I plan on building institutions that help tackle some of those challenges for America and its allies.”

His departure comes at a time when Washington is increasing its focus on AI regulation, national security, data centre expansion, and competition with China. Reuters reported that Krishnan played a central role in shaping the administration's framework for AI policy and governance.

Born in Chennai, Krishnan was appointed Senior White House Policy Adviser on Artificial Intelligence after Donald Trump's return to office in January 2025.

Before joining the administration, he held senior roles at major technology companies and was a general partner at venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz. He also worked closely with Elon Musk following Musk's acquisition of Twitter.

Krishnan’s tenure included participation in international AI diplomacy efforts and the development of the administration's AI Action Plan, which has served as a key policy document guiding the US approach to artificial intelligence.

He did not announce his next role or identify any successor.

title: NVIDIA, LG Group to Build AI Factory for Robotics, Mobility, Data Centres
content:
LG Electronics will use NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab to simulate, train, and validate household robots before deployment.

What Actually Matters.

NVIDIA and LG Group are collaborating to create an AI factory supporting various technologies including robotics and data centres.

The partnership aims to integrate AI applications across LG's diverse operations, enhancing efficiency in consumer electronics and mobility.

NVIDIA and LG Group have partnered to build an AI factory that will support the development of robotics, autonomous driving systems, data centre technologies, and GPU cloud services.

The AI factory will provide computing infrastructure for training, simulation, validation, and deployment of AI applications across LG Group’s businesses. The companies said the initiative combines NVIDIA’s AI factory platform with LG Group’s operations in consumer electronics, robotics, mobility, smart spaces, and data centre technologies.

“Together, the companies are connecting AI model development, physical AI data generation, robot simulation and training, edge deployment and factory-scale digital twins into a unified workflow for building physical AI systems,” NVIDIA said in a statement.

As part of the collaboration, LG Electronics will use NVIDIA’s robotics tools, Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab, to simulate, train and validate household robots before deployment. The company is also exploring the use of NVIDIA Isaac GR00T, an open vision-language-action model, for home robots and modular robotics platforms.

NVIDIA and LG Electronics plan to jointly develop reference robots that will be integrated into the NVIDIA Isaac GR00T ecosystem.

To address robotics training data requirements, LG Electronics is building a physical AI data factory that will generate synthetic training data using NVIDIA Cosmos world foundation models. The company said the platform is intended to support robotics and industrial AI projects in South Korea and other markets.

The companies will also work on AI-driven manufacturing systems. LG Group plans to combine production data from its manufacturing facilities with NVIDIA’s AI infrastructure and digital twin technologies to develop an autonomous manufacturing ecosystem linking procurement, production, logistics, and delivery through real-time data and AI.

LG CNS will integrate NVIDIA’s robotics technologies, including Isaac frameworks, Cosmos models and GR00T foundation models, into its PhysicalWorks industrial robot platform. The company said the effort will accelerate AI adoption in logistics and manufacturing operations.

Beyond robotics, the partnership extends to AI infrastructure. LG Electronics and NVIDIA will collaborate on cooling distribution units, cold plates and modular data centre technologies aligned with NVIDIA’s DSX AI factory platform.

LG Uplus, together with LG Electronics and LG Energy Solution, plans to build AI factories based on NVIDIA DSX architecture. The company said the facilities will combine NVIDIA’s accelerated computing infrastructure with LG’s energy and telecommunications capabilities to support AI cloud and GPU services.

LG CNS also plans to build AI factories powered by NVIDIA GPUs, while LG Uplus is preparing a large-scale AI data centre designed to accommodate NVIDIA's latest GPU systems.

LG Energy Solution will work with NVIDIA on 800-volt direct-current data centre energy solutions based on NVIDIA's battery energy storage system qualification guidelines.

In the automotive sector, LG Electronics will align its advanced driver-assistance systems and in-vehicle AI technologies with the NVIDIA DRIVE platform. The companies said the collaboration will focus on sensor, compute, and software architectures based on NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion.

LG Electronics also plans to use NVIDIA DRIVE AGX computing platforms in future mobility applications, including AI-powered cockpit systems and edge AI processing.

LG Innotek, which supplies sensing, connectivity, and lighting components for vehicles, said it plans to work with NVIDIA on components designed for NVIDIA-based autonomous driving platforms.

The partnership also includes work on sovereign AI. NVIDIA and LG AI Research are collaborating on EXAONE, a Korean AI model family available to enterprises, developers and researchers.

LG AI Research said it used NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, the NeMo framework, Nemotron datasets and TensorRT-LLM software during the development and deployment of EXAONE models.

LG Group is evaluating broader deployment of EXAONE and agentic AI technologies across its businesses, including through ChatEXAONE, the group's enterprise chatbot platform.

title: TCS Bags Multi-Year AI-Led Transformation Deal from Canada Life
content:
The deal will see TCS modernise Canada Life's infrastructure operations across Europe using AI-led automation, data centre modernisation, and software lifecycle management services.

What Actually Matters.

TCS has secured a significant AI-led transformation deal with Canada Life for its European operations.

The partnership focuses on modernising Canada Life's IT infrastructure and improving operational resilience through automation.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has secured a multiyear infrastructure transformation and managed services contract from insurance and pensions provider Canada Life, marking another large AI-focused deal for the Indian IT services major in the financial services sector.

While the companies did not disclose the contract value, TCS described it as a "multimillion-euro" agreement under which it will modernise and manage Canada Life's IT infrastructure services across its European operations.

As part of the engagement, TCS will deploy its artificial intelligence and digital capabilities to modernise Canada Life's data centres, core infrastructure, end-user computing environment, and software lifecycle management processes. The initiative aims to improve operational resilience, increase automation, and enhance the user experience for customers.

The project will support Canada Life's broader technology modernisation efforts across Europe and is expected to help the insurer scale technology services more efficiently while responding faster to changing business requirements. The programme will focus on delivering performance-driven IT services and supporting the company's long-term technology strategy.

“Working with TCS marks the next stage of our journey to modernise the technology foundations that underpin our business, and it was important to choose a partner that understands our long-term vision and shares our commitment to people and innovation,” Caroline Dibbs, Chief Information and Transformation Officer, Europe for Canada Life, said in a statement.

Vinay Singhvi, Head of UK and Ireland at TCS, said the partnership would help Canada Life improve operational efficiency, strengthen resilience and build a more agile IT ecosystem.

“By leveraging our deep domain expertise, we will help Canada Life achieve greater operational efficiency, enhance resilience, and create a more agile, responsive IT ecosystem to support their long-term growth,” Singhvi noted.

The engagement will also see TCS expand its infrastructure services talent base across the UK, Ireland, the Isle of Man, and Germany through investments in training, certification, and career development programmes.

The deal adds to TCS' portfolio of insurance sector engagements in the UK and Europe and strengthens its position in the banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) segment, a key vertical for the company.

TCS said the partnership reinforces its expansion strategy in the UK and Ireland, which it views as a strategic hub for delivering end to end services to insurance clients across the region.

title: Snowflake Unveils Its Blueprint for the Agentic Enterprise
content:
Snowflake’s latest AI push brings agents, model training and governance together on a single enterprise platform.

What Actually Matters.

Snowflake aims to transition enterprises from AI experimentation to deploying autonomous systems effectively.

The company introduced new AI capabilities, including Snowflake CoCo, CoWork, and Horizon Catalog for governance.

Snowflake announced a series of new AI, governance and interoperability offerings at Snowflake Summit 2026, as the company seeks to help enterprises move from AI experimentation to deploying autonomous systems at scale.

The company introduced new capabilities across Snowflake CoCo, its AI-powered coding agent, Snowflake CoWork, an AI assistant for knowledge workers, and Snowflake Horizon Catalog, its governance platform.

It also expanded support for open data architectures, enabling organisations to use and govern data across cloud environments and enterprise systems without duplicating datasets.

“The future of enterprise AI will be defined by how well organisations connect intelligence, trusted data, and action across the business,” said Vijayant Rai, Managing Director, India at Snowflake.

“At Snowflake Summit 26, we’re introducing innovations that help power the agentic enterprise, giving organisations a trusted foundation and control plane to build AI faster, operationalise it securely at scale, and enable teams and AI agents to work together from a shared business context wherever data lives,” he added.

A key focus of the announcements was Snowflake CoCo, formerly known as Cortex Code. The company expanded the coding agent to work across desktop, mobile, Slack, VS Code, Claude Code and Microsoft Excel. Snowflake said the platform allows developers to automate workflows, build applications and operationalise AI using conversational prompts.

Snowflake also launched Datastream, a managed streaming service for Apache Kafka, designed to bring real-time data into Snowflake for AI applications and agents. The company said the service will allow organisations to build AI systems that operate on continuously updated data.

For business users, Snowflake introduced new capabilities within Snowflake CoWork, formerly Snowflake Intelligence. Features such as Cortex Sense, Deep Research, Artifacts, User Skills and personalisation are intended to help employees interact with enterprise data through a context-aware AI assistant.

The company also launched Cortex Training, which provides managed infrastructure for customizing and training foundation models directly within Snowflake's platform.

On the governance front, Snowflake expanded Horizon Catalog with new features to provide shared business context and oversight for AI systems. The company introduced Horizon Context, which it said helps ensure employees, applications and AI agents operate using the same business definitions and data context.

Additional security features include Agent Identity and updates to Snowflake Trust Centre, giving organisations greater visibility and control over AI systems and autonomous agents.

Snowflake also announced Adaptive Compute, a capability that automatically allocates compute and software resources based on workload requirements.

The company further expanded interoperability support through new capabilities for Apache Iceberg, including support for Iceberg v3, Snowflake Storage for Apache Iceberg Tables, external engine access management and the Iceberg REST Scan Plan API.

According to Snowflake, these capabilities allow organisations to access and govern data across Snowflake environments, external data lakes and open systems without moving or copying information.

The company said future integrations will also enable organisations to interact with enterprise data using natural language through CoCo and CoWork, while Automatic Data Agents and Agent Sharing will allow shared datasets to be converted into AI agents with governance controls built in.

title: Anthropic Calls for Options to Pause AI Development
content:
As self-improving AI models advance, Anthropic says governments and AI labs should develop verification systems that could support a slowdown or pause in frontier AI development.

What Actually Matters.

Anthropic advocates for mechanisms to pause or slow frontier AI development amidst rapid advancements.

The company highlights the potential for AI systems to autonomously improve their own successors.

Anthropic has called for options to slow or temporarily pause frontier AI development, arguing that AI systems are increasingly contributing to the development of future AI systems and could eventually become capable of improving their own successors.

The proposal examined the prospect of recursive self-improvement, a scenario in which AI systems automate an increasing share of AI research and engineering work.

It said recursive self-improvement is not inevitable, but could arrive sooner than many institutions are prepared for. Anthropic presented internal and public benchmark data to support its argument that AI is already accelerating AI development.

The company said more than 80% of the code merged into its production codebase is now authored by Claude, while the typical engineer merged roughly 8 times as much code per day in the second quarter of 2026 as in 2024.

Although Anthropic noted that lines of code are an imperfect productivity metric, it argued that the figures demonstrate a substantial increase in engineering output.

Today, Anthropic engineers on average ship 8x as much code per quarter as they did compared to 2021-2025. pic.twitter.com/QCc9cqGgf4

— Anthropic (@AnthropicAI) June 4, 2026

The report also points to advances in AI-assisted research. Anthropic said Claude has become increasingly capable of executing experiments, debugging complex systems, reviewing code, and solving open-ended engineering problems with limited human intervention. While humans still set research priorities and evaluate results, the company argues that the boundary between human-led and AI-led development is narrowing.

“We also see evidence that people at Anthropic are using Claude to do work that simply wouldn’t have happened otherwise, like building exploratory tooling and addressing long-deferred cleanup,” said Anthropic. “For example, in April 2026, Claude shipped over 800 fixes that reduced a class of API errors by a factor of one thousand. The engineer overseeing Claude estimated that a human would have taken four years to complete this work.”

According to Anthropic, the key question is whether future systems will develop the judgement required to select important research directions rather than merely execute tasks.

The company said early internal evidence suggests progress in this area, though significant gaps remain between current models and a system capable of autonomously driving AI research.

Anthropic outlined several potential futures, including one in which AI labs gain compounding productivity benefits from increasingly automated research and development, and another in which AI systems become capable of designing and refining successor models themselves.

In the latter scenario, humans would primarily oversee, validate and verify the outputs of AI-operated research systems.

Against that backdrop, Anthropic argued that the world should have the option to slow development if advanced AI capabilities begin to outpace governance, safety research or societal adaptation.

“If it were possible to effectively slow the development of this technology to give ourselves more time to deal with its immense implications, we think that would likely be a good thing,” the company wrote.

The paper does not call for an immediate halt to AI development. Instead, Anthropic said it would research verification systems and coordination mechanisms that could make a future slowdown credible and enforceable.

The company argued that any meaningful pause would require participation from multiple frontier AI developers and governments, along with methods to verify that all parties had actually reduced or halted development.

Anthropic said it plans to convene policymakers, researchers, civil society groups and AI companies to examine questions surrounding recursive self-improvement, coordination and AI governance, and to publish further research in the coming months.

The report comes as Anthropic expands access to its most advanced cybersecurity model, Claude Mythos Preview. This week, the company widened Project Glasswing from roughly 50 initial participants to about 200 organisations across more than 15 countries and has discussed extending access to European institutions through the programme.

Anthropic says Glasswing partners have already identified more than 10,000 high- and critical-severity software vulnerabilities using Mythos.

The expansion also follows a string of frontier model releases from the company, including Claude Opus and Sonnet variants that have ranked among the industry's leading coding models, alongside Anthropic's growing focus on autonomous software engineering and cybersecurity workflows.

title: [Exclusive] Tech Mahindra is Working on World Models, Eyes ARC-AGI Milestone This Year
content:
Earlier this year, the company launched an 8-billion-parameter Hindi-first education LLM under the IndiaAI Mission.

What Actually Matters.

Tech Mahindra is developing AI world models and targeting the ARC-AGI challenge as part of its AGI initiative.

The research, led by the Makers Lab, aims to create advanced reasoning systems tailored for the Indian context.

Tech Mahindra is building AI world models and working on the ARC-AGI challenge as part of a broader push towards AGI, with the company targeting tangible outcomes from its research efforts later this year, AIM has learnt.

The initiative is being led by the company’s Makers Lab, which is exploring world models, next-generation vision-language models (VLMs), and AGI systems from an Indian context, and was selected under the IndiaAI Mission to build sovereign language models.

People familiar with the matter said the research goes beyond conventional LLMs, focusing on enabling AI systems to understand, simulate, and reason about the world.

The company is also working on the ARC-AGI challenge, a benchmark widely regarded as one of the toughest tests of general intelligence in machines. The effort forms part of a larger programme to build foundational AI capabilities from the ground up rather than relying solely on existing foundation models.

The work marks Tech Mahindra’s most ambitious AI research project yet and signals an expansion of its focus from sovereign language models to more advanced reasoning systems.

Earlier this year, the company launched an 8-billion-parameter Hindi-first education LLM under the IndiaAI Mission, becoming the only IT services firm selected by the programme to build its own foundational model.

The latest research direction is closely aligned with the vision articulated by Nikhil Malhotra, who has for several years advocated developing world models as a path towards more capable AI systems.

In an earlier interaction with AIM, Malhotra described his concept of "Dream AI", a neurosymbolic architecture that combines symbolic reasoning with deep reinforcement learning. He argued that today's AI systems excel at pattern recognition but lack a genuine understanding of the world.

"Symbolism helps us build world models, and Transformers enable actions based on those models," Malhotra had said.

According to him, world models allow AI systems to simulate environments and reason about consequences before taking action, reducing dependence on massive datasets and enabling more contextual decision-making. The approach combines symbolic AI, reinforcement learning, and neural networks to create agents capable of learning from simulated experiences rather than purely from historical data.

The research areas now being pursued by Makers Lab suggest that several of the ideas behind Dream AI are moving from concept to active development. Alongside world models, the team is also investigating new VLM architectures and broader AGI-related capabilities.

title: From Chip Talent to Chipmaker: NetraSemi Bets on India’s Semiconductor Future
content:
In its latest content experiment, Founders Fund swaps podcasts for Mafia, pitting Silicon Valley’s biggest names against one another.

What Actually Matters.

Founders Fund is launching a new media initiative, replacing traditional podcasts with a reality-style game show called Mafia.

The inaugural episode features notable figures from Silicon Valley, including Sam Altman and Palmer Luckey, highlighting their social strategies.

Founders Fund is making an unconventional push into media, bringing some of Silicon Valley’s most recognisable figures together for a reality-style game show built around deception, deduction, and social strategy.

The venture capital firm this week launched MAFIA the GAME, a new video series on YouTube and X that places leading founders, investors, and technologists around a table to play the popular party game Mafia.

The debut episode, titled Can Tech Legends Find the Liar?, brought together OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Anduril Industries Co-founder Palmer Luckey, Blueprint Founder Bryan Johnson, Figma Co-founder and CEO Dylan Field, Signal founder Moxie Marlinspike, and Flexport founder and CEO Ryan Petersen.

The cast also includes investor Cyan Banister, writer Tim Urban, professional poker player Liv Boeree, AI policy expert Ryan Beiermeister, Founders Fund partner Trae Stephens, and several other founders, investors, and technologists.

The 33-minute first episode was filmed at San Francisco’s historic Tosca Cafe, a location with symbolic ties to Silicon Valley history. The venue previously served as the backdrop for the famous ‘PayPal Mafia’ photograph published by Fortune in 2007, making it a fitting setting for a game centred on trust and betrayal.

In Mafia, participants are secretly assigned roles, with a small group designated as the mafia. Their objective is to eliminate other players without being identified, while the rest of the group attempts to uncover the impostors through discussion and voting. The format turns every conversation into a test of persuasion and credibility.

The project is being spearheaded by Founders Fund Chief Marketing Officer Mike Solana, who has increasingly positioned the firm at the intersection of technology, culture, and media. Solana described the show as a more engaging way to understand influential founders and investors than traditional venture capital podcasts and panel discussions.

The episode quickly leans into the personalities of its participants. Luckey’s humour makes him an early target of suspicion, while Johnson’s well-known obsession with longevity becomes the source of jokes from fellow players.

Beyond the game itself, the series reflects a broader trend of technology firms and venture capital investors experimenting with original media formats. Rather than relying solely on podcasts, newsletters, or conference appearances, firms are increasingly producing entertainment-focused content to build audiences and shape their public identities.

Additional episodes are expected to be released weekly, as Founders Fund tests whether viewers are interested in watching some of the technology sector’s biggest names compete not over startups or investments, but over who can best deceive.

title: Tamil Nadu Bets ₹18,600 Cr with L&T on Data Centre-Led Industrial Expansion
content:
Three projects are expected to create about 8,200 employment opportunities across the state.

What Actually Matters.

Tamil Nadu has signed MoUs with L&T for three major projects, involving a ₹18,600 crore investment.

The projects aim to support the state's vision of a $1.5 trillion economy by 2036.

The Tamil Nadu government has signed Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with Larsen & Toubro (L&T) for three major projects involving a combined investment of ₹18,600 crore, marking a significant step in the state’s industrial expansion strategy aimed at achieving its $1.5 trillion economy vision by 2036.

The agreements were exchanged in the presence of Chief Minister Thiru C. Joseph Vijay, Industries Minister Selvi S. Keerthana, L&T Managing Director S N Subramanian, and senior government officials at the State Secretariat.

The largest component of the investment is a ₹15,000 crore Information and Data Centre project in Kancheepuram district, which is expected to generate around 500 direct jobs. The initiative is positioned as a key infrastructure pillar in Tamil Nadu’s growing digital economy and data-led industrial ecosystem.

Alongside the data centre development, the MoUs also include a ₹2,500 crore electronics accessories manufacturing facility will be set up in Coimbatore, expected to generate around 2,000 employment opportunities, while a ₹1,100 crore shipbuilding yard at Kattupalli port in Tiruvallur district is projected to create approximately 5,700 jobs, further strengthening the state’s industrial and maritime manufacturing ecosystem.

Together, the three projects are expected to create about 8,200 employment opportunities across the state.

The initiative underscores Tamil Nadu’s continued focus on attracting large-scale investments across both digital and traditional industrial sectors.

Officials said the projects are intended to strengthen manufacturing capacity, expand data infrastructure, and boost employment generation, aligning with the state’s long-term economic growth objectives

title: Persistent Taps Databricks, MSOE to Train Students in Production-Grade AI Systems
content:
The initiative aims to prepare students for the growing demand in enterprise AI as organisations move from experimentation to large-scale AI deployment.

What Actually Matters.

Persistent Systems collaborates with Databricks and MSOE to equip students for enterprise-scale AI roles.

The initiative includes a hands-on AI Hackathon to bridge academic learning and industry demands.

Persistent Systems has partnered with Databricks and Milwaukee School of Engineering (MSOE) to help prepare students for enterprise-scale AI roles through a hands-on AI engineering initiative.

The collaboration centred on an AI Hackathon organised with the MSOE AI Club providing students with practical experience in building and managing AI systems for real-world business environments. The initiative aimed to bridge the gap between classroom learning and industry requirements as enterprises increasingly move from AI experiments to large-scale deployments.

Using the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, participants worked with tools such as Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Agent Bricks and Databricks Workflows. The program focused on areas including AI governance, scalable AI pipelines, workflow automation and production-grade AI architectures.

“The AI market is shifting from isolated pilots to enterprise-wide operationalisation, demanding engineers fluent in governed data, scalable platforms and production-grade execution,” Sameer Dixit, Corporate Vice President and Head of Data, AI and Integration, Persistent, said.

He added that the hackathon was designed to provide students with real-world platform experience and engineering discipline early in their careers while strengthening connections between academia and industry.

Persistent’s senior architects and project leaders worked directly with participants, introducing them to architectural thinking, governance frameworks and deployment considerations that are critical to enterprise AI projects.

According to John Young, Global Managing Director – Partner Solution Architects at Databricks, organisations are increasingly standardising on platforms that combine data, analytics and AI.

“Preparing talent to work in these unified environments is becoming critical. Collaborations like this help students build that foundation early, so they can contribute meaningfully from day one in enterprise settings,” he noted.

“The hackathon brought valuable motivation, perspective and experience into the classroom and challenged students to think beyond the academic lessons of their coursework,” Derek Riley, PhD, Professor, Program Director of Computer Science, Milwaukee School of Engineering, said.

The program is part of Persistent’s broader collaboration with Databricks through which the company helps enterprises modernise data platforms and scale analytics, generative AI and enterprise AI adoption.

title: Most Enterprises Lack Infrastructure to Scale AI, Shows Tata Communications Report
content:
The study shows that users in India watch videos daily, driving commerce and discovery of products across the nation now.

What Actually Matters.

A significant majority of users in India engage with videos on Meta platforms daily, with 97% participation overall.

Reels are particularly popular among Gen Z, with 89% using the feature daily, showcasing strong engagement across various demographics.

About 97% of surveyed users in India watch videos on Meta platforms daily, a study commissioned by Meta and conducted by IPSOS indicates. The research shows video engagement is similar across geographies, with urban usage at 98% and rural usage at 94%.

The data highlights the usage of Reels, a short-form video feature, across demographic segments. Among Gen Z respondents, 89% report using Reels daily. Usage is also noted among women at 85% and NCCS A audiences at 88%.

The report identifies beauty and makeup, fashion and trends, lifestyle, fitness and wellness, comedy and humour, sports, and travel as the genres with the most engagement on Reels.

The study outlines the role of video in commerce. According to the findings, Reels drive 81% of product discovery, 66% of consideration, and 47% of purchase influence among its users.

Furthermore, 84% of Gen Z consumers and 73% of rural users discover products and brands through Meta platforms. In the financial services sector, 76% of rural users engage with Meta daily, while 54% of female financial product owners interact with creators on the platform daily.

The automotive sector shows a path-to-purchase pattern starting with discovery at 82%, moving to consideration at 68%, and ending with purchase at 50%.

Saugato Bhowmik, Director, CPG, D2C, Automotive, at Meta, said, “India’s video boom isn’t urban-led anymore but it’s nationwide, cutting across GenZ, women and premium audiences. Creators, culture and commerce are converging on Reels in ways we haven’t seen before. For brands, this isn’t just a content play but it’s a always on content-to-commerce play. Reels are where discovery starts, trust is built, and purchase decisions are made.

title: LTM Launches Managed Security Service with Cisco to Secure Enterprise AI Deployments
content:
The offering combines Cisco's Secure Access platform with LTM's managed cybersecurity services as enterprises look to strengthen security around generative AI deployments and hybrid work environments.

What Actually Matters.

LTM has launched a managed Secure Service Edge offering in collaboration with Cisco to enhance security for enterprise AI deployments.

The solution integrates Cisco's Secure Access platform and LTM's cybersecurity services to support zero trust security frameworks.

LTM, formerly LTIMindtree, has launched a managed Secure Service Edge (SSE) offering in partnership with Cisco, as enterprises increasingly seek to secure access to applications and generative AI tools in cloud-based and hybrid work environments.

The offering, unveiled at Cisco Live 2026 in Las Vegas, is built on Cisco Secure Access, the networking giant's SSE platform, and combines Cisco's security capabilities with LTM's managed cybersecurity services.

The solution is aimed at helping enterprises adopt zero trust security frameworks while managing access to applications, data and AI models. It brings together capabilities such as Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA), Secure Web Gateway (SWG) and Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) under a unified policy framework, enabling organisations to manage security controls across users, devices and locations from a single platform.

According to LTM, the managed service will be backed by its cybersecurity operations network, including more than 4,000 security professionals and nine Cyber Defense Resiliency Centers, which provide round-the-clock threat monitoring and response services.

“Modern enterprises need AI-powered security that adapts to how people work today, anywhere, on any device, at any time. Our partnership with Cisco delivers a unified, cloud-native SSE solution that simplifies protection, improves visibility, and empowers organisations to operate securely at scale,” Chandan Pani, Chief Information Security Officer, LTM, said in a statement.

Raj Chopra, Senior Vice President and Chief Product Officer, Cisco Security, said the collaboration combines Cisco's security portfolio with LTM's managed services capabilities to help enterprises deploy and scale security services more efficiently.

“LTM’s managed SSE solution balances business agility with a seamless user experience. Cisco’s security portfolio—including Secure Access— has been purpose-built to be consumed as a service, enabling organisations to adopt and scale modern security with greater simplicity and speed,” said Chopra.

The launch comes as enterprises face growing challenges around securing generative AI applications and ensuring compliance as AI adoption expands across business functions.

title: DSP Launches First Overseas GCC in Bengaluru to Expand Global Database Management Capabilities
content:
The India centre has been set up in partnership with SansoviGCC by GoodWorks Group.

What Actually Matters.

DSP has launched its first overseas global capability centre in Bengaluru to enhance its international expansion.

The centre will provide managed services, database consultancy, and cloud solutions across major platforms.

UK-based enterprise database management company DSP has entered India with the launch of its first overseas global capability centre (GCC) in Bengaluru, marking a key step in its international expansion strategy.

The new centre will focus on delivering managed services, database consultancy, and cloud solutions across Oracle, Microsoft, and multi-cloud environments. It will support global clients in managing mission-critical database infrastructure and developing enterprise-scale technology solutions.

The India centre has been set up in partnership with SansoviGCC by GoodWorks Group and will be hosted at GoodWorks GCC Nexus in Prestige Tech Park, Bengaluru.

The facility was inaugurated by Sanjeev Gupta, CEO of Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM), along with KT Rajan, Director of Technology, Innovation, Education and Skills at the British Deputy High Commission, and other industry representatives.

Speaking at the inauguration, DSP Group Chief Operating Officer Paul Cocks said Bengaluru’s talent ecosystem made it a strategic choice for expansion, adding that the GCC will strengthen the company’s consulting and technology capabilities across the Oracle ecosystem. He said the centre will play a key role in combining global expertise with local talent to deliver value to clients worldwide.

Officials from KDEM said DSP’s entry reflects growing global confidence in Bengaluru as a GCC hub, highlighting the state’s deep talent pool and established innovation ecosystem.

Industry partners, including GoodWorks Group, said the centre would enhance DSP’s ability to scale operations in enterprise database management and cloud services.

DSP, headquartered in the United Kingdom and founded in 1999, provides managed services, consulting, and support for Oracle, SQL Server, and multi-cloud technologies. The company serves clients across start-ups, mid-market firms, and large enterprises in Europe and North America.

title: TrueFan AI raises $10 million in Series A Round Led by Baring PE India, Z3Partners
content:
The startup's innovative AI model allows businesses to create personalised video content at scale, eliminating traditional production bottlenecks.

What Actually Matters.

TrueFan AI raised $10 million in a Series A funding round led by Baring Private Equity Partners India and Z3Partners.

The startup's AI model enables businesses to create personalised video content at scale, streamlining production processes.

Enterprise AI video platform TrueFan AI has raised $10 million in a Series A funding round led by Baring Private Equity Partners India and Z3Partners. It also saw participation from IAN Alpha Fund and 3Lines Venture Capital, as demand for AI-generated video content continues to grow among large enterprises.

The Gurugram-based startup said it has developed a foundational AI video model that enables businesses to create personalised video content at scale, eliminating the need for traditional production cycles. The platform currently serves more than 100 enterprises across sectors, including banking, healthcare, consumer goods and media.

According to the company, it has scaled from generating five million videos annually to more than 20 million over the past year, while recording 11-fold revenue growth in the last 20 months. Its customers include Bajaj Finance, HDFC Bank, Axis Max Life Insurance, Cipla, BharatPe, Zomato and Goibibo.

“AI has fundamentally changed the economics of video creation,” Nimish Goel, Co-Founder and CEO of TrueFan AI, said in a statement. “It is inevitable that video generation will become as simple as typing an email. With that, video shall become the core layer of communication for enterprises. TrueFan is building the infrastructure for that inflection, enabling organisations to generate and distribute contextual video content on demand.”

The company has created AI avatars for more than 150 celebrities, including Shah Rukh Khan, Ranveer Singh, Kareena Kapoor, Rohit Sharma and Rishabh Pant, allowing brands to generate significantly more content from a single recording session. It says its platform can produce up to 5,00,000 videos per minute in over 175 languages.

Arul Mehra, partner at Baring Private Equity Partners India, said enterprise adoption was a key factor behind the investment. “The platform is already deeply embedded in the workflows of some of India’s largest enterprises, which reflects both the strength of the product and the scale of the shift underway in enterprise video communication,” he said.

The funding will be used to support international expansion and further investment in AI infrastructure. The company is also developing real-time AI video agents for customer support, sales and onboarding applications, and has begun pilot deployments with enterprise clients.

title: AI Job Apocalypse or Productivity Boom? Silicon Valley Can’t Decide
content:
The partnership will bring Lovable’s AI-powered software development tools to Google Cloud’s enterprise marketplace, making them easier for businesses to deploy and manage.

What Actually Matters.

Lovable has signed a multi-year deal with Google Cloud to enhance its AI-powered software development tools.

The partnership will significantly increase Lovable's usage of Google Cloud infrastructure and AI services.

Stockholm-based AI startup Lovable has signed a multi-year agreement with Google Cloud that will significantly expand its use of Google’s infrastructure and AI services.

While financial details of the deal were not disclosed, the partnership is expected to increase Lovable’s Google Cloud usage by five times. The agreement also gives the company broader access to AI models from both Google and Anthropic, including Gemini and Claude, which are widely used for coding and software development tasks.

The move comes as Lovable continues its rapid growth in the AI software space. The startup, known for its AI-powered ‘vibe-coding’ platform that helps users build software using natural language prompts claims it crossed $400 million in annualised revenue earlier this year. The company also says that more than half of Fortune 500 companies use its platform in some capacity.

As part of the expanded partnership, Lovable’s AI agents will be made available through Google Cloud’s enterprise marketplace allowing businesses to access and deploy the company’s tools more easily. The integration is expected to simplify procurement and billing for enterprise customers.

The deal will also see Lovable integrate with Wiz, the cybersecurity firm that Google acquired for $32 billion. The integration will help identify and fix security vulnerabilities in code generated by both humans and AI systems.

The partnership could also benefit Anthropic which has received significant investment from Google. Increased usage of Claude through Lovable’s platform may help drive adoption of Anthropic’s AI models among enterprise customers.

The announcement highlights the growing relationship between AI startups and major cloud providers as demand for AI infrastructure continues to rise. For Google, the deal strengthens its cloud ecosystem and helps attract more enterprise AI workloads. For Lovable, it provides access to advanced AI models and scalable infrastructure needed to support its fast-growing customer base.

The agreement reflects how cloud providers and AI startups are increasingly working together to meet the growing demand for AI-powered software and enterprise applications.
