title: US Telecom Major Expands India Footprint with Global Technology Centre in Hyderabad
content:
The Finnish tyre maker will use AI and automation across application management and support services as TCS deepens its presence in the Nordic manufacturing sector.

What Actually Matters.

TCS has partnered with Nokian Tyres to enhance its IT operations through AI and automation.

The collaboration will focus on application management, development, and support services across various business functions.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has signed a strategic partnership with Finnish tyre manufacturer Nokian Tyres to modernise its IT operations using artificial intelligence, marking another deal for the Indian IT services major as it looks to position itself as an AI-led technology partner for global enterprises.

Under the engagement, TCS will expand Nokian Tyres’ use of AI across application management, development and onsite support services.

The partnership will cover end-to-end application management, including development, maintenance and support for systems used across engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, commercial and corporate functions, according to a stock exchange filing on June 4.

The companies, however, did not disclose the financial terms of the agreement.

The deal comes at a time when large IT services firms are increasingly pitching AI-led transformation projects to manufacturing clients, moving beyond pilot programmes to embed automation and AI into core business operations.

"This strategic partnership with TCS will enable Nokian Tyres to have a globally unified, agile, and efficient operating model that supports business needs,” Timmy McLellan, Chief Information Officer, Nokian Tyres, said in a statement. He added that the partnership would also create a foundation for wider adoption of automation, data driven solutions and artificial intelligence.

Nokian Tyres, listed on Nasdaq Helsinki, reported net sales of €1.4 billion in 2025 and employs around 4,000 people globally. The company manufactures premium tyres for passenger vehicles, trucks and heavy machinery.

According to TCS, the collaboration aim to improve the efficiency, resilience and scalability of Nokian Tyres' IT environment. The company said AI and agentic automation will be integrated into IT operations to accelerate issue resolution, lower operational costs and strengthen digital infrastructure.

Anupam Singhal, President and Head of Manufacturing at TCS, said the partnership reflects a broader shift in manufacturing towards AI-enabled operations and intelligent digital ecosystems.

“We are building a modern, insight-driven technology foundation to help Nokian Tyres accelerate innovation, respond faster to market shifts, and elevate manufacturing outcomes,” he said.

The agreement further strengthens TCS’ footprint in the Nordic region, where the company has operated since 1991 across Finland, Sweden, Norway and Denmark. The region has emerged as a key market for engineering, manufacturing and industrial transformation projects as enterprises increase investments in AI and automation.

title: More American Businesses Are Using DeepSeek Than Expected
content:
Ramp’s transaction data from more than 50,000 businesses shows DeepSeek becoming the platform's top trending software vendor.

What Actually Matters.

DeepSeek has become the top trending software vendor on Ramp's platform as of June 2026.

American businesses are increasingly opting for DeepSeek over traditional alternatives like OpenAI and Anthropic.

DeepSeek has emerged as one of the fastest-growing software vendors among businesses on Ramp’s spend management platform in June 2026, according to new data from Ramp Economics Lab.

The Chinese AI company topped Ramp’s monthly list of vendors showing breakout growth relative to their existing market share, ahead of event management platform PheedLoop, inference providers Fireworks AI and fal AI, software design tool Paper, and GPU cloud provider Vast.ai.

The ranking is based on transaction data from more than 50,000 businesses using Ramp’s corporate card and bill-pay platform.

Ramp said the growth reflects companies actively paying DeepSeek directly rather than merely running open-source versions of its models on their own infrastructure.

“Firms are sending and receiving data through DeepSeek directly,” wrote Ramp lead economist Ara Kharazian. “To be clear: this is not just self-hosted open source usage.”

Kharazian also adds that he didn’t expect American firms to use DeepSeek.

“In probably the biggest sign that companies are looking for cheaper alternatives to OpenAI and Anthropic, some are willing to use cheaper, Chinese models, sending U.S. data back and forth from China-hosted servers,” he wrote in a post on X.

DeepSeek previously experienced a brief surge in adoption before the adoption rate fell back. According to Ramp's AI Index, the company reached roughly 0.3% business adoption before declining to 0.1%. The latest spending data suggests renewed interest from US companies despite ongoing scrutiny around Chinese AI providers and data security.

“American model companies should take note of this competitive pressure anyway, via cheaper models or smart routing to help firms better manage spiralling AI spend,” adds Kharazian.

The broader rankings point to growing enterprise demand for open-source AI infrastructure.

Three model-serving and inference platforms—Fireworks AI, fal AI, and DeepInfra—appeared among the top-trending vendors, suggesting businesses are increasingly deploying open-source models rather than relying exclusively on proprietary offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic.

Anthropic led Ramp’s separate ranking of fastest-growing vendors by market-share growth, followed by AI note-taking startup Granola, developer platforms Vercel and Netlify, Canva, Grammarly, Figma, Perplexity AI, Tailscale and Higgsfield AI.

The data also suggests that AI adoption has not displaced several established software categories. Design platforms Paper and Figma both appeared in the rankings, while web infrastructure providers Vercel and Netlify continued to post strong growth among Ramp customers.

title: Google’s New Gemma Model Brings Multimodal AI to 16GB Laptops
content:
While announcing the new Gemma 4 12B, Google also said Gemma 4 models have now surpassed 150 million downloads across the developer community.

What Actually Matters.

Google has launched Gemma 4 12B, a multimodal model designed for local use on 16GB laptops.

The model supports text, image, and audio inputs through a unified architecture, enhancing its versatility.

Google has introduced Gemma 4 12B, a new open-weight multimodal model designed to run locally on consumer hardware while supporting text, image and audio inputs through a single unified architecture.

The model sits between Google’s smaller E4B model and its larger 26B Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) system, offering what the company describes as near-26B benchmark performance at less than half the memory footprint.

Google said Gemma 4 models have now surpassed 150 million downloads across the developer community.

Gemma 4 12B is the first mid-sized Gemma model to include native audio capabilities. According to Google, the model can run locally on laptops equipped with 16GB of VRAM or unified memory, targeting multimodal reasoning tasks, agentic workflows and offline AI applications.

A key technical change is the model’s encoder-free multimodal architecture. Most multimodal systems use dedicated vision and audio encoders that convert inputs into embeddings before passing them to the language model. Gemma 4 12B removes those components and processes visual and audio inputs directly within the model backbone.

For vision, Google replaced the traditional vision encoder with a lightweight embedding module consisting of a matrix multiplication layer, positional embeddings and normalisation steps. For audio, the company eliminated the audio encoder entirely, projecting raw audio signals into the same token space used by text.

“What makes Gemma 4 12B stand out is its streamlined approach to processing visual and audio inputs,” Google said. The company said removing separate encoders reduces memory requirements and latency while simplifying deployment on local hardware.

The model also includes Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) drafters, which generate multiple future tokens simultaneously to reduce inference latency. Google is releasing Gemma 4 12B under the Apache 2.0 licence and making it available through tools including LM Studio, Ollama, Hugging Face Transformers, llama.cpp, MLX, SGLang and vLLM.

Alongside the model release, Google is launching a new Gemma Skills Repository that contains reusable agent components for developers building applications on top of Gemma models. Production deployment options include Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Model Garden, Cloud Run and GKE.

The launch extends Google's recent push into smaller and more efficient AI models.

In recent months, the company introduced Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite, a model aimed at high-volume developer workloads with lower latency and cost, while continuing to expand the Gemini Flash family for production inference.

Gemma 4 12B also follows the broader Gemma 4 rollout, which introduced E4B and 26B variants focused on multimodal reasoning and agentic workflows, as Google increases its investment in models that can run directly on laptops, phones and other edge devices.

title: MeitY Picks TCS, NEC India and Kyndryl for Government AI Projects
content:
The other companies selected are Cactus Technology Solutions Pvt Ltd (CTSPL), CoRover Pvt Ltd and Innefu Labs Ltd.

What Actually Matters.

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology has selected six companies for AI projects under the Digital India programme.

The empanelment allows access to a common pool of AI vendors for various government projects.

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has selected six companies, including Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), NEC Corporation India and Kyndryl Solutions, to provide artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) services and personnel for government projects under the Digital India programme, according to a report by Moneycontrol.

The empanelment, carried out by the National e-Governance Division (NeGD), will enable central ministries, state departments, public sector undertakings and affiliated organisations to access a common pool of AI vendors for projects spanning citizen services, analytics, process automation and operational efficiency.

The other companies selected are Cactus Technology Solutions Pvt Ltd (CTSPL), CoRover Pvt Ltd and Innefu Labs Ltd. The six firms emerged from a competitive bidding process that drew around 80 participants, including major consulting and technology companies such as Deloitte, EY, PwC, KPMG, Fractal Analytics and Gnani, the report said.

According to Moneycontrol, the empanelment will remain valid for two years, with an option to extend it by an additional year. The initiative is aimed at streamlining the procurement of AI services across government departments by standardising commercial terms and reducing onboarding timelines.

Among the selected vendors, Innefu Labs submitted the lowest bid at ₹40.67 lakh, followed by TCS at ₹42.89 lakh. NEC Corporation India quoted ₹48.98 lakh, CTSPL bid ₹52.74 lakh, Kyndryl submitted a bid of ₹55.70 lakh, while CoRover quoted ₹69 lakh.

The move comes as the government accelerates efforts to integrate AI into both public-facing services and internal administrative functions.

Under the empanelment framework, government agencies can directly engage any of the approved vendors for AI-related assignments, although they are required to keep NeGD informed of such engagements, according to the report.

title: IIT Delhi, Cadence Launch AI Lab for Semiconductor Talent
content:
IIT Delhi and Cadence have established an AI-enabled lab to nurture semiconductor talent and support startups.

The lab provides access to industry-standard electronic design automation tools, bridging the gap between education and industry.

The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi and Cadence Design Systems have launched an AI-enabled innovation lab to train semiconductor talent, support research, and help early-stage startups in India.

The IIT Delhi–Cadence Innovation Lab will give students and researchers access to electronic design automation (EDA) tools used by the semiconductor industry. The lab aligns with the India Semiconductor Mission and the government’s Design Linked Incentive (DLI) scheme.

“Students at IIT Delhi now use the same AI-enabled tools they’ll see on day one in industry, closing the gap from classroom to tapeout,” said Alok Jain, Corporate Vice President and India Managing Director at Cadence. He added that industry-grade technology, project-based learning, and startup support would help improve workforce readiness for India’s semiconductor sector.

The multidisciplinary centre will provide access to more than 200 Cadence solutions across chip design verification, digital implementation, analogue design, and system design analysis. IIT Delhi students, researchers, and educators will use the same AI-enabled workflows that engineers use in professional settings.

Cadence said the move aims to improve engineering productivity and strengthen the use of AI in VLSI design.

IIT Delhi has also introduced Cadence-developed courses as part of the programme. These courses combine classroom teaching with project-based labs and assessments. The institute said the curriculum moves beyond theory by exposing students to practical tools and real-world engineering problems. Industry experts and Cadence professionals will also deliver guest lectures.

The lab will introduce an Early Master’s Research pathway for selected fourth-year undergraduate students from IITs and NITs. Cadence experts and IIT Delhi faculty will mentor students across research areas.

The initiative will also support pre-seed semiconductor startups through an incubator programme. The programme will offer selected startups a lower-cost route to first tape-out and prototype development.

Prof Jayadeva, professor in charge of the Cadence-IIT Delhi Innovation Lab, said the partnership would help expand research output, prepare students for careers, and support founders in moving from ideas to prototypes.

title: Most Enterprises Lack Infrastructure to Scale AI, Shows Tata Communications Report
content:
77% of enterprise leaders view artificial intelligence as a priority, yet 65% rely on outdated infrastructure.

Only 29% of enterprises have infrastructure capable of scaling to meet AI demands.

Enterprises face challenges scaling artificial intelligence capabilities due to legacy infrastructure, shows a report by Tata Communications and Bloomberg Media Studios, titled ‘Building Durable AI Advantage’. The study surveyed 501 executives at enterprises with revenues exceeding $500 million across North America, Europe, and Asia.

The survey states that 77% of enterprise leaders consider artificial intelligence a board-level priority. However, 65% of these enterprises operate on legacy or developing infrastructure. Only 29% of respondents report that their infrastructure can scale to meet business demands.

The report identifies five areas affecting AI implementation: foundation, integration, skills, governance, and return on investment. Regarding foundational infrastructure, less than half of the enterprises have modernised network connectivity, hybrid deployment flexibility, or data architecture.

In terms of integration, 28% of leaders report difficulties integrating artificial intelligence with legacy systems, and 38% state that integration concerns cause delays in procurement.

Skills shortages are cited by 30% of enterprises as a barrier, a figure that rises to 45% for enterprises with revenues over $5 billion. Governance processes also impact implementation, with 42% of enterprises identifying security and compliance reviews as a source of delays.

Sumeet Walia, President and Chief Revenue Officer, Tata Communications, said, “AI has become one of the defining business priorities of our time, but the real differentiator is no longer AI itself but it’s the infrastructure and integration that enable AI to deliver value at scale. Our research shows that while enterprise ambition is accelerating, readiness remains uneven.”

“AI is a tightly coupled ecosystem of compute, power, connectivity and platforms, which are no longer independent systems. They are becoming one unified infrastructure. AI is accelerating this convergence, which Tata Communications addresses through its digital fabric of solutions, it is where we are uniquely positioned to enable customers to achieve their business goals,” he added.

title: Meta Rolls Out AI Business Agent Across WhatsApp Messenger and Instagram
content:
Meta has launched its Business Agent to enhance customer interactions on WhatsApp, Messenger, and Instagram.

Over one million businesses currently utilise the Meta Business Agent, with daily interactions exceeding one billion.

Meta has announced the global expansion of its Business Agent to help businesses automate customer interactions across WhatsApp, Messenger and Instagram.

The company said more than one million businesses are already using a Meta Business Agent on WhatsApp and Messenger, with over one billion active conversations between people and businesses taking place daily across WhatsApp, Messenger and Instagram.

“Today, we’re introducing Meta Business Agent – AI that lets every business show up for every customer as if they had an infinite team behind them,” the company said in a statement.

Businesses can set up the agent within minutes or integrate it with existing enterprise systems. The tool can answer business-specific questions, recommend products from a catalogue, book appointments, qualify leads, escalate conversations to human agents when required and complete sales transactions.

Meta is also extending Business Agent support to Instagram. The company said businesses can initially activate the feature for free, while paid subscription plans will be introduced in the coming months.

Alongside customer support functions, the AI agent will provide business owners with a daily briefing summarising missed conversations and insights from customer interactions.

“Because the Meta Business Agent responds to customers, it doubles as a partner that can deliver a morning briefing to catch you up on chats you missed overnight and provide insights on your threads,” Meta said.

The company said it is initially rolling out these management features to a select group of businesses using the WhatsApp Business app, Instagram Pro, Messenger and Meta Business Suite. Future updates will allow the agent to assist with tasks such as market research, product analysis, calendar management and competitive intelligence.

Meta also unveiled the Meta Business Agent Platform, a new infrastructure layer that allows companies to build, customise, and deploy AI agents at scale. The platform can connect with hundreds of third-party systems, including Shopify, Zendesk and Shopee, allowing agents to perform actions on behalf of businesses.

According to Meta, the platform includes enterprise controls, guardrails and measurement tools that allow companies to define operational rules and deliver personalised customer experiences through messaging applications.

The company is also introducing new discovery features on WhatsApp. Users will soon be able to find businesses powered by Meta Business Agent by searching for a business name or by sharing business contact information within chats.

Meta said the updates are intended to help businesses manage customer interactions and improve accessibility across its messaging platforms.

title: No Market Is Adopting AI at Work Faster Than India: BCG
content:
India is a global leader in workplace AI adoption, with employees using AI more frequently than in most major economies.

A significant percentage of Indian frontline AI users report saving at least one full workday each week due to AI tools.

India has emerged as a global leader in workplace AI adoption with employees using AI more frequently than workers in most other major economies, according to the latest AI at Work report by Boston Consulting Group (BCG).

The report found that Indian frontline workers and managers are among the most active AI users globally. Around 70% of Indian frontline AI users said they save at least one full workday every week using AI tools while 96% reported that AI has already changed the skills required for their jobs. Both figures are the highest among the 14 markets surveyed.

India also recorded the highest level of AI-driven job satisfaction. About 88% of frontline employees said AI has made their work more enjoyable and satisfying.

Globally, AI adoption among frontline workers has reached 74%, rising by more than 20 percentage points over the past two years. India and the Middle East are leading this trend, while countries such as the United States, France and Italy lag behind.

The report also highlights growing expectations for AI agent software systems capable of performing tasks autonomously. In India, 86% of frontline employees believe AI agents could handle at least half of their work within the next three years, significantly higher than the global average of 52%.

“India’s leadership in AI adoption reflects a workforce that has embraced new ways of working with remarkable speed and openness,” said Nipun Kalra, India Leader at BCG X.

He added that Indian organisations are now moving towards transforming workflows and business operations using AI. However, the report notes that many companies have yet to fully capitalise on AI’s benefits. Around 66% of regular AI users globally said they receive little or no guidance on how to use the time AI saves to pursue more strategic work.

BCG found that organisations with a clear AI strategy are significantly more likely to see measurable business benefits and improved employee satisfaction. Companies redesigning end-to-end workflows around AI reported stronger gains than those simply introducing new AI tools.

The findings are based on a survey of 11,749 employees across 14 countries and multiple industries, examining how AI is reshaping work, leadership and employee expectations worldwide.

title: US Telecom Major Expands India Footprint with Global Technology Centre in Hyderabad
content:
The company is expected to scale operations to nearly 1,000 employees by 2027.

What Actually Matters.

T-Mobile USA has inaugurated a Global Technology Centre in Hyderabad, covering a large facility to enhance its operations.

The centre aims to become an innovation hub, focusing on software engineering, AI, and digital solutions.

US-based telecommunications company TMUS Global Solutions (T-Mobile USA) has inaugurated its Global Technology Centre in Hyderabad, encompassing a new 2.5 lakh sq ft facility.

T-Mobile, one of the largest wireless network operators in the United States, serves over 140 million customers and powers next-generation connectivity solutions.

During the inauguration, Duddilla Sridhar Babu, Telangana’s Information Technology, Electronics, Communications, Industries and Commerce, and Legislative Affairs Minister, stated, “When they committed to building from Hyderabad, we promised them access to the best technology talent in the country. Today, seeing them onboard hundreds of skilled professionals and establish one of their fastest-growing centres in such a short span is a strong validation of Hyderabad’s ability to deliver world-class talent at scale.”

The new facility will function as a strategic innovation hub, developing capabilities across software engineering, cloud platforms, data analytics, cybersecurity, DevOps, automation, AI, and next-generation digital solutions. It is expected to scale operations to nearly 1,000 employees by 2027.

Chandra Gupta, Vice President, Information Technology, TMUS Global Solutions, said, “Hyderabad offers a strong combination of technology talent, innovation capabilities, and an established ecosystem that aligns with our long-term goals. Our Global Technology Centre in Hyderabad will play an important role in strengthening our engineering and digital capabilities, while enabling teams to build solutions that support our customers and business priorities.”

Hyderabad continues to attract Fortune 500 companies establishing specialised technology centres beyond traditional outsourcing, spanning sectors such as telecom, life sciences, retail, FMCG, travel, and hospitality.

With this addition, Hyderabad now hosts over 450 GCCs employing more than 3,00,000 professionals, further consolidating its status as a leading global technology hub.

title: Tech Mahindra Rebrands ADMS to Push AI-Led Software Modernisation
content:
Tech Mahindra is also introducing a "Service Tokens" pricing mechanism, designed to offer clients greater modularity in how they consume services and more predictable cost structures.

What Actually Matters.

Tech Mahindra has rebranded its ADMS to focus on AI-led enterprise application modernisation.

The new offering emphasises autonomous AI to transform software management for organisations.

Tech Mahindra has announced the launch of a next-generation services portfolio that places AI at the heart of enterprise application development and modernisation. The Agentic Development & Modernisation Services (ADMS) offering is strategic pivot for the Pune-headquartered firm, which is betting on autonomous AI to reshape how organisations manage their software estates.

The launch carries symbolic weight beyond its technical scope. Tech Mahindra is deliberately repurposing the familiar industry acronym ADMS, long associated with Application Development and Maintenance Services, to now stand for Agentic Development and Modernisation Services.

The rebranding reflects a broader industry shift away from traditional, labour-intensive software delivery models towards intelligent, self-adapting systems that require far less human intervention.

At its core, the portfolio is built around four interconnected pillars. The first focuses on platform modernisation, helping enterprises rebuild ageing infrastructure into modular, API-first architectures capable of supporting AI-driven processes. The second pillar, agentic software engineering, embeds AI agents directly into development and DevSecOps workflows, with the goal of improving delivery speed and engineering quality.

The third area addresses autonomous operations, bringing together intelligent automation, knowledge graphs, and AIOps capabilities to enable real-time monitoring and self-healing system environments. The fourth pillar centres on what Tech Mahindra calls an Autonomous Quality Fabric, a continuous, agent-driven approach to quality assurance that runs in parallel with DevOps pipelines.

The portfolio is underpinned by a suite of proprietary platforms and accelerators, including Swifter.io, AppGinieZ, Reforge, and LitmusT. Delivery will follow what the company terms a Vector Squad model, pairing human engineers with AI agents.

Tech Mahindra is also introducing a "Service Tokens" pricing mechanism, designed to offer clients greater modularity in how they consume services and more predictable cost structures, a move likely aimed at making enterprise AI adoption more commercially accessible.

Kunal Purohit, President of Next Gen Verticals at Tech Mahindra, highlighted the scale of the opportunity the company is positioning itself to capture. “This will be driven by the rising demand for intelligent operations, autonomous software engineering, and outcome-driven transformation,” Purohit said. “With Agentic Development & Modernisation Services, Tech Mahindra is helping enterprises accelerate this transition by enabling more adaptive, resilient, and context-aware application ecosystems that define the future of autonomous enterprises.”

The announcement arrives as competition intensifies among global IT services providers to stake out credible positions in agentic AI.

For Tech Mahindra, which employs more than 147,000 professionals across 90-plus countries and serves over 1,100 clients worldwide, the launch represents an attempt to move up the value chain at a moment when traditional application management work faces commoditisation pressure.

The company frames the initiative as consistent with its wider ambition to help clients transition from conventional digital environments to what it describes as intelligent, composable, AI-native ecosystems.

The IT services company said the initiative will create a specialised cadre of engineers trained in AI native development, agentic AI and modern software architectures as enterprises move from AI pilots to production scale deployments.

What Actually Matters.

Cognizant has launched the 'Ace Team' programme to develop specialised AI-focused engineers for enterprise AI adoption.

The initiative combines selective hiring and an elite talent pathway within a centrally governed engineering community.

Cognizant has launched a new engineering talent programme aimed at building a specialised pool of AI focused developers, indicating the growing emphasis among IT services firms on developing in-house capabilities to support enterprise AI adoption.

The Nasdaq-listed company on Wednesday announced the launch of its ‘Ace Team’ programme, which it described as a combination of a selective hiring initiative, an elite talent pathway and a centrally governed engineering community.

The company said members of the Ace Team will work on client projects using AI native tools, modern software architectures and outcome driven engineering methods.

Engineers selected under the programme are expected to contribute to building production grade AI applications, including retrieval augmented generation (RAG) systems, agentic AI workflows and large language model integrated applications.

According to Cognizant, the programme is aligned with its three strategic priorities – improving productivity through AI and industrialising AI adoption across enterprises. The company said the initiative is intended to support the development of niche AI offerings and large scale technology modernisation programmes.

Selection for the programme will be based on technical capabilities, AI proficiency and communication skills rather than educational pedigree alone. Candidates will undergo assessments covering areas such as full stack AI development, data structures and algorithms, prompt engineering, RAG systems, agentic AI and modern front end technologies.

In the first phase, the programme will be open to existing offer holders and select off campus candidates, including graduates from leading institutions.

The development comes at a time when global technology services firms increasingly invest in specialised AI talent amid rising enterprise demand for generative AI and agentic AI deployments.

Rajesh Varrier, President – Global Operations, Chairman and Managing Director of Cognizant India, said enterprises are rapidly shifting from AI experimentation to real world implementation, increasing the need for AI ready engineering talent.

“The launch of the Cognizant Ace Team program marks a critical step in strengthening our engineering depth as enterprises move rapidly from AI experimentation to real-world execution. Delivering measurable, scalable AI outcomes increasingly depends on AI-ready skills and strong engineering fundamentals,” Varrier said in a statement.

Cognizant said it plans to expand participation over time to include students from premium campuses, partner institutions, existing employees and lateral hires with up to three years of experience.

title: Hexaware Adds Governance, Lifecycle Management Features to AI Agent Platform Agentverse
content:
The IT services firm said the latest enhancements are aimed at helping enterprises move AI projects beyond pilot stages by improving governance, security and lifecycle management of AI agents.

What Actually Matters.

Hexaware's enhancements to Agentverse aim to help enterprises scale AI projects beyond pilot stages.

New features include policy-aware connectors and role-based access controls for better governance and compliance.

Indian IT firm Hexaware Technologies has rolled out new governance, development and lifecycle management capabilities for Agentverse, its enterprise AI agent platform, as the company looks to address challenges around scaling AI deployments beyond experimentation.

The enhancements come nearly three months after Hexaware launched Agentverse and are designed to help enterprises manage, govern and deploy AI agents at scale.

While companies across industries are increasing investments in AI, many projects remain confined to pilot stages because of concerns around governance, security, compliance and alignment with business objectives.

According to the company, Agentverse now includes policy-aware connectors for integrating with enterprise systems, enhanced memory and contextual intelligence capabilities, and governance features such as role-based access controls, audit trails and observability dashboards.

These are aimed at helping enterprises maintain compliance and oversight while deploying AI agents across business functions.

The company has also introduced Agentic Studios, a development environment that provides a structured workflow covering stages from design and approval to testing, deployment and operations.

The tool is compatible with major cloud environments including Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services, and is intended to reduce development cycles for AI applications.

A third addition is AI agent lifecycle management, which enables enterprises to monitor and govern AI agents throughout their lifecycle, from deployment to retirement. Hexaware said the capability is designed to ensure AI systems remain accountable and aligned with business objectives over time.

“The industry spent the last few years proving that AI agents can execute tasks. The harder challenge, and the one we built Agentverse to solve, is ensuring those agents remain accountable, governable, and aligned to business objectives throughout their lifecycle. This update is designed to make that possible,” R Srikrishna, CEO & Executive Director, Hexaware, said in a statement.

Siddharth Dhar, President and Global Head of AI at Hexaware, said the update adds governing intelligence layer that enables enterprises to embed, manage, and continuously evolve AI across the entire operational landscape.

The announcement comes as IT services firms increasingly position themselves around agentic AI platforms and governance frameworks, responding to growing enterprise demand for tools that can securely deploy and manage AI agents in production environments.

content:
This marks a significant jump from December last year, when Microsoft had announced that Infosys, TCS, Wipro and Cognizant would together deploy more than 200,000 Copilot licences.

What Actually Matters.

Infosys, TCS, and Wipro have expanded Microsoft 365 Copilot deployments to over 300,000 employees, indicating a shift towards widespread AI adoption.

This increase reflects a move beyond pilot programmes, as large IT firms fully integrate AI into their operations.

Microsoft’s push to embed generative AI into enterprise workflows is gathering pace in India, with Infosys, TCS and Wipro collectively scaling Microsoft 365 Copilot deployments to more than 3,00,000 employees, indicating how large IT services firms are moving AI adoption beyond pilot programmes.

The latest expansion marks a significant jump from December last year, when Microsoft had announced that Infosys, TCS, Wipro and Cognizant would together deploy more than 200,000 Copilot licences, with each company committing to over 50,000 seats.

According to Microsoft, Infosys, TCS, and Wipro have each crossed the 100,000-user mark for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

The announcement comes as Indian IT services firms increasingly position themselves as large scale adopters of AI even as they build solutions for global clients.

“This is the shift we are seeing with our most ambitious customers: moving from experimenting with AI to building their businesses around it,” Puneet Chandok, President, Microsoft India and South Asia, said. “The best AI deployments translate an organisation’s own intelligence into decisions that reshape customer engagement, business processes and growth — and global IT majors are doing exactly that with Microsoft.”

Infosys said its plan to deploy Copilot to more than 100,000 employees across delivery, engineering and corporate functions has resulted in monthly active usage exceeding 91%. The Bengaluru headquartered company has integrated the tool into its broader Infosys Topaz AI strategy aimed at embedding AI into internal workflows and client engagements.

“The real opportunity with AI lies in how deeply it is embedded into everyday work,” Salil Parekh, CEO and MD, Infosys, said. “We are focused on operationalising this at scale with Infosys Topaz – integrating AI across our workflows to enhance enterprise effectiveness and strengthen our ability to unlock AI value for our clients,” he added.

TCS said it has enabled more than 100,000 associates with Microsoft 365 Copilot, using the technology across reporting, meeting management, documentation, analysis and other knowledge intensive tasks. The company said the deployment forms part of its effort to build an AI-first culture and shape the Human + AI operating model of the future.

Wipro is driving an AI-first transformation, deploying AI at scale across its own operations and global clients through Wipro Intelligence, a unified suite of AI-powered platforms. The company said it has reached over 95% monthly active usage of Microsoft 365 Copilot, with associates generating 7.5 million prompts each month and averaging 23 actions per user per week.

The milestone highlights India's growing importance in Microsoft's AI strategy. Chandok recently said India is among the fastest growing markets for Copilot adoption globally, with enterprises increasingly moving from experimentation to production deployments.

Microsoft has been investing heavily in AI infrastructure in India. Recently, the tech giant said it is launching its largest domestic facility in Hyderabad, backed by a $17.5 billion infrastructure commitment.

title: Microsoft Launches Scout, an Autonomous AI Agent Built on OpenClaw for Microsoft 365
content:
Factory says its new model-routing system automatically switches between AI models to reduce coding costs by 20–25% while maintaining up to 99% of Claude Opus 4.7's benchmark performance.

What Actually Matters.

Factory Router automates the selection of AI models to optimise coding tasks and reduce costs.

The system can lower token spending by 20–25% while achieving near-Claude Opus 4.7 performance.

Factory has launched Factory Router, a new AI model-routing system designed to reduce enterprise software engineering costs by automatically selecting the most appropriate model for each coding task.

The product entered private research preview on June 1 and is available through the company’s CLI and desktop applications.

The company said Factory Router reduces token spending by 20–25% while maintaining near-frontier performance by dynamically assigning workloads across a mix of frontier and lower-cost models.

If a selected model struggles with a task, the system can escalate the session to a more capable model and reroute workloads across providers when endpoints degrade or capacity becomes constrained.

Factory benchmarked the system against Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7. According to the company, Factory Router achieved 99% of Opus 4.7's pass rate at 20% lower cost per session on Terminal-Bench 2, and 96% of Opus performance at 25% lower cost on Legacy-Bench.

The launch targets a growing concern among enterprises deploying AI coding tools at scale: rising inference costs.

Factory argued that organisations frequently route routine work, such as documentation updates, code refactoring, bug fixes, and search-heavy investigations, through premium reasoning models, thereby increasing token consumption without necessarily improving engineering output.

Rather than introducing a new model, Factory Router serves as an orchestration layer that evaluates each Droid session and selects from a pool of frontier- and efficiency-focused models. Less demanding tasks can be handled by lower-cost models, while more complex engineering work can be routed to frontier systems.

Factory CEO Matan Grinberg wrote in a post on X, “If your daughter needs tutoring in algebra, you can probably find someone cheaper than Albert Einstein.”

“Giving every task to GPT-5.5 or Opus 4.8 is overkill.” He said many software engineering tasks can be completed “10x cheaper and 10x faster” using smaller models, forming the basis for Factory Router's automated model-selection system.

Factory said Router delivers 99.9%+ request reliability through provider failover, dedicated throughput allocations for enterprise customers and routing across multiple providers and capacity sources. Enterprise administrators can further customise routing behaviour through policy controls, workflow guidance and organisation-wide model governance settings.

Factory published additional benchmark data describing what it calls the cost-performance “Pareto frontier” for AI coding workloads.

According to the company, Router operates near the point where cost reductions remain substantial while benchmark performance declines only marginally. More aggressive routing configurations reduced Terminal-Bench 2 costs to 56% of the Opus baseline but lowered pass rates to 81%, while Legacy-Bench costs fell to 30% of baseline costs with pass rates dropping to 49%.

The company raised a $150 million Series C in April, led by Khosla Ventures, with participation from Sequoia Capital, Blackstone and Insight Partners, valuing the company at $1.5 billion.

The announcement also drew attention from executives across the AI tooling ecosystem.

Reacting on X, Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue said automatic routing could “redistribute value capture and usage towards many more models than just frontier ones,” particularly open-source and lower-cost alternatives.

Delangue argued that requiring users to manually select models creates enough friction that many default to frontier models for all tasks.

The launch comes as enterprises increasingly scrutinise AI spending amid a broader debate around maximising AI usage and token consumption as a measure of productivity.

While companies have aggressively rolled out coding assistants and AI agents, investors and executives are increasingly asking whether rising inference bills are translating into proportional gains in software output.

title: OpenAI Wants Codex to Replace More Than Coding
content:
New update marks OpenAI’s push to make Codex a platform for analysts, designers, sales teams, investors, and other knowledge workers.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI is broadening Codex's scope beyond coding to serve various professional roles.

The new update features role-specific plugins tailored for analysts, designers, and sales teams.

OpenAI is expanding Codex beyond software development with a new set of role-specific plugins, annotation tools, and a preview feature that allows businesses to generate and share interactive websites and applications.

The company said more than 5 million people now use Codex every week, with non-developers accounting for roughly 20% of users and adopting the platform more than three times faster than developers.

The update introduces six role-specific plugins aimed at analysts, marketers, designers, sales teams, investors, and bankers.

According to OpenAI, the plugins package together applications, workflows, instructions, and skills tailored to specific job functions, requiring no coding knowledge to use. The initial set combines 62 applications and 110 skills.

The data analytics plugin connects Codex to tools including Snowflake, Databricks Genie, Hex, and Tableau, enabling users to analyse business data, investigate changes in key metrics, and generate reports and dashboards.

A creative production plugin integrates services such as Figma, Canva, Shutterstock, Picsart, and Fal for campaign asset creation and image generation. Other plugins target sales operations, product design, public equity investing, and investment banking, drawing on platforms including Salesforce, HubSpot, FactSet, LSEG, Moody’s, PitchBook, and Hebbia.

The sales plugin for Codex. pic.twitter.com/GWjRyebinS

— OpenAI (@OpenAI) June 2, 2026

OpenAI said organisations can customise existing plugins or build and distribute their own internally. Additional plugins covering corporate finance, private equity, marketing strategy, management consulting, and legal workflows are planned.

The company also said it is working toward an open plugin ecosystem that would allow partners to deploy integrations directly into Codex and ChatGPT.

Alongside the plugin rollout, OpenAI introduced Sites, a new feature entering preview for Business and Enterprise customers. Sites allow users to generate and host interactive web applications directly within Codex and share them with colleagues through a URL.

OpenAI said the feature can create dashboards, planning tools, project hubs, review workspaces, galleries, and other lightweight applications from prompts, with content that can be updated through ongoing interactions with Codex.

Building apps has never been easier.

With Sites, Codex can turn your work, ideas, and plans into an interactive website or app your team can explore, use, and share with a URL.

Rolling out to Business and Enterprise plans, before expanding more broadly. pic.twitter.com/fF17Y2EzCP

The company said Sites are designed to transform documents, analyses, and planning materials into collaborative interfaces.

Example use cases include customer review portals, financial scenario planners, launch management hubs, operational dashboards, and internal knowledge repositories. OpenAI is also working with partners including Vercel, Wix, Replit, Figma, Webflow, and Emergent as it develops a broader Sites ecosystem.

OpenAI is also extending Codex's annotation capabilities beyond software projects. Users can now highlight specific elements within documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and websites to request targeted revisions.

The company said annotations can be used to update interface elements, trace the source of claims, revise charts, or modify selected content without regenerating an entire document.

The launch comes as OpenAI positions Codex as a broader platform for knowledge work. In a separate report published alongside the announcement, the company said Codex has surpassed 5 million weekly active users, up more than sixfold since the launch of its desktop application in February.

Knowledge workers now represent around 20% of users, while personal users account for more than 5%, with both groups growing faster than the platform's developer base.

OpenAI said data analysis, research, and knowledge-artifact creation are among the fastest-growing Codex use cases. The company reported week-over-week growth of 110% in data-analysis tasks, 37% in research activities, and 36% in the production of reports, presentations, contracts, spreadsheets, PDFs, images, audio, and video. More than half of users in these categories now work with PDFs and spreadsheets through the platform.

The company also reported a shift toward parallel task execution. Around 50% of Codex users now run multiple tasks simultaneously during the day, up from less than one-third in mid-April.

OpenAI said the trend reflects how users increasingly use Codex to coordinate several workstreams at once, from data analysis and reporting to scripting, research, and application development.

title: Neo4j to Launch ‘Alternative to Palantir Gotham’ By Acquiring Graph Aware
content:
The graph database company plans to combine GraphAware’s intelligence analysis software with its own graph platform to target government, defence and law-enforcement customers seeking sovereign AI deployments.

What Actually Matters.

Neo4j plans to acquire GraphAware to enhance its offerings in government intelligence software.

The combined platform will provide an alternative to Palantir Gotham, emphasising data sovereignty.

Neo4j has agreed to acquire GraphAware, a company that develops intelligence analysis software for law enforcement, defence and government agencies, as it moves into the government intelligence software market with what it describes as an ‘open alternative to Palantir Gotham’.

The deal will combine GraphAware’s Hume intelligence analysis platform with Neo4j’s graph intelligence technology, creating a unified offering for defence, law enforcement, cyber security and public-sector customers.

The acquisition forms part of Neo4j’s previously announced $100 million AI investment programme and is intended to accelerate the company’s push into AI-powered intelligence analysis, including agentic systems that can connect, analyse and reason over large volumes of fragmented data.

GraphAware Hume is already built on Neo4j’s graph database and is used by government agencies for investigative and intelligence workflows.

Neo4j said the combined platform will provide agencies with an alternative to proprietary intelligence systems such as Palantir Gotham while allowing customers to retain control over where data is stored, how systems are deployed and how information can be migrated.

“For over a decade, governments have utilised intelligence analysis software from Palantir,” Neo4j Founder and Chief Executive Emil Eifrem said. “Now they will have a legitimate choice with GraphAware Hume, powered by the Neo4j graph intelligence platform.”

The companies are positioning the combined offering around open standards, interoperability and data sovereignty at a time when governments are increasingly scrutinising where sensitive data resides and how AI systems are deployed.

Neo4j highlighted support for the Graph Query Language (GQL) standard and deployment options spanning sovereign cloud environments, private infrastructure and on-premises systems.

GraphAware’s software is designed for analyst-led investigations and intelligence operations. The platform connects data across people, organisations, locations and events, allowing investigators to identify relationships, build contextual understanding and collaborate across teams.

Existing deployments include the Western Australia Police Force, the U.S. Department of Defense and a European national cyber defence agency, according to the companies.

GraphAware will continue operating as a standalone business unit within Neo4j after the transaction closes, with founder and chief executive Michal Bachman remaining in charge of the business.

Neo4j said customer operations and existing deployments will remain unchanged during the integration process.

The acquisition comes as graph databases gain prominence in AI deployments, particularly for knowledge graphs, retrieval systems and agent architectures that require structured context and explainable reasoning.

Neo4j said demand for AI-related graph deployments has increased significantly, with the company reporting a fourfold increase in customers building AI-ready data systems and a growing share of those workloads moving into production.

The transaction is expected to close in the third quarter of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals, including foreign investment review in Australia.

Founded in Sweden in 2007 and now headquartered in San Mateo, California, Neo4j is one of the best-known graph database companies, providing software that helps organisations analyse relationships across large, connected datasets.

The company was valued at more than $2 billion in its 2021 Series F funding round and reported surpassing $200 million in annual recurring revenue in 2024 as demand for AI and knowledge graph infrastructure increased.

title: Uber Limits AI Coding Tool Spend to $1,500 Per Employee a Month: Report
content:
The company has introduced monthly spending limits on agentic coding tools, including Claude Code and Cursor, after exhausting its AI coding budget earlier this year.

What Actually Matters.

Uber has set monthly spending caps for AI coding tools after exhausting its budget early in the year.

Each employee is limited to $1,500 per month per AI coding tool, allowing separate allowances for different platforms.

Uber Technologies has introduced spending caps on AI-powered coding tools used by employees after the company exhausted its AI coding budget earlier this year, according to a Bloomberg report.

The ride-hailing company is limiting staff to $1,500 per month in token spending per AI coding tool, an Uber spokesperson told Bloomberg.

The limits apply separately to each tool, meaning usage on one platform does not reduce an employee's allowance on another.

The restrictions were introduced over recent months and apply to agentic coding products such as Anthropic’s Claude Code and Cursor.

Unlike conventional chatbot deployments, coding agents often consume large volumes of tokens while carrying out multi-step tasks, increasing infrastructure and software expenses even as the underlying model.

The spending limits follow comments from Uber executives earlier this year that the company had already exhausted its planned 2026 AI coding tools budget within the first four months of the year.

Uber CTO Praveen Neppalli Naga has said surging adoption of tools such as Claude Code had pushed spending well beyond internal forecasts, while the company expanded AI-assisted software development across its engineering organisation.

Reports at the time indicated that a large majority of Uber engineers were regularly using AI coding tools, driving a sharp increase in token consumption and software costs.

Uber's move comes amid a broader industry debate over “tokenmaxxing”—the practice of maximising AI model usage on the belief that higher token consumption leads to greater productivity.

Uber COO Andrew Macdonald recently questioned whether rising AI usage could be directly linked to more useful consumer-facing products, arguing that companies will increasingly need to justify AI spending against measurable business outcomes.

Similar discussions have emerged across large technology companies as agentic coding systems generate rapidly growing infrastructure and API costs.

The debate has spread beyond Uber. Microsoft has reportedly reduced internal Claude Code deployments amid rising AI costs, while Google executives have acknowledged growing enterprise scrutiny of AI spending and returns.

According to a report from Axios, Salesforce has emphasised the ROI on AI usage and efficiency rather than raw model consumption.

The company has even criticised ‘tokenmaxxing’ the idea that more AI usage automatically means more value, and introduced internal metrics focused on business outcomes instead of token volume.

Across the industry, companies are increasingly evaluating whether higher token consumption and broader AI adoption are translating into measurable productivity gains and business outcomes.

title: ONDC Secures ₹430 Cr as Tech Giants and Public Banks Back India's Open Commerce Push
content:
India's government-backed digital commerce network draws investment from Zoho, Uber, Paytm, SBI, and Amul as it pivots to an ambitious next-generation strategy.

What Actually Matters.

ONDC is raising ₹430 crore to enhance India's open digital commerce ecosystem.

Investment comes from major firms like Zoho, Uber, Paytm, and public banks.

India's Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) is set to raise ₹430 crore in a funding round that brings together a mix of technology firms, financial institutions, and public sector giants, a move that signals growing conviction in the country's open digital commerce experiment.

According to regulatory filings accessed from the Registrar of Companies, ONDC has already received ₹220 crore in the first tranche of this raise. The funds were raised through the allotment of 2.2 crore equity shares at a face value of ₹100 each, issued on a private placement basis following a board resolution passed on 12 May 2026.

Zoho emerged as the single largest contributor, putting in ₹70 crore, while ride-hailing giant Uber and fintech platform Paytm each committed ₹60 crore. BSE Technologies, the technology arm of the Bombay Stock Exchange, made up the remainder with ₹30 crore.

The remaining ₹210 crore is expected to arrive in one or more subsequent tranches from a combination of existing shareholders and new strategic partners. The National Stock Exchange, the Quality Council of India, Punjab National Bank, dairy cooperative Amul, and the National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India are each expected to contribute ₹30 crore, while the State Bank of India will put in ₹60 crore.

The fundraise marks a pivotal moment for ONDC, which was established under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) as a challenger to the closed ecosystems operated by global e-commerce behemoths. The fresh capital will underpin ONDC's transition to its so-called 2.0 strategy, with a focus on AI-driven and agentic commerce, digital public infrastructure projects such as DigiCatalog, quality assurance programmes, and sector-wise expansion.

ONDC's chief financial officer Krishan Agarwal said the investments represent an affirmation that open digital networks are fundamentally reshaping how commerce is conducted in India, creating a level playing field for businesses of all sizes.

The participation of Zoho builds on a deepening relationship between the Chennai-based SaaS company and the network. Zoho has integrated a number of its products — including Vikra, Zoho ERP, Zoho Books, Zoho Inventory, and Zoho Commerce — with the platform to help micro, small, and medium enterprises digitise operations and access customers via ONDC-enabled channels.

For Uber, the investment follows meaningful traction on the network. The company's metro ticketing service is live across five cities, and more than 10 million metro rides have so far been booked through the Uber app via ONDC. Paytm, one of the earliest advocates for the platform, has also scaled its ONDC-linked services considerably.

The fintech firm says it now facilitates more than 300,000 tickets daily across metro and bus services in 21 cities.

Prabhjeet Singh, President of Uber India and South Asia, said that India has been at the forefront of building digital public infrastructure that is inclusive, interoperable, and transformative at scale, adding that the investment places the company at the heart of that innovation journey.

ONDC is currently operational across 616 cities and has onboarded more than 7.64 lakh sellers and service providers. The network processed 218 million transactions across its various categories during the 2025–26 financial year. With banking heavyweights, cooperative institutions, and technology leaders now rallying behind it, the platform appears well-positioned to graduate from a proof-of-concept into a foundational layer of India's digital economy.

Zyoin Group has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM) to support the growth of global capability centres (GCCs) in Karnataka.

The partnership aims to help companies set up, expand and scale GCC operations in the state by combining talent advisory with ecosystem support. Under the agreement, Zyoin Group will provide GCC advisory, talent intelligence and employer branding support, while KDEM will facilitate industry engagement and strategic initiatives to attract global companies.

Sanjeev Kumar Gupta, chief executive officer of KDEM, said the partnership would strengthen Karnataka’s GCC ecosystem, including emerging technology clusters such as Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad-Belagavi and Kalaburgi.

The two organisations said they will support firms across different stages of the GCC lifecycle, including market entry, operational setup and expansion.

The collaboration comes as Karnataka continues to attract multinational companies looking to establish or expand GCCs in India. The state remains one of the country’s major GCC hubs due to its technology ecosystem, talent availability and policy support, according to the release.

The partnership will also focus on knowledge sharing and workforce planning to address changing business needs. Both organisations said the collaboration would support operational readiness for global companies and contribute to the next phase of GCC growth in Karnataka.

The initiative will also examine startup and innovation collaborations, as well as employment opportunities.

“Karnataka continues to lead India’s GCC transformation journey, and this collaboration with KDEM is an important step toward strengthening the state’s position as a global digital and enterprise hub,” said Anuj Agrawal, Founder and CEO of Zyoin Group and Workplace Awards.

He added that the partnership would support organisations through different stages of the GCC lifecycle, “from entry and scale-up to long-term capability building”.

title: Google’s New Feature Verifies Calls to Stop AI Impersonation Scams
content:
The technology is being rolled out globally through the Phone by Google app on Android 12 and newer devices, beginning with Pixel smartphones.

What Actually Matters.

Google has launched a feature to detect fake calls that utilise spoofed numbers and AI-generated voices.

The system focuses on verifying the device making the call rather than just the caller's voice.

Google has introduced a new fake call detection feature for Android devices that identifies callers who use spoofed phone numbers and AI-generated voices to impersonate trusted contacts.

According to Google, scammers are increasingly combining phone number spoofing with AI voice-cloning technology, making fraudulent calls appear legitimate. In many cases, victims see a familiar contact name and number on their screen while hearing a voice that sounds identical to someone they know.

To counter this threat, the company developed a verification system that focuses on confirming the device making the call rather than relying solely on the caller’s voice.

“Even if scammers manage to copy someone’s voice, they may not be able to fake the phone behind it,” the company said while announcing the feature.

The system operates via what the company calls a digital handshake between Android devices. When a trusted contact calls using the Phone by Google app, their device silently sends a verification signal confirming that the call is genuinely originating from that phone.

If a scammer spoofs the number but cannot provide the verification signal, the recipient’s device checks with the actual phone associated with that contact. If the genuine device confirms that no call is being made, Android displays a warning indicating that the caller may be impersonating someone known to the user.

The company has also built the feature using Rich Communication Services (RCS), allowing other applications and companies to potentially adopt similar protections in the future.

The company is betting that verifying the source of a call may become one of the most effective ways to protect users from the next generation of AI-driven scams.

title: Microsoft Launches 7 AI Models Across Coding, Voice and Reasoning
content:
Microsoft also introduced Frontier Tuning, a reinforcement learning system that lets organisations customise AI models using their own workflows and data.

What Actually Matters.

Microsoft introduced seven new AI models aimed at reducing reliance on OpenAI and Anthropic.

The models cover various functions including reasoning, coding, image generation, transcription, and voice.

At Microsoft Build 2026, Microsoft announced seven new in-house AI models spanning reasoning, coding, image generation, transcription and voice as it looks to reduce dependency on OpenAI and Anthropic.

The new model family includes MAI-Thinking-1, a reasoning model; MAI-Code-1-Flash for coding tasks; MAI-Image-2.5 and its Flash variant for image generation and editing; MAI Transcribe-1.5 for speech-to-text; and MAI-Voice-2 for speech generation.

Microsoft said MAI-Image-2.5 supports text-to-image generation and image editing, surpassing the Arena score of Nano Banana Pro. The company added that MAI-Voice-2 provides speech generation across 15 languages, while MAI-Voice-2-Flash, due to launch later, will offer similar capabilities at a lower cost.

The company added that the models will be available through Azure Foundry and developer platforms, including Hugging Face and GitHub.

Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI, said Microsoft expects a further thousand-fold increase in AI training compute over the next three years, leading to more advanced capabilities and broader adoption of AI technologies.

“Our ultimate goal is what we call Humanist Superintelligence,” Suleyman said. “That means advanced AI systems designed to serve people and organisations, not replace them.”

Microsoft said MAI-Thinking-1 was trained without distillation from third-party models and matches leading systems on software engineering benchmarks. The company also said MAI-Code-1-Flash, a 5-billion-parameter model, is designed for integration with GitHub Copilot, Visual Studio Code and Microsoft’s software ecosystem.

Alongside the model launches, Microsoft introduced Frontier Tuning, a reinforcement learning approach that allows organisations to adapt models using their own workflows and operational data.

The company said a tuned MAI model for Excel matched the performance of GPT 5.4 while being up to 10 times more efficient. It also said a customised MAI model achieved the highest win rate in tests conducted to meet consulting firm McKinsey’s enterprise standards at roughly one-tenth the cost of competing models.

Microsoft also announced a collaboration with the Mayo Clinic to develop a healthcare-focused AI model. The model will combine Mayo Clinic’s clinical expertise and de-identified clinical data with Microsoft's AI technology. According to the company, the system will initially be deployed within Mayo Clinic's environment before becoming available to other organisations through Azure Foundry after validation.

The company said the healthcare model will be owned by Mayo Clinic and is intended to support clinical reasoning, diagnosis and treatment planning while maintaining patient trust and responsible data stewardship.

Microsoft said all MAI models were developed using internally built infrastructure, licensed datasets and the company's Maia 200 AI chip. The company reported a 1.4-times efficiency improvement from its hardware and software co-design efforts.

The new group includes organisations from sectors such as power, water, healthcare, communications and hardware.

What Actually Matters.

Anthropic's Project Glasswing now includes around 150 organisations across more than 15 countries.

The initiative aims to enhance cybersecurity for critical software in various sectors, including healthcare and communications.

Anthropic on June 2 announced that it is expanding Project Glasswing, its cybersecurity initiative to secure critical software, to approximately 150 additional organisations across more than 15 countries.

The expansion follows the company’s initial rollout in April, when about 50 partners were granted access to Claude Mythos Preview, an AI model trained to identify software vulnerabilities. Anthropic recently said those partners had discovered more than 10,000 high- and critical-severity security flaws using the system.

The new group includes organisations from sectors such as power, water, healthcare, communications and hardware, areas that were less represented in the initial cohort. Many of the new participants are software vendors and nonprofit maintainers whose codebases are used by governments and organisations worldwide.

“What each partner has in common is that a successful attack on their codebase could be catastrophic,” Anthropic said. The company added that for most partners, “a major attack could affect more than 100 million people, with important ramifications for both global and national security.”

Anthropic said the expansion is part of its broader effort to improve software security through AI while helping the cybersecurity industry adapt to increasingly capable AI systems.

The company warned that “cheap, fast AI models with powerful cyber capabilities are around the corner” and reiterated its expectation that many AI developers could have models with capabilities comparable to Claude Mythos Preview within six to 12 months.

“Mythos Preview continues a long-term trend that we’ve been warning about for some time,” Anthropic said, adding that some future models could be released without safeguards that prevent misuse, potentially increasing the frequency and unpredictability of cyberattacks.

As part of its efforts to support defenders, Anthropic said it recently launched Claude Security, a product that uses its public frontier models, including Claude Opus 4.8, to scan codebases and suggest patches. The company is also making available, upon request, to trusted security teams, tools developed for Project Glasswing participants to help identify vulnerabilities more quickly.

Anthropic said the cybersecurity challenge is shifting from vulnerability discovery to the processes of verification, disclosure and patching. Many Project Glasswing partners are already using Mythos Preview to generate software patches and conduct pre-release security checks, according to the company.

The model can also be applied to penetration testing, threat detection and response, and modernising legacy software by rebuilding codebases in memory-safe programming languages, Anthropic said.

The company said it is discussing ways to scale vulnerability review and patching efforts in open-source software and is working on improving vulnerability disclosure practices for open-source maintainers.

Looking ahead, Anthropic said it plans to further expand Project Glasswing, focusing on critical infrastructure providers, maintainers of essential open-source software and safety testers. It also intends to broaden its Cyber Verification Program, which would provide Mythos-class capabilities to more organisations for specific cyber defence tasks.

“We're working as quickly as we can to safely release Mythos-level capabilities in general access,” Anthropic said, while acknowledging that safeguards capable of preventing misuse of advanced cyber models remain an unresolved challenge across the AI industry.

title: After Mahabharat, JioStar Plans More AI-Led Productions, To Hire Around 80 AI Specialists
content:
Among the projects currently in development are Makaraj, a new television series, Hanuman, a feature film based on the Ramayana and several short-form micro-dramas.

What Actually Matters.

JioStar is expanding AI use in content creation following the success of its AI-generated series Mahabharat: Ek Dharmayudh.

The company plans to produce new shows and films entirely created by AI to reduce production costs.

JioStar, the streaming joint venture between Reliance Industries and Disney is planning to expand its use of AI in content creation after the strong performance of its AI-generated series Mahabharat: Ek Dharmayudh.

According to a Bloomberg report, the company is developing a slate of new shows and films that will be written, animated, voiced and edited entirely using AI. The move is aimed at reducing production costs while meeting growing demand for digital entertainment.

The decision follows the success of Mahabharat: Ek Dharmayudh, a 100-episode AI-generated adaptation of the ancient Indian epic. The series reportedly attracted 6.5 million views on its first day of release in October, more than double the average viewership on JioHotstar.

The company plans to produce more AI-generated content and hire around 80 AI specialists and engineers to support the initiative.

The company recently appointed veteran American screenwriter and producer Stephan Bugaj to lead its generative AI content strategy. His team is currently recruiting talent to expand the company’s AI-focused entertainment efforts.

JioStar’s push comes at a time when media companies in India and China are increasingly experimenting with AI-generated content to serve audiences that consume large amounts of short-form video on smartphones.

title: IBM Pledges $10 Billion for Quantum Push Over Five Years
content:
The funding will support R&D, manufacturing, partnerships and fault-tolerant quantum systems by 2029.

What Actually Matters.

IBM will invest over $10 billion in quantum computing over the next five years.

The funding aims to enhance research, manufacturing, and partnerships for quantum technology.

IBM has announced that it will invest more than $10 billion in quantum computing over the next five years to expand research, manufacturing and partnerships. This comes as it works towards building the world’s first large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer by 2029.

The company said the funding will cover research and development, capital expenditure, manufacturing scale-up, mergers and acquisitions, and ecosystem expansion. The move aims to strengthen its quantum computing roadmap and support US leadership in the sector.

“The quantum era is no longer ahead of us; it has started,” said Arvind Krishna, Chairman and CEO of IBM. “Our clients, partners and users around the world are tapping into IBM quantum computers to do work that was impossible a few years ago.”

The company said the investment builds on its current quantum infrastructure, which includes more than 90 quantum systems deployed globally through cloud and on-site installations.

IBM operates quantum centres in locations such as New York and Germany, while partner deployments span institutions in Japan, South Korea, Spain and Canada. The company also plans to add systems in Chicago and at the Quantum Valley in Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh, India.

IBM said it remains on track to launch IBM Quantum Starling in 2029. The company claims the system will execute 20,000 times as many operations as current quantum computers. Starling will also serve as the foundation for IBM Quantum Blue Jay, a system designed to run one billion quantum operations across 2,000 qubits.

“The pace of discovery with quantum computers is accelerating rapidly, and this investment powers our ability to deliver the next generation of quantum hardware, software, and manufacturing,” Krishna said.

IBM added that its quantum network now includes more than 340 organisations across sectors such as healthcare, financial services, academia and government. Since 2017, the company said it has signed more than $1.1 billion in quantum-related client contracts.

The company also highlighted plans for Anderon, which it described as the world’s first pure-play quantum wafer foundry. It will contribute $1 billion in cash, intellectual property and assets to the project with support from the US Department of Commerce.

IBM said it expects partners using its quantum systems to demonstrate quantum advantage in 2026. The company pointed to recent projects involving protein modelling, magnetic material simulations and molecular research as signs of progress.

IBM also said its open-source quantum software platform, Qiskit, is now used by nearly 70% of quantum developers and has executed more than four trillion quantum circuits.
