title: Microsoft Launches Scout, an Autonomous AI Agent Built on OpenClaw for Microsoft 365
content:
Microsoft Scout is integrated with Microsoft 365 services, including Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, and SharePoint.

What Actually Matters.

Microsoft has launched Scout, an autonomous AI agent designed to operate within Microsoft 365 applications.

Scout functions as an always-on agent, acting independently based on user priorities and organisational policies.

Microsoft on June 2 introduced Microsoft Scout, an always-on AI agent that can act autonomously on behalf of users across Microsoft 365 applications, marking the company’s entry into a new category of agents it calls Autopilots.

Omar Shahine, Corporate Vice President of Microsoft Scout, said Autopilots are “always-on agents that work autonomously, with their own identity, and act on your behalf.”

Unlike traditional AI assistants that respond to prompts, Scout remains active in the background and can take actions across workplace applications based on user priorities and organisational policies.

The company said an early version of Scout has already been used internally by Microsoft employees. It is now being extended to a select group of customers through a private preview program and made available experimentally through Microsoft's Frontier initiative.

Access to Scout requires Frontier enrollment, Intune policy configuration, and an opt-in attestation. Users with a GitHub Copilot license can then download and install the experience, Microsoft said.

Microsoft Scout is integrated with Microsoft 365 services, including Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, and SharePoint. It can access workplace data such as chats, emails, calendars, and contacts, while users interact with the agent primarily through Teams. The company said Scout can also connect to browsers, local resources, and model context protocol servers through its desktop application.

According to Microsoft, Scout is built to reduce routine coordination work by scheduling meetings across time zones, identifying important upcoming meetings, preparing briefing materials, and blocking calendar time for approaching deadlines. The agent can also flag risks such as stalled decisions and monitor ongoing work without requiring repeated prompts.

“Microsoft Scout reduces the coordination work that builds throughout the day,” Shahine said. “It can proactively schedule and coordinate meeting times across time zones, flag important meetings, and generate the materials you need to prepare while keeping you in the loop.”

The system is powered by Work IQ, a framework that Microsoft said helps the agent learn how users work, what they prioritise, and which tasks require attention. “Work IQ carries work forward, becoming more useful, relevant, and aligned to your priorities,” Shahine said.

Microsoft said Scout is built on OpenClaw, an open-source technology project, and that the company is contributing policy conformance capabilities back to the project.

Organisations using OpenClaw will be able to verify whether their environments meet security and compliance requirements and obtain audit-ready validation, Microsoft said.

To address enterprise governance requirements, Microsoft said each Scout agent operates under its own governed Microsoft Entra identity rather than a shared service account. The company added that credentials are scoped to specific tasks, protected from logs and diagnostics, and managed under the same controls used for Microsoft services.

Microsoft also said Scout operates within existing organisational controls, including access permissions, approval workflows for sensitive actions, and data protection policies enforced through Microsoft Purview.

title: TCS Expands Euroclear Partnership to Modernise Sweden's Securities Depository Infrastructure
content:
The IT major will deploy its BaNCS and Quartz platforms at Euroclear Sweden as part of the depository operator's Nordic transformation programme.

What Actually Matters.

TCS is enhancing its partnership with Euroclear to modernise Sweden's central securities depository infrastructure.

The implementation will utilise TCS BaNCS and Quartz platforms to create a scalable and cloud-ready system.

TCS has expanded its partnership with Euroclear Group to support the modernisation of Sweden's central securities depository (CSD).

Under the agreement, Euroclear Sweden will deploy TCS BaNCS for Market Infrastructure and Quartz, the Indian IT services company's digital solutions suite, to build a cloud ready and scalable CSD platform aligned with evolving European market standards, the company said in a statement on June 3.

The move marks the next phase of a relationship between the two companies that has already seen TCS support Euroclear's depository operations in Finland. The Swedish implementation forms part of Euroclear's broader "One Nordic" strategy aimed at creating a unified technology and operating platform across Sweden and Finland.

TCS said its BaNCS platform will support core registry functions, depository services, cross border settlement and asset servicing across asset classes. The Quartz platform will add capabilities around distributed ledger technology and AI, enabling support for tokenised assets, decentralised settlement models and real time operational insights.

As part of the transformation, Euroclear plans to migrate the Swedish market to the European Central Bank's TARGET2 Securities (T2S) platform, a pan European settlement infrastructure designed to improve efficiency and standardisation across securities markets.

The transition will be carried out through a phased IT migration programme.

"Having established one of Europe’s most advanced CSD infrastructures in Finland, we are pleased to extend our decade-long partnership with TCS to Sweden,” Hanna Vainio, CEO, Euroclear Sweden and Finland said in a statement. “This collaboration is a pillar of our 'One Nordic' vision, allowing us to harmonise business and IT practices onto a single, resilient platform.”

The announcement adds to TCS' growing portfolio of large-scale financial market infrastructure projects globally, an area where the company has been positioning its BaNCS suite as a platform for exchanges, central securities depositories and other market infrastructure institutions.

“Building on our joint success in Finland, we look forward to working with Euroclear to bring high levels of sophistication in functionality, standards compliance and technology to the Nordics market leveraging TCS BaNCS and Quartz, our market-leading products for financial market infrastructures,” said R Vivekanand, President, BFSI Products & Platforms at TCS.

title: Snowflake, Anthropic Expand Cortex AI to Push Agentic AI into Enterprise Core
content:
The expanded partnership will support a range of enterprise use cases using Claude tools within Snowflake’s ecosystem.

What Actually Matters.

Snowflake and Anthropic are expanding their partnership to help enterprises deploy AI applications securely.

The collaboration aims to meet the demand for production-ready AI systems in regulated data environments.

Snowflake and Anthropic have announced an expansion of their partnership to help enterprises deploy AI applications more securely and efficiently using governed business data.

The announcement was made at Snowflake Summit 2026 in San Francisco where the companies highlighted growing demand among enterprises for production-ready AI systems that operate within secure and regulated data environments.

Under the partnership, Anthropic’s Claude models will continue to power Snowflake Cortex AI, allowing organisations to build AI agents, automate workflows and analyse business data without moving sensitive information outside the Snowflake platform.

“The rapid adoption of models like Claude through Snowflake Cortex AI reflects a broader shift in what enterprises expect from AI,” Christian Kleinerman, Executive Vice President of Product at Snowflake, said.

He added that customers want AI that works directly on their governed data, not in isolated systems. Together with Anthropic, we’re helping organisations move from experimentation to production faster and laying the foundation for the agentic enterprise.

“Snowflake customers are increasingly using Claude to power cybersecurity investigations, accelerate financial analysis, build production data apps and many other workflows,” Steve Corfield, Head of Global Business Development and Partnerships at Anthropic, said.

“Snowflake brings the governed data environment enterprises already rely on, and Claude brings the reasoning to put that data to work,” he noted.

Several companies, including Block, Carvana, Indeed, Notion, and eSentire, are already using the combined capabilities of Snowflake and Anthropic in their business operations.

The companies also announced deeper collaboration across products such as Snowflake Cortex Code, an AI-powered coding assistant and Snowflake Intelligence, an enterprise AI agent designed to help employees query and analyse business data using natural language.

The partnership reflects a broader trend of enterprises moving beyond AI experimentation and adopting governed AI systems that combine advanced reasoning capabilities with security, compliance and enterprise-grade controls.

title: Cars24 Launches Dedicated AI Labs With $20 Million to Back Tech Founders
content:
Pre-owned car platform Cars24 has launched "AI Labs" with a $20 million investment. Partnering with OpenAI, AWS, and ElevenLabs, the initiative will build in-house AI-native products and fund early-stage startups building transformative technologies.

What Actually Matters.

Cars24 launched AI Labs with a £16 million investment to develop AI-first products and support early-stage startups.

The initiative aims to build in-house AI capabilities, collaborate with leading AI companies, and fund transformative AI technologies.

Cars24 has announced the launch of a dedicated AI Labs, a multi-pronged initiative focused on building AI-first products and supporting ambitious founders.

As part of this commitment, the platform plans to invest $20 million into the technology. According to a Press Trust of India (PTI) report, this significant investment will be directly funnelled into "startups and teams building transformative AI technologies".

The company outlined that AI Labs will operate across three key pillars: creating AI-native products and contributing to open-source innovation, working closely with leading AI companies to accelerate adoption and experimentation, and providing capital and support to startups building category-defining AI businesses.

Over the last few years, AI has transitioned from a backend experiment to a central pillar for the firm. Cars24 noted that AI has become "deeply embedded across the company's operations, helping teams move faster, make better decisions and create better customer experiences."

An Inc42 report highlighted that the IPO-bound, Gurugram-based used-car marketplace describes the initiative, branded as Cars24 Labs, as its "build, partner, and investment arm." Inc42 further reports that the programme "is intended to reduce external reliance by bringing more AI work in-house" while actively incubating early-stage tech entrepreneurs.

The initiative is designed to act as a holistic launchpad, helping founders turn breakthrough ideas into real-world companies. Instead of offering capital alone, the lab will provide mentorship, cloud infrastructure, distribution opportunities, and access to frontier AI tools.

To achieve this, Cars24 has established strategic collaborations with major global tech players. "The initiative brings together partners including OpenAI, AWS, and ElevenLabs, creating an ecosystem where builders can access world-class technology, expertise, and support as they bring new products to market," the company stated.

Commenting on the launch, Vikram Chopra, Founder and CEO of Cars24, emphasised the monumental scale of the current technological landscape.

"Every major technology shift creates a handful of companies that go on to define the future. We believe AI is the biggest shift of our generation, and the opportunity ahead is far larger than anything we've seen before," said Chopra.

"We want to back founders early, help them move faster, and support the people building things that seem impossible today but inevitable tomorrow," he added.

According to The Economic Times, the initiative comes at a strategic time for the SoftBank-backed marketplace. The firm is currently preparing for a public listing, recently reporting a 27 per cent on-year growth in adjusted net revenue for FY26, whilst successfully narrowing its EBITDA losses by 36%.

title: Infosys Expands DNB Bank Partnership to Overhaul Financial Crime Systems
content:
The Indian IT giant will help DNB Bank consolidate anti-money laundering and fraud monitoring systems onto a cloud-based platform.

What Actually Matters.

Infosys is modernising DNB Bank's financial crime operations by consolidating systems onto a cloud-based platform.

The partnership aims to replace legacy infrastructure with a unified system for monitoring and investigations.

Infosys has expanded its engagement with Norway's DNB Bank ASA to modernise the lender's financial crime operations, as banks increasingly invest in technology platforms to strengthen anti-money laundering and fraud detection capabilities.

Under the expanded partnership, the tech giant will help DNB consolidate its financial crime management functions onto NICE Actimize's X-Sight Enterprise platform, replacing fragmented legacy infrastructure with a unified system for monitoring, screening and investigations.

DNB, Norway's largest bank, will consolidate functions including customer and payment screening, customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, and fraud detection onto a single software-as-a-service platform with a unified case management system.

Infosys, which will serve as the systems integration partner, will be responsible for enterprise architecture design, platform integration and data migration as part of the transformation programme.

The Bengaluru-headquartered IT services company said the platform will combine anti-money laundering and fraud monitoring capabilities. It would provide the bank with a consolidated view of customer risk and help detect increasingly sophisticated financial crime patterns through artificial intelligence and automation.

“Legacy systems are struggling to keep pace with the rapid evolution of financial crime. By consolidating anti-money laundering and fraud capabilities onto an AI-enabled enterprise cloud platform, we’re helping DNB Bank ASA move from fragmented controls to a unified, intelligence-led operating model,” Dennis Gada, Executive Vice President and Global Head of Banking & Financial Services, Infosys said in a statement.

The move comes as financial institutions globally face growing regulatory scrutiny and rising compliance costs, prompting investments in cloud-based and AI-enabled systems to improve detection accuracy and reduce manual investigation efforts.

“Protecting customers and the integrity of the financial system requires us to continuously raise the bar on detection and investigation,” said Elin Sandnes, COO and Group Executive Vice President Technology & Services, DNB.

The deal adds to Infosys' portfolio of large-scale banking transformation engagements, an area where major IT services companies are increasingly positioning AI-led modernisation projects as a growth driver amid a gradual recovery in discretionary technology spending by financial institutions.

Maharashtra has moved a step closer to securing one of India's largest digital infrastructure investments, with Australian data centre operator AirTrunk receiving a letter of intent (LoI) for land allotment at the Raigad Pen Growth Centre for its proposed data centre project.

The announcement was made by Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis following a meeting with AirTrunk Founder and CEO Robin Khuda. The proposed project involves an investment of approximately ₹2 lakh crore and is expected to create a data centre ecosystem with a planned capacity of 3 gigawatts (GW).

According to the CM, the project will be developed at the Raigad Pen Growth Centre, also referred to as Orange City, and is expected to play a significant role in strengthening Maharashtra's digital infrastructure and data economy.

AirTrunk, one of the world’s largest hyperscale data centre operators, is backed by global investment firm Blackstone. The company has been expanding its footprint across the Asia-Pacific region to support growing demand for cloud computing, AI, and digital services.

The proposed Maharashtra facility is expected to support the increasing need for large-scale computing infrastructure driven by AI workloads, cloud adoption, and data localisation requirements.

The meeting was also attended by Paul Murphy, Australia's Consul-General, highlighting the growing technology and investment partnership between India and Australia.

If implemented as planned, the project would rank among the largest data centre investments announced in India and further strengthen Maharashtra's position as a key destination for digital infrastructure and technology investments.

Meanwhile, Maharashtra is going all in to emerge as the leading destination for data centre investments, with the state government fast-tracking approvals and execution of projects announced during the World Economic Forum Annual Meeting in Davos.

Speaking last week, Fadnavis said the state is actively working to translate investment commitments into operational infrastructure.

content:

What Actually Matters.

Coforge has launched the Nexa platform to enhance automation in the global insurance sector.

Nexa aids insurers in streamlining underwriting, claims processing, and product development using existing systems.

Indian IT firm Coforge has announced the launch of its agentic AI platform, Nexa, aimed at the global insurance industry.

The platform is designed to help insurance carriers automate functions across underwriting, claims processing, product development and platform modernisation while continuing to use their existing core insurance systems.

In a press statement, the company said the platform sits atop insurers’ existing technology infrastructure and uses AI orchestration capabilities to streamline workflows without requiring the replacement of incumbent systems.

The platform is built on Coforge’s One AI framework and includes a marketplace of more than 30 AI assets tailored for insurance operations. The offerings also include an AI-powered submission centre for underwriting, an automated state-rollout factory for regulatory filings, product-rollout automation tools, AI-driven global expansion capabilities, legacy platform modernisation tools, and an agentic claims-triage system.

According to Coforge, these modules can help insurers accelerate product launches, improve underwriting productivity, automate claims routing and reduce modernisation costs.

“Purpose-built for the global insurance market across Property & Casualty, Life & Annuities, and Speciality, as well as MGAs and intermediaries, Nexa addresses critical industry challenges through a suite of integrated, production-grade capabilities,” Rajeev Batra, Executive Vice President (EVP) and Global Practice Head of Insurance, Coforge, said.

Coforge said the platform has been built with human oversight and auditability features and can be deployed either as individual modules or as a broader "insurance in a box" model.

The company plans to position Nexa as a key component of its insurance-focused growth strategy, betting that insurers will increasingly adopt AI-driven operational platforms to improve efficiency and speed up decision making while preserving existing technology investments.

The launch comes at a time when insurers globally are exploring agentic AI systems capable of executing multiple tasks with limited human intervention, moving beyond traditional automation and chatbot-based deployments.

title: DPIIT, BHASHINI Join Hands to Enable Multilingual Access Across India's Investment Ecosystem
content:
The partnership aims to integrate multilingual capabilities across DPIIT platforms.

What Actually Matters.

DPIIT and BHASHINI have partnered to enhance multilingual access across India's investment ecosystem.

The collaboration aims to integrate multilingual capabilities into DPIIT's digital platforms.

The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and the Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen multilingual digital access across India's investment and industrial ecosystem.

The collaboration, signed under the "BHASHINI Seva/Sanchalan – A BHASHINI Sahayogi Program," seeks to integrate multilingual capabilities into DPIIT's digital platforms using the BHASHINI platform, India's national language digital public infrastructure.

Under the agreement, entrepreneurs, startups, investors, businesses, and citizens will be able to access government information, services, and policy resources in any of the 22 languages recognised under the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, helping reduce language barriers in India's rapidly expanding innovation and investment landscape.

The initiative will focus on enabling multilingual governance and service delivery through a range of BHASHINI-powered solutions, including Udyat, Mitra, AppMitra, and Pravakta. The partnership will also support the integration of translation APIs, development of domain-specific language models, creation of multilingual glossaries, deployment of voice-enabled technologies, and expansion of linguistic datasets.

According to the government, the collaboration is aimed at making India's investment ecosystem more inclusive by ensuring that access to startup services, industrial schemes, policy communication, and citizen engagement is not limited by language.

The two organisations will also work on strengthening multilingual AI models tailored to sectors such as investment promotion, industrial development, entrepreneurship, and innovation. The focus will be on building voice-first and AI-enabled experiences that can serve users across India's diverse linguistic landscape.

Officials noted that multilingual technologies are becoming increasingly important in expanding participation across India's startup, manufacturing, and innovation ecosystems. The initiative is expected to improve access to economic opportunities for users who may not be comfortable engaging with digital services in English or a limited set of languages.

Beyond technology deployment, the partnership will encourage language data contributions, awareness programmes, capacity-building initiatives, and broader adoption of multilingual AI tools among institutions and stakeholders connected to DPIIT.

title: Zoom Launches AI Assistant ZoomMate to Turn Meetings Into Actions
content:
ZoomMate can search enterprise data, automate workflows, generate presentations and reports and perform actions across platforms such as Salesforce, Jira, Slack, ServiceNow, Google Workspace and Microsoft tools.

What Actually Matters.

Zoom has launched ZoomMate, an AI-powered workplace assistant.

ZoomMate aims to convert meeting discussions into actionable tasks.

Zoom Communications has launched ZoomMate, a new AI-powered workplace assistant designed to help employees turn conversations into completed tasks without switching between multiple applications.

According to Zoom, the AI assistant can search enterprise data, automate workflows, generate presentations and reports and perform actions across platforms such as Salesforce, Jira, Slack, ServiceNow, Google Workspace and Microsoft tools.

“Before, during and after the meeting, ZoomMate connects what was decided to what needs to happen next across every system where your work lives,” Russell Dicker, Chief Product Officer at Zoom, said.

The platform introduces what Zoom calls agentic AI capabilities, allowing the assistant not only to provide information but also to execute tasks.

For example, ZoomMate can schedule meetings, update CRM records, create follow-up tasks, draft customer emails, trigger onboarding workflows and generate project plans directly from meeting discussions.

One of its key features is Agentic Search, which allows employees to search across Zoom and connected enterprise systems. Instead of only finding documents, ZoomMate can surface customer records, support tickets, project updates, meeting discussions and knowledge-base content while respecting organisational access controls.

“The market is moving away from isolated AI helpers and toward tools that can better connect decisions, data, and workflows across an organization,” said Melody Brue, Vice President and Principal Analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, said in the press release.

Zoom said the tool can also automatically generate presentations, spreadsheets, reports and other business deliverables from meeting conversations, reducing manual work for employees.

The launch is part of Zoom’s broader vision of creating a “system of action”, where workplace conversations become the starting point for execution rather than ending as meeting notes.

ZoomMate is currently available to customers in North America starting at $20 per user per month, with expansion to additional regions, including Asia-Pacific expected later this year.

title: Cricketer KL Rahul Partners With str8bat to Launch AI-Powered Batting Platform
content:
The partnership brings KL Rahul’s batting philosophy to str8bat’s AI platform allowing players to learn from professional-level insights tailored to their game.

What Actually Matters.

Cricketer KL Rahul collaborated with str8bat to introduce an AI-powered batting platform.

The 'KLR1 x str8bat' kit combines Rahul's batting philosophy with str8bat's GenAI learning platform.

Indian cricketer KL Rahul partnered with Bengaluru-based sports technology startup str8bat to launch an AI-powered batting platform. str8bat combines performance analytics with personalised coaching insights, enabling players to access professional-level feedback through data-driven training.

The partnership introduces the ‘KLR1 x str8bat’ kit which integrates KL Rahul’s batting philosophy, preparation methods and decision-making approach into str8bat’s GenAI-powered learning platform.

The company said the initiative aims to help cricketers better understand their batting performance through objective data rather than relying solely on instinct and traditional coaching methods.

At the centre of the platform is Power Score, str8bat’s proprietary batting metric that combines bat speed, impact speed, sweet-spot percentage and timing index into a single score to measure batting performance consistently across sessions.

Founded in 2017, str8bat has built a sensor-based batting intelligence platform that attaches directly to a cricket bat and captures metrics such as bat speed, swing path, impact zones, timing efficiency and shot execution. Unlike many sports analytics systems, the platform does not require cameras, wearables or specialised infrastructure.

According to Gagan Daga, Co-founder and CEO of str8bat, the company’s goal is to democratise access to performance intelligence for cricketers across skill levels.

“At str8bat, our focus is simple - every cricketer should have clear, objective insight into their game. Through our GenAI platform, players will be able to see their own data and learn from KL Rahul’s approach to cricket,” Daga added.

Rahul said that the platform provides greater clarity into the technical aspects of batting that are often difficult to measure.

“str8bat’s insights helped me understand where I needed more work. It changes the quality of practice because it starts training with intent,” he noted.

The company currently works with organisations including Cricket Australia and IPL franchise Rajasthan Royals and claims to have more than 25,000 users across professional academies, high-performance centres and grassroots cricket programmes.

The announcement comes as sports organisations increasingly adopt AI and performance analytics to enhance athlete development.

With the new partnership, str8bat aims to combine personalised coaching, sensor-driven insights and generative AI to make elite-level batting intelligence accessible to cricketers worldwide.

Wipro will acquire an additional 20% stake in Aggne Global Inc., taking its holding to 80%, as it deepens its push into AI-led transformation services for the insurance sector.

Wipro will increase its stake in Aggne Global Inc. to 80% through a $28.5 million buyout.

The acquisition aims to enhance Wipro's capabilities in AI-led transformation services for the insurance sector.

IT services firm Wipro said its step-down subsidiary Wipro IT Services LLC will acquire an additional 20% stake in Aggne Global Inc. for $28.5 million, increasing its ownership in the insurtech company to 80%.

The transaction is expected to close by June 5, subject to customary closing adjustments, the Bengaluru-based IT services company said in a regulatory filing.

The latest acquisition follows Wipro's February 2024 purchase of a 60% stake in Aggne Global Inc. and its affiliate, Aggne Global IT Services Pvt. Ltd.

With the additional investment, Wipro said it will further consolidate its position in the insurance technology segment, particularly in property and casualty (P&C) insurance.

Wipro said the increased stake would strengthen its capabilities in delivering artificial intelligence and intellectual property-led transformation services for insurers, adding that the acquisition would bolster its competitive position in the insurance sector, where enterprises are increasingly investing in automation, AI-driven claims processing, underwriting and customer experience platforms.

Aggne Group provides a range of AI and Intellectual Property-driven services designed to help insurers transform operations, drive new efficiencies, and deliver optimal customer experiences.

Aggne has reported steady growth over the past three years, with revenue rising from $18.9 million in FY24 to $24.2 million in FY25 and $27.5 million in FY26.

Wipro’s shares opened trading at ₹208 apiece on the NSE on June 2, up 0.7% from the last closing price of ₹206.4 per share.

title: Anthropic Files for IPO, Eyes Public Market Debut
content:
Backed by Amazon and Google, the AI startup is valued at $965 billion and has emerged as one of OpenAI’s biggest rivals.

What Actually Matters.

Anthropic has confidentially filed for an IPO, marking a significant step towards going public.

The company is valued at approximately $965 billion, becoming one of the most valuable AI firms globally.

AI startup Anthropic has confidentially submitted a draft registration statement on Form S-1 to the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), marking the company’s first formal step toward a potential initial public offering (IPO).

The filing gives the Claude-maker the option to go public once the SEC completes its review process, although the company said the offering remains subject to market conditions and other factors.

“Today, Anthropic, PBC confidentially submitted a draft registration statement on Form S-1 to the US Securities and Exchange Commission for a proposed initial public offering of our common stock,” the company said in a statement on June 1. “This gives us the option to go public after the SEC completes its review.”

Anthropic added that the proposed IPO “will depend on market conditions and other factors,” noting that the number of shares to be offered and the offering price have not yet been determined.

The move comes as Anthropic has emerged as one of the world’s most valuable AI companies, fueled by growing demand for its Claude family of AI models and coding tools. The company recently raised $65 billion in a Series H funding round, valuing it at approximately $965 billion post-money, according to Anthropic.

Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers, Anthropic has become one of OpenAI’s closest rivals. Its products, including Claude and Claude Code, have gained traction among enterprises and software developers, helping position the company at the centre of the AI boom.

The filing sets the stage for what could be one of the most closely watched technology IPOs in recent years.

Anthropic joins a growing list of high-profile technology firms, such as SpaceX and OpenAI, that are exploring public market debuts amid a renewed investor appetite for growth and AI companies.

Anthropic emphasised that the announcement was issued under Rule 135 of the Securities Act of 1933 and “is not an offer to sell securities; nor is it a solicitation of an offer to buy them.” The company said any future offering would be conducted in accordance with applicable securities laws and registration requirements.

A timeline for the IPO has not been disclosed, and Anthropic has yet to reveal financial details, the proposed stock exchange listing, or a target valuation for the offering.

title: Cognizant Introduces Frontier Engineer, Business Operator Roles for AI-Powered Enterprises
content:
The company estimates a $4.5 trillion gap between AI’s potential and the results enterprises are currently achieving.

What Actually Matters.

Cognizant has introduced new roles to help businesses leverage AI investments effectively.

The Frontier Certified Engineer role focuses on redesigning processes for AI-enabled operations.

Cognizant has announced the creation of two new job categories — Frontier Certified Engineer and Frontier Business Operator — as part of its strategy to help organisations translate AI investments into business outcomes.

The company said the roles are being developed at scale and will be supported by SkillSpring, its proprietary training platform that prepares workers for AI-focused jobs.

The initiative is an extension of Cognizant’s AI Builder strategy, which seeks to address what the company estimates is a $4.5 trillion gap between AI’s potential and the results enterprises are currently achieving.

According to Cognizant, Frontier Certified Engineers will work with clients to redesign business processes for AI-enabled operations. The role will focus on identifying areas where AI can reshape workflows, reduce operational friction, and improve efficiency.

Frontier Business Operators, meanwhile, will be responsible for managing a workforce that combines human employees, AI agents, and automation systems. Their role will focus on overseeing operational performance and deploying AI tools alongside human decision-making to achieve business objectives.

“The question every enterprise is asking is why AI results aren’t showing up yet. The answer is talent and process,” said Thirumala Arohi, Senior Vice President and Head of Learning and Development at Cognizant.

Arohi said AI has exposed 93% of jobs to automation, but much of the associated labour value remains unrealised because organisations lack the workforce structures needed to deploy the technology effectively.

“The reason is not the technology; it is the workforce architecture,” Arohi said. “Frontier Certified Engineers who design for agentic outcomes and the Frontier Business Operators who own them are a new kind of professional, trained from day one to turn AI capability into business reality.”

The new roles will be trained through SkillSpring, which provides structured learning programs covering AI fluency, process design, data interpretation, and operational management. Cognizant said the platform is intended to shorten training timelines and provide clients with access to workers prepared for AI-driven environments.

Cognizant said the initiative reflects its broader focus on building the human and operational systems required for enterprises to deploy AI at scale as organisations seek to generate measurable returns from their AI investments.

title: Cadence Launches Autonomous AI Engineer for Chip Design
content:
Cadence said the AI agent can cut semiconductor verification cycles from five weeks to less than a day.

What Actually Matters.

Cadence has launched an autonomous AI engineer for chip design, achieving Level-5 autonomy.

The new system, powered by NVIDIA, aims to automate complex chip verification workflows.

Cadence Design Systems has announced a fully autonomous virtual AI engineer for chip design at Computex 2026, marking what the company called the industry’s first Level-5 autonomous agentic AI system for semiconductor development.

The system, powered by NVIDIA technologies, extends Cadence’s ChipStack AI Super Agent platform and aims to automate complex chip verification workflows.

The company said the platform also uses NVIDIA’s Nemotron models and runs within the OpenShell runtime, a sandboxed environment designed to secure autonomous AI agents. Cadence said the system enables semiconductor companies to run dynamic simulations in automated workflows while protecting sensitive design data.

“We see our customers using AI to let their expert engineers take on more ambitious silicon designs with greater speed and confidence,” said Paul Cunningham, Senior Vice President and General Manager of the System Verification Group at Cadence. “With the ChipStack AI Super Agent, we’re taking the next step, moving from AI that assists engineers to autonomous virtual engineers that can implement real design and verification work.”

The company added that the platform can deliver more than 40 times faster RTL validation cycles and reduce a verification loop from five weeks to less than a day.

The Level-5 autonomy allows Cadence to independently execute chip design and verification tasks like specification understanding, RTL generation, verification planning, simulation, formal analysis, debugging and design convergence. Engineers can still supervise and guide the workflows when required.

The AI system integrates with collaboration environments and tools such as Codex and Claude Code. It also evaluates intermediate results, determines next actions and iterates towards task completion without relying on step-by-step prompts.

Cadence acquired ChipStack in November 2025 and launched its first product in February 2026. In April, the company expanded the platform into a broader portfolio of AI super agents, including ViraStack AI Super Agent for analog design and InnoStack AI Super Agent for digital implementation and signoff.

The Level-5 autonomous capabilities of the ChipStack AI Super Agent and the AgentStack orchestration framework will be available to early-access customers in the second half of 2026, the company added.

The government's new AI scholarship programme will depend on how effectively it teaches creators to work alongside rapidly evolving AI systems.

What Actually Matters.

India's creator ecosystem is transitioning from informal to a structured employment sector.

Job postings for creator-related roles have significantly increased, highlighting their growing importance.

What began as a largely informal and fragmented creator ecosystem in India is now evolving into a structured employment sector.

According to a report from Indeed, creator-related job postings surged 919% between 2020 and early 2026, reflecting a shift by companies from one-off influencer collaborations to dedicated in-house creator and content teams.

The report found that creator-focused roles, which represented roughly 1 in 1,000 marketing jobs in 2020, now account for nearly 1 in 100 marketing-related openings nationwide.

The trend highlights how content creation, community engagement, and digital storytelling are becoming core business functions rather than peripheral marketing activities.

Recognising the growing importance of the creator economy and the rising demand for technology-enabled creative talent, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB), in partnership with the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT), has announced 15,000 scholarships to train young professionals in artificial intelligence.

The programme will focus on high-growth sectors such as media, entertainment, gaming, animation, visual effects (VFX), and digital content creation. Supported by global technology companies including Google and YouTube, the initiative seeks to address the growing skills gap emerging as AI reshapes creative industries.

The ministry will offer specialised training modules, mentorship opportunities, access to advanced tools, and hands-on learning experiences designed to prepare participants for AI-enabled creative workflows.

The move comes as organisations increasingly seek professionals who can combine creative capabilities with technical fluency.

Despite the rapid expansion of India’s influencer ecosystem, the report noted that demand for structured creator roles is outpacing the available talent pool, creating a widening skills gap across the sector.

Creator Economy Becoming More AI-Driven

In a discussion with AIM, Nipun Sharma, CEO of TeamLease, remarked that the programme exemplifies a broader transformation in how employers assess talent in the digital and creative industries.

"Industry-led AI skilling initiatives are critical in building a future-ready creative workforce because they align learning directly with how work is evolving," Sharma says.

He notes that the creator economy is no longer driven solely by content production.

He stated that the creator economy today is no longer just about content but involves combining creativity with technology, data, and platform understanding. His data shows that hiring is becoming increasingly capability-led, with employers prioritising digital fluency, AI awareness, and content-tech integration even in entry-level roles.

Sharma argues that involving platforms such as Google and YouTube can significantly improve the relevance of training programmes by exposing learners to real-world tools and workflows.

"When platforms like Google and YouTube are involved, training reflects real tools, workflows, and audience dynamics,” he says, arguing that it reduces the gap between learning and employability, enabling creators to move from content production to scalable, monetisable digital careers."

The initiative also highlights how AI is becoming embedded across multiple stages of content creation, from ideation and production to audience engagement and analytics.

"This initiative clearly signals that AI is becoming fundamental to the creator economy, not optional," Sharma says. “Content creation is increasingly being augmented by AI across editing, scripting, localisation, analytics, and audience targeting."

He states that companies are increasingly looking for professionals with hybrid skills that span creativity and technology.

"Our data indicates that sectors linked to digital content, marketing, and platform-based services are seeing sustained hiring momentum, with employers actively seeking hybrid skill sets that combine creativity with technology."

He adds that the institutionalisation of AI-focused training programmes indicates that AI-enabled creativity is transitioning from a niche employability requirement to a mainstream one.

Why Course Design Matters

While experts broadly welcomed the scholarship programme, some cautioned that access alone will not guarantee meaningful outcomes.

Samyak Chakrabarty, co-founder, Nimaya, a nonprofit that equips young women from underserved communities with GenAI and creator-economy skills, tells AIM that the quality and structure of AI education will ultimately determine whether the initiative succeeds.

"I think that scholarships on paper are a fantastic idea, and access to the availability of AI training is very important," he states.

However, he warns against treating AI education as a collection of basic prompting exercises.

"AI is a big word, right? He suggests. So it's really important that the courses that they're getting the scholarship for are properly curated, because merely learning ChatGPT or anybody else giving a course on AI is not really teaching fundamentals of how to build an intuitive relationship with AI."

Chakrabarty states that AI technologies are evolving too rapidly for static skills training to remain effective.

"The people who will be poised to most successfully use it will actually understand it as an entity that they are working with, or they are making them do their work," he says.

Building Long-Term AI Literacy

Chakrabarty further stresses that understanding how AI systems operate is more important than simply learning how to issue prompts.

"If you just do these random prompting courses, but if you don't know how AI imagines, how can you imagine what you want it to do for you?," he states.

Summarising his view on the initiative, he says that democratising access remains valuable, but curriculum design will be the real differentiator.

On paper, giving scholarships for courses that teach AI is great at democratising access, but one cannot fully say it will bridge the gap of exposure because the curation and design of the courses is more important than the fact that they're free.

The scholarship programme is one of the government's largest AI-focused skilling initiatives, specifically targeted at the creative industries.

As AI tools become deeply integrated into content production, digital storytelling, gaming, animation, and media workflows, policymakers and industry leaders increasingly view AI literacy as a critical employability skill.

The success of the initiative may ultimately depend on whether it can move beyond tool-based training and create a generation of creators capable of combining creativity, technological understanding, and critical thinking in an AI-driven economy.

Salesforce's stake in AI startup Anthropic has reached approximately $5 billion as the company nears its IPO.

Salesforce began investing in Anthropic in early 2023 and has participated in multiple funding rounds.

Salesforce’s investment in AI startup Anthropic has grown to about $5 billion, according to a Bloomberg report, as the Claude developer moves closer to a public market debut after confidentially filing for an initial public offering (IPO).

The enterprise software company reportedly began backing Anthropic in early 2023 with an investment of roughly $50 million and has participated in each of the startup’s subsequent fundraising rounds.

The value of Salesforce’s stake has surged alongside Anthropic’s rapid rise in valuation, which recently reached about $965 billion following a $65 billion funding round.

The holding now represents a significant portion of Salesforce’s investment portfolio. According to the report, Salesforce’s strategic investments were valued at approximately $7.8 billion at the end of April, before Anthropic’s latest fundraising round. At its current estimated value, the company’s stake accounts for roughly two-thirds of that portfolio.

Anthropic confidentially filed for an IPO on June 1, setting the stage for one of the most closely watched public offerings in the AI sector. The company has emerged as one of the industry’s biggest winners, surpassing OpenAI in private-market valuation after its latest funding round.

Salesforce has integrated Anthropic’s technology across its products, including Slack and its Agentforce platform. Salesforce Chief Executive Marc Benioff has also said the company plans to spend $300 million on Anthropic tokens in 2026.

In a February blog post, Salesforce Ventures said its original investment was made when there was little evidence that AI research labs could generate large commercial businesses.

“We first invested in Anthropic’s Series C in early 2023, and we’ve stood by their side through every subsequent round since, including their latest Series G in February 2026,” the company wrote.

Bloomberg reported that other investors, including Zoom through its venture arm, have also seen substantial increases in the value of their Anthropic holdings as investor demand for AI companies has intensified.

The capital raise includes $30 billion in underwritten public offerings, consisting of $15 billion in mandatory convertible preferred stock and $15 billion in Class A and Class C shares.

Alphabet said its cloud backlog nearly doubled quarter over quarter to more than $460 billion. The company also reported 350 million paid subscriptions and said more than 8.5 million developers use its AI models each month.

Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, and Morgan Stanley are serving as joint book-running managers for the underwritten offerings, while Goldman Sachs is acting as placement agent for the Berkshire Hathaway transaction. title: Anthropic Expands Project Glasswing to 150 Organisations Across 15 Countries
content:
The new group includes organisations from sectors such as power, water, healthcare, communications and hardware.

What Actually Matters.

Anthropic's Project Glasswing now includes around 150 organisations across more than 15 countries.

The initiative aims to enhance cybersecurity for critical software in various sectors, including healthcare and communications.

Anthropic on June 2 announced that it is expanding Project Glasswing, its cybersecurity initiative to secure critical software, to approximately 150 additional organisations across more than 15 countries.

The expansion follows the company’s initial rollout in April, when about 50 partners were granted access to Claude Mythos Preview, an AI model trained to identify software vulnerabilities. Anthropic recently said those partners had discovered more than 10,000 high- and critical-severity security flaws using the system.

The new group includes organisations from sectors such as power, water, healthcare, communications and hardware, areas that were less represented in the initial cohort. Many of the new participants are software vendors and nonprofit maintainers whose codebases are used by governments and organisations worldwide.

“What each partner has in common is that a successful attack on their codebase could be catastrophic,” Anthropic said. The company added that for most partners, “a major attack could affect more than 100 million people, with important ramifications for both global and national security.”

Anthropic said the expansion is part of its broader effort to improve software security through AI while helping the cybersecurity industry adapt to increasingly capable AI systems.

The company warned that “cheap, fast AI models with powerful cyber capabilities are around the corner” and reiterated its expectation that many AI developers could have models with capabilities comparable to Claude Mythos Preview within six to 12 months.

“Mythos Preview continues a long-term trend that we’ve been warning about for some time,” Anthropic said, adding that some future models could be released without safeguards that prevent misuse, potentially increasing the frequency and unpredictability of cyberattacks.

As part of its efforts to support defenders, Anthropic said it recently launched Claude Security, a product that uses its public frontier models, including Claude Opus 4.8, to scan codebases and suggest patches. The company is also making available, upon request, to trusted security teams, tools developed for Project Glasswing participants to help identify vulnerabilities more quickly.

Anthropic said the cybersecurity challenge is shifting from vulnerability discovery to the processes of verification, disclosure and patching. Many Project Glasswing partners are already using Mythos Preview to generate software patches and conduct pre-release security checks, according to the company.

The model can also be applied to penetration testing, threat detection and response, and modernising legacy software by rebuilding codebases in memory-safe programming languages, Anthropic said.

The company said it is discussing ways to scale vulnerability review and patching efforts in open-source software and is working on improving vulnerability disclosure practices for open-source maintainers.

Looking ahead, Anthropic said it plans to further expand Project Glasswing, focusing on critical infrastructure providers, maintainers of essential open-source software and safety testers. It also intends to broaden its Cyber Verification Program, which would provide Mythos-class capabilities to more organisations for specific cyber defence tasks.

“We're working as quickly as we can to safely release Mythos-level capabilities in general access,” Anthropic said, while acknowledging that safeguards capable of preventing misuse of advanced cyber models remain an unresolved challenge across the AI industry.

title: India Tech Hiring Hits 28-Month Low as Active Job Demand Falls 17% YoY
content:
Tech sector openings have dropped to 93,000, marking the steepest monthly decline in a year amid US uncertainty, according to Xpheno.

What Actually Matters.

India's tech sector experienced its sharpest hiring slowdown in over two years, reaching a 28-month low.

Active tech job demand fell by 17% year-on-year, with 93,000 openings recorded in June.

India’s technology sector is facing its sharpest hiring slowdown in more than two years, with active tech job demand falling to a 28-month low in June, according to a new report by Xpheno.

The report estimates 93,000 active technology openings in the country, down 17% from a year earlier and 14% lower than May, marking the steepest month-on-month decline recorded in the past 12 months.

The report attributes the downturn to multiple developments in the United States, a key market for India's technology services industry, which have dampened hiring sentiment across technology cohorts. According to the findings, active tech demand has now fallen to levels last seen in January 2024 and is 22% below the peak recorded in March 2026.

The hiring slowdown has been broad-based. Full-time technology openings declined 15% month-on-month to 68,000, while entry-level openings fell 23% from May and 44% compared to June 2025. IT services, the largest consumer of technology talent, recorded a 16% month-on-month decline and a 31% year-on-year drop in active demand.

In contrast, global capability centres (GCCs) continued to show resilience. Active tech demand from GCCs stood at 17,000 openings, up 31% year-on-year despite a modest 6% month-on-month decline.

The report also highlighted concerns around the potential return of Indian technology professionals from the United States amid uncertainty surrounding H-1B visa holders. It noted that increasing repatriation of technology talent could place additional pressure on an already weak domestic job market.

Commenting on the trend, Co-Founder Kamal Karanth said, “Uncle Sam spooks Indian Tech Jobs market… active demand hits 28-month low.”

“Indian tech sector’s active talent demand has been hit sharp and hard by multiple unexpected developments in and from the USA. Overall active tech talent demand is on a race to the bottom again, with June’s demand outlook hitting a record 28-month low. The negative start to the new Fiscal 2027, post March 26, seems to continue further and intensify going further into the first quarter,” he added.

The report noted that technology hiring has remained subdued over the past five quarters, with the sector now accounting for 44% of India's total active job demand, marking the third consecutive month that its share has remained below the 50% threshold.

title: Canada’s CIBC, Swiss Nestlé Pick Hyderabad for New GCCs
content:
Hyderabad today hosts over 450 GCCs, employing more than 1.35 lakh professionals, while housing firms such as JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Vanguard, Wells Fargo, HSBC, and more.

What Actually Matters.

CIBC and Nestlé are establishing global capability centres in Hyderabad, expanding the city's multinational presence.

Hyderabad currently hosts over 450 GCCs, employing more than 135,000 professionals across various sectors.

Canada’s Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) and FMCG major Nestlé are setting up global capability centres (GCCs) in Hyderabad, according to a report by The Times of India (TOI).

The centres will add to the city’s growing network of multinational technology and operations hubs. According to the report, CIBC plans to launch its Hyderabad GCC in July, while Nestlé expects to open its centre in the coming months.

The development comes as Hyderabad continues to attract multinational firms across banking, financial services and consumer sectors. CIBC’s facility will reportedly house over 2,000 professionals and stem from an investment commitment made during the Telangana Rising Global Summit 2025.

This could encourage more banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) firms to choose Hyderabad for similar centres. The city already houses firms such as JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, UBS, Vanguard, Wells Fargo, Deutsche Börse, HSBC, US Bancorp, Barclays, American Express and Zurich Insurance.

While Bengaluru remains the goldmine of GCCs, Hyderabad is catching pace faster than ever. The city today hosts over 450 GCCs, employing more than 1.35 lakh professionals.

US-based LPL Financial also launched its first India GCC in the city and is building towards hundreds of hires across technology, data analytics, risk and product engineering.

According to Xpheno’s June 2026 Active Tech Jobs Outlook report, the city had around 8,000 active tech openings. While that marked a 20% month-on-month and 50% year-on-year drop, the city continues to attract multinational GCC investment across the banking, financial services, and consumer sectors.

Nestlé’s planned GCC will support Hyderabad’s FMCG and food processing ecosystem, as the centre is expected to focus on innovation and supply chain development while creating jobs in the city.

According to the Nasscom-Zinnov GCC Landscape Report 2026, India hosted an estimated 2,117 GCCs in FY26, with more than 500 new centres added over the past five years. Two-thirds of new GCCs launched in the last two years chose tier-1 cities, underlining the pull of hubs such as Hyderabad for multinational firms seeking technology and operations talent.

Meanwhile, US-based aerospace and advanced engineering firm SARGAD plans to establish a global innovation centre in Hyderabad. According to TOI, company representatives met Telangana CM Revanth Reddy during the World Economic Forum 2026 in Davos. The proposed facility will support Hyderabad’s ambitions to strengthen its aerospace and advanced engineering ecosystem.

title: [Exclusive] UIDAI CEO to Also Lead IndiaAI Mission
content:
The CEO of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), Saurabh Vijay, will also take charge as the CEO of the IndiaAI Mission.

What Actually Matters.

Saurabh Vijay, CEO of UIDAI, will also lead the IndiaAI Mission following Abhishek Singh's reassignment.

This change signals a consolidation of leadership in India's critical digital and AI initiatives.

The Chief Executive Officer of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), Saurabh Vijay, will also take charge as the CEO of the IndiaAI Mission, according to confirmations from the UIDAI office and a source within IndiaAI under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY).

The development comes weeks after Abhishek Singh, the former CEO of the IndiaAI Mission, was reassigned as Director General of the National Testing Agency (NTA), leaving the position vacant amid a broader bureaucratic reshuffle.

Saurabh Vijay, an IAS officer, assumed charge as CEO of UIDAI in mid-May 2026. His additional role at IndiaAI signals a consolidation of leadership across two of the government’s most critical digital infrastructure and artificial intelligence initiatives.

The move also reflects the government’s increasing alignment between foundational digital identity systems and emerging AI infrastructure. UIDAI, which manages Aadhaar, has been central to India’s digital public infrastructure, while the IndiaAI Mission is tasked with scaling artificial intelligence capabilities across sectors.

During his tenure, Singh had focused on deploying AI at scale across public systems. Under his leadership, India activated 38,000 GPUs and pushed for shared compute infrastructure to support startups and researchers. His approach emphasised building an indigenous AI ecosystem while maintaining openness to global collaboration.

Singh’s reassignment followed the India AI Impact Summit 2026, where he reiterated the need for a sovereign AI approach centred on control over data and systems without isolating India from global innovation.

With Vijay now taking additional charge, attention is expected to shift toward how India integrates its existing digital public infrastructure, including Aadhaar, with AI-driven governance and service delivery systems.

Supporting the operational side of the IndiaAI Mission is Kavita Bhatia, who continues as Chief Operating Officer. Bhatia brings over 24 years of experience in e-governance and technology within MeitY. She has played a key role in several large-scale digital initiatives including Mobile Seva, Aadhaar authentication, Aadhaar Data Vault, e-Sign, and Single Sign-On.

Between 2002 and 2022, she led MeitY’s e-Governance Division, overseeing initiatives that enabled more than 1 billion digital transactions. Her work on Aadhaar authentication has supported secure service delivery for over 1.3 billion users.

Under the IndiaAI Mission, the government had selected 12 Indian AI startups to build sovereign AI models for the country. Sarvam, BharatGen, Tech Mahindra, and few others have already announced their models at the India AI Impact summit in February.

title: Hitachi Energy India Aims for 30% Boost in Data Centre Growth with ‘Grid-to-Rack’ Solution
content:
The power solution will enhance energy supply for data centres and increase the market size for power infrastructure spending by 10-15%.

What Actually Matters.

Hitachi Energy India aims to increase its data centre market share to 30% with a new 'grid-to-rack' power solution.

The 'grid-to-rack' solution is expected to expand the company's addressable market by 10-15% in power infrastructure spending.

Hitachi Energy India aims to increase its share of the country’s data centre sector from a previous target of 10-15% to 30%. This new approach will offer a comprehensive ‘grid-to-rack’ power solution, Venu Nuguri, the Managing Director and CEO, told Reuters.

As a subsidiary of Zurich-based Hitachi Energy, Hitachi Energy India produces and supplies power equipment and grid technology for various industries, particularly data centres. The company holds roughly 50% of India's high-voltage direct current (HVDC) market, providing equipment that facilitates the transmission of electricity over long distances.

Previously, the firm estimated its addressable market in the data centre sector to be 10-15% of overall spending, encompassing both equipment and software solutions.

According to Nuguri, the ‘grid-to-rack’ solution will streamline energy supply for data centres, covering everything from the grid connection to distribution at the server rack level. This addition is expected to increase the company’s market size by another 10-15% in power infrastructure spending within the overall data centre industry.

Recently, Hitachi Energy India announced plans for a ₹20 billion (about $210.53 million) investment to establish a new large power transformer facility in Gujarat, bringing its total capital expenditure to ₹40 billion across 19 factories in eight locations. The company ended 2026 with an unprecedented order backlog of ₹296 billion.

Furthermore, Nuguri mentioned that the firm is “actively exploring” potential acquisitions in areas like data centres, digital technology, and power consulting to address any capability gaps.

According to consulting firm ​IMARC Group, the Indian data centre market, valued at $5.55 billion in 2025, is projected to reach $13.11 billion by 2034, with a CAGR of 10.01% from 2026 to 2034. This growth is driven by rapid digital transformation, increased cloud adoption, and rising AI/ML workload requirements.

India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) 2023 and initiatives like BharatNet are boosting investment, with hardware expected to hold 50% of the components market in 2025. Maharashtra, primarily Mumbai, accounts for the largest regional shares at 26%.

title: Figma Brings Local Code Editing to its AI Suite
content:
New Figma Make update lets teams edit production code and collaborate without leaving the platform.

What Actually Matters.

Figma's new update allows users to edit production code directly within the platform.

The features enable designers, developers, and product teams to collaborate on code and manage Git workflows.

Figma has launched new capabilities in Figma Make, its proprietary AI suite, allowing users to work directly in production codebases from within the platform, as product teams increasingly seek tighter links between design and development.

The update enables designers, developers, and product teams to visually edit interfaces, annotate changes, collaborate on code, and manage Git workflows without leaving Figma. The features are available in limited beta through Figma Make’s desktop app for Mac users. The company said the rollout began on May 28, and users can join a waitlist for early access.

Figma described the update as its “first step toward bringing together freeform design, prototyping with code, and shipping to production”. The beta includes direct editing, annotations, chat, and pull request creation. These features will not consume AI credits during the beta period. The pricing details for AI credits will be announced later.

While the company has simplified the setup for non-technical users, the process still requires refinement. For now, the functionality is best suited for designers who already have access to their organisation’s codebase.

The launch marks Figma’s latest push into code-based product development as AI reshapes software workflows. The company said teams can now connect running applications to Figma Make and work directly with real codebases instead of static prototypes.

Figma said the new capabilities aim to remove friction between design and engineering teams. Users can make direct visual edits to interfaces by selecting elements and changing layouts, colours, fonts, or sizing. Figma Make then identifies the relevant code and applies the edits.

For changes that go beyond visual properties, such as interactions or animations, users can annotate interface elements with instructions. The company said these annotations give its AI agent contextual information to make code-level updates.

“‘Design vs code’ is a false dichotomy,” Figma mentioned in a statement. “Tools should not limit the ability to move between these worlds.”

The company argued that coding tools still lag behind collaborative design software. “We’re still stuck in 2016 when it comes to collaboration,” it said, adding that many users do not find integrated development environments and terminals intuitive.

The update also adds support for Git workflows. Teams can create branches, revert commits, and manage version histories directly in Figma Make. Changes remain as local commits until teams open a pull request through their standard engineering review process.

Figma said teams will also be able to share code changes through links. Once teammates gain access to a branch, they can view edits, build on changes, and compare revisions through commit histories.

The platform also allows users to move screens, pages, and components between Figma Make and the Figma design canvas. Teams can edit these visually and sync decisions back into code.

“The goal is to close the loop entirely,” the company said, describing a workflow where teams can move between design feedback and code development in one place.

title: Persistent Expands Europe Footprint as AI Modernisation Demand Rises
content:
Persistent Systems will add more than 90 engineers from Estonia-based IT consulting firm, Concise, expanding its Eastern European delivery network.

What Actually Matters.

Persistent Systems is enhancing its presence in Eastern Europe by acquiring over 90 engineers from Concise.

The expansion aims to strengthen AI-led transformation capabilities and local delivery networks for European clients.

Persistent Systems has signed an agreement to expand its presence in Eastern Europe by integrating a team of more than 90 professionals from Estonia-based software engineering and IT consulting firm, Concise, as the Pune-headquartered IT services company looks to strengthen its AI-led transformation capabilities in Europe.

The transaction, which remains subject to closing conditions, will give Persistent new delivery centres in Tallinn and Tartu, and deepen its nearshore delivery capabilities for European clients, according to a company statement issued on June 1.

The move comes as enterprises increase spending on AI-enabled operations, automation and digital infrastructure modernisation, prompting technology services firms to expand local delivery capabilities and specialised engineering talent in key markets.

Persistent said the addition of the Concise team would strengthen its expertise in AI-led product engineering, distributed systems and cloud-native technologies. The company also expects the deal to enhance its capabilities in sectors such as mobility, logistics, smart infrastructure and connected ecosystems.

While financial details of the transaction were not disclosed, the company said the expansion would strengthen its European nearshore delivery model and support customers undertaking large-scale platform modernisation and AI adoption programmes.

The company is also seeking to deepen its relationship with a strategic customer in the enterprise mobility segment through expansion.

“Enterprises are increasingly rearchitecting core systems and digital infrastructure to support AI-enabled operations, automation and globally connected business environments. This is accelerating demand for partners that can modernise complex operational systems, integrate AI into critical workflows and support globally distributed operations at scale,” said Kuljesh Puri, Executive Vice President of Communications, Media and Technology at Persistent.

The acquisition reflects a broader trend among Indian IT services firms to strengthen their European delivery networks and domain expertise as clients seek regionally aligned technology partners capable of supporting AI deployments while meeting governance and regulatory requirements.

title: NVIDIA Releases Open Source AI Models Built for the Physical World
content:
Cosmos 3 combines physical reasoning, world modelling and action generation in a single architecture.

What Actually Matters.

NVIDIA has launched Cosmos 3, an open-source model for physical AI integrating reasoning, world generation, and action generation.

The new model includes Cosmos 3 Nano and Cosmos 3 Super, alongside various training resources and synthetic datasets.

NVIDIA has released Cosmos 3, a new open-source foundation model for physical AI that combines physical reasoning, world generation and action generation within a single architecture.

The company is making Cosmos 3 Nano (8B parameters) and Cosmos 3 Super (32B parameters) available, along with training scripts, deployment tools, model checkpoints, and six synthetic datasets for robotics, autonomous driving, warehouse automation, and other physical AI applications.

The release consolidates capabilities that were previously spread across separate Cosmos models. Cosmos 3 uses a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture built around two interconnected components: a vision-language ‘Reasoner’ tower and a diffusion-based ‘Generator’ tower.

A clip of a video generated by Cosmos 3 for the autonomous driving domain. Source: NVIDIA

The Reasoner processes multimodal inputs, including text, images, videos, audio and actions to understand physical environments, while the Generator produces future observations and action sequences conditioned on that understanding.

According to NVIDIA, the architecture is designed to eliminate the need for orchestration across multiple models and inference pipelines.

The Reasoner can operate independently for perception and analysis tasks, while generation workloads activate both towers, allowing the model to combine scene understanding with predictive world modelling and action generation.

The company is releasing two model sizes targeting different deployment environments. Cosmos 3 Nano, with 8 billion parameters, is designed for workstation-class systems, including NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs, and for real-time robotics applications.

Cosmos 3 Super, at 32 billion parameters, targets datacenter deployments on Hopper and Blackwell GPU platforms for synthetic data generation and large-scale physical reasoning workloads. It supports multiple input-output combinations, covering text-to-image generation, video prediction, video reasoning, action-conditioned world modelling and robot policy learning.

NVIDIA positions the model as a foundation for applications including robotic manipulation, autonomous driving systems, warehouse monitoring, smart spaces and embodied AI agents.

Alongside the models, NVIDIA is open-sourcing six synthetic data generation datasets through Hugging Face. The datasets cover embodied robot scenes, physical interaction simulations, spatial reasoning tasks, digital human environments, autonomous driving scenarios and warehouse operations.

Some datasets include physics annotations, such as object velocities, centre-of-mass displacements, and semantic segmentation labels, intended for post-training and evaluation workflows.

NVIDIA is also releasing post-training recipes covering supervised fine-tuning and action-oriented training. The workflows allow developers to adapt Cosmos 3 to domain-specific datasets and use cases, including forward-dynamics prediction, inverse-dynamics modelling, and policy generation for robotics systems.

For deployment, Cosmos 3 is available through NVIDIA NIM microservices. The initial release includes the Cosmos 3 Reasoner NIM, while a Generator NIM is planned.

NVIDIA also introduced Cosmos Human Evaluation (HUE), an open-source benchmark framework that evaluates generated videos using binary fact-verification questions across semantic alignment, physical laws, geometric reasoning and visual integrity.

The framework is intended to provide a more granular assessment of physical AI video generation systems than existing leaderboard-based evaluations.

According to NVIDIA, Cosmos 3 leads its parameter classes on VANTAGE-Bench and ranks at or near the top of several public physical AI and video-generation benchmarks, including PAI-Bench, R-Bench, Physics-IQ and RoboLab.

The company also said Cosmos 3 currently ranks as the leading open-source model on selected image and video-generation leaderboards tracked by Artificial Analysis.

title: AI Coding Startup Cursor to Hire 200 Across Asia-Pacific in Major Expansion Push
content:
The company plans to strengthen its presence in Asia-Pacific by adding 200 employees and expanding operations in Singapore, Japan, Australia and India, while also launching a new office in London.

What Actually Matters.

Cursor plans to hire 200 employees across Asia-Pacific to meet growing demand for AI-powered software development tools.

The hiring will focus on customer-facing and technical roles in key markets such as Singapore, Japan, Australia, and India.

AI coding startup Cursor is planning a major expansion across the Asia-Pacific region, aiming to hire 200 employees over the next six months as demand for AI-powered software development tools continues to grow.

According to a report by Business Insider, the San Francisco-based company will recruit employees across Singapore, Japan, Sydney, Melbourne and India. The hiring drive will primarily focus on customer-facing and technical roles, including go-to-market teams, field engineers and AI deployment engineers.

The expansion comes shortly after Cursor secured a significant partnership with SpaceX, further strengthening its position in the rapidly growing AI coding sector.

Speaking about the company’s growth plans, Nick Miller, Senior Engineer at Cursor, said, “Cursor intends to expand its presence across Asia-Pacific while also establishing a new office in London by July. The company is additionally exploring smaller office locations across Europe.”

Earlier this month, Simon Green, APJ President at Cursor, launched the company’s Singapore office. The company is also hiring a recruiter for its Singapore operations as it scales its regional workforce.

Cursor currently employs around 800 people across its offices in San Francisco and New York. The company has approximately 90 open positions listed across locations, including Australia, New York, Berlin, London and the Netherlands.

The startup has attracted attention in recent months following its partnership with SpaceX. In April, SpaceX announced an agreement that gives it the option to acquire Cursor for $60 billion or pay $10 billion for the company's work.

“Excited to partner with the SpaceX team to scale up Composer. A meaningful step on our path to build the best place to code with AI,” noted Michael Truell, CEO of Cursor.

Cursor’s client list includes major technology companies such as Stripe, Coinbase, Discord, Salesforce, Neuralink and NVIDIA, reflecting growing enterprise demand for AI-assisted software development tools.
