title: Bellatrix, South Korean TelePIX Set Sights on VLEO Satellite Launch by 2028
content:
The collaboration seeks to address growing demand for high-resolution Earth observation data across sectors such as defence, environmental monitoring, and disaster response.

What Actually Matters.

TelePIX and Bellatrix Aerospace aim to launch a Very Low Earth Orbit satellite by 2028.

The partnership focuses on high-resolution Earth observation data for various sectors.

South Korea-based TelePIX has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Bengaluru-based Bellatrix Aerospace to jointly develop a Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) Earth observation satellite, with a technology demonstration launch planned for 2028.

The two companies signed the agreement at TelePIX’s satellite payload development facility, SpaceLab, in Daejeon, South Korea.

Under the partnership, TelePIX will integrate its optical payload, Chouette, with Bellatrix Aerospace’s Air-Breathing Electric Propulsion-powered satellite platform to develop a satellite capable of operating in VLEO, typically between 150 km and 250 km above Earth.

“We are excited to partner with TelePIX, whose innovative wide-swath optical payload technology is exceptionally well-suited for VLEO missions,” said Rohan M Ganapathy, CEO of Bellatrix Aerospace. He added that commercially viable VLEO constellations would require larger satellite platforms and advances in propulsion technology.

By operating closer to Earth than conventional Low Earth Orbit satellites, VLEO systems can deliver sharper imaging. However, lower altitudes also create stronger atmospheric drag, which requires propulsion systems capable of sustaining long-term operations.

As part of the agreement, Bellatrix Aerospace will provide the satellite platform, including propulsion, thermal control, power, and attitude control systems. TelePIX will contribute its Chouette optical payload and support system integration.

The companies said they will also collaborate on launch operations, early orbit activities, and satellite mission management. Following in-orbit validation, they plan to explore constellation-scale deployments and commercial VLEO missions.

TelePIX said Chouette has been designed for VLEO environments and offers a wide-swath imaging system with more than double the observation width of comparable satellites currently available. The company also plans to use its AI-based image processing technology alongside the payload.

“VLEO satellites are emerging as a key segment of the next-generation high-resolution Earth observation market, and advanced satellite operation technologies are essential for stable long-term operations,” said Seongick Cho, CEO of TelePIX.

He added that the company plans to extend TelePIX’s optical payload technology into the VLEO domain while strengthening the foundation for global market expansion through this partnership.

The partnership also reflects growing cooperation between India’s private space ecosystem and international NewSpace firms. India has seen rising private-sector participation in the space industry following regulatory reforms and market liberalisation.

title: SoftBank Announces Plan to Build 5 GW of AI Data Centre Capacity in France
content:
The initial phase includes a €45 billion investment to establish 3.1 GW of AI data centre capacity in the Hauts-de-France region.

What Actually Matters.

SoftBank plans to invest up to €75 billion to develop 5 GW of AI data centre capacity in France.

The initial phase involves a €45 billion investment for 3.1 GW of AI data centres in the Hauts-de-France region.

SoftBank Group has announced a significant investment plan to develop and operate 5 GW of AI data centre capacity in France, with a total investment of up to €75 billion.

The initial phase involves a €45 billion investment to establish 3.1 GW of AI data centre capacity in the Hauts-de-France region, disclosed during the 2026 Choose France summit.

“AI is entering a new era, and the countries that build the infrastructure for this transformation will shape the future of technology, industry and society,” Masayoshi Son, Chairman and CEO, SoftBank Group, said in a statement. “SoftBank is proud to make this major commitment to France. With its industrial capabilities, talent base and national ambition, France is uniquely positioned to become a leading AI infrastructure hub in Europe.”

This initiative represents SoftBank Group’s largest investment in AI infrastructure in Europe, designed to facilitate the rapid expansion of AI by increasing access to advanced computing resources in France.

“[The investment] reflects our country’s substantial assets: fast access to the most reliable electrical grid in Europe… By partnering with leading French companies EDF on the Bouchain data center and Schneider Electric for a robotised plant, SoftBank displays a long-term commitment to building the future of an industry-centric AI in France,” Roland Lescure, French Minister of Economy, Finance, & Industrial, Energy, and Digital Sovereignty, added.

The first phase will focus on achieving 3.1 GW of AI data centre capacity in the Hauts-de-France region by 2031, with planned data centres located in Dunkirk (Loon-Plage), Bosquel, and Bouchain.

“This project marks a significant milestone in Dunkirk’s strategy to become a leading hub for the digital economy. It comes alongside an ongoing competitive tender process for a state-of-the-art data centre at the Port of Dunkirk’s Western Harbour,” Maurice Georges, CEO of the Port of Dunkirk and Patrice Vergriete, Chairman of the Dunkirk Urban Council and Mayor of Dunkirk, said.

Moreover, SoftBank Group intends to identify further sites across France, bolstering the nation’s position as a key European center for cutting-edge digital infrastructure. Collaborating with SB Energy and other strategic partners, SoftBank Group will spearhead these projects.

According to the company, these AI data centres will meet the growing demand for high-performance computing across a wide range of stakeholders, including AI companies, cloud service providers, businesses, public institutions, and research organisations.

title: Karnataka Forms Quantum Task Force to Drive State’s Quantum Technology Ambitions
content:
The 16-member panel will guide policy, infrastructure development, and ecosystem growth as Karnataka seeks to establish itself as India’s leading quantum technology hub.

What Actually Matters.

Karnataka has established a Quantum Task Force to enhance its position as a national leader in quantum technology.

The task force will oversee the implementation of the Karnataka Quantum Technology Roadmap, promoting research and industrial growth.

The Karnataka government has constituted a high-level Karnataka Quantum Task Force to accelerate the state's ambitions of becoming a national hub for quantum technology, research, innovation, and industrial adoption.

The Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology, and Science and Technology Department issued the order following the launch of the Karnataka Quantum Technology Roadmap at the recent Quantum India Bengaluru Summit.

The task force has been mandated to oversee the implementation of the roadmap and provide strategic direction for the state's emerging quantum ecosystem.

Leading the 16-member committee is Prof Arindam Ghosh, JRD Tata Chair Professor and JC Bose National Fellow at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc). The Director of the Department of Science and Technology, Government of Karnataka, along with the Managing Director of Karnataka Science and Technology Promotion Society (KSTePS), will serve as the Member Secretary.

The task force brings together representatives from academia, research institutions, industry, startups, and government departments. Key academic and research members include Prof Urbasi Sinha of Raman Research Institute, Prof B Gurumoorthy of FSID-IISc, Prof Akshay Naik of Quantum Research Park, Ajith Padyana of VTU-VRIF Centre for Deep Technologies, Prof Rajesh Gopakumar of ICTS, and Taslimarif Saiyed of C-CAMP.

Industry representation includes L Venkata Subramanian, CEO of Qbit Force and former Head of IBM Quantum India, who was recently inducted into the Reserve Bank of India's expert committee on the Quantum Secure and Adaptive Financial Ecosystem (Q-SAFE).

Other industry members include Nagendra Nagaraj of QPiAI, Naganand Doraswamy of IdeaSpring Capital, Wing Commander S Sudhakaran (Retd.) of QuGates Technologies, and Seema Ambastha of L&T Data Center and Cloud Services.

Senior government officials from the Commerce and Industries Department, the Higher Education Department, and the Department of ITBT and Science and Technology are also part of the committee.

According to the government order, the task force will play a central role in policy formulation, ecosystem development, startup support, talent creation, and industry engagement in quantum technologies. The committee will also advise on attracting investments and fostering collaborations between academia, industry, and government.

One of its most significant responsibilities will be guiding the development of critical quantum infrastructure projects, including the proposed Quantum City in Hesaraghatta, which is envisioned as a major hub for quantum research, innovation, startups, and advanced technology development.

title: Intel, 3DGS Explore Advanced Semiconductor Packaging Facility in Odisha
content:
The proposed project could position Odisha as a major hub for semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging, AI infrastructure, and next-generation data centres.

What Actually Matters.

Intel and 3D Glass Solutions plan to explore an advanced semiconductor packaging facility in Odisha.

The project aims to enhance India's semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem and attract global technology players.

The Odisha government has announced that Intel Corporation and 3D Glass Solutions (3DGS) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to explore the establishment of an advanced semiconductor glass core packaging substrate manufacturing facility in the state.

The proposed project, which remains subject to regulatory approvals, funding support from both the state and central governments, and other business conditions, is expected to significantly strengthen India's semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem.

According to the state government, the facility could become one of the largest technology investments in Eastern India and serve as a catalyst for the development of semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging, AI infrastructure, next-generation data centres, and digital technologies in the region.

The announcement aligns with Odisha's broader ambition to build a globally competitive semiconductor and digital infrastructure ecosystem under its Vision 2036 roadmap and India's Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative.

Commenting on the development, Babu Mandava, CEO of 3D Glass Solutions, said, “We are grateful for the strong support of the Odisha government and excited about our collaboration with Intel in exploring this opportunity. This initiative has the potential to establish India as a key global hub for advanced glass substrates and semiconductor packaging, supporting high-growth sectors such as AI, high-performance computing, and next-generation electronics.”

The state government said the initiative represents a strategic opportunity to attract global technology players, research institutions, and industry stakeholders to help build what it describes as one of Asia's most advanced semiconductor and digital infrastructure ecosystems.

Naga Chandrasekaran, Executive Vice President and General Manager, Intel Foundry, said, “Intel Foundry is proud to collaborate with 3DGS in exploring this opportunity with the Odisha government. As a pioneer in glass core substrate technology, we are excited about the potential of this collaboration to accelerate the commercialisation of next-generation advanced packaging solutions globally.”

Highlighting the state's long-term objectives, Mukesh Mahaling, Odisha's Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, Health and Family Welfare, and Parliamentary Affairs, said, “Odisha remains focused on building a conducive ecosystem that promotes innovation, facilitates investments, creates job opportunities, and drives inclusive growth across industries.”

Ashwini Vaishnaw, Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, Railways, and Information and Broadcasting, said, “This initiative reflects India’s larger vision of strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities and positioning the country as a global economic powerhouse.”

The Chief Minister of Odisha called the proposed investment a landmark moment for the state’s technology ambitions.

title: OpenAI Begins Hiring Engineers for Robotics Division
content:
The company envisions everyone having a personal robot that does everything they need.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI is actively hiring engineers for its new robotics division to enhance societal utility.

The immediate goal is to develop robots that assist skilled workers in infrastructure projects.

OpenAI is recruiting engineers for its robotics division across hardware, machine learning, systems, and operations, according to Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman.

“OpenAI Robotics is hiring, looking for exceptional full-stack hardware, ops, systems, and ML engineers to help us program and manufacture robots that are useful for society,” Altman wrote on X on May 31.

According to him, the company’s near-term focus is on building robots that can assist skilled workers in developing infrastructure. “In the short term, we are focused on robots to support skilled workers to build our future infrastructure.”

“In the long term, we imagine everyone having a personal robot doing anything they need,” he added.

The company said the new unit, called OpenAI Robotics, has grown out of its world simulation research programme led by researcher Aditya Ramesh. Altman said the effort combines robotics hardware development with machine learning research

The company is asking interested candidates to email their background and evidence of accomplishments directly to its robotics recruiting team.

The announcement marks OpenAI’s return to robotics after shutting down an earlier robotics effort in 2020. That programme produced the Dactyl robotic hand, which was designed to manipulate objects such as a Rubik’s Cube.

Business Insider reported in January that OpenAI had quietly built a robotics lab in San Francisco and was training robotic arms to perform household tasks. Those tasks included folding laundry and putting bread in a toaster. The company has reportedly been exploring ways to combine robotic systems with its AI models.

title: ​​Windows PCs Enter the Agentic Era with NVIDIA RTX Spark
content:
NVIDIA and Microsoft have introduced a new category of Windows PCs powered by the RTX Spark superchip.

The RTX Spark integrates CPU, GPU, and memory for enhanced AI processing and everyday computing.

Microsoft and NVIDIA on May 31 announced a new category of Windows PCs powered by NVIDIA’s RTX Spark superchip, bringing AI processing directly onto personal computers.

The announcement was made during NVIDIA GTC Taipei and is positioned around running AI agents and large AI models locally on Windows devices.

The companies said RTX Spark integrates CPU, GPU and memory into a single architecture built for AI workloads, graphics processing and everyday computing.

“Builders and creators today are reimagining how things get done, and they need reimagined hardware, silicon and platform capabilities to support them,” said Microsoft in a statement. “They need PCs capable of running graphically intensive tasks efficiently, highly capable AI models, and a platform that simply and securely runs agents locally.”

According to the company, future Windows experiences powered by RTX Spark will be accessible through the Windows interface and taskbar.

NVIDIA’s RTX Spark superchip delivers up to one petaflop of AI performance. The platform combines NVIDIA’s Blackwell RTX architecture with Arm-based CPU cores and up to 128 GB of unified memory, enabling AI workloads to run directly on Windows devices.

NVIDIA partnered with MediaTek to develop the Arm-based CPU that powers RTX Spark.

NVIDIA is also bringing its OpenShell framework to Windows, built on new security and containment capabilities introduced by Microsoft. OpenShell is NVIDIA’s framework for connecting AI agents with applications and system tools.

The companies said AI agents such as Hermes Agent and OpenClaw will run on Windows using OpenShell, allowing users to perform tasks locally instead of relying on cloud services.

Microsoft said users will retain control over how AI agents operate on Windows, with tools that provide visibility into what data and system resources agents can access.

The first RTX Spark-powered Windows devices are expected to arrive this fall, including laptops and compact desktop PCs from Microsoft Surface, ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo and MSI.

The launch deepens NVIDIA's push into the Windows PC market, where Intel, AMD and Qualcomm have traditionally supplied processors. Reuters reported in 2023 that NVIDIA was developing Arm-based chips for Windows devices, a move that is now materialising with RTX Spark.

content:

PwC India and Leah have expanded their partnership to enhance enterprise AI adoption through agentic AI systems.

The collaboration aims to move organisations from task-level automation to hybrid human-AI operating models.

PwC India announced on 28 May an extension of its strategic partnership with Leah to help enterprises execute large-scale AI-led business transformations using agentic AI systems.

The collaboration combines PwC India’s industry, transformation and technology consulting capabilities with Leah’s Agentic OS platform, which is designed to orchestrate, run and govern AI agents across enterprise environments.

The companies said the partnership aims to help organisations move beyond task-level automation toward operating models powered by hybrid human-AI workforces.

According to the firms, the alliance will focus on enabling enterprises to deploy vertically trained AI agents tailored to specific industries, business functions and operational workflows.

The partnership will also support enterprise-grade governance, explainability, auditability and secure deployment options, including on-premises environments.

Manpreet Singh Ahuja, Partner and Chief Clients and Industries Officer at PwC India, said that as the industry moves from experimentation to scaled deployments, the enterprise AI advantage will come from scaled agentic operations and vertically trained agents, finely tuned to contextual and process nuances.

“Our alliance with Leah helps clients to not only embed Agentic AI in their functional activities but also leverage domain-specific AI with enterprise orchestration, governance, and secure deployment options, including on-premises environments,” he said.

Ajuha further noted that PwC can help clients across finance, HR, and supply chain processes, and, with tailored agents, they are helping organisations drive accelerated value with agentic AI across their operations.

Meanwhile, Leah said its Agentic OS platform is designed to address enterprise challenges around rapid value realisation by enabling orchestration across systems, workflows and data while supporting governance requirements such as traceability, auditability and human oversight.

Sarvarth Misra, CEO and Co-founder of Leah, said, “The enterprise AI advantage won't come from bolting AI onto existing solutions — it will come from AI-native platforms that combine with agentic architecture.”

The alliance will also focus on integrating agentic workflows into existing ERP, procurement, finance, and enterprise platforms rather than building standalone systems.

The announcement comes as enterprises increasingly look to operationalise AI beyond pilots and experimentation, with a growing focus on governance, orchestration, and the scalable deployment of AI agents across core business functions.

title: AI Infrastructure and Sovereignty Imperative: Why the Stakes Have Never Been Higher
content:
DuckDuckGo says users are increasingly turning to its AI-free search options and privacy-centric browsing experience.

What Actually Matters.

DuckDuckGo is experiencing a significant increase in app installs and user traffic amid criticism of Google's AI-driven search changes.

Concerns over Google's AI features include inaccurate responses and reduced website visibility, prompting users to seek alternatives.

Privacy-focused search engine DuckDuckGo is seeing a surge in app installs and user traffic amid growing criticism of Google’s latest AI-powered Search overhaul.

The backlash began after Google announced major updates to its Search platform during its annual developer conference, Google I/O, where the company expanded AI-generated search summaries, conversational AI features and its new ‘AI Mode.’ The update allows users to ask follow-up questions directly within Search instead of browsing traditional web links.

While Google described the move as the future of online search, many users raised concerns over inaccurate AI-generated responses, reduced visibility for websites and the inability to fully opt out of AI-powered features.

According to DuckDuckGo, app installs in the United States increased by an average of 18.1% week over week between May 20 and May 25, peaking at 30.5% on May 25. On iOS devices, installs reportedly grew by an average of 33%.

Gabriel Weinberg, CEO of DuckDuckGo, said “Google is force-feeding AI with no way to opt out,” reacting to Google’s Search changes.

“As a result, their results are getting worse, not better. We want to be the place that puts users in charge and allows them to decide how much or how little AI they want,” he added.

The company also reported increased traffic to its AI-free search page, which disables AI-generated summaries and AI-created images by default.

Third-party analytics firm Apptopia also found that DuckDuckGo’s average daily downloads in the US rose by 29% during the same period.

While DuckDuckGo positions itself as an alternative to search engines that rely heavily on AI, it still provides access to optional AI features via its Duck.ai platform, though it maintains a strong focus on protecting user privacy.

“Not only do we respect user choice, but also user privacy. We don’t collect search histories or chats, and nothing is used for AI training,” Weinberg said.

title: OpenAI Codex Usage in India Jumps 27x in 2026
content:
India is now among the top five countries globally for Codex adoption and among the top ten for engagement.

What Actually Matters.

India has seen a significant increase in OpenAI Codex usage, with a 27-fold rise in weekly active users since early 2026.

The country is now ranked among the top five globally for Codex adoption and in the top ten for user engagement.

OpenAI reported that weekly active Codex users in India increased 27-fold since early 2026, with daily interactions over 20-fold by late April, based on data shared at Mumbai Tech Week.

The company said India is now among the top five countries globally for Codex adoption and among the top ten for engagement. The figures add to earlier OpenAI data, indicating that India is one of its most active markets for advanced AI usage.

OpenAI said usage is expanding beyond software development. More than 25% of Codex requests in India are now for non-coding tasks, including information synthesis, document drafting, research automation, workflow organisation, and communication-related work.

The company linked the growth to broader adoption among founders, researchers, students, operators, and business teams. “Adoption is not just happening among software engineers,” said Thomas Jeng, Head of Startups for APAC at OpenAI.

He added that users are increasingly employing Codex to “turn ideas into working outcomes faster” and to move “from intent to execution across almost all aspects of work.”

India's growing use of Codex is also being supported by a broader builder ecosystem and enterprise deployments.

OpenAI said it has previously announced Codex-related collaborations with Indian companies, including Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, and Razorpay, across software engineering and enterprise workflow applications.

In February, OpenAI's ‘Signals’ reportidentified India as the fastest-growing market for Codex, with usage for coding tasks running at roughly three times the global average. The company also said coding activity was concentrated in major technology hubs, with Telangana ranking first, followed by Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

OpenAI has continued to expand Codex beyond its original coding focus in recent months. The company recently added mobile access via the ChatGPT app, introduced new workflow features such as Goal Mode and richer context handling, and rolled out GPT-5.5 as the latest recommended model for coding, research, and knowledge work tasks.

OpenAI has also reported rapid global growth for the product, with more than 4 million developers using Codex weekly as of April.

title: Airbus, BMW Partner with Mistral AI as Europe Pushes for AI Independence
content:
The partnerships highlight Europe’s push to build trusted AI US alternatives for aerospace, defence and automotive industries.

What Actually Matters.

Airbus and BMW are partnering with Mistral AI to develop trusted AI alternatives in aerospace and automotive sectors.

The collaborations aim to enhance AI applications in aviation, defence, and vehicle development, focusing on security and reliability.

European aerospace giant Airbus and German automaker BMW have announced separate partnerships with French startup Mistral AI as European companies increasingly look for alternatives to US-based AI providers.

According to a joint statement released on May 28, Airbus will collaborate with Mistral AI to expand the use of AI across its aviation, defence and space businesses. The partnership will allow Airbus to access Mistral AI’s products and research teams to develop custom AI systems for aerospace operations.

The companies said the collaboration would focus on “trusted” and “secure” AI systems, especially for sensitive defence and aerospace applications.

Catherine Jestin, Executive Vice President Digital at Airbus, said, “This partnership paves the way for the deployment of high-impact, high-value use cases of trusted and responsible AI in aerospace.”

Airbus and Mistral AI plan to work on AI-powered engineering simulations, onboard AI systems for aircraft and spacecraft, automated technical documentation and edge AI systems capable of running directly on hardware to support flight safety and object recognition.

The partnership will also explore defence-related applications such as cyber investigations and coding support in highly secure environments.

“Together, we will deploy Mistral’s fully integrated AI stack to accelerate innovation, contribute to improving flight safety, and deliver greater value for customers,” noted Timothée Lacroix, Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of Mistral AI.

The announcement comes as European companies and institutions grow increasingly concerned about their dependence on US-based AI firms such as OpenAI and Anthropic, particularly over data sovereignty and security risks.

On the same day, BMW announced a separate partnership with Mistral AI focused on improving crash simulations and vehicle development through AI.

Dr Franz Decker, CIO and Senior Vice President of the BMW Group, said, “For the BMW Group, the use of industrial data is a key factor in translating artificial intelligence into value creation.” He added that by combining their engineering datasets with Mistral AI’s model training capabilities, the company is building specialised AI which supports complex development tasks.

The automaker noted that it currently conducts thousands of virtual crash tests every week and has accumulated more than one petabyte of historical simulation data over the years.

The collaboration comes as global automakers increasingly adopt AI across manufacturing, autonomous driving research, safety systems and vehicle development to reduce costs and accelerate production cycles.

title: Sarvam AI Begins Hiring for New San Francisco Office
content:
The hiring drive comes amid reports that Sarvam is in talks to raise up to $300 million at a valuation of up to $1.5 billion.

What Actually Matters.

Sarvam AI is expanding its presence in the US with a new office in San Francisco.

The company aims to recruit AI talent, primarily for research roles.

Indian AI startup Sarvam AI is gearing up for a deeper presence in the United States, with plans to establish an office in San Francisco and actively recruit AI talent from the Bay Area.

The development was revealed by Hemant Mohapatra, Partner at Lightspeed and an early backer of the company.

“Beautiful evening in SF, a wonderful housefull event with Pratyush Kumar of Sarvam AI talking about the company’s plans, hiring for an SF office, scaling out compute, building v. large models, and global GTM,” he wrote in a post on X.

A Sarvam AI engineer told AIM that the hiring push will focus largely on research roles.

The expansion comes as the Bengaluru-based startup looks to tap into global AI talent while continuing to build foundational AI models tailored for India.

Founded in 2023 by AI researchers Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar, Sarvam has positioned itself as a sovereign AI company focused on Indian languages, speech technologies, and large language models.

Sarvam has gained prominence over the past year through its government-backed efforts to build indigenous AI models and the launch of open-source large language models built for Indian use cases.

The company earlier this year introduced its 30-billion and 105-billion parameter models and launched the Indus AI chatbot, placing it in direct competition with global players such as OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic.

The hiring push comes as Sarvam is reportedly in talks to raise between $200 million and $300 million in a fresh funding round that could value the startup between $1.2 billion and $1.5 billion.

Update: This story has been updated with additional information from a Sarvam AI engineer, who said most of the planned hires in San Francisco will be for research roles.

title: CHiPS Deploys Salesforce MuleSoft for Chhattisgarh’s Digital Dwaar Platform
content:
CHiPS plans to expand API integrations across state departments and applications, strengthen governance and security frameworks.

What Actually Matters.

CHiPS has implemented Salesforce MuleSoft to enhance the Digital Dwaar platform for data sharing among government departments.

The platform aims to replace time-consuming manual data processes with efficient API-based access to information.

The Chhattisgarh Infotech Promotion Society (CHiPS) has partnered with Salesforce to deploy MuleSoft as the technology backbone of Digital Dwaar, the state's API-based data exchange platform designed to enable data sharing across government departments.

Digital Dwaar serves as a centralised platform where government departments can publish and consume data services through a single API framework.

According to CHiPS, the system replaces manual data coordination processes that previously took days or weeks with API-based access to information. The implementation was carried out by Salesforce consulting partner Watsoo.

Arundhati Bhattacharya, President and CEO of Salesforce South Asia, said state governments are making infrastructure decisions that will influence public service delivery for years. “Our partnership with Chhattisgarh highlights this transformation, and we are committed to helping India develop the digital and AI foundations required for population-scale impact,” she said.

The platform is intended to address challenges arising from fragmented government systems and manual data exchange processes. CHiPS said the API-led integration strategy provides centralised visibility and control over data flows while enabling real-time data availability, standardised integration frameworks, and monitoring capabilities across departments.

The agency said the deployment has reduced manual data exchange processes and integration timelines while improving service delivery and decision-making through faster access to data. It added that centralised monitoring has strengthened data security and compliance.

“Digital Dwaar represents a foundational shift in how we think about data and service delivery,” said Shri Prabhat Malik, IAS, CEO of CHiPS. “With MuleSoft, we’ve moved from isolated systems to a connected ecosystem where data flows securely, instantly, and at scale across all departments.”

Malik said the platform would serve as the foundation for future digital governance initiatives in the state and support the next phase of citizen service delivery.

CHiPS plans to expand API integrations across state departments and applications, strengthen governance and security frameworks, and use the platform’s data layer for analytics and policy insights. The roadmap also includes support for AI-enabled public services.

title: Anthropic Surpasses OpenAI With $965 Bn Valuation, Launches Claude Opus 4.8
content:
Anthropic reported that its annualised revenue run rate crossed $47 billion.

What Actually Matters.

Anthropic has achieved a valuation of $965 billion, surpassing OpenAI's valuation.

The company raised $65 billion in a Series H funding round to enhance research and infrastructure.

Anthropic has raised $65 billion in a Series H funding round, valuing the AI company at $965 billion post-money. The company also launched Claude Opus 4.8, the latest version of its flagship AI model.

Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital led the funding round. Anthropic said the capital will be used to advance safety and interpretability research, expand compute infrastructure, and scale products and partnerships as demand for Claude continues to grow.

The funding round makes Anthropic the world’s most valuable AI startup, surpassing OpenAI’s most recent valuation of $852 billion. The AI company raised $122 billion in March.

The announcement comes as Anthropic reported that its annualised revenue run rate crossed $47 billion earlier this month, driven by increasing enterprise adoption of Claude.

“Claude is increasingly indispensable to our growing global community of customers, and we work tirelessly to make tools like Claude Code and Cowork more helpful, more powerful, and more adaptable to their needs,” said Krishna Rao, Chief Financial Officer of Anthropic.

“This funding will help us serve the historic demand we are experiencing, stay at the research frontier, and bring Claude to more of the places where work happens,” Rao added.

The round also included $15 billion in previously committed investments from hyperscalers, including $5 billion from Amazon.

Anthropic said strategic infrastructure partners Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix also joined the round. The company said these partnerships would help support future compute requirements as demand for Claude grows.

The company added that it has recently expanded compute capacity through agreements with Amazon for up to five gigawatts of new infrastructure, and with Google and Broadcom for five gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity.

Anthropic also secured access to GPU capacity in SpaceX’s Colossus 1 and Colossus 2 systems.

Opus 4.8 With Improved Coding, Agentic Capabilities

Anthropic said Claude Opus 4.8 improves performance across coding, reasoning, agentic tasks and practical knowledge work benchmarks while maintaining the same pricing as Opus 4.7.

The model tops benchmarks like 69.2% on SWE-Bench Pro and 74.6% on Agentic Terminal Coding, beating rivals including OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 and Google’s Gemini 3.1 Pro.

“Early testers have found Claude Opus 4.8 to be more reliable and sharper in its judgement when it’s performing agentic tasks,” Anthropic said.

Pricing remains unchanged at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens for regular usage. Fast mode pricing is set at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.

Claude Opus 4.8 is available through claude.ai and the Claude API under the model name claude-opus-4-8.

The company also launched dynamic workflows for Claude Code in research preview. The feature enables Claude to plan tasks and run hundreds of parallel subagents within a single session, allowing it to execute large-scale code migrations and verify outputs before delivering results.

Anthropic further introduced effort controls on claude.ai and Cowork, giving users the ability to adjust how much compute the model uses for a task. Higher effort settings provide deeper reasoning and longer processing, while lower settings prioritise speed and lower rate-limit consumption.

According to the company, Opus 4.8 is around four times less likely than Opus 4.7 to leave flaws in generated code unreported.

“One of the most prominent improvements in Opus 4.8 is its honesty,” Anthropic said. “Opus 4.8 is more likely to flag uncertainties about its work and less likely to make unsupported claims.”

Besides that, Anthropic said it plans to make Mythos-class models more widely available after introducing additional cybersecurity safeguards.

The company also updated its Messages API, allowing developers to insert system entries directly into message arrays to modify instructions during a task without interrupting prompt caching.

title: Google Partners with Polaris School of Technology to Launch AI and Cloud-Focused Degree Programme
content:
Google collaborates with Bengaluru's Polaris School of Technology to integrate certified pathways, AI tools, and multi-million-rupee credits into a new degree.

What Actually Matters.

Google partners with Polaris School of Technology to create a four-year Computer Science degree programme in India.

The programme integrates Google-certified cloud and big data learning pathways to bridge the gap between academia and industry needs.

On 28 May, Google announced a strategic partnership with the Bengaluru-based Polaris School of Technology to co-create one of India’s first four-year Computer Science programmes, built around Google-certified cloud and big data learning pathways.

The collaboration aims to address the widening gap between traditional academic education and real-world industry requirements by integrating Google’s cloud infrastructure, artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem, and professional certifications directly into the undergraduate curriculum.

As part of the newly launched initiative, Polaris will introduce a specialised track in Cloud & Big Data. This curriculum has been co-created with input from academia and industry, aligned with Google's standards.

To ensure practical relevance, Google engineers and partner faculty will directly deliver portions of the programme through dedicated academic modules and semester-long projects. Students will gain first-hand exposure to production-grade cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, AI-native workflows, and large-scale data environments.

Beyond curriculum integration, students enrolled in the programme will receive access to cutting-edge AI stacks, including Gemini and Google Cloud tools. The partnership also includes Google certification pathways valued at up to ₹10 lakh. Furthermore, Polaris will provide up to ₹25 lakh in Google Cloud credits for selected student founders and technical projects, enabling them to build prototypes on the same infrastructure stack used by global startups and enterprises.

“The gap between computer science education and the realities of modern software has become too large to ignore. This collaboration is about bringing students closer to the systems, tools and standards that define global technology today,” Mukul Rustagi, CEO of Polaris School of Technology, said. “We want students to graduate not just with theoretical knowledge, but with meaningful exposure to the environments where the world’s most important technology is actually built.”

The agreement also extends beyond the classroom, offering students access to Google’s broader developer ecosystem. Undergraduates will be able to attend official technical events and developer conferences, providing networking opportunities from the earliest stages of their careers.

Navisha Prabhakar, Regional Lead, Google for Education, South & West India, stated that at Polaris, they observed a leadership team ready to rethink traditional education and achieve meaningful student outcomes through technology, collaboration, and practical learning. She emphasized that the ambition and dedication to transformation aligned naturally with Google’s vision for the future of education.

The partnership is expected to further scale the institution's capacity to prepare graduates for the global tech sector.

Wipro is enhancing its partnership with ServiceNow to facilitate agentic AI workflows across various business functions.

The integration aims to automate processes in IT, HR, procurement, and cybersecurity, improving operational efficiency.

IT services firm Wipro has expanded its partnership with ServiceNow to help enterprises deploy agentic AI workflows across key business functions, including IT, human resources, procurement and cybersecurity, as technology services firms sharpen their focus on enterprise AI adoption.

Under the expanded collaboration, the Bengaluru-headquartered company will integrate its Wipro Intelligence suite of AI platforms and solutions with the ServiceNow AI Platform, according to a statement on May 28.

The partnership aims to streamline how enterprises initiate, manage and execute workflows across internal systems by reducing manual coordination and improving operational visibility.

The move comes at a time when large IT services firms are increasingly positioning themselves as implementation and orchestration partners for enterprise AI adoption, particularly around agentic AI systems that can independently manage and execute business processes with limited human intervention.

As part of the collaboration, Wipro said some of its existing offerings, including SmartProcure, Telco Autonomous Networks and Cyber Transform, will leverage ServiceNow’s AI platform capabilities. The company said these solutions are designed to improve procurement workflows, telecom service operations, and cybersecurity incident response and governance.

“AI isn’t new to enterprises, but connected, governed, and outcome-driven AI is,” Amit Zavery, President, Chief Operating Officer, and Chief Product Officer at ServiceNow, said in a statement. “That’s what this partnership makes real. When agentic AI runs inside secure workflows, ideas start delivering real results and the agentic enterprise becomes possible.”

Meanwhile, Malay Joshi, Chief Executive Officer of Wipro’s Americas 1 Strategic Market Unit, said enterprises often struggle with executing AI deployments at scale despite growing interest in the technology.

“For most enterprises, the real challenge with AI is not ambition, but execution at scale. Our expanded partnership with ServiceNow is designed to bridge that gap through a consulting-led, AI-powered approach that translates business priorities into industry-aligned AI solutions,” Joshi noted.

The companies said the partnership would provide enterprises with a unified interface for managing work requests across departments, while embedding governance, auditability and operational tracking into workflows.

The announcement adds to a growing list of partnerships between IT services providers and enterprise software companies aimed at monetising demand for generative and agentic AI deployments across industries.

title: OpenAI Commits $250 Million to Prepare Economies for AI-Driven Job Disruption
content:
The funding will support research, labour-transition programmes, and economic policy experiments focused on managing the long-term effects of advanced AI systems on jobs, wages, and wealth distribution.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI is allocating $250 million to address economic disruption caused by AI advancements.

The initiative will support research and programmes aimed at managing labour transitions and economic policy.

OpenAI said its nonprofit arm, the OpenAI Foundation, will commit an initial $250 million towards research, grants, pilot programmes, and partnerships focused on managing AI-driven economic disruption and labour-market changes.

The initiative will focus on measuring AI’s economic effects, supporting workers during transitions, and developing long-term economic security systems.

The AI company said the funding will support organisations through grants and institutional partnerships, while the Foundation also builds internal research and policy programmes.

OpenAI said existing economic systems are poorly equipped to measure how AI-generated value will be distributed if gains shift away from wages and towards digital goods, lower-cost services, or capital owners. “A central question is not only what AI can do, but where that value accrues,” the company said.

It wants to fund updated labour-market infrastructure similar to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics and O*NET systems to better track employment shifts, wages, firm behaviour, and changing job structures as AI systems become more capable.

OpenAI also said current automation studies often fail to capture how firms reorganise work or how AI may create labour-complementary roles alongside displacement.

A part of the initiative will focus on low and middle-income countries, where the company believes AI could expand access to expertise, public services, and economic mobility. It is also set to focus on region-specific infrastructure and local deployment models rather than standardised global approaches.

The company, which is preparing to go public, also said it may fund experiments involving access to unemployment insurance, wage-loss insurance, job-transition assistance, and worker retraining programmes, while acknowledging that traditional retraining efforts have produced mixed results.

OpenAI’s proposal also includes research into sovereign wealth funds, taxation tied to capital and economic rents, windfall-profit systems, and adaptive fiscal policies tied to indicators such as labour-share declines or concentrated AI gains.

Another part of the initiative focuses on simulation and forecasting infrastructure. OpenAI said it wants to support “multi-agent economic simulations that use AI to model how economies might evolve as capabilities improve.”

The announcement expands the role of the OpenAI Foundation beyond its earlier focus on AI governance, education, healthcare, and democratic participation. The Foundation was introduced earlier this year as part of OpenAI’s broader public-interest initiatives, separate from its commercial operations.

Other frontier AI companies have also increased work around economic forecasting and public-sector planning tied to AI deployment.

Anthropic has expanded research into labour-market effects and governance frameworks for advanced AI systems, while Google DeepMind has increased work on AI-enabled economic modelling and simulation systems.

title: OpenAI’s New Tax AI Tool Processed 7,000 Returns With ‘Up to 97% Accuracy’
content:
Co-developed with Thrive Holdings, the Codex-powered tool uses a three-step loop to continuously improve tax-preparation workflows.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI and Thrive Holdings developed a self-improving AI tool for tax preparation, tested across over 30 accounting firms.

The Tax AI system significantly reduced accountants' preparation time and improved overall throughput.

OpenAI and Thrive Holdings have co-developed a self-improving AI system for tax preparation that was piloted across Crete’s network of more than 30 accounting firms during the recent U.S. tax season.

The system, called Tax AI, processed around 7,000 tax returns and was designed to automate document extraction, field mapping, and portions of tax return preparation while keeping human accountants in the review loop.

According to OpenAI, the system reduced the time accountants spent on tax preparation by roughly one-third and increased overall throughput by about 50%.

Rather than operating as a fully autonomous filing system, Tax AI functions as a bounded automation layer. Human practitioners continue to review and approve final returns, while ambiguous cases are routed back to product and engineering teams.

The companies built the system on top of OpenAI’s Codex model using a three-part improvement loop in which practitioner corrections are captured as structured feedback, repeated failures are converted into evaluation datasets, and Codex is used to investigate issues, propose fixes, and validate improvements against regression tests before deployment.

OpenAI says the system “drafts returns with up to 97% accuracy,” though the blog’s primary benchmark focuses on “correct field completion” rates rather than a single aggregate accuracy metric.

When Tax AI was first deployed, only about a quarter of returns were completed with at least 75% of fields filled correctly before human review.

Within six weeks, that figure rose to 86%. The company also said nearly 60% of returns were at least 90% complete before correction, while around 9.5% required no field-level corrections.

Initially focused on simpler W-2 and 1099 workflows, the system later expanded into more complex filings involving K-1 forms, rental real estate schedules, and multi-document reconciliation tasks.

The broader significance of the project lies less in tax software itself and more in the engineering framework behind it. OpenAI and Thrive describe Tax AI as a model for building “self-improving agents” that learn from production feedback through structured evaluation pipelines and agent-assisted software iteration.

The companies say they are now applying the same architecture to bookkeeping, auditing, and operational workflows, such as IT help desk automation.

The deployment is part of a broader partnership announced earlier this year in which OpenAI took an equity stake in Thrive Holdings, aiming to modernise industries that still rely heavily on legacy operational systems.

title: Cognizant, Travelport Partner With Anthropic To Build AI-Powered Travel Infrastructure
content:
The collaboration aims to bridge the gap between AI-powered travel planning tools and legacy booking systems that still rely heavily on manual workflows and human agents.

What Actually Matters.

Cognizant partners with Travelport and Anthropic to enhance travel technology through AI.

The collaboration aims to modernise legacy booking systems and automate manual tasks currently managed by human agents.

Cognizant has announced a strategic collaboration with Travelport and Anthropic to modernise travel technology infrastructure using AI.

The partnership will see Cognizant deploy Anthropic’s Claude models across Travelport’s travel retailing and distribution platforms to improve how software is built, tested and maintained. The companies said the collaboration aims to bridge the growing gap between AI-powered travel planning tools and traditional booking systems that often struggle to process complex traveller requests.

According to the companies, the move is expected to help airlines, hoteliers, travel management companies and online travel agencies automate several manual tasks currently handled by human agents. These include itinerary management, ticket exchanges, refunds, rebookings and disruption handling.

“The travel industry runs on some of the most complex technology infrastructure in the world. This collaboration is about giving Travelport the tools to move faster and deliver higher quality at scale to meet the challenge of a changing travel distribution landscape,” said Ravi Kumar S, CEO at Cognizant.

John Mangelaars, CEO of Travelport, said AI is already reshaping the future of the travel sector. He added that collaborating with Cognizant and Anthropic gives them a genuine AI superpower.

The companies said the initiative will initially focus on Travelport Trip Services, the platform responsible for bookings, exchanges and servicing operations. The system will also use Anthropic’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) which allows AI agents to interact directly with external systems and live travel data.

“Claude’s large-context reasoning abilities make it suitable for handling 'large, complex codebases' common in travel infrastructure systems”, added Rich O’Connell, Head of Alliances, Anthropic.

Cognizant stated that Claude will also power AI-assisted software development, automated test creation and pull-request reviews through its Neuro AI multi-agent accelerator platform. The company expects these capabilities to significantly reduce Travelport’s software delivery cycle times.

title: TCS Partners Mistral to Build Custom Enterprise AI Models at Scale
content:
TCS has partnered French AI startup Mistral to help enterprises build custom AI models using proprietary data.

What Actually Matters.

TCS has partnered with Mistral to enhance custom AI model development for enterprises.

The collaboration aims to address concerns around data sovereignty and regulatory compliance in AI deployment.

TCS has partnered with French AI startup Mistral to jointly build and deploy custom AI systems for enterprises, as India’s largest IT services company sharpens its focus on large-scale enterprise AI adoption.

As part of the partnership, TCS will become the first global systems integrator (GSI) partner for Mistral Forge, the French company’s enterprise AI platform that allows organisations to build and fine tune domain-specific AI models using their own proprietary data and enterprise knowledge.

The companies said the collaboration will focus on helping enterprises and governments design AI systems with greater control, governance and regulatory alignment, amid rising concerns around data sovereignty and AI deployment risks.

“This partnership expands TCS’ AI ecosystem, uniquely positioning TCS to create a differentiated solution proposition for our clients. Together with Mistral, we will solve for specific industry challenges, regulatory requirements, and sovereign needs for our enterprise customers,” said K Krithivasan, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director at TCS.

The partnership will initially target sectors such as banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), manufacturing, healthcare and the public sector. TCS said it will leverage Mistral Forge to develop custom AI models tailored to enterprise workflows and operational requirements across regions including North America, Europe, the UK and Asia-Pacific.

The move comes as global IT services firms race to deepen partnerships with AI model makers and hyperscalers to strengthen their enterprise AI offerings. Indian IT firms including TCS, Infosys, Wipro and HCLTech have increasingly tied up with AI ecosystem players as enterprises move from pilot projects to production-scale deployments.

TCS will also set up a dedicated Centre of Excellence for Mistral to drive joint innovation, industry-specific AI solutions and project delivery capabilities. The centre will additionally provide early access to Mistral’s beta models and support training and governance capabilities around AI deployment.

“TCS’ global scale and contextual industry knowledge make them an ideal partner for Mistral,” said Arthur Mensch, CEO and Co-founder at Mistral.

He added that the companies will enable enterprises to move from experimentation to AI deployment with systems that are open, production-ready and aligned with their strategic and operational requirements.

Mistral has emerged as one of Europe’s most prominent AI startups, positioning itself as an alternative to US-based AI companies through its open-source and enterprise-focused AI models.

title: Devin Maker Cognition Raises $1 Bn at $26 Bn Valuation as Adoption Grows
content:
The company said its annualised revenue run rate has reached $492 million.

What Actually Matters.

Cognition secured over $1 billion in funding, achieving a valuation of $26 billion.

The startup's annualised revenue run rate has reached $492 million, reflecting significant growth.

AI coding startup Cognition has raised more than $1 billion in a funding round that values the company at $26 billion, the company announced on May 27.

The round was led by Lux Capital, General Catalyst, and 8VC, with support from existing investors including Founders Fund and Elad Gil, alongside new investors Ribbit Capital, Atreides, and Layer Global.

The company said its annualised revenue run rate has reached $492 million, while enterprise usage has grown more than tenfold since the beginning of the year.

Cognition launched Devin two years ago as what it described as the first AI software engineer. Since then, the company said cloud-based AI agents have moved from niche adoption to mainstream software development workflows.

“As we’ve scaled, Cognition has become a trusted partner for the world’s largest and most impactful organisations,” the company said in a statement.

Cognition said enterprises, including Citi, Mercedes-Benz, Goldman Sachs, Elevance, Dell, Santander, the U.S. Army, and the US Navy, are using Devin. The company added that startups such as Exa, Modal, Eight Sleep, and OpenRouter have also adopted the platform to automate parts of software development.

The company highlighted several customer deployments. Mercedes-Benz reduced an eight-month legacy modernisation project to eight days using Devin, according to Cognition.

Itaú, Latin America’s largest bank, now fixes 70% of security vulnerabilities automatically with Devin, the company said. Cognition also said Infosys and Cognizant have integrated Devin into software delivery workflows.

Cognition described itself as an “independent agent lab” that works with multiple foundation model providers. The company said engineering teams are increasingly focused on balancing cost and performance as AI token usage rises across the industry.

“Teams today care more than ever about the ratio of price to performance, which requires using the right model for the right task,” the company said.

Earlier this year, Cognition expanded its model training efforts and launched SWE-1.6, a model that it said is now the most-used model in Windsurf. The company said customers have adopted the model for its speed and cost efficiency, with performance reaching up to 950 tokens per second.

Cognition said software development is shifting toward ‘self-driving’ workflows where engineers focus more on structuring problems while AI agents execute tasks. The company added that 89% of code committed by engineers internally is now committed by Devin, with the remaining code generated by local agents in Windsurf.

Organisations can find more vulnerabilities than ever before, but the sheer volume forces them to fix their fundamentals first.

What Actually Matters.

Organisations are discovering more vulnerabilities, but the volume is overwhelming security teams.

Mozilla experienced a significant increase in security bug fixes after deploying Mythos.

Anthropic’s preview of Mythos now features a scoreboard showcasing the real-world achievements of companies involved in Project Glasswing, which have spent several weeks working with the model.

The data emerging from these early deployments paints a startling picture of a security landscape that has been completely accelerated by automation.

Mozilla revealed that before deploying Anthropic’s Mythos, Firefox typically fixed around 20–30 security bugs per month. After introducing the model in early 2026, the number of fixes rose to 76 in March and 423 in April, with 271 of those vulnerabilities directly linked to Mythos-assisted discovery.

It helped the company find numerous critical issues and exposed historical legacy bugs, including a 15-year-old flaw in an HTML element and a 20-year-old XSLT vulnerability.

Staying on top of this unprecedented volume of bugs “led to a lot of work and long days over the last few months,” Mozilla noted, adding that over 100 people contributed code to this effort to ship the most secure Firefox yet.

The company also said it felt a sense of ‘vertigo’ when the findings first came into focus. “For a hardened target, just one such bug would have been red-alert in 2025, and so many at once makes you stop to wonder whether it’s even possible to keep up,” wrote Mozilla in a blog post. It expects many more companies defending bugs to feel the same way.

Besides Mozilla, the UK’s AI Security Institute (AISI) reported that Mythos is the first model to solve both of its highly complex cyber ranges.

A newer checkpoint of the model successfully navigated “The Last Ones” (a 32-step simulated corporate network attack) in 6 out of 10 attempts, and became the first ever to crack the previously unsolved “Cooling Tower” range, succeeding in 3 out of 10 runs.

Palo Alto Networks said that after scanning 130+ products, including models such as Claude Mythos and GPT-5.5-Cyber, it patched 26 Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) covering 75 issues—far above its usual monthly volume of fewer than 5 CVEs.

In Anthropic’s testing across 1,000 open-source projects, Mythos found 6,202 high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities and 23,019 total bugs.

The Talent Paradox & The Fallacy of Patching Faster

John Scimone, the Chief Security Officer of Dell Technologies, told AIM that the industry’s longstanding talent shortage is being offset by models like Mythos, which accelerate vulnerability discovery.

“As somebody who's built and led cybersecurity teams for decades, the number one challenge I've had, regardless of whether it has been attracting, recruiting, and retaining qualified talent,” says Scimone.

He argues AI is a force multiplier despite the surge in discovered vulnerabilities that may increase the workload on humans.

“Potentially you need more people to then understand the issues [found by the model] and resolve them — but when you look at the big picture, the net result is that you can produce cybersecurity outcomes far more efficiently with less dependency on that expert labour, which can produce far greater scale and impact.”

Scimone advocates fighting fire with fire and believes that any human-expert challenge can also be solved through extended use by the models themselves, pointing to the high percentage of code generated by AI coding models.

Besides suggesting that Mythos will change how human experts work, it also raises the need to fundamentally rewire how human experts have worked and built their workflows.

In an interaction with AIM, Keshava Murthy, co-founder and CEO of Matters.ai, an AI security firm, says there needs to be a fundamentally different approach to building patching workflows and that companies cannot hire their way out of the problem.

“When a vulnerability can be turned into a working exploit in under three days, traditional cycles of scanning, scoring, scheduling, and patching consume time enterprises simply do not have,” says Murthy. “Even well-resourced teams cannot sprint on every finding simultaneously, forcing them to make difficult choices about what to fix first.”

Similarly, Cloudflare shared how the instinct to simply “patch faster” became a dangerous trap in their experience with Mythos.

While the model excelled at complex exploit chain construction and automated proof generation, Cloudflare warned that compressing the response cycle to meet extreme SLAs, like two hours from disclosure to patch, inevitably requires skipping critical regression testing.

“The bugs you ship when you skip regression testing tend to be worse than the bugs you were trying to patch,” the company noted in its blog post.

Cloudflare found that pointing a generic coding agent at a repository fails; instead, deploying a specialised, multi-stage “harness” in which multiple AI agents work within narrow scopes and cross-validate findings drastically reduced triage noise.

Rather than chasing every alert across the board, Murthy adds that companies should reassess their standard severity scores, as many lack business context.

“A critical CVE in an isolated system holding no sensitive data is practically less urgent than a medium CVE in a core system processing healthcare data,” says Murthy. “By routing incoming vulnerability signals through a real-time map of where sensitive data actually lives, it automatically prioritises the alerts that pose a genuine business risk.”

He adds that it isn’t about patching faster across the board, but about being ‘ruthlessly’ accurate about which ten things actually matter right now, and securing those before the window closes.

Ultimately, organisations must shift toward application-level architectural changes that block exploit paths by default, making exploitation harder even when vulnerabilities remain unpatched.

Mythos Unmarks the True Cost of Tech Debt

Besides the human bottleneck that Mythos may introduce, Mozilla also stated that it helped fix legacy bugs on its platform.

“The emergence of Mythos changes the tech debt conversation completely,” tells Vrajesh Bhavsar, CEO of Operant AI, a runtime cybersecurity platform for agentic AI systems, in an interaction with AIM.

For decades, enterprises assumed that if a legacy bug survived years of audits, it was hidden well enough to be safe. Bhavsar notes that Mythos destroys that assumption entirely, proving that twenty years of tech debt can be mapped and weaponised at machine speed.

Similarly, Murthy argues that legacy systems were frequently reviewed by genuinely skilled people working under human constraints.

“Human reviewers face time limits and a natural tendency to trust long-running, stable software,” he says. “AI carries no such assumptions, reading millions of code lines with consistent attention and finding complex patterns across subsystems that individual reviewers might miss.”

For many enterprises, the legacy risk profile is much higher than assumed, states Murthy, and the decision to leave older systems alone usually rests on the belief that they are stable.

“Enterprises must determine which legacy architectures have actual, traceable routes to sensitive data through APIs or shared credentials,” he says, adding that a structural flaw in an authentication layer safeguarding customer records is regarded as a different category of problem compared to the same flaw in an isolated reporting tool. Securing technical debt requires treating it as a tiered risk based solely on what each system can access.

The Move to Runtime Defence

The fundamental issue, Bhavsar warns, is that traditional ‘identify and patch’ playbooks completely break down against these new models.

“Every security tool most organisations rely on was built before emergent behaviour was a proven threat,” he explains. “They were designed to catch known threats, moving at human speed, exploiting anticipated weaknesses.”

Because AI capabilities now rely on organic learning rather than explicit programming, the threat landscape has fundamentally shifted. “Emergent behaviour is none of those things, it is unexpected, it operates at machine speed, and by definition it has not been seen before,” Bhavsar points out.

Instead of treating foundational tech debt as a slow-burning risk for a future roadmap, Bhavsar states that companies must accept it as an immediate, active exposure.

Cloudflare also found that Mythos exhibited inconsistent organic refusals, where equivalent exploit-generation tasks sometimes succeeded and sometimes failed depending on framing or execution context, suggesting that emergent safety behaviours alone are insufficient as a reliable security boundary.

All things considered, Mythos will now force organisations to rethink their cybersecurity infrastructure and how teams operate, both in preparing to fix bugs it identifies and in anticipating how attackers might use models like these once they eventually land in their hands.

“The Mozilla situation makes the problem viscerally concrete, and Mozilla is one of the most technically sophisticated organisations in the world. They had the engineers, the culture, and the infrastructure. They still got overwhelmed,” says Bhavsar.

“Enterprises cannot hire their way out of this problem,” he says.

Bhavsar explained that for enterprises without 100 developers on standby, updating their patching cycle is not the answer. “The patching model itself is broken,” he adds. He advocates for stopping reliance on patching as the primary defence and shifting to active runtime defence, detecting and blocking anomalous AI behaviour as it occurs, not after.

“That should be a layer that does not wait for a threat to be named, catalogued, or patched, but watches behaviour as it happens and blocks anomalies the moment they emerge.”

title: Snowflake Signs $6 Bn AWS Deal to Push Enterprise Agentic AI
content:
Snowflake said the partnership will help enterprises run AI applications directly on governed data without moving sensitive information across systems.

What Actually Matters.

Snowflake has entered a $6 billion multi-year agreement with Amazon Web Services to enhance enterprise AI capabilities.

The partnership focuses on integrating AI services and improving joint market strategies through AWS Marketplace.

Snowflake announced a multi-year collaboration agreement with Amazon Web Services (AWS), including a $6 billion infrastructure commitment over five years, as the company looks to expand enterprise adoption of generative and agentic AI technologies.

The agreement will deepen product integrations between the two companies across AI services, expand joint go-to-market efforts through AWS Marketplace, and increase investments in customer success programs, workload migrations, and industry-focused AI solutions.

Snowflake said the $6 billion commitment, its largest infrastructure agreement with AWS to date, will cover Graviton compute and AI-related spending as demand for AI and data workloads continues to grow.

“AI has generated enormous excitement, but for enterprises, the real challenge and opportunity is turning intelligence into action,” said Sridhar Ramaswamy, CEO of Snowflake. “We are moving into the era of the agentic enterprise, where AI systems don’t just answer questions, but help organisations reason over trusted data, coordinate workflows, and drive real business outcomes.”

Matt Garman, CEO of AWS, said enterprises are increasingly moving beyond AI experimentation toward deploying AI agents for operational use cases.

“Snowflake has built on AWS since day one, and their deepened commitment to run on Graviton delivers the world-class performance, flexibility, and cost savings customers need to run data warehousing and AI workloads at scale,” Garman said.

Snowflake said the expanded collaboration will help enterprises run AI applications directly on governed enterprise data without moving sensitive information across systems.

The company’s Cortex AI platform enables use cases including text-to-SQL, summarisation, sentiment analysis, and entity extraction within the Snowflake environment.

The company added that Snowflake workloads on AWS use Graviton processors for compute efficiency and Amazon EC2 GPU instances for AI model training and inference.

The partnership also expands commercial collaboration through AWS Marketplace. Snowflake said it has surpassed $7 billion in lifetime AWS Marketplace sales since becoming available on the platform.

The company also crossed $2 billion in annualised marketplace sales in calendar year 2025, with transaction growth more than doubling year over year.

As part of the agreement, Snowflake and AWS will jointly work to simplify procurement and deployment of AI and data services for enterprise customers through AWS Marketplace.

Snowflake also said it is expanding its footprint on AWS infrastructure globally, with launches completed or underway in 10 new regions, including Auckland in New Zealand, Cape Town in South Africa, Bangkok in Thailand, and the AWS European Sovereign Cloud.

Several customers are already deploying AI applications using Snowflake on AWS, according to the companies.

Snowflake and AWS are expected to showcase additional details around their enterprise AI strategy at Snowflake Summit 2026.

title: Gujarat Partners With Meta for AI-Powered Citizen Services, Digital Infra
content:
The chatbot, which will be available in Gujarati and English, is designed to help citizens access 20 government services directly through WhatsApp

What Actually Matters.

Gujarat has partnered with Meta to enhance citizen services through AI and digital infrastructure.

A WhatsApp-based chatbot will facilitate access to 20 government services in Gujarati and English.

The Gujarat government has partnered with Meta to explore innovation across artificial intelligence (AI), next-generation wearable technologies, and digital infrastructure, with the aim of strengthening citizen-centric governance and inclusive digital development.

As part of the collaboration, the state government and Meta signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to launch a WhatsApp-based conversational chatbot under Gujarat’s ‘Sugam Digital’ initiative. The partnership is expected to run over a two-year period.

The chatbot, which will be available in Gujarati and English, is designed to help citizens access 20 government services directly through WhatsApp. The platform will support services including grievance redressal, income, caste and EWS certificates, ration card updates, revenue records, and official affidavits. The chatbot will also include voice capabilities to improve accessibility for users across rural and urban regions.

Speaking on the partnership, Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel said the state has consistently led the way in digital adoption, adding that the collaboration with Meta represents a major step toward building future-ready digital infrastructure. He said the state aims to leverage AI and emerging technologies to improve citizens’ lives while ensuring transparent, inclusive, and accessible digital governance.

Hareet Shukla, Principal Secretary, General Administration Department, Government of Gujarat, said the initiative is intended to make governance more accessible, efficient, and citizen-friendly. He noted that the Sugam Digital initiative on WhatsApp is designed to ensure that critical government services can be accessed directly by citizens, including those in remote areas, without requiring physical visits to government offices.

Arun Srinivas, Managing Director and Country Head at Meta, said AI and digital technologies have the potential to significantly improve citizen services, simplify access to governance, and help small businesses adopt advanced digital capabilities. He added that WhatsApp’s widespread familiarity and ease of use make it an effective platform for extending public services to even the most remote parts of the country, and said Meta is pleased to support Gujarat’s vision of creating more inclusive and accessible digital governance.
