title: GPT-5.5 Beats Claude and Gemini in New Long-Horizon Coding Benchmark
content:
DeepSWE is a new benchmark for testing real-world AI coding capabilities.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI's GPT-5.5 outperformed other AI coding models in the new DeepSWE benchmark.

DeepSWE tests AI models on original software engineering tasks, unlike traditional evaluations.

OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 has emerged as the top-performing AI coding model on DeepSWE, a new long-horizon software engineering benchmark designed to test whether frontier AI agents can independently complete realistic software development tasks from start to finish.

The benchmark places GPT-5.5 significantly ahead of competing models from Anthropic and Google, with Claude Opus 4.7 scoring 54% and Gemini 3.1 Pro managing just 10%. GPT-5.5 achieved the highest score overall at 70%, followed by GPT-5.4 at 56%.

DeepSWE is developed by researchers from Datacurve Co-Founder Charley Lee, CEO Serena Ge, and Founding Engineers Wenqi Huang and Leonard Tng. It evaluates AI models on original software engineering tasks written entirely from scratch.

Unlike traditional coding evaluations that focus on isolated bug fixes or pre-existing GitHub pull requests, DeepSWE tests whether agents can perform full-stack engineering work with minimal guidance.

According to the researchers, DeepSWE was created to better reflect how developers actually use AI coding models today.

Existing public benchmarks such as SWE-Bench Pro often contain detailed implementation clues, code snippets, and references to existing fixes that models may already have seen during training.

“This makes DeepSWE a cleaner test of whether an agent can solve a novel software engineering problem, rather than recall, retrieve, or rediscover a public fix,” the report stated.

The benchmark consists of 113 tasks spanning 91 open-source repositories across TypeScript, Go, Python, JavaScript, and Rust. AI agents are given short, behaviour-focused prompts and must independently explore repositories, determine architecture, implement functionality, and verify correctness.

The evaluation framework uses a standardised harness called mini-swe-agent, which provides all models with identical tooling and prompts.

The tasks themselves are substantially more complex than earlier benchmarks. On average, DeepSWE solutions require 668 lines of code across seven files, compared to roughly 120 lines across five files in SWE-Bench Pro.

Researchers also focused heavily on evaluation reliability. Instead of inheriting tests from historical pull requests, DeepSWE uses custom behavioural verifiers designed specifically for each task. These tests assess observable software behaviour rather than checking for specific implementation patterns.

“The analyser disagreed with the SWE-Bench Pro verifier on 32% of trials and with the DeepSWE verifier on 1.4%,” the report noted, adding that “nearly a third of SWE-Bench Pro's pass/fail decisions appear incorrect to a careful reader of the same trajectory.”

The benchmark also revealed distinct behavioural patterns among model families. Claude models frequently failed to implement multi-part requirements, whereas GPT based models showed stronger instruction fidelity and consistency across repeated runs.

“GPT reads the prompt and the visible repository contract literally, and produces a patch that honours both,” the researchers wrote. “The behaviour is consistent across runs.”

The report also found that stronger models increasingly verified their own outputs without explicit prompting. Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.4 wrote new repository-native tests in over 80% of DeepSWE runs.

“We notice that models are a lot less likely to write their own tests on SWE-Bench Pro than on DeepSWE,” the authors stated, attributing the difference to SWE-Bench Pro’s prompt design, which discourages modifying test logic.

Beyond accuracy, the benchmark measured efficiency across runtime, token usage, and cost. GPT-5.5 achieved its 70% score with a median runtime of 20 minutes and approximately 47,000 output tokens per trial, making it one of the most efficient high-performing models tested.

The DeepSWE team acknowledged that the benchmark still has limitations, including restricted language coverage and a focus on open-source repositories with at least 500 GitHub stars. Future versions are expected to include additional languages such as C++ and Java, as well as more bug localisation and refactoring tasks.

title: Mphasis Launches AI Enterprise Platform Tria, Rolls Out Modernisation, Optimisation Offerings
content:
The IT services company is positioning Tria as a platform-led AI system aimed at helping enterprises move from AI experimentation to execution.

What Actually Matters.

Mphasis has introduced Tria, a platform-led AI system aimed at automating decision-making across various enterprise functions.

The company launched two new product lines, Mphasis Modernise and Mphasis Optimise, to facilitate enterprise transformation using the Tria platform.

Mphasis has launched “Mphasis Tria”, an enterprise AI platform designed to help enterprises move beyond AI pilots and automate decision-making across operations, technology, and commercial functions.

The Bengaluru-headquartered company also unveiled two market-facing product lines—Mphasis Modernise and Mphasis Optimise—that will use the Tria platform for enterprise transformation engagements.

The launch marks Mphasis’ latest push to strengthen its platform-led AI strategy at a time when large technology services firms are increasingly looking to build proprietary AI platforms and agentic AI systems to drive higher-margin, recurring revenue streams.

Mphasis said Tria combines enterprise data, reasoning systems and agentic execution capabilities into a unified stack aimed at enabling “governed enterprise agency”, a model where AI systems can support coordinated and accountable business actions rather than functioning as standalone copilots or automation tools.

“Through Mphasis Tria, Mphasis is introducing a new category of enterprise transformation, one that moves beyond autonomous AI systems into governed Enterprise Agency, reflecting the belief that enterprises do not simply need more AI models or automation, but the ability to convert intelligence into coordinated, accountable action/s,” said Nitin Rakesh, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director, Mphasis, in a statement.

The platform has been built using the company’s existing intellectual property assets, including its NeoIP suite and Ontosphere knowledge platform.

According to the company, Tria is structured across three layers. The “Insight” layer serves as the foundational layer, powering the structured knowledge graph and contextual intelligence engine that creates enterprise-wide visibility and understanding.

The “Foresight” layer, powered by Continuum AI, transforms data and context into actionable insights through advanced cognitive and reasoning capabilities. It enables causal reasoning, optimization, simulation, and enterprise decision intelligence. The third “Execute” layer is the agentic execution and orchestration layer that enables intelligent automation and coordinated enterprise actions at scale.

Mphasis said the acquisition of Theory and Practice and its Continuum AI platform helped complete the Tria stack by adding decision intelligence capabilities between enterprise context and execution systems.

“Most enterprises do not lack data, dashboards, models, or AI experiments. What they lack is the ability to turn that intelligence into coordinated, accountable action that drives measurable business outcomes,” said Srikumar Ramanathan, Chief Solutions Officer, Mphasis.

The announcement comes as IT services companies globally race to reposition themselves around generative AI and agentic AI capabilities amid growing enterprise demand for automation-led productivity gains and decision intelligence systems.

title: Byju’s Founder Raveendran Sentenced for 6 Months in Singapore Contempt Case
content:
The court found that Raveendran had disobeyed multiple court orders related to the disclosure of his assets.

What Actually Matters.

Byju Raveendran has been sentenced to six months in jail for contempt of court in Singapore.

The court found Raveendran disobeyed multiple orders regarding asset disclosure.

Byju’s Founder Byju Raveendran has been sentenced to six months in jail by a Singapore court for contempt of court, according to a Bloomberg report. The court found that Raveendran had disobeyed multiple court orders related to the disclosure of his assets.

The development marks another major setback for the once high-flying Indian edtech company, which had earlier become one of India’s most valuable startups during the pandemic-driven online learning boom.

Raveendran founded Think & Learn Pvt Ltd, popularly known as Byju’s, and transformed it into one of India’s largest edtech firms backed by several global investors. At its peak, the company attracted investments from international firms and sovereign wealth funds, rapidly expanding across markets through acquisitions and aggressive growth strategies.

However, the company later faced mounting financial troubles, delayed filings, layoffs, governance concerns and legal disputes with investors and lenders.

The latest case in Singapore is linked to efforts by foreign investors to recover losses tied to their investments in the company. A subsidiary of the Qatar Investment Authority is among the entities pursuing legal action against Raveendran in Singapore courts.

According to reports, the court held him in contempt after finding that he failed to comply with several directions regarding his assets. Qatar Holdings, which participated in a funding round for Byju’s, was represented by law firm Drew & Napier in the matter.

The sentencing also comes amid ongoing legal battles in the United States, where lenders are attempting to recover losses from a $1.2 billion loan linked to the company.

Byju’s was once considered one of India’s biggest startup success stories and a symbol of the country’s booming edtech ecosystem. But over the past two years, the company has faced increasing scrutiny over its financial management and operations.

The latest ruling further adds to the legal and financial challenges surrounding Raveendran and the struggling edtech firm.

title: Razorpay Launches Payment CLI for Developers and AI Agents
content:
The launch is part of Razorpay’s broader push to build AI-ready financial infrastructure and reduce manual workflows tied to payments management.

What Actually Matters.

Razorpay has introduced a Command Line Interface (CLI) for developers to manage payments without using dashboards.

The CLI enables direct interaction with payment systems through simple commands, enhancing developer and AI workflows.

Indian fintech company Razorpay has launched the Razorpay Command Line Interface (CLI) in India, allowing developers and AI systems to manage payments directly from coding environments without logging into dashboards.

The company said developers, AI builders, and AI assistants can now issue refunds, manage orders, check transactions, and access payment information from within their coding setup using simple commands.

The CLI can work with AI-powered coding tools and agentic workflows, including platforms such as Anthropic’s Claude Cowork and OpenAI Codex, enabling AI agents to interact with Razorpay directly from those environments.

For instance, developers or AI assistants can use commands such as “Show me my latest payment” or “Refund this transaction,” with the Razorpay CLI securely fetching the requested information.

“The way businesses work with software is changing fast. Dashboards will continue to exist, but they can no longer be the only way businesses interact with payments,” said Khilan Haria, Chief Product Officer at Razorpay, said in a statement.

“Businesses increasingly expect payments to work naturally inside the tools and automation systems they already use every day. With Razorpay CLI, a developer can test integrations automatically, a finance team can reconcile payments without relying on manual processes, and AI agents can interact with Razorpay directly from coding environments,” Haria added.

According to the company, the CLI will help businesses automate payment operations and reduce repetitive manual tasks. Razorpay also said the system is expected to support more autonomous payment-related workflows handled by AI agents over time.

The company said the launch builds on its earlier investments in AI-native infrastructure, including its MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, which allows AI systems to interact with Razorpay services.

Razorpay said its long-term goal is to make its payment capabilities accessible through APIs, code environments, automation tools, and AI agents in addition to dashboards.

title: HCLTech Launches Autonomous Finance Platform Built on Google Cloud’s Gemini Enterprise
content:
The platform aims to automate finance and accounting workflows such as invoice processing, order management and financial planning.

What Actually Matters.

HCLTech has introduced an autonomous finance platform using Google Cloud’s Gemini Enterprise AI stack.

The platform automates various finance and accounting workflows, reducing manual intervention.

IT services company HCLTech on Tuesday launched an autonomous finance platform built on Google Cloud’s Gemini Enterprise AI stack, as technology vendors increasingly look to embed agentic AI capabilities into core enterprise functions.

The Noida-headquartered company said the platform is designed to automate finance and accounting operations across areas such as Invoice-to-Pay, Order-to-Cash, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) and Record-to-Report.

The launch comes at a time when global IT services firms are racing to position themselves as partners in enterprise AI transformation, moving beyond pilot projects and isolated automation use cases.

HCLTech said the platform runs on top of existing ERP and SaaS systems and is designed to reduce manual intervention in finance workflows. The company added that the platform can autonomously execute, learn from and optimise finance operations over time.

“ERP and SaaS platforms digitised finance, but they did not fundamentally change how work gets done,” said Upjit Ghuman, Executive Vice President and Global Head of BPO, HCLTech.

He added that by reducing manual intervention, CFOs and finance teams can focus on judgment-driven, strategic and value-creating work.

He said the platform introduces an “agentic AI fabric” that allows finance processes to operate with a high degree of autonomy, enabling finance teams to focus more on strategic decision-making.

The platform combines Google Cloud’s Gemini Enterprise AI capabilities and cloud infrastructure with HCLTech’s finance and business process operations expertise.

“Gemini Enterprise and Google’s AI stack are built to handle the complex orchestration required by the world’s largest enterprises,” said Kevin Ichhpurani, President, Global Partner Ecosystem at Google Cloud. He added that HCLTech’s finance platform built on this foundation combines deep domain understanding with proven engineering excellence.

The launch also reflects a broader trend in the IT services sector, where companies are increasingly packaging AI capabilities into industry-specific platforms instead of offering only traditional consulting and implementation services.

title: TCS Bags AI-Led Transformation Deal From Sweden’s SKF to Modernise Global IT Operations
content:
The long-term engagement will see TCS manage SKF’s global IT landscape and help the industrial manufacturer build AI-led operations across applications, infrastructure and enterprise systems.

What Actually Matters.

TCS has secured a long-term contract with SKF to modernise its global IT operations through AI-led transformation.

The partnership will enhance SKF's applications, infrastructure, data, security, connectivity, and end-user services on a global scale.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has secured a long-term strategic contract from Swedish industrial manufacturer SKF to modernise its global technology operations and build AI-led enterprise capabilities, as India’s largest IT services firm deepens its push into large-scale transformation deals centred on artificial intelligence.

Under the partnership, TCS will provide managed services across SKF’s applications, infrastructure, data, security, connectivity and end-user services operations globally, according to a company statement issued on May 27.

The Mumbai-headquartered IT major said the engagement will involve modernising SKF’s existing technology landscape using AI-led workflows, while also helping standardise operations and accelerate the adoption of next-generation enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems.

The financial details of the contract were not disclosed.

The deal comes at a time when large global enterprises are increasingly looking to embed AI capabilities into core operations, prompting IT services companies to reposition traditional infrastructure and applications management work around AI-enabled transformation programmes.

“The next decade of industrial manufacturing will be defined by how deeply companies integrate AI into how they design, produce, and serve. SKF intends to lead that shift,” SKF chief executive Rickard Gustafson said in the statement.

TCS Managing Director and Chief Executive K Krithivasan said the partnership aimed at building a “resilient, scalable digital foundation” for SKF while applying AI and data-driven intelligence to improve agility and long-term competitiveness.

SKF, which makes bearings, seals, lubrication systems and industrial monitoring solutions, operates in around 130 countries.

For TCS, the deal further strengthens its presence in the Nordic region, where the company has operated since 1991. Currently, over 20,000 TCS employees support leading enterprises in Sweden, Finland, Norway, and Denmark.

The partnership also reflects a broader trend among global manufacturers looking to overhaul legacy technology systems while building AI capabilities into business processes and products.

“Together, we are applying data-driven intelligence and AI to create an agile enterprise that can adapt to technological and market change while supporting long-term sustainable growth and competitiveness. This collaboration reflects our joint commitment to making SKF an AI-native, industry-leading, technology-driven industrial manufacturer,” Krithivasan added.

title: Anthropic Appoints Sangeeta Bavi to Lead Startups, Growth in India
content:
Sangeeta Bavi has been appointed as Head of Digital Natives, Startups and Growth for Anthropic in India.

Bavi's role involves collaborating with founders and growth-stage companies to adopt AI technologies.

AI company Anthropic has appointed Sangeeta Bavi as Head of Digital Natives, Startups and Growth for India.

Bavi announced the move in a LinkedIn post on May 26, saying the role aligns closely with her long-standing work with founders and startup ecosystems.

“Founders have always held a special place in mine,” Bavi wrote. “Their ambition, resilience and belief that they can change the world have taught me more than any other form of learning.”

About joining Anthropic, she said its people, mission and way of thinking “clicked deeply.” She described the company as “a place built on the conviction that AI must be safe and genuinely beneficial for humanity.”

The appointment comes as Anthropic accelerates its India expansion. Earlier this year, the company named Irina Ghose as Managing Director for India and plans to open its first India office in Bengaluru.

Backed by Google and Amazon, Anthropic has been increasing its focus on enterprise AI adoption and developer ecosystems globally. India has emerged as one of the company’s key markets, particularly for coding and technical AI use cases.

In her new role, Bavi is expected to work closely with founders, startups, and growth-stage companies adopting AI technologies.

“India is at an extraordinary inflection point,” she wrote. “Our founders and growth-stage companies are not just adopting AI, they are building with it, scaling with it, and taking it to every corner of the economy.”

Before joining Anthropic, Bavi spent more than a decade at Microsoft, where she led the company’s Digital Natives and startup initiatives in India and South Asia. Her work included building programs for early-stage startups, growth companies, and unicorns, while helping shape Microsoft’s startup engagement model in India.

DeepSeek has permanently reduced the price of its V4 Pro model by 75%, significantly impacting global AI pricing strategies.

The price cut is expected to heighten competition among AI companies, forcing rivals to reconsider their pricing structures.

Chinese AI startup DeepSeek has permanently slashed prices for its flagship V4 Pro model by 75%, a move that could intensify competition in the global AI market and further pressure rivals on pricing.

In a statement released on May 22, DeepSeek said that V4 Pro now costs $0.003625 per million input tokens for cache hits, $0.435 per million input tokens for cache misses, and $0.87 per million output tokens.

A token is a unit of text processed by an AI model.

— DeepSeek (@deepseek_ai) May 22, 2026

DeepSeek released the V4 series, including the Pro and lighter Flash variants, in April, positioning the models as the beginning of an era of cost-effective one million context length with strong reasoning, coding, and math performance.

The company did not specify the exact reason behind the permanent reduction. However, the announcement comes amid growing expectations around wider availability of Huawei’s Ascend 950 AI chips, which DeepSeek has previously cited as critical to improving the performance and scalability of its V4 models.

When the company unveiled V4 last month, it said the more advanced Pro version was priced as much as 12 times higher than the lighter Flash variant because of “constraints in high-end compute capacity.”

At the time, DeepSeek had indicated that prices would likely “fall sharply” once Huawei’s Ascend 950 supernodes entered large-scale deployment in the second half of the year.

Huawei’s AI chip business has gained momentum as US export restrictions continue to block NVIDIA from selling its most advanced AI chips in China. At the same time, restrictions on chipmaking equipment have constrained Huawei’s ability to rapidly scale production of its Ascend processors.

DeepSeek’s aggressive pricing strategy is expected to increase pressure on AI companies globally as competition intensifies around inference costs and enterprise adoption of large language models.

title: Rajasthan Partners With Wadhwani AI to Deploy AI Tools for Agriculture Services
content:
The foundation will provide technical support to the state government for a period of three years without any financial burden on the government.

What Actually Matters.

Rajasthan government has partnered with Wadhwani AI to implement AI-driven agricultural solutions.

The partnership provides technical support for three years without financial costs to the government.

The Agriculture Department of the Rajasthan government has signed a non-financial memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Wadhwani AI Foundation through Lords Education Group to introduce AI-driven solutions for agricultural services and farmer support across the state.

According to an official release, the agreement was signed at Pant Krishi Bhawan in Jaipur in the presence of senior officials from the department.

Under the partnership, Wadhwani AI will provide technical support to the state government for a period of three years without any financial burden on the government.

Agriculture Commissioner Naresh Kumar Goyal said the initiative aligns with the state government’s broader plans to develop AI-based agricultural models and establish a centre of excellence focused on AI-enabled farming and rural services.

The department stated that Rajasthan has already created digital farmer IDs for nearly 95 lakh farmers across the state. These IDs include land records, khasra details, and Aadhaar-linked credentials, forming a digital agriculture database that can support crop insurance systems, fertiliser distribution monitoring, and urea tracking mechanisms.

As part of the collaboration, several AI-powered tools will be introduced to improve farmer outreach and agricultural decision-making.

One of the platforms, Agrivani, is a multilingual AI chatbot that will allow farmers to interact through voice or text in local languages and receive agriculture-related guidance and advisory support.

Another platform, CropAce, uses computer vision technology to detect crop diseases and pest infestations from photographs uploaded directly from farms. The system is designed to provide treatment recommendations verified by agricultural experts.

The partnership will also include deploying a smartphone-based Soybean Grain Analyser application to help farmers digitally assess soybean quality, grading standards, and protein content.

Moreover, the Agri AI Collect and News Monitoring platform will support digital field record management and help administrative departments with agriculture-related monitoring and decision-making.

Officials said the collaboration reflects the growing use of AI and digital infrastructure in Indian agriculture, particularly in areas such as crop monitoring, advisory systems, farmer databases, and agricultural governance.

title: Shunya Labs Releases Open Standard for Stuttering Annotation
content:
SAML is an XML-based specification that extends W3C SSML standards and includes schema validation to ensure interoperability across tools.

What Actually Matters.

Shunya Labs has introduced SAML, the first open-source standard for annotating stuttering in speech datasets.

SAML addresses fragmentation in stuttering research by providing a unified annotation framework for improved interoperability.

Shunya Labs has launched Stuttering Annotation Markup Language (SAML), which it claims is the world’s first open-source standard for annotating stuttering in speech datasets, designed to improve interoperability across speech research and clinical workflows.

The Gurugram-based company said the framework was developed to address longstanding fragmentation in stuttering research, where different laboratories and institutions rely on separate annotation systems, making it difficult to compare datasets or reproduce findings.

SAML is an XML-based specification that extends W3C SSML standards and includes schema validation to ensure interoperability across tools. The framework supports annotation of dysfluencies such as repetitions, prolongations, and blocks, alongside a severity scale ranging from 0 to 8 based on duration. It also supports multi-speaker annotations for conversational and dialogue-based research.

According to the company, more than 80 million people globally are affected by stuttering, while inconsistent annotation standards have limited large-scale collaboration and reproducibility in speech research.

“SAML was created to provide a shared framework that researchers, clinicians, and developers can adopt across studies and tools,” said Founder and Chief Scientist Sourav Bandyopadhyay. “Standardisation is critical if speech research is expected to become interoperable, reproducible, and collaborative at scale.”

To encourage adoption, the company has made the specification, training resources, schema documentation, validation suite, and conversion tools freely available to the research community.

title: TCS launches Sovereign Cloud Offering in Europe to Focus on Data Localisation
content:
TCS’ SovereignSecure Cloud platform targets governments and regulated sectors as enterprises across the EU step up focus on data sovereignty, regulatory compliance, and secure AI adoption.

What Actually Matters.

TCS has introduced its SovereignSecure Cloud platform in Europe to meet rising demands for data sovereignty and compliance.

The offering targets governments and regulated sectors in the EU, focusing on data control amid regulatory changes.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has launched its SovereignSecure Cloud platform in Europe, as India’s largest IT services company looks to tap rising demand for data sovereignty, localisation, and compliance-led cloud infrastructure across the region.

The offering is aimed at governments, public sector entities, and regulated industries in the European Union (EU), where enterprises are increasingly looking for greater control over data, operations, and digital infrastructure amid evolving regulatory requirements and geopolitical concerns.

The Mumbai-headquartered IT major said the platform combines sovereign cloud architecture with artificial intelligence capabilities and is designed to help enterprises comply with EU regulations without compromising on operational flexibility and interoperability.

The launch comes at a time when European enterprises are reassessing dependence on global cloud providers and supply chains, while also trying to accelerate AI adoption. Technology services firms and hyperscalers have increasingly been rolling out sovereign cloud offerings globally as governments tighten scrutiny around cross-border data flows and digital infrastructure control.

TCS said the European offering follows the rollout of the platform in India in 2025, and subsequent expansion into Kenya, East Africa, and the Philippines.

According to the company, the European version of SovereignSecure Cloud has a multi-layered architecture comprising a sovereign cloud layer built with hyperscalers, a national sovereign cloud layer for country-specific localisation requirements, and an enterprise cloud services layer based on TCS’ EU-specific enterprise cloud framework.

“European organisations are looking to strike a balance between addressing supply chain and sovereignty risks while ensuring leverage of frontier technologies to be globally competitive. TCS SovereignSecure Cloud solutions mark an important milestone for TCS in Europe, as our customers can now benefit from a pragmatic approach to cloud that ensures resilience and sovereignty that is contextualised to the enterprise,” Sapthagiri Chapalapalli, Head of Europe, TCS, said in a statement.

Alongside the cloud launch, TCS also introduced a Sovereignty Consulting and Delivery Framework in the EU. The framework is intended to help organisations classify workloads based on risk and apply different levels of sovereign controls, rather than adopting a uniform approach across all systems.

Europe remains a key market for Indian IT services firms, particularly in sectors such as banking, manufacturing, telecom and retail.

“As enterprises and governments across Europe accelerate their digital transformation journeys, the need for secure, compliant and sovereign cloud architectures has never been more critical,” TCS stated.

content:
The move is partly tied to cost-cutting efforts, with Microsoft’s financial year ending on June 30.

What Actually Matters.

Microsoft is phasing out Claude Code in favour of GitHub Copilot CLI for its engineering teams.

The decision aligns with Microsoft's cost-cutting initiatives as its financial year concludes on June 30.

Microsoft is reportedly beginning to phase out the use of Anthropic’s Claude Code internally, with several engineering teams being directed to transition to GitHub Copilot CLI instead, according to a report by The Verge.

The report stated that Microsoft’s Experiences + Devices division—which oversees products including Windows, Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, and Surface—is planning to remove most Claude Code licenses by the end of June.

Sources reportedly said that the move is partly tied to cost-cutting efforts, with Microsoft’s financial year ending on June 30. It reflects a wider challenge for technology companies as large-scale use of generative AI tools continues to drive up costs.

Earlier, Uber’s Chief Technology Officer, Praveen Neppalli Naga, reportedly said the company had already depleted its entire 2026 budget for AI coding tools within the first four months of the year due to extensive employee usage.

According to the report, Microsoft developers in the division are expected to migrate to Microsoft’s in-house GitHub Copilot CLI in the coming weeks.

Claude Code had reportedly gained traction among Microsoft engineers and even non-technical staff as a tool for rapid software prototyping and coding assistance. Earlier this year, Microsoft expanded internal access to the Anthropic-powered coding assistant and encouraged engineers to compare it against GitHub Copilot.

However, The Verge reported that Claude Code’s growing popularity may have conflicted with Microsoft’s broader push to position Copilot CLI as its primary command-line AI coding tool.

Copilot CLI is designed to operate outside integrated development environments such as Visual Studio Code and forms part of Microsoft’s larger Copilot ecosystem strategy.

Despite the phase-out, Anthropic’s models will remain accessible through Copilot CLI alongside OpenAI and Microsoft’s in-house AI models. Microsoft is also expanding the use of Copilot CLI across its engineering teams and has asked employees to share bug reports and feedback before access to Claude Code ends.

At the same time, Microsoft continues to maintain ties with Anthropic through other agreements. According to reports, Microsoft became one of Anthropic’s largest customers earlier this year and signed a deal in November to offer Claude models through Microsoft Foundry.

LTM, formerly LTIMindtree, has partnered with UK-based travel food and beverage operator SSP Group to modernise its IT infrastructure and application support operations using artificial intelligence tools.

Under the engagement, the Larsen & Toubro group company will provide end-to-end IT infrastructure support and application maintenance services for SSP Group, which operates food and beverage outlets across airports, railway stations, and travel hubs globally.

content:
HCLTech has expanded its partnership with Pegasystems to help enterprises modernise legacy technology systems using AI, as IT services firms sharpen their focus on AI-led transformation deals.

What Actually Matters.

HCLTech has expanded its partnership with Pegasystems to modernise legacy technology systems using artificial intelligence.

The collaboration aims to automate the migration of older enterprise systems into cloud-native applications.

IT Services firm HCLTech has expanded its partnership with US-based software company Pegasystems to help enterprises modernise legacy technology systems using artificial intelligence, as tech firms increasingly sharpen their focus on AI-led transformation deals.

The companies said on May 25 that HCLTech will combine its AI Force platform with Pega Blueprint, Pegasystems’ AI-driven workflow and application design platform, to help clients automate the discovery, documentation and migration of older enterprise systems into cloud-native applications.

The collaboration comes at a time when global enterprises are looking to reduce costs associated with maintaining ageing technology estates, while also accelerating the adoption of AI-enabled applications and workflows.

Unlike traditional migration projects that largely shift applications from on-premise infrastructure to the cloud, the companies said the offering aims to help enterprises retire legacy systems altogether through automated workflows, AI-generated application designs and migration-ready data structures.

“Enterprises worldwide are burdened by the high costs, risks and inefficiencies of outdated, siloed legacy systems. HCLTech AI Force and Pega Blueprint can help organisations transform their estates through AI-led discovery and modernisation while maximising value for their Pega investments,” the companies said in the statement.

The offering will use generative AI and agentic AI capabilities to automate parts of the modernisation process that have traditionally required significant manual effort.

“Our long-standing partnership with Pega continues to inspire real innovation. By combining HCLTech AI Force with Pega Blueprint, we are making legacy modernisation faster, smarter and more accurate,” Sadagopan Singam, Executive Vice President, Global Head of Enterprise Platforms and Edge Services, Digital Business Services at HCLTech, said in the statement.

John Higgins, Chief of Client and Partner Success at Pegasystems, said enterprises are looking to modernise systems while maintaining scalability, security and resilience.

The partnership also reflects a broader push among Indian IT services companies to deepen alliances with enterprise software firms and hyperscalers as AI adoption reshapes large technology transformation contracts.

HCLTech said the platform will support the rapid deployment of applications on the Pega platform and enable continuous optimisation after migration.

The Noida-headquartered company reported consolidated revenue of $14.7 billion for the 12 months ended March 2026.

title: Persistent Systems Teams Up With Kong to Simplify Enterprise AI Governance
content:
The collaboration will combine Persistent’s enterprise modernisation expertise with Kong’s API connectivity platform to help businesses govern, integrate and manage AI workloads at scale.

What Actually Matters.

Persistent Systems and Kong have partnered to simplify AI governance for enterprises.

The collaboration focuses on managing and integrating AI systems across hybrid and multi-cloud environments.

Persistent Systems and Kong Inc. have announced a strategic partnership to help enterprises securely scale AI systems from experimentation to production.

The collaboration will combine Persistent’s engineering and enterprise modernisation expertise with Kong’s API and AI connectivity platform to help businesses manage, govern and integrate AI systems across hybrid and multi-cloud environments.

The companies said enterprises are increasingly facing challenges not in accessing AI models, but in managing how APIs, data pipelines, AI models and applications connect and operate at scale. Through the partnership, both firms aim to provide a unified “control layer” for enterprises to securely govern AI systems while reducing operational complexity.

The partnership will also support organisations in modernising legacy API environments and securely deploying generative and agentic AI workflows. According to the companies, the system will include safeguards such as personally identifiable information (PII) protection, centralised access management, policy-based controls and end-to-end observability tools.

“Enterprise AI will not be defined by who has access to models. It will be defined by how effectively organisations can govern how intelligence flows across their systems,” said Anand Krishnan, Executive Vice President, Persistent Systems.

“APIs are no longer just integration points. They are the control layer for enterprise AI.”

Meanwhile, Ken Kim, Senior Vice President and Head of Business Development at Kong, said APIs are becoming critical infrastructure for connecting AI services, data and model endpoints across enterprise environments.

“At Kong, we are building the AI connectivity infrastructure so organisations can secure, manage, govern and scale traffic across APIs and AI workloads on any model or any cloud,” Kim noted.

The companies also stated that the collaboration would help enterprises move beyond isolated AI use cases and build production-grade AI systems with improved governance, security and compliance capabilities.

title: OpenAI Offers $445,000 to Study Self-Improving AI
content:
The researcher would work on areas such as defending AI systems against data poisoning attacks.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI is hiring a researcher for its safety division, offering a salary of up to $445,000.

The role focuses on recursive self-improvement of AI models and associated safety risks.

OpenAI is hiring a researcher for its safety division with a compensation package reaching as high as $445,000, as the company intensifies work on risks tied to AI models that may eventually improve themselves without human intervention.

According to a report by Business Insider, the role sits within OpenAI’s Preparedness team and focuses on “recursive self-improvement,” a concept where AI models could autonomously enhance their own capabilities over time.

The job listing reportedly offers a salary range between $295,000 and $445,000 and seeks candidates capable of reasoning about future threats that may not yet be fully visible. OpenAI is specifically looking for researchers who can think in a “tasteful and strategic” manner while addressing emerging AI safety risks.

Business Insider reported that the researcher would work on areas such as defending AI systems against data poisoning attacks, improving tools that interpret AI reasoning processes, and evaluating how AI could automate highly technical forms of labour.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has previously spoken about the company’s ambition to develop an “automated AI researcher” by 2028, while also acknowledging the technical and safety challenges involved.

The Preparedness team reportedly also examines broader risks associated with frontier AI models, including cybersecurity threats and dangerous model behaviour. The move comes amid ongoing debates around whether leading AI labs are scaling capabilities faster than safety protections.

Concerns around self-improving AI are also becoming more visible across the broader industry.

Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis recently said humanity may already be in the “foothills of the singularity,” referring to a future where AI systems improve themselves faster than humans can effectively monitor.

Meanwhile, Anthropic has repeatedly discussed the importance of alignment and constitutional AI techniques as models become more capable.

title: EY, Microsoft Launch $1 Billion Enterprise AI Initiative
content:
The joint services will initially target core business functions such as finance, tax, risk management, human resources, and supply chain logistics.

What Actually Matters.

EY and Microsoft are investing over $1 billion to scale artificial intelligence in business operations.

The initiative targets core functions like finance, tax, risk management, and human resources.

Professional services organisation EY and tech giant Microsoft have committed to a joint investment of more than $1 billion over the next five years. The initiative is designed to help businesses scale artificial intelligence across their operations and transition from isolated experimental pilots to broad, enterprise-wide execution.

Under the new agreement, integrated teams consisting of EY industry professionals and Microsoft "forward deployed engineers" will work directly with corporate clients. This deployment will utilise Microsoft’s specialised AI-native engineering approach to accelerate adoption across change management delivery models. The joint services will initially target core business functions such as finance, tax, risk management, human resources, and supply chain logistics. These solutions will be tailored for specific sectors, primarily focusing on financial services, industrials and energy, consumer and retail, government, and healthcare.

The collaboration relies heavily on data and operational feedback from EY’s internal adoption of Microsoft technologies. EY was one of the first organisations to adopt Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite, and is currently scaling Copilot across its global workforce of more than 400,000 people to embed agentic AI capabilities enterprise-wide. EY claims that the initial deployment of Copilot to 150,000 users recorded a boost in productivity, which the firm reinvested into client delivery and learning.

Beyond the initial Copilot rollout, EY has integrated various AI systems into its own business units to validate their performance. The modernisation of its finance operations using the Microsoft Power Platform and intelligent agents via Copilot Studio resulted in 95% faster lead times and a 37% reduction in operational costs.

In its assurance division, a new multi-agent framework integrated with Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Foundry, and Microsoft Fabric was embedded into the EY Canvas platform, encompassing the workflows of 130,000 professionals across 160,000 audit engagements. Additionally, early adoption of Microsoft Azure AI Document Intelligence on its Global Tax Platform reduced manual workloads by up to 90% by automatically extracting essential data from documents, the company stated.

The initiative aims to address a broader market challenge where organisations have struggled to move past early-stage generative AI experimentation to achieve measurable performance gains across multiple departments. The offering will feature a fully integrated operational structure, utilising shared governance, aligned commercial models, and mutual accountability across both corporations.

"With access to a single, integrated team, clients will have at their disposal both Microsoft’s market-leading engineering depth, alongside EY teams’ deep industry knowledge and change management capabilities. By combining people and innovation in this next phase of the alliance, clients will be empowered to realise the transformative power of agentic AI within the enterprise," Janet Truncale, EY Global Chair and CEO, said in a statement.

"Our initiative combines Microsoft’s trusted AI platform and engineering teams with EY’s industry capabilities and experience as Client Zero, applying these technologies across their own organisation, to help customers move beyond pilots to enterprise execution, enhancing decision-making and delivering measurable impact," Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft’s Commercial Business, added.

title: OpenAI Beats Anthropic by Nearly $1 Bn in Quarterly Revenue
content:
Both OpenAI and Anthropic are planning to go public this year.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI generated approximately $5.7 billion in revenue, leading Anthropic by nearly $1 billion in the first quarter of 2026.

The growth in OpenAI's revenue is driven by increased enterprise adoption of ChatGPT and demand for its developer tools.

OpenAI generated approximately $5.7 billion in revenue during the first quarter of 2026, giving it a roughly $1 billion lead over rival Anthropic, according to a report by The Information.

The report added that OpenAI’s quarterly revenue growth was driven by expanding enterprise adoption of ChatGPT, growing demand for its developer tools and rapid uptake of Codex, the company’s AI coding platform.

Despite trailing OpenAI in quarterly revenue, Anthropic is seeing rapid growth of its own. The Wall Street Journal recently reported that Anthropic generated about $4.8 billion in first-quarter revenue and is projecting that figure to more than double to roughly $10.9 billion in the second quarter, potentially putting the company on track for its first quarterly operating profit, estimated at $559 million.

The sharp rise has been fuelled largely by enterprise demand for Claude models, particularly among software developers, financial institutions and large corporate customers adopting AI tools internally.

At the same time, OpenAI is aggressively scaling its business ahead of a widely anticipated IPO filing. The company is currently generating around $25 billion in annualised recurring revenue, according to The Information. However, its spending commitments remain substantial due to investments in AI chips, data centres and model development.

Anthropic, meanwhile, in April said that its annualised revenue run rate crossed $30 billion in 2026, a dramatic increase from about $9 billion at the end of 2025.

The company has benefited from strong demand for coding-related AI products and strategic partnerships with major cloud providers, including Amazon and Google, both of which have invested billions of dollars into the startup.

Both OpenAI and Anthropic are planning to go public this year. OpenAI is reportedly working with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley on an IPO that could be filed within days or weeks, targeting a September debut on public markets.

Anthropic is reportedly exploring an IPO that could happen as early as October 2026, with some bankers expecting the offering to raise more than $60 billion. Separately, reports citing The New York Times said Anthropic has discussed fundraising at valuations approaching $950 billion, potentially surpassing OpenAI’s latest reported valuation of $852 billion.

title: BDIA Pushes for Sovereign Digital Infrastructure Framework to Power India’s AI & Data Economy
content:
The event also marked the formal public launch of BDIA as a not-for-profit industry association focused on advancing sovereign digital infrastructure.

What Actually Matters.

BDIA advocates for a national sovereign digital infrastructure to enhance India's AI and data economy.

The Bharat Digital Samvad forum aimed to shift India from a digital consumer to a sovereign digital ecosystem builder.

Bharath Digital Infrastructure Association (BDIA) has called for a national sovereign digital infrastructure framework as India enters the next phase of growth in the AI and data economy, with industry leaders and policymakers pushing for stronger domestic capabilities across cloud, AI, cybersecurity and digital infrastructure.

The industry body made the announcement during its flagship policy forum Bharat Digital Samvad: The Foundation Forum.

Held under the theme ‘From Adoption to Command: Architecting India’s Sovereign Digital Future’, the summit brought together government officials, technology executives, policy experts and digital infrastructure stakeholders to discuss India’s transition from being a large-scale digital consumer to building and controlling the foundational layers of its digital ecosystem.

The event also marked the formal public launch of BDIA as a not-for-profit industry association focused on advancing sovereign digital infrastructure and enabling collaboration between industry, government, academia and strategic institutions.

Key discussions at the forum centred around reducing dependence on foreign-controlled digital ecosystems, strengthening sovereign cloud and compute infrastructure, advancing trusted AI frameworks and creating policy support for domestic technology providers.

The summit featured policy sessions focused on sovereign compute infrastructure, digital governance frameworks, indigenous hardware capabilities and market access mechanisms for Indian technology companies.

According to the association, BDIA will submit a comprehensive policy recommendation framework to government stakeholders covering areas such as sovereign AI standards, trusted cloud certification systems, domestic digital product certification and long-term digital governance frameworks.

Speaking at the event, Piyush Somani, who is also Chairman and MD of ESDS Software Solution, said India has reached a defining stage in its digital transformation journey.

He noted that while the country has emerged as a global leader in digital adoption, the next phase of growth must focus on building digital infrastructure that is designed, governed and scaled from within India.

Somani added that as AI, cloud and cybersecurity increasingly become core to economic growth and national resilience, India must strengthen domestic technology capabilities and reduce strategic dependencies across critical digital infrastructure layers.

Secretary General Abhishek Bhatt said the forum reflected growing urgency among policymakers and industry stakeholders to establish a stronger framework around India’s digital sovereignty ambitions.

According to Bhatt, discussions at the conclave highlighted the need for collaborative policymaking, ecosystem investments and procurement reforms to ensure India not only adopts digital technologies at scale but also owns and develops the infrastructure powering its digital economy.

Industry leaders at the event also highlighted the importance of frameworks such as Bharat Cloud Certification (BCC), Trusted Indian Digital Product (TIDP) and Digital Sovereignty Maturity Models (DSMM) to support indigenous innovation, domestic IP creation and trusted digital ecosystems.

The forum concluded with participants backing the creation of a nationally aligned sovereign digital infrastructure framework aimed at strengthening India’s position as a globally competitive and self-reliant digital economy.

title: LTM Wants to Acquire Randstad’s Tech and Consulting Business in Europe, Australia
content:
The proposed acquisition, pegged at over $500 million in annual revenue, is part of a broader partnership between the two companies.

What Actually Matters.

LTM aims to acquire Randstad's tech and consulting business in Europe and Australia, focusing on regulated industries.

The proposed acquisition targets operations in several European countries and Australia, generating significant annual revenue.

LTM (formerly LTIMindtree) has offered to acquire the technology and consulting services business of staffing major Randstad across parts of Europe and Australia, as the Indian IT services firm looks to deepen its presence in regulated industries and expand its AI-led services portfolio.

The proposed deal covers Randstad’s technology and consulting operations in France, Germany, Belgium, Luxembourg, and Australia, representing more than $500 million in annual revenue, the companies said.

The acquisition would strengthen LTM’s footprint in sectors such as aerospace and defence, automotive, utilities, and banking and financial services, while also adding regional delivery capabilities through centres in Romania and Portugal.

The transaction comes as Indian IT services companies increasingly look at acquisitions and partnerships to bolster domain expertise, gain local market access, and sharpen AI capabilities amid slowing discretionary technology spending globally.

“The deal would augment LTM’s global AI-centric capabilities with local domain and nearshore expertise crucial for delivering digital and AI transformation for customers in a sovereign-compliant and scalable model,” the company said in a statement.

The proposed acquisition is part of a broader partnership between the two firms. This includes a five-year IT services agreement under which LTM will support AI-led transformation initiatives for Randstad’s India global capability centre, along with a strategic managed services partnership for talent support.

“The proposed agreement is aligned with our five-year strategy to build a more resilient, diversified, balanced portfolio. By combining our global AI-centric capabilities with local context and industry depth, this acquisition would strengthen our ability to deliver compliant, domain-driven AI services and sovereign solutions in markets that are strategically important to us,” Venu Lambu, CEO and Managing Director, LTM, said in a statement.

Randstad chief executive Sander van ‘t Noordende said the partnership would allow the company to streamline its portfolio while continuing to offer technology services to clients through LTM.

The deal is proposed to be executed through LTIMindtree UK, a wholly owned subsidiary of the company, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.

title: Spotify, Universal Music to Launch Licensed AI Remixes and Covers
content:
The partnership marks one of its first major licensing deals for mainstream AI-generated music creation.

What Actually Matters.

Spotify and Universal Music Group are launching a feature for AI-generated covers and remixes on the platform.

This partnership ensures artists are compensated for their work in AI-generated music.

Spotify has partnered with Universal Music Group (UMG) to introduce AI-generated covers and remixes on its platform, allowing fans to create personalised versions of songs using generative artificial intelligence while ensuring artists are compensated for the use of their work.

The feature will be introduced as a paid add-on for Spotify Premium subscribers, although the company has not yet revealed pricing details or a launch timeline. The tool is expected to allow users to generate remixes and covers of songs from participating artists through licensed AI systems.

The agreement marks one of the first large-scale collaborations between a major music streaming platform and a record label aimed at formally integrating generative AI into mainstream music experiences.

“The company’s approach was focused on building AI tools with artist consent and proper compensation mechanisms,” Spotify co-CEO Alex Norström said in a statement.

“Solving hard problems for music is what Spotify does and fan-made covers and remixes are next. What we’re building is grounded in consent, credit and compensation for the artists and songwriters that take part,” he added.

He noted that Spotify and UMG were working towards creating “a richer, more beneficial experience for fans and a more rewarding outcome for artists and songwriters.”

Lucian Grainge, UMG Chairman and CEO, described the collaboration as an opportunity for artists to strengthen fan engagement while opening up additional revenue streams through AI-generated music experiences.

The partnership comes amid growing legal scrutiny of AI music-generation platforms such as Suno and Udio, both of which have faced copyright infringement lawsuits from major record labels over the alleged unauthorised use of copyrighted music for AI training.

Spotify said its AI systems would instead operate through direct licensing agreements with rights holders, rather than using copyrighted material without approval.

The company had previously indicated that it was working with major labels including UMG, Sony Music Group, and Warner Music Group to build “artist-first” AI products through formal agreements.

The announcement was made during Spotify’s Investor Day event, where the company also unveiled several AI-powered products for audiobooks, podcasts, and creator tools.

The deal could signal a broader shift in how major music companies approach generative AI, with licensed AI-generated music potentially becoming a new revenue model for the streaming industry.

title: ByteDance’s CapCut Teams Up With Google Gemini for Conversational AI Image Editing
content:
Chinese app CapCut and Google are deepening their collaboration by integrating AI-powered creative editing workflows into the Gemini app.

What Actually Matters.

CapCut has partnered with Google Gemini to integrate AI-powered editing tools within the Gemini app.

The collaboration enables users to edit photos and videos directly through the AI assistant platform.

Chinese video and image editing platform, CapCut, has partnered with Google Gemini to bring AI-powered editing tools directly into the Gemini app, allowing users to edit photos and videos without leaving the AI assistant platform.

The announcement was made through a post on X where CapCut said users will “soon” be able to access its creative editing capabilities within Gemini. The company added that it sees the future of content creation becoming “more conversational, intuitive and intelligently integrated across tools and experiences.”

While the companies have not revealed detailed features or a release timeline, the integration is expected to allow Gemini users to modify, enhance, or edit visual content using CapCut’s existing AI-powered editing suite.

CapCut, owned by Chinese tech company ByteDance, already offers several AI-driven tools including automatic video editing, AI image generation, templates, effects, subtitles, and smart visual enhancements. Over the past year, the platform has increasingly focused on AI-assisted content creation as competition among editing and generative AI platforms grows.

The partnership also signals Google’s continued push to expand Gemini beyond a text-based AI assistant into a broader creative ecosystem. By integrating third-party editing tools directly into Gemini, Google appears to be positioning the platform closer to AI-powered creative workflows that combine generation, editing, and publishing within a single experience.

This is not the first collaboration between Google and CapCut. In late 2025, Google Photos introduced an “Edit with CapCut” feature within its annual photo recap tool, allowing users to export photos directly to CapCut using customised templates.

The latest partnership expands that relationship further by bringing CapCut’s editing capabilities closer to Gemini’s AI interface.

title: Hexaware to Acquire Consulting Firm CPS to Deepen AI, Cloud Transformation Push
content:
The move is aimed at deepening Hexaware’s presence in high-value financial services transformation projects and expanding its advisory-led enterprise business.

What Actually Matters.

Hexaware is acquiring CPS to enhance its consulting and AI capabilities for financial services transformation projects.

The acquisition aims to strengthen Hexaware's advisory-led enterprise business and consolidate its position with existing high-profile clients.

IT services firm Hexaware Technologies is acquiring UK and UAE-based Consulting Professionals Services (CPS) to strengthen its consulting, AI and cloud transformation capabilities, especially for large financial services clients.

The Mumbai-headquartered company said on May 19 that it has entered into an agreement to acquire the consulting and professional services firm and expects the transaction to close within two weeks.

Financial details of the deal were not disclosed.

CPS provides technology consulting and professional services spanning regulatory compliance, governance and risk, technology infrastructure and business transformation, primarily to an FTSE 100 client.

The acquisition comes at a time when Indian IT services companies are sharpening their consulting and advisory capabilities to capture larger AI-led transformation mandates from global enterprises. Companies are increasingly looking to combine traditional IT outsourcing with higher-value consulting around cloud migration, governance, compliance and AI implementation.

Hexaware said it already has an existing relationship with the FTSE 100 client served by CPS and is among its top IT service providers. The acquisition is expected to help consolidate a larger share of the client’s technology spending under Hexaware.

“With CPS, we gain access to high-performance talent in the UAE and UK. This acquisition adds scale and strengthens our credibility in program assurance and cloud engineering, which is significant as we expand our delivery locations and workforce diversity,” said Parameshwaran Iyer, Country Head for UK and Ireland at Hexaware.

The company said the deal would strengthen its ambition to become a larger AI and cloud transformation partner for financial institutions and other blue-chip enterprises, expanding capabilities from advisory and consulting to implementation and operations.

The move also underlines a broader trend of mid-tier IT firms pursuing targeted acquisitions in consulting and domain-specialist firms to bolster AI credentials and improve access to large enterprise accounts, particularly in banking and financial services, where regulatory and governance requirements are becoming more complex.

“Having worked extensively in the financial services and market infrastructure sectors for a number of years, we believe this transaction will enable us to deliver greater value to our clients, drawing on the wider capabilities of Hexaware,” said Amjad Riaz, Managing Partner, CPS.

Hexaware posted a revenue of ₹3,613 crore for the quarter ended March 31, while net profit rose 7.5% YoY to ₹351.6 crore.

title: Tamil Nadu Creates Dedicated AI Ministry in Cabinet Reshuffle
content:
Mphasis, through its foundation arm, will fund a new AI hub to drive applied research, policy insights, and responsible AI adoption.

What Actually Matters.

Mphasis is collaborating with the Indian School of Business to create an AI-focused research hub.

The initiative involves a ₹20 crore investment aimed at fostering AI research and innovation over four years.

IT services firm Mphasis has partnered with the Indian School of Business to set up an artificial intelligence (AI)-focused research and innovation hub, with the company committing around ₹20 crore over four years through its philanthropic arm.

The proposed ‘Mphasis AI Hub’ aims to accelerate AI-led research, innovation, and capacity building for societal and sectoral impact. The initial focus will be on healthcare and financial services, where enterprises are increasingly experimenting with AI-led automation, analytics and decision-making tools, Mphasis said.

The investment, routed through the Mphasis F1 Foundation, comes at a time when Indian IT services firms are stepping up collaborations with universities and research institutions to strengthen AI talent pipelines and build domain-specific AI use cases amid growing enterprise demand.

According to Mphasis, the hub will function as a dedicated interdisciplinary AI research centre at ISB and support applied research, policy studies, digital literacy initiatives, and frameworks to evaluate the business impact and sustainability of AI deployments.

The initiative will also work to develop AI learning resources, faculty-led teaching innovations, and collaboration between academia, industry, and government stakeholders.

“As AI continues to reshape industries and redefine how organisations operate, this research platform, combined with ISB’s academic expertise, will advance responsible, informed decision-making,” Deepa Nagraj, Senior Vice President & Global Head - ESG, Sparkle Innovation Ecosystem, and Communications, Mphasis, said in a statement.

Professor Madan Pillutla, Dean of ISB, said the collaboration would support the institution’s efforts to build research around ethical and responsible deployment of AI technologies. “We are thankful for this collaboration with Mphasis, as this reflects our belief that AI, when guided by rigorous research and ethical frameworks, can drive meaningful change across sectors and communities,” he added.

The partnership reflects a broader push by technology companies to move beyond AI pilot projects towards long-term ecosystem building, especially in sectors such as healthcare and BFSI, where regulatory scrutiny and responsible AI adoption are becoming increasingly important.

On May 20, Persistent Systems partnered with the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad to introduce a framework to help enterprises evaluate and scale AI investments.

For IT firms, such tie-ups also help strengthen relationships with enterprises looking for sector-specific AI capabilities while creating access to academic research and skilled talent.

content:
After Kerala, Tamil Nadu also got a dedicated Ministry for Artificial Intelligence.

What Actually Matters.

Tamil Nadu has established a dedicated ministry for artificial intelligence, becoming the second Indian state to do so.

The new ministry will focus on AI, information technology, and digital services, aiming to enhance the state's technological landscape.

Tamil Nadu has become the second state in India to establish a dedicated ministry for artificial intelligence, following a cabinet expansion by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay.

The Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology, and Digital Services portfolio will be headed by R Kumar, a Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) legislator from the Velachery assembly constituency.

The move makes Tamil Nadu one of the first states in the country to carve out a separate AI-focused department, on the lines of a model introduced in Kerala.

TVK's manifesto, released in April, set a target of ₹1.5 lakh crore for Tamil Nadu’s economy by 2036 and promised India's first dedicated Ministry of Artificial Intelligence, an AI university, and an AI city to position Tamil Nadu as the AI capital of India. The manifesto also spoke of innovation centres in Madurai, Coimbatore, Salem, and Tiruchy, with a stated target of nurturing 1,000 deeptech companies.

The technology proposals were tied to employment.

TVK pledged five lakh annual internships with stipends, a fixed timetable for government recruitment examinations, and monthly assistance for unemployed graduates registered with employment offices. Free AI-enabled competitive exam preparation centres are also part of the plan, intended to help students in smaller towns prepare for UPSC, engineering entrances, and bank examinations without the cost of private coaching in Chennai.

The manifesto's proposals span a range of sectors, including AI in agriculture for crop advisory, AI in public hospital diagnostics, and AI in government services to reduce paperwork and speed up the delivery of certificates and benefits.

title: Anthropic to Pay SpaceX $1.25 Bn Per Month, Hits $10.9 Bn Quarterly Revenue
content:
SpaceX plans to trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ‘SPCX.’

What Actually Matters.

SpaceX has officially filed for an IPO, targeting a valuation of $1.75 trillion.

The company plans to trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol 'SPCX.'

Elon Musk’s SpaceX has officially filed for an initial public offering, setting the stage for what could become one of the largest IPOs in history at a $1.75 trillion valuation and potentially giving Musk control of two publicly traded trillion-dollar companies alongside Tesla.

In a prospectus filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on May 20, SpaceX said it plans to trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ‘SPCX.’

Founded in 2002, SpaceX has evolved from a rocket startup into NASA’s largest launch partner following the retirement of the US space shuttle programme in 2011. Beyond launch services and defence contracts, the company now operates the Starlink satellite internet network, manages a constellation of roughly 10,000 satellites, and houses AI unit xAI, which previously acquired social media platform X, formerly Twitter.

In its filing, SpaceX estimated its total addressable market at $28.5 trillion, describing the pursuit of trillion-dollar opportunities as part of its “repeatable business model.”

The company identified several major growth areas, including an $870 billion broadband opportunity for Starlink, a $740 billion market for Starlink’s mobile business, a $600 billion digital advertising opportunity tied to X, and a $2.4 trillion market for AI infrastructure.

SpaceX said the largest opportunity lies in enterprise applications, which it valued at $22.7 trillion based on estimates from the Digital Cooperation Organisation.

“We believe we are still in the early days of AI transforming enterprises, with AI-powered enterprise applications poised to reshape the digital economy,” the company said in the prospectus.

The filing also revealed that SpaceX is working with Tesla on an AI agent platform called Macrohard, designed to emulate digital work and potentially build an AI-operated software company.

SpaceX reported revenue of $18.67 billion in 2025, up 33% year-over-year. However, the company swung to a net loss of $4.94 billion amid a sharp rise in expenses, particularly research and development.

The company’s Starlink satellite internet business emerged as its primary revenue driver, generating $11.4 billion in 2025, up nearly 50% from a year earlier.

Meanwhile, SpaceX’s AI division—which includes xAI (now SpaceXAI) and social media platform X—brought in $3.2 billion in revenue during 2025 but recorded an operating loss of $6.4 billion as the company aggressively expanded AI training data centre capacity.

title: NVIDIA Hits Record Quarter With $81.6 Bn Revenue as Blackwell Fuels AI Spending
content:
The chipmaker forecasts another strong quarter as Blackwell demand and AI infrastructure spending continue to rise.

What Actually Matters.

NVIDIA achieved record revenue of $81.6 billion for FY 2027, driven by AI infrastructure and Blackwell system sales.

The company forecasts second-quarter revenue of $91 billion, indicating sustained AI compute spending despite challenges in China.

NVIDIA reported record first-quarter revenue of $81.6 billion for FY 2027, up 85% year-on-year, as demand for AI infrastructure and its Blackwell systems lifted data centre sales.

The company also projected second-quarter revenue of $91 billion, signalling continued spending on AI compute despite a slowdown in China-related business.

The chipmaker reported net income of $58.3 billion for the quarter ended April 26, up 211% from a year earlier, while diluted earnings per share rose to $2.39 from $0.76. NVIDIA said data centre revenue reached a record $75.2 billion, accounting for the majority of total sales.

The company also announced an additional $80 billion share repurchase authorisation and raised its quarterly dividend to $0.25 per share from $0.01.

“The buildout of AI factories, the largest infrastructure expansion in human history, is accelerating at extraordinary speed,” said Jensen Huang, CEO at NVIDIA. “Agentic AI has arrived, doing productive work, generating real value and scaling rapidly across companies and industries.”

The semiconductor giant attributed much of the quarter’s growth to the ramp-up of its Blackwell 300 products and demand for networking technologies such as InfiniBand, Spectrum-X Ethernet and NVLink.

Data centre revenue rose 92% year-over-year and 21% sequentially. Hyperscale customers accounted for around half of that revenue, while the rest came from AI cloud providers, industrial firms, enterprises, and sovereign customers.

The company said it shipped no Hopper data centre products to China during the quarter, compared with $4.6 billion in the same period last year. NVIDIA also excluded any China data centre compute revenue from its second-quarter guidance.

Huang also mentioned earlier that the company’s market share in China has fallen to zero due to US export controls blocking sales of advanced AI chips to the country.

The company has also changed how it reports revenue to reflect what it sees as future growth areas. It now divides its business into data centre and edge computing. Within the data centre, it will separately report hyperscale and AI cloud, industrial and enterprise (ACIE) revenue.

The shift comes as the company pushes beyond cloud providers into sovereign AI projects, enterprise deployments and industrial use cases. Quarterly trends showed continued growth across both hyperscale and enterprise-linked demand, according to company data.

Alongside its earnings, NVIDIA also expanded capital returns to shareholders. The company returned about $20 billion during the quarter through stock buybacks and dividends. Its board approved an additional $80 billion share repurchase programme on May 18, without an expiry date.

The surge in revenue comes after NVIDIA has found itself at the centre of a widening geopolitical debate over AI infrastructure and chip exports to China. Huang has publicly argued against tighter export curbs, saying the US should continue selling advanced chips to China rather than ceding the market to domestic rivals such as Huawei.

Huang also joined high-level US-China discussions this month, as Washington weighed approvals for NVIDIA’s H200 chip sales to selected Chinese firms.

At the same time, in a recent podcast interview, Huang said he would not start NVIDIA again if given a second chance, reflecting on the “pain and suffering” behind building the company over three decades.

The demand for Blackwell systems continues to outpace supply. Investors are also watching how NVIDIA navigates rising competition from rivals such as AMD and cloud firms building in-house chips, even as Huang argues that demand for AI computing infrastructure is still in its early stages.
