title: Figma Brings AI Agent for Real-Time Design Collaboration
content:
The launch adds to Figma’s existing AI products, including its prompt-to-prototype tool, Figma Make, and the Figma Model Context Protocol server.

What Actually Matters.

Figma has launched an AI-powered design agent for real-time collaboration within its multiplayer canvas.

The tool is designed to enhance product design workflows, enabling teams to generate and refine designs seamlessly.

Figma has launched an AI-powered design agent embedded directly into its multiplayer canvas, aiming to help product teams generate, edit, and refine designs in real time. The company said the tool is built for product design workflows and will initially roll out in beta to paid Figma Design users over the coming weeks.

The company said the agent will not consume AI credits during the beta period, and users can join a waitlist for early access.

The agent works within Figma’s collaborative design environment, enabling teams to create design layers, automate repetitive tasks, test ideas, and receive feedback without leaving the canvas.

Figma said the tool is designed to understand workflows, design systems, and team context, while enabling designers, engineers, product managers, and marketers to work together using natural language.

“As building software gets easier, what matters most is setting direction: deciding what to work on, how it should function, what the experience should feel like,” said Loredana Crisan, Chief Design Officer at Figma.

The launch comes as software teams increasingly adopt AI tools to speed up product development. Figma said its design agent acts as a collaborator rather than a chatbot and works alongside users directly on the canvas.

The company said the tool understands product design concepts, Figma-specific workflows, and team standards developed over time. Teams can also work with multiple agents simultaneously in parallel threads without switching between tools.

“Teams can now collaborate with agents on the multiplayer canvas to test out ideas, visualise edge cases, and refine concepts together without over-indexing on the more tedious parts,” Crisan said.

Figma said the agent can automate tasks such as component setup, layout fixes, and bulk edits while staying connected to existing design systems and canvas conversations. The company added that the tool lowers the barrier to design for non-design teams by enabling users to work through natural-language prompts.

The launch adds to Figma’s existing AI products, including its prompt-to-prototype tool, Figma Make, and the Figma Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, which lets teams connect with third-party coding agents.

According to the company, weekly active users of its MCP server grew fivefold in the first quarter of 2026, reflecting growing demand for AI-assisted product development. Figma said teams can now move between design and code more smoothly by using the agent to create concepts and Figma Make to turn them into working applications.

“I work in Figma because it’s always felt like a natural extension of my hand,” said Andy Madrick, a product designer at Notion, who participated in the company’s early access programme.

“Once I attached my design libraries, I was able to move from design to code at a velocity I haven’t found in any prior workflow,” Madrick added.

title: Anthropic to Pay SpaceX $1.25 Bn Per Month, Hits $10.9 Bn Quarterly Revenue
content:
OpenAI is preparing to confidentially file draft IPO paperwork in the coming weeks.

What Actually Matters.

Anthropic is projected to generate $10.9 billion in revenue for the second quarter of 2026, marking significant growth.

The company has signed a major agreement with SpaceX, committing to pay $1.25 billion monthly for infrastructure support until 2029.

AI startup Anthropic is on pace to generate $10.9 billion in revenue during the second quarter of 2026, more than doubling its first-quarter sales and potentially marking the company’s first profitable quarter, WSJ reported.

The projected revenue surge comes as demand for Anthropic’s Claude family of AI models accelerates across enterprise, developer, and consumer markets.

The report added that the company generated $4.8 billion in revenue during the first quarter, taking total revenue for 2026 to $10 billion.

If achieved, the second-quarter figure would exceed Anthropic’s total revenue for all of last year, underscoring the blistering pace at which the AI market is expanding.

The company’s growth has been accompanied by a sharp increase in infrastructure demand. To address that demand, Anthropic recently signed a major infrastructure agreement with SpaceX to utilise the full compute capacity of the Colossus 1 data centre in Memphis, Tennessee. Under the agreement, Anthropic will reportedly pay SpaceX $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, according to SpaceX’s S-1 IPO filing/prospectus.

Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers and executives, Anthropic has emerged as one of the strongest challengers in the generative AI race. The company is best known for its Claude models and coding-focused products such as Claude Code, which have gained traction among enterprises and developers.

Anthropic’s rapid growth has also intensified investor interest. The company is reportedly in discussions to raise fresh funding at a valuation of about $900 billion, placing it among the world’s most valuable private technology firms.

Anthropic recently launched Claude Mythos Preview, a model with advanced cybersecurity capabilities, months after tensions between the company and the US Defence Department became public.

Despite its momentum, Anthropic faces intensifying competition from OpenAI, which private investors reportedly value at more than $850 billion.

OpenAI is confidentially preparing to file draft IPO paperwork in the coming weeks and could go public as early as September, while Anthropic is also reportedly exploring an IPO in 2026.

title: Scapia Raises $63 Mn Led by General Catalyst to Build AI-First Capabilities
content:
Scapia has raised $63 million, led by General Catalyst, to enhance its AI-first capabilities.

The funding will support customer acquisition, product development, and building an AI-first organisational culture.

Indian travel-fintech company Scapia has raised $63 million in a funding round led by General Catalyst, with participation from existing investors Peak XV Partners and Z47.

The company said the capital will be directed towards customer acquisition, product development, and building what it describes as an AI-first organisation.

"This round will help us strengthen our product suite further, bring more value to our customers through more offerings, scale the brand and bring in the best talent as we double down on building an AI-first culture and product approach. Our focus remains unchanged: building products that help our users travel and lead richer lives," Anil Goteti, Founder and CEO of Scapia, said in a statement.

The funding comes months after Scapia started offering co-branded credit cards in partnership with Federal Bank and BOBCARD. According to reports, it was the first in India to launch a dual-network co-branded credit card covering both Visa and RuPay networks. It also offers zero forex markup on international transactions and an Airport Privileges programme covering dining, retail, and duty-free access, in addition to lounge entry.

The company reported that flight bookings on its platform grew 5–6x year-on-year, while hotel bookings grew eight times. It attributed a portion of this growth to users in tier-2 and tier-3 cities.

"India's next wave of great consumer companies will be built around behaviours that are genuinely new - not just digital versions of what came before. Scapia understood early that a generation of Indians for whom travel is a baseline expectation, not an aspiration, needed a financial product designed around that identity. The 7x customer growth last year and the depth of what they've built across the travel stack give us real confidence in where this goes," remarked Neeraj Arora, CEO India and MENA at General Catalyst.

Sakshi Chopra of Peak XV Partners added, "Scapia has created a seamless travel-fintech experience spanning payments, rewards, zero forex markup and travel benefits in a way that deeply resonates with users. The team has combined strong product thinking with sharp execution, and we are excited to continue partnering with them as they scale."

"As consumer experiences turn AI-native, we are convinced Scapia will earn its place as a household name for the modern Indian traveller," noted Vikram Vaidyanathan, Managing Director at Z47.

title: Acceldata Launches Hybrid-Native Platform for Enterprise AI
content:
Acceldata launched the platform to help enterprises run AI and analytics across distributed data environments.

What Actually Matters.

Acceldata has launched a platform to support AI workloads across diverse data environments, addressing challenges in governance and infrastructure.

The platform targets enterprises using cloud, on-premises, hybrid, and sovereign infrastructures amidst growing operational complexity.

Acceldata has launched an autonomous data and AI platform to help enterprises run AI workloads across distributed data environments, as companies face growing challenges in governance, infrastructure readiness, and fragmented systems.

The platform is now available globally and targets enterprises operating across cloud, on-premises, hybrid, and sovereign infrastructure. The launch comes as enterprises expand AI adoption but struggle to scale systems built on fragmented data architectures.

Acceldata said the platform introduces a new compute model that allows analytics and AI agents to operate on enterprise data wherever it resides. Built on the company’s xLake architecture, the platform routes workloads across infrastructure, enforces governance, and manages data quality in hybrid-native environments.

“The lakehouse architecture was built for human access. It broke in the agentic era,” Rohit Choudhary, Co-founder and CEO of Acceldata, said in a statement.

The company said enterprises increasingly face operational complexity as they manage data across multiple cloud and on-premises systems. Many organisations also face rising infrastructure costs and inconsistent data quality as they scale AI initiatives, and traditional systems built around centralised data movement are becoming harder to maintain.

“We started Acceldata with the conviction that enterprise data would never consolidate, and that hybrid would be the durable reality,” Choudhary said. He added that enterprises, including those in India’s growing global capability centre (GCC) ecosystem, are increasingly operating across cloud, on-premises, and sovereign environments with governance requirements.

India’s emerging GCC hub, particularly in cities such as Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, and Chennai, is where enterprises increasingly drive AI, cloud, and data transformation initiatives. Acceldata said its engineering teams in Bengaluru work with global customers and GCCs to address distributed enterprise data challenges.

The platform also includes features such as workload routing for analytics and AI, governance enforcement, infrastructure optimisation, and observability tools to monitor data pipelines and detect anomalies. Acceldata said these capabilities aim to help enterprises improve trust in AI systems and reduce operational costs.

“We’re building the operating system for the AI-native enterprise, one runtime that spans every cloud, data centre, and edge, so intelligence is no longer trapped by where the data happens to live,” said Ashwin Rajeeva, Co-founder and CTO at Acceldata.

As enterprises race to deploy AI at scale, nearly half of large AI initiatives risk failure due to weak governance, legacy systems and poor workforce readiness, according to the report.

What Actually Matters.

Nearly 43% of large-scale enterprise AI initiatives are expected to fail due to inadequate governance and legacy systems.

Organisations are under pressure to deliver measurable AI value within 18 months, complicating deployment efforts.

IT services giant HCLTech has warned that nearly 43% of large-scale enterprise AI initiatives are expected to fail as companies struggle to translate aggressive AI ambitions into measurable business outcomes amid shrinking timelines for returns, according to a new report released on May 19.

The report, titled The AI Impact Imperatives, 2026, is based on a survey of 467 senior executives overseeing AI investments at enterprises with annual revenue of more than $1 billion.

It found that while adoption of AI across IT operations, software engineering and business functions has become widespread, organisations are facing mounting pressure to demonstrate measurable value within 18 months.

The findings come at a time when global enterprises are accelerating spending on generative AI and agentic AI systems, pushing technology service providers such as HCLTech, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services and Wipro to reposition themselves around AI-led transformation deals.

The study highlighted growing strain on legacy application environments, fragmented data ecosystems and operating models that were not built to support autonomous, continuously learning systems. It also pointed to weak coordination between technology teams and business leaders as a major reason why AI programmes fail to move beyond pilot stages.

“AI has moved from being a technology initiative to becoming an enterprise operating reality,” Vijay Guntur, Chief Technology Officer and Head of Ecosystems at HCLTech, said in the report. “The pressure to move fast is real, but without the right investment in people, in helping them understand, trust and work effectively alongside AI, speed can just as easily amplify failure as success.”

The report also underlined rising enterprise interest in agentic AI and physical AI applications spanning manufacturing, engineering and operational environments, marking a shift beyond traditional digital workflow automation. However, it warned that these emerging systems are raising new concerns around accountability, governance and oversight.

A key finding in the report was the lack of investment in change management despite enterprises increasingly embedding AI into core workflows.

Moreover, the study noted that many organisations are deploying AI systems without adequately preparing employees expected to work alongside them, making workforce readiness a primary execution risk.

With the rupee at a historic low against the dollar, it is expected to boost Indian IT margins. However, analysts say that is a narrow read.

What Actually Matters.

The rupee's depreciation boosts margins for Indian IT companies that invoice in USD.

Despite margin benefits, analysts warn against expecting a surge in outsourcing demand.

As the rupee sinks to record lows against the US dollar, Indian IT companies may enjoy a familiar boost to margins as they primarily invoice global clients in USD. But investors expecting a surge in outsourcing demand are reading the currency story wrong.

The Indian rupee is trading at over 96 to the US dollar this week, its weakest yet. It has depreciated by over 6% since the Iran war began in late February. For an industry that earns in dollars and pays salaries in rupees, that looks like an obvious windfall. Indian IT stocks have responded accordingly.

On May 19, Infosys’ shares jumped 4.77% as the weakening rupee boosted export visibility. TCS also rallied along with other Nifty IT stocks, with an intraday high of ₹2,377 apiece. The Nifty IT index closed the day 3.23% higher.

However, analysts are less impressed. The question circulating in boardrooms and analyst calls is whether the currency's slide translates into anything other than a temporary margin boost.

“Currency volatility has very little influence on large outsourcing decisions,” Gaurav Vasu, Founder and CEO of cognitive intelligence platform UnearthInsights, tells AIM. “CIOs in North America, the UK, France, or any other geography work with a fixed annual budget and pre-decided allocations, such as a set amount for systems of record and a set amount for services. A 5% or 10% move in the rupee does not suddenly shift their services spend from 10% of the budget to 20%.”

The rupee’s fall also does not affect the basic mechanics of how large deals are structured.

"In deal talks, rupee depreciation so far has not mattered much," says Praveen Bhadada, CEO and MD of consulting firm Neovay Global. "Big contracts are priced in dollars, so a weak rupee doesn't make the work cheaper for the client, though it certainly makes it more profitable for the vendor."

Now, the opportunity before investors and IT giants is whether they can build on the momentum of the Indian industry, seemingly more attractive with the rupee sliding, to bring in new business, accelerate deal signings, or improve the competitive position of Indian IT vendors.

How Rupee Depreciation Boosts Revenues

Indian IT firms earn most of their revenue in US dollars and euros, then convert those receipts into rupees to pay their domestic costs: salaries, real estate, and operations. When the rupee weakens, each dollar converts to more rupees, adding to the bottomline.

In FY26, the weaker rupee cushioned what would otherwise have been a far sharper margin hit—absorbing the impact of significant wage hikes, investments in AI infrastructure, rising onsite visa costs in the United States, and persistent pricing pressure from clients demanding more productivity for the same spend. In that sense, the currency acted as a buffer.

Uddheshya Goel, a financial advisor at Empirica India, expects that cushion to show up in forward guidance. "Depreciation of the rupee is positive for the overall export industry and especially the IT industry, because IT is a major component of exports in India. We can see improvement in their revenue growth guidance in the next quarter," he says.

“But companies don't tender out deals based on rupee depreciation because these are multi-year deals and there are lock-ins,” Goel adds.

A significant portion of these gains is being reinvested into AI enhancement.

“The currency gain is real, but most firms are pouring it back into AI talent, partnerships, and sales. So the tailwind is quietly funding the very AI capabilities clients are demanding as discounts,” Bhadada observes.

Clients Notice, and Adjust

In deals being actively negotiated—such as a new outsourcing contract, renewal, or a multi-year engagement—clients are factoring in the knowledge that their vendor is benefiting from the currency move. That awareness gets baked into the pricing conversation.

“On renegotiations, no clients have come back to reopen signed contracts. Pricing is under pressure because clients understand that vendors are benefiting from the weaker rupee, and that is factored into deals being negotiated for the short- and mid-term. But existing signed contracts do not get reopened just because the rupee has moved over the last two weeks,” adds Vasu.

Bhadada takes the longer view. “If the depreciation sustains, clients will ultimately always claw the benefit back through pricing. We will have to wait and watch,” he observes.

Large vs Mid-Tier Firms

Within the Indian IT sector, not all companies benefit equally from rupee depreciation. The key variable is not company size but the geography of revenue. The more a company earns from the United States—where billings are in dollars—the more it gains when the rupee weakens against the dollar, specifically.

Over the past decade, mid-tier Indian IT firms have tended to be more concentrated in the North American market than their tier-1 counterparts. Firms like TCS, Infosys, and HCLTech have diversified significantly across Europe and Asia-Pacific, diluting their exposure to the dollar-rupee move.

While tier-1 companies have largely passed AI productivity gains back to clients through innovation credits, discounting, and pricing concessions, mid-tier firms have also persuaded clients to reinvest that same money into new work.

In the fiscal year gone by, Coforge bagged a $158 million, five-year contract with a UK-based client. Persistent Systems added five large clients for AI modernisation and data engineering. Zensar Technologies landed a $210 million contract with a financial services player, while LTM (formerly LTIMindtree) signed a seven-year, $100 million contract with a European medtech company for AI solutions.

The rupee's fall has certainly prevented several tier-1 companies from reporting the kind of margin compression that would have alarmed investors and triggered guidance cuts. However, set against what AI is doing to the traditional IT services model, the rupee's movement is a sideshow.

"In the current times, the focus on AI is outweighing anything else," Bhadada says.

Clients are asking vendors to demonstrate that AI-augmented delivery can compress timelines, reduce headcount requirements, and produce measurable productivity gains. That question will determine far more about the trajectory of Indian IT revenues than any exchange rate.

title: OpenAI Model Solves 80-Year-Old Geometry Problem
content:
The proof was independently checked by external mathematicians, while a companion paper explaining the argument and its implications was also released.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI's model has disproved a central conjecture in discrete geometry that remained unresolved for nearly 80 years.

This solution addresses the planar unit distance problem first posed by mathematician Paul Erdős in 1946.

An internal model developed by OpenAI has disproved a central conjecture in discrete geometry that had remained unresolved for nearly 80 years, in what researchers describe as the first autonomous AI solution to a major open mathematics problem.

The result concerns the planar unit distance problem, first posed by Hungarian mathematician Paul Erdős in 1946. The problem asks: among nnn points placed on a plane, how many pairs can be exactly one unit apart?

For decades, mathematicians believed the maximum number of such pairs grew only slightly faster than linearly, a conjecture associated with Erdős. OpenAI said its model constructed an infinite family of point configurations that exceeded the previously assumed limit by a polynomial factor.

The proof was independently checked by external mathematicians, while a companion paper explaining the argument and its implications was also released. According to OpenAI, the proof emerged from a general-purpose reasoning model rather than a system specifically trained for mathematics.

“This has been one of Erdős’ favourite problems,” said Noga Alon, a combinatorialist at Princeton University. “The solution of the problem by the internal model of OpenAI is, in my opinion, an outstanding achievement, settling a long-standing open problem.”

The problem has been regarded as one of the most important questions in combinatorial geometry because of its simple formulation and resistance to proof.

Tim Gowers, a Fields Medal winner, described the development as “a milestone in AI mathematics.”

The proof also renewed discussion about AI’s role in scientific research. OpenAI said the result suggests advanced reasoning models may eventually contribute to research in fields including physics, biology, engineering, and materials science by maintaining long chains of reasoning and identifying connections across disciplines.

OpenAI said the work highlights a future in which AI systems assist researchers by exploring technical ideas, while human experts continue to decide which problems matter and how results should be interpreted.

title: Persistent, IIM Ahmedabad Roll Out Framework to Help Enterprises Measure Returns on AI Bets
content:
The framework, called ‘AI Value Compass’, aims to help enterprises prioritise AI projects and improve governance as companies struggle to scale pilot programmes into measurable business outcomes.

What Actually Matters.

The 'AI Value Compass' framework helps enterprises assess and scale their AI investments effectively.

It focuses on evaluating AI initiatives based on business alignment, operational integration, and governance.

Persistent Systems has partnered with the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Ahmedabad to introduce a framework to help enterprises evaluate and scale AI investments, as companies increasingly grapple with turning experimental AI projects into tangible business outcomes.

The Pune-based IT services company on May 19 said the framework, called ‘AI Value Compass’, is designed to help enterprises assess AI readiness across business alignment, operational integration, data preparedness, governance and workforce readiness.

The move comes at a time when enterprises globally are accelerating spending on generative AI and agentic AI, but many continue to face challenges in scaling pilot projects into production deployments with measurable returns.

Unlike technology-centric AI adoption models, the company noted that the framework evaluates AI initiatives through an enterprise operating model lens. Persistent said the study was developed jointly with IIM Ahmedabad through a research collaboration combining industry and academic inputs.

“At the core of the research is a structured methodology that evaluates AI initiatives across five critical enterprise vectors: business alignment, people readiness, operational integration, data preparedness and risk and governance,” the company said in the statement.

The company added that the framework is intended to help enterprises identify readiness gaps early in the AI lifecycle, prioritise high-impact initiatives based on objective criteria, strengthen data, operational and governance foundations, improve adoption readiness by aligning teams, and increase the predictability and consistency of AI-driven business outcomes.

Jaideep Vijay Dhok, Chief Operating Officer, Technology at Persistent, said enterprises now have wider access to AI technologies, but the focus is shifting towards making the “right investment and execution choices at scale”.

“As organisations advance in their AI journeys, the need for structured approaches to assess readiness, sequence initiatives, and align AI efforts with business priorities is becoming more important,” Dhok said.

Ankur Sinha, Professor, Operations and Decision Sciences, IIM Ahmedabad, said many enterprises continue to focus on localised efficiency gains instead of using AI for broader strategic transformation.

“Our study with Persistent highlights fundamental gaps, including the absence of clear AI leadership, lack of a coherent strategic vision, poorly defined success metrics, and weak ownership and governance structures that significantly constrain the ability of organisations to unlock long-term value from AI,” Sinha noted.

Persistent said it is already using the framework in client engagements and plans to further refine it through continued industry-academia collaboration.

The announcement also reflects a broader trend of Indian IT services firms increasingly partnering with academic institutions, hyperscalers and AI ecosystem players to build frameworks, accelerators and governance models for enterprise AI adoption.

title: ANSCER Robotics Raises $5.4 Mn to Expand Industrial Automation
content:
The robotics startup will use fresh capital to scale products, US operations, and partner network.

What Actually Matters.

ANSCER Robotics has secured $5.4 million in Series A funding to enhance its product platform and expand US operations.

The funding aims to tackle low automation adoption in warehouses, where around 80% operate with minimal automation.

Industrial robotics startup ANSCER Robotics has raised $5.4 million (about ₹45 crore) in a Series A funding round led by IAN Alpha Fund, with participation from Info Edge and other angel investors.

The Bengaluru-based company will use the funding to strengthen its product platform, expand operations in the United States, and grow its partner ecosystem across global markets.

The funding comes as industries face labour shortages, supply chain disruptions, and pressure to improve operational efficiency. ANSCER said it aims to address low automation adoption in warehouses and factories through connected automation systems that reduce manual work and improve productivity. According to the company, nearly 80% of warehouses still operate with little to no automation, citing McKinsey & Company data.

“Industrial automation is entering a new era where machines are moving beyond following instructions toward understanding context, learning from operations, and working alongside enterprise intelligence,” said Ribin Mathew, CEO of ANSCER Robotics.

He added that the company plans to scale its India-built automation platform globally and make advanced automation more accessible for industrial customers.

The startup also recently opened a manufacturing facility in Bengaluru with a 20,000 square feet testing zone where robots undergo performance and endurance testing before deployment. The company said the facility can manufacture more than 1,000 robots annually to support deployments across factories and warehouses.

The facility will support its partner-led deployments as it expands globally. It also plans to accelerate the development of next-generation automation systems for connected industrial environments.

“Industrial automation is rapidly evolving from a focus on efficiency to becoming a strategic driver of resilience, intelligence, and competitiveness for global enterprises,” said Rajnish Kapur, Managing Partner at IAN Alpha Fund.

He said ANSCER’s combination of robotics, software, and deployment capabilities positioned it to address growing global demand for automation systems.

Founded in 2020 by Ribin Mathew, Ebin Sunny, Raghu V and Raj Mohan, ANSCER Robotics builds autonomous robots and software systems for factories and warehouses. The company operates from Bengaluru and maintains a sales and support office in Dallas, serving customers across the US, Europe, and Asia Pacific.

title: Techno Digital Opens Mumbai Edge Data Centre in Partnership with RailTel
content:
The centre has been built to support sovereign and compliance-driven workloads, an increasingly important consideration for enterprises navigating India’s evolving data governance landscape.

What Actually Matters.

Techno Digital has launched a new Mumbai Edge Data Centre in collaboration with RailTel to support compliance-driven workloads.

The facility is designed to meet Rated-3 infrastructure standards, ensuring enterprise-grade reliability and efficiency.

Techno Digital, the digital infrastructure arm of Techno Electric and Engineering Company Limited (TEECL), has commissioned a new Mumbai Edge Data Centre in Mahalakshmi, South Mumbai, in partnership with RailTel Corporation of India, a Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprise.

The facility, announced on May 19, is fully operational and built to Rated-3 infrastructure standards, designed to deliver enterprise-grade reliability through a cost-efficient, right-sized infrastructure footprint. The Mumbai Edge Data Centre is an addition to the city’s digital infrastructure landscape that targets the latency-sensitive demands of one of India's most concentrated financial and commercial hubs.

The data centre addresses a long-standing pain point for enterprises operating across Mumbai’s major financial districts. Situated in Mahalakshmi, the facility offers latency of less than 150 microseconds from BSE in Nariman Point and Fort, and less than 250 microseconds from NSE in BKC, enabling markedly improved responsiveness for real-time applications. Its proximity to key business districts, including BKC, Worli, Lower Parel, and Fort, means enterprises can deploy infrastructure far closer to their operations, improving execution speed and overall system performance, the company said in a statement.

The facility thrives on RailTel’s nationwide fibre network spanning over 63,000 kilometres, ensuring broad connectivity across the country. Its location near Mumbai’s cable landing stations is vital for its capacity for high-speed global connectivity, while maintaining low-latency domestic performance. The centre has also been built to support sovereign and compliance-driven workloads, an increasingly important consideration for enterprises navigating India's evolving data governance landscape.

Following Mumbai, the company plans to launch five additional Edge locations “in quick succession”, with a long-term roadmap to scale to 102 locations over the next three to four years, totalling 200MW.

Ankit Saraiya, Director and CEO of Techno Digital, said, “As India’s digital economy scales, infrastructure requirements are evolving beyond capacity to include proximity and performance. The Mumbai Edge Data Centre is designed to align infrastructure with demand centres, particularly in high-performance environments such as financial services and real-time platforms.”

Meanwhile, Amit Agrawal, President of Techno Digital, said, “In a city like Mumbai, where milliseconds can impact outcomes, infrastructure placement becomes critical. This facility combines low-latency architecture, strong connectivity, and sovereign infrastructure to support performance-critical workloads ranging from trading and fintech platforms to real-time AI inferencing and enterprise applications. It is designed to deliver the reliability and responsiveness required in latency-sensitive environments.”

title: AI, Data Analytics Can Help Detect Corruption in Govt Tenders: CAG’s K Sanjay Murthy
content:
The use of AI-led monitoring systems and data-based analysis can enable regulators and audit bodies to identify suspicious procurement patterns at an early stage.

What Actually Matters.

AI and data analytics are vital for detecting corruption in government procurement processes.

Collaboration between audit bodies and competition regulators is essential for safeguarding public funds.

AI and data analytics could become critical tools in detecting corruption and collusion in government procurement, Comptroller and Auditor General of India K Sanjay Murthy said on May 20, urging stronger collaboration between India’s audit and competition watchdogs to protect public funds.

Speaking at the 17th Annual Day of the Competition Commission of India, Murthy said the growing scale and complexity of public procurement require technology-driven oversight systems capable of identifying anti-competitive practices such as bid rigging and cartelisation.

He noted that closer coordination between the CAG and the Competition Commission of India (CCI) would help authorities detect unfair practices in government tenders more effectively while improving transparency and accountability in public spending.

According to Murthy, the use of AI-led monitoring systems and data-based analysis can enable regulators and audit bodies to identify suspicious procurement patterns at an early stage, reducing financial leakages and strengthening governance outcomes.

He also stressed that anti-competitive conduct in public procurement has a direct impact on citizen welfare by affecting how efficiently taxpayer money is spent.

The remarks come as government institutions and regulators across India increasingly explore the use of AI, analytics and digital governance technologies to modernise compliance systems and improve oversight across public sector operations.

title: Informatica Expands Partnerships with Databricks & Snowflake to Build Governed Infrastructure for Agentic AI
content:
nformatica integrated its Intelligent Data Management Cloud with Databricks Agent Bricks through MCP servers to improve AI agent interoperability.

What Actually Matters.

Informatica has expanded partnerships with Databricks and Snowflake to enhance operational capabilities for agentic AI systems.

The integration of Informatica's Intelligent Data Management Cloud with Databricks improves AI agent interoperability through Model Context Protocol servers.

At the Informatica World 2026 in Las Vegas, Informatica announced expanded partnerships with Databricks and Snowflake to help enterprises operationalise agentic AI systems using governed enterprise data.

The announcements reflect a broader shift in the enterprise AI market, where organisations are moving beyond experimentation and prioritising scalable AI deployments with stronger governance, interoperability and metadata management layers.

As part of its expanded collaboration with Databricks, Informatica introduced native integration between its Intelligent Data Management Cloud (IDMC) and Databricks Agent Bricks through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. MCP is emerging as a standard for interoperability between AI agents and enterprise systems. The integration allows enterprises to invoke Informatica services such as metadata search and address validation directly within AI workflows without requiring custom integrations.

“The organisations that win the AI race will be those that put trusted, governed data in front of their agents from day one,” said Rik Tamm-Daniels, Vice President, Ecosystems and Technology, Informatica.

The company also introduced a connector for Databricks Lakebase, designed to ingest and govern transactional OLTP data flowing into production AI systems. Another update enables enterprises to publish “golden records” from the Informatica Master Data Management platform directly into Databricks SQL with pre-configured schemas for customer, supplier, product and location datasets.

Moreover, Informatica announced expanded governance interoperability through Unity Catalog tag extraction, allowing governance tags from Databricks Unity Catalog to surface within Informatica’s Cloud Data Governance and Catalog platform.

“Customers consistently ask us to help them operationalise agents with well-governed data that can scale in production,” said Stephen Orban, Senior Vice President, Product Ecosystem and Partnerships, Databricks.

Alongside the Databricks announcements, Informatica also expanded its partnership with Snowflake around AI governance and open-format data ecosystems. The company introduced support for MCP-based integrations with Snowflake Cortex AI, allowing governed enterprise data to be directly connected to AI agents and analytics workloads operating on Snowflake infrastructure.

Informatica also announced broader governance support for open-format ecosystems such as Apache Iceberg environments, enabling enterprises to maintain unified governance across structured and unstructured data systems spanning hybrid and multi-cloud architectures.

“We’re embracing Unity Catalog and adding the holistic interoperability enterprise customers are asking for to securely democratise all their enterprise data assets,” Tamm-Daniels added.

title: Mistral AI Acquires Emmi AI to Build a European Industrial AI Stack
content:
Mistral aims to be the dominant AI partner for manufacturers and industrial enterprises operating in sectors including aerospace, automotive, semiconductors, and energy.

What Actually Matters.

Mistral AI has acquired Emmi AI to enhance its capabilities in industrial AI for key sectors.

Emmi AI's expertise in physics-based modelling will accelerate industrial simulation workflows.

European AI powerhouse Mistral AI has acquired Emmi AI, a physics-focused AI startup founded in Linz, Austria.

Emmi brings deep expertise in industrial simulation and physics-based modelling. With the deal, Mistral hopes to be the dominant AI partner for manufacturers and industrial enterprises operating in high-stakes sectors, including aerospace, automotive, semiconductors, and energy.

Emmi AI is developing physics AI models to accelerate industrial simulation workflows. The company counts more than 30 researchers and engineers on its team.

Emmi's co-founders and the full team are expected to join Mistral AI's Science and Applied AI divisions in May 2026, bringing with them capabilities in areas ranging from real-time power grid stabilisation to injection moulding simulation and automotive safety testing.

Beyond the technical and commercial rationale, the acquisition carries significant geographical significance. Linz will formally become a Mistral AI office, joining an international network that includes Paris, London, Amsterdam, Munich, San Francisco, and Singapore.

Mistral has also signalled its intention to hire further talent locally across Austria, Germany, and Lithuania, where the Emmi team is currently based.

"This strategic acquisition cements Mistral AI's leadership in industrial AI and positions us as the partner of choice for manufacturers in high-stakes sectors like aerospace, automotive, or semiconductors. It empowers our customers with a fully integrated platform to solve complex challenges, transform core R&D processes, and accelerate high-value innovation," Arthur Mensch, Co-founder and CEO of Mistral AI, said in a statement.

"This acquisition marks a turning point for industrial innovation. By engineering the first comprehensive AI stack fuelled by Physics AI, we are set to deliver real-time simulations and sophisticated digital twins. We aim to break through long-standing technical barriers that have slowed progress for decades, enabling our partners to solve the world's most daunting engineering challenges," Co-founder and Chief Science Officer Guillaume Lample added.

Johannes Brandstetter, Emmi AI's co-founder and Chief Science Officer, spoke of the broader implications for the AI4Science movement. "At Emmi AI, we have dedicated ourselves to solving high-stakes physical challenges, ranging from the real-time stabilisation of power grids to the intricate simulation of injection moulding and automotive safety testing.”

“Together, we are providing the foundational intelligence required to design and build the next generation of aircraft, vehicles, and semiconductors," he added.

The acquisition arrives at a moment of heightened focus on European technological sovereignty, with the continent's leading AI companies increasingly looking to anchor critical industrial capabilities domestically.

title: isolved Expands India Operations With New Hyderabad GCC Focused on AI Innovation
content:
For isolved, real estate economics emerged as a key factor in the decision to establish its GCC in Hyderabad over other cities.

What Actually Matters.

isolved has established a new Global Capability Centre (GCC) in Hyderabad to enhance its AI-driven capabilities.

The GCC will serve as a strategic engineering and innovation centre for isolved's People Cloud platform.

isolved, a US-based human capital management (HCM) solutions provider, has expanded its India presence with a new GCC in Hyderabad. Advisory firm Zinnov played an enabling role in setting up the GCC.

The new facility, located at 23 Nordwest, spans 28,000 sq ft and will serve as a strategic engineering and innovation centre supporting the company’s unified People Cloud platform.

The expansion is part of isolved’s broader efforts to scale AI-driven capabilities, product engineering, and platform delivery as it builds what it describes as a “platform of action” for the future of HCM.

The company plans to hire around 400 employees in India by the end of 2027 across engineering, AI, product development, and back-office operations, including payroll and tax processing.

Speaking to AIM at the launch, Yogesh More, GM, isolved India, mentioned that the company has now entered a major scaling phase. “As part of this growth strategy, there was a clear need to expand capabilities across technology, implementation, and customer support. That is one of the key reasons why isolved chose India—and specifically Hyderabad—to establish its GCC,” he said.

The company evaluated multiple cities, including Pune and Bengaluru, before finalising Hyderabad. While Bengaluru continues to dominate India’s GCC landscape with its mature ecosystem and deep enterprise networks, factors such as infrastructure scalability, talent availability, and real estate economics played an important role in the decision-making process.

The Hyderabad GCC is expected to evolve into a centre of excellence for engineering and AI innovation, supporting isolved’s push toward more personalised and AI-integrated HCM solutions.

“Hyderabad is emerging as an AI talent hub that will support our technology growth,” said More. “As the HCM industry undergoes rapid transformation, isolved’s GCC in India positions us to accelerate product modernisation and innovation, enabling data-driven decision-making for businesses.”

More indicated that AI innovation emerging from the Hyderabad centre will increasingly focus on personalised workflows, AI-enabled platform capabilities, and next-generation agentic AI experiences integrated into the company’s HCM ecosystem.

More also highlighted Hyderabad’s advantages in attracting GCC investments, including its expanding talent ecosystem, relatively lower operational costs, and infrastructure scalability, compared to more saturated markets such as Bengaluru.

In short, Hyderabad is increasingly attracting not only life sciences and pharmaceutical GCCs, traditionally associated with the city, but also enterprises across HR technology, AI, SaaS, and enterprise software sectors seeking large-scale engineering and product capabilities.

With more than 200,000 employers using its HCM platform and over 9 million employees served across the United States, isolved’s India expansion reflects the broader trend of global enterprises building AI-focused engineering hubs in India to support long-term product innovation and operational scale.

title: Informatica Deepens AI Integrations with AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft
content:
The announcements, made at Informatica World 2026, are centred around helping enterprises deploy agentic AI systems across multi-cloud environments.

What Actually Matters.

Informatica is enhancing AI systems integration with major cloud providers to optimise enterprise AI infrastructure.

The company aims to support agentic AI deployment while ensuring data governance and interoperability across multi-cloud environments.

Informatica has announced a series of integrations with Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft as the company pushes deeper into enterprise AI infrastructure and governance.

The announcements, made at Informatica World 2026, are centred around helping enterprises deploy agentic AI systems across multi-cloud environments while maintaining governance, interoperability, and trusted access to enterprise data.

With AWS, Informatica introduced deeper integration of its headless data management services and CLAIRE AI capabilities into AWS AI ecosystems, including AWS Agent Registry and Amazon Quick. The company said its Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers will allow enterprises to invoke Informatica services, such as metadata discovery, governance controls. and data management, directly within AWS-based AI workflows.

The company also announced that its CLAIRE AI agent skills will integrate with AWS Agent Registry, enabling organisations to discover, share and reuse AI agents and tools across enterprise environments.

“The organisations that win the AI race will be those that put trusted, governed data in front of their agents from day one,” Rik Tamm-Daniels, Vice President, Ecosystems and Technology, Informatica, said in a statement.

Alongside the AWS announcements, Informatica expanded its collaboration with Google Cloud by integrating its conversational AI assistant, CLAIRE GPT, directly into Google Cloud environments. The integration allows enterprise teams to interact with data systems using natural language prompts for governance checks, metadata discovery, data quality assessment, and catalogue enrichment.

Informatica also extended support for Google’s Gemini Enterprise ecosystem and announced compatibility with Google’s Agent2Agent interoperability protocol, which enables AI agents across different enterprise systems and cloud environments to communicate with each other.

Separately, the company announced expanded collaboration with Microsoft. Informatica said its headless Intelligent Data Management Cloud will now be available within Microsoft Foundry, enabling enterprises to integrate Informatica’s governance and data management capabilities into Microsoft AI development workflows.

The company also expanded integration with Microsoft Fabric to improve interoperability between analytics systems, AI applications, and enterprise governance layers.

title: Blackstone, Google Launch TPU Cloud Venture With $5 Bn Commitment
content:
The new company will offer data centre capacity, networking, operations, and access to Google Cloud’s TPUs through a compute-as-a-service model.

What Actually Matters.

Blackstone and Google formed a joint venture for AI computing infrastructure.

The new company will provide cloud access to Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs).

Blackstone and Google on May 18 announced a joint venture to build a new US-based company that will provide cloud access to Google’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), as demand for AI computing infrastructure rises.

Blackstone said it will commit an initial $5 billion in equity capital to the venture, which aims to bring 500 megawatts (MW) of capacity online in 2027, with plans to expand over time.

The new company will offer data centre capacity, networking, operations, and access to Google Cloud’s TPUs through a compute-as-a-service model. Customers will be able to access the chips outside Google Cloud’s existing platform.

Google’s TPUs are custom AI chips designed for training and inference workloads. At Google Cloud Next 2026, the search giant unveiled its eighth-generation lineup, including the TPU 8t, optimised for training massive models, and the TPU 8i, for inference and agentic AI workloads that require rapid reasoning and multi-step execution.

The company said the processors have been used internally for more than a decade and currently support products including Gemini, as well as workloads for AI labs, financial firms, and high-performance computing applications.

Blackstone named Benjamin Treynor Sloss, a longtime Google executive involved in the company’s infrastructure and operations business, as Chief Executive Officer of the new venture.

“We see a generational opportunity to invest capital at scale, building AI infrastructure,” Jon Gray, President and COO of Blackstone, said in a statement. “This new company has enormous potential as it helps to meet the unprecedented demand for compute.”

Thomas Kurian, CEO of Google Cloud, said the partnership would “help meet growing demand for TPUs, which are optimised specifically for efficiency and performance in the AI era.”

The partnership comes as technology companies and infrastructure investors increase spending on AI data centres and computing hardware to support the expansion of generative AI services.

Blackstone said Google will provide hardware, including TPUs, along with software and related services to the venture. The company said the arrangement is intended to give enterprises more flexibility in running AI workloads on Google-designed chips.

Jas Khaira, Head of Blackstone N1, said the venture was designed to back infrastructure platforms tied to long-term AI demand. “Google’s TPUs, a decade in the making and foundational to the AI economy, are exactly the kind of platform BXN1 was built to back,” he said.

title: Google Brings AI Educator Series to India, Partners With UNICEF to Boost Learning Outcomes
content:
While Anthropic was already led by former OpenAI executive Dario Amodei, Karpathy’s arrival adds another prominent early OpenAI figure to its ranks.

What Actually Matters.

Andrej Karpathy has joined Anthropic, enhancing its team with another former OpenAI figure.

Karpathy believes the coming years will be crucial for advancements in large language models.

Former OpenAI researcher and Tesla’s former AI director Andrej Karpathy has announced that he has joined Anthropic, marking a notable talent shift in the intensifying AI race between major frontier labs.

In a post on X, Karpathy said, “I think the next few years at the frontier of LLMs will be especially formative. I am very excited to join the team here and get back to R&D.”

Since his departure from OpenAI, Karpathy has remained active in AI education, particularly through widely watched YouTube lectures and technical explainers, where he broke down complex machine learning concepts for developers and researchers.

His educational work helped cement his reputation as one of the AI industry’s most influential communicators beyond research itself.

In 2024, he founded Eureka Labs, an AI-focused education startup focused on building learning experiences around machine learning and large language models, including its flagship LLM101n course.

While Karpathy did not reveal specifics regarding the future of Eureka Labs, he indicated that his educational work is only paused, not abandoned, writing: “I remain deeply passionate about education and plan to resume my work on it in time.”

Andrej @karpathy is back in the game! I would have loved for him to rejoin @OpenAI, but I'm happy he's at any frontier lab pushing the field forward. It’s easy to frame this as zero-sum among the labs, but in truth we’re collectively advancing the most important tech of our era. https://t.co/BHoTBjPrd0

— Noam Brown (@polynoamial) May 19, 2026

(Noam Brown is a research scientist at OpenAI)

According to a report from Axios, Karpathy is set to help Anthropic launch a new team focused on pretraining research using Claude's AI models.

Karpathy is widely credited with popularising the term “vibe coding,” which he coined to describe a style of software development where users build applications by describing what they want in natural language and letting AI generate much of the underlying code.

The term has since become shorthand for a new wave of AI-assisted app building enabled by platforms such as Replit, Lovable, and similar tools that allow users to create software through prompts rather than traditional coding workflows.

Karpathy also recently drew attention for his open-source project AutoResearch, a lightweight autonomous AI experimentation framework that lets AI agents run and evaluate machine learning experiments automatically on a single GPU.

The project, published on GitHub, became one of the more widely discussed examples of Karpathy’s broader vision for AI-assisted research workflows, with agents iterating through experiments, selecting improvements, and committing changes with minimal human intervention.

Karpathy’s move to Anthropic carries symbolic weight because one of OpenAI’s founding researchers is now joining a rival AI company established by former OpenAI executives, including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei. Karpathy is generally described as a founding member or founding researcher of OpenAI.

“I think the next few years at the frontier of LLMs will be especially formative,” Karpathy said while announcing his move. He is joining a company that in recent months has increasingly focused on AI models built for software development, an area closely aligned with Karpathy’s own interests, reflected in several coding and AI-assisted development projects he has shared on X.

title: Google Brings AI Educator Series to India, Partners With UNICEF to Boost Learning Outcomes
content:
Google’s initiatives, announced at the Education World Forum 2026 in London, will cover teacher training in six Indian languages and span four countries.

What Actually Matters.

Google is expanding its AI education efforts in India, bringing the AI Educator Series to schools and higher education.

The AI Educator Series will offer mobile-first training for teachers, localised into six Indian languages.

Google is expanding its artificial intelligence education efforts in India, with plans to roll out its AI Educator Series across Indian schools and higher education institutions. It has also announced a new multi-country partnership with UNICEF to improve learning outcomes for underserved students.

Both initiatives were announced at the Education World Forum 2026 in London.

The Google AI Educator Series (GES), which was originally launched in the United States to provide free Gemini training to K-12 and higher education faculty, will now be extended to Indian educators. The programme offers practical, mobile-first training tailored to the specific needs of teachers and faculty across the country.

Google has confirmed partnerships with the governments of Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, and Assam, the Union Territory of Ladakh, and the Punjab School Education Board to deliver the initiative. In its first year, the training will be localised into six Indian languages—Assamese, Hindi, Marathi, Telugu, Odia, and Punjabi—beginning with select state pilots.

The company said it is actively looking to expand its collaboration to additional states, higher education institutions, and regulatory bodies.

UNICEF Partnership Targets Digital Divide

In a separate but related announcement, Google for Education and Google.org are partnering with UNICEF on a first-of-its-kind initiative to support education innovation in India, Brazil, Pakistan, and Kenya. The three-year programme will focus on improving literacy and numeracy outcomes, training educators, and building more accessible school systems.

The partnership will integrate AI-powered tools including Gemini, NotebookLM, and Google's India-first ReadAlong app, which supports foundational reading fluency through guided practice. Google.org will fund the initiative, and Google will provide technology access, product workshops, and ongoing technical support for UNICEF staff, local governments, and education leaders.

"We will responsibly integrate AI-powered tools to help accelerate progress and reimagine learning, pairing Google's technology with UNICEF's deep expertise in building education systems to ensure every student has the tools they need to succeed," Google said in its announcement.

UNICEF will publish annual impact reports measuring the effectiveness of solutions deployed across each country, with the goal of identifying approaches that are scalable and replicable globally.

The announcements build on Google's existing education commitments in India, which include helping establish India's first AI-enabled state university and integrating Gemini into student learning and test-preparation platforms. Google.org's AI Opportunity Fund has also recently been expanded across the Asia-Pacific region, covering 19 countries and targeting millions of students, teachers, and workers with AI skills training.

title: Meta to Axe 10% of Workforce as It Shifts 7,000 Employees to AI Teams: Report
content:
The changes are part of a broader overhaul at Meta as the company ramps up spending on AI infrastructure and products.

What Actually Matters.

Meta is undertaking a significant workforce restructuring this week.

The company plans to lay off 10% of its global workforce.

Meta is preparing to carry out a sweeping workforce restructuring this week, including layoffs, employee transfers, and organisational changes tied to its AI ambitions, Reuters reported.

The Facebook parent plans to lay off 10% of its global workforce on May 20 while moving around 7,000 employees into new AI-focused initiatives, according to a memo from Chief People Officer Janelle Gale accessed by Reuters.

The restructuring, together with previous transfers and the rollback of 6,000 open roles, will affect roughly 20% of the company’s workforce.

The changes are part of a broader overhaul at Meta as the company ramps up spending on AI infrastructure and products, while also redesigning internal operations around AI agents and automation.

Meta employed 77,986 people at the end of March, according to company filings. Employees in North America were instructed to work from home on Wednesday as the layoffs are carried out.

According to the Reuters report, the restructuring includes eliminating managerial positions and reassigning employees to newly created AI-focused groups, including Applied AI Engineering, Agent Transformation Accelerator, and Central Analytics.

The initiatives aim to develop AI agents capable of autonomously performing tasks currently handled by human workers.

The restructuring has triggered internal backlash among employees. More than 1,000 staff members have signed a petition opposing the installation of mouse-tracking software intended to help train Meta’s AI systems by replicating how humans interact with computers.

Workers have also criticised executives internally over privacy concerns tied to the tracking technology and over the company’s silence following earlier reports about impending layoffs.

title: Salesforce to Spend Nearly $300 Mn on Anthropic Tokens in 2026
content:
Salesforce currently has around 15,000 engineers, many of whom now work with AI tools such as Anthropic Claude.

What Actually Matters.

Salesforce anticipates spending nearly $300 million on Anthropic tokens in 2026.

Much of the anticipated spending will be directed towards coding-related work.

Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff said the company expects to spend nearly $300 million on Anthropic tokens in 2026.

Speaking on the All-In podcast, Benioff said much of the spending would go towards coding-related work, while praising AI coding agents and Anthropic’s models for improving efficiency across Salesforce.

“These coding agents are awesome. Anthropic is awesome,” Benioff said.

Salesforce currently has around 15,000 engineers, many of whom now use AI tools such as Anthropic models, OpenAI Codex, and Cursor in their development workflows.

Benioff added that AI tools are helping Salesforce reduce development costs and accelerate product creation. The company is also working on new coding capabilities within Slack, the workplace collaboration platform Salesforce acquired in 2021.

“You’re going to see some cool stuff with Slack and code I’m not ready to talk about yet,” he said. “But there’s no question that we are in a new moment in coding.”

Benioff also said companies will increasingly need an “intermediary layer” capable of deciding which AI tasks should be routed to expensive frontier models such as Anthropic’s Claude and which can be handled using smaller, cheaper models.

Tokens are units of text processed by large language models, and AI companies generally charge enterprise customers based on the number of tokens consumed. Analysts say a $300 million annual spend would make Salesforce one of Anthropic’s largest commercial customers.

Benioff has previously linked AI adoption to workforce efficiency gains at Salesforce. Last year, he said AI agents helped the company reduce its support organisation from 9,000 employees to 5,000.

Despite the freeze on engineering hires, Salesforce continued expanding in other parts of the business, saying it planned to add between 1,000 and 2,000 salespeople to drive enterprise adoption of its AI products.

title: Google DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis Was Early Investor in Anthropic: Report
content:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei reportedly considers Demis Hassabis a role model.

What Actually Matters.

Demis Hassabis, Google DeepMind's head, was an early angel investor in Anthropic.

Hassabis's investment showcases his broad influence within the AI industry.

Google DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis was an early investor in Anthropic, the Financial Times reported.

The report added that Hassabis made an angel investment in Anthropic before the company emerged as one of the world’s fastest-growing AI startups.

Anthropic is now in early talks to raise at least $30 billion in a new funding round that could value the company at more than $900 billion, potentially making it more valuable than OpenAI, valued at $852 billion.

Hassabis’s investment highlights his influence across the AI industry, where former researchers from Google DeepMind have launched more than a dozen startups since 2021, collectively raising at least $14 billion, according to PitchBook and Dealroom data cited by FT.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei considers Hassabis a role model, according to the report. Google has separately invested billions of dollars into the OpenAI rival through cloud and AI partnership agreements.

FT also reported that Hassabis has backed companies founded by former colleagues, including Inflection AI, launched by DeepMind co-founder Mustafa Suleyman, and Ineffable Intelligence, founded by longtime collaborator David Silver.

Meanwhile, senior DeepMind executives have moved into influential positions across Google’s AI operations. DeepMind CTO Koray Kavukcuoglu was recently elevated to Chief AI Architect at Google, while Pushmeet Kohli was promoted to Chief Scientist at Google Cloud.

“Demis has a huge amount of soft power at Google and beyond,” Matt Clifford, Co-founder of Entrepreneurs First and a longtime associate of Hassabis, told FT. “He was a pioneer before it was obvious what AI was, and the availability of capital for his protégés is pretty striking.

title: Karnataka Fast-Tracks Drone Testing Facility Near Bengaluru, Policy Framework
content:
Representatives from ideaForge, Aereo, Asteria Aerospace, NewSpace Research & Technologies, and Vecros, among others, attended the meeting.

What Actually Matters.

Karnataka aims to be India's leading drone innovation hub.

The state plans to accelerate drone testing infrastructure.

The Karnataka government plans to accelerate the development of drone testing infrastructure and strengthen policy support for the sector, as part of its broader push to position the state as India’s leading drone innovation hub.

The move was discussed during a high-level drone industry consultation on May 15, chaired by Priyank Kharge, Karnataka’s Minister for Electronics, IT & Biotechnology and Rural Development & Panchayat Raj, in collaboration with the Drone Federation of India.

The consultation brought together drone startups, industry stakeholders, and ecosystem enablers to discuss infrastructure development, regulatory support and adoption of drone technologies across sectors. Representatives from ideaForge, Aereo, Asteria Aerospace, NewSpace Research & Technologies, and Vecros, among others, attended the discussion.

“Karnataka is committed to leading India’s drone economy by moving decisively on infrastructure, policy enablement, and real-world adoption,” Kharge said. “Our focus is on creating shared testing facilities, simplifying regulatory pathways, and enabling a strong ecosystem for startups and industry to innovate and scale.”

A major focus of the meeting was the creation of a dedicated drone flight testing facility near Bengaluru. The government said it plans to fast-track operationalisation of the facility while enabling early-stage industry access alongside institutional partnerships and supporting infrastructure development.

The discussions also centred on streamlining approvals and standard operating procedures for emerging drone applications, strengthening workforce training and startup support, and expanding drone adoption in governance and public service delivery.

Among the proposals discussed was the launch of an annual ‘Bengaluru Drone Festival’ featuring drone racing, hackathons, innovation showcases, and public engagement activities to position Bengaluru as a national centre for drone technology.

This infrastructure will boost advanced research in various engineering fields.

Schaeffler India has launched a new computational research infrastructure at the Foundation for Science Innovation and Development in Bengaluru, aimed at strengthening advanced research capabilities in high-performance computing, sustainable mobility, materials engineering, and energy systems.

The initiative, announced recently, is part of Schaeffler India’s broader collaboration with the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) and is expected to support large-scale simulations, data-intensive modelling, and advanced analytics for research and industry projects.

As part of the project, the facility has been upgraded with dedicated lab space, advanced in-rack cooling systems, power backup infrastructure, and high-performance hybrid computing workstations and clusters designed to improve computational efficiency and accelerate scientific research.

The enhanced infrastructure will support IISc faculty, FSID-incubated startups, external startups, MSMEs, and industry partners engaged in collaborative R&D projects. It is also expected to indirectly benefit PhD scholars, undergraduate and postgraduate students, postdoctoral researchers, and the wider academic ecosystem.

Meanwhile, Schaeffler India has also signed a Master Research Agreement (MRA) with IISc to enable multiple future collaborative research projects.

CEO Harsha Kadam said the initiative reflects the company’s long-term commitment to industry-academia collaboration and research-driven innovation.

“At Schaeffler India, we are committed to building skills and manufacturing excellence rooted in India’s unique strengths, aligned with its needs, and geared towards creating lasting value. Such efforts depend on strong academia-industry collaboration, with institutions like the IISc playing a critical role in equipping researchers with the right tools and expertise,” Kadam said.

He added that the facility, supported under Schaeffler India’s CSR programme HOPE, would enable research across multiple streams while strengthening the pipeline of joint projects between the company and IISc.

Sai Gautam Gopalakrishnan said the initiative would help build a large-scale computational ecosystem with a long-term target of achieving peak computing performance of nearly 32 PFLOPs through a mix of CPUs and GPUs.

“With the long-term aim of creating a computational facility with a peak performance of around 32 PFLOPs, comprising a mixture of CPUs and GPUs, the facility will be highly beneficial for the research groups at IISc, startups incubated at FSID, and industries that collaborate with FSID/IISc,” he said.

B Gurumoorthy, Director of the Foundation for Science Innovation and Development, said the new infrastructure would significantly enhance FSID’s ability to support interdisciplinary research and industry collaboration.

“This collaboration with Schaeffler India marks an important step in enhancing FSID’s capabilities in high-end simulations, data-intensive research, and next-generation technology development. We see this as a strong example of how industry-academia partnerships can accelerate research and innovation with real-world relevance,” he said.

According to the company, the partnership aims to accelerate scientific research outcomes, strengthen workforce capabilities, and support the development of industry-relevant solutions in advanced engineering and mobility technologies.

title: Uttar Pradesh Hosts Conclave to Explore AI Ambitions as Lucknow Emerges as Tech Innovation Hub
content:
Uttar Pradesh, especially Lucknow, is emerging as a suitable centre for AI innovation in India.

What Actually Matters.

Uttar Pradesh is advancing its AI goals, with Lucknow becoming a key innovation hub.

The 'AI Transformation Conclave 2026' involved many administrators discussing AI in governance.

Uttar Pradesh is accelerating its AI ambitions, with the state positioning Lucknow as a growing centre for AI innovation, governance transformation, and deeptech investment.

The state recently held the ‘AI Transformation Conclave 2026’ in Lucknow, where more than 50 IAS officers and senior administrators from across the country participated in discussions around AI-led governance and digital transformation.

A key highlight of the conclave was a high-level workshop titled “The AI-Powered Public Administrator: Competencies for a New Era of Governance,” conducted by Subi Chaturvedi, Founder of NIHIT and Sherpa of Working Group-7 of the India-US CEO Forum.

“Uttar Pradesh, especially Lucknow, is emerging as the most suitable centre for AI innovation in India,” Chaturvedi said, adding that the city is evolving from a cultural centre into a hub for innovation and technology under the current administration.

She noted that investments and deeptech operations by companies such as InMobi are contributing to the development of a broader ecosystem encompassing governance, research, digital infrastructure, talent and entrepreneurship in the state.

The conclave also featured discussions around Uttar Pradesh’s AI policy roadmap, including the recently approved ₹368 crore AI City project in Lucknow’s Vrindavan Yojana and the ₹225 crore allocation earmarked for the UP AI Mission.

Manoj Kumar Singh, Chief Executive Officer of the State Transformation Commission, said Uttar Pradesh is working towards becoming a national model for AI-driven governance, which could further support the state’s ambition of a trillion-dollar economy.

Meanwhile, Alok Kumar, Principal Secretary of the IT and Electronics Department, said the government is committed to building infrastructure for emerging technologies, including AI, quantum computing, and deeptech innovation.

The conclave also explored the role of AI in cybersecurity, digital governance, MSMEs, startups, and citizen-centric services. Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ‘MANAV’ framework, Chaturvedi emphasised the importance of ethical, accountable, and human-centric AI systems.

NIHIT, the platform behind the initiative, operates under the India-US CEO Forum and is supported by InMobi, Mastercard, and Tata Sons to promote collaboration in innovation, startups, MSMEs, cybersecurity, and supply chain ecosystems between India and the United States.

title: SAP Powers TCS’ Large-Scale Payroll Transformation in Cloud Migration
content:
Cloud migration consolidates TCS’ multinational payroll operations onto a single SAP platform, delivering faster processing and improved resilience with no operational downtime.

What Actually Matters.

TCS has modernised its global payroll operations by migrating to SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud, enhancing efficiency.

The transition consolidates payroll functions across countries into a unified cloud-based platform, improving resilience.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has successfully modernised its global payroll operations by transitioning to RISE with SAP S/4HANA Private Cloud, achieving up to 40% faster payroll processing with zero disruption to ongoing operations, SAP announced on May 18.

The transformation consolidates TCS' payroll operations across multiple countries and regions into a unified, cloud-based environment built on SAP S/4HANA Cloud on AWS. The initiative was designed to improve consistency, strengthen operational resilience, and build a scalable digital foundation aligned with the company's long-term technology roadmap.

The phased migration was supported by robust validation frameworks, including multiple mock cycles and parallel payroll execution, embedded throughout the transition to ensure accuracy, regulatory compliance, and operational stability across regions.

The overhaul delivered several measurable improvements. Payroll processing speeds increased by 30-40% through better batch performance and faster cycle completion.

The new architecture also standardises global payroll processing while preserving local flexibility within a single environment to accommodate country-specific regulatory and business requirements. More than 20 high-volume interfaces across HR, finance, and third-party systems were integrated to maintain data integrity and operational stability. The company also gains a future-ready digital core intended to support analytics-led insights and intelligent capabilities aligned with SAP's broader innovation roadmap.

Janardhan Santhanam, Chief Information Officer at TCS, said, “As one of SAP's strategic partners, TCS believes in leading by example. This transformation reflects our commitment to building a cloud-first, digital enterprise core. Executing a modernisation of this scale with minimal disruption demonstrates how global organisations can transform while strengthening agility and resilience.”

The migration also resulted in a more streamlined payroll architecture, reduced fragmentation, and improved visibility across operations—outcomes TCS says will support more data-driven and adaptive workforce management going forward.

Rahul Baheti, India Growth Officer at SAP Indian Subcontinent, said, “This milestone with TCS demonstrates how RISE with SAP can support the most demanding, mission-critical workloads at a global scale—securely, resiliently, and without disruption. It also reflects the strength of a longstanding partnership built on shared innovation and trust, as SAP and TCS continue to collaborate to help enterprises reimagine and modernise core business processes for the future.”

The project was supported by AWS as a hyperscaler partner, highlighting the growing momentum among large enterprises to migrate core business processes to cloud platforms. The SAP–TCS partnership, which spans years of collaborative enterprise technology work, underpins the transformation.

TCS, which generated consolidated revenues of over $30 billion in the fiscal year ended March 2026, employs a highly skilled workforce spread across 56 countries. SAP, listed on the NYSE under the ticker SAP, has provided enterprise application software to organisations worldwide for more than 50 years.
