title: AI Isn’t the Problem, Adoption Is: Megha Sinha and Sreekanth Menon Launch New Book
content:
The authors say enterprise AI adoption often breaks down due to low trust, unclear accountability, and workflows that were never redesigned for how employees actually work.

What Actually Matters.

Enterprise AI adoption often fails due to low trust and unclear accountability.

Organizations struggle because they do not redesign workflows for AI systems.

Megha Sinha, former Vice President for AI Platforms and Enterprise AI Solutions at Genpact, has launched Human-First Equation for AI Adoption, a new book co-authored with Sreekanth Menon. Senior VP, Global AI Practice & Innovation, who is also a member of the AIM Leaders Council.

In a LinkedIn post, Sinha said enterprises often struggle with AI adoption, not because the technology fails, but because organisations fail to redesign workflows and build trust around AI systems.

“AI systems do not fail. The models work. The dashboards load. The governance reviews are complete. And still, adoption quietly collapses,” she wrote.

The book explores how enterprises can improve AI adoption through trust, empathy, workflow redesign, and change management. According to the authors, behavioural resistance and unclear accountability remain major barriers even when AI systems are technically successful.

Menon, in a separate LinkedIn post, described the book as the culmination of years of industry experience and collaboration.

“This book represents years of experience, months of thinking and discussion, and weeks of collaboration to actually put together everything on paper,” he wrote, adding that he was eager to see the conversations the book would spark among readers.

The launch comes amid growing enterprise investments in generative and agentic AI, as organisations increasingly focus on improving adoption and business outcomes beyond pilot deployments.

Sinha also noted that the book release follows her exit from Genpact in April after six years with the company.

title: HCLTech, Red Hat Partner to Roll Out Enterprise AI Infrastructure Solutions
content:
The collaboration will strengthen HCLTech’s AI Factory ecosystem as enterprises increasingly move from AI experimentation to large-scale deployment.

HCLTech has announced a strategic collaboration with IBM-owned software firm Red Hat to deliver enterprise-grade artificial intelligence infrastructure solutions as companies accelerate adoption of AI across their operations.

The partnership will strengthen HCLTech’s AI Factory ecosystem, which brings together multiple technology partners to offer AI infrastructure solutions to enterprise customers, the company said in a stock exchange filing on May 14.

Under the collaboration, the HCLTech AI Factory with Red Hat will be built on Red Hat AI Enterprise and will provide a unified platform for running AI workloads across on-premises, cloud and edge environments.

The companies said the solutions are designed to improve infrastructure efficiency and reduce inference costs through model optimisation, distributed serving and unified operations, while offering an enterprise-grade data foundation with governance and lineage to support reliable AI operations at scale.

“Enterprises are moving beyond experimentation to operationalising AI across their core businesses,” said Rampal Singh, Senior Vice President and Global Business Head – Hybrid Cloud Business Unit at HCLTech. “The HCLTech AI Factory with Red Hat is designed to help organisations industrialise AI, bringing together the right foundational building blocks to translate AI investments into measurable business outcomes.”

Ryan King, vice president, AI and Infrastructure Partners at Red Hat, said the collaboration would help enterprises deploy and manage AI workloads consistently from data centres to the edge.

“The launch of HCLTech AI Factory, powered by Red Hat AI Enterprise, is a significant milestone in bringing enterprise-grade AI to our customers,” said King. “This collaboration helps enterprises industrialise AI, translating their investments into real business value.”

The announcement comes at a time when IT services companies are deepening partnerships with global technology firms to capitalise on rising enterprise spending on generative AI infrastructure, platforms and deployment services. HCLTech has been expanding its AI-led offerings across cloud, engineering and digital transformation segments as clients increasingly seek large-scale AI implementation.

HCLTech reported an 11.2% year-on-year rise in FY26, to ₹1,30,144 crore ($14.66 billion), while the net income for the full year stayed largely flat at ₹17,361 crore ($1.96 billion), down 0.2% YoY.

title: Karnataka, Chile Explore Deeptech, Startup Partnerships in Bengaluru
content:
The engagement builds on the Letter of Intent signed between Karnataka and Chile during the Bengaluru Tech Summit.

What Actually Matters.

Karnataka and Chile are exploring partnerships in deep technology, clean energy, and biotechnology.

Discussions focused on expanding cooperation in emerging technologies and startup exchanges.

Karnataka is looking to deepen its global innovation partnerships with Chile, with both sides exploring collaboration opportunities in deeptech, clean energy, biotechnology, and startup ecosystems during a high-level meeting held in Bengaluru.

The Chilean delegation, led by Minister of Foreign Affairs Francisco Pérez Mackenna, met Priyank Kharge, IT-BT minister, Karnataka, as part of Chile’s broader India engagements aimed at strengthening technology and innovation partnerships.

The discussions focused on expanding cooperation across emerging technologies, startup exchanges, research partnerships, and sustainable industrial innovation under the framework of the Global Innovation Alliance (GIA).

The engagement builds on the Letter of Intent signed between Karnataka and Chile during the Bengaluru Tech Summit, which established a framework for collaboration in startups, emerging technologies, research, and skill development.

“Karnataka today is a global hub for deep-tech, AI, biotech, aerospace, and advanced research, backed by one of the strongest talent pipelines in the world,” said Priyank Kharge.

“As partners under the Global Innovation Alliance, we must move beyond agreements on paper to actionable collaboration. We are keen to work with Chile on startup exchanges, market access programmes, and building joint innovation corridors, including R&D centres, incubators, and accelerators. Chile’s position as a gateway to Latin America presents a significant opportunity for our startups to scale globally,” he added.

Mackenna said Chile sees strong opportunities to partner with Karnataka as it transitions toward a knowledge- and technology-driven economy.

“Chile is actively advancing its transition towards a knowledge- and technology-driven economy. Our engagement with Karnataka reflects our interest in building strong innovation partnerships that enable technology exchange, talent collaboration, and access to dynamic startup ecosystems,” he said.

“We see strong potential to work together across sectors such as clean energy, digital technologies, and emerging industries, while also strengthening Chile’s role as a bridge between India and Latin America,” he added.

Among the key areas discussed during the meeting were renewable energy partnerships, including green hydrogen, marine biotechnology, aquaculture technologies, and AI applications across traditional industries.

Both sides also emphasised the need to move beyond MoUs toward implementation-focused partnerships through structured startup exchange programmes, market access initiatives, and deeper ecosystem linkages under the GIA framework.

Following the meeting, the Chilean delegation visited C-CAMP to explore Karnataka’s biotechnology innovation ecosystem and understand its role in supporting startups, translational research, and life sciences innovation.

title: OpenAI Brings Codex to ChatGPT Mobile App for Remote Coding Work
content:
The feature allows users to monitor, approve, and manage coding tasks running across laptops and remote environments directly from their phones.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI has added Codex support to the ChatGPT mobile app.

This feature allows users to manage coding tasks remotely via their phones.

OpenAI has introduced Codex support in the ChatGPT mobile app, allowing users to monitor and manage coding tasks running across laptops, remote machines, and managed environments directly from their phones.

The feature, currently rolling out in preview on iOS and Android, is available across all ChatGPT plans, including Free and Go. The support for connecting phones to the Windows Codex app is expected later.

OpenAI said more than four million people now use Codex every week.

“Now you can do that from your phone,” the company said in its announcement, referring to actions such as answering questions, approving commands, reviewing outputs, or changing directions while Codex handles long-running work.

According to OpenAI, the mobile experience mirrors the live state of whichever machine Codex is connected to, including laptops, Mac minis, or remote development environments.

Users can access active threads, approvals, plugins, project context, screenshots, terminal output, test results, and code diffs in real time while files and credentials remain on the connected machine.

“This is more than the ability to remotely control a single task or dispatch new tasks to your computer,” OpenAI said. “From your phone, you can work across all of your threads, review outputs, approve commands, change models, or start something new.”

The company said Codex relies on a secure relay layer that keeps trusted machines reachable without exposing them directly to the public internet. The infrastructure also synchronises session state and context across devices that are signed in to ChatGPT.

OpenAI outlined several use cases for the mobile integration, including investigating bugs, reviewing refactoring decisions during commutes, preparing summaries for customer calls, and initiating new coding tasks while away from a desk.

In one example, the company said users can ask Codex to inspect files, reproduce browser issues, run tests, and work toward fixes while they are away from their computer.

The company also announced that Remote SSH support is now generally available, enabling Codex to connect directly to managed remote environments. The desktop app can detect SSH hosts from a user’s configuration and allow projects and threads to run inside remote machines.

OpenAI said the same relay infrastructure makes those remote environments accessible across authorised ChatGPT devices, enabling users to begin work on desktop systems and continue supervising tasks from mobile devices.

The company additionally introduced programmatic access tokens for enterprise and business users. OpenAI said these scoped credentials can be used for CI pipelines, release workflows, and internal automations.

Hooks, now generally available across all plans, can be configured to scan prompts for secrets, run validators, log conversations, create memories, or customise Codex behaviour for specific repositories and directories.

OpenAI also announced support for HIPAA-compliant use of Codex in local environments for eligible ChatGPT Enterprise workspaces. The company said the capability is intended to help healthcare organisations support patient care and operational workflows.

title: Telangana's Life Sciences Hub Hits $145 Bn, Draws ₹84,000 Cr in 2 Years
content:
Hyderabad now hosts technology and innovation centres of nine of the world’s 10 ten life sciences companies.

What Actually Matters.

Telangana's life sciences sector has reached a valuation of $145 billion.

The state attracted significant investments, totalling ₹84,000 crore, in the last two years.

Telangana has emerged as a $145 billion life sciences ecosystem, driven by ₹84,000 crore ($8.8 billion) in investments over the past two years, marking the fastest expansion phase in the state’s history.

The milestone was highlighted during the seventh board meeting of the Telangana Life Sciences Foundation, chaired by D Sridhar Babu, IT Minister, Telangana, in Hyderabad.

According to the foundation, Telangana’s life sciences sector has nearly tripled in size since 2016, positioning Hyderabad among the world’s leading hubs for pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, medical technology, and health-tech innovation.

A major highlight of the ecosystem’s growth is that Hyderabad now hosts technology and innovation centres of nine of the world’s top 10 life sciences companies, making it the only region outside the United States to achieve this distinction.

The rapid expansion has been attributed to policy continuity, global partnerships, and institution-building initiatives aimed at strengthening the state’s integrated life sciences ecosystem.

“Telangana’s life sciences sector has witnessed unprecedented growth over the past two years. A focused ecosystem-building effort, anchored in strong institutional leadership and policy continuity, has helped attract investments, forging global partnerships, and accelerating innovation and growth. We are at the cusp of the next phase of growth enabled by the initiatives in the Next Generation Life Sciences Policy,” D Sridhar Babu said.

The Minister also called for faster implementation of committed investments linked to the proposed Green Pharma City project, noting that investment MoUs worth nearly ₹20,000 crore ($2.1 billion) should be grounded at the earliest.

The meeting additionally introduced Sarvesh Singh as the foundation’s new CEO. Singh outlined the organisation’s priorities for 2026-27, including accelerating implementation of the state’s life sciences policy and advancing initiatives such as the Telangana School of Life Sciences.

title: HCLTech Leads $300 Million Funding for Sarvam AI, Elevating Valuation to $1.5 Billion: Report
content:
In addition to HCLTech’s $150 million, Sarvam will receive $50 million from Bessemer Venture Partners and another $100 million from a consortium of investors, including NVIDIA.

What Actually Matters.

HCLTech is leading a $300 million funding round for Bengaluru-based Sarvam AI, with a valuation of approximately $1.5 billion.

The funding includes $150 million from HCLTech, $50 million from Bessemer Venture Partners, and $100 million from a consortium including NVIDIA.

HCLTech is set to lead a $300 million funding round in Bengaluru-based startup Sarvam AI with an investment of around $150 million, Moneycontrol reported. The round is expected to value Sarvam AI at approximately $1.5 billion post-money, potentially making it one of India’s most valuable homegrown artificial intelligence startups.

The report said venture capital firm Bessemer Venture Partners is likely to invest another $50 million, while the remaining $100 million is expected to come from a group of investors including NVIDIA, Prosperity7 Ventures, Activate, Glade Brook, and some existing backers. Sources familiar with the matter told Moneycontrol that discussions are at an advanced stage and the deal could close in the coming weeks.

If completed, the investment could be considered a rare move, made by an Indian IT services company into a domestic AI startup. Industry observers see the move as a strategic shift for legacy IT firms as generative AI and automation increasingly reshape outsourcing, software development, and enterprise services businesses.

The proposed funding round is also expected to be the largest private-market funding deal for an Indian AI startup this year. Sarvam AI had previously raised about $41 million in a seed and Series A round in 2023 from investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Peak XV Partners, and Khosla Ventures.

Founded by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar, Sarvam AI is a leading company advancing India’s AI initiatives. The startup focuses on developing large language models, multilingual AI systems, and voice-based tools tailored for Indian languages and enterprise needs. Earlier this year, it open-sourced its Sarvam-30B and Sarvam-105B models, which were trained on government-supported infrastructure.

Presented at the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi, these models serve as India-centric alternatives to global systems like ChatGPT and Gemini, optimised for Indian languages, local contexts, and speech interactions.

title: Rajasthan Enters Semiconductor Race With First Chip Packaging Plant in Bhiwadi
content:
the facility currently has an annual packaging capacity of 60 million semiconductor units

What Actually Matters.

Rajasthan has established its first semiconductor plant in Bhiwadi.

This facility signifies Rajasthan's entry into India's chip manufacturing sector.

Rajasthan on Thursday entered India’s semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem with the inauguration of its first semiconductor plant in Bhiwadi, marking a major push toward electronics and chip manufacturing in the state.

The semiconductor ATMP/OSAT facility of Sahasra Semiconductors, along with the Electronics Manufacturing Cluster (EMC) developed by ELCINA at Salarpur, Khushkhera, was virtually inaugurated by Ashwini Vaishnaw in the presence of Bhajan Lal Sharma and Bhupender Yadav.

Calling it a “historic day” for Rajasthan, Ashwini Vaishnaw said the state’s entry into semiconductors marked its participation in a strategically critical industry with growing geopolitical significance.

The minister highlighted India’s rapid growth in electronics manufacturing over the last 12 years, stating that production has increased six-fold to nearly ₹13 lakh crore, while exports have reached around ₹4.24 lakh crore. He added that mobile phones have now become India’s top export commodity.

Vaishnaw credited the growth to initiatives such as Make in India, Digital India, Atmanirbhar Bharat, the Indian Semiconductor Mission (ISM), Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes, Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMC), and the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS).

Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma said Rajasthan had recently introduced its Semiconductor Policy in March 2026 and emphasised the state government’s plans to develop the Delhi NCR-adjacent region into a manufacturing hub.

Bhupender Yadav noted that while Bhiwadi was traditionally known for the automobile sector, the region is now emerging as a center for semiconductor and electronics manufacturing as well.

The newly inaugurated ELCINA Electronics Manufacturing Cluster has been developed across 50.3 acres with a project cost of ₹46.09 crore, including ₹20.24 crore in support from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology under the EMC scheme.

The cluster has already attracted planned investments exceeding ₹1,200 crore from 20 companies involved in semiconductor packaging, electronic components, EV parts, industrial electronics, RFID technologies, and air-conditioner manufacturing.

According to officials, 11 companies are already operational within the cluster, with cumulative investments of over ₹900 crore and employment generation for more than 2,700 people.

The semiconductor ATMP/OSAT facility developed by Sahasra Semiconductors has emerged as India’s first commercially operational memory packaging facility from the SME sector.

Built under MeitY’s SPECS scheme with an investment of over ₹150 crore, the facility currently has an annual packaging capacity of 60 million semiconductor units, including products such as Micro SD cards, NAND flash-based products, and Chip on Board (CoB) packaging.

The company plans to scale capacity to nearly 400–600 million units annually over the next two to three years.

Officials said over 60% of the facility’s production is already being exported to markets including the United States, Germany, France, Eastern Europe, China, and Nepal, positioning India as an emerging player in trusted global semiconductor supply chains.

title: Amazon Continues Layoffs Amid Expanding AI Investments, India Push
content:
The layoffs come even as Amazon continues to significantly expand its investments in AI and cloud infrastructure globally.

What Actually Matters.

Amazon is continuing to reduce its workforce, including recent cuts in its Selling Partner Services unit.

These layoffs are part of a broader company strategy focused on efficiency and leaner operations.

Amazon has reportedly cut more jobs this week, with layoffs impacting employees within its Selling Partner Services (SPS) division, according to a report by Business Insider. The SPS unit works closely with millions of third-party merchants selling on Amazon’s marketplace, assisting with onboarding, logistics, and account support.

The latest cuts follow nearly 30,000 layoffs announced across multiple waves since late last year. Earlier this year, Amazon had also reduced a small number of roles within its robotics division. While the company did not disclose the exact number of employees affected this week, it described the layoffs as impacting a “relatively small number” of roles.

Amazon reportedly said it routinely reviews its organisational structure to align with long-term priorities and added that impacted employees would receive healthcare support, severance packages, and job placement assistance.

The layoffs come even as Amazon continues to significantly expand its investments in AI and cloud infrastructure globally. CEO Andy Jassy has repeatedly stressed efficiency, automation, and leaner operations as key priorities for the company.

Amazon has been aggressively integrating AI across retail operations, logistics, customer support, advertising, and AWS. The company has also expanded its investments in custom AI chips such as Trainium and Inferentia, while deepening its partnership with AI startup Anthropic as part of its broader generative AI strategy.

The company has simultaneously strengthened its ambitions in India. At the recent AWS Summit Bengaluru 2026, Amazon announced an additional $35 billion investment in India by 2030. This comes on top of the nearly $40 billion it has already invested in the country, taking Amazon’s total planned investment in India to approximately $75 billion by the end of the decade.

Amazon said the investments would support cloud infrastructure, AI innovation, logistics, data centres, and the expansion of digital services in India, positioning the country as a major hub in its global AI and cloud strategy.

title: Ministry of Ayush Partners with BHASHINI to Expand Multilingual AI Healthcare Services
content:
The collaboration aims to improve multilingual accessibility across Ayush portals and services using AI-based translation, speech and voice technologies.

What Actually Matters.

The Ministry of Ayush signed an MoU with BHASHINI to enhance multilingual access to Ayush digital platforms using AI technologies.

The initiative aims to make Ayush services available in all 22 scheduled Indian languages, improving healthcare accessibility.

The Ministry of Ayush, on May 14, signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD) under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to expand multilingual access across Ayush digital platforms using artificial intelligence-powered language technologies.

The collaboration aims to make Ayush services and knowledge systems accessible in all 22 scheduled Indian languages recognised under the Constitution by integrating BHASHINI technologies into the ministry’s digital ecosystem.

The initiative, launched under the ‘BHASHINI Rajyam - A BHASHINI Sahayogi Program’ will integrate BHASHINI’s translation, speech and voice technologies into various Ayush digital services, portals and AI-enabled tools developed under the Ayush Grid initiative.

According to the ministry, the partnership is expected to improve accessibility to healthcare and wellness-related information across diverse linguistic regions, particularly in rural and underserved areas.

Under the Ayush Grid initiative, the Ministry of Ayush has been working on digital healthcare systems covering sectors such as healthcare delivery, research, education, drug administration and capacity building. The collaboration with BHASHINI would help strengthen multilingual communication for systems related to Ayurveda, yoga and naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa and Homoeopathy.

The MoU was signed by Subodh Kumar, Director, Ministry of Ayush, and Amitabh Nag, Chief Executive Officer of the Digital India BHASHINI Division in the presence of senior officials from both ministries.

Speaking during the event, Ayush Secretary, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, said that making Ayush knowledge available in regional languages was important for inclusive healthcare delivery and wider public outreach.

The initiative would support the creation of domain-specific multilingual terminology databases and contextual AI models tailored for healthcare and wellness communication.

The ministry added that BHASHINI technologies have already been integrated into certain Ayush platforms, including the Yoga Portal and the Ayush Grid master portal, where they reportedly received positive feedback from users accessing services in local languages.

During the event, BHASHINI showcased several AI-enabled tools, including multilingual doctor-patient interaction systems capable of generating prescriptions, real-time meeting transcription tools, voice-based CV-building solutions and technologies aimed at preserving India’s ancient manuscripts.

The collaboration reflects its broader effort to build a more inclusive, accessible and citizen-centric digital healthcare ecosystem using emerging AI technologies.

The feature allows users to monitor, approve, and manage coding tasks running across laptops and remote environments directly from their phones.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI has added Codex support to the ChatGPT mobile app.

This feature allows users to manage coding tasks remotely via their phones.

OpenAI has introduced Codex support in the ChatGPT mobile app, allowing users to monitor and manage coding tasks running across laptops, remote machines, and managed environments directly from their phones.

The feature, currently rolling out in preview on iOS and Android, is available across all ChatGPT plans, including Free and Go. The support for connecting phones to the Windows Codex app is expected later.

OpenAI said more than four million people now use Codex every week.

“Now you can do that from your phone,” the company said in its announcement, referring to actions such as answering questions, approving commands, reviewing outputs, or changing directions while Codex handles long-running work.

According to OpenAI, the mobile experience mirrors the live state of whichever machine Codex is connected to, including laptops, Mac minis, or remote development environments.

Users can access active threads, approvals, plugins, project context, screenshots, terminal output, test results, and code diffs in real time while files and credentials remain on the connected machine.

“This is more than the ability to remotely control a single task or dispatch new tasks to your computer,” OpenAI said. “From your phone, you can work across all of your threads, review outputs, approve commands, change models, or start something new.”

The company said Codex relies on a secure relay layer that keeps trusted machines reachable without exposing them directly to the public internet. The infrastructure also synchronises session state and context across devices that are signed in to ChatGPT.

OpenAI outlined several use cases for the mobile integration, including investigating bugs, reviewing refactoring decisions during commutes, preparing summaries for customer calls, and initiating new coding tasks while away from a desk.

In one example, the company said users can ask Codex to inspect files, reproduce browser issues, run tests, and work toward fixes while they are away from their computer.

The company also announced that Remote SSH support is now generally available, enabling Codex to connect directly to managed remote environments. The desktop app can detect SSH hosts from a user’s configuration and allow projects and threads to run inside remote machines.

OpenAI said the same relay infrastructure makes those remote environments accessible across authorised ChatGPT devices, enabling users to begin work on desktop systems and continue supervising tasks from mobile devices.

The company additionally introduced programmatic access tokens for enterprise and business users. OpenAI said these scoped credentials can be used for CI pipelines, release workflows, and internal automations.

Hooks, now generally available across all plans, can be configured to scan prompts for secrets, run validators, log conversations, create memories, or customise Codex behaviour for specific repositories and directories.

OpenAI also announced support for HIPAA-compliant use of Codex in local environments for eligible ChatGPT Enterprise workspaces. The company said the capability is intended to help healthcare organisations support patient care and operational workflows.

title: AI-Native Startup Exaforce Secures $125 Mn to Scale Agentic Security Operations
content:
Beyond geographic expansion, the company intends to bolster its presence in research and development by enhancing multi-model AI capabilities and aiding enterprises in operationalising agentic workflows.

What Actually Matters.

Exaforce secured $125 million in Series B funding to enhance its agentic security operations.

The investment will focus on advancing multi-model AI capabilities and improving security team workflows.

AI startup Exaforce has announced a $125 million Series B funding round to advance its "agentic" security operations. The round was led by HarbourVest, Peak XV, Mayfield, Khosla Ventures, Seligman Ventures, and AICONIC.

This latest round follows a $75 million Series A raise last year, bringing the firm’s total capital raised to $200 million.

The company has earmarked the investment for the advancement of Exaforce’s core platform, specifically its multi-model AI and real-time knowledge graph to empower security teams to investigate, detect, and neutralise threats.

Unlike traditional security layers that act as a secondary "add-on," Exaforce aims to be the primary environment where defenders operate. By leveraging a real-time data architecture, the platform addresses the latency issues that often plague legacy systems during high-stakes breaches.

“We built Exaforce to be the platform defenders actually work in, not just an AI layer on top of existing tools,” said Ankur Singla, CEO of Exaforce, in a statement. “It starts with a real-time knowledge graph that gives agents complete context from the start, and extends into rich investigation and visualisation experiences that put security engineers and AI agents on the same page.”

Vinod Khosla, Founder of Khosla Ventures, noted that the platform’s impact goes beyond simple automation. "The biggest opportunity in enterprise security is flipping the economics, so that defenders, not attackers, hold the leverage. When the cost of defence drops by an order of magnitude, the entire calculus of security changes. Exaforce is the architecture that makes that possible," he stated.

With the fresh capital, Exaforce plans to scale its global footprint, targeting aggressive go-to-market strategies in Japan and Europe. Beyond geographic expansion, the company intends to bolster its presence in research and development by enhancing multi-model AI capabilities, aiding enterprises in operationalising agentic workflows, and providing managed detection and response support to improve resilience across critical infrastructure.

title: Cisco to Cut Nearly 4,000 Jobs in Q4 Amid AI Shift
content:
The networking company plans workforce cuts while increasing investments in AI, silicon, optics, and security.

What Actually Matters.

Cisco plans to cut nearly 4,000 jobs, affecting less than 5% of its workforce, as part of a strategic shift.

The company is increasing investments in artificial intelligence, security, silicon, and optics amid rising competition.

Networking company Cisco will cut nearly 4,000 jobs in the fourth quarter of FY26 as it shifts investments towards artificial intelligence, security, silicon, and optics, the company’s CEO, Chuck Robbins, wrote in an email to employees that was posted on the company’s blog.

The layoffs will affect less than 5% of Cisco’s global workforce, with notifications beginning on May 14 in line with local laws and regulations.

The announcement came alongside Cisco’s third-quarter (January 25 to April 25, 2026) earnings, where the company reported record revenue of $15.8 billion, up 12% year-on-year.

Robbins said the company is restructuring amid intensifying competition and customers accelerating AI infrastructure spending.

“We are making changes today that will result in the reduction of our overall workforce in Q4 by fewer than 4,000 jobs,” Robbins wrote in the email to employees. He added that the company must “continuously shift investment toward the areas where demand and long-term value creation are strongest.”

Cisco said it will continue hiring and investing in areas tied to future growth, especially AI-related technologies. The company identified silicon, optics, security and AI adoption across operations as priority areas for investment.

Robbins said the company’s current performance came despite “a rapidly changing market, with intensifying competition, and a global shortage of components critical to support our portfolio and the AI buildout from our customers.”

The company also outlined support measures for affected employees.

Cisco said impacted workers would receive pro-rated FY26 bonuses, access to placement services and one year of access to Cisco U courses and certifications. According to the company, its placement programme has helped 75% of participants secure new roles.

Cisco said managers would directly communicate details regarding timelines, benefits and support resources to affected employees in each country. The company plans to discuss the changes further during its Cisco Beat meeting on May 21.

“To those leaving Cisco, thank you for your contribution, your dedication, and the mark you have made on this company,” Robbins wrote. “We are deeply grateful and are committed to handling this transition with the care, clarity, and respect that defines our culture.”

title: DoT Signs ₹2,432 Crore BharatNet Deal to Connect Rural Andhra Pradesh
content:
Under the BharatNet rollout, the state will upgrade existing fibre infrastructure, connect newly created Gram Panchayats and extend internet access to nearly 4,000 villages on demand.

What Actually Matters.

The Department of Telecommunications signed a ₹2,432 crore deal to enhance broadband connectivity in rural Andhra Pradesh.

The project will upgrade existing fibre infrastructure and connect nearly 4,000 villages to improve internet access.

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), on May 14, signed an agreement with the Andhra Pradesh government and related agencies for the implementation of the Amended BharatNet Programme (ABP) in the state aimed at expanding broadband connectivity across rural regions.

The agreement was signed between Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN), DoT, the Andhra Pradesh government, Andhra Pradesh BharatNet Infrastructure Limited (APBIL), Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) and Andhra Pradesh State FiberNet Limited (APSFL) at Sanchar Bhawan in New Delhi.

The Centre has approved financial support of ₹2,432 crore for the project which will focus on strengthening digital infrastructure and improving last-mile internet connectivity in rural Andhra Pradesh.

According to the government, the programme will cover 13,426 Gram Panchayats across the state. This includes upgrading 1,692 Phase-I Gram Panchayats from linear to ring topology to improve network resilience, covering 11,254 Phase-II Gram Panchayats, and including 480 newly created Gram Panchayats.

Moreover, connectivity will be extended to 3,942 villages on a demand basis to further strengthen rural broadband access.

The signing ceremony was attended by senior officials including Shyamal Misra, Administrator of Digital Bharat Nidhi, Anand Khare, Director General (Telecom), DoT, Geetanjali Sharma, CEO of APBIL and Papa Sudhakara Rao, Director (Enterprise Business), BSNL.

The ABP was approved by the Union Cabinet in August 2023 with the objective of upgrading and expanding the existing BharatNet network to provide future-ready broadband connectivity across rural India.

Under the Andhra Pradesh rollout, APBIL will implement the programme in the state.

The government said the initiative is expected to support more than five lakh rural home fibre connections with financial assistance from the Centre. It is also expected to improve access to digital services such as e-governance, online education, telemedicine, digital payments and other citizen-centric services in remote and underserved areas.

The agreement marks an important step towards accelerating digital inclusion and strengthening telecom infrastructure in rural Andhra Pradesh as part of the broader vision of building a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.

Ride-hailing company Uber will set up its first data centre in India in partnership with Adani Group, Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi announced on May 13 after meeting Gautam Adani in Ahmedabad.

“Great to meet Gautam Adani in Ahmedabad this morning and build on our existing partnership with the Adani group,” Khosrowshahi said in a post on X. “As India fast emerges as a leading innovation hub for Uber, we are setting up our first data centre in the country with the Adani Group to test and deploy our tech.”

He also held discussions with Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu on improving airport last-mile connectivity and sustainable urban mobility initiatives.

title: Wealthtech Startup ZFunds Launches AI Assistant ‘ZIVA’ for Mutual Fund Managers
content:
The platform offers mock client calls, portfolio insights, and multilingual AI support for MFD workflows.

What Actually Matters.

ZFunds launched ZIVA, an AI assistant for mutual fund distributors and wealth managers.

ZIVA aims to simplify advisory workflows and help independent distributors expand their businesses.

Gurugram-based mutual funds platform ZFunds has an AI assistant for mutual fund distributors (MFDs) and wealth managers, as the company looks to simplify advisory workflows and help independent distributors scale their businesses.

Called ZIVA (ZFunds Intelligent Virtual Assistant), the AI-powered platform is designed to act as both a “thinking partner” and an execution engine for wealth managers, assisting them with portfolio reviews, market and fund research, client communication, business insights, and meeting preparation.

The wealthtech platform said the tool can help distributors conduct mock client calls, generate personalised portfolio recommendations, capture meeting insights and access real-time market analysis.

Citing data from ZFunds’ pilot rollout, the company said its platform reduced distributor workload by up to 60% by automating manual portfolio analysis and client servicing tasks. During the pilot involving 500 top partners, more than 5,000 client-ready proposals were generated using ZIVA, while users conducted over 9,000 minutes of mock client meetings on the platform.

“Distributors need support beyond data and research —they need help solving real, everyday problems. With AI-powered infrastructure, we are enabling them to deliver highly personalised investor experiences while scaling their practice. We are bringing enterprise-grade AI capabilities to independent distributors,” Manish Kothari, Co-founder of ZFunds, said in a statement.

The company said ZIVA aggregates research from authorised and compliant sources and converts it into actionable insights tailored to each distributor’s business. The platform enables users to construct goal-aligned portfolios, conduct portfolio reviews, and receive contextual prompts based on investor history and profiles.

In addition to portfolio intelligence, ZIVA also supports meeting preparation and client engagement workflows. The platform can prepare advisers using past notes, recent account activity and document summaries while enabling real-time note-taking, recording, transcription, and automated meeting summaries.

The AI assistant also includes multilingual voice and text capabilities across languages, including Hindi, Gujarati, Bengali, Tamil, and Telugu.

ZFunds said the platform also features a marketing engine that helps automate client engagement by generating ready-to-use communication and social media content, enabling distributors to maintain consistent investor interaction.

title: AI Can Add $500 Bn to India’s Economy by 2030: IBM-IndiaAI Study
content:
The report highlighted a widening gap between India’s AI ambitions and enterprise readiness.

What Actually Matters.

AI could contribute over $500 billion to India's economy by 2030.

There is a gap between India's AI ambitions and enterprise readiness.

India’s AI ambitions could add more than $500 billion to the country’s economy by 2030, according to a new joint study by IBM and IndiaAI, even as a majority of Indian enterprises admit they are lagging behind global peers in AI adoption.

The report, titled ‘From promise to power: How AI is redefining India’s economic future’, highlights a widening gap between India’s AI ambitions and enterprise readiness. While 80% of Indian business leaders believe AI investments will directly influence the country’s GDP growth, 72% of organisations surveyed acknowledged they lag behind global competitors in adopting AI at scale.

The findings come at a time when India is aggressively positioning itself as a global AI powerhouse through investments in digital infrastructure, sovereign AI capabilities, skilling initiatives, and enterprise modernisation.

According to the study, 73% of surveyed executives believe India will emerge as a leading global AI nation by 2030, driven by rapid advances in AI adoption across industries and growing government-industry collaboration.

Speaking at the launch of the report, S Krishnan, Secretary of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, said India is increasingly shaping the global AI narrative rather than simply participating in it.

“India is no longer just participating in the global AI conversation; we are helping shape it. Our vision is clear. AI must evolve as an extension of our people’s aspirations, driving inclusive growth and national progress. Guided by our vision of Viksit Bharat, we are advancing a human-centric approach to AI rooted in trust, ethics, and national sovereignty,” he said.

The report identified sovereign and hybrid AI infrastructure as emerging priorities for Indian enterprises, particularly in regulated industries and public systems. About 74% of executives surveyed said control over where data resides is critical, reflecting growing demand for sovereign AI architectures that balance innovation with data governance and national control.

Rather than fully isolated systems, enterprises are increasingly leaning toward hybrid cloud environments that combine domestic control with global innovation ecosystems. Seven in 10 executives said hybrid approaches improve control over data location without substantially increasing costs.

However, infrastructure readiness remains one of the biggest challenges in India’s AI journey.

The study found that 77% of respondents cited a lack of accessible, affordable, and secure cloud infrastructure as a major barrier to AI readiness, while 57% pointed to uneven data quality.

The findings suggest that India’s AI success may depend less on access to advanced models and more on strengthening foundational enterprise data systems and compute infrastructure.

Sandip Patel, Managing Director, IBM India and South Asia, said India’s AI opportunity will ultimately depend on how organisations operationalise AI responsibly and at scale.

“AI has the potential to become one of the most powerful growth engines for India’s economy,” Patel said. “What will set India apart is not just the scale of adoption, but how organisations build trusted AI agents and systems on strong data foundations, hybrid architectures, and a workforce empowered to work alongside AI.”

The study also underscored the scale of India’s looming AI talent challenge.

Currently, only around 30% of employees possess the AI literacy levels businesses say they require. By 2030, enterprises expect that figure to rise to nearly 57%, implying that India may need more than 350 million AI-skilled professionals within the decade.

To bridge the gap, initiatives such as IndiaAI FutureSkills are expanding AI labs and training programs across tier-2 and tier-3 cities, reflecting a broader push to democratise access to AI education and enterprise skilling.

Despite growing enthusiasm around AI, the report showed that most enterprises are still in the early stages of implementation. Only 15% of organisations surveyed are currently scaling AI through significant cross-functional investments, while the remaining 85% continue to operate pilot-stage AI programs.

Governance also remains a concern. Nearly 68% of enterprises cited gaps in AI governance as a barrier to scaling AI adoption, though many companies are beginning to integrate governance frameworks into operational systems.

The study concluded that India’s AI leadership ambitions will depend on how quickly enterprises can move from experimentation to scaled deployment while simultaneously strengthening infrastructure, governance, partnerships, and workforce readiness.

title: SAP Expands AI Stack with Anthropic, Palantir in Agentic Enterprise Push
content:
“For the mission-critical processes of our customers, ‘almost right’ just isn’t good enough,” said Christian Klein, CEO of SAP.

What Actually Matters.

SAP launched its Autonomous Enterprise strategy with a unified AI platform.

The new platform integrates AI agents into core business processes.

SAP has unveiled its Autonomous Enterprise strategy, introducing a unified AI platform and a suite of agent-led applications, while expanding partnerships with companies including Anthropic and Palantir Technologies.

Announced at SAP Sapphire 2026, the offering combines a new SAP Business AI Platform with an Autonomous Suite designed to run core business processes end-to-end using AI agents embedded within enterprise workflows.

“For the mission-critical processes of our customers, ‘almost right’ just isn’t good enough,” said Christian Klein, CEO of SAP, adding that the platform anchors AI agents in business data and governance to deliver “accurate, compliant and secure outcomes.”

At the centre of the announcement is the SAP Business AI Platform, which unifies SAP’s existing technology stack, data cloud and AI capabilities into a single governed environment. The platform uses a knowledge graph to map enterprise data and relationships, allowing AI agents to operate with business context. Developers can build agents and workflows through Joule Studio using no-code and pro-code tools on SAP-managed infrastructure.

SAP’s expanded partner ecosystem underpins the strategy. Anthropic’s Claude models will be integrated into SAP’s platform to power enterprise agents across functions such as HR and procurement. Meanwhile, Palantir Technologies will work with SAP on complex data migration and transformation scenarios, alongside other implementation partners.

Additional partnerships span cloud providers including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft, as well as AI and infrastructure players such as NVIDIA, Cohere and Mistral AI.

On top of this, SAP introduced the Autonomous Suite, which deploys more than 50 domain-specific AI assistants across functions such as finance, supply chain and human resources. These assistants coordinate over 200 specialised agents to execute tasks.

One example includes an Autonomous Close Assistant aimed at reducing financial closing timelines from weeks to days.

SAP also expanded its industry-specific AI offerings, showcasing use cases such as predictive maintenance in the energy sector. In a collaboration with European energy company RWE, SAP said its AI agents can analyse historical incident data to identify root causes and automate maintenance workflows.

The company unveiled a new interface called Joule Work, positioning it as the primary way users interact with SAP systems. Instead of navigating multiple applications, users can describe outcomes, with AI orchestrating workflows, data and agents in the background. The interface will be available across desktop, mobile and voice.

To accelerate adoption, SAP announced a €100 million fund for partners building and deploying AI agents on its platform. It also updated its RISE with SAP and GROW with SAP programs to include access to AI assistants and introduced tools to automate ERP migration tasks, claiming reductions in migration effort of more than 35%.

title: Proximal Cloud, NxtGen Partner to Enable Sovereign AI Deployments in India
content:
The partnership targets regulated sectors with compliant, private AI infrastructure and local data control.

What Actually Matters.

Proximal Cloud and NxtGen are partnering to offer secure sovereign AI deployments in India.

The collaboration targets government and regulated sectors requiring compliant, private AI infrastructure.

Proximal Cloud on May 12 announced a strategic partnership with NxtGen to enable secure, compliant, and scalable sovereign AI deployments for enterprises and government organisations in India.

Under the collaboration, NxtGen will support Proximal Cloud’s enterprise AI platform, including its flagship Enterprise Deep Research platform, which is designed to help organisations manage data sprawl across complex enterprise systems and build intelligence layers for private data.

The companies said the partnership is aimed at enabling deployment-ready AI systems for government and regulated sectors, allowing organisations to adopt advanced AI capabilities while adhering to evolving regulatory and security requirements.

The collaboration will focus on addressing challenges related to compliance, data sovereignty and operational control. By combining Proximal Cloud’s ‘data-adjacent AI’ approach with NxtGen’s cloud and infrastructure capabilities, enterprises and institutions will be able to deploy AI systems within locally governed environments designed to ensure security, reliability and alignment with regulatory mandates.

Renu Raman, Founder and CEO of Proximal Cloud, said, “Bringing AI to where data resides is central to enabling secure and scalable adoption. Our collaboration with NxtGen allows organisations to deploy advanced AI capabilities within environments that meet stringent regulatory and operational requirements, while maintaining full control over their data.”

AS Rajgopal, Managing Director and CEO of NxtGen, said, “For government bodies and regulated enterprises, sovereign AI is now a baseline requirement. NxtGen has spent years building the infrastructure, compliance depth, and operational frameworks that make this a reality for Indian organisations rather than a roadmap item. Our collaboration with Proximal Cloud puts that foundation to work, giving institutions in the most accountability-driven sectors the ability to deploy advanced AI capabilities on Indian soil, under Indian control, without compromise.”

The announcement comes amid growing demand from enterprises and public sector organisations for sovereign AI infrastructure that enables local data governance, compliance and secure deployment of AI workloads within India.

With this investment, Zoho seeks to support MSMEs in their digital transformation and contribute to India's economic growth.

What Actually Matters.

Zoho has invested ₹70 crore in ONDC to support the development of Indian technology and empower MSMEs.

The investment aims to increase technology accessibility and inclusivity for businesses of all sizes in India.

Zoho Corporation has announced a ₹70 crore investment in the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) to promote the development of homegrown technology in India. This move is part of Zoho's plans to enhance technology accessibility and inclusivity for businesses of all sizes.

“India’s economy depends heavily on MSMEs, yet they face challenges on all fronts—from limited market access to structural constraints imposed by conventional digital platforms that rarely align with their unique needs. ONDC, which is an excellent initiative, gives power back to MSMEs, enabling them to expand their customer reach and achieve sustainable growth,” Sivaramakrishnan Iswaran, CEO of Zoho Payment Technologies and Global Head of Finance and Operations BU, Zoho, said in a statement.

ONDC aims to democratise Indian commerce through open digital frameworks that enhance interoperability and inclusivity. By addressing high entry barriers and fragmented systems, it aims to empower businesses of all sizes. With 218 million transactions projected for FY 2025-26, ONDC is establishing essential infrastructure for India’s next phase of growth.

Zoho facilitates MSME digitisation through the ONDC Network using apps such as Vikra, Zoho ERP, and Zoho Commerce. This investment will further develop the ecosystem and accelerate adoption, enabling more businesses to participate in the digital economy.

“Zoho shares with ONDC its philosophy of building sovereign technology to champion accessibility, flexibility, and inclusion of businesses of every size. We further believe that the private sector must play its part in nation-building,” he added.

ONDC’s interoperable model is enhancing digital commerce across retail, logistics, and finance. For example, ONDC DigiDukaan onboarded 10,000 kirana stores recently, while order volumes for rural workers increased 11-fold in FY 2025-26.

In logistics, the FIFO fleet allocation model scaled 50 times in six months, aiding gig workers. Moreover, ONDC-powered metro ticketing is now live across nine systems, demonstrating its reach beyond traditional e-commerce.

title: Google Turns the Mouse Pointer Into an AI Agent With Gemini
content:
It can identify text, images, objects, locations and other on-screen elements in real time.

What Actually Matters.

Google is developing an AI-powered mouse pointer, integrating Gemini models.

This new pointer allows users to interact with on-screen content using voice commands and gestures.

Google is rethinking one of the oldest elements in computing, the mouse pointer, by turning it into an AI-powered interface that can understand what users are pointing at and what they want to do with it.

In a blog post published on May 12, Google outlined a new concept for an AI-enabled pointer, powered by Google’s Gemini models.

It lets users interact with content using short voice commands and gestures instead of detailed prompts. In one example, a user points at a building in an image and says, “Show me directions.”

“The mouse pointer has been a constant companion on computer screens,” the company said. “Despite how technologies have changed, the pointer has barely evolved in more than half a century.”

According to Google, the system can identify text, images, objects, locations and other on-screen elements in real time. The company said this could allow users to summarise PDFs, convert tables into charts, edit images, or turn handwritten notes into actionable lists using simple pointer-based interactions.

We’re reimagining a 50-year-old interface - the mouse pointer - with AI. 🖱️

These experimental demos show how people can intuitively direct Gemini on their screens using motion, speech, and natural shorthand to get things done 🧵 pic.twitter.com/p6fhgNcopz

— Google DeepMind (@GoogleDeepMind) May 12, 2026

Google said current AI tools often interrupt workflows because users must manually copy content into chat windows. The company said its goal is to build AI that works directly inside the apps and interfaces people already use.

“We want the opposite: intuitive AI that meets users across all the tools they use, without interrupting their flow,” the researchers wrote.

Google is already bringing parts of the system into products such as Google Chrome and Googlebook.

Starting May 12, users can use Gemini in Chrome to ask questions about selected parts of a webpage instead of writing full prompts.

Google is already putting this vision into hardware as well.

The company has also introduced Googlebook, a new category of laptops built around its Gemini AI models, as it pushes to redesign personal computing around AI-powered interactions.

A central feature of the new laptops is Magic Pointer, an AI cursor developed with the Google DeepMind team. Google said the feature allows Gemini to understand what users are pointing at on screen and offer contextual actions.

“Just wiggle your cursor and watch it come alive with Gemini, offering quick, contextual suggestions every time you point at something on your screen,” the company said.

Google said users could point at a date in an email to create a meeting or select two images, such as a living room photo and a couch, to visualise them together.

title: India Deploys AI Push to Detect Mule Accounts, Cyber Financial Fraud
content:
The collaboration between I4C and RBIH aims to improve the sharing of fraud risk intelligence and enhance the resilience of India’s digital payments ecosystem.

What Actually Matters.

The I4C and RBIH collaboration aims to enhance fraud detection in India's digital banking ecosystem using AI.

The partnership focuses on improving the sharing of fraud risk intelligence and operational coordination between the two organisations.

The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the Ministry of Home Affairs, and the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen AI-driven detection of mule accounts and cyber-enabled financial frauds across India’s banking ecosystem.

The collaboration aims to improve the sharing of fraud risk intelligence, analytical support, and operational coordination between the two organisations to strengthen fraud prevention systems in digital banking and payments.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah stated that the government is working continuously towards building a “cyber secure Bharat.” “Mule accounts are big hurdles in curbing cyber crimes,” Shah said in a post on X.

He added that the partnership between I4C and RBIH would “unleash the power of artificial intelligence to combat cyber fraud” by enabling faster identification and removal of hidden mule accounts through AI-powered fraud detection systems.

Mule accounts are bank accounts used by cybercriminals to transfer or launder illegally obtained money. Such accounts are often created using fake identities or by unsuspecting individuals and pose a major challenge in tackling online financial fraud.

Under the MoU, I4C will share mule account-related intelligence and suspect identifiers from its Suspect Registry with RBIH. The data will be integrated into AI-driven fraud detection systems such as MuleHunter.ai, which has been deployed across banks to identify suspicious transactions and financial activities.

RBIH will use the datasets to train and enhance fraud-risk assessment models to improve proactive fraud detection and prevention mechanisms in the digital payments ecosystem.

The collaboration is expected to improve the resilience and safety of India’s digital banking ecosystem while increasing public trust in digital financial services.

The initiative is also part of I4C’s broader efforts to strengthen India’s cybercrime response infrastructure through platforms such as the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal and other intelligence-sharing mechanisms.

title: NetApp & Red Hat Partner to Strengthen Data Protection for OpenShift Virtualization
content:
The partnership introduces new NetApp tools optimised for Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization, helping enterprises protect and scale AI-driven workloads across hybrid and multicloud environments.

What Actually Matters.

NetApp and Red Hat's partnership enhances data protection for OpenShift environments across hybrid and multicloud settings.

New tools are optimised for handling AI-driven workloads, improving scalability and disaster recovery for enterprises.

NetApp has announced a strategic collaboration with Red Hat to improve data protection, disaster recovery and scalability for enterprises using Red Hat OpenShift virtualised environments across cloud and on-premises infrastructure.

The partnership introduces new NetApp data management capabilities optimised for Red Hat OpenShift and OpenShift Virtualization, designed to help enterprises manage growing virtual machine (VM) and container workloads more efficiently in the AI era.

According to Red Hat’s State of Virtualization report, 90% of organisations believe virtualisation supports innovation, while 71% have more than half of their IT infrastructure virtualised. As businesses increasingly handle larger volumes of AI-driven data, companies said enterprises require faster, more predictable backup and recovery systems.

Dallas Olson, Chief Commercial Officer at NetApp, said traditional backup systems often struggle to meet recovery and operational requirements as virtualised environments scale.

“NetApp’s latest innovations with Red Hat enable predictable backup and recovery behaviour even as the VM environment grows. Customers can now migrate, operate, and protect large-scale VM and container environments on Red Hat OpenShift with greater speed, predictability and operational confidence,” he added.

As part of the collaboration, NetApp introduced enhanced backup and recovery services for Red Hat OpenShift environments. The company noted that the updated system uses Change Block Tracking (CBT) technology, allowing incremental backups instead of scanning entire virtual machine disks, helping reduce backup time, storage costs, and compute overhead.

The companies also announced public preview support for NetApp Disaster Recovery on Red Hat OpenShift and OpenShift Virtualization environments. The Disaster Recovery-as-a-Service (DRaaS) platform is designed to provide guided failover and recovery workflows for Kubernetes-based virtual machines.

Moreover, Google Cloud NetApp Volumes and the Trident CSI driver are now generally available for Red Hat OpenShift Dedicated on Google Cloud, enabling enterprises to run both containers and virtual machines with simplified operations and scalability.

Steve Gordon, Senior Director of Product Management for Hybrid Cloud Platforms at Red Hat, said the collaboration aims to help enterprises modernise disaster recovery systems and improve operational efficiency for hybrid cloud environments.

The partnership will further strengthen enterprise virtualisation infrastructure by offering more scalable, resilient and AI-ready data management solutions for businesses operating across hybrid and multicloud ecosystems.

title: India Launches AI-Powered Tools to Improve Monsoon, Rainfall Forecasting
content:
Two AI-enabled weather forecasting systems will provide hyperlocal predictions of monsoon progression and rainfall.

What Actually Matters.

India has launched two AI-enabled weather forecasting systems for improved hyperlocal predictions.

The systems aim to enhance disaster preparedness, agriculture planning, and public decision-making.

India has introduced two new artificial intelligence-enabled weather forecasting systems to improve hyperlocal weather predictions and strengthen disaster preparedness, agriculture planning, and public decision-making.

Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh on Tuesday launched the AI-driven “Forecast of Monsoon Advance over Different Parts of the Country” and a “High Spatial Resolution Rainfall Forecast for Uttar Pradesh” pilot service developed under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

The systems have been jointly developed by the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, Pune and the National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting.

Addressing the launch event in New Delhi, Dr Singh said India’s forecasting systems have undergone a major transformation over the past decade through technological advancements, improved modelling systems, and expanded observational infrastructure.

“IMD has today become an integral component of governance, disaster preparedness, agriculture planning and everyday public decision-making,” the Minister added.

According to the ministry, the AI-enabled monsoon forecasting platform will provide probabilistic forecasts of monsoon progression every Wednesday up to four weeks in advance. The service has been designed to support farmers across 16 states and more than 3,000 sub-districts through the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare's dissemination framework.

The system combines AI-based forecasting models, statistical techniques and extended-range prediction systems to provide more operationally useful forecasts for agriculture and rural planning.

The second system, introduced as a pilot project for Uttar Pradesh, will generate rainfall forecasts at 1 km spatial resolution up to 10 days in advance. The service uses AI-driven downscaling methods and integrates data from Doppler weather radars, satellites, automatic rain gauges, and automatic weather stations.

Dr Singh noted that the initiative marks a shift from conventional forecasting to impact-based and decision-support forecasting capable of delivering location-specific and actionable weather information.

The Minister also highlighted the expansion of India’s weather infrastructure, including increasing the number of Doppler weather radars from around 16 a decade ago to nearly 50 currently, with 50 more planned under Mission Mausam.

What Actually Matters.

TCS and Rezolve AI have partnered to enhance retail through agentic AI-powered commerce solutions.

The collaboration focuses on integrating Rezolve AI's Brainpowa platform into retail workflows for improved shopping experiences.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has announced a global strategic partnership with Rezolve AI to help retailers adopt agentic AI-powered commerce solutions at enterprise scale. The collaboration marks TCS’ entry into the growing agentic commerce market where AI systems can independently assist customers, make recommendations and automate parts of the shopping journey.

Under the partnership, TCS will help retail companies use Rezolve AI’s proprietary commerce platform, brainpowa™ to build AI-driven shopping experiences across conversational commerce, intelligent product discovery and automated checkout systems.

The companies said the partnership aims to help enterprises integrate production-grade AI tools directly into their existing commerce workflows enabling businesses to modernise digital retail operations and improve customer engagement.

Daniel M Wagner, Chief Executive Officer of Rezolve AI, described the collaboration as a major step for the company’s expansion in enterprise AI commerce.

“This partnership is a major commercial milestone for Rezolve AI. TCS brings extraordinary reach, deep enterprise trust, and global execution capability. Together, we are creating a clear pathway to take agentic commerce from platform innovation to enterprise-scale deployment,” Wagner said.

He added that the partnership is expected to accelerate enterprise adoption of Rezolve AI’s technology and strengthen its position in the AI-powered commerce sector.

Shekar Krishnan, Head of Retail, UK and Europe at Tata Consultancy Services, noted that businesses are increasingly looking for AI solutions that deliver measurable business outcomes.

“Our partnership with Rezolve AI combines TCS’ global transformation capabilities with a specialised AI-powered commerce platform built for real-world enterprise deployment. Together, we aim to help customers modernise digital commerce in ways that improve customer experience and commercial performance,” Krishnan added.

As part of the collaboration, retailers will also be able to experience the AI commerce solutions through TCS’ global network of Pace Port™ innovation centres.

The partnership combines TCS’ enterprise relationships and global delivery network with Rezolve AI’s AI-native commerce technology focused on the retail industry. The companies said the collaboration will support the responsible and scalable deployment of AI-led commerce solutions across international markets.

Thinking Machines Lab has developed a multi-stream, micro-turn design that allows the model to continuously receive and respond to information in real time.

What Actually Matters.

Mira Murati's startup, Thinking Machines Lab, has unveiled new AI models for real-time human-AI collaboration.

These interaction models handle audio, video, and text simultaneously, without external software.

Mira Murati’s AI startup, Thinking Machines Lab, has introduced a research preview of interaction models, a new class of AI models that can handle real-time collaboration with humans across audio, video, and text without relying on external software scaffolding.

The company announced TML-Interaction-Small, a 276B-parameter MoE model with 12B active parameters that treats conversation as a live stream instead of a stop-start chat box.

In a blog post published May 11, the company said the models are built from scratch to support continuous interaction, allowing users and AI systems to communicate simultaneously rather than through traditional turn-based exchanges.

Thinking Machines says its interaction models instead break audio, video, and text into 200-millisecond micro-turns, allowing the AI to listen, observe, speak, draw, search, and use tools simultaneously during an ongoing interaction.

The company said the approach aims to make AI systems more responsive and collaborative during tasks that require ongoing human input. For example, the model understands timing-based instructions, such as waiting four seconds before responding.

“We think interactivity should scale alongside intelligence; the way we work with AI should not be treated as an afterthought,” Thinking Machines said in the post.

The company said current AI systems are largely optimised for autonomous task completion, where users provide instructions upfront and wait for the model to finish. According to the company, this creates what it described as a “collaboration bottleneck” because users cannot continuously guide, clarify, or interrupt the system during work.

Thinking Machines argued that most real-world work depends on ongoing interaction between people and AI systems rather than fully autonomous operation. It said current models operate in “a single thread”, meaning they stop perceiving new information while generating responses and cannot process simultaneous streams of communication.

To address this, the company said it developed a “multi-stream, micro-turn design” that enables the model to continuously receive and respond to information in real time across different modalities.

The startup also criticised the use of external systems, or “harnesses”, that many existing AI products rely on for features such as interruptions and multimodal interaction. It argued that interactivity should be built directly into the model architecture itself.

“For interactivity to scale with intelligence, it must be part of the model itself,” the company said.

Thinking Machines said the goal is to allow humans and AI systems to collaborate “the same way we do with other people: messaging, talking, listening, seeing, showing, and interjecting as needed.”

title: SwishX Launches Agentic AI Platform for Pharmaceuticals & Medtech Companies
content:
Based in Bengaluru, the startup provides AI-driven insights to help firms with marketing and distribution to global markets.

What Actually Matters.

SwishX has launched an AI platform aimed at transforming sales and marketing for pharmaceutical and medtech firms.

The platform integrates AI with global market insights to assist companies in expanding into new markets.

AI-native commercial excellence platform SwishX has launched an agentic AI platform for pharmaceutical and medtech firms, aiming to revolutionise sales, marketing, distribution, and business expansion through AI.

As it launches in India, SwishX helps pharmaceutical companies expand into other markets by integrating AI with global market insights. The startup aims to expand its operations throughout Latin America, Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Africa.

The Bengaluru-based startup independently assesses thousands of tenders worldwide, identifies the most promising win opportunities, analyses documents of over 500 pages, suggests potentially winning pricing strategies, and creates proposals in minutes.

Moreover, it modifies lengthy marketing PDFs into personalised video reels for doctors, reducing the timeline from weeks to just one day, as the company claims.

“India’s pharma sector…drives revenues of over $65 billion, and emerging markets combined drive $400 billion while distributing into over 200 countries…Companies often struggle to know where losses are happening, what is selling, which tenders matter most, or how effectively teams are executing in the market. AI agents change that completely,” Dushyant Sapre, Founder & CEO, SwishX, said in a statement.

According to the startup, SwishX is purpose-built specifically for the complexity of emerging markets. India alone has over 1.2 million pharmacies, compared to just ~1,00,000 in the US. Moreover, 30-60% of procurement happens through government tenders, and rate contracts and generic competition are significantly more intense.

In the long run, SwishX intends to create a fully integrated AI system that encompasses the entire value chain of life sciences firms, accelerating the discovery of generic and biosimilar drugs, facilitating drug development, and enabling autonomous commercial execution across multiple markets.

title: Toxic Work Culture Holds Back Microsoft, Amazon Employees From Indian Firms: Survey
content:
A new survey from Blind eveals that workplace culture and burnout concerns are outweighing salary considerations for tech professionals evaluating Indian companies.

What Actually Matters.

Indian tech professionals are open to joining homegrown companies like Flipkart, Zoho, and Zomato.

Concerns about toxic workplace culture and work-life balance deter many from Indian firms.

Indian technology professionals are increasingly open to joining homegrown companies such as Flipkart, Zoho, and Zomato, but concerns around toxic workplace culture continue to hold many back, according to a new survey by Blind, an anonymous community platform for verified professionals.

The survey, conducted between April 27 and May 6 this year, gathered responses from 1,205 India-based professionals across the technology sector to understand how employees perceive Indian-origin technology firms compared to global employers.

Findings show that 48% of respondents would either actively look at or seriously consider joining an Indian homegrown company if they were laid off from their current role tomorrow. Specifically, 13% said they were “actively looking at them already”, while 35% said they would “seriously consider” making the switch.

However, enthusiasm for Indian companies is being tempered by concerns over workplace conditions rather than salary differences.

A majority of respondents identified workplace culture as the primary concern. Around 47% cited toxic culture as their biggest hesitation in joining a homegrown company, while another 18% pointed to work-life balance concerns. Combined, this means 65% of respondents prioritise workplace quality over economic concerns such as compensation, with only 18% citing pay gaps as their primary worry.

When asked which Indian homegrown company they would choose to join, Flipkart emerged as the top choice, with 20% of respondents choosing it. Zomato and Swiggy followed at 14%, while Zoho received 10%. Paytm and PhonePe stood at 7%, followed by Freshworks at 6%.

Traditional IT services firms, despite employing millions across India’s technology workforce, received limited interest. TCS, Infosys, and HCL collectively accounted for only 3% of responses.

Notably, 40% of respondents selected ‘none of the above’, suggesting that many professionals either do not see Indian firms as attractive long-term workplaces or believe that few companies currently offer working conditions comparable to those of global technology firms.

Blind also reveals that one verified Flipkart employee wrote on the platform, “You will feel at home if you have no life outside of work”, while a Zoho employee criticised the company’s work culture, citing “No WFH. No overtime benefits. Weekends have to be sacrificed for work. Poor work-life balance.”

Notably, the strongest interest in Indian homegrown companies appears to come from employees currently working at global technology firms.

Among respondents open to joining Indian companies, Microsoft employees accounted for 7.6%, followed by Amazon employees at 6.8%, Oracle at 4.1%, and Google at 3.2%.
