title: LTTS, Emerson Partner for Engineering and Testing Solutions
content:
The companies will set up a centre of excellence in Mysuru to support product engineering and testing automation.

What Actually Matters.

LTTS and Emerson are collaborating to develop engineering and testing solutions across multiple sectors.

A centre of excellence will be established in Mysuru to enhance product development and test automation.

Emerson (previously National Instruments) and L&T Technology Services (LTTS) have announced a partnership to develop engineering and test solutions for sectors including industrial, transportation, semiconductors, aerospace and defence.

The companies said LTTS will act as a global system integrator and technology development partner for Emerson’s NI test platform.

The partnership will also see LTTS establish a centre of excellence (CoE) at its Mysuru campus in India. The facility will use Emerson’s NI software and hardware platforms to support product development, engineering, test automation and validation workflows.

Ritu Favre, President for Emerson’s Test and Measurement business, said engineering environments were becoming “increasingly software defined, data centric and interconnected.” She added that the collaboration would help customers “move from engineering uncertainty to operational confidence.”

Under the agreement, LTTS will support the design, deployment and lifecycle management of systems engineering platforms across industries. The companies said the collaboration will include joint customer engagements and the development of industry-specific solutions.

The CoE in Mysuru will serve as a global hub for joint solution development and industrialisation efforts. LTTS and Emerson said the facility will also focus on license enablement and client support models.

Alind Saxena, Executive Director and President of Strategic Initiatives and Growth Markets at LTTS, said the partnership would strengthen the company’s ability to build and deploy engineering systems at scale.

LTTS, a subsidiary of Larsen & Toubro, provides engineering research and development services across sectors, including transportation, telecom and medical devices, while Emerson is an automation company headquartered in Missouri.

title: TSMC Approves Fresh $20 Bn for Arizona Chip Plant, $31.3 Bn for Future Fabs
content:
The chipmaker ramps up spending on advanced capacity amid rising AI demand and fresh speculation about Tesla’s future chip plans.

Image Source: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., Ltd.

What Actually Matters.

TSMC has approved over $51 billion in new investments for advanced chipmaking capacity and facility systems.

The $31.3 billion allocation aims to support TSMC's long-term capacity plans amid rising AI demand.

At a recent board of directors meeting in Taiwan’s Hsinchu, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) approved more than $51 billion in new investments, including a $31.3 billion capital appropriation and a further $20 billion injection into its wholly-owned Arizona subsidiary.

This comes as the world’s largest contract chipmaker accelerates its global expansion plans. The company said the $31.3 billion allocation will support advanced technology capacity, fab construction and facility systems.

The scale of the spending highlights how aggressively TSMC is moving to secure advanced chipmaking capacity amid surging AI demand and increasing geopolitical pressure to localise semiconductor production in the United States.

TSMC said in a statement shared with AIM that the capital appropriation would help meet “long-term capacity plans based on market demand forecasts and TSMC’s technology development roadmap”.

The Arizona investment arrives as the US pushes for more domestic semiconductor manufacturing. TSMC’s Arizona operations have become central to Washington’s broader strategy to reduce dependence on Asian chip supply chains.

The board decisions also come days after reports linked Tesla’s future AI chip roadmap to US foundry expansion plans. A report published by Wccftech cited unnamed sources claiming Tesla could shift part of its AI6.5 chip production from TSMC to Intel Foundry under pressure from the Trump administration.

While TSMC made no reference to Tesla or Intel in its board resolutions, its Arizona expansion could strengthen its position in the race to build advanced AI chip production facilities in the US.

In April, Tesla CEO Elon Musk said on X that Tesla’s AI6.5 chip would “further improve performance using TSMC 2nm in Arizona”.

TSMC also recently approved its Q1 FY26 financial statements during the meeting. The company reported consolidated revenue of NT$1.13 trillion and net income of NT$572.48 billion for the quarter.

In May, the giant announced a continued partnership with Applied Materials for its new EPIC Center in Silicon Valley and Sony Semiconductors to build next-generation image sensors.

Moreover, on April 28 and 29, the company sold all its shares in Arm Holdings, primarily owned by the Japanese conglomerate SoftBank Group, according to a company filing accessed by AIM.

title: Indian Judiciary Goes Digital with AI Chatbot & Integrated Case Management System
content:
The digital initiatives are aimed at improving transparency, coordination and citizen access as India’s judiciary accelerates its technology-driven reforms.

What Actually Matters.

India's judiciary is enhancing services through two major digital initiatives aimed at improving transparency and citizen access.

The 'One Case One Data' initiative integrates information from various courts into a single digital platform for easier access.

India’s judiciary has announced two major digital initiatives aimed at improving judicial services and making court-related information more accessible to citizens across the country. Chief Justice of India, Surya Kant, on May 11, introduced the ‘One Case One Data’ initiative and launched an AI-powered chatbot named ‘Su Sahayata’ in the Supreme Court.

The announcements were made before the beginning of the day’s proceedings in the Supreme Court. The initiatives are part of the judiciary’s broader push towards digital transformation and technology-driven reforms.

Under the ‘One Case One Data’ initiative, information from High Courts, district courts and taluka courts across India will be integrated into a single digital platform. The system aims to create a unified case management structure that allows case-related information from different courts to be accessed in one place.

Speaking about the initiative, the Chief Justice said, “We are commencing the ‘One Case One Data’ initiative with multi-level information of all High Courts, district and taluka court details embedded. We look forward to developing an efficient case management system.”

The initiative is expected to improve coordination between courts, simplify case tracking and make judicial data management more organised and transparent. It will also help litigants, lawyers and judicial officials access information more efficiently.

Alongside the digital data platform, the Supreme Court also launched ‘Su Sahayata’, an AI-powered assistance chatbot integrated into the court website. The chatbot has been developed by the National Informatics Centre in collaboration with the Supreme Court Registry.

According to the Chief Justice, the chatbot will provide guidance on Supreme Court procedures, filing systems, case-related queries and other essential judicial services.

“We are also launching ‘Su Sahay’, an assistance chatbot for our website developed by the NIC in collaboration with the Registry. This will provide a simple and convenient interface for citizens to seek front-end guidelines and guidance in accessing essential services of the Supreme Court,” the CJI noted.

The AI-based system is expected to make court services easier to understand and access for the public to understand.

title: HrdWyr Raises $13 Million to Build AI Native Chips for Physical AI
content:
The funding round, led by Ideaspring Capital, also saw participation from Singularity AMC, Avatar Growth Capital and existing investor Persistent Systems.

What Actually Matters.

HrdWyr secured $13 million in Series A funding for AI chip development.

The company focuses on AI-native chips for edge computing applications.

Semiconductor startup HrdWyr has raised $13 million in a Series A funding round led by Ideaspring Capital, as the company looks to accelerate development of its AI native chip products for edge computing applications and expand globally.

The round also saw participation from Singularity AMC, Avatar Growth Capital and existing investor Persistent Systems.

The Bengaluru-based company said the fresh capital will be used to scale its AI-native System-on-Chip (AISoC) products and deepen customer engagements across key international markets.

HrdWyr is building purpose-built AI chips designed for industries where power efficiency, low latency and real-time processing are critical. The startup said its semiconductor architecture is designed to enable Physical AI, in which intelligent systems operate directly in real-world environments rather than solely through cloud-based computing.

“The real power of AI will be unlocked as we enter the era of Physical AI, where advanced intelligence seamlessly integrates with real-world systems,” said Ramamurthy Sivakumar, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of HrdWyr. “This inflexion point demands a fundamental rethinking of how computing systems are conceived, architected and deployed.”

The company’s technology stack is built around what it calls a ‘True Edge Autonomy’ framework, which integrates reinforcement learning-based AI directly into chip architecture to improve on-device intelligence and responsiveness.

HrdWyr said it operates as a full-stack fabless semiconductor company, differentiating itself from traditional IP licensing and semiconductor services firms.

Investors said HrdWyr’s focus on energy-efficient AI chips aligns with the growing demand for domestic semiconductor capabilities and intelligent edge systems across sectors such as consumer electronics, electric vehicles and industrial applications.

“HrdWyr is building a family of AI chips addressing power management and efficiency across multiple sectors, including white goods, EVs and data centres. This is very important to Ideaspring’s thesis of building products from India for the world and also becoming self-reliant in semiconductors,” Naganand Doraswamy, Managing Partner and Founder, Ideaspring Capital, said.

The startup recently announced a strategic collaboration with audio and wearables brand boAt, marking an early validation of its consumer technology applications.

title: Applied Materials, TSMC Deepen Chip Partnership for New Centre in Silicon Valley
content:
The companies will jointly develop semiconductor technologies for AI scaling at Applied Materials’ EPIC research facility, which is scheduled to be operational this year.

What Actually Matters.

Applied Materials and TSMC are partnering to develop semiconductor technologies for AI scaling at the EPIC Centre in Silicon Valley.

The collaboration focuses on materials engineering and process integration to enhance energy-efficient chip performance.

Applied Materials and TSMC have announced a partnership to develop semiconductor technologies for the next phase of AI scaling at the former’s EPIC Centre in Silicon Valley. The collaboration will focus on materials engineering, equipment innovation, and process integration technologies to improve energy-efficient chip performance from data centres to edge devices.

The investment for EPIC Centre was announced in 2023 to accelerate the commercialisation of next-generation semiconductor technologies. Applied has stated that the centre represents a planned investment of about $5 billion over time and will become operationally ready this year. The company described the facility as its largest investment in semiconductor equipment research and development in the United States.

Applied Materials stated that the partnership builds on more than 30 years of collaboration between the two firms and aims to reduce the time taken to move new technologies from research to high-volume manufacturing.

Prabu Raja, President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials, said that TSMC, as a founding partner of the EPIC Center, would gain earlier access to Applied Materials’ innovation teams and next-generation equipment.

Applied Materials said the partnership will target challenges linked to advanced logic scaling as AI workloads increase. The companies plan to work on process technologies that improve power, performance and area efficiency across leading-edge logic nodes.

Gary Dickerson, President and CEO of Applied Materials, said that bringing teams together at the EPIC Center would help accelerate the technologies needed to address the growing complexity of chipmaking.

The companies also plan to develop advanced process integration approaches to improve yield, variability control and reliability as semiconductor devices move towards vertically stacked architectures. They will also focus on new materials and manufacturing equipment for complex 3D transistors and interconnect structures.

“As semiconductor device architectures evolve with each new generation, the demands on materials engineering and process integration continue to increase,” said Y.J. Mii, Executive Vice President and Co-Chief Operating Officer at TSMC. He said large-scale AI development requires broader industry collaboration and described the EPIC Center as an environment that can accelerate the readiness of equipment and processes for next-generation technologies.

title: Ilya Sutskever Reveals $7 Bn OpenAI Stake While Accusing Sam Altman of Dishonesty
content:
Sutskever also confirmed that after Altman’s temporary ouster, OpenAI board members held discussions with Anthropic regarding a possible merger.

What Actually Matters.

Ilya Sutskever's OpenAI stake is valued at approximately $7 billion.

Sutskever accused Sam Altman of a consistent pattern of dishonesty.

OpenAI co-founder and former chief scientist Ilya Sutskever testified on May 11 that his ownership stake in OpenAI is currently worth about $7 billion, as he took the stand in the high-stakes legal battle between the company and billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk.

Speaking in a California courtroom during the third week of the trial, Sutskever also revealed that his OpenAI stake was worth around $5 billion in November 2025.

The testimony came as the case examines OpenAI’s shift from its nonprofit roots into a commercial AI giant pursuing massive fundraising and potentially a trillion-dollar IPO.

Sutskever’s appearance quickly turned into a detailed account of the dramatic 2023 leadership crisis at OpenAI. He testified that he had spent about a year gathering evidence for OpenAI’s board that CEO Sam Altman displayed a “consistent pattern of lying.”

During testimony, Sutskever confirmed he had been considering action against Altman for at least a year before the November 2023 board vote that temporarily removed Altman as CEO. He said he prepared a document compiling evidence of Altman’s alleged dishonesty at the request of the board and confirmed Altman’s conduct included “undermining and pitting executives against one another.”

Sutskever also testified that he had discussed removing Altman with former OpenAI chief technology officer Mira Murati after the two spoke about Altman’s behaviour “for a long time.”

Altman’s conduct was “not conducive to any grand goal”, including the creation of safe AGI, Sutskever said in court.

Sutskever played a central role in Altman’s dramatic firing and rehiring in November 2023 while serving on OpenAI’s board. However, after concerns emerged that the company could collapse, Sutskever later expressed regret for his “participation in the board’s actions” and ultimately voted to reinstate Altman.

The trial stems from Musk’s lawsuit accusing OpenAI and Altman of abandoning the organisation’s nonprofit mission in pursuit of profit. Musk, who co-founded OpenAI and left its board in 2018, is seeking $150 billion in damages from OpenAI and its backer, Microsoft, to be paid to the nonprofit entity. He is also seeking the removal of Altman and OpenAI President Greg Brockman from their roles.

Sutskever also confirmed that after Altman’s temporary ouster, OpenAI board members held discussions with rival AI startup Anthropic about a possible merger that would have placed Anthropic leadership in control of OpenAI. He testified that he was “not excited” about the idea of merging OpenAI with another company.

The former OpenAI chief scientist said he largely avoided the internet during the chaotic weekend following Altman’s firing and was initially unaware of contingency plans, including Microsoft’s proposal to absorb Altman, Brockman, and OpenAI employees into a new subsidiary.

Sutskever left OpenAI in 2024 and later launched his own AI startup, Safe Superintelligence.

Earlier on Monday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella testified that Microsoft’s investment in OpenAI was a “calculated risk,” arguing that the partnership delivered significant strategic and marketing value for the tech giant.

Altman is expected to testify on May 12, while closing arguments in the trial are scheduled for Thursday, May 14.

content:
The bank is deploying GenAI, GST intelligence and document AI to digitise Re-KYC and profile updates.

What Actually Matters.

Axis Bank has launched AI-powered compliance solutions to streamline regulatory processes for Current Account customers.

The new Digital Business Profile Update Service allows businesses to update details through a fully digital, paperless process.

Axis Bank has announced the launch of a unified suite of AI-powered compliance transformation solutions for its Current Account customers, aimed at simplifying complex and time-consuming regulatory processes for businesses.

The new offerings include an AI-powered Re-KYC solution and an AI-driven Digital Business Profile Update Service, both designed to deliver faster, more accurate and fully digitally compliant journeys.

The Digital Business Profile Update Service enables Current Account customers to seamlessly update business details, such as Nature of Business, through an end-to-end digital and paperless process.

Leveraging generative AI and real-time GST filing data, the service automatically predicts and assigns the most appropriate occupation code from more than 3,000 options, eliminating the need for manual data entry, paperwork or branch visits.

According to the bank, a process that earlier required extensive manual effort and considerable time can now be completed instantly with improved accuracy using GST-verified intelligence.

Axis Bank said the service offers zero paperwork, instant submission and a frictionless digital experience for customers, while reducing manual effort, operational workload and errors for frontline and operations teams.

The bank added that the deployment represents one of the first large-scale applications of large language models integrated with GST intelligence to improve efficiency while strengthening compliance controls.

In parallel, the bank has rolled out its AI-powered Re-KYC solution for non-individual Current Account customers across India as part of its ongoing compliance enhancement initiatives. The solution covers key customer constitutions that account for nearly 90% of Re-KYC volumes.

The Re-KYC platform uses advanced document intelligence to automatically identify, extract and validate multiple KYC documents submitted within a single PDF.

The system also guides branch users in real time by proactively flagging missing documents, data gaps and quality issues at the point of data entry, shifting compliance from a reactive post-submission check to a proactive, prevention-led approach.

Axis Bank said early outcomes indicate a significant reduction in rework and follow-ups, faster turnaround times and improved productivity for branch and operations teams. The guided workflows are expected to improve First Time Right performance and establish stronger, scalable compliance controls across the network.

Commenting on the launch, Sameer Shetty, Group Executive of Digital Business, Transformation and Strategic Programmes at Axis Bank, said, “With the introduction of AI-powered compliance solutions, critical manual and error-prone processes are being replaced with seamless, insight-driven operations.”

Shetty added that the combination of generative AI, document intelligence, and real-time GST data allows us to simplify complex workflows at scale, benefiting customers with faster, paperless experiences while strengthening compliance and operational resilience.

“These launches represent an important step in our broader ambition to build future-ready, AI-led systems that enhance trust, transparency, and convenience across every business banking touchpoint.”

On the other hand, OpenAI earns $5 million per employee.

What Actually Matters.

Anthropic leads AI companies in revenue efficiency, generating £9 million per employee.

OpenAI earns £5.6 million per employee, placing it behind Anthropic in this metric.

Anthropic currently leads the AI sector in revenue efficiency, generating $9 million per employee, according to data from research firm EpochAI.

This figure places the company ahead of OpenAI, which earns $5.6 million per employee. Should either firm pursue an initial public offering (IPO) in the near future, its revenue per employee would surpass that of any existing public technology company.

Epoch AI stated that Anthropic has 3,328 employees as of April 2026, while OpenAI had 4,432 employees in February 2026.

For comparison, NVIDIA generates roughly $5.1 million in revenue per employee with a workforce of approximately 42,000. Google, with a massive headcount of 191,000 employees, generates a significantly lower $2.1 million per staff member.

While financial data for established public corporations is sourced from mandatory regulatory filings, the figures for private entities like Anthropic and OpenAI were derived from the EpochAI AI Companies Database. It calculates performance benchmarks by aggregating and analysing verified public media reports and industry disclosures.

Despite achieving unprecedented revenue growth, both OpenAI and Anthropic are operating at significant financial deficits.

OpenAI projects a $14 billion loss for 2026 alone, nearly three times its 2025 loss. The company's trajectory suggests a cumulative cash burn of $115 billion through 2029, with profitability not expected until the 2030s.

Conversely, Anthropic is demonstrating a faster path toward financial sustainability, despite its own heavy capital consumption. Driven by strong enterprise adoption and an estimated annualised revenue run rate of $30 billion achieved in early 2026, the company forecasts reducing its cash burn to approximately one-third of its revenue this year.

Anthropic projects that this burn rate will further decrease to 9% by 2027, positioning the firm to reach the break-even point by 2028.

EpochAI also suggested that Anthropic could surpass OpenAI in annualised revenue by mid-2026. Since reaching the $1 billion milestone, Anthropic’s revenue has grown at 10x per year, significantly outpacing OpenAI’s, which is growing at 3.4x per year.

As of May, OpenAI has raised roughly $180–190 billion in total funding, while Anthropic has raised roughly $64–70 billion.

content:
The automaker reports 8% conversion uplift as AI voice agents handle a surge in launch-time inquiries.

What Actually Matters.

Mahindra deployed AI voice agents to manage customer inquiries during the XUV 7XO launch, enhancing outreach efficiency.

The AI system, named ‘nAIna’, automated outbound calls while ensuring natural-sounding interactions.

Mahindra & Mahindra has deployed AI-powered voice agents in partnership with ElevenLabs to manage customer outreach and inquiries during the launch of its flagship SUV, the XUV 7XO.

Ahead of the January launch, Mahindra AI, the group’s dedicated AI division, faced the challenge of handling a sharp spike in inbound and outbound customer interactions, a phenomenon typically associated with major vehicle launches. These included reconnecting with fresh and previously lost leads, responding to customer queries, registering inquiries, and booking test drives.

Instead of rapidly scaling conventional call center operations, Mahindra AI deployed ‘nAIna’, its conversational AI voice agent powered by ElevenLabs’ text-to-speech technology. The system was designed to automate outbound calls at scale while maintaining natural-sounding, low-latency interactions.

The AI voice agents enabled always-on customer engagement, allowing Mahindra to continue outreach and support beyond traditional call centre hours. The deployment was aimed at maintaining conversation quality during peak demand periods without significantly increasing operational overhead.

According to the company, ElevenLabs provided the voice layer that made interactions more responsive and human-like. By integrating ElevenLabs’ text-to-speech API into Mahindra’s existing workflows, the automaker expanded outbound calling capacity while ensuring a consistent customer experience.

Mahindra said the deployment delivered measurable business outcomes, including additional qualified inquiries and an approximately 8% uplift in conversions compared to previous outreach methods.

The company views the XUV 7XO rollout as a proof point for using AI voice agents as a force multiplier during high-demand events such as vehicle launches. By automating first-contact conversations and inquiry handling, dealership and human support teams were able to focus on higher-intent customer interactions and follow-ups.

“Large-scale launches need new ways to manage customer conversations. During the XUV 7XO launch, our partnership with ElevenLabs helped us successfully deploy AI voice agents to support peak demand and helped route queries to dealerships,” said Manjari Upadhye, Chief Marketing Officer, Automotive Division, M&M Ltd.

Mahindra AI said it plans to extend the use of AI voice agents beyond launch campaigns into broader customer engagement workflows, creating what it describes as an always-on intelligent voice layer across the automotive lifecycle.

title: Cyient Semiconductors Launches India-Made GaN Power Chip Family
content:
The company introduced seven GaN power ICs built with Navitas technology for AI, telecom, and e-mobility applications.

What Actually Matters.

Cyient Semiconductors has launched its first family of gallium nitride power ICs for the Indian market.

The new chip family includes seven 650V-rated devices for AI, telecom, and e-mobility applications.

Cyient Semiconductors has launched its first family of gallium nitride (GaN) power integrated circuits for the Indian market, marking the company’s entry into commercial GaN semiconductor products.

A subsidiary of Cyient, it introduced seven 650V-rated devices developed under a technology license from Navitas Semiconductor.

The new chip family targets applications across AI data centres, telecommunications systems, consumer fast chargers, industrial power supplies, and e-mobility charging platforms. Cyient Semiconductors said it expects to begin sampling the products by June 2026.

“With this launch, Cyient Semiconductors is introducing its first family of GaN power ICs, marking our entry into high-performance power semiconductors with a strong roadmap for expansion,” Suman Narayan, CEO at Cyient Semiconductors, said in a statement. “These highly integrated devices are designed to accelerate adoption and support next-generation power applications.”

The launch follows a strategic collaboration between Cyient Semiconductors and Navitas announced in December 2025. Under the agreement, Cyient Semiconductors will license Navitas’ GaN technology for use in India and will also act as a second-source supplier for selected Navitas devices already in mass production.

Chris Allexandre, President and CEO at Navitas, said India remains a key market as the company pivots its India strategy to focus on GaN-based product enablement and customer success.

Cyient Semiconductors said customers can contact the company directly for product datasheets, samples, and technical support. It operates two centres in India, three in Europe, and one in the United States.

GaN semiconductors are increasingly used in power electronics because they enable faster switching speeds and lower energy losses than silicon-based devices. Companies are deploying these chips in high-performance computing systems, electric vehicle charging infrastructure, and compact consumer chargers.

The first product line includes seven integrated GaN power devices packaged in DPAK form factors. The devices combine control, drive, and protection functions with integrated EMI management and current sensing. Cyient Semiconductors said the design aims to simplify system integration and reduce customers’ time-to-market.

The company plans to expand its GaN portfolio through partnerships with local outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) companies. Cyient Semiconductors said the licensing arrangement with Navitas could later support domestic manufacturing of GaN devices in India.

title: Delhi-NCR Raises $1.7 Billion in Q1 2026 Driven by Large Funding Rounds
content:
Gurugram dominated the funding landscape, attracting 52% of all capital raised in the region, equivalent to $876 million.

What Actually Matters.

Delhi-NCR funding rounds decreased in Q1 2026 compared to last year.

A few large deals significantly influenced the total capital raised.

Delhi-NCR has recorded 110 funding rounds between January and March, down from 153 rounds during the same period last year, according to a new report by Tracxn. While total funding declined only 11% year-on-year, the market became dramatically more concentrated.

Three deals alone—Nxtra Data’s $710 million private equity round, Inox Clean Energy’s $344 million Series D funding, and Wingify’s $150 million Series A—accounted for nearly 71% of the quarter’s total capital inflow.

The remaining 107 deals split just $500 million.

Notably, enterprise infrastructure attracted $869.1 million during the quarter — a dramatic jump from just $624,000 in Q4 2025—almost entirely driven by Nxtra’s data centre investment round.

Environment tech followed with $434 million, largely due to Inox Clean Energy’s raise, while enterprise applications secured $243 million.

Together, these three sectors absorbed over $1.5 billion of the total quarterly funding.

The report suggests that investors increasingly view digital infrastructure, renewable energy, and enterprise software as foundational economic assets rather than speculative growth plays.

Even among the top-performing business categories, data centre providers emerged as the single largest recipient of capital, followed by advanced solar energy generation and marketing optimisation platforms.

Consumer-facing sectors such as grocery ecommerce, EV manufacturing, and EV charging featured in the rankings, but attracted significantly smaller investments.

The numbers also point to a widening gap between large, institutionally backed companies and the broader startup ecosystem.

Late-stage funding reached $1.2 billion in Q1 2026, but most of that capital flowed into just two large transactions. Early-stage startups raised $362 million, while seed-stage companies secured $147 million.

Investors are still deploying capital, but with greater selectivity, favouring companies operating in AI infrastructure, clean energy, cloud computing, and enterprise resilience.

This concentration also reflects growing investor caution amid uncertain global macroeconomic conditions and delayed IPO activity.

Delhi-NCR’s exit landscape further reinforced the trend toward strategic consolidation. The region recorded nine acquisitions during the quarter but only one IPO.

The standout transaction was Brahma’s reported $1.2 billion acquisition by Polymarket, making it the quarter’s largest exit by a wide margin.

Other acquisitions included CarInfo’s acquisition by Cars24, while brands such as Forest Essentials and Internshala also changed hands through strategic deals.

Geographically, Gurugram dominated the funding landscape, attracting 52% of all capital raised in the region, equivalent to $876 million.

Noida followed with 27%, and Delhi accounted for 20%.

Together, the three cities absorbed nearly all of the quarter’s funding activity, reinforcing the NCR region’s continued importance in India’s enterprise and infrastructure economy.

title: Humyn Labs Highlights Multilingual AI Speech Recognition Gaps With New Benchmark Report
content:
The benchmark is based on human-verified conversational audio collected from 22 Indian states.

What Actually Matters.

Humyn Labs launched BRIDGE, a benchmark report assessing AI speech recognition for Indian and Global South languages.

The report reveals significant accuracy issues in widely-used AI speech tools, mishearing one in three words in Indian languages.

Humyn Labs, a physical and voice AI data infrastructure company, has launched BRIDGE (Benchmark of Regional & International Data for Global Evaluation), an independent benchmarking report that evaluates the performance of AI speech recognition systems across Indian and Global South languages.

The company claims it is the largest benchmark of its kind, covering 15 commercial AI models across more than 22 non-English languages and dialects spoken by over 5.5 billion people globally.

The report evaluated popular speech recognition tools from companies including OpenAI, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, and Indian AI providers, Sarvam AI and Gnani.ai.

According to the findings in the report, many widely used AI speech tools struggle to accurately recognise Indian language conversations, with some systems reportedly mishearing one in every three words. The report noted that traditional industry metrics such as Word Error Rate (WER) fail to fully capture how AI systems perform on multilingual and code-switched speech common in countries like India.

Manish Agarwal, Co-founder of Humyn Labs, said, “The models are grading their own work. ASR providers published their own accuracy scores using benchmarks built on English-first, internet-trained datasets with little independent validation.”

He added that enterprises have been making “million-dollar deployment decisions” based on benchmarks that often do not reflect how users in the Global South actually speak.

Unlike conventional benchmarks, BRIDGE uses a seven-metric evaluation system that includes Semantic Similarity, Code-Switch F1, Loan Word WER, Phoneme-Informed Error Rate, and Word Information Lost alongside standard WER and Character Error Rate.

The report found that handling code-switched conversations where speakers mix English with Indian languages mid-sentence remains a major challenge for AI systems. Deepgram Nova-3 recorded the highest Code-Switch F1 score of 0.906 while several other global models scored significantly lower.

“The models aren’t the only problem, but the metrics are. You cannot evaluate non-English speech with a scoring system designed for English phonology and call it rigorous,” said Ishank Gupta, Co-founder of Humyn Labs.

The benchmark was built using human-verified, field-collected conversational audio from 22 Indian states rather than scripted or internet-scraped speech data.

title: Flo Mobility Raises $2.5 Million to Drive Global Expansion in Construction Robotics
content:
The Bengaluru-based physical AI startup is building solutions for the construction industry to autonomise construction sites across India and expand globally.

What Actually Matters.

Flo Mobility secured $2.5 million in pre-Series A funding.

The company aims to automate various tasks in the construction industry.

Bengaluru-based Flo Mobility, a physical AI solutions startup for the construction sector, has secured $2.5 million in a pre-Series A funding round co-led by Mela Ventures and Arali Ventures. This investment will be used to enhance manufacturing, improve its vertical AI and autonomy framework, expedite deployments throughout India, and venture into international markets.

Established in 2021 by CEO Manesh Jain and COO Pratik Patel, Flo Mobility is innovating in the use of physical AI solutions in the construction industry, one of the largest, yet least automated, fields globally.

“The market imperative of today, [such as] acute labour shortage driving up timelines and costs in construction, coupled with the evolution of technology, i.e. rapid development of vision models and lowering costs of hardware components, makes for great timing for Flo Mobility to make a ‘material movement’ in the construction robotics landscape,” Rajiv Raghunandan, Managing Partner at Arali Ventures, said in a statement.

Flo Mobility is creating a specialised robotics platform for construction that combines proprietary hardware, AI models, and autonomous software for perception, intelligence, and action. Starting with material movement, the company aims to automate tasks like tiling, wall finishing, and screeding.

The Flo Hauler, the company’s first product, is a battery-powered Autonomous Mobile Robot (AMR) that navigates unstructured terrain and operates across multiple floors. It can carry loads of up to 1.5 tonnes, transporting heavy construction materials efficiently between storage areas and job sites.

“Our robots do not replace the skilled labour that builds India’s cities; they free that labour to do the work that matters. This funding gives us the firepower to scale our deployments, build more robots, and expand internationally. We’ve proven the model. Now we're going to take it to every major construction market in the world,” Jain said in a statement.

With over 60 robots deployed across 10 states, Flo Mobility is collaborating with major developers such as L&T and Godrej Properties.

“Manesh and Pratik’s…traction with marquee logos in the industry in India and early proof-points in the Middle East validates the approach, and we're excited to partner with them as they scale globally,” Viju George, Partner at Mela Ventures, stated.

With this fundraising, the company aims to enhance product development, strengthen its presence in India, and expand into the Middle East.

title: OpenAI Launches $4 Billion Deployment Company Backed by Top Investors
content:
The Deployment Company will function as a standalone business unit while remaining closely connected to OpenAI’s research and product teams.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI has launched a new business unit, the OpenAI Deployment Company, to assist enterprises with AI system deployment.

This new company will embed Forward Deployed Engineers within client organisations to integrate AI into daily operations.

OpenAI has launched the OpenAI Deployment Company, a new business unit to help enterprises build and deploy AI systems across critical workflows, while also agreeing to acquire applied AI consulting firm Tomoro as part of the effort.

The company said the OpenAI Deployment Company will embed Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) inside customer organisations to help redesign workflows, integrate AI systems into daily operations, and deploy production-grade AI applications connected to enterprise data and tools.

The new entity launches with more than $4 billion in initial investment and is majority-owned and controlled by OpenAI. The company said it plans to use the capital to expand operations and acquire additional firms that can accelerate AI deployment.

In connection with the launch, OpenAI has agreed to acquire Tomoro, which works on enterprise AI deployment projects for companies including Tesco, Virgin Atlantic and Supercell. The acquisition will add about 150 Forward Deployed Engineers and deployment specialists to the new business.

“Successful AI deployment is about empowering people and teams to do more,” OpenAI said in the announcement. The company added that FDEs would work with “business leaders, operators, and frontline teams to identify where AI can make the biggest impact.”

OpenAI said the initiative reflects a broader shift in enterprise AI adoption, where companies are moving beyond experimentation toward integrating AI into core operations.

“Over the past several years, more than one million businesses have adopted OpenAI’s products and APIs,” the company said. “The next stage of enterprise AI will be defined by how effectively businesses can deploy this technology into real-world use cases.”

The OpenAI Deployment Company has been formed in partnership with 19 investment firms, consultancies and system integrators. The partnership is led by TPG, with Advent, Bain Capital and Brookfield as co-lead founding partners.

Other founding partners include Goldman Sachs, SoftBank Corp. and Warburg Pincus.

Consulting and systems integration firms participating in the initiative include Bain & Company, Capgemini and McKinsey & Company.

According to OpenAI, the Deployment Company will function as a standalone business unit while remaining closely connected to OpenAI’s research and product teams. The company said this structure would allow enterprise customers to build systems aligned with future frontier AI capabilities.

“A typical OpenAI Deployment Company engagement will begin with a focused diagnostic of where AI can create the most value,” OpenAI said. The company added that engineers would then “design, build, test, and deploy production systems” connected to customer infrastructure and workflows.

The acquisition of Tomoro is subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions, with the transaction expected to close in the coming months.

title: IRCTC-Approved Travel App ConfirmTkt Launches AI Agent to Help Book Trains
content:
ixigo-owned ConfirmTkt’s new feature, AI Seat Finder, analyses real-time train data and suggests alternate trains, routes, and boarding points.

What Actually Matters.

ConfirmTkt has launched AI Seat Finder, a feature designed to simplify train ticket booking through conversational AI.

The AI Seat Finder analyses real-time train data, suggesting alternate trains, routes, and boarding points for users.

IRCTC-authorised travel app ConfirmTkt has launched “AI Seat Finder”, a new conversational AI-powered feature to help train travellers find confirmed tickets more easily. The feature, powered by TARA, an AI-native agent developed by ixigo, is now available on the ConfirmTkt app in both Hindi and English.

Integrated directly into the app, AI Seat Finder analyses real-time train availability and guides users towards confirmed tickets and alternate travel options. The feature allows travellers to interact with the app in a conversational way through queries such as “Show me confirmed train tickets after 5 PM” or “Which trains with confirmed seats will reach the earliest?”

The platform also suggests alternate trains, routes, boarding points, and departure timings when preferred trains are waitlisted. According to the company, the feature is designed to simplify the train booking experience, which is often marked by uncertainty and multiple steps.

“Getting a confirmed train ticket in India has always involved a degree of uncertainty and effort. With AI Seat Finder (powered by TARA), we are reimagining this experience by making it conversational and outcome-driven. Instead of navigating multiple options and screens, users can now simply express their intent and let the app guide them to the best possible journey,” Dinesh Kumar Kotha, CEO of ConfirmTkt and ixigo Trains, said in a statement.

He added that this is a significant step in the company’s vision of building an AI-first travel experience that is simpler, more accessible, and built around the needs of Indian travellers.

The company said the feature is particularly aimed at improving accessibility for users in non-metro and high train-traffic regions across India.

To promote the feature, ConfirmTkt has launched a campaign featuring RCB players and will run across television, digital platforms, social media, outdoor advertising, and in-stadium promotions during the cricket season.

title: Genpact Expands Partnership with Google Cloud to Build AI Agents for Finance Operations
content:
The partnership will combine Genpact’s finance and operations expertise with Google Cloud’s AI infrastructure to create ‘agentic AI’ systems for forecasting, accounts payable and financial planning.

What Actually Matters.

Genpact and Google Cloud aim to develop AI-powered solutions for finance operations, focusing on the 'Office of the CFO'.

The partnership seeks to transition companies from small AI experiments to large-scale 'agentic AI' systems for automating financial workflows.

Genpact has expanded its partnership with Google Cloud to develop and scale AI-powered solutions for finance operations, especially for the ‘Office of the CFO’. The announcement, made on May 8, focuses on helping companies move from small AI experiments to large-scale ‘agentic AI’ systems that can automate and improve financial workflows.

Under the expanded alliance, Genpact will combine its expertise in finance and business operations with Google Cloud’s AI and cloud technologies to create AI agents that can assist finance teams in tasks such as forecasting, cash flow management, accounts payable and financial planning.

Kevin Ichhpurani, President of Global Partner Ecosystem at Google Cloud, said, “The collaboration will help businesses deploy AI in real production environments rather than limiting it to pilot projects.” He added that Genpact’s industry expertise brings “critical industry context to core finance workflows” and that Google Cloud is pleased to expand the partnership through its Agent Marketplace.

The first solution launched under the partnership is called ‘Genpact Finance One - Revenue Lens Agents’. It is now available through Google Cloud’s Agent Marketplace and is designed to help companies improve revenue forecasting, manage cash flow more efficiently, and reduce manual work for finance teams.

Vijay Vijayasankar, Global Agentic AI Officer at Genpact, noted that many CFOs have experimented with AI but very few have fully AI-powered finance functions. The partnership aims to close the gap between AI promises and actual business results. According to him, the AI agents are designed to “execute, learn, connect and deliver outcomes.”

Genpact also plans to introduce more AI-driven finance tools in the future covering areas such as record-to-report operations, accounts payable, and financial analysis.

The companies said they are already working with major global enterprises across healthcare, retail and pharmaceutical sectors to modernise finance operations and improve productivity using AI-powered workflows.

The sequential jump in Q4 profit was driven by growth in its international business and rising demand for AI-led modernisation projects, while domestic revenue saw a hit.

What Actually Matters.

Sonata Software's Q4 profit rose due to international business growth.

Increased demand for AI-led modernisation projects contributed to profit.

Sonata Software on May 6 reported a 25% sequential rise in consolidated net profit for the March quarter, aided by growth in its international IT services business and increased demand for AI-led modernisation projects.

The company posted a consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of ₹130.5 crore in Q4FY26, up 25% quarter-on-quarter and 21.4% year-on-year (YoY).

Consolidated topline for the quarter stood at ₹2,536.2 crore, down 17.7% sequentially and 3.1% YoY, as domestic product and services revenue saw a 25% sequential decline.

EBITDA before other income, forex and exceptional items rose 4.2% sequentially to ₹208.7 crore.

For the full fiscal year FY26, Sonata reported consolidated revenue of ₹10,701.2 crore, up 5.4% YoY, while PAT rose 9.3% to ₹464.4 crore.

Sonata said it won two large deals during the quarter and is positioning itself as a strategic partner for enterprises undertaking AI modernisation initiatives.

“We won two large deals in Q4FY26 and remain confident in Sonata’s growth momentum, by becoming the strategic partners to our clients to enable the AI modernisation journey,” said Rajsekhar Datta Roy, CEO-designate of the company. “We will continue to invest in AI capabilities and partnerships to further accelerate our pivot to AI.”

The company has been increasing its focus on AI-led services through its Harmoni.AI platform and agentic AI offerings. Sonata said over 90% of its workforce has been AI-trained as it pushes deeper into enterprise AI adoption, cloud transformation and automation services.

Its international IT services business reported revenue of ₹779.2 crore in the March quarter, up 5.5% sequentially. Segment PAT rose 40.6% quarter-on-quarter to ₹84.2 crore. In dollar terms, the international IT services business reported revenue of $82.4 million, largely flat sequentially.

The company added seven new customers during the quarter.

In March, Sonata Software informed stock exchanges that its subsidiary, Sonata Software North America has initiated legal proceedings in the United States to recover unpaid dues and damages from one of its clients. The matter was filed before the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware.

title: OpenAI Introduces GPT-Realtime-2 With GPT-5-Level Reasoning for Voice Assistants
content:
The new campus will house over 700 employees across engineering and customer-facing functions in Sector 129.

What Actually Matters.

Adobe has opened its seventh office in India, located in Noida, focusing on innovation and AI-led growth.

The new campus will accommodate over 700 employees working in engineering and customer-facing roles.

Adobe has opened a new office in Noida as part of its continued investment in India. This new facility marks the seventh office for this company in India and the third in Uttar Pradesh.

Adobe added that the office reflects its focus on India as a hub for innovation, product development, and AI-led growth. The campus, located in Sector 129, will accommodate more than 700 employees working across engineering and customer-focused roles.

“As the world is transformed by AI and agentic technologies, Adobe is at the forefront reimagining what’s possible and shaping the future of innovation,” said Abhigyan Modi, Country Manager for Adobe India and Senior Vice President of Document Cloud. He added that teams in India play a “critical role” in advancing the company’s AI strategy.

Adobe said the Noida office uses technology-focused workplace systems to support collaboration and product development. “The new Adobe office represents our focus on creating an environment where people can do their best work,” said Swati Rustagi, Vice President of Employee Experience at Adobe India. “Every aspect of the campus fosters co-creation and collaboration.”

Adobe began operations in India in 1997 as an engineering and research centre. The company now employs more than 8,000 people in the country, making India its largest workforce base outside the United States. Its India teams contribute to over one-third of the company’s innovation efforts.

The company has also expanded its AI and education initiatives in recent months.

In February 2026, Adobe announced free access to tools, including Adobe Firefly, Adobe Photoshop, and Adobe Acrobat, for Indian students at accredited institutions. It also partnered with Airtel to offer Adobe Express Premium to 360 million users in India.

Adobe recently appointed Manoj Kohli, former CEO of Bharti Airtel and ex-SoftBank India head, to its International Advisory Board. The company also strengthened its India leadership team with the appointments of Shamik Basu, former VP at Microsoft, and Manoj Nagpal, former MD at OpenText India.

OpenAI has unveiled three new real-time audio models aimed at developers building voice assistants, customer support systems, translation tools and live transcription services.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI has launched three new real-time audio models for voice assistants and customer support systems.

GPT-Realtime-2 features GPT-5-level reasoning, allowing for complex task handling and natural conversations.

OpenAI has launched a new set of voice intelligence features in its API, introducing three real-time audio models designed to make AI voice conversations more natural, responsive and capable of handling complex tasks as people speak.

The company announced the launch of GPT-Realtime-2, GPT-Realtime-Translate and GPT-Realtime-Whisper, aimed at developers building voice assistants, customer support systems, translation tools and live transcription services.

“Voice is becoming one of the most natural ways people interact with software, especially while multitasking, travelling or seeking support in different languages. The new models are designed to help AI systems not only respond faster but also understand context, reason through requests, and continue conversations more naturally,” OpenAI stated.

GPT-Realtime-2 is OpenAI’s first voice model with GPT-5-class reasoning abilities. The model can handle interruptions, recover from mistakes, call multiple tools at once and maintain longer conversations using a larger 128K context window. Developers can also adjust the reasoning level based on the complexity of a task.

The company said the model supports more human-like interactions by allowing AI agents to use phrases such as “let me check that” while processing requests. They added that the model performs significantly better than earlier versions in live audio intelligence and instruction-following benchmarks.

OpenAI also introduced GPT-Realtime-Translate, a live translation model that supports over 70 input languages and 13 output languages. The model translates conversations in real time while keeping pace with the speaker. The tool could be useful for customer support, education, travel, media and global business communication.

Prateek Sachan, Co-founder and CTO of BolnaAI, said, “The translation model performed well across Indian languages. In our evaluations across Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu, GPT-Realtime-Translate delivered lower word.”

The third model, GPT-Realtime-Whisper, is a low-latency speech-to-text system that transcribes conversations in real time as users speak. The model can be used for captions, meeting notes, customer support workflows and healthcare or recruitment applications.

Josh Weisberg, Senior Vice President and Head of AI at Zillow, said, “The new model improved the company’s voice AI performance significantly. What stood out about GPT-Realtime-2 was the intelligence and tool-calling reliability it brings to complex voice interactions. On our hardest adversarial benchmark, this translates to a 26-point lift in call success rate after prompt optimisation.”

The new voice models are now available through its Realtime API with built-in safeguards against misuse and support for enterprise privacy and EU data-residency requirements.

title: IndiaAI & ICMR Sign MoU to Build Ethical AI Ecosystem for Indian Healthcare
content:
The collaboration aims to strengthen the use of artificial intelligence in healthcare through shared datasets, AI research and public health innovation.

What Actually Matters.

IndiaAI and ICMR have signed an MoU to enhance the ethical use of AI in healthcare.

The collaboration aims to create a connected AI ecosystem by integrating health datasets and AI capabilities.

The Indian government’s AI initiative, IndiaAI Mission, has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) to accelerate the responsible use of artificial intelligence in healthcare.

The collaboration announced on May 7 by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) aims to create a more connected and interoperable AI ecosystem for healthcare in India. The partnership will combine IndiaAI’s technology infrastructure and AI capabilities with ICMR’s expertise in biomedical research and public health.

Under the agreement, both organisations will work together on AI-driven healthcare innovation, research and deployment. The partnership will focus on improving access to high-quality healthcare datasets, enabling advanced AI research and developing solutions for public health challenges.

One of the key components of the collaboration is the integration of ICMR’s anonymised and ethics-approved health research datasets into IndiaAI’s AIKosh platform. The datasets, AI models and toolkits developed under ICMR’s Medical Information Data for AI Solutions (MIDAS) framework will be made accessible to researchers, startups, and innovators.

IndiaAI will also provide ICMR with subsidised access to GPU-based and high-performance computing infrastructure.

The two organisations will additionally co-develop AI applications targeting public health priorities in India. These projects will use ICMR’s disease-burden data along with IndiaAI’s computing and AI ecosystem support.

The collaboration builds on earlier partnerships between the two institutions. In September 2025, IndiaAI and ICMR’s National Institute for Research in Digital Health and Data Sciences were recognised as Pioneer Countries under the HealthAI Global Regulatory Network, a multilateral initiative launched with the United Kingdom and Singapore to promote responsible AI governance in healthcare.

The new partnership is expected to support innovation while ensuring ethical standards, data privacy and regulatory compliance in AI-based healthcare systems.

Voice AI company Krisp has introduced VIVA 2.0 to help AI-powered voice agents handle interruptions, background noise, and conversational cues.

What Actually Matters.

Krisp has launched VIVA 2.0 to enhance the reliability of AI-powered voice agents in noisy, real-world environments.

The updated platform features lightweight, real-time audio models for better understanding of interruptions and conversational cues.

Voice AI company Krisp has launched VIVA 2.0, a new version of its voice infrastructure platform designed to improve the reliability of AI-powered voice agents and conversational systems operating in real-world environments.

The company said the updated platform introduces a new generation of lightweight, real-time audio models that help AI systems better understand interruptions, detect accents, identify synthetic speech, and predict when users have finished speaking.

The launch comes as enterprises increasingly adopt voice AI systems for customer service, IVRs and automated support operations. According to the company, voice agent usage grew 9x in 2025, but many systems continue to struggle outside controlled demo environments due to background noise, interruptions, and speech recognition errors.

“Voice is becoming the primary interface between humans and AI,” said Robert Schoenfield, EVP of Licensing and Partnerships at Krisp. He added that those conversations don’t happen in clean environments. They happen in the real world, shaped by noise and subtle human cues.

Krisp said VIVA 2.0 works as an infrastructure layer, sitting between speech-to-text and language models, helping clean and interpret audio signals before AI systems process them.

One of the key additions is Turn Prediction v3, a multilingual model that predicts when a speaker has completed a sentence without relying on text transcription. The company said this helps reduce awkward interruptions and improves conversational flow.

The platform also introduced Interrupt Prediction, which distinguishes between genuine interruptions and simple conversational acknowledgements such as “hmm” or “yes.”

Krisp has also added a set of real-time “signal detectors” capable of identifying accents, speaker gender and AI-generated speech. According to the company, the accent detection feature can route audio to speech recognition systems optimised for specific accents, improving transcription accuracy.

The upgraded Voice Isolation v3 model aims to reduce background noise and improve speech recognition quality during calls.

The company noted that the platform currently processes over 12 billion minutes of voice AI traffic annually and is integrated into more than 130 voice AI products, including Telnyx, LiveKit, and Vapi.

title: Karnataka Plans Advanced Spacetech Testing Infra, SME Involvement for Commercial Launches
content:
Pixxel, KaleidEO, Astrogate Labs, GalaxEye, Ananth Technologies, Centum Electronics, HAL, and IN-SPACe participated in the discussions

What Actually Matters.

Karnataka aims to be India's premier commercial space innovation hub.

The state is planning to enhance space infrastructure and manufacturing.

The Karnataka government has intensified its push to position the state as India’s leading commercial space innovation hub, with plans to strengthen infrastructure, manufacturing, testing capabilities, skilling, and data-driven applications across the spacetech ecosystem.

The Department of Electronics, IT, and BT convened a high-level consultation chaired by Priyank Kharge, Karnataka Minister for Rural Development & Panchayat Raj and IT/BT, bringing together startups, academia, industry leaders, and institutional stakeholders to deliberate on the next phase of the state’s space economy ambitions.

The discussions followed the recent launch of Karnataka’s Centre of Excellence (CoE) for Space Technology that focuses on building a comprehensive ecosystem spanning upstream and downstream space applications, advanced manufacturing, and innovation.

Addressing the roundtable, Kharge said, “Spacetech is a key pillar in Karnataka’s deeptech stack under our DeepTech Decade vision. Karnataka is uniquely positioned to lead the next phase of India’s commercial space growth by building deep capabilities across innovation, advanced manufacturing, data, upstream, and downstream applications.”

He further highlighted the importance of shared infrastructure for startups and MSMEs, stating, “Common testing and validation infrastructure can significantly reduce barriers for startups and MSMEs while accelerating product development cycles and commercial readiness. Equally, space data is becoming foundational to the new-space economy, with applications across agriculture, climate resilience, logistics, disaster management, and governance. Karnataka must lead not only in launches and innovation, but across the entire space value chain.”

A major focus of the consultation was the proposed establishment of a Common Assembly, Integration and Testing (AIT) facility in Karnataka, particularly to support functional and environmental testing for startups and manufacturers. According to the department, land parcels around Bengaluru are being evaluated, with work expected to begin in the coming weeks under a public-private partnership model to create advanced testing infrastructure.

Stakeholders also discussed enabling easier access to existing testing infrastructure available across government institutions, academia, and industry, while exploring the development of dedicated space manufacturing parks and cluster-based industrial ecosystems aligned with Karnataka’s Space Policy.

Dr N Manjula, Secretary, IT BT Department, said Karnataka’s early policy interventions have helped shape its leadership position in the sector. She stated Karnataka's draft Space Policy, reflecting our early commitment towards building a globally competitive commercial space ecosystem. “Our policy vision is anchored in long-term ecosystem leadership spanning infrastructure, manufacturing, research, talent development and industry collaboration,” she said.

The consultation also focused on expanding SME participation in the space supply chain and strengthening workforce development through the state’s NIPUNA skilling initiative.

Representatives from leading spacetech startups and organisations, including Pixxel, KaleidEO, Astrogate Labs, GalaxEye, Ananth Technologies, Centum Electronics, HAL, and IN-SPACe, participated in the discussions, alongside research institutions and academia.

title: Udemy Adds AI Avatars & Custom Scenarios to Its Role Play Learning Tool
content:
The edtech platform’s latest update brings immersive video and enterprise-grade customisation to its applied skills practice feature.

What Actually Matters.

Udemy has enhanced its AI Role Play feature with lifelike video avatars and advanced customisation options.

Organisations can create tailored Role Play scenarios for specific job roles and skill levels.

Udemy has announced a significant expansion of its AI-powered Role Play feature, introducing lifelike video avatars and deeper customisation tools to make workplace skills practice more realistic and scalable for enterprise clients.

The update, announced on May 8, allows organisations to build bespoke Role Play scenarios tailored to specific job roles, industries, and skill levels. Learners can now practise high-stakes professional conversations—from sales negotiations and conflict resolution to feedback delivery and leadership discussions—with AI avatars designed to simulate real-world interactions.

Hugo Sarrazin, President and CEO of Udemy, framed the update as a shift from passive learning to active performance. “Developing certain professional skills requires practice in environments that mirror the real world,” he said. “By expanding our Role Play capabilities with greater customisation and immersive video, we’re helping organisations and individuals turn learning into action, building confidence and capability in the moments that matter most.”

The practical applications are particularly notable for sales teams. Organisations can now design Role Play scenarios built around their own products, markets, and customer profiles, allowing staff to rehearse discovery calls, objection handling, and negotiation tactics before engaging live prospects.

Udemy says its platform already hosts more than 15,000 instructor-created Role Play scenarios, and the feature has facilitated over 400,000 interactive simulations since launch—spanning leadership, communication, and professional development. The company draws on data from millions of learners globally to personalise experiences, with content delivered across multiple languages.

Sarrazin added that the enhancements are designed to close the gap between training and on-the-job impact. “Adding immersive video and customisation to our Role Play technology strengthens Udemy’s ability to deliver learning that translates directly to on-the-job performance,” he said. “With these enhancements, Udemy’s Role Play technology can be even more impactful in enabling learners to build communication skills, executive presence, and decision-making under pressure.”

The move is part of Udemy’s broader push to position itself as an AI-first workforce development platform. The Nasdaq-listed company, headquartered in San Francisco, counts Samsung SDS America, Tata Consultancy Services, Volkswagen, and the World Bank Group among its enterprise customers.

title: Ramp Builds AI Model Better than Claude Opus for Navigating Spreadsheets
content:
Built on top of the Qwen models, Fast Ask is designed to navigate and retrieve data from spreadsheets.

What Actually Matters.

Ramp and Prime Intellect developed Fast Ask for spreadsheet data retrieval.

Fast Ask uses the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B architecture for improved speed and accuracy.

Fintech company Ramp and AI infrastructure company Prime Intellect have developed Fast Ask, an AI model designed to navigate and retrieve data from business spreadsheets.

It is based on the open-weights Qwen3.5-35B-A3B architecture to process queries faster and with greater exact-match accuracy than Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.6 model.

“A spreadsheet agent is only as good as the information it retrieves,” the developers from Ramp wrote in a post on X, explaining that standard models frequently fail to extract necessary data on their first attempt.

We partnered with @PrimeIntellect to build Fast Ask, a small RL-trained subagent that helps our Sheets agent find answers in spreadsheets. It scores +4% over Opus on exact match accuracy at Haiku latency. pic.twitter.com/GJQvHJjABl

— Ramp Labs (@RampLabs) May 7, 2026

“Given a question like ‘What was the revenue from March to May?’, Fast Ask navigates the workbook, reads the relevant ranges, and returns a compact answer for the main agent to use,” Ramp stated.

Prior to developing the new model, Ramp observed high exploration overhead in its production environment. “The main agent spent 17.8% of all tool calls opening tabs, reading ranges, and filtering irrelevant sheets before it had the data needed to answer,” the company stated. This frequent data scanning wastes processing tokens on irrelevant rows and increases the risk that the model will anchor on decoy information.

To resolve this inefficiency, Ramp collaborated with Prime Intellect to apply reinforcement learning (RL) post-training to a Qwen model, with 3 billion active parameters.

“This was a good fit for RL because spreadsheet retrieval is repeated often, latency sensitive, and has clean feedback,” Ramp wrote. “The model either returns the right cent amount, date, invoice ID, yes/no, or row reference, or it does not. That let us optimise the retrieval policy directly with deterministic rewards.”

The engineers trained Fast Ask across 100 steps using synthetic business datasets designed to mimic real-world financial workflows, including revenue rollups and invoice reconciliation.

The training environment incorporated adversarial elements such as decoy sheets and ambiguous identifiers to build robust navigation policies.

The resulting Fast Ask system increased exact-match task completion accuracy by 10 percentage points compared to its base model.

During evaluation, the subagent outperformed Claude Opus by four percentage points while operating at the much lower latency profile of Claude Haiku 4.5. The developers attributed this success heavily to training parameters rather than sheer computing power.

“The important work was not in model architecture or scale but in environment design: the right tasks, a minimal tool interface, and a reward function grounded in how the product actually works in production,” Ramp reported.

This is one of the many internal AI advances Ramp has made over the past year. The company has deployed a suite of automated tools, including procurement agents and systems designed to detect AI-generated fake invoices.

Ramp has also built Inspect, an internal background coding agent that autonomously writes, tests, verifies, and submits code changes. Ramp says Inspect now contributes a substantial share of merged pull requests internally. In March, Ramp deployed an agentic AI system to continuously monitor, triage, and propose fixes for its Ramp Sheets software, an AI-native spreadsheet editor.

title: IIT Madras Global Research Foundation Plans $7.5M Deeptech Hub in Silicon Valley
content:
The institute's first US centre, located in Menlo Park, aims to connect Indian deeptech startups with global capital, mentorship, and markets.

What Actually Matters.

IIT Madras Global Research Foundation is establishing its first US centre in Menlo Park to enhance Indian deeptech innovation.

The centre focuses on startup incubation, industry-academia partnerships, and venture engagement to support high-potential innovations.

Indian Institute of Technology Madras Global Research Foundation (IITM Global) will establish its first centre in the United States, located in Menlo Park, California, in a push to bring Indian deeptech innovation into the heart of Silicon Valley.

The West Coast centre was formally launched on April 24, in partnership with CA Startups.

It will focus on deeptech research and commercialisation, startup incubation, industry–academia partnerships, and venture engagement to support high-potential innovations. It also aims to attract global innovation back into India, creating a two-way corridor between the two countries.

The centre will be developed with a total planned investment of $7.5 million, including a greenfield investment of $4.5 million from IITM Global. Its primary mandate is to serve as a launchpad for Indian deeptech startups seeking access to global capital, markets, mentorship, and strategic partnerships.

Prof V Kamakoti, Director of IIT Madras and Chairman of IITM Global, described the expansion as a natural progression of the institute's long-term ambitions. "This expansion into the United States represents a natural progression of IIT Madras' vision to take Indian research and innovation to the global stage. The Menlo Park center will enable deeper collaboration with global industry leaders, academia, and venture ecosystems, fostering cutting-edge innovation and talent exchange," he said in a statement.

Prof Raghunathan Rengaswamy, Director of IITM Global, highlighted the significance of the West Coast location. "Our West Coast presence positions us at the heart of global technology innovation. This center will catalyse translational research, scale deeptech startups, and build enduring partnerships that bridge India and the United States," he said.

Prof. Preeti Aghalayam, Dean of Global Engagement at IIT Madras and a Director of IITM Global, framed the initiative in terms of opportunity for students and researchers. "This initiative is about creating a seamless global innovation corridor. It will empower students, researchers, and entrepreneurs to engage meaningfully with international ecosystems, enhancing both impact and opportunity," she said.

Thirumalai Madhavnarayan, CEO and Director of IITM Global, pointed to the centre's role as a strategic anchor for the foundation's broader US operations. "With a focused investment approach, we aim to build a platform that accelerates deeptech ventures from lab to global markets, while also attracting global innovation into India," he said.

In addition to the Menlo Park facility, IITM Global has announced plans for a second centre on the US East Coast, intended to complement the West Coast hub by connecting with leading policy, financial, and academic ecosystems across the country.

title: OpenAI Introduces GPT-Realtime-2 With GPT-5-Level Reasoning for Voice Assistants
content:
OpenAI has unveiled three new real-time audio models aimed at developers building voice assistants, customer support systems, translation tools and live transcription services.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI has launched three new real-time audio models for voice assistants and customer support systems.

GPT-Realtime-2 features GPT-5-level reasoning, allowing for complex task handling and natural conversations.

OpenAI has launched a new set of voice intelligence features in its API, introducing three real-time audio models designed to make AI voice conversations more natural, responsive and capable of handling complex tasks as people speak.

The company announced the launch of GPT-Realtime-2, GPT-Realtime-Translate and GPT-Realtime-Whisper, aimed at developers building voice assistants, customer support systems, translation tools and live transcription services.

“Voice is becoming one of the most natural ways people interact with software, especially while multitasking, travelling or seeking support in different languages. The new models are designed to help AI systems not only respond faster but also understand context, reason through requests, and continue conversations more naturally,” OpenAI stated.

GPT-Realtime-2 is OpenAI’s first voice model with GPT-5-class reasoning abilities. The model can handle interruptions, recover from mistakes, call multiple tools at once and maintain longer conversations using a larger 128K context window. Developers can also adjust the reasoning level based on the complexity of a task.

The company said the model supports more human-like interactions by allowing AI agents to use phrases such as “let me check that” while processing requests. They added that the model performs significantly better than earlier versions in live audio intelligence and instruction-following benchmarks.

OpenAI also introduced GPT-Realtime-Translate, a live translation model that supports over 70 input languages and 13 output languages. The model translates conversations in real time while keeping pace with the speaker. The tool could be useful for customer support, education, travel, media and global business communication.

Prateek Sachan, Co-founder and CTO of BolnaAI, said, “The translation model performed well across Indian languages. In our evaluations across Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu, GPT-Realtime-Translate delivered lower word.”

The third model, GPT-Realtime-Whisper, is a low-latency speech-to-text system that transcribes conversations in real time as users speak. The model can be used for captions, meeting notes, customer support workflows and healthcare or recruitment applications.

Josh Weisberg, Senior Vice President and Head of AI at Zillow, said, “The new model improved the company’s voice AI performance significantly. What stood out about GPT-Realtime-2 was the intelligence and tool-calling reliability it brings to complex voice interactions. On our hardest adversarial benchmark, this translates to a 26-point lift in call success rate after prompt optimisation.”

The new voice models are now available through its Realtime API with built-in safeguards against misuse and support for enterprise privacy and EU data-residency requirements.
