title: TSMC, Sony Semiconductor Plan Joint Venture for Next-Gen Image Sensors
content:
The companies will establish a joint venture at Sony’s new fabrication facility in Kumamoto prefecture, Japan.

Image source: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., Ltd.

What Actually Matters.

TSMC and Sony Semiconductor Solutions are forming a joint venture for next-generation image sensors at Sony's new facility in Japan.

Sony will maintain majority control in the joint venture, leveraging its design expertise alongside TSMC's manufacturing capabilities.

Sony Semiconductor Solutions and TSMC have signed a preliminary agreement to form a strategic partnership to develop and manufacture next-generation image sensors. The companies said they plan to establish a joint venture at Sony’s new fabrication facility in Kumamoto prefecture, Japan.

Under the proposed structure, Sony will remain the majority and controlling shareholder in the joint venture. The companies said the partnership will combine Sony’s image sensor design expertise with TSMC’s semiconductor manufacturing and process technologies.

Shinji Sashida, President and CEO of Sony Semiconductor Solutions Corporation, said that Sony plans to strengthen its operations by developing higher-value products and technologies.

They also plan to expand image sensor applications in physical AI areas such as automotive and robotics.

The companies signed a non-binding MoU for the partnership. They are now discussing possible investments for the joint venture, along with Sony’s additional capital investment in its existing Nagasaki plant. The companies said they will phase out these investments based on market demand and support from the Japanese government.

TSMC Senior VP and Deputy Co-COO, Kevin Zhang, said Sony has been TSMC’s long-term partner in the CMOS image sensor business. He added that the agreement marks a key step in advancing sensing technologies for the AI era.

The companies said the joint venture still depends on signing a final binding agreement and meeting customary closing conditions.

Recently, TSMC introduced its A13 process technology to meet rising demand for AI, high-performance computing, and mobile applications. But the new node builds on A14’s process and will enter production only in 2029, one year after A14.

Moreover, on April 28 and 29, the company sold all its shares in Arm Holdings, primarily owned by the Japanese conglomerate SoftBank Group, according to a company filing accessed by AIM.

title: Google for Startups, Antler India Launch Two-Phase AI Programme for Indian Founders
content:
The programme targets startups with live products and verified traction, combining Google's technical curriculum with Antler's venture track.

What Actually Matters.

Google for Startups and Antler India have launched a two-phase AI programme for Indian startups with existing products and traction.

The programme includes an online immersion with technical and venture tracks, covering AI tools and investment insights.

Google for Startups and Antler India have jointly launched the Google for Startups Immersion, a hybrid programme aimed at founders, CTOs, and technical leads building AI-led companies in India. Applications opened on May 8 and will close on May 22.

The programme is structured in two phases—an online immersion followed by an invitation-only offline session—and is explicitly designed for startups that already have a live product and early traction. Idea-stage startups without a deployed product are not eligible.

The first phase will run online across four sessions and is open to up to 5,000 founders across India. The technical track will cover AI Studio, Antigravity, and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform through hands-on implementation sessions. Running in parallel, the venture track, led by Antler India, will address the current AI investment climate, unit economics, and what defensibility means to investors today.

The second phase is scheduled at Google's Ananta office in Bengaluru. It is reserved for the top 25 startups from the online cohort. Selection will involve a joint review by Google and Antler, followed by 20-minute rapid interviews from a shortlist of 50 startups. The in-person day will include live architecture whiteboarding with Google Cloud Customer Engineers, one-on-one office hours with Antler's team on go-to-market strategy, pricing, and fundraising, as well as an off-the-record fireside chat and founder mixer.

"The Google for Startups Immersion is designed for founders who are already building and want to go deeper on implementation. We want to help strong technical teams work more closely with Google's AI tools and infrastructure, while also giving them access to the business perspective they need to scale," Ragini Das, Head of Google for Startups India, said in a statement.

Antler India partner Nitin Sharma framed the programme within a broader shift in India's startup ecosystem. "India's AI moment is finally here. We are now emerging as the world's next exciting ecosystem to build for all layers of the AI stack. The talent is exceptional, and the ambition is increasingly global. Through our Residency programs, Antler has worked with founders from day zero, from validating an idea through to the first investment. The Google for Startups Immersion extends that philosophy: we are meeting founders where they already are, including those with a live product and real traction, and helping them build game-changing ventures."

Antler India operates through a $75 million India fund and has backed over 115 startups across sectors, including AI, fintech, deeptech, health, and climate. Globally, the firm has invested in over 1,300 startups across 30 cities and aims to support more than 6,000 by 2030.

Prof. Preeti Aghalayam, Dean of Global Engagement at IIT Madras and a Director of IITM Global, framed the initiative in terms of opportunity for students and researchers. "This initiative is about creating a seamless global innovation corridor. It will empower students, researchers, and entrepreneurs to engage meaningfully with international ecosystems, enhancing both impact and opportunity," she said.

Thirumalai Madhavnarayan, CEO and Director of IITM Global, pointed to the centre's role as a strategic anchor for the foundation's broader US operations. "With a focused investment approach, we aim to build a platform that accelerates deeptech ventures from lab to global markets, while also attracting global innovation into India," he said.

In addition to the Menlo Park facility, IITM Global has announced plans for a second centre on the US East Coast, intended to complement the West Coast hub by connecting with leading policy, financial, and academic ecosystems across the country.

title: Vi Partners With PhysicsWallah to Bundle Mobile Data With Competitive Exam Prep
content:
The educational material spans kindergarten to Class 12, along with preparation for examinations such as JEE, NEET, UPSC, CUET, GATE, Olympiads and defence entrance tests.

What Actually Matters.

Vodafone Idea has collaborated with PhysicsWallah to launch Vi Edu+, a prepaid service for students preparing for competitive exams.

Vi Edu+ combines unlimited mobile data with access to PhysicsWallah's educational resources, including lectures and practice tests.

Telecom operator Vodafone Idea (Vi) has partnered with edtech platform PhysicsWallah to introduce a new prepaid offering aimed at students preparing for board and competitive examinations.

Called Vi Edu+, the service combines unlimited mobile connectivity with access to PhysicsWallah’s educational platform ‘Pi’, allowing students to access study material, lectures, practice tests and AI-powered learning tools through bundled recharge plans.

The offering has been launched initially in Rajasthan and Eastern Uttar Pradesh circles, with plans for phased expansion to other regions.

Under the partnership, students purchasing the Vi Edu+ prepaid packs will receive unlimited 4G/5G data, voice calls, daily SMS benefits and a 28-day subscription to PW Pi Pro. The recharge pack is priced at ₹375 in Rajasthan and ₹409 in UP East.

The companies said the initiative is designed to make structured digital learning more affordable and accessible, particularly for students who may not have easy access to coaching centres or premium online subscriptions.

PhysicsWallah’s Pi platform includes more than 30,000 video lectures, handwritten notes, revision series, practice tests and AI-powered doubt-solving tools. The content spans kindergarten to Class 12, along with preparation for examinations such as JEE, NEET, UPSC, CUET, GATE, Olympiads and defence entrance tests.

The platform also offers courses in technology, finance, design, marketing, and generative AI, reflecting the increasing demand for skill-based online learning among students and young professionals.

Commenting on the partnership, Avneesh Khosla, Chief Marketing Officer at Vi, said, “The company is looking to move beyond connectivity and integrate education into its core offerings.”

He added that the partnership with PhysicsWallah will allow them to deliver credible and structured educational content to a wider audience, especially those who aspire to learn and grow but are constrained by affordability or access.

Prateek Maheshwari, Co-founder of PhysicsWallah, said, “The collaboration aims to simplify digital learning by combining educational resources with everyday mobile usage.”

The collaboration also reflects the growing convergence of telecom and edtech sectors as companies look to tap into India’s expanding digital learning market, particularly in smaller cities and emerging education hubs.

title: IBM, Yotta to Build Agentic AI Platform with Sovereign Capabilities for Indian Enterprises
content:
IBM and Yotta also plan to bring IBM Sovereign Core to India by deploying it on Yotta’s Shakti Cloud.

What Actually Matters.

IBM and Yotta will create an agentic AI platform for Indian enterprises.

This platform will combine IBM's AI software with Yotta's sovereign cloud infrastructure.

IBM and Yotta Data Services plan to build an agentic AI platform for enterprises and government organisations in India, combining IBM’s AI software stack with Yotta’s sovereign cloud infrastructure.

The proposed platform will use IBM’s watsonx Orchestrate and run on Yotta’s Shakti Cloud, targeting organisations looking to deploy AI systems while meeting requirements around data residency, security, and regulatory compliance.

The companies said the platform is intended to help enterprises deploy and manage AI agents across functions such as IT service management, finance, procurement, human resources, and customer support.

They will jointly pursue proof-of-concept deployments, solution co-creation, and technical enablement initiatives across sectors, including banking and financial services, manufacturing, public sector, and digital-native businesses.

The announcement comes as enterprises move from pilot AI projects to operational deployments and seek infrastructure that allows governance and compliance controls alongside AI automation.

As part of the collaboration, IBM and Yotta also plan to bring IBM Sovereign Core to India by deploying it on Yotta’s Shakti Cloud.

IBM Sovereign Core is a software platform that helps organisations build and operate sovereign AI environments with compliance monitoring, governed AI execution, and operational controls.

“AI innovation in India must be anchored in sovereignty, security, and performance. Together with IBM, we propose to enable enterprises to harness the power of agentic AI on a secure, India-hosted cloud, so they can innovate with confidence while maintaining control over their data and operations,” Sunil Gupta, Co-founder and CEO of Yotta Data Services, said in a statement.

The platform combines compliance monitoring, identity management, encryption, governed AI execution, and audit-ready controls within a single deployment framework. It is built on Red Hat OpenShift and Red Hat AI.

By hosting the platform on Yotta’s India-based infrastructure, the partnership aims to support enterprises and government organisations in meeting data residency mandates and operating AI workloads within sovereign boundaries.

“This collaboration will combine IBM’s AI capabilities with Yotta’s sovereign cloud infrastructure to help organisations scale AI responsibly—embedding sovereignty, governance, transparency, and trust from the outset,” said Sandip Patel, Managing Director, IBM India and South Asia.

Yotta said its Shakti Cloud provides GPU infrastructure and AI services for enterprises, including AI labs, inference services, and Kubernetes clusters with GPU resources. The company operates data centre parks in Navi Mumbai and Greater Noida and is part of NVIDIA’s cloud partner ecosystem.

title: Voice AI Startup Krisp Launches Infra Platform to Make AI Agents Reliable
content:
Voice AI company Krisp has introduced VIVA 2.0 to help AI-powered voice agents handle interruptions, background noise, and conversational cues.

What Actually Matters.

Krisp has launched VIVA 2.0 to enhance the reliability of AI-powered voice agents in noisy, real-world environments.

The updated platform features lightweight, real-time audio models for better understanding of interruptions and conversational cues.

Voice AI company Krisp has launched VIVA 2.0, a new version of its voice infrastructure platform designed to improve the reliability of AI-powered voice agents and conversational systems operating in real-world environments.

The company said the updated platform introduces a new generation of lightweight, real-time audio models that help AI systems better understand interruptions, detect accents, identify synthetic speech, and predict when users have finished speaking.

The launch comes as enterprises increasingly adopt voice AI systems for customer service, IVRs and automated support operations. According to the company, voice agent usage grew 9x in 2025, but many systems continue to struggle outside controlled demo environments due to background noise, interruptions, and speech recognition errors.

“Voice is becoming the primary interface between humans and AI,” said Robert Schoenfield, EVP of Licensing and Partnerships at Krisp. He added that those conversations don’t happen in clean environments. They happen in the real world, shaped by noise and subtle human cues.

Krisp said VIVA 2.0 works as an infrastructure layer, sitting between speech-to-text and language models, helping clean and interpret audio signals before AI systems process them.

One of the key additions is Turn Prediction v3, a multilingual model that predicts when a speaker has completed a sentence without relying on text transcription. The company said this helps reduce awkward interruptions and improves conversational flow.

The platform also introduced Interrupt Prediction, which distinguishes between genuine interruptions and simple conversational acknowledgements such as “hmm” or “yes.”

Krisp has also added a set of real-time “signal detectors” capable of identifying accents, speaker gender and AI-generated speech. According to the company, the accent detection feature can route audio to speech recognition systems optimised for specific accents, improving transcription accuracy.

The upgraded Voice Isolation v3 model aims to reduce background noise and improve speech recognition quality during calls.

The company noted that the platform currently processes over 12 billion minutes of voice AI traffic annually and is integrated into more than 130 voice AI products, including Telnyx, LiveKit, and Vapi.

title: Mira Murati Says Sam Altman Was ‘Creating Chaos’ at OpenAI During Musk Trial
content:
Murati briefly served as OpenAI’s interim CEO after Altman was temporarily removed by the board in 2023.

What Actually Matters.

Mira Murati testified that Sam Altman created distrust among OpenAI executives.

Altman reportedly made conflicting statements and was deceptive with his colleagues.

Former OpenAI Chief Technology Officer Mira Murati testified in federal court on May 6 that CEO Sam Altman created distrust among senior executives as the company accelerated the development and deployment of its AI models

Murati’s recorded testimony was played in a federal courtroom in Oakland, California, during the second week of billionaire Elon Musk’s lawsuit against OpenAI.

“My concern was about Sam saying one thing to one person and completely the opposite to another person,” Murati said during the testimony. She added that Altman was “creating chaos” and, at times, was deceptive with her and other executives.

The lawsuit, filed by Musk in 2024, alleges that OpenAI improperly transitioned into a for-profit company and abandoned its original charitable mission. Musk is seeking $150 billion in damages from OpenAI and Microsoft, with the funds intended to benefit OpenAI’s nonprofit arm.

If successful, the case could disrupt OpenAI’s commercial ambitions and potentially benefit Musk’s competing AI venture xAI, which is now part of SpaceX.

Murati, who briefly served as OpenAI’s interim CEO after Altman was temporarily removed by the board in 2023, said the CEO often pitted executives against one another and undermined her authority as CTO.

Despite those concerns, she said she still wanted Altman to remain Chief Executive and sought more clarity from the board about its decision to remove him.

“OpenAI was at catastrophic risk of falling apart,” Murati said. “I was concerned about the company completely blowing up.”

The trial has emerged as a critical moment for OpenAI, whose AI models have become deeply embedded across industries, schools, businesses, and government institutions.

Former OpenAI board member Shivon Zilis also testified, citing internal concerns surrounding the release of ChatGPT. According to Zilis, the board “voiced extreme concern” about releasing ChatGPT “without any semblance of board communication.”

When asked whether she had internally raised concerns about Altman, Zilis said “there had been a couple of instances.”

Zilis, who is mother to four of Musk’s children, currently works at his company Neuralink.

Testimony from Musk, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, and other former executives has revealed deep disagreements over OpenAI’s direction, leadership structure, and funding strategy.

Court proceedings also disclosed that Musk had attempted to settle with Brockman days before the trial began and had at one point felt like “a fool” for continuing to fund OpenAI.

title: InMobi Acquires AI-Powered iOS Growth Platform MobileAction for Ad Intelligence
content:
Green-only NBFC Ecofy is doubling down on distributed clean energy finance.

What Actually Matters.

Ecofy has raised $15 million from Mirova to expand its green lending for solar and electric mobility.

The company serves over 130,000 customers across India, focusing on last-mile and small-enterprise borrowers.

Ecofy, a climate-focused non-banking financial company (NBFC), has secured $15 million from Mirova, an affiliate of Natixis Investment Managers, to scale its lending portfolio across rooftop solar and electric mobility. The deal marks Mirova's fourth investment in India under its dedicated energy transition strategy for emerging markets.

Founded in 2022 by Rajashree Nambiar and Govind Sankaranarayanan, and registered with the Reserve Bank of India, Ecofy has grown to serve over 130,000 customers across 26 states and more than 500 cities in just three years. The company counts Eversource Capital, British International Investment, FMO, and Finnfund among its existing backers.

Ecofy will deploy the fresh funding toward onward lending for residential and commercial rooftop solar installations, along with electric vehicles, primarily two- and three-wheelers. The focus on last-mile and small-enterprise borrowers.

“We are backing platforms that demonstrate the ability to deploy capital efficiently at the ground level, combining scale, local reach, and measurable impact,” Priyanka Mehrotra, Investment Director at Mirova, said in a statement.

The deal arrives amid growing investor interest in India's climate financing ecosystem, particularly in distributed renewable energy and electric mobility—segments considered critical to the country's decarbonisation roadmap.

Vivek Khandelwal, Head of Treasury at Ecofy, noted that access to long-term, mission-aligned capital is central to building out a robust financing ecosystem for India's green transition, particularly for households and small businesses adopting rooftop solar and EVs.

As policy tailwinds from PM Surya Ghar and EV subsidy schemes continue to spur demand, the analytical question becomes whether specialised green lenders can outpace larger banks and embedded-finance challengers in customer acquisition and credit underwriting at scale.

InMobi expects the acquisition to strengthen its advertising capabilities.

What Actually Matters.

InMobi has acquired MobileAction to enhance its advertising capabilities within the iOS ecosystem.

MobileAction offers AI-powered app analytics and App Store Optimisation, serving notable clients like Google and Meta.

Global technology company InMobi has acquired MobileAction, an AI-powered platform specialising in iOS app growth and App Store Optimisation (ASO). The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

InMobi expects the acquisition to strengthen its advertising capabilities in helping brands reach new app users across the iOS ecosystem, both through organic growth and AI-powered optimisation.

Founded in 2013 and headquartered in San Francisco, MobileAction offers AI-driven app analytics, with expertise in Apple Ads and ASO, and counts Google, Meta, DoorDash, Square, Zalando, Playtika, and Priceline among its global clientele.

The platform's data assets encompass over 90 million creatives, 6 million keywords, 5 million apps, 100,000 publishers, and 500,000 advertisers.

For InMobi, the deal extends the company's full-stack advantage, pairing its agentic commerce consumer platform, Glance, with a global advertising offering now further enhanced by MobileAction's specialised iOS expertise, it noted in a statement.

Rohit Dosi, Vice President and General Manager at InMobi, described the rationale behind the move. "As the advertising ecosystem shifts toward AI-led intelligence and platform-native expertise, marketers need partners who can deliver both scale and precision. MobileAction's AI-powered platform and leadership in helping marketers drive growth for their apps make this a highly strategic addition to InMobi Advertising. Together, we're better positioned to help marketers and brands drive sustainable, intelligent growth in an agentic world," he said.

"Joining InMobi marks an exciting next chapter for MobileAction. I look forward to partnering with Rohit, and I am confident our shared vision for the future of agentic AI-driven advertising—spanning innovation, data-driven decision-making, and customer impact—will allow us to accelerate our roadmap and deliver even greater value to marketers worldwide," MobileAction's Founder and CEO Aykut Karaalioglu added.

Following the close of the transaction, MobileAction will continue to operate as a dedicated platform. Its teams across the United States, Europe, and Turkey will join the InMobi Group. InMobi has indicated plans to invest further in MobileAction's product development and global go-to-market efforts. Key focus markets are the US, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East, and North Africa.

title: Skyroot Aerospace Becomes Unicorn With $60 Mn Funding Ahead of Vikram-1 Launch
content:
The Hyderabad-based company said the fresh capital will be used to scale manufacturing and establish a higher launch cadence for Vikram-1 missions.

What Actually Matters.

Skyroot Aerospace achieved unicorn status after a $60 million funding round.

The new capital will support increased manufacturing and more frequent Vikram-1 launches.

Indian space tech company, Skyroot Aerospace, became a unicorn after raising nearly $60 million in a funding round that valued the company at $1.1 billion, ahead of the maiden orbital launch of its Vikram-1 rocket.

The equity round was co-led by Sherpalo Ventures and GIC, with participation from funds managed by BlackRock, Playbook Partners, Shanghvi Family Office, the founders of Greenko Group, Arkam Ventures, and other investors. As part of the investment, Sherpalo founder Ram Shriram will join Skyroot’s board.

The Hyderabad-based company said the fresh capital will be used to scale manufacturing, establish a higher launch cadence for Vikram-1 missions, and accelerate development of Vikram-2, a one-tonne-class launch vehicle powered by a cryogenic stage.

The funding comes weeks before the planned maiden flight of Vikram-1, which Skyroot describes as India’s first privately developed orbital rocket. The vehicle is designed to carry satellites of up to 350 kilograms to low Earth orbit and offer dedicated launch services to global satellite operators.

“We at Skyroot are excited about the upcoming Vikram-1 launch, India's first private orbital rocket, marking a significant milestone both for India and the global space sector,” said Pawan Kumar Chandana, Co-Founder and CEO of Skyroot Aerospace. “This investment signals confidence from some of the world's most reputed investors in Skyroot.”

Skyroot previously made history in 2022 when it launched Vikram-S, the first privately built Indian rocket to reach space.

Ram Shriram, Founder and Managing Partner at Sherpalo Ventures and a founding board member at Alphabet Inc., said the company has made significant progress since its early days.

“I’ve believed in the Skyroot team since the early days, and that conviction has only deepened as the team marches forward to the launchpad with Vikram-1, India’s first private orbital-class rocket,” Shriram said. “Skyroot is building the foundational infrastructure for that future with the best cost-to-performance ratio in the orbital-launch industry.”

Founded by former ISRO scientists Pawan Kumar Chandana and Naga Bharath Daka, Skyroot develops the Vikram series of launch vehicles to provide on-demand launch access for small satellite operators.

The company said its technology stack includes carbon composite rocket structures along with solid, liquid, and cryogenic propulsion systems developed in-house at its Hyderabad facilities. Its engines include 3D-printed components designed to support rapid manufacturing and launch operations.

With the latest funding round, Skyroot said it has now raised nearly $160 million in total from investors, including GIC and Temasek, as it expands commercial launch operations in the growing private space market.

title: Yellow.ai Launches Multilingual Voice AI Platform With Cloning Support
content:
Yellow.ai’s enterprise voice AI system is built as a fully integrated architecture for speech recognition, conversational AI, and voice synthesis.

What Actually Matters.

Yellow.ai has launched 'Nexus Vox', a multilingual voice AI platform supporting over 500 languages and dialects.

The platform features voice cloning capabilities, allowing enterprises to replicate voices from short audio samples.

Bengaluru-based Yellow.ai has launched ‘Nexus Vox’, a new enterprise voice AI platform capable of cloning voices and supporting over 500 languages and dialects, including Indian regional languages and Hinglish, as companies race to improve multilingual customer support.

The company describes the platform as an enterprise voice AI system built as a fully integrated architecture rather than relying on multiple third-party APIs for speech recognition, conversational AI, and voice synthesis.

According to the company, Nexus Vox delivers response latency below 400 milliseconds, a benchmark which is close to natural human conversation. The platform also includes voice cloning capabilities, allowing enterprises to replicate voices from short audio samples and deploy them across multiple languages.

The launch comes at a time when enterprises are increasingly adopting AI-powered customer service tools, particularly in markets like India, where multilingual communication remains a major operational challenge.

“Enterprise voice AI has been a Frankenstein’s monster — several vendor APIs stitched together, each adding latency and introducing points of failure,” Raghu Ravinutala, CEO and Co-founder at Yellow.ai, said in a statement.

The platform was specifically shaped by Indian enterprise use cases involving code-switching between languages, regional dialects, and noisy real-world environments.

It includes features such as real-time sentiment detection, omnichannel deployment across telephony and web platforms, and integration with Indian language AI models developed by Sarvam AI under the IndiaAI Mission.

The technology is already being used in sectors such as insurance, banking, aviation, and customer service. The company cited deployments including AI voice support systems for motor insurance claims and multilingual customer service operations.

Founded in 2016, Yellow.ai currently serves more than 600 enterprises across 85 countries, while continuing to expand its engineering and AI operations in Bengaluru.

title: MongoDB Bets Big on Enterprise AI With Unified Production-Ready Platform
content:
MangoDB’s new capabilities aim to help enterprises deploy AI agents faster, cheaper, and at scale.

What Actually Matters.

MongoDB aims to streamline enterprise AI deployment with a unified platform, reducing complexity in managing AI applications.

New features include automated embedding generation and persistent agent memory to enhance AI agent performance and scalability.

MongoDB has unveiled a series of new AI-focused capabilities to help enterprises deploy and manage AI agents in production environments, positioning its database platform as a unified infrastructure layer for enterprise AI applications.

Announced at the company’s MongoDB.local London 2026 event, the new offerings include automated embedding generation, persistent agent memory, enhanced performance capabilities, and expanded deployment flexibility across cloud and on-premises environments.

The company said enterprises have historically relied on multiple disconnected systems to manage vector search, memory, embeddings and operational databases for AI applications, creating complexity and scalability challenges. MongoDB is now attempting to consolidate these functions into a single platform.

“The hardest part of running agents in production isn't the model. It's the data layer underneath it,” said CJ Desai, President and Chief Executive Officer of MongoDB, in a statement. “To trust an agent at scale, it has to retrieve the right context, hold memory across sessions, and operate at machine speed, wherever the enterprise needs it.”

The announcement comes as enterprises increasingly move beyond AI experimentation toward deploying AI agents for customer service, workflow automation, and enterprise decision-making. Industry demand is now shifting toward infrastructure that can reliably support real-time retrieval, memory retention and high-volume inference in production environments.

Among the key announcements was Automated Voyage AI Embeddings for MongoDB Vector Search, currently in public preview. The feature automatically generates embeddings whenever data is written or updated, allowing AI agents to retrieve more accurate and up-to-date contextual information without requiring enterprises to build separate embedding pipelines.

MongoDB said the capability significantly reduces the engineering overhead traditionally associated with semantic search infrastructure. Its Voyage AI embedding models currently rank first on the Retrieval Embedding Benchmark, according to the company.

The company also announced the general availability of LangGraph.js Long-Term Memory Store, which enables persistent cross-conversation memory for AI agents built using JavaScript and TypeScript.

“When AI tools and agents produce a wrong answer, the instinct is to blame the model,” said Pablo Stern, CPO of AI and Emerging Products, MangoDB. “But the data platform is what enables the agent with the right context and memory to act correctly.”

MongoDB additionally introduced version 8.3 of its database platform, which it claims delivers up to 45% higher read throughput, 35% higher write throughput, and 30% faster complex operations compared with MongoDB 8.0, without requiring application-level code changes.

“The requirements of enterprises running AI at scale are what we build for. MongoDB 8.3 makes agent workloads faster and cheaper to run on infrastructure customers already have,” said Ben Cefalo, CPO of Core Products.

MongoDB said its platform supports deployment across AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, hybrid environments and on-premises infrastructure.

As part of the update, MongoDB announced the general availability of cross-region connectivity support for AWS PrivateLink, enabling database traffic between MongoDB Atlas clusters across AWS regions to remain entirely within AWS’ private network infrastructure.

Murati briefly served as OpenAI’s interim CEO after Altman was temporarily removed by the board in 2023.

What Actually Matters.

Mira Murati testified that Sam Altman created distrust among OpenAI executives.

Altman reportedly made conflicting statements and was deceptive with his colleagues.

Former OpenAI Chief Technology Officer Mira Murati testified in federal court on May 6 that CEO Sam Altman created distrust among senior executives as the company accelerated the development and deployment of its AI models

Murati’s recorded testimony was played in a federal courtroom in Oakland, California, during the second week of billionaire Elon Musk’s lawsuit against OpenAI.

“My concern was about Sam saying one thing to one person and completely the opposite to another person,” Murati said during the testimony. She added that Altman was “creating chaos” and, at times, was deceptive with her and other executives.

The lawsuit, filed by Musk in 2024, alleges that OpenAI improperly transitioned into a for-profit company and abandoned its original charitable mission. Musk is seeking $150 billion in damages from OpenAI and Microsoft, with the funds intended to benefit OpenAI’s nonprofit arm.

If successful, the case could disrupt OpenAI’s commercial ambitions and potentially benefit Musk’s competing AI venture xAI, which is now part of SpaceX.

Murati, who briefly served as OpenAI’s interim CEO after Altman was temporarily removed by the board in 2023, said the CEO often pitted executives against one another and undermined her authority as CTO.

Despite those concerns, she said she still wanted Altman to remain Chief Executive and sought more clarity from the board about its decision to remove him.

“OpenAI was at catastrophic risk of falling apart,” Murati said. “I was concerned about the company completely blowing up.”

The trial has emerged as a critical moment for OpenAI, whose AI models have become deeply embedded across industries, schools, businesses, and government institutions.

Former OpenAI board member Shivon Zilis also testified, citing internal concerns surrounding the release of ChatGPT. According to Zilis, the board “voiced extreme concern” about releasing ChatGPT “without any semblance of board communication.”

When asked whether she had internally raised concerns about Altman, Zilis said “there had been a couple of instances.”

Zilis, who is mother to four of Musk’s children, currently works at his company Neuralink.

Testimony from Musk, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, and other former executives has revealed deep disagreements over OpenAI’s direction, leadership structure, and funding strategy.

Court proceedings also disclosed that Musk had attempted to settle with Brockman days before the trial began and had at one point felt like “a fool” for continuing to fund OpenAI.

title: Hexaware Q1 Revenue Rises 12.6% on AI-Led Deal Wins; Margin Slips 133 bps
content:
The Mumbai-based company posted revenue of ₹3,613 crore for the quarter ended March 31, while net profit rose 7.5% year-on-year to ₹351.6 crore.

What Actually Matters.

Hexaware's Q1 revenue increased by 12.6% year-on-year, driven by AI-focused deals.

Net profit for the quarter rose by 7.5%, reaching ₹351.6 crore.

Hexaware Technologies reported a 12.6% year-on-year (YoY) increase in revenue for the first quarter of CY26, as the IT services company sharpened its focus on artificial intelligence-led transformation deals amid growing enterprise spending on AI adoption.

The Mumbai-based company posted revenue of ₹3,613 crore for the quarter ended March 31, while net profit rose 7.5% YoY to ₹351.6 crore.

In dollar terms, revenue remained largely flat, declining 0.1%, sequentially, to $388.5 million.

Hexaware’s EBIT margin stood at 13% for the quarter, down 133 basis points YoY.

“The most defensible moat in the AI world is trust in relationships with customers. Our customers trust us to be their AI transformation partner to bring the power of AI to all facets of their IT and business,” CEO R Srikrishna said in the earnings statement, adding that the company sees a “significant growth opportunity” through 2026.

Hexaware, which has been positioning itself as an AI-first IT services firm, said several of its large deal wins during the quarter were centred around AI, automation and cloud transformation. These included an AI-led fab optimisation mandate from a US-based data storage company and an agentic application maintenance and support deal from a digital workspace platform.

The company also secured consolidation and cloud migration deals across banking, manufacturing and professional services sectors, highlighting continued enterprise demand for cost optimisation and technology modernisation.

Hexaware noted that revenue growth during the quarter was led by healthcare and insurance, which grew 13.5% YoY, while banking revenue rose 21.1%.

However, the technology, products and platforms vertical declined 23.5% YoY, showing continued weakness in discretionary spending among tech clients.

Europe emerged as the fastest-growing geography for the company with 11.6% YoY growth, while revenue from the Americas grew 2.5%.

Hexaware’s EBIT margin stood at 13% for the quarter, down 133 basis points YoY. The company generated strong cash flows, with operating cash flow to trailing 12-month profit at 125.1%.

CFO Vikash Jain said the company’s strong cash generation and balance sheet enabled it to declare its first interim dividend of ₹8.5 per share.

The company ended the quarter with a headcount of 33,798 employees, while voluntary attrition in its IT services business stood at 11.1%. Hexaware added two more clients in the $10 million-plus revenue category during the quarter, taking the total count to 34.

title: AI 3D Modelling Platforms Open New Digital Opportunities for Artisans in Assam
content:
Tripo Studio is an AI-based 3D creation tool that allows users to generate and edit 3D models using text prompts, images and automated AI workflows.

What Actually Matters.

AI 3D modelling platforms are enabling Assam's artisans to explore digital content and online commerce.

Tripo Studio simplifies 3D design by allowing users to create models using text prompts and images.

As Assam’s creative economy expands beyond traditional art forms into digital content and online commerce, creators and small businesses are beginning to explore artificial intelligence-powered 3D design tools to showcase local culture in new formats.

One such platform gaining attention is Tripo Studio, an AI-based 3D creation tool that allows users to generate and edit 3D models using text prompts, images and automated AI workflows. The platform is being positioned as a way to simplify 3D design for artisans, students and entrepreneurs who may not have access to expensive software or specialised training.

Traditionally, creating professional 3D models required advanced technical expertise, costly software subscriptions, and powerful computing systems. For many creators in smaller cities and towns, these barriers limited access to digital design and animation tools.

Tripo Studio aims to reduce this gap through AI-driven features such as text-to-3D model generation, image-based model creation, AI texturing, rigging and model segmentation.

The platform allows users to convert simple prompts into 3D objects within seconds. For instance, artisans can create digital representations of Assamese silk gamosa, jewellery or cultural artefacts by entering text descriptions instead of manually designing models from scratch.

The tool also includes image-to-3D capabilities, enabling creators to upload photographs of products, textiles or landscapes and convert them into editable 3D assets. According to the company, this can help local businesses create product showcases for e-commerce, marketing campaigns, and digital storytelling.

For creators working on cultural preservation and regional branding, AI texturing and segmentation features are being highlighted as particularly useful. These tools help preserve visual details such as silk textures, pottery finishes or traditional patterns while simplifying the editing process.

Another feature, AI rigging, allows users to automatically animate 3D objects. This makes it easier for students, digital artists and small businesses to create animated content for social media, educational projects or advertisements without advanced animation knowledge.

The growing interest in such tools reflects a broader trend in which AI is increasingly being integrated into India’s creative and digital economy. Across sectors, including design, gaming, education, and marketing, AI-generated visual content is becoming increasingly accessible to smaller creators and regional businesses.

In Assam, the technology could also support local artisans seeking to expand their reach online. Weavers in Sualkuchi, for example, can potentially use 3D visualisations to help customers better understand textile designs before purchasing products digitally.

The platform positions itself as an accessible alternative to traditional 3D software by offering faster workflows and lower entry barriers. Most of its tools are designed to automate processes that previously required manual editing and technical expertise.

At a time when digital commerce and regional content creation are rapidly growing, AI-powered 3D platforms like Tripo Studio are opening new possibilities for creators in smaller markets to experiment with digital storytelling while preserving local cultural identity.

IBM and Yotta also plan to bring IBM Sovereign Core to India by deploying it on Yotta’s Shakti Cloud.

What Actually Matters.

IBM and Yotta will create an agentic AI platform for Indian enterprises.

This platform will combine IBM's AI software with Yotta's sovereign cloud infrastructure.

IBM and Yotta Data Services plan to build an agentic AI platform for enterprises and government organisations in India, combining IBM’s AI software stack with Yotta’s sovereign cloud infrastructure.

The proposed platform will use IBM’s watsonx Orchestrate and run on Yotta’s Shakti Cloud, targeting organisations looking to deploy AI systems while meeting requirements around data residency, security, and regulatory compliance.

The companies said the platform is intended to help enterprises deploy and manage AI agents across functions such as IT service management, finance, procurement, human resources, and customer support.

They will jointly pursue proof-of-concept deployments, solution co-creation, and technical enablement initiatives across sectors, including banking and financial services, manufacturing, public sector, and digital-native businesses.

The announcement comes as enterprises move from pilot AI projects to operational deployments and seek infrastructure that allows governance and compliance controls alongside AI automation.

As part of the collaboration, IBM and Yotta also plan to bring IBM Sovereign Core to India by deploying it on Yotta’s Shakti Cloud.

IBM Sovereign Core is a software platform that helps organisations build and operate sovereign AI environments with compliance monitoring, governed AI execution, and operational controls.

“AI innovation in India must be anchored in sovereignty, security, and performance. Together with IBM, we propose to enable enterprises to harness the power of agentic AI on a secure, India-hosted cloud, so they can innovate with confidence while maintaining control over their data and operations,” Sunil Gupta, Co-founder and CEO of Yotta Data Services, said in a statement.

The platform combines compliance monitoring, identity management, encryption, governed AI execution, and audit-ready controls within a single deployment framework. It is built on Red Hat OpenShift and Red Hat AI.

By hosting the platform on Yotta’s India-based infrastructure, the partnership aims to support enterprises and government organisations in meeting data residency mandates and operating AI workloads within sovereign boundaries.

“This collaboration will combine IBM’s AI capabilities with Yotta’s sovereign cloud infrastructure to help organisations scale AI responsibly—embedding sovereignty, governance, transparency, and trust from the outset,” said Sandip Patel, Managing Director, IBM India and South Asia.

Yotta said its Shakti Cloud provides GPU infrastructure and AI services for enterprises, including AI labs, inference services, and Kubernetes clusters with GPU resources. The company operates data centre parks in Navi Mumbai and Greater Noida and is part of NVIDIA’s cloud partner ecosystem.

title: Chiratae Ventures Launches Sonic DeepTech Cohort, Commits up to $10 Mn
content:
This initiative provides startups in deeptech sectors with access to NVIDIA Inception resources.

What Actually Matters.

Chiratae Ventures has launched the Sonic DeepTech 2026 cohort, investing up to $10 million in innovative startups.

Startups gain access to NVIDIA Inception resources, enhancing their technical innovation and business growth.

Chiratae Ventures has launched its Sonic DeepTech 2026 cohort in Bengaluru, investing up to $10 million in Ctrl B, Interact AI, SuprSend, TakeMe2Space, SuprSend, and a stealth startup.

The startups in this batch will have access to NVIDIA Inception resources to help them enhance technical innovation and business growth at every stage. Benefits include advanced AI developer tools, training, discounted pricing on NVIDIA products, exclusive partner deals, and connections to a global network of investors and industry players.

TakeMe2Space is developing nanosatellite infrastructure for edge AI computing and Earth observation, facilitating interconnected data systems. CtrlB has created a serverless data lake platform that reduces costs for observability data storage and analytics with a cloud-native, diskless architecture.

Interact AI offers an advanced AI avatar that enhances traditional chatbots, providing audio-visual, product-aware conversational agents for sales and marketing. SuprSend has built a multi-channel notification infrastructure that simplifies communications through a single API. The final investment is in a stealth vertical AI platform.

"India is in a unique position right now, with a wealth of talent, research momentum, and founders creating potentially category-defining DeepTech companies. Through Sonic, India's premier DeepTech investment initiative in partnership with NVIDIA, Chiratae is stimulating this ecosystem for global scaling," Sudhir Sethi, Founder of Chiratae Ventures, said in a statement.

The Sonic DeepTech programme is aimed at supporting founders facing complex challenges in traditionally neglected sectors, offering up to $2 million in seed funding with decision timelines as short as 48 hours.

The programme focuses on areas where Chiratae Ventures believes India can emerge as a global leader, including energy and climate, quantum technologies, robotics and advanced manufacturing, space technologies, applied AI/ML, biotech and medtech, and the digital economy. Besides financial backing, it also links founders with industry partners and ecosystem networks to expedite their scaling journey.

In addition to the investments made, the programme recognised 14 Sonic DeepTech Disrupters—startups showing promise across the programme’s deeptech focus areas.

Chiratae's Sonic DeepTech programme will reopen applications later this year to support more startups.

title: Google Brings Reddit & Forum Advice Into AI Search Results
content:
The update marks a significant shift in how Google’s AI Overviews surface real-world perspectives alongside traditional web results.

What Actually Matters.

Google's AI search now incorporates advice from Reddit and other online forums, reflecting users' preference for community knowledge.

The update enhances AI Overviews by including community perspectives directly in search results, offering more context to users.

Google has updated its AI-powered search experience to pull in advice and perspectives from Reddit, social media, and other online discussion forums. The move reflects how users increasingly turn to community knowledge when searching online.

The company announced five new updates to its AI Mode and AI Overviews features on May 6, with the most notable change being the inclusion of firsthand community voices directly within search results. AI responses will now include a preview of perspectives from public online discussions, social media, and other firsthand sources. Google is also adding more context to these links, like a creator’s name, handle, or community name, to help users decide which discussions they might want to read or participate in.

For example, if a user wants to research how to take great pictures of the northern lights, they might see quotes from a photography forum offering advice on exposure time, along with clickable links—featuring the specific community name—so they can jump to the full conversation.

“For many searches, people are increasingly seeking out advice from others,” Google explained in its official blog post. The trend is well established—it is common for users to append Reddit to a Google search query when they want a human, experience-based answer rather than a curated article or a brand website.

The update is part of a broader redesign of how Google surfaces links in its generative AI features. Other changes include suggestions for further reading at the end of AI responses, linking to in-depth articles on different facets of a topic, highlights for links from a user’s news subscriptions, more inline links placed next to relevant text within AI responses, and desktop hover previews that show a website’s name or page title before a user clicks

To address concerns over source reliability, Google is also adding more contextual information to cited links. This is similar to how ChatGPT or Claude sometimes provides links intended to back up their claims, TechCrunch reported. The idea is to help users make a more informed decision about whether to click through and investigate further.

The subscription highlights feature adds another layer of trust. In early testing, Google found that people were significantly more likely to click links that were labelled as coming from their own subscriptions. Publishers who want to enable this can link their subscriptions with Google through a developer form.

Google said it continues to enhance how it shows and ranks links in its generative AI search experiences, using techniques like query fan-out, which helps it dive deeper into the web to find the most relevant sites for a given search.

title: Broadcom Launches VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 to Power Enterprise AI
content:
VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 combines virtual machines, containers and AI workloads, reducing complexity while improving efficiency for enterprise deployments.

What Actually Matters.

Broadcom has introduced VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 to facilitate enterprise deployment of AI workloads with improved security and reduced costs.

The platform supports mixed compute environments and is compatible with hardware from AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA.

Broadcom has launched VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1, a new infrastructure platform designed to help enterprises deploy production-scale AI workloads with improved security and lower costs.

The platform is designed as a private cloud solution that supports AI applications, Kubernetes, and mixed compute environments across hardware from AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA.

The launch comes amid growing concerns around the cost and security of AI infrastructure. According to Broadcom’s Private Cloud Outlook 2026, 56% of organisations are already running or planning to run AI inference workloads on private cloud, while reliance on public cloud has declined year-on-year.

“As more enterprises turn to AI for driving competitive advantage, they face three critical challenges: data and IP privacy concerns, surging infrastructure costs and their readiness for the world of agentic AI. VCF 9.1 is a single unified platform that addresses all three,” Krish Prasad, Senior Vice President and General Manager of the VMware Cloud Foundation division at Broadcom, said in a statement.

VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 combines virtual machines, containers and AI workloads into a single system, allowing enterprises to avoid managing multiple infrastructure stacks. Broadcom noted that features like memory optimisation, storage compression, and automated operations can help reduce costs while improving efficiency.

The platform also integrates zero-trust security, compliance monitoring, and ransomware recovery tools to protect sensitive AI models and data. These features are becoming increasingly important as organisations scale AI while managing regulatory and cybersecurity risks.

Industry partners also highlighted the growing need for controlled AI environments. “Enterprises need infrastructure that delivers breakthrough AI performance while maintaining data sovereignty and control,” said John Fanelli, Vice President of Enterprise Software at NVIDIA.

With support for an open hardware ecosystem and improved scalability, Broadcom is positioning VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 as a flexible alternative to public cloud infrastructure.

title: Ex-OpenAI CTO’s Startup Has the Highest Talent Density
content:
Thinking Machines Lab and OpenAI sit at opposite ends of the scale spectrum—one a 140-person elite research lab, the other a 4,500-person AI giant. Yet, both lead Paraform’s talent density rankings

What Actually Matters.

Thinking Machines Lab, founded by Mira Murati, leads the Paraform Talent Density Index.

This ranking assesses technology firms based on market demand for their employees.

Thinking Machines Lab, founded last year by former OpenAI Chief Technology Officer Mira Murati, has secured the top position in the inaugural Paraform Talent Density Index.

The ranking, which evaluates technology companies based on market demand for their workforce rather than raw headcount, awarded the startup a score of 0.817.

Thinking Machines Lab employs approximately 140 people and has $2 billion in funding. The firm recruited more than 30 senior staff from competitors OpenAI, Meta AI, and Mistral.

The startup maintained its hiring momentum despite several co-founder departures between late 2025 and early 2026.

The report noted that for the young laboratory, “this is what it looks like when a company's entire identity is built around who's inside the building.”

The recruitment data platform Paraform developed the index using an algorithmic assessment of candidate profiles, hiring trajectories, and interview conversion patterns. “Each company is assessed across a structured set of dimensions, including the technical depth of its team, hiring trajectory, calibre of prior employers represented on staff, domain expertise concentration, and performance signals observed across the Paraform network,” says the firm.

OpenAI ranked second with a score of 0.805 across its 4,500-person workforce. The ChatGPT developer serves as the primary training ground for the sector, supplying senior staff to nearly all top 15 firms on the list.

Paraform observes how rare this retention is at scale, stating, “Most companies lose technical sharpness as they grow. [Organisation] layers pile up, product demands take over, and the density thins out.”

Anthropic took third place with a score of 0.802 and $64 billion in funding. The index highlighted Anthropic's ability to maintain a high company-quality score past the 1,000-employee threshold.

Addressing the firm’s strict research focus, the authors state, “The company was uniquely built on a thesis—AI safety—that was supposed to shrink the pool. Instead, it became the magnet.”

Rounding out the top five are AI-native code editor Cursor and autonomous vehicle software provider Applied Intuition. Cursor implements rigorous hiring protocols for its 400-person team, including two-day on-site projects and a ban on AI tools during initial interviews.

Paraform’s index evaluates 50 companies, including Decagon, Cohere, LangChain, Ramp, Cognition, and others.

title: Taylor Swift’s Legal Play Signals New Fight to Protect Celebrity Identity in AI Era
content:
With Multi-Token Prediction technology, Google has now enabled developers to bypass traditional memory bottlenecks with Gemma 4.

What Actually Matters.

Google has enhanced its Gemma 4 AI models to accelerate text generation by up to 300%.

New Multi-Token Prediction technology addresses memory bottlenecks previously slowing processing.

Google has released new software architecture for its Gemma 4 AI models, designed to speed up text generation by up to 300%.

The company launched drafters for Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) to address memory-bandwidth bottlenecks that typically slow processing.

The Gemma 4 open-weights model family, released last month, has recorded 60 million downloads in its first few weeks, and provides open-source AI tools for developers building applications.

Standard LLMs generate text one token at a time, which forces processors to repeatedly move billions of parameters from memory to compute units. Google's update uses speculative decoding to decouple token generation from verification. The architecture pairs a heavy target model, such as the 31-billion-parameter Gemma 4, with a lightweight drafter.

This smaller drafter predicts multiple future tokens simultaneously using idle computational power. The larger target model then checks these suggestions in a single parallel pass.

Google’s Product Management Director Olivier Lacombe and Developer Relations Engineer Maarten Grootendorst noted in a blog post that standard autoregressive generation allocates identical processing power to obvious text continuations “as it does to solving a complex logic puzzle.”

The speed improvements apply across different hardware environments. Processing multiple requests simultaneously yields a 2.2x speed increase on Apple Silicon chips for the 26-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model.

The update also optimises the Gemma 4 E2B and E4B edge models through clustering techniques, preserving battery life on mobile devices. Because the primary model handles final verification, developers maintain “identical frontier-class reasoning and accuracy, just delivered significantly faster.”

To achieve these results, Google engineered the draft models to share the target model's cache and utilise its existing calculations. This architectural change ensures the drafters avoid operations that would “have to waste time recalculating context the larger model has already figured out.”

The MTP drafters are available under the Apache 2.0 open-source licence. Engineers can download model weights from repositories such as Hugging Face and Kaggle. Open-source development platforms like SGLang have also announced day-zero support for the update.

The software integrates directly with frameworks such as MLX and Ollama, enabling developers to immediately deploy faster autonomous agents and real-time coding assistants across consumer hardware.

title: Claude Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Others Score 0% on New SWE Benchmark
content:
ProgramBench tests SWE agents' ability to develop complete software projects holistically from scratch.

What Actually Matters.

Leading AI models like Claude Opus 4.7 and Gemini 3.1 Pro achieved 0% on a new software engineering benchmark.

ProgramBench assesses AI agents' capability to develop entire software projects independently.

Claude Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT 5.4 and others score 0% on the new benchmark developed by Meta, Harvard and Stanford.

The evaluation framework, called ProgramBench, tests the ability of software engineering agents to develop complete software projects holistically from scratch.

In this evaluation, agents receive a compiled software executable and its user documentation without any access to the original source code or the internet.

They must then write source code and a build script to produce a program that matches the original software's input-output behaviour.

The evaluation deployed these language models within the mini-SWE-agent framework. This scaffold provides the models with terminal access to execute commands and write files.

According to the researchers, technology companies increasingly use these models to “turn ideas expressed in natural language into full-fledged code repositories”, requiring the models to make independent, high-level architectural decisions. To achieve this, a software engineering agent operates as a language model “equipped with an agent scaffold to interact with a terminal environment”.

Researchers constructed 200 task instances from open-source GitHub repositories. These range from compact command-line utilities to widely used applications such as the PHP interpreter, the SQLite database, and the multimedia framework FFmpeg.

To verify the generated code, the team uses automated behavioural tests generated via agent-driven fuzzing. The creators noted that “existing benchmarks measure focused, limited tasks such as fixing a single bug or developing a single, specified feature.”

In contrast, ProgramBench forces the model to choose the programming language, formulate algorithms, and define data structures without a predetermined skeleton.

Out of nine tested models, none successfully passed all tests for any single task. Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.7 achieved the highest partial success, passing 95% of tests on just 3% of the instances.

The models demonstrated distinct patterns during the development cycle. Despite the complexity of the tasks, agents voluntarily submitted their solutions before reaching the maximum turn limit in 98.1% of the 1,800 runs, with only 1.9% exhausting the six-hour time allowance.

Furthermore, models frequently chose to write their solutions in Python, which accounted for 36% of all runs, even when the original software was written in C++, Rust, or Go.

When researchers conducted a separate test allowing unrestricted web access, the AI models frequently bypassed the reverse-engineering process. Despite explicit system instructions forbidding the behaviour, models looked up existing source code up to 36% of the time.

Analysis also revealed that these models construct software differently from human engineers. The study found that “models favour monolithic, single-file implementations that diverge sharply from human-written code.”

While human developers separate functions into modular directory structures, the models typically place all logic into a few root-level files.

Furthermore, the agents wrote substantially less code overall. They generated between 10 and 29% as many functions as the reference implementations, compensating by making individual functions up to 1.62 times longer.

title: In a First, IIT Guwahati Launches Hybrid MTech Course in Robotics and AI
content:
The programme will allow entry without a GATE score and looks to offer flexible learning for both fresh graduates and working professionals.

What Actually Matters.

IIT Guwahati has launched a hybrid MTech programme in Robotics and AI to enhance accessibility for graduates and professionals.

The programme does not require a GATE score, relying instead on an institute-level test or interview for admissions.

The Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati has launched a new MTech programme in Robotics and Artificial Intelligence, aiming to make advanced AI education more accessible to both fresh graduates and working professionals.

Offered by the School of Interdisciplinary Studies and Sustainability, the programme will follow a hybrid format combining online classes with on-campus lab sessions and final examinations. Notably, applicants do not need a GATE score, with admissions based on an institute-level written test or interview.

“The programme addresses the growing demand for expertise in intelligent systems, offering cutting-edge, interdisciplinary learning in machine learning, computer vision and robotics through a flexible format,” said Prof Hemant B. Kaushik, Dean of Outreach Education and Skilling at IIT Guwahati, in a statement.

Designed with flexibility in mind, the course offers multiple entry and exit options. Students can earn a postgraduate certificate or diploma, a Master of Science (Engineering), or complete the full MTech, depending on how long they remain enrolled. The minimum duration is two years, extendable to five years, allowing learners to balance studies with professional commitments.

All lectures will be conducted online and recorded for self-paced learning, while campus visits will enable hands-on training and interaction with faculty and industry experts.

The curriculum integrates robotics, AI, and automation with a strong focus on real-world applications. Students will also work on industry-relevant problems, gaining practical experience in areas such as robot kinematics, machine learning, and computer vision.

Graduates from the programme are expected to take up roles including robotics engineer, AI/ML engineer, automation specialist, and data scientist across industries and research institutions.

Applications for the inaugural batch are currently open, with a deadline of July 15, 2026 and classes scheduled to begin on August 10.

title: Freshworks to Cut 500 Jobs Amid AI-Led Restructuring Despite Strong Earnings
content:
Freshworks reported a 14% year-over-year constant-currency growth in quarterly revenue to $228.6 million in Q1 2026.

What Actually Matters.

Freshworks is reducing its global workforce by approximately 11% due to an AI-led restructuring.

The company aims to streamline operations and accelerate growth by focusing on AI and efficiency.

Freshworks will lay off around 500 employees—approximately 11% of its global workforce—as part of a restructuring effort to align operations with its growing focus on AI and efficiency.

The Nasdaq-listed company mentioned in its Q1 earnings call that the move is part of a broader shift to streamline operations and accelerate growth in key areas.

“We are realigning our organisation to accelerate our biggest growth drivers and move faster in the AI era. As a result, we are reducing our global workforce by ~11% (~494 employees). This shift allows us to lean into our momentum in EX and CX and build a more agile and competitive Freshworks for the future,” CEO Dennis Woodside stated in the call.

The layoffs come as SaaS companies globally face mounting pressure on profitability while investing heavily in AI-driven capabilities. Freshworks indicated that increased adoption of automation and AI tools has reduced the need for manual processes and multiple layers of coordination.

“We’ve invested heavily in technology, systems, and AI to work more efficiently. Our systems can now handle many of the manual tasks and fragmented handoffs that once required multiple teams to manage,” Woodside said, adding that Freshworks is removing management layers, centralising functions, and restructuring teams to better utilise these capabilities.

The company expects to incur a one-time restructuring charge of approximately $8 million, most of which will be reflected in its second-quarter 2026 results, according to CFO Tyler Sloat.

As part of the reorganisation, Freshworks has consolidated its Sales, Customer Success, and Support functions under a single leadership structure. It has also launched a dedicated India-based team focused on customer experience to improve retention and streamline go-to-market operations. Meanwhile, its field teams will now focus on employee experience, targeting mid-market and enterprise growth opportunities.

The restructuring has led to overlaps across sales, marketing, and support roles, contributing to the workforce reduction.

Meanwhile, in a recent interview with AIM, Woodside shared, “When I joined, the company was around $400 million in revenue, and I believed it could grow to a $1 billion and beyond. In fact, we’re set to cross $1 billion in ARR this year—a milestone only about 50 software companies globally have achieved.”

The company said impacted employees will receive severance packages based on tenure, along with bonuses, extended healthcare coverage, employee assistance programmes, and career transition support.

Freshworks reported a 14% year-over-year constant-currency growth in quarterly revenue to $228.6 million in Q1 2026. It narrowed the loss from operations at $8.1 million, compared with $10.4 million a year ago. The firm expects to grow at 13–15% in the second quarter.

title: Cabinet Clears 2 New Semiconductor Units Worth ₹3,900 Crore to Boost India’s Chip Ecosystem
content:
With these approvals, the total number of semiconductor projects cleared under the India Semiconductor Mission has risen to 12.

What Actually Matters.

The Union Cabinet has approved two new semiconductor manufacturing projects in Gujarat.

The projects represent a combined investment of approximately ₹3,936 crore.

The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has approved two new semiconductor manufacturing projects under the India Semiconductor Mission, further accelerating the country’s push to strengthen its domestic chip ecosystem.

The projects, with a combined investment of approximately ₹3,936 crore, will be set up in Gujarat and are expected to generate over 2,200 skilled jobs.

One of the approved proposals comes from Crystal Matrix Limited, which will establish an integrated compound semiconductor fabrication and assembly facility in Dholera. The unit will focus on manufacturing Mini and Micro-LED display modules using Gallium Nitride (GaN) technology, marking India’s first commercial-scale facility in this segment. The plant will also offer GaN foundry services and produce wafers used in applications ranging from televisions and smartphones to extended reality (XR) devices and smart wearables.

The second project, led by Suchi Semicon, involves setting up an Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) facility in Surat. The unit is expected to manufacture over one billion chips annually, serving sectors such as automotive, industrial automation, and consumer electronics.

With these approvals, the total number of semiconductor projects cleared under the India Semiconductor Mission has risen to 12, with cumulative investments reaching approximately ₹1.64 lakh crore. The government said the new facilities will complement India’s growing chip design ecosystem, supported by infrastructure initiatives across more than 300 academic institutions and over 100 startups.

The latest approvals come as momentum builds across the sector, with several previously sanctioned projects already in advanced stages of execution. Two facilities have commenced commercial shipments, while additional units are expected to become operational in the near term, signalling steady progress in India’s ambition to become a global semiconductor manufacturing hub.

Launched in 2022, the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM 1.0) has significantly accelerated the country’s semiconductor ambitions, with 10 projects approved so far, attracting a total investment of around ₹1.65 lakh crore.

Two units—Micron Technology and Kaynes Technology—have already commenced commercial production, while two more are expected to go live in 2026. Construction across multiple facilities is progressing rapidly, reflecting strong execution momentum. At the same time, India’s design ecosystem is expanding, with over 67,000 engineers and chip designers across 421 academic institutions and startups actively leveraging advanced Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools.

title: OpenAI Makes GPT-5.5 Instant as the New Default Model in ChatGPT
content:
GPT-5.5 Instant can draw on past chats, uploaded files, and connected services such as Gmail to tailor responses.

What Actually Matters.

OpenAI has made GPT-5.5 Instant the new default model for ChatGPT, replacing GPT-5.3 Instant.

The new model offers improved accuracy, fewer errors, and more concise responses.

OpenAI has updated ChatGPT’s default model to GPT-5.5 Instant in a bid to improve accuracy, reduce errors, and deliver more concise responses.

GPT-5.5 Instant is rolling out starting today to all ChatGPT users, replacing GPT-5.3 Instant as the default model and becoming available in the API as chat-latest. For paid users, GPT-5.3 Instant will remain accessible through model configuration settings for three months before it is retired.

OpenAI is also expanding personalisation features for Plus and Pro users on the web. GPT-5.5 Instant can draw on past chats, uploaded files, and connected services such as Gmail to tailor responses. The system determines when personalisation is useful and surfaces relevant context automatically.

The company said these capabilities will soon be extended to mobile devices, with further expansion planned across the Free, Go, Business, and Enterprise tiers in the coming weeks.

The company said GPT-5.5 Instant produces “52.5% fewer hallucinated claims” on high-stakes prompts in areas such as medicine, law, and finance, compared with its predecessor. It also reduced inaccurate claims by 37.3% in conversations that had previously been flagged for factual errors.

“Small improvements make a big difference,” the company said, noting that the model is used daily by hundreds of millions of people. The update focuses on “stronger and tighter answers,” a more natural tone, and improved use of prior context when personalisation is relevant.

The model also shows gains in benchmark evaluations across reasoning and technical domains. On the AIME 2025 math benchmark, accuracy increased to 81.2% from 65.4%. Performance on GPQA, which tests PhD-level science knowledge, rose to 85.6% from 78.5%. Improvements were also reported in multimodal reasoning and document parsing benchmarks.

OpenAI said GPT-5.5 Instant is better at deciding when to use web search and has improved capabilities in analysing images and handling STEM-related queries.

The company also highlighted changes in response style. GPT-5.5 Instant uses fewer words and lines on average while maintaining completeness. “Responses are tighter and more to-the-point without losing substance,” it said.

To address transparency, the company introduced memory sources, which show users what prior context influenced a response. Users can review, delete, or modify stored information, and shared conversations will not expose these sources.

“Users remain in control of what’s in memory,” the company said, adding that temporary chats can be used to avoid storing or referencing past interactions.

OpenAI recently launched GPT-5.5, positioning it as an agentic AI system that can independently execute complex, multi-step tasks across software, data, and research workflows with minimal human supervision.

title: Anthropic Secures Access to 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs Through SpaceX Deal
content:
Anthropic said it is doubling Claude Code’s five-hour usage limits for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans.

What Actually Matters.

Anthropic has secured access to over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs through a new partnership with SpaceX.

This deal will provide Anthropic with more than 300 megawatts of computing capacity at SpaceX's Colossus 1 data centre.

Anthropic has increased usage limits for its Claude products and signed a new compute partnership with SpaceX, gaining access to more than 300 megawatts of capacity at the company’s Colossus 1 data centre, according to an announcement made on May 6.

The AI startup said the deal would provide access to over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs within a month and would directly improve capacity for Claude Pro and Claude Max subscribers.

“We’ve signed an agreement with SpaceX to use all of the compute capacity at their Colossus 1 data centre,” Anthropic said in the announcement. “This gives us access to more than 300 megawatts of new capacity.”

Alongside the compute expansion, Anthropic said it is doubling Claude Code’s five-hour usage limits for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans. The company is also removing peak-hour rate reductions for Pro and Max users and increasing API rate limits for Claude Opus models.

The company said the changes are effective immediately and are aimed at improving the experience for heavy Claude users.

The SpaceX partnership adds to a series of infrastructure agreements Anthropic has announced in recent months. These include an agreement with Amazon for up to 5 gigawatts of compute capacity, including nearly 1 gigawatt expected by the end of 2026, and a separate 5-gigawatt agreement with Google and Broadcom that is scheduled to begin coming online in 2027.

Anthropic has reportedly signed a five-year, $200 billion agreement with Google Cloud.

Anthropic also referenced its strategic partnership with Microsoft and NVIDIA, which includes $30 billion worth of Azure capacity, as well as a $50 billion AI infrastructure investment with Fluidstack.

“We train and run Claude on a range of AI hardware—AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, and NVIDIA GPUs—and continue to explore opportunities to bring additional capacity online,” the company said.

Anthropic added that it has expressed interest in working with SpaceX on “multiple gigawatts of orbital AI compute capacity.”

The company also said part of its infrastructure expansion will focus on international markets to support enterprise customers in regulated sectors such as finance, healthcare, and government that require local data residency and compliance support.

“Some of our capacity expansion will be international,” Anthropic said, citing its collaboration with Amazon for additional inference infrastructure in Asia and Europe.

The company said it plans to add capacity in countries “whose legal and regulatory frameworks support investments of this scale” and where supply chains for hardware, networking, and facilities remain secure.

Anthropic also reiterated a recent commitment to cover consumer electricity price increases caused by its US data centres and said it is exploring ways to extend that policy internationally while investing in local communities hosting its facilities.
