title: Sarvam, YCP India to Drive Enterprise AI Adoption With Focus on Business Impact
content:
The partnership blends a sovereign AI platform with execution expertise to scale high-impact enterprise deployments.

What Actually Matters.

Sarvam and YCP India are forming a partnership to enhance AI adoption in enterprises, focusing on measurable business value.

The collaboration aims to transition from fragmented AI initiatives to structured, enterprise-wide deployments.

Sarvam and YCP India have announced a strategic partnership to accelerate AI adoption across leading enterprises, with a clear focus on delivering measurable business value rather than isolated experimentation.

The collaboration is designed to help organisations move from fragmented AI initiatives to structured, enterprise-wide deployments. By combining complementary strengths, the partnership aims to enable companies to embed AI into core business functions and operating models.

YCP India brings to the alliance its extensive experience in digital transformation, backed by strong execution capabilities, strategy advisory, and deep cross-sector domain expertise. The firm also contributes long-standing client relationships across global markets, positioning it to drive large-scale AI programs.

Sarvam, meanwhile, contributes its full-stack sovereign AI platform built in India. The platform spans language, voice, and multimodal capabilities, and is tailored to the needs of Indian enterprises, including regulatory compliance and cost-efficient deployment at scale.

The partnership will focus on three key areas. First, the companies will work with clients to identify and prioritise high-impact AI use cases, ensuring alignment with enterprise strategy, operating models, and existing technology landscapes.

Next, they will co-deliver solutions that integrate Sarvam’s technology stack with YCP’s domain and functional expertise.

Lastly, both firms will emphasise disciplined execution through joint delivery teams, with YCP working closely alongside Sarvam engineers to support implementation, change management, and rapid value realisation.

The companies noted that as foundational AI models continue to mature, competitive advantage will increasingly depend not on access to technology, but on the ability to apply it effectively within complex enterprise environments.

In a statement, Sarvam said it is partnering with YCP India to accelerate enterprise AI adoption in the country, adding that the collaboration combines its sovereign AI platform with YCP’s execution strength to help organisations identify high-impact opportunities and capture sustained value from AI.

The two firms said they expect the partnership to play a key role in helping enterprises translate AI potential into tangible and scalable business outcomes.

title: Cerebras Confirms IPO Launch Again, Targets $35 Bn Valuation
content:
The AI chipmakera plans to raise nearly $3 billion through a Nasdaq listing, as demand for inference infrastructure continues to rise.

What Actually Matters.

Cerebras Systems plans to raise nearly $3 billion through its IPO on Nasdaq, offering 28 million shares at $115 to $125 each.

The IPO follows regulatory clearance after a prior delay linked to national security scrutiny regarding an investor, G42.

AI inference chip company, Cerebras Systems, has launched its initial public offering (IPO) and plans to raise nearly $3 billion through a Nasdaq listing. The AI chipmaker said it plans to offer 28 million shares of Class A common stock at a price range of $115 to $125 per share under the ticker symbol ‘CBRS’.

The Sunnyvale-based company said that the proposed offering will be led by Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, Barclays and UBS Investment Bank as book-running managers for the IPO. Cerebras also plans to grant underwriters a 30-day option to purchase an additional 4.2 million shares.

Cerebras had first filed for an IPO in 2024 but delayed the listing after a national security review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS). The scrutiny centred on Abu Dhabi-based G42, which was both an investor and customer of Cerebras. The company later withdrew this filing in October 2025 and has now revived it after receiving regulatory clearance.

The IPO comes amid growing investor interest in AI infrastructure companies and follows reports of a major OpenAI partnership focused on AI inference computing. Recently, OpenAI committed to spending more than $20 billion over the next three years on servers powered by Cerebras chips. In addition, the total deal outlay could rise to $30 billion and may grant OpenAI up to a 10% stake in Cerebras.

Cerebras builds wafer-scale AI processors designed for large-scale training and inference workloads. The company said its Wafer Scale Engine 3 (WSE-3) processor is “the world’s largest and fastest commercialised AI processor.”

According to the company, the WSE-3 chip is 58 times larger than leading GPU chips and delivers inference speeds up to 15 times faster than GPU-based systems on open-source models. Cerebras said its systems are used by corporations, research institutes and governments across four continents.

The listing also follows a period of rapid company growth. Earlier reports noted that Cerebras turned profitable in 2025 after posting losses the previous year, while its valuation rose sharply during the AI infrastructure boom.

In February, the company also closed a $1 billion Series H financing at a post-money valuation of about $23 billion, tripling its valuation from just three months earlier.

The IPO arrives as technology companies continue to increase spending on AI infrastructure and compute capacity. Industry analysts expect demand for inference computing to grow as AI models move into wider enterprise and consumer use.

The broader market has also seen companies move towards long-term infrastructure partnerships to secure access to chips and compute resources. Cerebras now joins a growing group of AI infrastructure firms seeking to capitalise on that demand through public markets.

IIT Guwahati has launched a hybrid MTech programme in Robotics and AI to enhance accessibility for graduates and professionals.

The Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati has launched a new MTech programme in Robotics and Artificial Intelligence, aiming to make advanced AI education more accessible to both fresh graduates and working professionals.

Offered by the School of Interdisciplinary Studies and Sustainability, the programme will follow a hybrid format combining online classes with on-campus lab sessions and final examinations. Notably, applicants do not need a GATE score, with admissions based on an institute-level written test or interview.

“The programme addresses the growing demand for expertise in intelligent systems, offering cutting-edge, interdisciplinary learning in machine learning, computer vision and robotics through a flexible format,” said Prof Hemant B. Kaushik, Dean of Outreach Education and Skilling at IIT Guwahati, in a statement.

Designed with flexibility in mind, the course offers multiple entry and exit options. Students can earn a postgraduate certificate or diploma, a Master of Science (Engineering), or complete the full MTech, depending on how long they remain enrolled. The minimum duration is two years, extendable to five years, allowing learners to balance studies with professional commitments.

All lectures will be conducted online and recorded for self-paced learning, while campus visits will enable hands-on training and interaction with faculty and industry experts.

The curriculum integrates robotics, AI, and automation with a strong focus on real-world applications. Students will also work on industry-relevant problems, gaining practical experience in areas such as robot kinematics, machine learning, and computer vision.

Graduates from the programme are expected to take up roles including robotics engineer, AI/ML engineer, automation specialist, and data scientist across industries and research institutions.

Applications for the inaugural batch are currently open, with a deadline of July 15, 2026 and classes scheduled to begin on August 10.

title: Taylor Swift’s Legal Play Signals New Fight to Protect Celebrity Identity in AI Era
content:
Swift joins a growing list of celebrities taking legal steps to counter the misuse of AI-generated voices and likenesses.

What Actually Matters.

Taylor Swift is taking legal steps to protect her voice and image from AI misuse.

Her trademark applications include specific phrases and a stage image related to her upcoming album.

Singer-songwriter Taylor Swift has filed trademark applications in the United States to protect her voice and image amid growing concerns over the misuse of AI-generated content.

The filings submitted to the United States Patent and Trademark Office include two sound recordings featuring the phrases ‘Hey, it’s Taylor’ and ‘Hey, it’s Taylor Swift’, along with references to her 2025 album The Life of a Showgirl. A separate application covers a specific stage image from her performance, including visual elements such as lighting, costume, and props.

The move reflects a broader shift among celebrities seeking legal protection against the rapid rise of AI tools capable of generating realistic voice clones and deepfake images. Advances in generative AI now allow voices to be replicated from short audio clips, making it easier to create convincing imitations without consent.

Swift’s filings come amid increasing scrutiny over AI misuse. In 2024, explicit AI-generated images of the singer circulated widely online, sparking backlash and renewed calls for stronger regulation. Lawmakers in the US have since proposed measures such as the Preventing Deepfakes of Intimate Images Act, though comprehensive protections remain limited.

Other public figures have taken similar steps. Actor Matthew McConaughey has applied to trademark his voice and signature phrases, while celebrities like Tom Hanks have warned about unauthorised AI-generated likenesses being used in advertisements. Similarly, actress Scarlett Johansson previously pursued legal action over the use of an AI-generated avatar resembling her.

This trend signals a shift from protecting creative work to protecting identity itself. Trademark law, traditionally used for names and logos, is now being explored as a tool to safeguard voice and likeness in the absence of strong personality rights.

Yet, Swift’s move highlights how artists are adapting to an AI-driven landscape where control over identity is becoming as critical as control over content.

title: Samsung Becomes the First South Korean Firm to Cross $1 Tn Market Cap
content:
With this, Samsung joins the recent TSMC in the $1 trillion club as AI chip demand lifts Korean markets.

What Actually Matters.

Samsung Electronics has become the first South Korean company to reach a market capitalisation of $1 trillion.

The surge in Samsung's shares is attributed to rising demand for AI-related semiconductor products.

Samsung Electronics crossed the $1 trillion market capitalisation mark after a sharp rally in semiconductor stocks tied to rising AI demand. The South Korean chipmaker’s valuation crossed 1,717 trillion won (~$1.03 trillion) during trading in Seoul, making it only the second Asian company, after TSMC (in July last year), to reach the milestone.

Samsung shares have risen nearly 15% since and touched 267,250 won (~$181.90). The rally followed gains in US AI-linked chip stocks and strong investor interest in memory and high-bandwidth memory suppliers.

The surge also pushed South Korea’s KOSPI index above the 7,000 mark for the first time. Samsung and semiconductor firm SK Hynix together accounted for a large share of the index’s gains. SK Hynix’s market capitalisation currently stands at 1,142.82 trillion won (~$780 billion).

Samsung’s recent gains reflected wider investor confidence in AI-linked semiconductor firms. Samsung’s stock has more than doubled this year as demand for memory chips and AI accelerators continued to rise globally.

Among other semiconductor firms, Broadcom has a market capitalisation of $2.02 trillion, while AMD stands at nearly $579 billion. Micron Technology is valued at about $722 billion, and Xiaomi’s market capitalisation is 80,064.67 crore HKD (~$102 billion).

Reports have linked Samsung’s rise to strong AI infrastructure spending and demand for high-bandwidth memory chips, and Reuters reported that Samsung’s semiconductor business posted record quarterly profit last week, driven largely by demand for AI memory.

Samsung had also expanded its AI and semiconductor roadmap in recent months. Earlier reports said the company planned to mass-produce silicon photonic chips by 2028 as it looked to improve AI data transfer efficiency. The company had also emerged as a possible manufacturing partner for Apple’s US chip production efforts alongside Intel.

Samsung also strengthened its position in the AI memory market after securing an HBM4 supply deal for AMD’s AI GPUs. AMD CEO Lisa Su had visited South Korea during discussions around the partnership.

Samsung now joins a small group of global technology firms valued at over $1 trillion. NVIDIA remains the world’s most valuable chip company with a market capitalisation that hit $5 trillion late last year, making it the first company ever to achieve that feat.

Microsoft’s market capitalisation stands at $3.06 trillion, while Apple and Alphabet are valued at $4.17 trillion and $4.69 trillion, respectively. Amazon holds a valuation of $2.94 trillion, ahead of Meta Platforms at $1.54 trillion and Tesla at $1.22 trillion.

title: Jensen Huang Says NVIDIA’s China Chip Share Has Fallen to Zero
content:
Jensen Huang urges Washington to rethink export controls and keep US chip firms active in China.

What Actually Matters.

NVIDIA's market share in China has fallen to zero due to US export controls on advanced AI chips.

Jensen Huang believes conceding the Chinese market lacks strategic sense for American chip firms.

NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang said the company’s market share in China has fallen to zero, as US export controls blocked sales of advanced AI chips to the country. He said this during a recent podcast conversation with Ylli Bajraktari, President and CEO of the Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP).

In FY25, 13% of NVIDIA’s total revenue came from China and Hong Kong, despite the strict export controls.

He warned that the restrictions may have strengthened China’s push towards semiconductor self-sufficiency, adding that the US should continue promoting American technology leadership while allowing domestic chip firms to compete in key overseas markets, including China.

He urged policymakers to adopt a “dynamic” approach to export rules as the AI market evolves. The comments come as the US continues tightening restrictions on advanced semiconductor exports to China. The controls began in 2022 and later expanded to cover several NVIDIA chips designed specifically for the Chinese market.

According to reports, before the export curbs, the Chinese market accounted for nearly a quarter of the giant’s data centre revenue.

Huang argued that keeping American companies present in China would help preserve the influence of the US technology ecosystem globally. He said the US should aim to lead across “every layer” of AI, including energy, chips, infrastructure, models and applications.

He also warned that China has already built strengths in several parts of the AI stack. Huang pointed to the country’s energy production, engineering talent and growing pool of AI researchers. He said China’s AI ecosystem was advancing rapidly despite US controls.

Fears around AI job losses and adoption could potentially slow the US at a time when Asian countries are moving aggressively to deploy the technology. “The rest of Asia is embracing and adopting AI with great enthusiasm. This is how we get generally left behind,” he added.

His remarks come amid rising competition from Chinese firms such as Huawei and Cambricon Technologies, which have expanded their AI chip businesses as NVIDIA’s access to China narrowed.

A recent example of this trend is the launch of the DeepSeek V4 family of models. Huawei confirmed that its Ascend 950 AI chips will offer complete support for DeepSeek V4, while DeepSeek’s technical report indicated that inference costs are expected to decline substantially once Huawei’s Ascend 950 supernodes are deployed at scale in the second half of 2026.

Huawei is set to capture the largest share of China’s AI chip market this year, with sales jumping by at least 60%, as per reports. Some also state that various Chinese tech groups have placed large orders for Huawei’s latest Ascend processor 950PR.

title: ElevenLabs Crosses $500 Mn ARR, Adds BlackRock, NVIDIA Among New Investors
content:
The latest growth is driven by enterprises deploying voice-based AI agents across customer support, sales, hiring, and marketing functions.

What Actually Matters.

ElevenLabs reported significant growth, reaching over $500 million in annual recurring revenue.

New investors include major financial institutions and technology companies, alongside entertainment figures.

AI voice company ElevenLabs said it has crossed $500 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR) within the first four months of 2026, as it brought in new investors including BlackRock, Wellington Management, NVIDIA (via NVentures) and Santander.

The company also drew investment from entertainment and creative professionals, including Jamie Foxx, Eva Longoria, and Squid Game creator Hwang Dong-hyuk, along with existing investor Matthew McConaughey.

The investment marks the third close of ElevenLabs’ Series D round. New institutional investors also include D. E. Shaw and Schroders.

“We ended 2025 with $350 million in ARR, and in the first four months of 2026, we have already surpassed $500 million ARR,” the company said in a statement.

ElevenLabs said it will use the funding to expand research and product development across voice, video, and image generation, and to build agents that operate across voice, chat, and email channels. The company also plans to expand internationally with local teams.

“Every major enterprise will communicate with its customers and audiences through AI agents,” said Rob Mazzoni of Wellington Management. “The companies that power natural, human-like interactions at scale will become critical global infrastructure.”

Several enterprise users of ElevenLabs have also invested in the company. These include NVIDIA, Salesforce, Santander, KPN, and Deutsche Telekom.

The company said it will allow retail investors to invest in ElevenLabs through Robinhood Ventures.

Deutsche Telekom said it is using ElevenLabs’ platform for customer support agents, real-time translation during calls, and marketing content.

“Voice is the highest-stakes channel for any customer interaction, and the bar for quality, latency and security is extremely high,” said Karine Peters of T.Capital, the investment arm of Deutsche Telekom. “ElevenLabs is becoming a foundational enabler of Deutsche Telekom’s broader Industrial AI vision.”

The company has 530 employees across more than 50 countries and said it recently completed a $100 million tender offer alongside its Series D round.

title: Coforge Q4 Profit Doubles on Margins, AI Efficiencies; Flags Strong FY27 Outlook
content:
Former Indian cricketer Mithali Raj said AI is not just enhancing performance and storytelling, but also redefining the very nature of the sport.

What Actually Matters.

AI is making cricket more predictable by providing detailed, data-driven insights into player performance.

The extensive data available through AI has diminished the element of surprise within the sport.

Speaking at the Trailblazing Women Summit hosted by Salesforce, former India captain Mithali Raj said AI is steadily removing the element of surprise from cricket, as data-driven insights reshape how the game is played and analysed.

In a fireside chat with Salesforce President and CEO Arundhati Bhattacharya, Raj reflected on how AI has transformed traditional player analysis into a highly granular, data-rich process. “Teams today can break down performance across specific match situations, ranging from pitch conditions to bowler-batter matchups, making the game far more predictable than before,” she said.

“There’s so much data now, and it goes into great detail,” Raj said. “But it all comes down to what you choose to pick from it.”

Raj noted that this abundance of information has fundamentally changed the viewing and playing experience. “It has definitely removed the surprise element in the sport because everything is out there,” she shared, adding that even casual fans can now interpret cricket through a more analytical lens.

Raj also highlighted how AI is reshaping sports broadcasting. Predictive analytics, she explained, now informs on-air commentary, allowing broadcasters to back their instincts with probability-based insights.

“There are moments when you feel a wicket might fall, but now data tells you there’s a high probability in that situation,” she said. “That helps us build narratives when we’re live.”

Beyond cricket, Raj pointed to AI’s potential to democratise access to training, particularly for young athletes in rural India. With limited access to coaching and infrastructure, many aspiring cricketers can benefit from AI-powered tools, tutorials, and performance feedback.

“In many districts, children travel long distances just to access nets,” she said. “If AI can help them train and improve with limited resources, that’s a big opportunity.”

However, she cautioned that technology cannot replace the human side of sport. “AI doesn’t have the emotional connect,” Raj said. “In tough times, athletes need people who can support and motivate them.”

title: Coforge Q4 Profit Doubles on Margins, AI Efficiencies; Flags Strong FY27 Outlook
content:
Coforge said AI-led delivery helped sustain profitability, though reported earnings were partly boosted by a one-time tax adjustment.

What Actually Matters.

Coforge's net profit more than doubled sequentially due to margin expansion and deal wins.

Artificial intelligence in delivery significantly contributed to Coforge's sustained profitability.

IT solutions firm Coforge’s net profit for the fourth quarter of FY26 more than doubled sequentially, led by margin expansion, steady deal wins, and increasing use of artificial intelligence in delivery, even as the broader IT sector shows signs of slowing growth.

The company reported a consolidated profit of ₹612.3 crore ($64 million), compared to ₹250.2 crore ($26.2 million) in the previous quarter.

The strong bottomline was aided by an improvement in margins as well as a one-time deferred tax adjustment linked to the Cigniti merger, with the company indicating that normalised profit for the quarter was lower at around ₹447.3 crore ($47 million).

The company earned ₹4,450 crore ($466.4 million) for the quarter, up 5.2% sequentially, while EBIT margin (signifying operational profitability) rose to 16.6%, marking the company’s highest quarterly profitability.

Coforge said it is betting that AI-led delivery models, agent-based workflows, and outcome-linked pricing can drive both revenue expansion and margin gains at a time when the IT services industry is being reshaped by automation.

The company has also invested heavily in talent, with over 30,000 employees trained in AI and data capabilities, alongside a specialised pool of forward-deployed engineers embedded with clients to drive adoption and execution.

For the full fiscal year, the company posted revenue of ₹16,402.7 crore ($1.72 billion), up 39% year-on-year in rupee terms, while net profit rose 91.6% to ₹1,555.7 crore ($163 million).

Operating performance improved sharply during the year, with EBIT margin expanding 370 basis points to 14.4%, aided in part by efficiency gains linked to AI adoption and tighter execution.

“With an order executable of $1.75 billion, we enter FY27 with strong momentum and confidence. We expect to deliver robust revenue growth in FY27 and plan to deliver an EBITDA of more than 20.5% on a consolidated basis in FY27,” Sudhir Singh, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director of Coforge, said in a statement.

The company noted that AI-led efficiencies provide a path for further margin expansion in FY27. This comes at a time when IT services firms are grappling with questions around whether AI could compress traditional revenue streams.

Coforge noted that AI is opening up new areas such as data and integration, AI managed services and governance, while also reducing delivery costs.

Deal momentum remained firm in the quarter, with order intake at $648 million and a 12-month executable order book of $1.75 billion, up 16.4% year-on-year. The company also signed five large deals during the quarter, showcasing traction despite macro uncertainties.

Client concentration remains stable, with the top five customers contributing about a fifth of revenue, although these accounts are growing faster than the overall business, suggesting deeper mining of existing relationships, the company noted.

Headcount rose marginally to 35,777, with net additions of 436 employees in the quarter, while attrition stood at 10.8%, among the lowest in the sector.

Coforge’s performance is significant in a quarter influenced by seasonalities and other headwinds, where larger peers have reported weaker growth or cautious outlooks.

Shares of Coforge ended at Rs 1,168 on the BSE on Tuesday, up 1.42%.

title: Apple Explores Intel, Samsung for US Chip Production: Report
content:
Apple is evaluating alternative chipmakers as peers sign foundry deals amid supply constraints and AI demand.

What Actually Matters.

Apple is in early discussions with Intel and Samsung for US-based chip production.

The company is exploring alternatives to its main supplier, TSMC, amid rising chip demand.

Apple has held exploratory discussions with Intel and Samsung Electronics to produce its main device processors in the US, according to a Bloomberg report. The talks, still at an early stage, show Apple assessing options beyond TSMC, which is its primary supplier.

The move comes as chip demand rises and companies seek to localise production. Apple has reportedly discussed using Intel’s foundry services and has reviewed Samsung’s upcoming semiconductor plant in Texas.

Executives have allegedly visited the site, which is set to manufacture advanced chips, and the company is evaluating whether these partners can meet its performance, scale, and delivery needs.

The discussions do not confirm a supplier change, according to the report. Apple continues to depend on TSMC for processors used in iPhones and iPads. However, supply constraints linked to AI-driven demand have pushed companies to diversify sourcing, as recent earnings commentary also indicated.

Apple’s move reflects a broader industry trend. Several firms have already started working with alternative foundries. Tesla, for instance, has signed a multibillion-dollar deal with Samsung to manufacture AI chips for its vehicles and robotics systems.

Intel also recently announced that it will join the Terafab semiconductor venture, a fabrication project jointly owned by Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI. The companies plan to build a $25 billion chip manufacturing facility in Austin, Texas, with plans for a full-scale facility on the North Campus of Giga Texas.

Apple is also set to use Intel’s next-generation manufacturing process for future chip production, marking a key external customer win for Intel’s foundry business.

Intel and Samsung have been expanding their contract manufacturing businesses to compete with TSMC. Intel has repositioned its foundry unit to attract large clients, while Samsung continues to invest in advanced nodes and US-based fabs.

Samsung has reportedly indicated it expects to secure more advanced chip clients and is in talks with major technology firms for future orders. Its Texas facility, which Apple has evaluated, is also tied to existing customer commitments.

Despite this momentum, both Intel and Samsung still trail TSMC in advanced chip manufacturing. Apple remains cautious about shifting production, and the current talks may not lead to formal agreements.

title: Blue Machines AI Brings Multilingual Voice Automation to Aditya Birla Capital
content:
With voice agents now active across key businesses of Aditya Birla Capital, Blue Machines AI is pushing automation deeper into the customer lifecycle from acquisition to support.

What Actually Matters.

Blue Machines AI has implemented AI-powered voice agents across Aditya Birla Capital's key business segments in just six weeks.

The deployment enhances customer engagement in mutual funds, health insurance, and housing finance through automation.

Blue Machines AI has rolled out AI-powered voice agents across multiple businesses of Aditya Birla Capital, completing the deployment in just six weeks. The implementation spans the company’s mutual funds, health insurance and housing finance segments, marking one of the fastest large-scale voice AI rollouts in India’s financial services sector.

The solution integrates conversational AI directly into business workflows, enabling automation across customer outreach, onboarding and servicing functions.

In its mutual fund business, the voice agents are being used to improve investor engagement. They help users explore fund options, answer performance-related queries and guide them through investment processes such as SIPs and lump-sum investments.

Within the health insurance segment, the platform is focused on both advisor and customer engagement. Voice agents are being used to onboard policyholders, explain benefits, and provide updates to distribution partners.

The deployment also extends to housing finance, where the AI system supports field teams by handling documentation follow-ups, simplifying loan-related communication and guiding customers through application processes.

According to Nirmit Parikh, Founder and CEO of Blue Machines AI, the platform is designed to deliver reliable, large-scale interactions while meeting compliance requirements. The system integrates speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and large language models to enable natural conversations.

It also includes features such as multilingual support and a ‘hot-swap’ architecture, which allows switching between AI providers in case of disruptions, ensuring continuity in operations.

As financial institutions increasingly adopt automation, the use of voice AI is expected to expand across more stages of the customer lifecycle, including retention and advisory services.

title: Shekhar Kapur Joins Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence in Abu Dhabi to Connect Cinema & AI
content:
Kapur’s new role highlights how filmmakers and artists are increasingly shaping conversations around AI’s future and its creative potential.

What Actually Matters.

Shekhar Kapur has joined MBZUAI as an advisor for its AI x Arts Fellowship programme, bridging cinema and artificial intelligence.

Kapur views AI as a transformative and democratic technology, emphasising its potential impact beyond corporations.

Veteran filmmaker Shekhar Kapur has joined the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) in Abu Dhabi as an advisor to its AI x Arts Fellowship programme, marking a notable intersection between cinema and artificial intelligence.

Announcing the development on X, Kapur said he was “proud” to take on the role, calling it “both an honour and opportunity” to contribute and learn alongside global experts. He also described MBZUAI as “fast emerging as a global hub in research and development in AI”, underlining the UAE’s growing ambitions in the sector.

Known for films like Elizabeth and Bandit Queen, Kapur’s move reflects a broader shift where creative industries are increasingly engaging with AI-led innovation. The fellowship programme is expected to explore how storytelling, filmmaking and artistic expression evolve alongside advancements in machine intelligence.

Kapur has been vocal about AI’s transformative potential. In his recent post, he described it as “the most democratic technology humanity has ever touched,” suggesting that its real impact may emerge beyond corporations and institutions.

“Not from the top of the pyramid. From the bottom. From homes like this,” he wrote, highlighting how AI could expand access to education, design and research.

At the same time, he emphasised that human creativity will remain central. While AI may reshape workflows, Kapur noted that lived experience and intuition cannot be replaced by machines.

His appointment has drawn mixed but largely positive reactions online, with many welcoming the integration of arts into AI research.

The development also aligns with the UAE’s push to position itself as a global AI hub, with institutions like MBZUAI increasingly focusing on interdisciplinary collaboration between technology and the creative arts.

title: Anthropic & OpenAI Partner with Private Equity Firms to Scale Enterprise AI Deployment
content:
Krutrim said it has become financially self-sustaining and does not require immediate external funding, including from its founder.

What Actually Matters.

Krutrim has pivoted to a domestic AI cloud services model.

The company achieved ₹300 crore revenue in FY26 and its first annual net profit.

Krutrim, Ola Group’s AI firm, said it has pivoted to a domestic AI cloud services model, reporting revenue of about ₹300 crore in FY26, up threefold from FY25, and its first annual net profit, with a profit after tax margin of over 10%.

The company said the shift follows a business realignment in late 2025 that included reallocating capital and talent and pausing chip design work to focus on building and scaling its AI cloud stack. The company also recently shut down its AI assistant Kruti. The tool is not accessible via its standalone site, app platforms, or the Ola app.

“The company has reached an important milestone of being profitable, self-funded, and gaining market traction. Our AI cloud is built for Indian enterprises, by Indian engineers. The external client momentum we are seeing validates the depth of our platform,” a Krutrim spokesperson said.

Krutrim said its cloud platform is built in-house and deployed without external dependencies, with integration across the stack aimed at supporting enterprise AI workloads.

The company said it now operates a full-stack, domestically built AI cloud platform at production scale, serving sectors including mobility, manufacturing, customer operations, healthcare, and logistics.

The company reported growing external adoption, with more than 25 large enterprise customers across telecom, financial services, consumer internet, AI and deep-tech, healthcare, and logistics. It added that a majority of its GPU compute capacity is already committed to external enterprise workloads.

The customer base extends beyond the Ola Group, indicating wider enterprise use of its platform, the company said.

Krutrim said it plans to expand its enterprise cloud presence as demand for domestically built AI infrastructure rises.

title: Anthropic & OpenAI Partner with Private Equity Firms to Scale Enterprise AI Deployment
content:
The companies will help enterprises deploy their tools across different businesses.

What Actually Matters.

Anthropic, Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman, and Goldman Sachs formed a joint venture to integrate Claude into businesses.

This new firm will operate independently, supported by various asset managers.

Anthropic, Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman, and Goldman Sachs have launched a new $1.5 billion joint venture to help businesses integrate Claude into core operations, the companies announced on May 4.

The firm will operate as a standalone entity with Anthropic engineering and partnership resources embedded within its team. It is backed by a consortium of asset managers, including General Atlantic, Leonard Green & Partners, Apollo Global Management, GIC, and Sequoia Capital.

The company will focus on designing, building, and maintaining enterprise AI deployments, initially targeting investors’ portfolio companies as well as independent mid-sized firms.

“Enterprise demand for Claude is significantly outpacing any single delivery model,” said Krishna Rao, Chief Financial Officer at Anthropic. “This new firm brings additional operating capability to the ecosystem and capital from leading alternative asset managers.”

The initiative will address a shortage of skilled implementation partners, which executives identified as a constraint in enterprise AI adoption.

“We intend to build a scaled company to deploy Anthropic’s technology across a range of businesses in our portfolio and beyond,” said Jon Gray, President and Chief Operating Officer at Blackstone. “We believe it can help expand the number of highly skilled implementation partners.”

Patrick Healy, Chief Executive Officer at Hellman & Friedman, said the partnership aligns technical capability with investor reach.

Marc Nachmann, global head of asset and wealth management at Goldman Sachs, said the firm would support adoption among mid-market companies. “By expanding access to forward-deployed engineers, the new company can help portfolio companies and similar businesses accelerate AI adoption,” he said.

The firm will deploy engineers who work closely with Anthropic’s research and product teams to build systems that can adapt as AI models evolve.

Executives said the target sectors include healthcare, manufacturing, financial services, retail, real estate, and infrastructure, where demand for AI systems is increasing but technical expertise remains limited.

Meanwhile, OpenAI has finalised a $10 billion joint venture with a group of private equity firms to accelerate the deployment of its artificial intelligence tools across businesses, according to a Bloomberg report.

The new entity, referred to as The Deployment Company, will help companies integrate OpenAI’s technology into their operations, with a focus on portfolio companies owned by participating investors.

The venture has secured more than $4 billion in external capital from firms including TPG, Brookfield Asset Management, Advent International, and Bain Capital, while OpenAI is expected to contribute about $1.5 billion and retain operational control.

title: Karnataka Pioneers SpaceTech Centre of Excellence to Boost Commercial Innovation
content:
The Centre is designed to bridge the gap between research and real-world applications by enabling the commercialisation of space technologies.

What Actually Matters.

Karnataka has launched India's first state-led Centre of Excellence for Space Technology.

The Centre aims to commercialise space technologies and bridge the gap between research and application.

In a move to accelerate India’s growing space economy, the Karnataka government has launched the country’s first state-led Centre of Excellence (CoE) for Space Technology.

The initiative has been set up by the Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society in collaboration with the Satcom Industry Association India.

The Centre is designed to bridge the gap between research and real-world applications by enabling the commercialisation of space technologies. It will focus on advancing innovation while creating pathways for startups, enterprises, and researchers to scale solutions in the space sector.

Speaking at the launch, Priyank Kharge, Minister for Electronics, IT/BT, and Rural Development and Panchayat Raj in the Karnataka government, mentioned that the initiative builds on Karnataka’s long-standing leadership in technology and innovation, extending it into a strategically important domain. He added that the Centre would play a key role in translating research into economic value and employment opportunities.

The CoE SpaceTech Foundation aims to promote research and development in space technologies, support industry-aligned skill development, incubate startups, and enable cross-sector applications.

As part of its ecosystem-building approach, the Centre has also signed multiple partnerships with academic institutions and industry stakeholders. These collaborations will focus on emerging areas such as space biotechnology and microgravity research, while also strengthening talent pipelines and providing startups with training and market access.

The initiative comes at a time when India is looking to expand its footprint in the global space economy, with states increasingly playing a role in enabling innovation and private sector participation.

Meanwhile, Space startup Pixxel on Monday said it has entered a strategic partnership with Sarvam to develop and build India’s first orbital data centre satellite, Pathfinder.

title: Bagmane Prime Office REIT IPO Opens After Strong Anchor Interest
content:
The portfolio spans over 20 million square feet, with a committed occupancy of 98.8% as of December 2025.

What Actually Matters.

Bagmane Prime Office REIT's IPO opened after strong anchor investor interest.

The IPO aims to raise ₹3,405 crore through fresh issuance and an offer for sale.

The ₹3,405 crore initial public offering (IPO) of Bagmane Prime Office REIT, backed by global investment firm Blackstone, opened for subscription on May 5 after attracting robust demand from anchor investors.

Ahead of the launch, the Bengaluru-based REIT raised ₹1,149 crore by allotting over 11.49 crore units at ₹100 each to a mix of domestic and global institutional investors, according to exchange filings. The anchor book saw participation from major institutions, including mutual funds, insurance firms, and pension funds.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of units worth up to ₹2,390 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to ₹1,015 crore by existing unitholders. The issue is scheduled to close on May 7, with allotment expected by May 12 and listing on the NSE and BSE likely on May 15.

A significant portion of the proceeds—approximately ₹1,775 crore—will be used to acquire the Luxor asset at Bagmane Capital Tech Park, while around ₹1,025 crore will partly fund the acquisition of a 93% stake in another commercial portfolio asset. The remaining funds will be allocated for general corporate purposes.

Bagmane Prime Office REIT manages a portfolio of six Grade A+ business parks across key Bengaluru micro-markets, including Outer Ring Road (ORR) and the Secondary Business District (SBD).

The portfolio spans over 20 million sq ft, with a committed occupancy of 98.8% as of December 2025, leaving limited headroom for growth through vacancy absorption.

Company projections indicate that leasing of vacant office space is expected to contribute just about 1% of total growth through FY30. Between FY23 and the first nine months of FY26, Bagmane leased 7.2 million sq ft, of which 91.7% came from existing tenants expanding their footprint, while new tenant additions accounted for less than 9%.

Despite limited vacancy-driven upside, the REIT’s growth outlook is supported by its presence in supply-constrained, high-demand micro-markets. Vacancy levels remain low at around 4.1% in Bengaluru’s Outer Ring Road (ORR) and 5.4% in Secondary Business District (SBD), positioning the portfolio to benefit from steady rental appreciation.

According to JLL, rents in ORR are expected to grow at 5.2% annually through CY2028, while SBD rents are projected to rise at 6.5% over the same period—significantly outpacing broader Indian commercial real estate trends.

The REIT’s tenant base includes large, leading global technology companies such as Google, Amazon, NVIDIA, and Samsung.

In addition to office assets, the portfolio includes under-construction hospitality projects and solar power assets, diversifying its income streams. For FY25, Bagmane Prime Office REIT reported total income of ₹2,390.88 crore and a profit after tax of ₹897.10 crore, with an asset base exceeding ₹7,200 crore.

The IPO is being managed by leading investment banks, including Kotak Mahindra Capital Company, Axis Capital, and SBI Capital Markets.

title: MathCo partners with Google Cloud to push ‘workflow native AI’ adoption
content:
MathCo has partnered with Google Cloud to help enterprises move beyond isolated AI use cases and embed intelligence directly into end-to-end workflows.

What Actually Matters.

MathCo partners with Google Cloud to promote 'workflow native AI' for integrated workflows.

The collaboration aims to address challenges in translating AI adoption into measurable business outcomes.

MathCo has announced a collaboration with Google Cloud to help enterprises adopt what it calls “workflow native AI”, a shift from isolated AI use cases to fully integrated, end-to-end systems.

The partnership will leverage Gemini Enterprise including its agent platform and enterprise data connectivity to enable businesses to embed AI directly into workflows across functions.

The move comes at a time when companies are struggling to translate AI adoption into measurable outcomes. According to a 2026 Deloitte report while 66% of organisations report productivity gains from AI, only 34% are rethinking their business models around it. For many, revenue impact from AI still remains limited.

MathCo aims to address this gap through its “Systemic AI” framework which focuses on integrating AI across entire workflows rather than applying it to individual tasks. This means combining enterprise data, AI models and intelligent agents to allow systems to plan, reason and execute across multiple steps.

Aakarsh Kishore, Chief Product Officer at MathCo, said “The collaboration is focused not just on implementation but also on helping companies identify the right use cases and build strong data foundations to scale AI effectively.”

The approach is expected to impact multiple industries. In retail, for instance, AI can connect demand forecasting, pricing, and inventory planning into a single workflow. In consumer goods, it can link trade promotion planning with real-time performance tracking. In pharma, it can streamline processes such as content creation, approvals, and engagement tracking.

Gemini Enterprise acts as the central platform bringing together models, tools and data into a unified system. MathCo builds on top of this by embedding these capabilities into business processes to drive outcomes.

As enterprises deal with fragmented tools and low adoption, the focus is increasingly shifting from simply building AI systems to ensuring they work cohesively across teams and operations.

title: Persistent Systems Partners With IIT Kharagpur to Set Up AI Innovation Lab
content:
The collaboration aims to equip students with hands-on experience, combining academic learning with real-world AI engineering challenges.

What Actually Matters.

Persistent Systems and IIT Kharagpur are collaborating to establish an AI Innovation Lab focused on real-world AI challenges.

The initiative aims to enhance the synergy between industry and academia while preparing students for the AI-driven economy.

Persistent Systems has signed a memorandum of understanding with IIT Kharagpur to set up an AI Innovation Lab at the institute’s Department of Computer Science and Engineering.

The initiative is part of Persistent’s broader AI-first strategy and aims to strengthen collaboration between industry and academia while building talent for large-scale AI adoption.

The lab will focus on advancing research and applied development in areas such as healthcare analytics, education technology and financial intelligence. It will also be equipped with computational and laboratory infrastructure to support both teaching and real-world AI deployment.

According to the company, the goal is to move beyond experimentation and develop AI systems that are scalable, safe and aligned with real-world needs. The lab will bring together research, engineering and deployment, enabling students and researchers to work on practical challenges alongside academic work.

“The initiative is aimed at building strong foundations in research and engineering while addressing India-specific challenges,” Anand Deshpande, Founder and Managing Director of Persistent Systems, said. “The lab is part of efforts to prepare students for the growing demands of the AI-driven economy.”

Faculty members at IIT Kharagpur highlighted the importance of such collaborations in bridging the gap between academic learning and industry requirements. They noted that exposure to real-world problems and engineering practices can help students build more relevant and impactful solutions.

The lab is also expected to serve as a hub for knowledge exchange, fostering collaboration among academia, industry and policy stakeholders. In addition to research and training, it will help build reusable AI frameworks, domain expertise and talent pipelines.

title: BASF to Set Up Global Service & Digital Hubs in Hyderabad
content:
Hyderabad stands among the fastest-growing GCC hubs in the country, surpassing most major cities and adding over 75 GCCs in the past year alone.

What Actually Matters.

BASF will establish global service and digital hubs in Hyderabad, expected to be operational by the second quarter of 2026.

These hubs will support BASF's global operations, focusing on standardising processes and driving digital transformation.

German chemicals major BASF is set to establish a global service hub and a global digital hub in Hyderabad, further reinforcing the city’s position as a fast-growing global capability centre (GCC) destination.

The hubs are expected to become operational in the second quarter of 2026, as per the official release.

The company handed over a letter of intent (LOI) to Duddilla Sridhar Babu, Telangana’s Minister for Information Technology, Electronics, Communications, and Industries and Commerce.

The hubs will be operated under BASF Global Business Services Private Limited and will support the company’s global operations across functions such as finance, human resources, supply chain, regulatory services, and in-house consulting.

The integrated centres are expected to play a central role in standardising processes, driving operational efficiency, and enabling digital transformation across BASF’s global business units.

Hyderabad was selected following a competitive global evaluation, with the company citing the city’s skilled talent pool, business-friendly policies, and mature enterprise ecosystem as key factors.

Highlighting the state’s ambitions, Sridhar Babu said, “Today, Hyderabad stands among the fastest-growing GCC hubs in the country, surpassing most major cities and adding over 75 GCCs in the past year alone. We are now setting our sights even higher, with a target of over 100 new GCCs and more than one lakh jobs this year.”

“As we evolve from an incubation destination into a leading innovation and engineering capital, this growth is being anchored by forward-looking initiatives such as AIKAM, the industry-led Young India Skills University, and upcoming projects including a 200-acre AI city, a quantum hub, and 1BioLab,” he added.

The development underscores Hyderabad’s growing appeal across sectors, including technology, life sciences, and chemicals. The city already hosts major global enterprises, such as NVIDIA, Microsoft, Google, Vanguard, Eli Lilly and Company, Marriott International, and The Hartford.

Tobias Dratt, President of Global Business Services at BASF, said, “With the opening of our Global Service Hub in Hyderabad, we are creating a strong foundation for the future of Global Business Services. Hyderabad offers the right ecosystem and talent base to support scalable, high-quality services for BASF’s businesses worldwide.”

Meanwhile, Alexander Gerding, Managing Director of BASF India Limited and Head of BASF Group Companies in India, said, “The establishment of our global hub in Hyderabad marks a significant milestone and opens a new chapter in BASF’s long-standing presence in India. Building on our strong manufacturing and research and development footprint, this step directly supports our ‘Winning Ways’ strategy and strengthens our global capabilities.”

“With both our Global Business Services and Global Digital Services operating from the same location in Hyderabad, we’ll be able to harness shared strengths and collaboration opportunities, further reinforcing the city’s growing strategic importance within BASF’s global network,” Gerding added.

The Hyderabad hub will join BASF’s global network alongside centres in Berlin, Kuala Lumpur, and Montevideo, supporting coordinated, technology-led operations across regions

title: Carrier to Set up its Chiller Plant in Andhra’s Sri City
content:
The state signals a shift from data centre hosting to manufacturing, with an investment of ₹1,000 crore and job creation.

What Actually Matters.

Carrier Global Corporation will establish a chiller manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh's Sri City.

The project involves an investment of ₹1,000 crore and is expected to generate approximately 3,000 jobs.

The Andhra Pradesh government is going to break ground on a new manufacturing facility by Carrier Global Corporation in Sri City on May 6. The announcement came through an X post by Nara Lokesh, Andhra Pradesh’s Minister for IT, Electronics, and Human Resources Development, who said the plant will produce cooling systems for data centres.

The project involves an investment of ₹1,000 crore and is expected to generate around 3,000 jobs.

Lokesh said the facility marks a move beyond hosting data centres to manufacturing core components. He added that David Gitlin, Chairman and CEO at Carrier, will attend the event. The company plans to produce chillers, air handling units, and related infrastructure at the site.

Lokesh added that the state aims to “build what powers the data revolution”. He added that Andhra Pradesh is “moving beyond hosting data centres”. The focus now includes producing systems that support data infrastructure.

He said the project aligns with the state’s goal to become a hub for data centre infrastructure. The post also described Andhra Pradesh as “emerging as the data centre capital of India.”

The government expects the project to create both direct and indirect jobs as per the committed number. It also sees the investment as part of a wider push to develop industrial capacity linked to digital infrastructure. The plant will support demand for cooling systems used in data centres. These systems are key to maintaining operations in large-scale computing facilities.

Located in Tirupati district, about 55 km from Chennai, Sri City has emerged as a major industrial zone. It has attracted investments exceeding $4.5 billion and exports above $4 billion. The zone includes a multi-product Special Economic Zone, a Domestic Tariff Zone, a Free Trade and Warehousing Zone, and an electronics manufacturing cluster.

The park hosts over 220 companies from 30 countries across sectors. These include firms such as Isuzu Motors India, PepsiCo, Colgate-Palmolive, LG Electronics, Kimberly-Clark and Foxconn.

Sri City also benefits from transport links, including a national highway, nearby ports, airports, and rail access. The zone offers power, water, and plug-and-play factory facilities, along with a single-window clearance system.

title: Applied Materials to Expand Chip Packaging with NEXX Acquisition
content:
The Pathfinder satellite, in the 200 kg class, will carry data centre-grade GPUs typically used in terrestrial AI systems.

What Actually Matters.

Pixxel and Sarvam are collaborating to create an orbital data centre satellite, Pathfinder, by late 2026.

The Pathfinder satellite will host data centre-grade GPUs for in-orbit AI training and inference.

Space tech startup Pixxel has partnered with Sarvam to develop an orbital data centre satellite, with a launch targeted as early as the fourth quarter of 2026.

The satellite, named Pathfinder, will be designed, built, launched, and operated by Pixxel, while Sarvam will provide the AI infrastructure, enabling both training and inference directly in orbit.

The companies said the system will run full-stack language models on board without relying on ground-based cloud infrastructure.

The Pathfinder satellite, in the 200 kg class, will carry data centre-grade GPUs typically used in terrestrial AI systems. Unlike conventional satellites that use low-power processors, the system is intended to process data in orbit. It will also host Pixxel’s hyperspectral imaging camera to capture Earth observation data and analyse it in real time.

According to the companies, this approach reduces the need to transmit large volumes of raw data to Earth. Instead, the satellite will process imagery in orbit to identify patterns and generate insights, with applications in environmental monitoring, resource management, and infrastructure tracking.

“Ground-based data centres are facing increasing constraints around energy, land, regulation, and scale, and the current model is becoming harder to sustain environmentally,” said Awais Ahmed, CEO of Pixxel. “Orbital data centres open up a new frontier, where compute can be powered by solar energy, operate closer to space-based data, and move beyond some of the limits faced on Earth.”

Sarvam said the partnership extends its AI platform into space, with models developed in India running directly on the satellite.

“AI infrastructure is not just a software question—it is a sovereignty question,” said Pratyush Kumar, CEO of Sarvam. “Partnering with Pixxel allows us to extend that stack into space. Having India-built models running in orbit aboard an India-built satellite is the kind of capability the country needs to control its own intelligence infrastructure.”

The mission will test AI inference and data processing in orbit, including performance, power use, thermal conditions, and data workflows. The companies said the project is intended to establish the basis for future orbital data centre systems.

The satellite will be developed at Gigapixxel, a manufacturing facility being set up by Pixxel to scale satellite production to up to 100 units.

The partnership will demonstrate a model for deploying orbital data centre satellites for organisations with compute-intensive and strategic requirements.

Meanwhile, Agnikul Cosmos and NeevCloud are also working on an AI data centre in space, with a demonstration targeted around 2026. The plan involves converting the upper stages of Agnikul’s launch vehicles into orbital compute modules, with NeevCloud providing the AI and cloud stack for in-orbit inference.

title: Applied Materials to Expand Chip Packaging with NEXX Acquisition
content:
The deal aims to strengthen panel-level packaging capabilities for AI chip production and accelerate the adoption of large-format technologies.

What Actually Matters.

Applied Materials plans to acquire NEXX to enhance its chip packaging capabilities for AI production.

The acquisition will integrate advanced electrochemical deposition technology into Applied's offerings.

Applied Materials has signed a definitive agreement with ASMPT Limited to acquire its NEXX business, a supplier of advanced packaging deposition equipment for the semiconductor industry.

The company announced the deal in India and said it expects to close it in the next several months, subject to customary conditions. No regulatory approvals are required.

The acquisition will add NEXX’s panel-level electrochemical deposition technology to Applied Materials’ portfolio. The company said the move will support growing demand for larger and more complex AI chip packages.

With this deal, the NEXX team will join Applied’s Semiconductor Products Group and remain based in Billerica, Massachusetts.

Applied Materials said rising AI workloads are increasing demand for chiplet-based designs. These designs integrate GPUs, high-bandwidth memory, and input-output chips into a single package. The company added that advanced architectures such as 2.5D and 3D stacking require larger interposers and substrates.

It said this shift is driving a transition from 300-millimetre wafers to larger panel formats. These formats can reach sizes of 510 by 515 millimetres or more. The change enables higher output and larger chip designs.

Applied Materials said it already offers systems across digital lithography, physical vapour deposition, chemical vapour deposition, and etch. It also provides eBeam metrology and inspection tools. The addition of NEXX’s technology will expand its offerings and address a larger market.

“Having NEXX join Applied Materials complements our leadership in advanced packaging, particularly in panel processing,” said Prabu Raja, President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials, in a statement.

ASMPT NEXX President Jarek Pisera added that the deal will support the adoption of large-format packaging technologies. Applied Materials also added that the acquisition will help it develop co-optimised solutions for fine-pitch wiring.

It said that this will support advanced packaging roadmaps for chipmakers and systems companies. The company said forward-looking statements in the announcement are subject to risks and uncertainties. These include the ability to complete the transaction and integrate operations.

title: Infosys Bags $500 Million GCC Deal From Truist, To Build 4,500-Employee Hyderabad Hub
content:
The centre is reportedly expected to employ at least 4,500 people over time, making it one of the largest such engagements executed by an IT services provider.

What Actually Matters.

Infosys secured a significant deal with Truist Financial to establish a technology and operations hub in Hyderabad.

The contract involves Infosys building and operating the Global Capability Centre for five years before transferring it to Truist.

Infosys has secured its largest global capability centre (GCC) contract, winning a deal worth over $500 million from US-based Truist Financial to set up and run a technology and operations hub in Hyderabad, Mint reported.

The contract, won in March, will see Infosys establish and operate the GCC under a build-operate-transfer model, wherein it will manage the facility for five years before handing it over to the client.

The centre is expected to employ at least 4,500 people over time, making it one of the largest such engagements executed by an IT services provider, Mint earlier reported on April 29.

The Hyderabad facility will go beyond traditional IT services, supporting functions such as finance, human resources and sales, expanding the scope of GCCs from back-office operations to integrated enterprise hubs. Infosys plans to hire around 2,000 employees, including senior leadership, in the first year itself.

The deal deepens a relationship spanning over two decades between Infosys and Truist, and comes at a time when global enterprises are increasingly looking to India to build large-scale capability centres anchored in digital and AI-led operations.

India’s GCC ecosystem has also been expanding rapidly, driven by multinational corporations setting up captive hubs for technology, operations and innovation.

According to the report, Infosys is expected to generate at least $100 million in revenue from the arrangement, equivalent to about 0.5% incremental revenue in the current fiscal year.

Unlike traditional outsourcing contracts that focus on staffing or project delivery, Infosys will effectively build and run the entire centre before transferring it, showing a more strategic role for IT service firms in clients’ operating models.

This also comes amid mixed demand signals for Indian IT firms, with companies navigating slower discretionary spending and client-specific headwinds amid the rise of artificial intelligence and geopolitical tensions.

For the fourth quarter of FY26, Infosys reported revenue of $5.04 billion, registering a 4.1% year-on-year growth in constant currency, even as revenue declined 1.3% sequentially. For the full fiscal year, it crossed the $20 billion revenue milestone, reporting $20.16 billion in FY26 revenue.

title: Delhi Govt Looks to Partner With AI Startups to Enhance Governance, Public Services
content:
The Delhi government will collaborate with technology companies, startups, and research institutions to develop AI-driven solutions.

What Actually Matters.

The Delhi government is partnering with tech companies and AI startups.

This collaboration aims to enhance governance and public service delivery.

The Delhi government is increasingly collaborating with technology companies and AI startups to strengthen governance and improve the delivery of public services, as per a TOI report. The initiative focuses on integrating artificial intelligence across departments to enhance efficiency, transparency, and decision-making.

The state government will collaborate with technology companies, startups, and research institutions to develop AI-driven solutions across key sectors such as education, transport, urban planning, and air quality monitoring.

As part of this push, authorities are reportedly leveraging AI-driven tools such as predictive analytics, automation systems, and data intelligence platforms to streamline administrative processes and reduce operational delays. These technologies are being explored for use in areas including urban planning, public safety, traffic management, and citizen grievance redressal.

According to the report, officials believe that partnerships with startups bring agility and innovation, enabling faster deployment of scalable solutions tailored to real-world governance challenges. The approach also supports the broader goal of building a digitally empowered public infrastructure.

The move aligns with India’s ongoing efforts to adopt emerging technologies at scale, while fostering a collaborative ecosystem between government bodies, private enterprises, and the startup community. It also reflects a shift toward data-driven governance, where insights derived from AI can help improve policy implementation and service delivery outcomes.

As adoption grows, the Delhi government is expected to further expand these collaborations, positioning AI as a central pillar in modernising governance frameworks across the country.

Meanwhile, in a recent meeting with bank leaders and financial services stakeholders, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has recently flagged emerging risks from advanced AI models such as Claude Mythos, warning that India’s banking system may need “something far more versatile” to counter evolving cyber threats.

title: Bengaluru-based GalaxEye Launches Mission Drishti, ‘World’s First’ OptoSAR Satellite
content:
The satellite weighs 190 kg and is the largest privately developed Earth observation satellite from India.

What Actually Matters.

Bengaluru-based GalaxEye launched Mission Drishti, an Earth observation satellite.

Mission Drishti is the world's first OptoSAR satellite, combining SAR and electro-optical imaging.

Bengaluru-based space startup GalaxEye has launched its Earth observation satellite, Mission Drishti, aboard a Falcon 9 operated by SpaceX from Vandenberg, California.

Mission Drishti combines Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and electro-optical imaging on a single satellite platform, enabling imaging in all weather conditions, including through cloud cover and at night.

The satellite weighs 190 kg and is the largest privately developed Earth observation satellite from India. The company said the mission is the result of more than five years of research and development.

“Mission Drishti marks our first mission and the culmination of over five years of sustained R&D to develop this technology. With the satellite now successfully in orbit, our immediate focus is on completing its commissioning,” said Suyash Singh, Founder and CEO of GalaxEye. “We are already witnessing strong global interest in the datasets enabled by our OptoSAR payload.”

The satellite will undergo commissioning before initial imagery is delivered to customers in the coming weeks. The company said it has received interest from government and commercial users internationally.

Mission Drishti by GalaxEye marks a major achievement in our space journey. The successful launch of the world’s first OptoSAR satellite and the largest privately-built satellite in India is a testament to our youth’s passion for innovation and nation-building.

— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) May 3, 2026

GalaxEye has partnered with NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), the commercial arm of Indian Space Research Organisation, for global distribution of its satellite imagery.

Mission Drishti was developed with support from IN-SPACe, which provided access to testing infrastructure and regulatory approvals.

“The sustained effort over the last five to six years on confidence-building, capacity-building, and the commercialisation of India’s private space technology ecosystem is now showing tangible results,” said Pawan Goenka, Chairman of IN-SPACe. “Mission Drishti by GalaxEye is a fine example of this.”

The satellite is designed for applications across defence, agriculture, disaster management, maritime monitoring and infrastructure planning.

Founded in 2021, GalaxEye is a space technology company focused on Earth observation systems. It has raised over $20 million from investors, including Speciale Invest, Mela Ventures, Infosys, Ideaforge and Rainmatter.

Set up by five alumni of Indian Institute of Technology Madras, the company is building Earth observation systems using its OptoSAR technology. The founding team includes Singh, Denil Chawda (CTO), Kishan Thakkar (VP – Engineering), Pranit Mehta (VP – Sales Ops), and Rakshit Bhatt (VP – Product).

title: Google Photos Introduces AI ‘Wardrobe’ Feature Inspired by Clueless
content:
The upcoming feature will use AI to turn users’ photo libraries into a digital closet, enabling outfit creation and curation, organisation and virtual try-ons.

What Actually Matters.

Google Photos is set to launch an AI-powered 'Wardrobe' feature that transforms photo libraries into a digital closet.

The feature will allow users to organise clothing items and create new outfits through a mix-and-match interface.

Google is planning to introduce an AI-powered ‘Wardrobe’ feature to Google Photos, aiming to transform users’ photo libraries into a personalised digital closet.

The feature uses AI to scan images, and identify clothing and accessories worn by users. It then creates a structured wardrobe within the app where items can be sorted into categories such as tops, bottoms, and jewellery.

From there, users can mix and match pieces to create new outfits directly within the platform. These combinations can be saved and organised into mood boards for different occasions, or shared with others.

The feature also includes a virtual try-on capability, allowing users to preview how selected outfits might look in reality. The concept draws inspiration from the iconic digital wardrobe seen in the film ‘Clueless’, where the main character could browse and plan outfits using a computerised closet.

The company says AI will automatically generate a wardrobe from existing photos, though results may depend on the quality and type of images in a user’s library. Well-lit, full-body images are expected to deliver better accuracy.

While the feature is not live yet, it is expected to roll out first on Android later this summer, followed by iOS, where it will be available under the ‘Collections’ section.

With this move, Google enters a space already occupied by fashion-focused apps such as digital wardrobe planners and styling tools. The company is positioning AI as a way to make outfit planning more accessible, allowing users to organise and experiment with their clothing without needing separate platforms.

title: Cognizant to Acquire Astreya to Strengthen AI Infrastructure, Managed Services Capabilities
content:
The IT services firm looks to deepen capabilities in AI-led managed services and infrastructure amid a global surge in data centre investments.

What Actually Matters.

Cognizant is acquiring Astreya to enhance its AI-led managed services and infrastructure capabilities.

The acquisition aligns with Cognizant's strategy to become an 'AI builder' for large-scale AI operationalisation.

Cognizant has agreed to acquire IT managed service provider Astreya for an undisclosed amount, as the IT services firm looks to deepen capabilities in AI-led managed services and infrastructure amid a global surge in data centre investments.

The transaction, expected to close in the second quarter of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals, comes as Cognizant accelerates its shift to an ‘AI builder’ model, focused on helping enterprises operationalise AI at scale rather than limiting itself to advisory or pilot deployments.

Founded in 2001 and operating in over 35 countries, Astreya provides managed services across data centres, enterprise networks and digital workplace systems. It counts several large technology firms among its clients, including long-term engagements with multiple hyperscalers. The company has built an AI-led operations platform, AI OpsHub, which includes tools for analytics, automation and system monitoring.

For Cognizant, the acquisition adds production-grade AI operations capabilities at a time when enterprises are grappling with the complexity of deploying and managing AI infrastructure. The deal also strengthens its positioning in infrastructure services, a segment that is seeing renewed interest alongside large-scale investments in AI data centres globally.

“By acquiring Astreya and its proprietary AI tooling and production-grade infrastructure platform, which is complementary to Cognizant's AI builder stack, we will be even better-positioned to help clients architect their platform-led AI systems and operationalise them at scale,” Cognizant CEO Ravi Kumar S said in a statement.

Industry estimates cited by the company suggest AI data centre infrastructure spending could reach $6.7 trillion between 2025 and 2030, with the five largest hyperscalers expected to spend nearly $700 billion on infrastructure in 2026 alone.

The acquisition is also expected to expand Cognizant’s partnerships with platforms such as Google Cloud and ServiceNow, where Astreya already has established ecosystem relationships.

Cognizant noted that Astreya’s capabilities would allow it to offer ready-to-deploy AI operations tools and talent to clients, while giving Astreya access to a larger global delivery network and broader enterprise customer base.

“Joining Cognizant is the natural next chapter for the Astreya global team and, importantly, the clients who have trusted us to operate their most critical technology environments,” said Romil Bahl, President and CEO, Astreya. “We have spent the last several years making deliberate, disciplined investments in AI: building platforms, training specialists, and fundamentally redesigning how managed services are delivered.”

The move also follows a series of strategic shifts by large IT services firms to align with AI-led spending cycles, as traditional application development and maintenance work faces pricing pressure and slower growth.

The announcement comes alongside Cognizant’s unveiling of Project Leap, a company-wide transformation programme aimed at accelerating its shift to an AI-first operating model while tightening costs, with expected savings of $200-300 million in 2026.

For the quarter ended March 31, Cognizant reported revenue of $5.4 billion, up 5.8% year-on-year, or 3.9% in constant currency.

title: Cognizant Rolls Out Project Leap as a Major Workforce Reset to Fund AI Shift
content:
Cognizant has doubled down on AI-led efficiencies and cost savings, even as Q1 revenue rose 3.9% YoY in constant currency along with strong bookings.

What Actually Matters.

Cognizant introduced Project Leap to accelerate its shift to an AI-first operating model.

The initiative aims to tighten costs and improve productivity across the company.

IT services firm Cognizant has unveiled Project Leap, a company-wide transformation programme aimed at accelerating its shift to an AI-first operating model, while tightening costs and improving productivity.

The initiative, announced alongside the company’s March quarter results, is designed to fund investments in AI capabilities, integrated offerings, and strategic partnerships, while reshaping its workforce.

“By fostering a workforce that is properly sized, AI-enabled and possesses the skills required for success as well as optimising our technology footprint, we aim to streamline operations and enhance productivity through AI-led efficiencies, creating a more agile and cost-effective operating model,” the company said in a statement.

Cognizant expects the programme to generate between $200–300 million in savings in 2026, which will be reinvested into AI and transformation efforts.

However, the transformation will come with upfront costs. The company expects to incur $230–320 million in charges, largely tied to employee severance and related expenses, signalling a restructuring of its workforce as it pivots toward AI-led delivery.

According to a Mint report, the company is planning a fresh round of job cuts, and may lay off 4,000 employees—or roughly 1% of its global workforce.

For the quarter ended March 31, Cognizant reported revenue of $5.4 billion, up 5.8% year-on-year or 3.9% in constant currency, placing growth in the upper half of its guidance range.

The GAAP operating margin, which measures the percentage of revenue remaining after covering operating costs, declined 110 basis points to 15.6%, while the adjusted operating margin saw a marginal uptick of 10 basis points. Net income remained largely flat at $662 million, compared with $663 million a year earlier.

Earnings showed stronger momentum on an adjusted basis, with adjusted earnings-per-share rising 13.8% year-on-year to $1.40.

The company reported 21% year-on-year growth in bookings in the quarter under review, supported by seven large deals —deals with total contract value of $100 million or greater—including one mega deal exceeding $500 million in total contract value.

“We believe our AI builder strategy, deep industry expertise and scaled partnership ecosystem uniquely position us to bridge the AI velocity gap by helping clients convert their significant AI investments into tangible business outcomes,” noted Cognizant Chief Executive Officer Ravi Kumar S in a statement.

Cognizant maintained its 2026 full-year constant currency revenue growth guidance of 4% to 6.5%, indicating steady demand despite macro uncertainties. It expects full-year revenue in the range of $22.1 billion to $22.6 billion.

Meanwhile, savings from Project Leap have enabled the company to raise its full-year adjusted operating margin guidance by 20–40 basis points, up from its earlier forecast of 10–30 basis points.

Cognizant’s latest move follows a broader shift underway in the IT services sector, where firms are increasingly investing in AI to drive productivity gains while rebalancing headcount-heavy operating models.
